reviews.review: Great vibe. Friendly staff. I had a great cocktail - Melon E Melon.  Manilla Clams and the fried rice and pork. Great flavors. Will definitely be back. The large dishes looked great and perfect to share. Come hungry.

Fish Cheeks is a fantastic destination for those looking to experience Thai cuisine with a modern and exciting twist. From the moment I walked in, I was impressed by the vibrant yet sophisticated decor, which perfectly balances contemporary design with warm, inviting touches. The atmosphere is energetic but not overwhelming, making it a great place for both casual dinners and special occasions.

The food was absolutely phenomenal. I started with the spicy papaya salad, which had the perfect combination of heat, tanginess, and crunch--each bite was refreshing yet packed with bold flavors. The sticky ribs were another standout dish, incredibly tender with a beautifully caramelized exterior that had just the right amount of smoky sweetness. Every dish was thoughtfully presented, making the experience even more enjoyable.

What truly elevated the experience was the impeccable service. The staff was friendly, knowledgeable, and eager to provide recommendations, ensuring that each guest found something they would love. They were attentive without being intrusive, creating a relaxed and comfortable dining experience.

Overall, Fish Cheeks is a must-visit for anyone who appreciates high-quality Thai food with a contemporary flair. The combination of delicious dishes, stylish ambiance, and excellent service makes it a standout in NYC's competitive dining scene. I'll definitely be returning to explore more of the menu!

Have had Fish Cheeks on my list to visit for a long time and it did not disappoint! Almost every dish I got was a hit with my group! I think my view on Tom Yum soup was forever changed by the special they had that night! The only issue being the bowl they served it in was very hard to get the soup out. The corn som tum was also amazing and not what I expected at all! I will say that when people say to focus on the seafood related dishes I would listen to them! All the dishes we got were great but the crispy pork belly dish could not compare to everything else we got that night. Also a warning to those who cannot handle spice, definitely steer clear of anything with more than one chili on the menu, they mean business!

Food is amazing! I've never tasted such tender and flavorful roast chicken! Pork belly dish is great! The steamed fish tops my expectations, fresh and tender with aromatic spices and herbs. And the fish's presentation is a piece of art. For desert we had ice cream with pearls tapioca and sticky rice, fantastic finishing for our lunch!

Service was excellent! They changed our plates between different dishes. The service staff is friendly and checked on us frequently.

Ambiance is relaxing and cool.

Definitely going back soon!

Excellent Thai food! Everything was very tasty. Highlights would be the oysters and clams! I thought the wings were solid but I don't completely understand the hype. They didn't blow my mind. Had the tongue and cheek cocktail, which was a bit watered down. Glad to have taken advantage of the happy hour before 5pm (available all week long). The inside was very lively but still able to have a conversation with your dinner guest. Had a nice early dinner

We had a decent experience at Fish Cheeks on a Thursday evening. The decor is warm and inviting, but be prepared for a loud atmosphere. We started with cocktails, trying the Nam Gin Martini (excellent for garlic lovers!) and the Low ABV Spicy Mango (a bit too sweet for our taste).

For starters, we ordered the Mussel Gorlae and Squid Ink Calamari, both of which were extremely flavorful and a hit at our table.

For our main courses, we opted for family-style sharing and ordered the Crab Fried Rice (so good!), Coconut Crab Curry (packed with flavor, not too spicy), and Grilled Mackerel. Our server did warn us that the mackerel was 'fishy-forward', but unfortunately, it didn't quite work for us. The fish sauce was overpowering and clashed with the sweetness of the mango, creating an unbalanced flavor profile that we couldn't enjoy.

Overall, while Fish Cheeks lives up to the hype in some ways, we've had better Thai food elsewhere. Worth trying, but not a standout for us.

Came here for dinner. Ordered the market oysters and they were alright, didnt feel anything special on them. Ordered prawn karee and fried rice. They were alright as well. The ambiance was good a bit in the dim side. What I liked was the free side dish they provided: fried shrimp crackers. If the free side dish is better than their main course, then there is something not right with this place...

Food (all wonderful, would recommend!)
- steamed fish - very flavored, boneless soft fish
- coconut crab curry - spicy curry with generous crab chunks
- crab aob woonsen - glass noodles with a flavorful sauce and chunky crab pieces
- pakboong fai dang - delicious vegetable side dish
- ice cream Bo Lan - really tasty way to end our meal with pandan and jackfruit ice cream with amazing sticky rice

Service was timely, pleasant, no complaints 

Restaurant has two parts, decent size with a chic ambiance. Great evening dinner for a date night or get together with friends

This place is so good I had to go back! The first time, I had the steamed fish, crab fried rice, and cabbage--absolutely incredible. This time, I got the fish fried and paired it with a curry dish, and it was just as amazing. The flavors are rich, the food is fresh, and the service is top-notch. I sat at the bar again, and the staff was just as accommodating and friendly as before.

Highly recommend--this is a must-visit every time I'm in New York!

Yummy spot!! 
We had a rez for 12 on a sat and it was filling up as soon as it opened. The crab fried rice, crab curry, morning glory, all very satisfactory. We were 2 and finished everything- altho we were def full im ngl its like wild for us to go to a thai spot, order 3 things, and not have left overs (in other words, the portions r on the smaller side) 
More spacious inside than i would expect from this type of place. Eavesdropped on two tech bros next to us giving pep talks on how to be good managers/leaders. 
Want to come back and try the vegan stuff

Lucky to have snagged a table as my friend and I have been wanting to try this place. We  were seated promptly. You are within close quarters of other diners but nothing too crazy or overly cramped. This place has a welcoming ambiance with welcoming crowd. Our waiter was very patient explaining the menu and answering any questions, as well as providing recommendations. There were so many things we wanted to try. The corn salad was sweet and was a nice starter followed by the grilled cuttlefish. Cuttlefish was a decent portion for a starter, bit chewy but still tasty. We had to get the coconut crab curry to try, and it did not disappoint. It had an explosion of flavors and probably a dish I can order for myself. Tons of flavor. Steamed fish was cooked perfectly and the veggies is welcome addition to everything else we ordered. Could not finish all the food amongst 2 people. Everything was so tasty, it was hard to narrow down what to get. By the time, we finished, the restaurant and bar area was packed. A good date night, special occasion, or catch up with friends spot.

Really good Thai food forgot to take more pictures. 

Sat outside but it was really cozy. Service was good as well. 

A little spicier than I expected

Allergy friendly!

Fish Cheeks is 100% worth a visit if you enjoy Thai cuisine and flavors. I would recommend making a reservation ahead of time as the restaurant gets extremely busy during dinner hours, and you may be waiting for a while if you do a walk-in. The restaurant is quite lively, with dimmed lights during dinner time. 

I was pleased to find out that Fish Cheeks has a Happy Hour from 12-6pm everyday. During Happy Hour, all cocktails are $13 instead of $19. I really enjoyed the Tongue & Cheek cocktail, which was fruity and refreshing. I also had a Thai Iced Tea, which was good but had a bit too much ice as the glass was still over 60% full of ice when I finished the drink.  

The Grilled Pork Cheeks starter is SO delicious! The meat is extremely tender, and full of flavor. The sauce that comes with this appetizer is really unique and pairs well with the meat. As for mains, the Rawaaeng Duck Curry and 30 Days Dry Aged Beef Kaprow were both excellent, though I personally enjoyed the Duck Curry a bit more. The Beef Kaprow is spicier than I was expecting, and I probably should have asked for it to be a bit milder. Despite being a bit too spicy, I found the flavors of the dish to be incredibly tasty. The Duck meat in the Curry dish was extremely tender as well. I really enjoyed pairing this dish with the rice. I look forward to trying other dishes in a future visit to Fish Cheeks!

My friend and I came here for a restaurant week just last night. The restaurant is very cute and they dimmed the lights low about 15 minutes in to give that relaxing, warm ambiance. I started off with the Melon E Melon drink with our waiter Clem. I did enjoy that drink, but I had to try the Punch Drunk Love next. That was my favorite. It was refreshing. There's lychee in it so I couldn't say no to that. My friend only wanted one drink, and when she tried that one, she had to order it.

We had the chef seasonal bite and it was like ceviche. Clem said that the shrimp was cured ? I believe. As I've gotten older, I've gotten weird about texture, but it looked so fresh that I had to try it. That it was. It was spicy, it was fresh, it tasted like cilantro, it had a great kick. After about 20 seconds, then the fishy taste hit me so it kinda started tasting like the ocean. Next up was the starters. I had the wings as a recommendation from Clem and they were really good. They kind of reminded me of lemon pepper wings. I'm not a lemon pepper girl, but there was citrus, which could've been lemongrass, but there was a spice to it that reminded me of the pepper aspect of lemon pepper wings. For my entrée, I had Gaeng Toh-Maeh which was another recommendation from Clem. I was told that it was a specialty for the restaurant week menu. It's basically a curry sauce with fish and it comes with rice. I was not the biggest fan of whole black peppercorns in the dish nor the curry leaves. They had a bitter taste to them like bay leaves and the way that I was taught to cook, I was always taught to remove bay leaves since they are just there for flavor and very bitter when you bite into them. I'm not a curry girl but I really did enjoy that dish! For me, everything I was trying or wanted to try was meant to be something that I normally wouldn't order any other day. Originally, I was going to get the crispy rice, salad with pork as my starter instead of the wings, but I was advised to get the wings. I don't regret that decision. I feel like everything had such complex layers to it that complemented the dish and complemented each layer. I personally haven't felt like I came across dishes OR cocktails with such depth.

Now, at this point, I believe it was management that approached us saying that our reservation was up since it's only 90 minutes. I didn't book the reservation so I didn't know anything about it and I wasn't paying attention to the time either. We weren't shoveling food down our face. We were just enjoying our meal and having a good time but we did receive our entree a little over an hour after we arrived even though we put our order in all at once. I mentioned to my friend that it makes sense since most places normally have a timeframe for reservations. I looked at my phone to see that we had two minutes left before our reservation was over. We were asked if we could move to the bar and a round of drinks would be on them. I said sure because it was nothing that we could do anyway and our was time was almost up. As I was getting up, Clem rushed over and asked what was going on so I mentioned we were asked to move to the bar. It was weird because why didn't they mention to our waitress that they were moving us before actually asking can we move? Also, it would've been nice to have a heads up because we both were caught off guard. However, we went to the bar, got our comped drink, had our food boxed up, and we were served our desserts. The bartender was nice as well. That pandan ice cream needs to be sold in stores. It had sticky rice at the bottom. I almost feel like that needed to be a little bigger lolol. It was that good. My comped drink was the No Pad Thai Zone which wasn't bad but the melon cream on top was absolutely phenomenal.

I ordered the steam fish, crab fried rice, and pork belly. Steamed fish was more on the saltier side (but presentation was beautiful in the fish shaped dish) and it tastes very similar to Vietnamese steamed fish doused in a lot of herbs and fish sauce. The crab fried rice was my favorite! Pork belly was extremely crunchy but it was not as juicy as I thought it would be (more on dry side). Server was extremely nice and friendly :)
Everything I had to eat here was so good!! The cocktails are also great. I would 100% recommend the crab curry and the chu chee prawns. The inside is cute and the service is also good

Food and drinks were excellent! The pork belly was just alright, but the crab fried rice and crab curry was a 10/10. The Thai iced tea and limeade were also refreshing. The curry was a bit spicy, but not too bad. The other sides and rice helped cool it down. The inside was decorated very nicely. The service was also great. Food came out very fast.

Loved the food here so much! Our favorite dish was the pork cheek, so tender and the sauce was so perfect. The corn salad was good too, corn was sweet. Our other favorite dish was the steamed fish, the lemon and cilantro flavor was amazing. Ate half a bowl of rice just for the fish and the sauce. We also had the duck curry, the curry flavor was good but the duck was a little underwhelming. However, i'd definitely still want to come back and this place would be my top recommendation for food in NY! Big shout out to our server for being so accommodating when we wanted to split an iced thai tea between the two of us!
Wow!! Excellent food service and ambiance. When in the Bowery one must go to fish cheeks. Reasonable prices as well!

This restaurant was recommended by a lot of people and I had to try this place! 

My friend from Japan who lived in Thailand was visiting, she definitely approved for authenticity of all of the flavors in their food! 

The server was very helpful and knowledgeable, all of the dishes he recommended was SO good!

This place has a chill vibe but very busy, definitely recommend to make reservations.

This place was a 10 out of 10 for my entire family. It was the best experience ever.

This place is packed in for a good reason their food is packed with flavor and honestly such a memorable experience 

The staff is super friendly and very welcoming explaining the menu and making sure you're comfortable with what you're ordering. It is authentic Thai food so it's not going to be your typical pad Thai kind of place. 

Everything that was served was absolutely delicious and blasting with flavor. The wings have this scrumptious rub on them that just leaves you wanting more. 

We got a curry lamb dish that was to die for the curry was so divine. My mom absolutely loved it and then we also got a whole fish and that was so tender juicy and so fresh in line at the same time. 

This place also has a gluten-free menu so if you have celiac, that's something to flag. My mom has celiac, and they were very gracious with her allergy, making sure that everything we ordered did not have gluten in it or whatever she was eating did not have gluten in it.

The restaurant itself is super clean. It's really beautiful inside lots of colors and a play on the Thai agriculture and ART.

Solid spot for Thai style seafood. The main highlight was the steamed fish with Thai herbs, very delicious and surprised that it was completely boneless. Loved the Thai herbs sauce made it paired really well. Oysters, crab fried rice, coconut curry, shrimp in 3 crab sauce was all good.
I did order the $10 coco bah drink. In my opinion, it was nothing impressive. It was pretty pricey considering how small the glass was and half of it was ice.
Overall service was fast and workers were nice.

OMG! This place was an amazing first meal!!!!! We went here on a whim when we landed since it was close to our hotel and we loved the vibe inside once we sat down and continued to be amazed by our kind servers and the delicious food we ordered! The crab curry and wings were AMAZINGGGGGG!!!! Don't sleep on this spot!

It'd be perfect if they have more non-spicy options or make some of their food less spicy. I LOVE spicy food and actually have a very high tolerance but some dishes are even spicy to me so I can't imagine what it's be for others. But solid Thai food in the city with a cozy space. Service is just okay nothing to note.

Everything from food, to service, to ambiance was incredible. We sat at the bar and had a great time. They have happy hour until 6 and their cocktails are delicious and beautiful. I definitely would recommend the milk punch (it's very similar to a rum punch). The oysters were fresh and delicious, as was the shrimp. Everything was packed with flavor. We also loved the crab fried rice, which had so much crab in it. I came here with my friend who is gluten free/celiac and they have a whole GF menu. It's a great spot and I'm excited to come back!

Fish Cheeks provided a delicious meal overall, but a couple of the dishes were less successful than others,and be ready for an unapologetic acid and spice bomb.

The whole Branzino (steamed fish with thai herbs) in cilantro-lime broth was fantastic. Juicy, tangy, moist, wouldn't change a thing. The SomTum Corn Salad however was a little disappointing - maybe this would be better when corn was in season but it lacked the sweetness and freshness needed to balance the dish. The fried chicken wings were tangy and tasty.

The crispy rice salad was one of the best examples we've had, with deliciously crispy and flavorful rice mixed with tangy pork, ginger, peanuts, and herbs. Perhaps the best dish we had along with the Branzino.

 The crab fried rice was a family-friendly pleaser, as were the grilled pork cheeks. The dessert with sticky rice and jackfruit ice cream was a pleasant and taste bud-soothing end to the meal. 

We also loved the drinks, grateful for happy hour even on Xmas Eve - the punch with clarified milk and pandan was a needed balance to the acidity of the meal overall.

From the moment I encountered the host to the exit when Selena the manager bid me farewell, this was one of my most memorable culinary experiences in NYC.  Sweet atmosphere that made me feel like I was dining with family.  
Don't sleep on grabbing a seat at the bar.  Naan was an exceptional bartender and gave the most sincere recommendations that were on point.  Grilled cuttlefish with a sauce that will reinvent what spicy is and paired with the Prawn Karee, I wish I had more than one stomach.  Completed my meal with a Ferrand Chae Buay, the perfect cocktail to wrap up the experience.  
I was denied when I attempted to buy a small bowl to commemorate the dining experience but alas no one is perfect.  :)

Fish Cheeks has been on my list for a year and I finally got to try it out!

We visited Fish Cheeks for my cousin's birthday and it was such a great choice! From the service to the ambiance to the food - everything was amazing!

We started off with drinks and appetizers. The spicy mango margaritas were delicious but could have used a tad bit more spice. The corn salad was simple yet tasty and refreshing. And the chicken wings... I'm not sure how what they put in and on them but they are like crack (which I have never tried but I imagine it's like these wings lol). 

For our entrees, we always do family style so that we can try a number of options. We kicked it off with the 30 days Dry Aged Beef Kaprow and I didn't think any of the other choices could be anymore delicious. But then the Choo Chee Scallops arrived and I was blown away. Lastly, the Coconut Crab Curry came out and there were chunks of crab and hella flavor!

They only had one dessert which was an ice cream and we weren't really into the description so we went to Kith instead. 

Needless to say, we cannot wait to dine at Fish Cheeks again!

loved this spot! goes above and beyond the classic interpretation of thai cuisine. the duck curry dish was prepared perfectly, and i could eat the sauce like a soup! the lemongrass mussels were also delicious, got a side of rice to soak up all that good broth. definitely some of the best thai food in the city! servers were also super sweet and the summery ambiance was such a nice escape from the nyc winter chill.
I loved all the herbed salad, fish, cocktails, friendly staff, ambiance, and the happy hours, 12:00 -6:00 PM.  If you're a lover of spicy Thai sea food, it's worth a visit.

I've eaten here several times, and it's always delicious! My favorite appetizers are the somtum corn salad (super light and refreshing) and the crispy rice salad & pork (packed with flavor). My favorite entrees are the coconut crab curry (spicy!) and the steamed branzino. We order those every single time and they are soooo tasty. I've also tried the crab fried rice (very good) and the tofu pad prik khing (good) but we don't order those dishes as frequently. The only dish I've had a bad experience with is the mussels - we ordered them one time and they were rotten. The restaurant took care of it/ was apologetic though. Overall a great spot!

Worth a stop if you are visiting NYC and finding the best eats! 

I for one love spicy food and thai food. The fish was unforgettable, I loved all the herbs and the presentation. Crab curry had amazing flavor as well. It was worth the hype for me!

So so delicious. The crab fried rice and oysters came with a salty and sour cilantro sauce that went so well with everything. Obsessed with the crab fried rice with cilantro sauce -- thinking about it for days!!! The scallops were delicious too but too spicy for me so my dinner partner ate it all and loved it. The cocktails were delicious too!! The service was quick and the restaurant is large. Overall would recommend for dinner dates or larger groups!

My threshold for Thai places is high and this really surpassed my expectations. Came for New Years Day lunch.

Easy enough to get a reservation and got a lovely corner booth. The vibe of the place overall is super cute. Bright colors, fun staff shirts. The menu is overwhelming only because there were so many things I wanted.

Started with the cuttlefish. I honestly didn't remember the spice level indicated on the menu so I was shook when I tried the dipping sauce. The fish was so tender, a huge portion, and tasty. The dipping sauce packs a punch. So flavorful and a little numbing. Adding the cilantro on top of each bite really completes it. But the spice level is real.

For mains, grabbed the crab curry and the scallops. The former I was a bit worried about as I don't typically love coconut forward dishes. However, looking around it seems that everyone gets this dish and I get why. Lovely seasoning, tons of crab. It's labeled as four chili peppers but I really don't understand that- would at most give it 2 (maybe even 1?). But I don't think that's a bad thing and maybe the coconut just balanced it out very well. The scallop dish was a surprise. One for how many scallops you're given. Two for how tender they are. And three for just the overall taste. I wasn't sure what this specific curry paste would taste like and it was so so lovely. Both dishes came with jasmine rice but we were given the option of switching one to sticky rice, which we did, and I found this to be a lot more manageable for dipping into the sauces.

Also grabbed the pakboong fai dang side dish. I had never had this and wow was it spicy. Once I realized I thoroughly enjoyed it. Such rich combo of spice and the texture was not what I would have expected upon inspection.

The happy hour is essentially all day and is a great deal for drinks.

Service I felt like was mid until we accidentally dropped a glass and then I truly saw how attentive everyone in the restaurant could be. 

Overall such a great experience. It was ironically not our first choice but happened to be open for the holiday and now I'm so grateful it was!

One of my fave New York eateries! Literally everything is amazing, but for recommendations, I'd say to try the: crab curry, whole fried fish, whole steamed fish, shrimp and three crab sauce! As long as you like flavor, you won't be disappointed. Every bite is an experience.

Also, the staff is super friendly and the food comes fast. I seriously recommend any and everyone eat here.

This might actually be one of the best Thai places I've ever had in my life. Highly recommended by a friend of mine so I knew I had to come. Immediately when you walk in, you get a cozy ambiance with dim lighting and modern interior design. the atmosphere is casual and lively, with lots of groups enjoying their meals. Get a reservation if you can since there was a line when we arrived. 

We had a reservation at 8pm and got seated right away. Our server was extremely friendly and attentive, giving us suggestions on dishes and checking in periodically. The food was INCREDIBLE and I'm still reminiscing about it:

- complimentary shrimp chips: I had these chips growing up and it's been years since I've enjoyed one so this was the biggest surprise of the evening for me. Light and crispy, with fun shapes and colors. brought me back to my childhood and a very good starter.
- somtum corn salad: chill and refreshing appetizer to start off your meal -- you can really taste the sweetness of the corn and I liked the crunchiness of the beans. The lime added a layer of sourness while the chili provided a spice kick.
- pakboong fai dang: tender, well cooked and subtle flavors but there's spice from the red chili oil that enhanced the taste
- steamed fish with thai herbs: this was SO GOOD. I couldn't believe how tender  the fish was -- it literally melts in your mouth. The soup is sour and spicy which is a great contrast to the fish. 

Great portion sizes and prices were reasonable for this type of restaurant. If you're looking for a comforting meal in NoHo, would highly recommend Fish Cheeks!

The fried fish is a must-try, crispy on the outside, tender on the inside and full of flavor. The menu comprises of many shareable dishes with variety of texture and taste that complement each other beautifully.

Fish Cheeks is one of my favorite spots in the city, and every visit feels like a celebration of bold, authentic flavors. The whole steamed fish with herbs is the highlight for me--it's perfectly cooked, tender, and deboned with care. The flavors are vibrant yet comforting, reminding me of my mother's cooking in the best way. It's a dish that feels both nostalgic and elevated.

The pork cheeks here are another standout--rich, flavorful, and melt-in-your-mouth tender. They're a must-try for anyone who loves a hearty and satisfying dish.

I've also visited during happy hour, and the cocktails are as thoughtfully crafted as the food. They're refreshing, inventive, and pair beautifully with the small plates offered.

The ambiance is lively and welcoming, perfect for everything from date nights to catching up with friends. Fish Cheeks has become a go-to for me when I'm craving exceptional Thai food with a touch of home and creativity. Highly recommend!

Super delicious Thai food! I tried the following items: 1) green curry, 2) crab fried rice, 3) pakboong fai dang (morning glory vegetable w/ chili, garlic + soybean).

I loved the crab fried rice & pakboong fai dang (morning glory vegs) - superb! It was so flavorful. I would reorder these items next time.

The green curry (vegan) was very interesting. The green curry sauce was delicious + had a nice spice kick to it. There were so many farmers market vegetables in it - some were a bit hard to chew but it was definitely very crunchy. 

Friendly staff + nice decor.

My friend and I both graduated from NYU together in the field of Social Work and decided to meet up as a congratulations lunch and I was going to meet with her to help her study for the ASWB exam. She chose the restaurant Fish Cheeks and I was really excited to try it. 

When I got to the restaurant, I wasn't aware that we needed to make a reservation in order to get a table. Luckily a table was open for two people and we were able to be seated despite how busy it was. 

I ordered the green curry which was vegan and included Thai basil, red finger chili, roasted seasonal vegetables, and served with rice. My friend ordered the coconut crab curry which has three chili peppers next to it on the menu and includes southern-style curry with crab meat, house-made curry paste, betel leaf, makrut lime leaf, and also served with rice. 

The food was delicious and the atmosphere was casual, but also classy. Our food came out relatively quickly and the person who was serving us was very informative and answered all of our questions. I really enjoyed my time at Fish Cheeks and it's the perfect place to eat amazing food and catch up with a friend.

Food: Fish Cheeks is a hidden gem that consistently delivers delicious and flavorful dishes. The steamed fish with Thai herbs is a standout, a must-try for every visit. The zabb wings are another crowd-pleaser, offering a perfect balance of spice and flavor.

Cost: The pricing is reasonable, especially considering the quality and flavor of the food.

Environment: While the ambiance is simple and unassuming, it creates a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The restaurant can accommodate large parties, making it a great choice for group dining.

Service: The service is excellent, with friendly and attentive staff. They are knowledgeable about the menu and are always happy to make recommendations.

Uniqueness: Fish Cheeks offers a unique dining experience, combining classic Thai flavors with innovative dishes. The focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients sets it apart from other Thai restaurants.

If you like shots I highly recommend the Ya Dong Party shots. The street liquor is interesting but my favorite part is the pandan ice tea chaser that comes with the shot. They were so much fun. You can also get the pandan ice tea on its own as well. 

We came here with a group of four and ordered many dishes to try. 

- Zabb Wings 
- Somtum Corn Salad 
- Grilled Cuttlefish 
- Rawaaeng duck curry 
- Crab Aob Woonseng
- Steamed fish with Thai herbs 
- Pork dish (can't remember if it was the pork belly or pork cheeks) 

While all the dishes were delicious, none of them actually stood out as much for me. Maybe it's because I had such high expectations because of the great reviews and recommendations from friends. My favorite dish was the crab aob woonseng because I liked the subtle umami flavor of the glass noodles in the steel pot. It's also the dish that tastes a bit different from the others. A lot of the dishes were served with similar spicy sauce (which I'm not a big fan of) as well as this acidic lime-y flavor. I felt the flavor profile from the overall dishes felt flat and similar. The duck curry was underwhelming, definitely not the best I've had. For the price, I was definitely disappointed by the taste and quality of the food. 

Overall we still had a great time here with great ambiance! If you want to give this place a try definitely make reservations beforehand.

We had the absolute pleasure of dining at Fish Cheeks, and I can't recommend it enough! From the moment we walked in, we were greeted by the warm, welcoming atmosphere and friendly staff. The vibe is vibrant and cozy, with just the right balance of energy and comfort.

The service was great --attentive, knowledgeable, and with just the right amount of charm. Our server made fantastic recommendations, and we felt truly taken care of throughout our meal.

Every dish was a perfect balance of bold flavors and fresh ingredients. From the aromatics to the perfectly cooked fish, everything was bursting with flavor and we could taste the care that went into every bite.

Fish Cheeks truly nails it with both authenticity and innovation. Whether you're a fan of traditional Thai flavors or looking to try something new, this spot does not disappoint. Highly recommend--it's a must-visit!

I've gotten take out and eaten in the restaurant as well. Both are great but it's a bit hectic to get a table here so if you don't want to deal with the commotion, make a reservation ahead of time or order to-go. The space inside is huge so they can accommodate a lot of people. 

Food is delicious here. A lot of bold flavors and variety of textures. Their steamed branzino in cilantro lime broth is excellent. I'd order it over and over again. Also! Crispy rice salad yum! 

I love their non alcoholic options for drinks too!  Pandan lemongrass iced tea is beyond! I ordered two because I loved it so much.

Food was good but used to be better. 
I liked the rice and ice cream dessert. 
Please fix the product and work on consistency.

My friends and I came during Restaurant Week but didn't end up doing the pre set courses, although the menu looked terrific. Their drink menu is so fun and unique (and they offer some mocktails too!). I ordered the coconut crab curry and *chefs kiss*! It's so tasty! Everyone in our party loved their food. Finished off our meal with the ice cream bo lan, also delicious! Grab a reservation stat!

Went for oyster happy hour and it was good. $22 for a dozen with some green acidic sauce, fried shallots, and lemons. The green sauce was great and satisfied that oyster craving
No horseradish available though, bummer 
Drink was good-- $13 for HH!
Everything was good
Went here for a friend's birthday and basically ordered the entire menu. Everything was very tasty and had a perfect balance of salty, sweet, spicy, and sour flavors. The drinks were great too!

Food was great, and portions for mains were perfect to share. I really enjoyed the corn salad and the crab fried rice. The full fish was OK for me, and the spicy curry wasn't actually as spicy as I thought it would be. I would eat here again.

Fish Cheeks is one of those places I always recommend to my friends if they're craving Thai food. It's always a hustling and bustling spot, and the food hits every single time. For those that are spice lovers, Fish Cheeks is for you, they don't mess around! If your spice tolerance isn't good, BE WARNED!! 

My partner and I arrived at 7PM on a Monday. No matter what day it is, I highly recommend making a reservation! We were pretty hungry so we thought we ordered a lot, but we ended up finishing everything. 

The duck curry wasn't bad, but the portions were a bit on the smaller side, so I probably wouldn't get this again. 

The steamed fish is one of my favorites. If you're not a fan of sour things, this probably isn't for you. It's very lime heavy, but I LOVE it. 

The sautéed cabbage was so yummy and had the perfect amount of smokiness and char, but also a bit expensive for the small portion of cabbage. The crab fried rice is also a staple! Lots of crab chunks and a good dish to share. 

Fish Cheeks overall is a great spot for a family style dinner. It's not your typical Thai spot, and it's a go to of mine. Cant wait to come back!

Visited for its hype and online fame. Nice environmenr and service. However in the current restaurant scene in nyc where Thai restaurants are pulling out all their top-notch recipes for the heated competition, fish cheeks felt quite underwhelming for its price point. The signature steamed fish was seasoned quite blandly and the crab curry felt over priced for its portion and taste.

We were lucky there was no wait & we were immediately seated (came here yesterday (sunday) ~3pm. Cute decor & comfortable seating. Staff + service was excellent.

We ordered to share: 1) green curry, 2) crab fried rice, 3) pakboong fai dang (morning glory vegetable w/ chili, garlic + soybean).

Green curry (vegan) which comes w/ a small side of rice - the green curry base was very delicious and smooth + had the right spice. This item to us was spicy enough - I had runny nose afterwards LOL. There was many different seasonal farmers market vegetables in this dish (cauliflower, thai eggplant, carrot, bell peppers, etc). We have never tried vegan green curry but it was an experience.

Crab fried rice - WOW! I highly highly recommend this dish. The dish does not look special but when you eat it, it was orgasmic! So much flavors in this dish + the 2 sauces was amazing! I would reorder this next time!

Pakboong fai dang (morning glory vegetable w/ chili, garlic, soybean) - This dish was also super amazing + flavorful! Super delicious! I would reorder this next time as well!

Excellent Thai food! We will be back to try their other foods next time!

My friend and I came here for dinner because of their gluten free menu, but more importantly we want to try this restaurant. We were greeted with complimentary gluten free shrimp chips with a spicy chili jam. These were addicting. We started off with the tongue cheek mocktail and cocktail versions. Both were tasty and paired well with the following dishes: 

Special Tom Yum Soup - this was off the menu special item of that day. The spicy sour soup was comforting and filled with a variety of shellfish: Squid, shrimp, Mussels and fish. Too bad this is not a regular item on their menu. 

Crab Fried Rice - this dish is solid definitely worth ordering as quality and quantity is on par with Manhattan prices. I even took some leftovers home which my parents ended up consuming. 

Steamed Fish with Thai herbs - this dish is served hot; the branzino is filleted as it fell off the bone. The cilantro lime broth was very good even comparable to the ones I've had in other Thai restaurants in Queens. We devoured everything except the head and brought that home for the Asian parents to consume. 

Service was great. Our server was knowledgeable. The dishes are served family style so solo dining is not ideal. Ambiance was smaller than I thought, there is a small instep to get to the bathroom. However, great place worth trying especially for restaurant week or even a small group lunch or dinner.
Been here twice food is great drinks are good had the steamed fish and the crab rice, fried chicken everything was so good.

This place has been raved about from my friends and it lived up to the hype! I loved getting to try authentic dishes outside of pad Thai, pad see ew, etc. 

Our favorite items: 
- Coconut Crab Curry 
- Zabb Chicken Wings 
- Steamed Fish 

Everything is full of flavor, umami spices, and herbs. Service was pretty fast. The ambiance is dark and candle lit (like most NYC restaurants). Price is a little steep but I thought it was worth trying out at least once! I recommend making a reservation or coming on a weekday during non-peak hours.

I love this restaurant. There isn't a single bad thing on the menu and I've had about 75% of the dishes. I've been going since 2018 and I've never had a single complaint. I went last night and the pork belly kaprow dish has changed. I noticed this earlier in the year but I was hoping it was just a fluke. Is it still juicy, perfectly cooked, and delicious? Yes but now it's served dry with a chili garlic sauce on the side instead of in a crispy, caramelized holy basil sauce. I'm heartbroken. I brought my sister, my niece, my now fiancée, and a friend to this restaurant and it's our favorite. Please please bring it back. I'm begging

Walked in on a Tues evening and got seated right away outdoors with heating. Cozy enough for a small group! Would still recommend getting a reservation early if possible when weather gets cold. 

We keep coming back here for the Zabb wings, our absolute favorite. Service was attentive throughout our dinner. We love Fish Cheeks .

Apps were delicious but the entrees did not meet my expectations. 

Shrimp and corn salad were super yum. 

Had the coconut curry and the tomyum special. The curry was good but underwhelming. The tomyum was very good actually. 

Drinks were yum, meal came with complimentary shrimp chips. 

Place definitely had great ambiance, cute date spot. Service was friendly and attentive as well, being we sat at the bar. 

Definitely glad I tried it out. Not sure if i would return simply because there is better thai options elsewhere.

Yum! I'm skeptical of fancy Thai spots but Fish Cheeks definitely lives up to the rave reviews. We tried the chicken wings, duck, and scallops and I'll be dreaming of eating this meal again in the future. 10/10 so good!

One of the best Thai posts in the city by far!! Service was very friendly and attentive. Ambiance is very lively and fun, even at opening 5pm!

They had no available Resys on the site for 6 but we emailed and were able to get a table on a weekend at 5pm! Luckily they also have Happy Hour -- none of their drinks were misses for us, we even ordered a second round! "Punch Drunk Love" and "No Pad Thai Zone" were my top picks!

The food feels very authentic and flavors all pack a punch! Some of our favorites were the grilled pork cheeks, duck curry, and tom yum soup!
Raymond was super friendly and the food was amazing! Music really set the mood and the best oysters!

Everything was great and the ambiance was vibrant! I can handle spice but when they put a chili next to it on the menu they mean it! A lot of times when places say it's spicy I don't tend to think so but this place lives up to that! 

Happy hour from 12-6 everyday is awesome! Including cocktails/beer/ and oysters. Both of our drinks were good. 

The Zabb wings were ADDICTING. The seasoning was sour sweet and spicy and cooked wonderfully. The crispy rice salad is just like nahm khao just spicier. Coconut crab curry was really spicy but really coconuty and creamy and was excellent!

Ambiance of this place is nailed down!

It can be hard to get a reservation, but definitely worth it. We were seated within five minutes of getting there. The space is clean but a little crowded due to the amount of people. We ordered the oysters, wings, coconut crab curry and the crab fried rice. All of the food was delicious but the wings were surprisingly our favorite. We would love to come back to try the fish!

It's not bad. But it left much to desire. We just went to Bangkok Supper Club a few days ago, then this. Their food is just alright. The woosen was just okay. The steamed fish was just mediocre. The best is probably the curry crab, but the neighborhood Thai joint does it better. Overall, not the best Thai place in nyc. Not worth the hype around this place

The best grilled fish I have ever had in my life, hands down. Do not walk, run to get the grilled mackerel. 

Amazing vibe, excellent drinks, friendly staff (shoutout Sasi). Also had the Coconut Crab Curry and pork cheeks, both amazing impeccable flavoring. I haven't been this impressed in awhile.

This place is overly salty and seems to be a common theme amongst negative reviews. The zaab wings and scallops were both too salty and lacked balance unlike other thai restaurants. 

Don't get me wrong, I'm not a health freak but this was extremely salty today. I had two bowls of rice

Maybe I ordered the wrong thing, but I was pretty disappointed in my dish. I ordered the tofu dish and it was spicy yet lacking of any other flavor. Service was good and I was seated quickly without a reservation but the one thing I ordered failed to deliver. I don't eat meat and I only saw one other thing on the menu I could eat otherwise so I probably won't be back.

Wow, truly a fantastic restaurant. I heard so much hype about this place before trying it and all my expectations and hopes were met. Plainly, the food is delicious and the flavors feel faithful to the spirit of Southeastern Asian cuisine while putting a very unique spin on things. To call it "fusion" doesn't give it the respect it deserves. Truly great.

I selected this restaurant from several Thai options in the area due to its high ratings. Unfortunately, after dining there last night, several of us fell ill. Some experienced nausea, while others dealt with diarrhea. We're unsure if it was the crab dish, which had a very fishy smell, or perhaps the chicken or the vegetable soup. Regardless, the experience was completely unacceptable. If they are not upholding proper food safety standards, it's concerning that patrons might risk food poisoning, especially on a Saturday night. I'm not sure what the health department's role is in this, but I will certainly not be returning to this establishment. I am incredibly disappointed.

Hands down best Thai food I've ever had. The coconut crab curry is 10/10. Customer service is amazing, I can't remember the hostess name, but she is a sweetheart. Always a vibe inside, we sat at the bar the most recent time and it was great. 
I've been several times and they never miss a beat.
Honorable mention as another fav is the fried pork belly. Also get the spicy mango drink -- 10/10. 
Can't wait to come back!

Been wanting to come here for a while but could never snag a reservation at a decent time. Finally just tried walking in and luckily got a table! 
I see why everyone raves about this place. Everything is consistently good with a bit of a flair. From the food to the service to the decor. Service isn't uppity which is great. It's a fun time.

Ok this is a top-tier Thai restaurant right here-- it's either my favorite or in my top 2 favorite Thai restaurants in manhattan.

We ordered 3 dishes to share between the two of us. We were extremely full, but we will definitely re-order these same 3 dishes when we come back.

- Steamed fish: 100/10 (simply fantastic. Loved the use of the Thai spices and the fish was cooked to perfection.)
- Crab curry: 100/10 (amazing crab curry. They definitely didn't skimp out on the crab meat and the curry was perfectly sweet and spicy.)
- Crab fried rice: 10/10 (fantastic fried rice to have with the curry.)

Service was good and the ambiance was very casual.

Fish Cheeks was highly recommended by both family and friends, and I finally got to visit!

The restaurant has both outdoor and indoor seating. It's pretty dark and loud once inside but def part of the overall ambiance. Our server's friendly and checked in on us often.

Corn salad had a kick but was still sweet, light, and refreshing. Crab Woosen was one of the few non-spicy options and it didn't disappoint in terms of flavors. Crab meat had some shells and cartilage that I had to pick out from my mouth though. Ice cream Bo Lan was the highlight! The jackfruit pandan ice cream was absolutely delicious and it went so well with the sticky rice and evaporated milk. I would totally just come for drinks and dessert.

Sadly, I had to dock off 1 star since customization to less spicy/non-spicy was not available. I really cannot handle spice so I wasn't able to try a lot of the dishes.

Pretty dang good! As a Thai - having these delicious street foods turned upscale in a comfortable setting in NY is like a dream. 

Here are the dishes we had & I recommend trying all of them:

Somtum Corn salad - fresh corn in a papaya salad dressing, I still like the 'papaya salad' much better but this is a refreshing new take on it with interesting textures and flavors.

Crispy rice salad & pork - the most delicious dish we ordered last night. Sour fermented pork, lightly spicy, crunchy peanuts, cabbage leaves to wrap it with..all the Thai spices + the umami-punch was amazing! Highly recommend.

Muscles with lemongrass - good and tender, nice flavors. 

Zabb wings - flavorful!

"30-day dry aged beef krapow"
This is an interesting take on this staple Thai dish.  The rich smoky flavors with depts of the dry-aged process elevated this dish to another level. Also it was cooked in high heat, probably with red flames overtaking the wok, it had an open flame flavor which added another layer of fiery taste to it. It also came with a crispy fried eggs with runny yolk which is the way it's commonly served in Thailand + a side and "prik-nam-pla" (chili fish sauce) and we drizzled that all over this dish with rice...the result was awesome deliciousness!

Tippy top tier. Absolutely no notes. Quick service and extraordinary food. I love the cilantro sauce they paired with the oysters and mussels. Crab aob woosen was so flavorful with big lump crab meat pieces. 

The crab fried rice was buttery and wonderful. I'd eat here every day if I could lol.

Thanks for the food, and I will definitely be back!

Worth the hype! LOVED the crab fried rice and enjoyed the chicken wings as well. My mocktail was perfection and we had great service from the host stand onto Mark, our waiter, who was so lovely. 

Excellent wheelchair accessible outdoor seating area (though you do have to roll on cobblestones to get to some tables). There are no steps to get inside, I didn't check out the bathroom.

Crab Fried Rice was so good and the two sauces it came with really enhanced its flavor. The cocktails were decent, probably would only buy them again during happy hour. Definitely will be back to try more dishes!

Fish cheeks is a solid Thai place, and pretty busy but spacious inside. To start off, they gave us some shrimp chips and a dipping sauce that seemed to also taste like fish and was really good. We got the Tom Yum special, which was delicious and full of seafood, though not the best Tom Yum I've had. We also got a corn salad, which was light and refreshing, along with chicken wings and crispy pork belly that were both well seasoned. We also got some drinks, including the tongue in cheek and punch drunk love. The tongue in cheek was very good and fruity without being too sweet, but the punch drunk love tasted more like coconut than pandan, which isn't my preference. I'd be interested in going again to try their coconut crab curry!

Great service, the waitress was very kind :)
The food is impressively tasty and creative. One of my favorites from the meal was the whole steamed fish -- it was covered in garnishes and smelled out of this world. The ambiance of Fish Cheeks is also very cozy!

We had a reservation for two at noon. They seated us and by then multiple people had already been waiting before it opened. By 12:30 the restaurant was fully packed. The seating is pretty close to each other. I could smell the woman next to me and her perfume very distinctly. We ordered Thai tea with coconut milk (I'm lactose intolerant) which was sweet and yummy. 4/5 solid.
We also got the coconut crab curry and the steamed fish with extra rice. The coconut crab curry to me was not worth $30. It was smaller and underwhelming taste wise. It has three peppers to signify its spice level and the first bite felt very spicy but after that it starts dulling bite after bite. I felt the curry did not do justice to the could've beens. It could've been richer, creamier... there was just something not there to make it feel worthwhile for the cost. Still yummy.

The steamed fish though was a different story. Tender, juicy, and the lime broth it came in brought the whole dish together. It was something you can't get anywhere else and the whole dish had a limey kick, with a balance to so many flavors- citrusy, sweet, tangy, salty and they debone the fish for the main inside skeleton. The fish was truly a delight.

After eating the fish, I can understand how this restaurant is so popular. The inside was nice where you can see the bar area and seating is inside and on the patio. It has great vibes and loved the little details like the fish lamps over the bar/ counter.

Our server was prompt and attentive. We felt the service was great!
kind of an overhyped thai restaurant and the prices are on a pricier side. the food was not bad but given the portions, might not return. decent service.
Fish cheeks is always a good idea. Zaab wings and full branzino for the win! Cocktails are good too!

Where do I begin?
The restaurant manager who updated the reservation when the online system refused to the consistent check-in and birthday surprise.
I love an experience and I aim to cultivate unforgettable ones.
The libations and cuisine were superb.
Punch Drunk Love wet my palette and left me feeling right. The cuttle fish, mussels and crab fried rice hit the spot. Great company and engaging staff created am engaging atmosphere.

This place has been on my list for so long. I was excited to get a last minute resy for dinner. The vibes of this place are solid except for the tables being super close to each other. 

The crab fried rice was very yummy and would highly recommend. It was better with the vinegar sauce on the side (sadly they charge extra ~$2 if you want more of this). 

The crab curry was terrible. I think we got a bad batch as all of my friends who have been here before have loved it. My friend and I have a high spice tolerance, but this curry was practically numbing. We had a few bites and stopped because we couldn't taste any flavor, just a numbing spice. This was a huge waste of $30.

Service was okay, but not great. We mentioned the curry being way too spicy and the server said it might just be an off day

A New York Classic for good Thai seafood! The fish is what they're known for, and for good reason. It's delicious. 

The shrimp app was decent but the wings app were  surprisingly really good. The branzino whole fish was the best! And I liked the fried rice a lot with crab. The Thai tea was good too.

The reason it's not getting 5 stars: The curry crab was not my favorite I think the flavor just wasn't for me. The cuttle fish also wasn't the best in my opinion but the spice level was perfect, it had a good kick with the sauce. I felt there could be stronger flavor profiles.

The service was great though and the atmosphere is nice 

Came here for lunch on a weekday and it was a great spot for sharing plates and trying everything. It fills up for dinner so def get a res but lunch time is normally open for walk ins.

Snagged a table for 3 on a Friday night as a walk-in. Waited only 30 minutes and enjoyed spacious outdoor seating. Service was kind and food was fantastic--we loved the Shrimp appetizer , though the mussels and chicken wings were also great (the wings are dry rub). For mains we split the crab curry and scallop dish. The crab curry was good, but the scallops were the star of the entire meal! So buttery and spicy and perfect umami flavor--also decent portion of scallops for the price. Can't wait to return and try more of their menu!

Celebrated my birthday here in 2023 and it was a knockout meal. The steamed fish might not sound interesting, but it was perfectly cooked in a heady herbaceous broth with tons of lime and we could not stop slurping it up! The corn salad is also wonderful, and the shellfish, too. We had a platter of steamed mussels in a deeply satisfying sauce. Not too many options for vegetarians but otherwise perfect.

The food was incredible, very good spot, didn't have a reservation but they still sat us at the bar, my phone was going to die one of the servers charged it for me amazing service and really incredible food

Lunch reservations were all booked and this was midweek. We stopped in and did snag a table for two. 

A hot reservation for this place. 
 Our waiter, I found, was from Thailand. 

My wife ordered the crab, and it was one on the menu without a pepper designation. My crispy duck had just the right amount of spice for me and came with a delicious curry sauce. I ate every last bit of rice, as it sopped up the  delicious sauce.  I wish there was more of it. 

Charming digs. One reviewer mentioned there was but a single unisex restroom but we heard there is another on the other side of the restaurant.
Cobble stone street in the middle of quiet NoHo neighborhood. On a spontaneous afternoon found this little gem. My green curry was well balanced. Worth coming back to try other menu items.

Amaaaaazing experience at Fish Cheeks. Went for the first time with a few friends and we were blown away by everything we ordered. We ordered a few appetizers and four entrees (if my memory serves me correctly) and that was enough to feed a table of five. Some favorites included the chicken wings, scallop entrée, crab fried rice, crab curry, fried fish... am I listing everything we ate? I was also very happy to see mocktails on the menu and ordered a tasty one, and everyone was happy with their cocktails as well. Our server was very helpful and friendly.
Incredibly flavorful menu, buzzy, upbeat ambience and good cocktails. Highly recommend Crispy Rice Salad and Pork but all dishes were tasty.

This Thai restaurant was primarily focused on Thai style seafood dishes. The oyster was very fresh and the seasoning was Thai style. The clams were very good but a bit salty. The fish was very tender and well cooked. The coconut curry had a really nice spice to it. We sat outside and the weather was perfect. I'd give this place a 4/5 because I personally like my Thai food with chicken, beef, or shrimp and I didn't see any of those options. 

Definitely a place everyone should try once in their life. We're from out of state and I wouldn't say we'd go back but if I lived in nyc it would be a great option for lunch or dinner. 

Service and ambiance was great!

Make a reservation before you go!!!

Went for a late lunch yesterday with one of my besties after an appointment in East Village. We were craving for either Japanese or Thai and when we couldn't find the other ramen spot, I remembered this Thai resto. Didn't have a reservation but I guess they keep a few spots open for walkin or for Resy Global Dining Access members. Sat and ordered our Thai iced teas first and foremost. Then decided we'd get crab fried rice and isan style grilled chicken. Food came out pretty quick and service was good. Both really delicious! I do recall enjoying their crab fried rice before but the isab style grilled chicken is unexpectedly so good, never tried this before. Portion esp. for the crab rice could be better compared to most Thai restaurants offering this. Other than that, a satisfying quick lunch! Rest room is clean which is always important.

Had a take out order of the Coconut Crab curry and Cabbage sautéed. At first glance, the food portion looks small but I can guarantee you. You are not going to find better Crab curry in NY than this place. The spiciness level is just right personally I'd called it mild but it's really great sautéed cabbage is amazing and a must order. 10/10

I cannot get over this place. The wings were amazing. The dry rub is like zesty but sweet but also has a hint of spice. The pork belly is a little bit on the spicier side for the sauce but overall very good and it comes with the rice, we also ordered the oysters which were amazing and I had a twist with chimichurri sauce instead of your normal cocktail sauce, which we loved. The service was very great. Our server was very friendly and informed us everything we needed to know as first comers. We were there on a weekday during happy hour where drinks were discounted and oysters were also discounted. Overall 10/10 experience we would totally come back! Just get ready for some spice!

Everything we had was so good! For appetizer, the corn salad was refreshing, the pork cheeks was done well, and we wished there were more mussels but very tasty and would get again. We tried the whole brazino fish which was very soft and fresh, but with the flame underneath it can get a bit overcooked if left out for a bit so don't let it linger. The duck curry was so flavorful and honestly plenty spicy for us - idk how we could have withstood the crab curry but we passed on that. The crab woosen was our surprise favorite and not one we've seen talked about. Ended it with a pandan ice cream sticky rice dessert, which tasted mostly of vanilla ice cream as the pandemic flavor didn't come through. Overall, every dish was great, but be prepared for smaller portions. It was a busy Tuesday night dinner slot during restaurant week, but had no issues with getting our reservation.

We came in with a reservation and were seated quickly, the restaurant was packed inside and on the patio. 

The menu doesn't display the classics but I loved their take of a more seafood forward menu. We ordered the mussels, oysters, whole fish, and crispy rice. I enjoyed all the dishes, they were umami, salty, spicy; all spot on. 

The highlights were the crispy rice and whole fish! The different textures in the crispy rice were so good and it was extra limey which I loved. The whole fish melted in your mouth and the sauce it was cooked in complemented it well. 

Service was a little spotty but overall was a pleasant experience!

5/5 for service - Starting with the good. For a table of 6 without a reservation for a Saturday at 1PM, the wait was only 20 minutes. They said we could have the table until 3PM because another table was coming then but it didn't feel rushed and the food came promptly. We actually stayed past 3PM. Our server, Gabe, was also very sociable and attentive. 

3/5 for food - Being this was my second time coming to Fish Cheeks, I can't help but compare to the first time. The food was incredible and so memorable pre-Covid. This time was lacking in favor in a way that seemed like the dishes became more "Americanized" and strayed far away from the authentic taste. Every dish had chili peppers next to them indicating the spicy level. We got the Coconut Crab Curry which was 3 chili peppers and supposed to be really spicy but it was just slightly spicy. Some of the dishes also came room temperate and not warm enough. For a table of 6, we ordered the following dishes:

2/5 for Oysters - Given it was happy hour, we ordered a dozen oysters for $22. The oysters were small and not fresh.

4/5 for Zabb Wings - The skin was spicy and sour because of the kaffir lime leaves, and the meat was juicy. It was $18 for 4 wings which is pricey for chicken wings.

2/5 for Grilled Pork Cheeks - This tasted like lean pork belly and was just mediocre.

5/5 for Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs - The branzino was fresh, deboned and tender.

2/5 for Crab Fried Rice - Nothing special but the green sauce was very good.

2/5 for Coconut Crab Curry - I had high expectations for this dish but the crab didn't taste like anything and the curry was lacking in flavor. It was missing more of the coconut taste and most likely fish sauce.

5/5 for Crab Aob Woonsen - This was my favorite dish. It looked underwhelming but the noodles were delicious and full of flavor.

second visit to try out other dishes. The zabb wings were very tasty with the dry rub, but a little on the saltier side. The mussels were ok with the lemongrass dipping sauce. 

The entrees were not as good the first time. The duck was tender but not fatty. The curry wasn't as flavorful. The crab woonsen was decent at best, although there were plenty of crab meat. The veggie dish was good. 

We definitely miss the fish dish that we tried the first time. Saw a lot of people order it on other tables so I'm sure it still remains a popular dish.

A MUST GO !! There are only 3 vegetarian options here, which is something I would tell them to change and add more !! But I had the red curry and veg fried rice and it was amazing !!! Omg, like mouth watering

I heard incredible things about this spot so I had to come try it out myself. My friend and I ordered the coconut crab curry, crab fried rice, and the crispy pork salad. My favorite was a crispy pork salad. They provided lettuce wraps and you could place the crispy pork filling and create rolls. The coconut crab curry was their specialty but personally, I thought it was too spicy. The crab fried rice was also really good featuring pretty large portions of crab. I usually consider myself pretty good with spice but honestly, this place was QUITE spicy. However, the portions were large and yummy. The service was also really good.

Have tried several times to get a reservation at Fish Cheeks and was finally able to wait list and get one on Resy yesterday.

Was the wait worth it? Still deciding!!!I've had better Thai food else where in less popular restaurants but the food was  good.

Tried the chickens wings and they were delicious, but four pieces for $18 bucks is a bit ridiculous. 

Tried the fried fish with herbs, which had no salt so it was pretty bland. Overhyped.

Tried the crab curry, which was delicious but laden with heavy cream and not coconut milk.

Space and ambience was fine.

Service and staff were snotty and uninviting....Last I check, this is not the French Laundry!

The wings here are absolutely bomb! I wish the dry rub could be sold separately to sprinkle. Aside from the wings, the drinks and the other food- duck curry and fried rice- were very flavorful and complex in flavor. The savory martini is a definitely a stand out, I have never had a drink like that before. That drink was like consuming a flavorful soup- imagine getting buzzed off of a soup! The service was attentive, and efficient. I truly cannot wait to visit again.

Came here for a birthday celebration 
Very accommodating and very friendly staff
The food here was good
I think it's my favorite crab fried rice and the green curry wow 
It gives American brunch vibes but really good Thai food ~ once you reconcile with it, it's a really solid spot

I've been meaning to try this spot for a while now and I'm glad that the food lived up to the hype! The steamed fish was delicious, as was the crab curry. Definitely recommend ordering an extra bowl of rice to mop up the sauce. 

However, the service was a bit of a let down. Despite making reservations in advance, the waitress had a lot of trouble seating us... We were ushered in and out of the restaurant a couple times before just left to sit by the bar/bathroom til something opened up, which was a bit disappointing.

My two friends and I stopped by for Happy Hour on Aug 31. There is strangely no sign on the outside and I had to ask the hostess if this was indeed the place. It was only 4:30pm and unfortunately the place was so packed, we were forced to sit outside. (There should at least be space, like the bar, where patrons can sit and have a drink, while waiting for the rest of their party party to arrive.)
The outside gentleman server was very hard to understand, as his accent was so thick. Then Fish Cheeks couldn't accommodate different variations of the Happy Hour drinks, which left two friends without options. The Happy Hour oysters weren't all that great and were very small. All in all, not a great experience.

For Manhattan, this was delicious and perfectly seasoned. But if I'm honest, it was salty and I was constantly reaching for water. We only ordered the fish but the total was ~50$ including tip and tax. if you take the train a few stops into Brooklyn, you can find these dishes but with larger portions and cheaper. I would go again if  a friend wanted to try something in Manhattan. But this would not be my first choice.

I've been here twice and I can't get enough. Everything is truly so delicious. The whole fish is incredible and loved the salad as well. I think the sauces they offer are super addicting.

I'm sure I'll be back many more times

Today I was sitting at the bar, enjoying my drink and meal (which was wonderful) and was made to feel very uncomfortable by someone behind the bar. There was a staff member in all black with glasses on who was staring at me and making comments to the bartender about me. This is very unprofessional and makes me not want to come back despite how good the service and food was.

As far as ambience goes, this is one of the best restaurants I have been in. It feels very intimate, and the lighting and decoration was excellent. For the food, I was not blown away. The Tongue-in-Cheek cocktail with lychee, hibiscus, and lime was very good, and I appreciated all the flavors. The Zabb wings were OK - somewhat dry, but the rub was good. The crab fried rice was similarly just OK, with some pieces of crab interspersed in the dish. Overall, a good meal, but nothing extraordinary. 3.5/5

This meal was among the best I've had in NYC. We got the corn salad, wings, steamed fish, and duck curry. It was soooo fire. The steamed fish changed my life - it was so fresh and bright and wonderful. Thank you fish cheeks we'll be back soon

Fish Cheeks is one of my favorite thai food places in NYC. Highly recommend the steamed fish. It is boneless and the thai herbs and lemon grass sauce make it addictive! The shrimp in 3 crab sauce is also great and would recommend. Service is great and would recommend making reservations as it can get busy and popular. There's seating both inside and outside.

Solid spot in NY. 

Coming for the HH is good too. They raised the price a smidge from when I last visited but green sauce that accompanied the oysters was good. 

I thought the steamed fish was so soft and I liked the chili sauce as well. 

The curry was very smooth in texture but my greedy self maybe thought there'd be a bit more crab within?

Crab glass noodle I expected to be a bit more flavor but I do love the texture of the glass noodles! 

Our cocktails were good too but I've been hearing about this savory cocktail (I think that Nam Gin Martini) that tastes like pho?! Please don't take it off the menu until I come back to NY to try!

My friends and I loved our experience at Fish Cheeks; everything tasted superb, with the favorites being the beef krapow and the crab curry. The wings were also a hit at the table! 

All the dishes have a baseline level of spiciness, so be prepared. Yet, the flavors and textures melded together so well that one wouldn't mind the spices. The happy hour is great as well, with discounted cocktails and oysters.

The only weak part of the dinner was the dessert, specifically the shaved ice, which just tasted icey without too much flavor or interesting textures. Overall a strong recommend and will be back!

It was recommended by someone we knew so we got excited to go there. But the dishes were not that good. Maybe it was at late lunch time so the servers were kept on pulling chairs and re arranged tables which was very noisy.
Service was excellent.. try the tongue and cheek cocktail . Food is definitely good. Glad to try.

The amount of times i've been recommended this place... I HAD to stop by on my trip to NY. I went with a rather large group so we were unfortunately split into two tables. My group of 5 split about 4 dishes - 1 appetizer and 3 entrees. 

Everything was delicious and this place deserves all the hype! We all shared:
Market Oysters 9/10, came with a side of mixed fish sauce that worked incredible with the oysters
Steamed fish 11/10... they weren't messing around with this. This reminded me of my childhood where we would have steamed fish with fish sauce and rice. This was that but MORE. Spicy, tangy, umami... yum yum yum! 
Crab Curry 8/10, this was good and I loved the meatiness of the crab. A solid pick if you're looking for something creamy and meaty
Crispy Pork Belly 7/10, I loved all the fried garlic on top but was just really crispy pork belly. 

Delicious food, nice people, and really cute vibes! Definitely a favorite in the city
The food and service are excellent! The spice level is actually Thai level spice. One of the best Thai experiences I've ever had.

Came here on a Saturday afternoon wanting to try the crab curry. Boy, it did not disappoint! The amount of spiciness to it was perfect and it had decent amount of lump crab meat. I wasn't feeling the beef krapow though, it was too salty, fried duck egg on it was delicious though. Oysters were super small! Not sure will come back for that.. and thai iced tea is $8?! May be we'll come back for only the crab curry lol.
Good Thai in a sea of Thai in nyc. We had a variety of dishes, but the fish, like the namesake, was very good! If you were interested, definitely come by and check this place out.

Came here for the first time on Saturday and this is now my favorite Thai restaurant in all of nyc and let me tell you I've tried a lot of Thai in nyc! The food and service were impeccable! We got oysters to start, the fried chicken, the grilled cuttlefish, Thai iced tea, pandan lemongrass tea, crab curry and branzino and they were perfection! Our server made the best recommendations and was so kind. You also MUST get the dessert here everything was absolutely delicious!

Came here as I was visiting New York this was a nice place to try Thai food that wasn't just your typical pad thai. I like that they offered different types of dishes for you to try. The one dish that's stood out to me was the corn salad chicken wings and steamed fish. The duck curry was a bit too heavy for me and the scallop curry was on the saltier side but the scallop was cooked well. For the veggies I got the morning glory a classic green veggies dish but it was too much sauce. So if you're afraid that this place will be bland don't worry it won't be. I really recommend getting the steam fish that was so delicious and the fish meat was very tender. The chicken wings had a small kick to it but very crispy. Service was great and it's a nice place to come here for lunch or dinner

on Saturday after the weekend walk my girlfriends and I went to eat at Fishcheeks for lunch..the food was so delicious..we order the steam fish, curry crab, crab fry rice and Thai ice tea..i will definitely come back..
Love this place. Crab fried rice BOMB! Crab curry bomb! Everything is soo fucking delicious !

Don't even finish reading this review, JUST GO! 

First off, my friend and I did not have a reservation but were able to get a table for 2 @ 9:30 on a Friday night (God was smiling down on us). The front is kind of non-descript and the inside is very cozy. The staff are attentive but not overbearing, I love that. Now the food, delicious. Everything we had was delicious, the Zabb wings, the crab rice and the steamed branzino. I honestly can't even pick a favorite. They were all seasoned to perfection and came very quickly after we ordered. Definitely a new favorite spot.

It's a great spot with a very clean and well-designed interior. The space is bright, with nicely spread-out tables, unlike some cramped places in New York. The service was attentive, friendly, and quick. Every dish I tried was excellent, especially the coconut crab curry, prawn curry, braised fish, and dry-rubbed wings. Overall, the food was of high quality, approachable Thai cuisine done really well.

Spent a few days in New York visiting a friend. Stopped by Fish Cheeks for dinner one night and we didn't have any expectations, but was blown away. Genuinely think this has been the best thai food experience I've had in the States. The vibes of the restaurant were amazing, and the service and food were even better! Our server provided us recommendations for the two of us, and luckily we took their advice! All the dishes were seasoned so well, my favorite was unexpectedly the wings -- I saw unexpectedly because I thought, "why would wings be the best thing at a thai restaurant?". I would highly recommend Fish Cheeks and wish they had a location where I lived!

I've been to this restaurant a couple different times and its always a home run. The ambiance is cute and fun, and the service is always on point. They do a phenomenal job with playing with flavors here that make me a big fan. I think portions can be a bit bigger but I'm also just greedy. Make a reservation before coming here because its always busy --even bar seating. My personal favorites are the crab fried rice and the prawns

This is my second time time at Fish Cheeks, and it DEFINITELY not my last! This restaurant has my favorite selection of Thai so far in NYC. Their Coconut Crab Curry never disappoints - it has the perfect level of spice and comes with a serving of rice. The amount of crab in the curry is ample as well. 

This was my first time getting the grilled mackerel and it was great! Just beware of a couple of bones that may be in the fish. 

The drinks were delectable. I got the "Tongue and Cheek" which had an egg white foam on top of a sweet flavor beverage. The spicy mango was like a spicy marg! 

My boyfriend and I appeared without a reservation on a Friday night but were able to get seated at a nice table pretty quickly! We received a text stating our table was ready within 10-15min when they stated it could take 45 min! Walk-ins seem to be pretty effective here but always approach with caution that it could take longer during other nights. 

Very excited to be back a million more times.

This place has been on my list of to try for quite a while and although I'm not disappointed, my expectations might've been a little too high. The flavor aspect hit the spot, but my sodium level was off the charts. By the end of this meal, I was chugging water because of the saltiness of the food. Don't get me wrong though, my meal here was still delicious and enjoyable.

We reserved the table for a party, which they don't have private room but we highly advise making reservations for a table suitable for a large party. We had to hit a minimum of $75 per person, which we thought would be easy, but we just missed it by a bit. We ordered: 

OYSTERS: Fresh despite how tiny they were, the fish sauce vinaigrette and dried shrimps were new toppings we never experienced. At this point, I don't think I can ever go back to standard vinaigrette and cocktail sauce, because this was amazing and balanced each other so well! 

ZABB WINGS: A little disappointing, because I heard so much hype about this. I wished the wings were a little crispier and also less salty. I get that this was their spin on lemon pepper wings, which wasn't entirely bad, but the execution wasn't anything stellar to me. 

GRILLED CUTTLEFISH: This was delicious and cooked to perfection, but boy did that fish sauce burn my mouth on fire. The cuttlefish had a great char to it and with the fish sauce, it was *chefs kiss. Due to my spice tolerance though, I could only handle so much of it though, but I really enjoyed this dish and would highly recommend it. 

COCONUT CRAB CURRY: Probably my favorite and it was definitely elevated with sticky rice. There were very generous pieces of crab doused in a flavorful and thick curry sauce. It soaked up very well in rice and this was actually a fan favorite. I didn't eat too much of it to experience this, but also heard that this was quite spicy and a little too salty towards the end. 

STEAMED FISH WITH THAI HERBS: This is a must order. Honestly, you only come here for this!!! The fish was super tender and the herbs penetrated the fish seamlessly. Call me lazy, but the cherry on top was that bone was already taken out of this LOL. 

30 DAY AGED BEEF KAPROW: Disappointing. This actually just tasted like a hamburger helper doused it fish sauce. It was way too salty and even the fried egg didn't cut into the saltiness. Had high hopes for this and I'm really wishing it was just an off day 

CRAB FRIED RICE: Great and fragrant! The sauces it came with really elevated the dish! Despite being such a simple dish, it really hit the spot for me.
