MORNING GLORY: Always have to get a veggie dish to be "healthy", but this made me chug glasses of water. The morning glory was cooked well, but I feel like it may have been over seasoned.

My group and I had a reservation and we were sat right away when we arrived. I would recommend to make a reservation if you plan to visit because they do look like they get busy!

This restaurant serves their food family style, so be prepared to share dishes with your party. We ordered 8 dishes and I went with a group of 8 people (including myself!) and it was a good amount of food for us all. The consensus was that we were able to get full enough. We ordered the steamed fish, coconut crab curry, coconut duck curry, crispy rice salad, pork belly chili garlic,  crab fried rice, shrimp in sauce, and crab abb woosen. My top three were the shrimp, fish, and crispy rice. I felt the fried rice could have been skipped, I wish it was more flavorful.

Our server was good and service was fast despite it being busy. The one thing that I wanted to point out was after we paid, a host came up to our table to ask if our service was "okay" since the tip was "low" (we tipped 15% based on the subtotal). She explained that she wanted to make sure that we had a good experience, but the way the conversation was going; it more so felt like they wanted us to add more to the tip.

I tried the crab fried rice at a food festival and had to go to the restaurant to try it again. It was so good that I also ordered a portion to-go and got a bottle of the sauce as well. The pork belly was super tender and crunchy as well. 

Service was really good. We were seated right away, our waiter was attentive and checked up on us throughout the meal. The restaurant is nicely decorated, clean, plenty of seating.

Fish Cheeks will change your brain chemistry. 

Get the branzino fish! It comes piping hot to your table, and the broth is the most savory, bright, delicious bath that makes the whole fish taste like the best Tom Kha soup you've ever had. For those who don't like cilantro - this dish will change your life. It shows you the magic of cilantro when paired correctly with herbs and citrus. 

We also loved the wings! They reminded us of spicy sweet chili Doritos lol but in the best way. Absolutely delicious. 

Crab curry was good, crab prices were buttery soft. The curry itself is not too too spicy, but it does build and sneak up on you after a few bites. 

Prawn Kare was a miss - prawns were way overcooked and rubbery and the prawn to curry ratio was off. Would suggest going to Soothr for top notch Kare. 

Ambiance is bumping, decor is super cute and modern. Service was great although we highly suggest making a reservation so you can be seated right away.

The food was so delicious. The service was absolutely amazing,the staff was attentive and extremely friendly. Best oysters I've ever had! The wings were piping hot when they came out and they were crispy on the outside, moist of the inside and the flavor unbelievable. Crab fried rice is the best and the sauces add another level of flavor. That ice cream shocked me with how good it was. They need to settle it by the pints. Not usually a fan of rice in dessert but every part of that dessert was perfect together.
10 out of 10 would recommend and will return.
1. No Pad Thai Zone
2. Oysters
3. Zabb Wings
4. Crab Fried Rice
5. Ice Cream Bo Lan

Came on a whim with no reservation on a Friday night around 9pm with my boyfriend and we waited maybe 15-20min for a table not bad at all! 

Ambience: very cool vibes inside fun Lightning fun and energetic - servers are very attentive as well and super helpful if needing recs for ordering 

Food: we opted to try the restaurant week specials so got an appetizer each, mains, and dessert. 

App: we got the clams as well as the crispy rice salad (not pictured) both were excellent 9/10 would get again 

Mains: 
crab curry - great flavor a tad spicy but very satisfying. If you don't have a good tolerance with spice I wouldn't recommend. 8/10

Steamed fish in banana leaf: the fish was cooked well just overall flavor was ok 5/10

Dessert: 
Shaved ice - not our jam didn't really like the flavor 4/10

Ice cream with sticky rice: 9/10 very good flavorful not too sweet was the perfect palate cleanser after dinner 

Overall would come back and try a few different dishes like the fried fish and pork cheeks !
Always great food and quality. The service is always top tier  flavored well just all around good place
Great food vibes and overall a nice evening We went for the fish and it did not disappoint

Finally coming here after 3 years in NYC. People had recommended this to me as the best Thai place in NYC so the hype was definitely there. I believe (?) they change their menu quite frequently but we got their Crab Fried Rice, Duck Curry, Woonsen, and an Pork Appetizer. Everything tasted great especially the Woonsen but giving this 4 stars because I didn't feel like anything stood out to me as exceptional. 

I will probably be back to try their Grilled Fish/Mackarel which I hear is the most notable thing to get! Recommend for great Thai food!

Amazing food and drinks
See that is what we left.. Nothing! So great

The only small flaw, if any, is that they only have two restrooms. And sometimes we need to wait for a little bit. But regarding other things like price, like food, like service, they're all great.

author.name: Yue M.
author.location: Upper West Side, New York, NY

reviews.review:
the food here was really delicious. we ordered the coconut crab curry, crab fried rice, and steamed fish with thai herbs. the steamed fish was crazy delicious - loved the lime - and the crab fried rice had amazing flavor and huge chunks of crab.

one star off for subpar service. our waiter could not have been more distant and disinterested. the restaurant is somewhat tight/compact per typical new york restaurants, and the waitstaff constantly bumped into our chairs and table.

note that if you're coming here for restaurant week, everyone at the table has to order off the restaurant week menu.

I came with very high expectations, as I've been recommended many times over Fish Cheeks. I left feeling like all of them had been matched!!

Our server was super nice and attentive; frequently refilled our waters, checked up on us, and never left us waiting. Food also came unbelievably fast for how busy the restaurant was; we got the appetizers within 10 minutes, and the rest of the food followed shortly. It's a really lively place, so the ambiance matched what we were looking for too!

The zabb wings were amazing; not super crispy but not meant to be. Really well seasoned and juicy, and just super unique flavors.

The corn salad is a must get appetizer. Nice and crisp, super sour, and overall really unique flavors. Very fresh and perfect as an appetizer.

The fried fish was overall good, but nothing special. The fish was yummy, but overall flavors were exactly what I expected. Fish also wasn't super well seasoned.

The beef kaprow was fantastic. A bit spicy, but really tart and really flavorful. Great with rice.

Overall, definitely worth the hype!

Is it "authentic" Thai?  I don't know.  I've never been to Thailand.  But, it's really good food.  We went with a large party and ordered just about everything on the menu to share.  Only one dish disappointed me.  Needless to say, we all ate more than we should.

We arrived a couple minutes early for our reservation so they had us wait outside. They then brought us inside but realized our table which was ready in the system still had people dining at it, so they brought us back out. Then about 5 minutes later they did the same thing, but finally just found us another table to sit at. The waitress explained the menu when my partner was in the bathroom, so I had to relay the information and hope I remembered everything. That being said, the food here was some of the tastiest I've had in a while, especially the crab curry and steamed fish. The Punch Drunk Love cocktail was also quite unique and deliciously sweet and silky. Overall, I think they could improve their system and service, some items were a bit pricey, but the food and drinks were delicious!
The fish with herbs is soooo good and the watermelon cocktail. The service was good and the happy hour oysters were delicious.

Came here for dinner twice and had good experiences (order the whole fish if you're in a group of 4) but came here recently and it was just OK. We made it in time for the happy hour - oysters are on the smaller side but fresh, cocktails $13 and they have other specials. We ordered the zaab wings which were cooked nicely and had a good amount of seasoning. Our crab fried rice was tinged with w heavy hand of butter which made it rich but a little greasy. The crab noodles were OK, the noodles itself were fine but the crab (presented whole, cut in half so you have to crack it) had a strong ammonia odor which is indicative of spoiled seafood - was mushy in texture. It was really pungent so we stopped eating it immediately. Could've been a better experience had the crab been fresh and checked before service... would not return for anything other than oysters and "safer" dishes that do not have spoilage issues. Not great for the tummy/bathroom issue once arriving home.

Finally returned to Fish Cheeks after a whole pandemic and then some. It had been too long! We went last Saturday for lunch, so we took advantage of the happy hour oysters at $12 for a half dozen - a refreshing treat on a sweltering hot day. Loved that it came with fried shallots!

We had to have the zabb wings again, which were just as limey and tasty as I remembered. Temperature wise they were piping hot though, which required some patience before completely devouring them. For entrees it was hard to decide against the coconut crab curry but we wanted to make room for the crab fried rice and the steamed fish instead. Absolutely no regrets. The fish was also very lime-forward and left us with lingering garlic breath for the rest of the day but it was so worth it. The fried rice was so tasty and addicting especially with those large chunks of fresh crab meat... I totally get the hype for this one. The only forgettable part of the meal was the pandan lemongrass iced tea - it was too light in flavor and basically just tasted like water for the last 1/3 of the drink. Otherwise definitely still one of the top Thai restaurants in the city.
Fantastic place to eat. Great food and service. We were promptly greeted and the waiter knew the menus very well.

Despite having a reservation, I was a bit disappointed that we still had to wait to be seated. However, the food did lift my spirits. We went for their happy hour oysters, which did not disappoint. We ate them so quickly that I didn't get a chance to take a photo unfortunately. The other dishes were great as well. Portion size was quite small for the price, but the flavors were great. Personally, it was a mix of traditional Thai flavors but some dishes have its twists to it to make it more palatable. I'm glad they catered to both! 

The restaurant itself is quite small, so I'd recommend making a reservation or you might have to wait in a long line. The interior was quite cute and since we went there at night, I thought that the evening vibes were lively, but still cozy.
Best Thai lunch in New York. Steamed fish is a must have as is the crab fried rice. Pandan ice cream dessert was incredible way to end our lunch.

Highly recommended Thai and the cutest place ever but very heavily seafood oriented and I'm not really a big seafood fan. Honestly my fav thing was the grilled cabbage and the corn salad that seemed to be subbing for a green papaya? scallops and crab curry and cocktails and everything else v solid...

Prawn karee 5/5

Jackfruit Pandan Ice Cream Dessert (4.5/5)

steamed fish with thai herbs 5/5

Zabb Wings (4.5/5)
Moist / Big pieces (kind of) / Seasoning was like this powdery lk sour seasoning but it was nice / A lil sweet a lil savory a lil sour / its nice but I AM NOT a fan of the powdered seasoning but it was nice overall

Coconut crab curry (3/5) I DO NOT LIKE SPICY FOOD

Crab Aob Woonsen (2.8/5)

Amazing place to go with a group of friends so you can try several dishes. 

We tried the following:

1. Crab fried rice: we got two of these, it was delicious. The rice itself wasn't anything CRAZY but there was sauce involved and it changed the game. 

2. Coconut crab curry: we also got two of these. There wasn't a ton of chicken but with the rice this was just amazing. 

3. Pork belly: the was also really yummy. Very flavorful, was my favorite but some people in the group don't eat pork so we only got one portion 

4. Steamed fish w Thai herbs: this fish was yummy, I think it was a signature. It was really cool presentation wise- it was also pretty fishy and definitely honey 

5. Mackerel: this was my favorite of the fish! We got two of these as well. Crispy on the outside, cooked to perfection 


I also tried the tongue in cheek drink. For the price, it was just okay. 

This place was awesome - will definitely go back if I can get a reservation. 

That's another thing! They accommodated my party of 8 on a Saturday night when we called so super cool

Great Thai restaurant located in NoHo with some great dishes. Highlights of the evening were the Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce and the Coconut Crab Curry. Both dishes were flavorful, with the shrimp dish being especially in your face with flavor. 

Service was great and our server gave great suggestions. The drinks here are also well made.

Food: 4/5 | Service: 4.5/5 | Experience: 3.5/5

I made a reservation for 2 for lunch on a weekday, and we were able to get seated immediately. Service was good. I am not sure if this is typical, but the front door was open so the restaurant became quite warm and pretty humid.

We ordered the coconut crab curry, pork belly chili garlic, and the pandan lemongrass iced tea. The crab curry was quite spicy but the crab was tender, and the curry was creamy. I wished there was a greater depth of flavor to the curry although I'm not sure I could get past the spice. The pork belly was crispy yet still a bit fatty. I wish the sauce it came with was not hot sauce but rather something acidic to cut the heaviness of the dish. The iced tea was very sweet, and I was not able to detect much of the citrus flavors; it tasted a bit like fruit loops, which was an interesting new flavor for me.

WOW the flavors were next level - aromatic, herbaceous, sour, and spicy.

Fish cheeks has been on my list for a while, and I finally had the chance to dine there with family. 

We loved the steam fish, which is presented beautifully in a hot griddle shaped like a fish. The meat is so juicy and tender, with an incredible and complex broth. Definitely recommend this dish!
We also enjoyed the oysters, crab fried rice, (crab curry was okay), and drinks.

The ambience is super cool and trendy! The service was excellent and they were able to seat us without a reservation (we walked in around 10 pm after a fun time at the Whitney Museum)!
Consistently good and always a favorite when I take visitors there. The raw shrimp appetizer and the chicken wings are the clear standouts while the steamed fish is an absolute must.
This was honestly some of the best fish I have had! Super flavorful and simple meal. We got the steamed fish and crab curry. The restaurant was very colorful and a fun vibe.

One of my favorite restaurants in NYC, if not the favorite. I've been here 5 or 6 times and every time it is perfect. It's one of my fav spots to take friends visiting from out of town and it always blows people away. 

Fav dishes are the oysters (the sauce is *incredible*), zaab wings, calamari, steamed fish, and crab fried rice. They're famous for their crab curry and it's good but I prefer many of their other menu items. 

They also have a great happy hour as well with cheap oysters and cocktails. Can't recommend this place enough.

The food was phenomenal! We had a crab or lobster curry that my husband and I still think about at least once a week. We are hoping to go back very soon! The service was quick, and the employees were kind! Love the vibe of the place, great for a date night or hanging with friends! Can't wait to go back!

Great Thai but not your typical pad thai and run of the mill Thai food. All family style and super flavorful dishes. Broad menu with veggies, seafood and plenty of good stuff for carnivores too. Well decorated inside w great service staff. 
Steam fish came out on hot griddle and keeps coming while you eat off it. Perfectly filleted so no bones and super delicate taste with tons of leaves and juices to season it. Also had the crab fried rice, cuttlefish and lettuce and pork appetizer. Fish cheeks lives up to the hype and is a great Thai place that's not your norm

Walked in on a Tuesday night. The place was packed. Luckily, they had a free table and let us have it for the next hour or so before their next round of reservations. 

They give the table shrimp chips with a chili jam at the beginning of the meal. Very standard shrimp chips, hard to dislike. Started the meal off with grilled pork cheeks. The pork cheeks were more lean than I thought they would be. I wanted something fattier and more tender. It was seasoned well, but I think it was also a rougher cut of pork cheeks than I'm used to. 

Got the steamed fish with Thai herbs. The fish was good. Tender and seasoned very well. It was mostly boneless, but there were small ones near the head of the fish. Sauce was good and light. Refreshing almost because of the lime/lemons in it. It was nice that they packed the head and sauce for us at the end of the meal. Make sure to get a bowl of rice on the side. I would say a bowl is good enough to split between two people.

Solid dinner. Definitely consider coming with a larger group though so you can try more things. The steamed fish itself was enough for two people and more.

Came a second time and service was still phenomenal. We arrived 30 min late and they still were able to seat us. We tried to order a different set of dishes and sadly, none were as good as our first visit (see prior review). Specifically:

The crab woonsen with noodles - 8/10. This was the best of this second trip - I liked the noodles with the green sauce it came with but there wasn't much crab meat and the meat was a little overcooked.

Zabb wings - 7/10. They had a unique seasoning/flavor to it, which I enjoyed, but not juicy. Definitely on the dry side. 

30 days dry aged beef kaprow - 6.5/10. We were shocked to see this come out as ground beef. Seemed bizarre. But otherwise it wasn't bad. 

Choo chee scallop - 7/10. There weren't a ton of scallops and the pieces were sort of small but the flavors were decent. We enjoyed using the leftover sauce from the dish for our white rice.

Re ambiance, we were able to sit inside this time and it was crazy loud. We could barely hear each other speak. We were seated next to one extremely loud party in particular. Given the noise, we actually would prefer the outdoor seating.

Ambiance was great; service was friendly; food was incredible!

Authentic Thai food with a serious kick. We dined with 5 kids (aged 3-17) and it was a bit of a mixed bag in terms of their spice tolerance. The younger kids loved the pork cheek with jasmine rice. The older kids tried some more items, but still found the spice level too much. 

The wings appetizer was one of my favorites of the night - crispy, crunchy, nicely spiced and the entire wing. I also enjoyed the crispy rice salad, but wish it was crispier. The pad prik khing was unique with the fried tofu instead of pork belly and I loved they spice level, so good with white rice. The crab fried rice was excellent. The crab woon sen was also great, both crab dishes featuring big chunks of lump crab. 

Would definitely come back! Scheduling via email for a group of 8 was fast and easy, too.
Food and service awesome! I would definitely go back here multiple times as I've been on my pescatarian journey!
Mark is a very friendly and knowledgeable about the  food they are serving. He provides us good service and very attentive too! Cheers!
our server was rude but food was so great!!!!! Absolutely loved the branzino, cuttlefish, and scallops. All 10/10. Crab curry was too sweet for me and crab aob woosen was short on crab.

Was able to grab a 3pm reservation on a Saturday for 2 people, which was just in time for the happy hour that ends at 6pm. We had the:
1. Dozen oysters: the oysters themselves were nothing special, but the green chili sauce (nam jim)  that comes with it really makes the dish a must have for happy hour. I wouldn't suggest ordering them outside of happy hour as the oysters are very small in size. 
2. Zaab chicken wings: crispy wings sprinkled with a powder mix of salt, sweet, and slightly spicy. The crispy kefir lime leaves were a nice addition with every few bites.
3. Crab fried rice: the fried rice alone is very flavorful, but with the addition of the nam jim and prik nam pla (fish sauce) really added a nice salty and flavorful kick.
4. Fried fish with garden herb salad: nice crispy and tender fish, it needed more sauce as it was a bit lacking in flavor but overall good. 
5. Morning glory: great flavor, but a few pieces were hard to chew (aka it was a bit old).

Overall, we would definitely come back to try their other dishes.

They didnt have resys or picked up the phone so we shlepped there and had no trouble getting two spots, tip one. Service iz nice with a gen-z flare of ok im going to try but Amanda at what time are we meeting for drinks. No honey, what im doing isnt important. Who? Oh right, what can I do for you Miss?!  We had the shrimp that, different, special,  tasty, tip two,  and the crab that regardless of the spicy warnings didnt da bomb in our face, shame.

Randomly was raw bar hopping with my best friend - and we chose to go to Fish Cheeks. The best oysters in town AND their oyster sauce on the side?! Dude ...... I'm coming back just for that green sauce.

I'm happy to say that @fishcheeksnyc lived up to the hype and everything we ordered was delicious! The steamed fish is a must order, and all the other dishes did not disappoint. A top notch Thai restaurant in the city even with the increasing competition!

Wow we ate some of the best fish in the city here. Delicious food experience! We ordered appetizers, the steamed whole fish and crab fried rice. Everything was excellent, sooo good, but the fish stole the show! Tender, cooked to perfection, with awesome spices and flavors. Highly recommend!

Fish Cheeks is a great seafood oriented Thai restaurant.  I sat outside as a walkup, given the inside seating was completely booked and it took them less than half an hour to seat me with no reservation. The ladies at the front desk managed the seating very well for this popular restaurant.

The menu offers a lot for everyone and I chose the wings and half a dozen oysters. The wings have a salty lime powdery coating that could be as addictive as Doritos, if it were not for the saltiness. They are flavorful and most people will enjoy them. The oysters were served with a similar salty lime sauce on the side as well as flakes of fried onions. The oysters themselves are small, certainly smaller than blue points, but not as small and creamy as those from the West Coast. They were fresh and I recommend serving them with a few wedges of lemon with more brine retained. Ken brought the lemons upon request. Eighteen bucks for four wings and seventeen for six oysters is a bit overpriced in my estimation.

The price points are the only weaknesses I can find at Fish Cheeks, for everything tastes so good. The crab fried rice I ordered and the steamed Branzino were excellent together. They bring out the whole fish fairly well filleted on a metal fish shaped container with some sort of burner underneath to keep it warm. The fish is in a slightly spicy broth with cabbage and the fish has such a desirable consistency to it, not overcooked. The cabbage offers a nice counterpoint to the fish, with its very apparent freshness that is not wilting from overcooking. I devoured the Branzino and crab fried rice. However, I am still looking for a place that serves crab fried rice like the now closed Pam's Real Thai. Can anyone tell me where to find the best crab fried rice in the City? The crab fried rice at Fish Cheeks, served with spears of angular cut cucumber, was a little short of crabmeat at $28 and some may find $40 for the Branzino a little high, but I cannot imagine anyone will not like what is crossing their palate.

The ice cream over sticky rice, Bo Lan, was a good finish to a great meal at Fish Cheeks. The warm and somewhat crispy caramelized sticky rice underneath the melting vanilla ice cream on top offers another counterpoint and texture that is very appealing and represents a lot of what your palate will experience at Fish Cheeks. Bring friends, bring your date, and enjoy the four star experience at Fish Cheeks.

Fish Cheeks is SOOOOO good!! As one could expect from their name, they specialize in seafood dishes, and they definitely do it right. They save half of their seating for walk-ins, so don't be afraid if u can't get a resy!

Rec:
- CRAB FRIED RICE!!
- Crab curry (be aware it's pretty spicy!))
- Thai tea

The fish was good, but not my fave? Probably personal preference

It's a bit of a shack type vibe which was interesting. Sat at the bar and had the loveliest bartender/server. Came through with recommendations on deck which was great cuz I think he nailed it. The wings are a must and a fried fish is always a hit. Love me a Thai minced meat dish with rice as well. I think went fine fish cheeks well and I'm satisfied

Came here ~an hour before closing and was able to get seated immediately without a reservation! We got the scallop curry and crab curry. Both were good but I wasn't amazed by it. There were a lot of flavors that were blended well together, but I feel like there was something missing. The decor in the restaurant was really nice though!

Came with my family on a Saturday with a reservation and was seated immediately. We came during happy hour and ordered a few cocktails ($13 each) and happy hour oysters (dozen for $22 or half dozen for $12). Our waiter Gabe was great and had awesome recommendations. We ordered the crispy rice salad and pork, sautéed cabbage, coconut crab curry, crab fried rice, and steamed fish (branzino) with Thai herbs.

Oysters: very fresh. Came with a side of green sauce that was a little spicy, and fried onions I believe. 

Crispy rice salad and pork: this was my absolute FAVORITE dish. It was salty, acidic, spicy...so balanced and the different textures were great. It comes with a wedge of cabbage which helps tame the spice. It was delicious! I could just eat this and I would've been happy.

Sautéed cabbage: absolute sleeper pick. If you saw it, it would look underwhelming, but it was so simple yet so good. When it came out, it smelled so good, and it tasted just as good. Would not have thought to get it if it weren't for our waiter! 

Coconut crab curry: very tasty and had a good kick. It was crab and sauce, no vegetables or anything else in it, which is fine! I'd say I've had better curries but it still doesn't take away from the fact that I still very much enjoyed it.

Crab fried rice: simple but enjoyable. I could probably do without it but it was tasty! 

Steamed branzino with Thai herbs: similar flavors to some of this green sauce that came on the side with our oysters and fried rice, which was pleasant.

Overall, I enjoyed the entire meal and had no complaints. I would definitely come back again!
Delicious if you can get a reservation. They had a good wine list. I had the scallops, corn salad, and mussels. Every thing was wonderful! Sat at a table outside, and had great service.

This may have been my favorite Thai place I've been to. The food was absolutely delicious. I did go for lunch so didn't get to try any of the drinks, but still so worth it for the food. The mussels and chicken were probably my favorites but everything was a close second for sure! The restaurant was still busy for lunch and the space is a bit tight, but we got a corner table which was nice. We arrived a bit before noon to beat a bit of the rush/wait. One thing, they served our appetizers then waited for us to finish before serving our main dish but we wanted to eat them together. We ended up waiting quite a while until realizing we had to ask for the main before the appetizer was finished. 

I will definitely be back here to try for dinner and drinks.

Easily one of the BEST, if not THE best Thai restaurants I have ever eaten in. Wife and I didnt have reservations and no snobbery about it and just had to wait 5-10 mins to get seated. 

Wife and I had the corn salad...superb!! Crunchy corn, amazing rice vinegar sauce and a few super fresh veggies. Didn't expect much from such a simple dish but It was just so good. Then shared the trout  and the crab curry. TBH, I dont love fresh water fish, but they look like they breaded and fried (or maybe just fried) the fish and again, with just the right spices and sauces and it was a winner. Crab curry had tons of real crab meat and the curry sauce was unlike any other I have experienced. 

Great vibe here in general and service was superb. They were all over us in a good way and super pleasant from start to finish. 

Can't wait for our next visit!!

Wings were good! They must've added some sort of lemon salt to it. It was the right amount of sour with the salty. Coconut crab was amazing. Fish was super soft. 

SPICE LEVEL IS WHITE SPICY! NOT ACTUAL SPICE. 

We ordered the highest level spicy dish and it was still mild at best  Food still tasted great but don't come here expecting the same level of Thai spice as you normally would
The crab curry is indeed amazing. I've been trying to eat here for months, finally did a few weeks ago.. everything we ordered was delicious. It's a must try!

Walked by this place and had to check it out as I haven't  had Thai food in a while and was craving ! This place didn't disappoint! We got seated right away as it was a weekday at 8:30p.

I love that the Curry was spicy, creamy, coconuty and heat warming. The Chicken wings and were tasty and juicy! 

The Steam Fish: five star dish. Ingredients include Cilantro, lime and chili. AND No fish bones! I was happy about that .. last but not least we also enjoyed the creamy, savory curry with succulent duck breast. It was small portion and little pricey but had to try!

 Atmosphere is fun and cool. I'd come back to try other things

I would give 4.5 stars if I could. 5 stars for the steamed branzino, 4 stars for everything else. The staff was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu (advised us on what to get and most importantly, what not to get since it was our first time dining there). The restaurant is nicely decorated, high ceilings, with one bathroom on each side of the restaurant. Doesn't exactly seem very Thai, but a nice space. Only very minor complaint is that the tables are a bit close together but that is not unique to here or enough not to go back.

We ordered 4 entrees as a group of 2 and were very full at the end. I think 3 entrees would be enough if you weren't very hungry. We tried the crab fried rice (the two sauces that came with it made the dish, especially the green sauce), the duck curry (very tasty and I would recommend, the duck was wonderfully crispy and the curry was delicious, came with rice), grilled isan chicken (enjoyable and authentic, came with two different sauces, one was sweet and the other more savory) and the steamed fish. 

The whole steamed fish was one of the most flavorful fish dishes I have had. Extremely tender fish in a cilantro lime broth with sour cabbage and spicy peppers. It was so good it was addictive. I could have eaten the whole dish by myself and was tempted to drink the broth.

I would definitely recommend Fish Cheeks, pretty authentic northern Thai cuisine and if you go, absolutely get the steamed branzino and the duck curry.

Delicious Coconut Crab curry and Krapow beef.  So much flavor and the food comes out pretty quickly.  Sticky rice was so good as well with the curry.  Plenty of food, we even took some home.  Highly recommend!  Had the Mackeral (very fishy and oily which is normal for this fish) but I loved the Branzino (steamed), and the Rainbow Trout during previous visits.  So good!  Skip the wings, this place is called Fish Cheeks (not Chicken Arms) so order the fish. Can't lose.
Food was spectacular, loved the twist the chef puts on the Thai spices, the chicken wings for example are so unique and flavorful. Crab curry was also spectacular!

Great but I think it's a bit overhyped on social media. Everyone raves that this is the best restaurant in NYC and it's tasty but I've had better Thai food.

I forgot which cocktail I got but the drink was so strong but it didn't taste strong which I like. I usually never get tipsy off one cocktail but theirs made me feel tipsy.

The coconut crab curry was tasty, but I wish they included more crab in there. The zabb wings were very lime heavy but we're just alright. The crab fried rice was really good with the fish sauce and green sauce. Huge portions for the crab fried rice. The pork cheeks were super fatty and paired well with the sauce (I'd pass if you are not a fan of fatty meats). The pork belly was the least favorite dish of mine because it was so salty.

Overall, decent place but it's a one and done place for me.
Food, Service and cocktails were great. The hostess was very pleasant. Our waiter(s)Kenny and Vinny were awesome as well.

Super underwhelming and overhyped. We went as a group of 6 and from the very beginning the service was rude and off putting. Coming from an Asian family, I know how to order food family style so when my family went (group of 6) we ordered over 7 dishes and the waitress said "you guys must not be hungry because this is not enough". Anytime we go to a new place we always want to test out the water and will sometimes reorder the same dish if we really like it so I had to explain it to her and she looks so annoyed with my answer. Even if we only ordered 7 entrees, who are you to judge? (With the 7 dishes, we actually needed to go boxes because we weren't able to finish it so don't let the waitress tell you how much you should order) 

Their curry and fried pork belly was also super spicy to the point where it wasn't edible for us. I will say the shrimp dish and fried chicken was good but not worth the price tag. The waitress never came back to check in on us and only came back when it was time to pay.

Also, it was SUPER COLD INSIDE and felt like all the food was cold the moment it was placed on the table.

TikTok and Instagram blew this place up and in my opinion, it was not worth it.

My roommates and I got a pretty late evening reservation here and service was pretty quick. Loved the ambiance in here! The decorations are lovely and it feels spacious. The smell of jasmine rice pervades the air and I felt instantly transported back to Asia. My friends like the steamed fish the best but the beef krapow was my personal fave. The beef is so flavorful and definitely spicy esp for someone who cant handle spice but eating it with the rice and the rich duck egg made it so enjoyable. The price for an extra duck egg is not cheap but I def considered it because it was so good lol. The steamed fish is their specialty and the branzino was perfectly cooked. It's also really nice that they debone it for you so it's super easy to scoop up all that delicious meat. We only ordered two entrees and an extra bowl of rice for the three of us but we were all left feeling pretty full

One of the best Thai restaurants I've been to. Steamed fish with herbs was superbly put together. So much flavor, the right amount of spicy heat, fleshy fish, presented on a warming plate-- it reminded me of Thailand. Morning glory was cooked and flavored well. The Riesling was flavorful, dry, and good finish. Promptly seated on a Saturday night. Server tended to us quickly and nice. Good sized seating space with enough room between tables for privacy. 100% would recommend to anyone looking for flavorful Thai food.

This is one of those places I was curious about but never went out of my way to go until I happened to come across an available reservation through Table One.  It was worth a little reserving ahead and upon going, I think part of the reason getting a rez is a challenge is because they do keep some availability for walk ins.   
Anyway, bottom line...the food is exceptional.  Service was fine but I would say it's in line with the pace given how in demand this place is. 
We started with the wings and pork cheek appetizers, both far exceeding expectations.   Usually wings are wings, but these were so flavorful and fall off the bone delicious.  Our mains were the steamed whole fish, with the broth being so good you could eat that alone, the crab fried rice, and the duck curry.   While the fish was hands down among the most flavorful I've ever had, the duck curry sets Fish Cheeks apart.   It's not the usual protein you see at your dime a dozen pad Thai restaurant, this was fall of the bone fabulous with this lovely peanut curry sauce that could make Top Chef envious.  
Lastly, vibe depends on what you make of it...we came on a Saturday night and found the crowd to be younger and typical Noho (we are in our 40s), but by the time we left we saw older families.  It went from almost too loud around 7 to relaxed by 8:30.  No complaints.  
Make the effort up go...we will be recommending to others and might just be back!!  Dreaming of that curry tonight for sure.

I had been meaning to try this place for a while, and I can say that it definitely lived up to the hype. The crab fried rice was a standout dish, with fresh and plentiful crab meat that added a delicious flavor to the dish. The freshness of the ingredients really shone through and made the dish even more enjoyable.

While the raw shrimp was unexpected, the veggies were equally tasty. The vibe inside the restaurant was great, adding to the overall dining experience. I would highly recommend trying the crab fried rice at this spot for a delicious and fresh meal in a welcoming atmosphere and friendly service.

I loved the whole fish branzino! It was perfectly tangy and so refreshing - perfect on a hot day. The fish was so fluffy and only had a few bones. The dry aged beef dish was also good and pretty spicy. The sauce paired well and cooled down the spice a bit if some find it to be too overwhelming. The inside of the restaurant has a warm atmosphere that is fitting for any occasion.

It's hard to get a reservation at Fish Cheeks. But I got one. I arrived on time to my reservation and was seated right away. Service was excellent! I had a 5:30 reservation, so I was able to take advantage of the happy hour special ($13 for specialty cocktails). I got the Tongue & Cheek. It was refreshing and tasty.

The food was so tasty, flavorful & delicious! I recommend:
- The Crab Fried Rice. Make sure to mix the sauce in the rice. It definitely adds some tasty flavor.
- The Steamed Fish came to the table on a fish shaped plate on top of a flame. 
- The Choo Chee Scallops has 1x chili pepper listed next to it on the menu but it wasn't too spicy.
Best Thai restaurant in NY hands down. Don't skip out on the crab fried rice and the steamed fish. Great cocktails, service, and vibes too !

Went here a few months ago and forgot to post a review but this place is amazing!!

Our waiter was legit amazing though I forget his name. He gave great info and recommendations which set the tone for our lunch. 

Oysters- GET THIS. So so good if you like oysters and the sauce on the side is to die for.

Chili pork and curry - these are solid dishes. Great flavor and taste but maybe too much for 2 people as I got sick of this by the end.

Steamed fish- ALSO GET THIS. Can't rave about this enough- best fish I've ever had. So flavorful and delicious

Drinks- tongue & cheek 9/10, no pad Thai zone 6/10, Thai tea 8/10. drinks were bad at all

This place has delicious food and a great atmosphere. The prices are definitely on the higher end so not a place I'd go to weekly but I will DEFINITELY be back for that fish

The bar isn't the best place to dine given the food on the plates takes up a lot of space. We preferred a table came in as a walk in at 5:15-5:30 was placed on the waitlist for 3 ppl the host came around about 40 mins later after I enjoyed cocktails at the bar and said they weren't able to give me the table because only 2 guests were there although we were willing to order for everyone. A bit pretentious for it to be not a fine dining restaurant. I explained when they asked would I be ok to stay at the bar I said I would prefer to sit at a table. And the second non host lady came over and said yea we can give you a table now this was about 60 mins into me being there. Fortunately the bar team was so lovely but eating a full meal spending almost $300 to sit at the bar is not cool. We had the curry crab, crab fried rice, wings were ok but you can skip those, whole steamed fish, glass noodles and 6 tongue and cheek cocktails with tequila instead of vodka it was nice they were able to sub in my spirit of choice. The hosts could be a bit more accommodating.

Really good, but really expensive. These reservations also go fast - I had to book it as the clock struck midnight to get a table for our group of 8. When we arrived we still had to wait a few minutes for the table to open up too.

Once seated though, everything was great. We got quite a few dishes to share amongst the group of us - coconut crab curry, stir fried pork belly, duck curry, corn salad, steamed fish, pork cheeks, wings, and sticky rice. I honestly thought the coconut crab curry was a little overrated as it was less flavorful than I expected. However, everything else I thought was spectacular. The wings were so light and crispy and well seasoned, pork cheeks were SO tender and juicy, duck curry was so savory and the meat was super tender. GET THE STEAMED FISH - the soup is so savory and well seasoned and the fish soaks it up so well.

Service was super friendly and accommodating as well. Overall, while the portions were small the food was really good and flavorful. I would definitely say it's worth trying at least once!

I stopped by here for lunch since I was in the area and I'm trying to check off more of my Yelp bookmarks. I was seated at the bar and the bartender/waiter immediately provided me with the menu and asked what I would like to drink. The bar seating had hooks under the counter to hang your stuff. I ordered the crab fried rice and I think it was one of the best fried rice dishes I've had in a restaurant. There were chunks of crab meat, the rice was just the right amount of savory flavor without being too oily. This made it easy to eat the whole dish by myself (yes it's under the "shared dish" section on the menu but it was just that delicious!) 

Service was good, the bartender checked in on me every now and then asking how my meal was. Being seated at the bar allowed me to watch the staff in action while enjoying my meal. They run a tight ship with the kitchen pushing out orders, the bartender making drinks and other staff prepping food for their dinner rush.

The restaurant is nestled in a busy neighborhood on a busy block with other trendy establishments. This might be the best one. I fully expected to have to wait in line, but surprisingly a table was ready immediately. I got my recommendation by Chef Ra (Ramen by Ra), so I scurried on over immediately after devouring one of her bowls. I chose oysters and chicken wings. Both were sensational. The oysters were small and briny like I like them, and the chicken was packed with a flavor punch I won't soon forget. They have a green sauce that they served with the oysters that is unlike anything I've tasted before. I cannot wait to go back. 

P.S.: try their Negroni. It's so delicious. And the crab fried rice is bomb as well.

We had a large party of 20+ people dine here for a birthday and it was a wonderful experience! Got great reviews about the food from everyone in the group! Our incredible waiter, Timothy, went above and beyond the call of duty to make our dining experience amazing! Pita, the maitre'd was a godsend both before and during the event. Thanks to Fish Cheeks, the celebrant had an incredible birthday! Yay!!!

I reserved a table at 9:30pm and came in a bit late due to traffic. Food was so good especially the rice dish. Coconut Crab Curry was also good but unfortunately served lukewarm. The coffee was very diluted and too much ice. We also got the lemongrass something drink which is terrible. Overall, food were good but not worth the wait and some were served lukewarm/ cold.

Nice and vibrant Thai spot. The coconut crab curry was good. The crab was very tender. The curry was not as spicy as I thought it'd be. The pork belly pad krapow was ok. The flavors were there, but it felt too hard/crunchy for me. It was a bit hard to eat, and I wish it would've been more tender in the middle/crispy on the outside instead. We were seated by the bar because it was a busy weekend night, but the service was amazing nonetheless.

The space was very cute, colorful and modern! The service was great. Our server even recommended other places to check out as we were visiting for the week. 
Overall, everything was well seasoned and tasty. My favorite was the Crab Fried Rice and the Scallops. The Wings' seasoning was savory and sour which was good, but I thought they were a bit dry inside. 
The portions were small for the price, but it's supposed to be a more elevated Thai restaurant. I recommend doing family style for the table! I would go back here.

Although quite pricey IMO, the food is stellar! It's Thai cuisine with a bit of a modern twist. 

We had reservations so we were immediately seated on arrival. The menu is family style, so grab a  few plates to share. We had the steam fish and the crab fried rice and surprisingly, my table for two was completely satisfied with two dishes. 

I love a good presentation and the steam fish was beautifully presented. The flavors were spot on! The crab fried rice, although simple was also delicious! 
Happy hour is from 12-6pm so all cocktails are $13. Regular priced at $19. We ended our meal by sharing the Ice Cream Bo Lan, which is very interesting with the sticky rice base. With the fish was $40 and the rice was $28, this isn't a cheap experience but definitely delicious.

I knew this place was very popular so I put off trying it for a while but I was definitely not disappointed when I finally bit the bullet and tried this place out. We went for dinner on a wednesday night and had to wait around an hour and a half for a table for three. Online, they are booked out for dinner for around three weeks in advanced so I highly recommend booking a reservation early. For appetizers we got the zaab wings and steamed mussels which were both pretty good. I would say the wings were not particularly memorable and I probably wouldn't order them again, but the mussels were great and I loved the sauce it came with. For entrees we got the grilled mackerel and coconut crab curry. The grilled mackerel was very fresh and came with pickled onions and other garnishes. The crab curry was absolutely delicious and came with plenty of crab meat.

my taste buds were pretty happy with me here !! the citrusy, fresh flavor from the fish combined with the creamy, spicy curry = perfect match. also whatever spice was on those wings... i need it. 

interior wise, appreciated the amount of natural light here! service was just OK.

what we ordered:
- steamed fish with thai herbs
- coconut crab curry
- zabb wings

We arrived a little before 5 PM on a Thursday and the food came out quickly. Service was excellent and waiters were friendly. It's helpful to make a reservation beforehand because it's a pretty popular restaurant. Nice decor and ambiance, good for both casual and more formal meals. Happy hour before 6! Dishes are good but a little on the expensive side. 

Steamed fish with Thai herbs (5/5): Whole steamed branzino with a savory and tangy sauce. The flavor combination was unique and delicious and the texture of the fish was soft. It comes over a flame so the dish is warm for a long time. 

Coconut crab curry (4/5): The most popular dish in the menu. Overall tasted good, but personally the spice overwhelmed the coconut too much for me. Portion size was also fairly small.

Fish cheeks is one of the most hyped restaurants in NYC, and it is deserving of its praise.

I tried the scallops, wings, steamed fish and green curry. The highlights were definitely the steamed fish and the scallops (not surprising since this place is known for their seafood!)

If you come here, you MUST get the steamed fish. It is extremely fresh, perfectly cooked, very juicy and the sauce is delicious. The sauce is sour / lime based as a heads up, but it works really well with the fish. The sauce is also not overpowering. It comes in a cool pan that is heated with a tiny flame as well.

The scallops were also delicious - they were cooked to perfection (not overcooked) and draped in a curry like sauce.

The wings are solid - well seasoned but quite spicy actually.

The green curry was average, I feel like I could have skipped this.

There are 2 bathrooms in the restaurant. The only downsides to Fish Cheeks is that it can get quite busy (make a reservation) and it is pricey. However, even though it was quite busy when we went, it wasn't overly loud and the service was still great.

Food, service, ambiance all went well n super cool. 
It is a very cute cozy restaurant. The foods were amazing. Love the foods . Definitely will come back again.

The pork cheek is a must order; so flavorful and rich. The coconut crab curry was also delicious, if sadly a bit too spicy for me (definitely have a lot of water on hand!) 

My only regret is that I couldn't try more dishes; I'll just have to be back!

I was really looking forward to trying this place, and my friend recommended it, saying it's really good.  We were able to grab a table during the middle of the day, when it wasn't crowded inbetween lunch and dinner.  

Service was good, the waiter was very attentive.  The food was hit or miss, I think it depends on what you order. The crab fried rice was the best dish, light, airy and tasty.  The whole branzino was good and flavorful, herbaceous, although you have to deal with a lot of bones for that kind of fish.  We also tried the 30 day beef kaprow which was a minced beef dish that was VERY spicy and oily (it gave me an upset stomach for the rest of the day and the day after that).

We were a group of 6 and were able to walk in around 4 PM on a Friday. There is plenty of seating and the entire store has great natural lighting. They have a large selection of drinks, mocktails, and food. Service was good and the drinks and food came quickly. They have a lot of unique drink options and everyone enjoyed their drink. The Zabb Wings were just the right texture and had a unique savory flavor and I would definitely go back just for the wings! We also ordered the Market Oysters, Coconut Crab Curry, Sauteed Cabbage, Crab Fried Rice, and Tofu Pad Prik Khing. The oysters were on the smaller side, and in general the portions were on the smaller side, but everything had good flavor. A lot of the food options are spicy so I would definitely preview the menu before if you don't eat spicy food. Overall the restaurant serves unique options that you won't find elsewhere!

Finally got a chance to try Fish Cheeks and got an afternoon reservation, which we got with Resy notifications as this spot gets booked quickly. Since we had reservations, we were seated right away after checking in. The servers were friendly and great with recommendations.

We started off with some drinks: Punch Drunk Love and Tongue & Cheek. All the cocktails are $19, but only $13 during happy hour which is daily until 6pm. Both of the drinks were good and smooth as the punch drunk love highlighted a pandan flavor and the Tongue & Cheek was lychee forward. We also got a Dozen Oysters ($22 for HH), but these for a bit disappointing as they were skimpy and tiny. The dishes we ordered were the Zabb Wings ($18), Grilled Pork Cheeks ($18), and Coconut Crab Curry ($30). The favorites and must order are definitely the wings and crab curry --easily a fan favorite! The wings have a crispy coating that's very well seasoned in a lemongrass rub. They even sell the seasoning for you to have at home. The curry had a lovely coconut curry aroma with a nice kick of spice. This dish was perfect for sharing over a bowl of rice. The found the pork cheeks being good, but nothing too special. It is very tender though. I hear the Steamed Fish is a must, but we were afraid it'd be too much food for two, so definitely will come back for that.

I get the hype and would come back here for sure. Loved all the atmosphere, decor, food, and vibes. I can see how picking the wrong items can be disappointing though, so may depend on if you pick the right items for your tastebuds.

Pretty good. Expensive since a lot has crab, but its understandable. However I think it's worth the price, but some things don't have to be as expensive such as the wings. Four or five wings for 18 dollars, although they are full wings.
Everything was easy, food was quick and tasty. Service was efficient though a little delay but got it done. Will return to check out more of the menu.

My friends have been wanting to go here for a while so I made a reservation for 1:30 pm on a Saturday. I would recommend making a reservation but a lot of people walked in and were able to get seated right away. The place itself is super spacious and there is a lot of seating inside. We decided to get everything family style to share.

-Zaab wings: These were not bad, the wings were tender but the flavors was just alright to me. 
-Crab Curry: Very yummy, it is listed as three spicy signs but I think that it is more of a two/one spicy level. Not too spicy, but so flavorful and creamy and a lot of crab in there. Highly recommend this dish.
-Green Curry: this one is vegan, listed as one spicy sign but I did not think it was spicy at all. Overall, pretty tasty! 
-Pork Belly Chili Garlic: Not bad but nothing too spicy. It was very crispy and some of the pieces got stuck in my teeth which I was not a huge fan of.

Overall, very unique thai dishes that I do not commonly see in thai places. Great for family styles and the cocktails looked really good. Would recommend checking this place out!.
It's always packed for a reason!!! HH is actually lovely. Food was delicious. Fun spot, yummy spot. Need to come back!

It's a small and packed restaurant space!
For drinks we got the Mango Sticky Rice and Tongue and Cheek, I wasn't really a fan of the MSR, it was strong and hard to drink but the Tongue and Cheek was good. To share we got Oysters, Coconut Crab Curry, Pork Belly Pad Kaprow, and the Pakboong Fai Dang. The curry was creamy and flavorful with lots of pieces of crab. The pork belly was good but we couldn't eat too much of it because it was sticky and crispy, it was just a lot to chew and on the heavier side but I'm glad we got to try it. The morning glory is SPICY but the addition of the green was much needed with the heavier entrees. Overall had a nice experience except that my partner had to use the bathroom and while waiting several workers kept telling him to go to different bathrooms across the restaurant, he was so confused!

We love fish cheeks and have been going there for years. The flavors transport me right back to Thailand (steamed fish is a must!) 
This is, arguably, one of the best Thai restaurants in the city!

Came here with my friend, we sat in a quiet area and my dad loves fishing and would always make home cooked meals with the fish he catches and I felt like I was back home again! 
Vinnie our server recommended us his favorite dishes and was so helpful and accommodating towards our dietary restrictions. He also helped us figure out some tasty mocktails that weren't on the menu and they were amazing! Got the dessert as well and was so full after doing it all drinks, appetizers, entrees, and dessert here!

Such great authentic Thai food!

Note: As someone who is gluten-free (celiac), they have a dedicated gluten free menu but our server mentioned that majority of the gluten-free items are still cross-contaminated (which isn't a huge issue for me). She said if you don't want cross-contamination, it's limited to about 2 items so I'd recommend giving them a call to ask before popping in.

We ordered:
- Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce (gf): incredible but SUPER spicy. If you can't handle spice, don't eat the chilis on the top.
- Chicken wings (not gf): was told they were extremely meaty and juicy.
- Coconut Crab Curry (gf): ugh, such amazing crab panang curry. so flavorful and just warms your soul
- Crab fried Rice (gf):
- Rawaaeng Duck Curry (gf): personally, I would skip this. it wasn't really memorable and even the server said it's typically not the most liked dish.
- Panang Negroni: I absolutely LOVE mezcal Negronis so this was exactly what I wanted and I loved it. I will say - if you're not a Negroni person, don't get this. It could come off as way too bitter or strong.

I've had Fish Cheeks on my radar for years. On one of my NYC trips last year, we decided to have dinner here. 

Pros:
Excellent dishes, both in quality and flavor
Slightly upgraded Thai classics - scallops and crab feature in the menu unlike your average Thai restaurant.
Great cocktail and wine menu

Cons:
Cramped space - though not atypical in NYC
Service could have been better
A bit pricey, though considering they use more expensive ingredients, it was expected. 

Verdict:
It's a nice dinner destination if you want a slightly more elevated Thai dining experience.

The service was great, although not a fan of servers pooling tips. I have wanted to visit for awhile now. The Thai tea was yummy. The flavors are delicious. My only complaints are Happy Hour drink prices are way too high. For a menu that advertises family style and sharing plates the portions especially the crab curry ( about 6 tablespoons) to share even between 2 people (with a starter ordered) is not enough for the price which leads to my main complaint is the prices are way too expensive - even for NYC for the food portions.

One of the best restaurants I've tried in New York. The Bronzino broth was RIDICULOUS. So many flavors working together in perfect unity. One of the best broth/sauces I've ever tasted. A must get. The crab curry dish was amazing too. Spicy with a sweet taste. The crab was really good too. My bro loved the fried wings.   

Great service, very friendly. Atmosphere was cool.

Ugh amazing food but definitely on the pricier end.. the portion sizes were also pretty small for each dish ): A lot of seating once you go inside but it does get crowded so I highly recommend making a reservation beforehand!

Still a great place to get Thai food. I had zaab wings from other places and this place is still the best. I just couldn't find anywhere else that can beat their zaab wings. Plus I always enjoy the oysters here. Sometimes it's just so hard to decide what to order when it's a party of 2 because there are so many delicious options on the menu. I haven't got the chance to try their duck yet since I'm always going back to the steam fish.
The food is amazing. I highly recommend the full fish. Such good flavors. The service was friendly. The restaurant is cute and good for groups. Just make a reservation first!

This Thai restaurant that specializes in seafood is all worth the great reviews. Make a reservation on Resy or they also accept walk-ins.

We got the oysters from happy hour and the mussels for appetizers. Both were delicious and super fresh.

For entrees, we got the coconut crab curry and their special of the day: khao kha moo. The special was mind blowing! They braised the pork so perfectly soft and tender with a crispy side. The coconut curry was creamy and spicy. 

We loved everything we ordered and would definitely come back again!

Came here with my friend and am happy to say I was pleasantly surprised! This place had great service and was such a good vibe. The only issue I had was that our table was kind of cramped and near the bathroom so we had a lot of people consistently squeezing by. 

We started off with the Thai iced tea and it was perfectly flavored and not too sweet! We then got an order of the coconut crab curry as well as the crab fried rice and both were exceptional! 

The crab curry was on the sweeter side, I usually like my curries spicier so I asked a waitress for some chilli oil but they were unfortunately too busy to get back to me about it. The crab fried rice however was one of the best ones I've had in NYC! The crab was incredibly soft and buttery and the sauces on the side complimented the dish so well! 

I would definitely come back and try more dishes here!

this place has been in my bookmarks for a while and I was so excited I got to go during my recent trip to nyc! my friend also recommended it as she's been a few times so I knew it had to be good!

we did a walk in at 12:30pm on a Thursday for 2 and luckily there was no wait! we were seated by the door though, which was super cold whenever someone opened the door but it wasn't a huge problem. the service was great - our waiter asked if we were returning or new customers and after I said it was my first time he told me about the food and recommendations. he continuously checked up on us and gave us extra wet naps as we ran out!

moving onto the food!
zarb wings: we started off w these wings for an app and the seasoning on them is delectable!! my friend said they can be a hit or miss sometimes but I was glad they were really good that day! the skin had a nice crisp and the pieces were huge (see pic)! one order came w 4 of them and the 2 of us could barely finish that. 

coconut crab curry: this has 3 chili peppers next to it and my friend and I are both not too good w spice but managed to eat this! the server also told us the spice varies on the type of chilis they have that day but we took the risk. it was super tasty and had nice chunks of crab in it but really had a kick! 

crab aob woonsen: this is a thin glass noodle dish w chunks of crab and we LOVED it! if I had to choose between this dish or the coconut crab curry, I would definitely order this again. the noodles had such a nice texture and it tasted more fresh w the celery & cilantro. it is more on the mild side so don't expect any spice on this! I thought this was a perfect balanced dish! the crab claws it came with were very over cooked and the meat inside was flaky which was off-putting, but this was the only downside of this dish. 

overall, the portions are great for sharing and the food is definitely great quality! I think the prices are a bit steep so I wouldn't go regularly but it's a great option for more authentic Thai cuisine!

Fish Cheeks was such a great rainy Saturday afternoon, accident. We stumbled upon it and we were able to walk in and get seating at the bar. Boy were we happy the drinks for phenomenal, probably one of the best curated cocktails I've ever had.  Happy hour oysters were a great deal, the green fish sauce was such a great touch. 

The coconut crab curry was utterly smooth, however the steamed rice was not the best for me. The steamed fish is a MUST, we cleaned the plate as it was perfectly
deboned. The fai dang veggies were a little too spicy for us but still delicious. I highly recommend coming here.

My Big Bro and I came to the Cheeks right as it opened as we didn't have a reservation, but we had clear eyes and full hearts, which is likely more important.

After initially being perturbed by a long line at 12pm on a Saturday, the patrons began to flow in and we were seated at the bar with the natural light flowing through the big window panes that overlook Bond Street. I honestly prefer bar seating most of the time, just way more mellow.

I was BIG hungry as I had just MOGGED the squat rack, pushing 135 for like 10 reps... Funny enough my nickname in high school was actually Big Hung, haha.

We sat and big bro does this thing he loves to do where he asks the waiter what they recommend, only to not get whatever is recommended ahahhaaha.

We opted to get the grilled cuttlefish, chicken wings, crab fried rice, and the steamed fish. I normally only highlight one dish, but this meal was a total team effort. WE NOT ME!

The cuttlefish was like a less chewy octopus that had some SPICE, it even tapped big bro out! Chicken Wings at $15 were a STEAL and delicious. Crab Fried Rice was the glue guy willing to do all the dirty work. Crab Fried Rice was Tony Allen, just a DAWG... It brought our palates back to earth before that steamed fish.

Steamed fish was PACKED with flavor, herbs, and spices and sits in a delectable cilantro lime broth that I may or may not have been eating by the spoon once we eliminated the fish. It was the perfect end to a perfect meal.

The Cheeks lived up to the hype, some of the best Thai food I've had in NYC... But the best I've ever had still belongs to Kalaya in Philly. If you ever in Philly you gotta get to Kalaya, it's spiritual.

IG @jnov_
Tiktok @jnov__

This place got cool vibes, the food was very flavorful and tasty. West coast style crab curry was thick and silky and full of coconut milk not water. steamed branzino was fresh and in perfect sauce. Also thoroughly enjoyed spicy rice salad (worth carbs cheating) and a side of veggies cooked just right. Would definitely come here again.

If you love oysters, martinis, and a great deal, the happy hour at Fish Cheeks will make you incredibly happy. Happy hour here goes from 12-6, 7 days a week. Specialty martinis are $13 (usually $19), and a dozen oysters are $21. This restaurant has extremely cool vibes, the interior is well decorated without being stuffy. Service was prompt and the oysters came out extremely fast, so we downed several dozen. They were super fresh and served with a spicy vinaigrette that paired so well with them. The cocktail list is truly something to marvel at - getting to sample these for just $13 when the level of ingredients in these cocktails would run you $25-30 anywhere else is really a treat. I had the fruity and refreshing Tongue & Cheek and the salty Nam Gin Martini and both were magnificent. Depending on what time you get here there may be a bit of a wait, but it's well worth it.

This is easily my favorite restaurant in the entire city. Definitely the kind of restaurant where you want to order at least 3-4 plates depending on the size of your party and then share family style. 

The coconut crab curry is to die for. It's the perfect amount of spicy and has a healthy portion of crab. I could eat just this everyday for the rest of my life and be happy. The prawn karee are also delicious and well seasoned. The prawns are always nice and big. The zabb wings are another must have. The restaurant is always busy and has a pleasant energy to it. Make sure you leave room for dessert. The ice cream bo lam is perfectly sweet and light after a spicy meal. Every time I go with someone new and they try the dessert they are absolutely surprised to have never tried something quite like it. 

The coco bah is another must have. A pleasantly refreshing non-alcoholic drink that again isn't quite like anything else you'll have around other places in the city.

Fish cheeks has been on my list for a long time and I'm so happy I finally went. The branzino and coconut crab curry are legit amazing! The shrimp relish was surprisingly good too. It's served with an assortment of vegetables (think butter lettuce, cucumbers, Thai eggplant). But it's legit just a dip that's very spicy. But I like spice so I enjoyed it. The drink options are also great - the spicy mango was my fav! I didn't realize I made a reservation for outside however the host accommodated us and switched us to the bar.

Honestly, I did expect more out of this restaurant. I don't think any of the dishes were bad, but I did not find anything above average, except for the crab fried rice because the green sauce was delicious. The rice salad and chicken wings were a little too salty for me, but the crunch to the chicken was really good. The coconut crab curry and fried fish weren't as flavorful as they could've been. I expected the curry to have more coconut flavor, but it seemed watered down. Overall, I think everything was average. 
The waiter was incredibly nice and attentive. He gave is good suggestions on what dishes to order and how many for our party of six. 
We sat outside and it was raining but the patio had a solid roof so the vibe was pretty nice and it was easy to have conversations.

This restaurant was amazing, it checked out all the boxes of great service, food, atmosphere! Prices are pretty on par for New York prices, but with the quality of the food, I would say this place is so worth the price!

Even writing this review is making me wish I could be eating here again right now.

First of all, make a reservation!! We tried to make a reservation two weeks before on a weekend lunch and there were no reservations. We decided to try our luck with a group of 4 and got there right at opening and were greeted right away and they were able to get us a table as long as we finished up before 1:30pm, which I assume was the next reservation for a table. We were thrilled, as the place quickly filled up after opening.

Lots of food items here had the spicy icon next to it, and I don't do the best with spice but it was doable and totally worth it. For appetizers, we did the grilled pork cheeks were delicious, so tender and juicy as well as the corn, which was super good and refreshing.

For entrees, we opted for the coconut crab curry and steamed fish which were both delicious!!

I feel like it's not often that all the dishes are a hit that we order, but everything was great! I would get everything again and looking forward to coming back here asap

The ambiance here is wonderful, and the staff is very welcoming. I ordered the poached monkfish as an appetizer, and while it was a bit too limey for my taste, pairing it with jasmine rice helped balance the flavors. Overall, it had a pretty good taste, resembling crab more than fish.

author.name: Hardeep S.
author.location: Central San Jose, San Jose, CA

reviews.review:
Went here for an early dinner last night. They make you wait for the whole party to be there and I was nervous because I was running 15min behind, but they had a table for us when I got there!
Happy hour 7 days a week goes until 6!! We got in at 545 so put in for HH cocktails and oysters right away. Even though it was early and a Sunday this place was still packed (and apparently had a 1 hour wait time for walk ins).
The first cocktail I got was the tongue in cheek which I didn't love, too floral tasting for me. My date had the specialty martini which was delicious and I ended up ordering for my second drink! 
The oysters were average tasting, small in size. Enjoyable enough but certainly not the reason to come here.
We then had the wings, which were enormous, hot and juicy haha, with a dry rub that tasted like a more complex version of what's on those "hint o lime" tortilla chips. The crab Woonsen was just okay, kinda just a bowl of noodles with a few pieces of crab, wouldn't order again. However the fried fish was PHENOMENAL- perfectly cooked with all these fresh herbs and vinaigrette, this dish definitely made the meal.
Vibes were good, busy and loud but not to an unbearable level at all. Service was pretty good too! Waitress was attentive and nice... there was a weird moment where I followed up on my cocktail order and she was like, you never ordered a cocktail, and I had to be like haha no um er we actually had a whole conversation about it hah - it's like, just say you forgot don't gaslight me! But she was so nice otherwise.
Even though I only found half the dishes to be really good, I'd still want to come back and try more items, because the menu looks amazing and the food that was good was SO SOOO good!

I was really excited to try Fish Cheeks as I had heard so many great things about the place. We got outdoor seating in the outdoor tents they have set up which was really lovely and private and perfect for my date night. Our server was incredibly attentive.

We ordered a Thai iced coffee, Zabb chicken, and the famous spicy crab curry. I thought the Zabb chicken was good, an interesting and unique spice blend I've never tasted before, but I wish it had come with a sauce. The flavors were kind of overpowering and overwhelming at times and it would've paired nicely with a sweet and sour sauce or an egg roll dipping sauce.

The spicy crab curry was also very good but I found it a small portion for the cost. Everything was pretty pricey for the size and that was my main gripe with the place, especially for all the raving reviews I had heard about Fish Cheeks previously. 

Overall, great food but not worth the price.

Fantastic Food.  Cool Ambiance.  Excellent Service.

I don't know about others but most of the time I would think of Thai food it would be a quick lunch or a casual dinner.  This is neither a quick lunch nor a casual dinner.  Food is top notch.  The Manhattan gives its corrections to the pricing obviously but this place still is worth every penny.  Prawn Karee that my daughter loved.  The Panang Negroni and Spicy Mango cocktails.  Pork Belly Pad Kaprow, oysters, Rainbow Trout all delicious, all wonderfully presented but make sure you have the reservation because the place gets really really really busy.

We managed to get a walk in table on a Friday night. The service was quick and helpful. It was def a bit crowded and hectic but the meal was so fantastic that we didn't mind. All the dishes we got were incredible but the seafood focused stuff was the highlight for sure. We will be back again soon!
Coconut crab curry was a Thai hug in a bowl. Spicy, creamy, rich, and complicated flavors all over perfect sticky jasmine rice. Attentive and kind waitstaff

Huge restaurant and was very excited to try as I usually don't have much Thai food! Servers were especially friendly and happy to provide recommendations and describe the dishes. 
However, for the price the portions are definitely way too small. 
We got the Thai tea - 3/5 standard, good not great. Sweet
Zabb wings - 3.5/5 really nice seasoning and very sour! Only ranked lower because I was not used to eating wings so sour so more of a personal preference. Cook was great too
Coconut crab curry - 3.5/5 was excited for the spice as it's one of the spiciest items on the menu and they warned us it's Thai level spicy. It absolutely is not Thai level spicy. It does have a kick but I would say more like a one pepper level and not even close to Thai spicy. Besides it not being spicy, the curry has wonderful soft crab chunks and really nice curry flavor! 
Lobster tom yum - 3.75/5 this was my favorite item but I don't think I'd get it again due to the price. It does have a bunch of great quality mussels and lobster was yummy too! It was less sour than I expected and had a really nice balanced seafood flavor throughout that I enjoyed. My friend who loves Tom yum said it is missing some oomphs but me who never has Tom yum thought it was still pretty yummy

Get the crab fried rice it's so good. I'm happy they expanded I love to see a great restaurant thrive and grow. Service is good here very attentive. It's a cute place for a girls night out or a quick date

Delicious food, and exceptional service! A must-try is their whole branzino - incredibly fresh and flavorful, perfectly paired with the crab rice. Despite not being fans of spice, the chicken wings were irresistible. The showstopper was the PanDam jackfruit dessert, which was truly incredible! The price aligns with the quality. We'll definitely return!

Great food and drinks, loved everything we got especially the raw shrimp appetizer. Fast service. Can't wait to come back and try more stuff (although was disappointed to see the beef tartare is no longer on the menu)

We were in a rush due to poor planning on our side, and they more than accommodating to give us one of the best meals I've had ever. Period. A great group setting outside, and I'm sure a great date night as well.

The receptionist pretty much ruined the night, arrogant and so much attitude from the moment we walked in. 
She put me and my husband at a table of 4 a front of entrance door with cold air coming in from door opening. I asked to be moved to a table of 2 farther from entrance knowing that other tables were open....she refused..
I proceeded to ask another receptionist and moved us within a second of asking. 
Food was ok, fried fish wasn't crispy, lacked more of the citrus sauce they put at the bottom. Wings were good, nice citrus kick. Crab curry was nothing special, lacked flavor. 
Our waiter was incredible and very helpful but once again receptionist had to ruin the end of meal.. The second the dinner plates were off the table, receptionist puts our bill on the table. Waiter didn't have time to ask if we wanted dessert...we told her we wanted dessert and she quickly snatched the bill out of my husband hands... I was so disturbed we demanded to pay right away to our waiter and leave. Please reconsider your receptionists. 
Thank you.

Really good restaurant if you love seafood and can take some spice! Ordered the shrimp later, steamed fish, zabb wings and the grilled cuttlefish. Service was great as well. Waiter was very knowledgeable and enthusiastic. Restaurant myself was quite spacious and not too loud. Would come back!

Came here for lunch and was blown away by the flavors in the food! The menu is unique (not a basic Thai restaurant) and the dishes felt like home-style cooking. I could feel the soul of the food.

The coconut crab curry was the highlight of the meal. The rich flavor of the crab had been infused into the curry and the crab marinated with the complex, deep spices of the curry. The crab aob woonsen and the crispy rice salad and pork were also really unique and tasty. Spice level was just perfect for all dishes--never overpowering.

The interior is very cute and themed. Service very attentive and caring. Highly recommend!

There are lots of food options, but didn't feel like the food had some sort of "authentic" taste? Maybe I am overreaching, but I didn't get a lot of citrus or basil or herbs/spices that I would typically associate with Thai. The prices are still pretty high, and I thought the cocktails were just ok. The whole fish was cool I guess but honestly was pretty flavorless and the fish was overcooked to a mushy texture. Nothing too memorable.

I don't come to NYC often but when I do, I always come for their baked fish. So good 

Their service is great and the ambience is perfect for a drink in the neighborhood or a date night
