Let's get this out of the way - it's an expensive restaurant for Thai food, but you're also in an trendy area with expensive shops around, so get over it. The setting is super cool with high ceilings and great decor, great vibe inside, with very attentive staff who are also great looking. 

Jumping right into the food.

Crab Curry: most delicious thing we had, and one of the best I've had in NY. Very thick, creamy broth and lumpy crabmeat. Flavors were outstanding. I'd come back only for this dish. 

Zabb Wings: super yummy with the citrus flavor.

Mussels: just alright, wouldn't order again. 

Pork cheek: Great flavor, super tender, portion is small. 

Prawn Karee: This was laughable - 3 prawns for $28 that weren't even giant. They were just normal size. Never mind the flavor was nice, the price was outrageous for what we got.

This place was legittttt. A bit pricy but the food was quite good. Ordered a range of good but the winners you must get are the coconut crab curry, the crab fried rice and the steamed fish.

The curry was nice and spiced and super creamy. The crab fried rice was my favorite and came with two addictive and flavorful Thai sauces. The steamed fish is a generous portion and is great with the white rice.

Our staff was super nice and helpful in navigating the menu also was super attentive. The interior was nice and the vibe was great - Sat night and it was popping!

First of all, service is impeccable. Our server Justin was attentive without being intrusive. The menu changed since I was here last but he provided great recommendations.

Now on to Food. We got the usual favorites: Crab Fried rice and Steamed Fish. Always a win, consistently delicious and never disappoints. 

I'm a big fan of their Crab Curry but for some who can't handle too much spice the Rawaaeng Curry is such a good alternative. The Duck was cooked just right and the curry was rich, savory and perfect with the rice 

The Lang Saeb, now this was absolutely out of this world. The meat was so tender that it would literally fall off the bones, the broth was garlicky and spicy: perfect for sipping on such a cold night. 

I appreciate that Fish Cheeks is constantly updating their menu and offering dishes that most Thai restaurants in New York would shy away from. We also loved hearing about how the ingredients are sourced and prepared to provide that authentic Thai flavor! We can't wait to see what's next!

I absolutely loved Fish Cheeks. We walked in ~5:15 PM on a Saturday evening, and they let us know it was about a 30 minute wait. We were seated ~30 minutes later so timing was prompt.
We came around HH so the oysters had a great deal. The oysters are on the smaller side, but were divine in freshness and flavor. We also got the grilled cuttlefish, which were incredible but even for me - a spice lover- was a bit on the hot side so beware! For entrees, we grabbed the crab fried rice and duck curry. Crab fried rice was good, but similar to what you can get in other Thai places, but duck curry was amazing! Impeccable flavor - I can't wait to go back

This place is amazing!! Literally everything we got was so good - The zabb wings were crispy and seasoned like mama noodles (iykyk), the oysters paired well with the chimichurri and fried shallots, the steamed fish was so tender and the sauce was to die for, and the crab coconut curry had so many seasonings I could swim in it!! I liked that the food also came out pretty fast and the service was attentive even though we were seated outside. Next time I'd def would want to try the crab glass noodle dish!

Nice Thai restaurant on the east side. You order with a waitress/waiter and then they have a QR code on the table to pay from if you can't seem to wave down your waitress/waiter. We didn't get the infamous fish as it was just two of us but it looked delicious. Instead we got the crab fried rice with LUMPS of crab meat and the shrimp. The food is a little pricey even for manhattan but the flavor is there.

I recently visited Fish Cheeks with a friend, and I must say, it absolutely lived up to its hype. We decided to indulge in a variety of dishes, and each one was a culinary adventure in itself.

First up, the Zabb wings caught our attention. Fried chicken with chili lime and fried makrut lime leaf? It was a flavor combination unlike anything I've ever tasted before. The wings were generously sized, juicy, and bursting with flavor.

Next, we couldn't resist the crab fried rice, and we were not disappointed. The abundance of crab meat in every bite was impressive, and the nam jim and pork nam pla sauce added an extra layer of deliciousness. Pairing it with the steamed fish and Thai herbs, a whole branzino in chili lime cilantro broth, was an absolute delight. Placing the fish on top of the rice elevated the flavors to another level.

We opted to sit at the bar, which offered fast service and ample space for our array of dishes. Unlike some cramped bars, this one had plenty of room to enjoy our meal comfortably. The Thai tea was a standout, tasting authentic and perfectly complementing the meal.

The ambiance was just right for a social evening, with low lighting adding to the cozy atmosphere. All in all, Fish Cheeks proved to be not just a dining experience, but a memorable culinary journey.

After years of anticipation, I finally had the pleasure of dining at Fish Cheeks, and let me tell you--it did not disappoint! Service was courteous. Ambiance is on the more casual side - vibrant but not too loud (still able to have a conversation without having to raise your voice) 

We visited during Restaurant Week and opted for the prix fixe menu, which allowed us to sample three dishes for $60 per person--a fantastic deal for the quality and variety of food we received.

The following dishes really stood out to me: 
* Coconut Crab Curry: The coconut crab curry was everything I had heard and more! Rich, creamy, and bursting with flavor, it was a true standout dish that left me craving more.
* Grilled Cuttlefish: As someone who isn't typically a fan of seafood, I was pleasantly surprised by how much I enjoyed the grilled cuttlefish. The texture was perfectly chewy, and the flavors were outstanding--definitely a dish I would order again.
* Pakboong Fai Dang: The pakboong fai dang, or morning glory (water spinach), was a delightful surprise. I never expected to enjoy this dish as much as I did! The morning glory was expertly seasoned and packed with flavor--a true testament to the skill of the chefs at Fish Cheeks.
Came with The Girls Friday night dinner . Not my first time they expand  the place, which is great more space . The food was delicious but the food portion was extremely small . Would not come back .

Expensive but so tasty!! 

We got the steamed fish, pork cheeks, prawn karee, crab fried rice.

WOW the best thai food ive had in a while! The flavors were phenomenal, with each dish offering layers of deliciousness. We ordered the crab curry, steamed branzino, crispy rice salad, shrimp, and wings, Normally, I'm not a fan of steamed fish as it tends to be bland, but the fish cheeks at this place completely won me over with their incredible flavor and texture. The crispy rice salad was another standout, although it became a tad salty as it cooled down, it remained incredibly tasty. The wings were bursting with flavor, so much so that I returned the next day to purchase their seasoning. Unfortunately, the curry didn't quite hit the mark for us; it lacked that special something we were hoping for. Nonetheless, the service was good, and the ambiance added to the overall charm of the experience.

Food are amazing and very good but the price is very high. i do like the food here but not sure if i'm coming back here again. the space is cute but very tight, tables are very close to each other not much privacy. 

Zabb Wings: 4/5 love the citrus flavor of the wings. but there are still feathers on the wings which is bit gross. 
Mussels: 3/5 flavor is a bit bland. the lemongrass flavor is not very strong  
pork cheek: 4/5 flavor is amazing, very tender and great dipping sauce, but the portion is tiny. 
Pla Pao: it's fun but messy to eat. fish is bland will need to add the sauce to be flavorful. i would go with steam fish instead. cabbage provided still has dirt on some of them, not washed throughly. 
Prawn Karee: 2/5 flavor is great but 3 prawns for $28 is steep, the prawns are normal size not even giant. this probably the one that threw me off. 
Crab Curry: 5/5 the best of all that we ordered. spicy and creamy , a lot of crab meat inside worth every penny. 
I ordered thai ice tea with less ice. and realized that my glass is much smaller than my friend's glass that has regular ice. 

Service is great, they came over to change the plate frequently and our waitress was really friendly , but coming to the bill the tip options starts with 20%.
I went for my birthday two years ago and I'm still thinking about it. The food is unbelievable, the service was wonderful. Cannot wait to go back.

Overpriced food, very small quantity, though decent flavor. This is for a delivery we received. When you order the $30 crab curry, you'd expect it to be bigger than a small plastic container. All the items we got were appetizer size from the vegetable to the pork jowl. The largest item we got was the jasmine rice. This is a bit disappointing to say the least. I understand how it might be difficult to run a restaurant but this is pinching the customers. 

Flavor is decent if you like super spicy food. Crab curry lit your mouth on fire as did the Pakboong. Not sure why people raved about the curry. It was so spicy, I guess you'd stop eating afterwards. Pork cheeks were solid and the chicken wings were okay. There's some spice in the chicken as wel

The steamed fish is a must at this place. It comes deboned and the sauce has a sour and spicy taste. The crispy rice with pork is also my favorite because I love a spicy and sour dish with a crunch. The crab curry was good but a little too spicy for me.

Fish Cheeks presents an ambitious take on Thai cuisine, striving to offer an outstanding culinary experience. However, my recent visit resulted in a mix of impressions, culminating in a 3/5. 

The Crab Fried Rice, featuring a combination of crab, rice, egg, scallion, cilantro, and cucumber, served alongside nam jim seafood & prik nam pla, promised an enticing dish. Yet, it failed to deliver on its promise. While competently prepared, the dish tasted indistinguishable from the myriad of fried rice dishes available across the city or even my own kitchen. Not kidding. The flavors, expected to present a vibrant harmony of freshness and depth given their popularity, instead whispered in muted tones, offering nothing that one couldn't easily replicate at home. For a dish carrying a hefty price tag, it was decidedly underwhelming, lacking any unique flair or twist that would justify its cost. It's also tiny portions. How is it their most popular item? You can get this exact fried rice in Chinatown for 95% cheaper and twice the portions. 2/5. 

Equally disappointing was the Pork Belly Pad Kaprow. Described as wok stir-fried crispy pork belly with holy basil, garlic, and chili, the dish's reality was a stark contrast to its mouth-watering description. The pork belly was overly hard and crunchy rather than being the succulent, flavorful centerpiece it ought to have been. Far from the tender, richly seasoned bites anticipated, each piece took a lot of work to chew, with the overpowering saltiness overshadowing the delicate balance of flavors for which Thai cuisine is celebrated. Additionally, the portion size left much to be desired, diminishing the dish's value. 2/5.

However, it wasn't all misses at Fish Cheeks. The cocktails served were a highlight, skillfully crafted and offering a refreshing reprieve from the meal's earlier disappointments. The inventive combinations and quality ingredients shone through, showcasing the bar's prowess. Excellent prices as well. 5/5.

Service, led by our server, Daniel, was a beacon of hospitality. Daniel's attentiveness, knowledge of the menu, and genuine warmth added a much-needed layer of enjoyment to our dining experience. His recommendations and care ensuring our comfort throughout the evening were commendable, highlighting the restaurant's commitment to guest satisfaction. Best of luck to his music career as well! 5/5.

Fish Cheeks presents a concept brimming with potential, underscored by moments of brilliance in its beverage program and service. However, the culinary execution, particularly of its highlighted dishes, needs to improve. For enthusiasts of Thai cuisine seeking the vibrant, bold flavors synonymous with the country's culinary heritage, the current offerings may feel lacking.

Love love love this restaurant. Every time I go even long line for hour it is worth time to wait. Even my friend is one of the partner of the restaurant but when I go, I never tell anyone and getting table as a regular customer. Business is a business so I always follow the rule. It is easy for me to order or ask the server if they have any new menu or something good to suggest because we talk the same language but many of staff there use English. Food remains good as it was before. So no complain and actually good that I come one in a blue moon to see if everything is good. Ps Jennifer S reply as owner of the restaurant I'm appreciated. I always support the local businesses and congratulate if the business growing big.

Amazing!! We had curry, chicken wings, steamed fish, and pork cheek. We got amazing foods and service. The steamed fish was super tender and delicious!! The one minus stat was curry because it was super spicy even though our server said it's not that spicy. Ambiance was good and clean.

**5 Stars! A Culinary Journey to Thailand in the Heart of Fish Cheeks**

As a food enthusiast and a lover of authentic Thai cuisine, I was thrilled to discover fish cheeks, a hidden gem nestled in the heart of NYC. From the moment I stepped through the door, I was transported to the vibrant streets of Bangkok, greeted by the warm and welcoming smiles of the staff.

**Ambiance and Decor:**

The restaurant's ambiance is simply stunning. The decor is a seamless blend of traditional Thai elements and modern touches, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The air is filled with the tantalizing aroma of spices, herbs, and grilled meats, immediately setting the stage for a culinary adventure.

**Menu and Food:**

The menu at Fish cheeks is a testament to the chef's mastery of Thai cuisine. Each dish is meticulously crafted using fresh and high-quality ingredients, ensuring an explosion of flavors in every bite. The spiciness level is customizable, catering to both those who crave the heat and those who prefer a milder experience.

**Service:**

The service at Fish cheeks is impeccable. The staff is attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about Thai cuisine. They are always ready to make recommendations and cater to your dietary needs. Their friendly and efficient service made the dining experience even more enjoyable.

**Overall Experience:**

My visit to fish cheeks was nothing short of extraordinary. The authentic Thai flavors, the cozy ambiance, and the exceptional service left an unforgettable impression. Whether you're a local looking for a taste of Thailand or a visitor seeking a culinary adventure, this restaurant is an absolute must-visit. I highly recommend it to anyone who appreciates authentic and flavorful Thai food.

**5 out of 5 stars! A well-deserved recognition for an exceptional dining experience.**
Great food, service was good. Communal ambiance, chill vibe overall. It was definitely worth the time and money. Must try the rest of their spots in the city
there was hair in my food and water was dripping from the ceiling onto my brother. enough said

Service was great but food was disappointing. Mussles seemed flavorless, pork cheeks were fatty, and the green curry was thin and lacked veggies. The server's were very helpful.. and maybe we overstated our need for less spicy.. but that shouldn't have left things just flat.. and neither of us had covid.. so our tastebuds are intact

Good Thai food place. Despite the focus on seafood, their duck curry was really nice! Crab fried rice was also good. We were there at a time they were having an orientation or some training lecture with the staff so it was strange watching them all sit at tables nearby so ambiance was off

I want to consider myself a regular here given the amount of times ive already come from NJ too. I have to say this was my favorite restaurant of 2023 and i still come as often as possible because of how good the food is. As someone who doesnt cook a lot of seafood at home, this place really hits the spot when I do crave fish. The fish is cooked to perfection and is so delicate and soft. 
I love the Pla Pao and the Steamed Fish, im always alternating between the two. Both are super flavorful and sharable. 
Zabb Wings are a MUST MUST, the seasoning is so stimulating- salty, sour, crispy, moist etc!
Crab Aob Woonsen glass noodles were also very flavorful but the amount of crab was small. There was a LOT of noodles and maybe 1-2 spoonfuls of crab. 
Oysters are a pass here, ive gotten them 3 times and the oysters are so small and barely any meat inside. 
Crispy Rice salad & Pork was a nice appetizer but wasn't my favorite dish. Still would recommend to try at least once! I would rather save my stomach space for the mail entree dishes. 
The jackfruit ice cream and sticky rice was confusing for me. I didnt know if I loved it or not? There wasnt enough jackfruit for me but the ice cream and sticky rice was pretty good! Probably just a one time thing for me haha.
Overall SOLID spot for thai food. I always leave STUFFED.

Coconut Crab Curry is as delicious as everybody says. When the portion arrives, you'll feel it's not much food, but once you add the rice, it's a full meal. The curry is very concentrated with flavor and you can tell they understand how to make it properly. Very spicy!

i would return to this place for sure to get more
of those yummy raw shrimp in 3 crab sauce. omg those were the highlight of my meal for sure. freaking flavor bomb! tangy and sweet with a kick of spice! it's best to be eaten with all the topping at once! mmm mmmm im thinking about the taste as im writing this lol. we also ordered chicken wings which were also really good! chili lime flavor and meat was tender and juicy juicy. for entree we got the crab aob woon senn and isan island chicken. aob woon senn had really good flavor and the crab meat were good - the only thing is i thought it was jus gonna be lump crab meant but there were pieces of
crabs in shell still - i felt that the meant on the crab wasn't as good and the meat was hard to really remove
from the shells. isan island chicken was jus ok, nothing too special. i would want to try the steam fish next time and the crab curry!

As someone who doesn't normally enjoy cooked seafood, fish cheeks is BOMB. The crab curry was fragrance and hearty but the steamed fish is a game changer. The soup base is phenomenal. So tangy, sweet and spicy, and leaves you wanting the next bite. Beyond that the fried chicken was well fried and dry rub delectable. 

Also the party shot is super unique and tasty. Early January is supposedly their slow season so you might be able to drop in without a reservation if you come soon!!

The food was tasty, but their "Coconut Crab Curry" ($30) "fan favorite" came in a bowl half full. A few spoonfuls and it was gone. Everything else came in such tiny portions that one might even need a magnifying glass to see it better. So, we (two adults and a kid) paid our bill of around $100 and I went to another place to eat until I was not hungry anymore. By far the worst dining experience this year. The good news is that there are plenty of good food places around Fish Cheeks where you can eat properly and feel full for a fraction of the price. If you are hungry don't go to Fish Cheeks because you'll leave hungry and with a lot less money. Total ripoff! Run far and run fast from Fish Cheeks!

https://www.fishcheeksnyc.com/menus/#main-menu-copy-1
Their menus are online! When you come into the restaurant, the servers have you scan the QR code to look at it. Everyday from 12 to 6 PM is happy hour which includes half-off raw oysters and $13 cocktails. My date wasn't into oysters but we did get some drinks - Punch Drunk Love and 24 Karrots. She said her drink was okay, it was carrot juice with Smokey flavors. Mine was quite sweet and very coconut-forward. It was much better after it watered down a bit as a dessert drink. 
The dishes here are meant to be sharable so our server suggested for us to get 2 apps and 2 entrees but we felt like that would have been too much so we got 1 app and 2 entrees which was perfect for the two of us. I think our favorite was the Zabb Wings because they were sizable, very crispy and have a yummy dry rub seasoning on them that was sweet, sour, and savory. The other two dishes were good with rice too. 
We went on a Saturday and had a reservation for outdoors but asked to be seated inside because it was freezing that day. There was a line at noon when they opened but there were people who got seated without a reservation.

I didn't think any of the main food was all that amazing for the price. The crab curry was good but super skimpy on the crab and not worth the money. It was also extremely spicy. The vegan tofu curry was good but needed more sauce. 
However, the dessert (jackfruit pandan icecream) was one of the best desserts I've ever had. It was super unique but incredibly creamy and delicious. I would come back just for this dessert.

Friend and I came into fish cheeks on a whim, on a very cold afternoon. We called ahead to see if there was any bar seating available as everything was booked online. Luckily, we got in at the bar, because everything was great from that point. The guy at the bar was one of the best waiters I've ever had: informative, kind and funny. We had the chicken wings and coconut crab curry. So good. Bonus: their happy hour. I'll be back.

Service 5/5
Ambiance 4/5
Food & Drink 4/5

This one had been on my hit list for some time after hearing Chrissy Teigen gave this restaurant a stamp of approval. I would say this was the most comparable Thai food I've had in the states to Thailand, with the exception of the curry that was ordered (nothing too special, a little bland). All other dishes were packed with what I thought was authentic but elevated flavor, love a good family style meal, substantial portions. Reservations are a must and I think sitting inside would have been preferred if it wasn't packed inside! I would go back

I was there on restaurant week. For a $45 meal, it was an overall fantastic experience.
I had Poached Monkfish for starter, which I was not completely satisfied with. The monkfish was lack of flavor, and the sauce was overly seasoned with lemon and sugar. The Chef must have adjusted the seasoning for the American, it was sweeter than the one I had in Thailand which I prefer.
Not only the starter, my crab coconut curry for entrees was also sweet, however, that do not stop it from being a great dish. The Tai spicy just something you can never resist. Lemon grass, turmeric, galangal, lemon l eaf, just work incredibly well with the coconut milk. But, I want to complain about the rice came with the curry, it was too sticky and soft for Tai curry, Tai curry usually comes with firmer rice such as Tai basmati rice, which is cooked with less water.
The dessert did hit my spot, I enjoyed it the most in the whole night. It was a masterpiece of "contrast", contrast between hot and cold, soft and crispy. The sticky rice was cooked for two different textures, a sticky and soft one and also some crispy rice, just AMAZING.

The bartender is friendly, even though I do not have fluent English, they were still able to explain the meal pretty well.

The environment gave me an American fast food vibe for some reason. But it is still serious enough for a casual dinner date.

This is likely the most famous Thai restaurant in NYC. People from all over the world seem to have heard about it. I don't think it's that mindblowing especially when there's so many good places in Hell's Kitchen, but the plating is pretty cool. None of the food is offensive and is alright, but wouldn't fight tooth and nail for your reservation.

This restaurant has been on my list to try for a long time. I loved the prawn karee - the egg mixture in the sauce made it creamy and decadent. The prawns were big but I wish it came with more since there were only 3. The crab curry did not come with a lot of crab and was a bit too spicy for me. Overall the dishes I tried were not good value but they were tasty. Looking to come back and trying more of the menu though!

Hands down the best Thai food in NYC.

The coconut crab curry is to die for. And the whole fish is excellent too.

Solid drinks and good service.

5/5

Solid drinks, particularly enjoyed the Spicy Mango flavor. The Zabb Wings with citrus topping were a hit as an appetizer. Ordered coconut crab curry, steamed fish, and pork belly for entrees, with the steamed fish being the highlight. Despite initially thinking we ordered a lot, we devoured the food and definitely plan to return for more. However, the coconut crab curry was a bit disappointing due to a small portion and tiny crab pieces.
back again. this time bought more folks with me. make sure to make reservations the line  goes out the door! and all because well, good food

First time here and it was ok but I don't get the hype yet. I've walked past here countless times and heard a mixture of praise and disappointment from others. I would maybe return again because I couldn't get the coconut crab curry that some reviews have highlighted, but this visit was underwhelming. 

Portions were laughably small. The corn salad was a nice and light starter with the faintest hit of spiciness, but it disappeared in only a few bites and I wish there was more. The pork cheek was shockingly dry and tough and the accompanying sauce couldn't rescue it. The duck curry (rice provided) was delicious and the meat was tender in the middle, but there wasn't much duck and the curry wasn't that warm.

I did appreciate the service and the ambience here - an attentive waiter and modern, bright interior. However, paying almost $45 post-tax and tip to share two small starters and a main made me kind of sad, especially since I left really hungry. Perhaps on a second visit some day I'll finally get the hype.

I don't know how many times people have told me this is the best Thai food in lower Manhattan, but this place certainly didn't disappoint.

Appropriately named "fish cheeks" it is a seafood forward restaurant, but there something for everyone. 

We had the wings and rice salad with pork as starters. Wings were super crunchy, but the salad was the standout.

For mains we had the coconut crab curry which was unlike anything I've had before. If didn't have any amount of self control, I could've polished off 3 bowls of rice with just the sauce alone.  If you like seafood, this is your heaven!

Used to like this place, but the portion is laughably small now (advertised as shared plate entrees but not even one-person portion). Also overpriced. Staff kept checking in to get us to leave but got our order wrong.

service was great but food was super salty and definitely not worth the price. oysters were good, pork cheeks were tasty but rather plain, other main dishes were very salty and the crab noodle was dry and cheaply made.

This is a southern Thai restaurant that claims it focuses on seafood. We arrived during happy hour and took a seat indoors. Great service, our server was polite and very friendly. The food however does not live up to the price tag. The HH oysters were small and had a slight metallic taste to them. The whole fried fishes was cooked well but the herb salad was was dry. The shrimp paste dip was strong but wasn't well balanced and was also too dry. 

Overall for the price there are better options, this place appears to be another insta trap. Okay food but not worth the $100+ price tag for a dinner for two.

Came here spontaneously and loved it! Their crab coconut curry was delicious and the perfect amount of spice. I'm always a bit hesitant to order crab at some restaurants because it can be overcooked, but the crab was tender and the perfect texture, with lots of it in the curry. It was a great comfort food for the cold weather especially.

We were seated by the bar because the tables were taken, but the ambiance was still great by the bar too!
Great food, something a bit different from most Thai restaurants in NYC. Highly recommend the chu chee skate. Fairly crowded and lively.

This place deserves all the hype it gets! We got the coconut crab curry, crab fried rice, and Isan style grilled chicken. All three dishes were incredible! Fair warning, the coconut crab curry is VERY spicy. I consider myself to have a pretty high spice tolerance but still found it somewhat hard to handle. The curry was so delicious though that I still finished it all! The grilled chicken was also a standout: perfectly flavored and juicy. The ambiance was very fun and energetic. Looking forward to coming back here someday!

A friend recommended this place and I really liked it! Their corn sum tom is super refreshing and light. I usually don't like steamed fish, but their steamed fish was tasty. 

The best time to go is during happy hour. Their drinks are tasty and somewhat strong. I've never been to Thailand, but I'm assuming their food selection might be as authentic as Thailand? There were more dishes didn't seem too familiar or at least not your typical "pad Thai" and whatever else they serve in Thai restaurants. Overall, it was worth the try. I'd like to come back if I'm ever visiting NY again.

Honestly the food was probably up there with food I had on holiday in Thailand! Really authentic flavors! I loved the chicken wings and the crab curry. I think the steamed fish is a little too tangy and could do with a bit less lime to be perfect but still good. The fried fish is also great!

This place! I heard from so many people as well as instagram vloggers that this is the place to be for thai food! It's hard to get a reservation during the popular lunch/dinner times, we had to reserve about 2 weeks ahead for weekend lunch. Loved the upbeat ambiance bc people seemed to genuinely enjoy this place! The food, omg, how can every dish be so flavorful and amazing? The steamed fish was so flavorful I couldn't let go of any soup left! 10/10, would definitely come again!

i've always wanted to try fish  cheeks because i've heard  such amazing things about their food  AND they have lots of gluten free  options. however, I was left a bit disappointed . the food was fine but I think because my expectations were so high, it fell kind of short. we got the duck  curry , fried fish , and sticky & regular rice  with a side of cabbage . duck  curry  was my favorite and the first few bites of the fried fish  were really good  but it was a bit too oily and dry after a while. good food but I would want to try something else next time!
This place was awesome, warm attentive service and thoughtful delicious food.  The ambiance is democratic. A big bright dining hall. Comfortable to sit for a long time

Thai food on a rainy day in NY hit diffffff

we were seated outdoors in one of those post-pandemic tented areas, and it was really freaking cold outside with the NY winter breeze hitting our poor little Californian souls for at least an hour (the wait was merciless) but it added to the experience i guess cuhs the warm thai food in that little camp-like tent tasted like HOME + HEAVEN LOL it sounds kinda sad that I type it out like that but basically: 

Food was really good. Wait was really long. Kinda pricey. I remember service was good too? Next time, would really like to be seated in doors and come during less busy hours.

Our second time here and we thoroughly enjoyed the food once more. 

- crab curry 
- fried rice salad
-fried fish
-fried chicken wings 
- pork belly 

These were all great options! Service was good and of course a packed restaurant.

One of my favorite Thai spots of all time, though few family and friends have thought it was just average 

Love their wings the most, they sell the seasoning salt for it now! Also great steamed fish rich savory comforting flavors. Just the right amount of spicy on all their dishes. Very fresh ingredients papaya salad also very yummy . Great meal for big groups.

Excellent Thai food, quick & friendly service, and a great place to come with a group! My friends and I arrived at 5pm on a weeknight and it was already pretty crowded, but it only took about 10 minutes to get a table. 

We ordered the Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs, Coconut Crab Curry, and a side of sauteed cabbage. The fish was tender and super flavorful, and the presentation was also lovely - the broth it came in was sooo good that I kept adding it to a side of rice even after we finished the fish. The curry was also delicious - the crab flavor was very mild and I don't think it made a huge difference on the flavor, but the dish as a whole was great. I didn't expect to love the cabbage as much as I did - it was garlicky, tangy, and a great textural complement to the main dishes.

It was happy hour so we ordered cocktails as well. I got the Kafae Cafe, which wasn't my favorite coffee-forward drink but it had an interesting kick. My friend ordered the Tongue & Cheek, which is one of their most popular cocktails and was really good.

Thai food is my favorite and I'm happy to have found another place that I love!

Culinary geniuses. Beyond tasty, vibrant and flavorful. The execution of service with delicious dishes encouraged us to order most of the menu! One plate after the other maintained its  incredible flavor and presentation . Some must haves are the steamed monk fish (don't google photos of the fish it'll scare you into the next realm of consciousness), hot chicken wings (crispy hot and sweet), branzino, sticky rice, crab curry, and mussels. Make reservations in advance. It's a pretty popular spot. Ambiance is warm, inviting and service is solid. You'll have a QR code to see the bill in real time and it gives options to pay in full or split between company easily. Enjoy!

A very Thai inspired restaurant that serves delicious food. 

If you're looking for authentic authentic, this won't be your place. The food is good albeit quite expensive for the portions. It's a big, fun, lively restaurant, but very, very loud! 

The crab fried rice was good. I got a few other dishes and they were all good, but I did feel it was overpriced. 

I'd come back once in a while, but there's other restaurants I love more within the same price bracket. Very friendly service.
Great food. You gotta try their cocktails, too. This type of restaurant is what makes NYC so special (and keeps me broke lol)
A really good experience, everything was delicious and the service was great also, I feel comfortable eating here

Wow what an experience. Some of the best Thai dishes I've had. I can see why this place is always booked out. Great looking restaurant and great food. A fun night here with friends trying out different dishes. The pork cheeks, sticky rice, chicken wings, fried fish, duck curry, Thai tea, and more. Every dish was just spectacular. My buddy kept raving about his visit here previously so I had to get a RESY reservation while in NYC. The vibe is chill but fun. The service was very attentive. And It's def a must try while in the city

Every dish was so salty it was inedible. We ordered the scallops, pork, crab noodles. Seafood quality did not taste fresh. Brought it up to the staff who was not receptive to the feedback and did not do anything about it.
Regret coming here and do not recommend.

Had a quick bite with friends here. I was amazed by their wings and crab FR! The cocktails were tasty and creative too! Relaxing and casual atmosphere, service was to the point! Definitely will be back to try more dish.

Food (5 stars): everything was so tasty here! My favorite is the steamed fish. Very citrusy and refreshing. We also tried the duck curry and the fried rice. Those dishes were all very flavorful. I will definitely be back here.

Service (4 stars): Service was fast and efficient! If you come on a weekday, the wait isn't too long.

The food was fire  
Will be back for the monkfish app and the cuttlefish grilled and spiced to perfection

The lobster tomyum was pretty great but the crab coconut curry took the car. The service was good and the drink cocoba was overrated but the food and the sea food options really tickled the senses , especially for a pescatarian. The ambiance' was cozy but nice for a hole in the wall spot and the greatest secret I discovered after trying to find a table for years is, show up at 9.30pm and they will get you off the waitlist

absolutely delicious food! 

started off with some complimentary prawn crackers and then ordered one appetizer and 2 larger plates and left stuffed!! the zaab wings were a little tricky to eat as the pieces were large but they were seasoned wonderfully. the coconut crab curry is a MUST order - only thing is, I wish there had been more crab pieces. 

drinks were delish & the servers were attentive and very helpful. super cute restaurant - we went for a birthday celebration and had a great time! would recommend :) 

**very heavily seafood based dishes***

Ate here a few weeks ago and still thinking about the food. We had a reservation and ate outside and everything was great, including the service - which can sometimes be spotty outside. Staff was very friendly.
Inside was very nice and cozy. Seems like this place stays pretty busy. We went on a Saturday evening and had no trouble getting a convenient reservation the night before.

The oysters were fresh and clean with a great green sauce that we have been deliberating what's in it since then. Kinda garlic / cilantro / culantro / herbal thing but also some fish sauce / sugar / lime that was really well balanced.

We got the whole branzino and all agreed it was one of the best things we'd had in general. Had the same, or similar, green sauce this time in broth form with a perfectly cooked fish that flaked so nicely. It went very well with the crab fried rice.

Duck curry was wonderful and well spiced, and the chicken wings were awesome. Would elaborate more on those but the branzino stole the show.

We spent about $50 per person including drinks and all left very satisfied. Would recommend.
Finally discovered Fish Cheeks, last month. My god! Crab Curry, Wings and crab fried rice were absolute stunners. Can't wait to go back with a group so I can sample EVERYTHING!

Loved the steamed fish and pork cheeks!

Food was great, no substitutions so make sure you're fine with the menu. Great for a group of friends so you can share items.

This was a rec from one of my best friends. I hate fish and I loved this darn place that I'm actually making fish.
Wow. Service was impeccable and the food... I ate every damn thing,

What a beautiful Thai restaurant.
I will always come back.

New York City is filled with a bunch of average trendy expensive restaurants. This however is NOT that. Fish Cheeks is one of those restaurants you're stunned by the fact that you hadn't tried it earlier. It is truly a phenomenal restaurant. Their crab curry was delicious with the perfect amount of flavor, that you walk out thinking about it. FYI it is spicy so if you don't like spicy be careful. We also got the Branzino and I never realized how much I could love branzino until I had this dish. The broth of the sauce is fantastic. Lastly, the cuttlefish which I've never had before but was also delicious. The stars of the show were the curry and branzino. Will definitely be coming back here to try other dishes.

Was just okay IMO. 

Have heard so many great things about this restaurant but it was quite underwhelming to be honest. 

We got a variety of different apps and entrees and none of them were stand out dishes. They also had a hefty price tag for their small portions. 

The service was also quite slow as the restaurant was fully booked and a line started to form outside. 

Ambiance was busy and loud. Really wanted to love this place but it just didn't hit the mark.

Managed to get a spot at the bar for dinner. Ordered the Kia king and a beer. Kua kling is a rare dish to find at a Thai restaurant and it was completely fire. Spice level was out of this world just how I like it. Extra points to the staff who were prompt, friendly and kind. The vibe is really cool, not too loud also great energy. or just a place to catch up with friends if you love great food.

From the moment you walk in, the aroma of the food greets you..what an amazing experience! I had the grilled cuttlefish and the fried fish, Not too spicy but so full of flavors. 

Our server Justin was so sweet taking time to explain the menu and making sure allergies and dietary restrictions were addressed. Top-notch service from beginning to end. 

I will definitely be back for Happy Hour!

The food is high quality and tastes amazing. The crab curry was great over rice, I just wish there was more. The chicken was really good and seasoned perfectly. The service is great and attentive and the ambiance is lively and fun.
I've visited three times, and each time has been consistently delightful. Everything is delicious and flavorful. Highly recommended without a second thought. Definitely one of my favorites.

I haven't been here since 2020 & literally cried when I had the curry again. It never disappoints, I actually DoorDashed some right now. 
Fish Cheeks can do no wrong, I also tried their new gin martini & tofu dish, 10/10! We never skip their oysters or morning glory. Service is always great, the friendliest staff with the best recommendations, ambience is casual yet cozy. It's a great spot for date or catch up with friends.

In my opinion, Fish Cheeks is worth the hype- I understand why it is so popular, the food was tremendous and just so so good.

Our group of 5 had a reservation (trust me, you will need it, the place fills up fast.)
Did you know they have Happy Hour 7 days a week?! Great deal, as you can get oysters (1/2 dozen for $11, 1 dozen for $21) and the specialty cocktails for $13. They have some intriguing cocktails (classic cocktails with a Thai/Asian twist!)- my favorite was the Tongue & Cheek (fruity and very tasty!)

For food, we got:
Grilled Pork Cheeks
Crab Fried Rice
Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs
Pork Belly Pad Kaprow
Calamari

The Steamed fish is a MUST- fabulous presentation, and so flavorful from the herbs.
Second favorite was the calamari (don't judge... but we ordered seconds of this one!)

Would definitely save this one as a treat or a way to wow an out of town friend.

Vibes through and throughout with amazing service and food. 

Food was perfectly spicy without being overwhelming. My favs were the calamari and the Branzino in that yummy sauce. I seriously wanted to pick up the plate and drink the sauce. Cocktails were tasty!!!!

This has been one of my favorite restaurant for many years. I just took it off my list. The food is still good (not great). The portion size changed to 2/3 of what it use to be and the price have gone up by over 15%. The staff turn quickly and many are less experienced and do not know the food. If you want more manageable noice level sit outside or come for lunch (same menu). The bill app is good in that it divides the bill the way you want but it defaults to 25% tip. Watch out on this.

Love love love this place! 

Was shopping in soho so I decided to stop by to put my name down and was seated in about an hour. 

I wasn't hungry so we only got the coconut crab curry and the Thai steamed fish and they were both soo good! The sauce for the steamed fish was chefs kiss. 

Will be coming back to try other items on the menu!
Super tasty Thai food... bit spicy at times, but worth the adventure. The appetizer chicken wings are a must.

Probably my favorite restaurant we ate at while I was in New York! We ordered the prawn karee, steamed fish, corn salad, cabbage, and wings. Everyone in our party enjoyed the food. The steamed fish is a must get when you're here - the fish is extremely tender and melts in your mouth. The flavors were also incredible. I also really enjoyed the prawn karee - super flavorful and rich so would definitely recommend eating with rice or something to balance it out. Corn salad was super refreshing and extremely fresh. 

Service was great and ambiance was also great. Slightly dim in the main room for a relaxed vibe. Overall would definitely recommend Fish Cheeks - make a reservation beforehand to make life easier!

Had a lovely meal here! Menu had so many options, with the coconut crab curry and the glass noodle dish with crab being my favorites. Cocktails were tasty too. Servers were very knowledgeable with helping us decide on what to order. Would definitely recommend!

Ambiance: we sat outside but their outdoor seating had heaters so it was very comfortable. The inside is very intimate and cute - overall great vibe. 

Service: our waitress was amazing and very attentive. We got seated right away but keep in mind you do have to book a reservation in advance! You might be able to get away with walking in and putting your name down but not sure about the wait. 

Food: now for the star of the show! Their food was absolutely amazing! Every single dish we got was to die for. The crab fried rice, the curry, the corn. I'd absolutely come back here!

The food here is so good! I stopped by with my Thai friends and they approved of all the dishes that we tried. Additionally, Fish Cheeks was so kind to help us serve a dessert with a candle on top to celebrate our friend's birthday. I will definitely be back to try out their other dishes!

Always a must when visiting New York! We couldn't get a reservation and tried our luck as walk-ins: The 30 min wait is def worth it! 

Our server Justin was incredible and offered fantastic suggestions: The Lobster Tom Yum, Steamed Fish and Duck Curry was perfect for the cold weather. 

An amazing experience overall.
Great farm to table upscale Thai experience. Crab fried rice is so good! Service and ambience is great as well.

Fish Cheeks has left me utterly impressed not once, but twice for lunch. The Thai cuisine here is nothing short of amazing. Each visit has been a delightful journey of flavors, leaving me eager for more. I can't recommend Fish Cheeks enough for those seeking an exceptional dining experience. The Zaab wings and curry if you need a recommendation!

The shrimp in 3 crab sauce is one of my favorite dishes in all of NYC - it's tangy (lime), spicy (chili + garlic), fresh (mint), sweet, delicious and an absolute flavor bomb in your mouth. I don't love the addition of bitter gourd to the dish but you can just not eat that part. The coconut crab curry (comes with rice on the side) is also really delicious but the portion is kind of small for the price. It's a little cramped and dark inside but the staff are attentive, friendly, and speedy.

I honestly feel like the more I go to Fish Cheeks the more I'm adamant that it's not only one of the best Thai restaurants in the city but also one of the best restaurants in the city in general.  One of the best HHs, great quality, and fantastic service- what's not to love?  I tried the Zabb wings this time around and they were very good- I definitely recommend ordering it with a side of their homemade sambal.  

A special shout out to Kat (one of the loveliest waitresses I've encountered) and the manager (for arranging for me to take home some house made sambal at a really reasonable price).  I plan on coming back more and visiting their new sister restaurant Bangkok Supper Club when I can snag a reservation :).
Great dinner and service. We were seated at table 23 on 11/17/23 at 7pm and our server was phenomenal! She was great. I recommend the curries!

Good, but expensive.

My friend has been recommending this place and thinks it's the best steamed fish dish in the city. I think it's super awesome that the fish comes de-boned and the sauce has good flavor. Personally I'm not a huge cilantro fan but this was still a good dish.

The pork cheek, prawns in curry sauce, and morning glory veggies were all good too and we got a side of sticky rice and normal rice to share between 3 of us.

The service and ambiance is nice, they told us about an hour wait on a Sunday night and it ended up being 30 mins. Recommend to try but I probably  wouldn't come back here consistently.

Such a great meal at Fish Cheeks - and our server Timothy only made it more enjoyable! He was so knowledgeable about the menu and recommended the steamed fish which is one of the most delicious things I've ever tried! Overall one of the best service experiences I've had in New York - thank you, Tim!

WOW what a meal! This was definitely one of the tastiest meals I've had in a long time, and easily a perfect 10/10 dining experience.

We were able to snag a table with only about a 45 min wait, as we didn't have a reservation. We sat on the patio, which had a heater and was covered with clear plastic wrapping.

For small plates, we had:
-Grilled pork cheeks - these were perfectly tender, and I love the sauce that it came with (though I wish it came with more)
-Nam Prik Goong Siap - this was definitely the most interesting dish we ordered - the relish was so delicious and flavorful, all the vegetables were crisp and unique, which made this a REALLY interesting dish

For large plates, we had:
-Coconut Crab Curry - this curry was perfectly seasoned, and the crab was delicious. This is definitely a dish you will want to share, and it went perfectly with the Khua Kling plate we also ordered
-Khua Kling - wow, this dish is Thai spicy and the heat really builds. At first you taste the deliciously seasoned short rib, and slowly the heat gets more intense and (if you like spicy food) leaves you feeling so satisfied. This paired so well with the coconut crab curry, as it helped balance out the heat and brought in some additional flavors.
-Crab Fried Rice - this was really good as well, definitely above average for fried rice
-Pork Belly Pad Kaprow - this pork was delicious, and also above average for a pork dish. This wasn't my favorite dish, and there were a couple pieces that were too rough to eat, but most of it was really delicious.

Overall the food was just hit after hit, and I would love to try every item on the menu. For me the Khua Kling is a must get if you like spicy food, and the Nam Prik Goong Siap is a must get if you want something really unique.

10/10 would go back and would recommend.

Ok this is in no way my favorite Thai place. The apps are great and the menu changes. Most of the food here is great except for the crab noodle dish. Dry crab that feels like you're eating dried play dough. The oysters are delicious and the cabbage wrap is also great. From the entrees the curry is probably the best thing to eat. The prices are interior and service are decent. The price is a little high but that's normal for Manhattan. It's a decent place for a quick bite. But again in no way my favorite. As always happy hunting

Obsessed. Everything we ordered was delicious and I would order it all again (except for the poached monkfish--that was bland and whatever)! The zabb wings are fire. So good. Love the seasoning, crispy skin, and juicy chicken. Shrimp in 3 crab sauce is delicious. Somtum corn salad looks and sounds simple but is packed with flavor and so light and refreshing. Crispy rice salad and pork is amazing. Grilled pork cheeks are perfect balance of flavors. The coconut crab curry and rawaaeng curry (duck) are both incredible--I preferred the duck but my friend preferred the crab. The pork belly pad kaprow was a personal fave. Soooo good. Drinks were amazing too. I literally can not wait to come back.
Excellent place if you need amazing food with rich flavor. A must go neighborhood spot
Great food great service  entrees and appetizers all excellent on the menu. Best to go with a group to try everything

overall 3.9/5 but i would come back to try the rest of the menu 

service
host - 2/5 i had to talk to the person in the host stand first. they saw me walk in and continued on their tab without greeting. they were general friendly but informed me i couldn't sit until my guest came, but that my table was waiting and i had to be up at 7:30. why not just let me sit then? had to wait outside on their patio (thankfully heated) 

server - fine. did minimum but nothing outstanding 3.5/5
bathroom- clean but there are only two. pee before you come or you may have to wait in a long line. there is hand sanitizer placed outside for clean hands. 

food

must get "punch drunk love" cocktail. sweet and smooth and makes you giggle 10/10

starts with comp shrimp chips with dip. delightfully done. sauce is amazing. there's way to little for the amount of shrimp chips they give you 3.8/5

pork cheeks - thinly sliced and fatty but like in the best way. sauce is tangy and spicy but with no heat. wish it was served with a knife or chopsticks 4.5/5

prawns - sauce is mild but flavorful. shrimps are huge and shell on (you've been warned). should be served with more than one rice if all plates are to share 4.2/5

crab curry - sauce is spicy and has an amazing linger. even though crab is soft and melts in your mouth it's overpowered by the sauce. it could be tofu and you may not notice the difference. 3.7/5

dessert - was fine. rice was better than ice cream. skip 2/5

One of the hardest places to get a reservation in the City. I made a reservation about a month beforehand after hearing all the raving reviews. We were seated promptly and was glad we came slightly before the end of happy hour so that we can get the last bit of the discounts.

- Coconut Crab Curry - I know that this is their most famous dish but I was not a fan. There weren't any crab in the mixture and for it to be $30 with no meat was kind of a lot. The curry was extremely spicy to the point that it numbed out all the other flavors. Would not recommend.
- Prawn Karee - I'm not going to lie, I think Soothr does it better. Don't get me wrong, the dish was still very good but I think Soothr's had a richness that Fish Cheek's didn't. The prawns were very fresh which I appreciated although they gave us only 3 completely unshelled prawns whereas at Soothr, they give you 10 shelled prawns.
- Grilled Pork Cheeks - This dish itself is worth 10 stars. By far, the best tasting dish and because this was our appetizer, I was extremely excited for the rest of the dishes although to no avail. The pork was extremely tender and I liked the balance of fat and meat all drenched up in a vinegar based jeaw sauce. The crispiness of the pork on the sides was the perfect compliment. I genuinely couldn't be more in love and I don't even like pork that much. I wasn't originally going to come back to Fish Cheeks, but this dish gave me hope that I just had not yet found what the most amazing entrees on the menu.
- Tongue & Cheek - Wasn't the biggest fan of this cocktail as it didn't taste like much although I did appreciate the sesame flavors on the top. I wish I had gotten the Punch Drunk Love instead, which my friend got, as it was one of the best cocktails I've ever had with the coconut and subtle pandan flavor.
- Ice Cream Bo Lan - I wasn't a big fan of this dessert although I did like the hot and cold mixture. The ice cream did not taste like jackfruit, it tasted like vanilla which was disappointing. I will say that it was extremely smart they used sticky rice as who knew ice cream and sticky rice would go so well together. Not a fan of the mung bean chunks as they were very hard, tasted like dried fruit in an otherwise soft mixture.

Other than the Punch Drunk Love cocktail and the Grilled Pork Cheeks, everything else was mediocre. But for the Pork Cheeks alone, I have to give it +1 star and maybe another try at Fish Cheeks because that dish was actually heavenly. But at the end of the day, if I had to choose between Fish Cheeks and Soothr, I would choose Soothr. Also, the servers took away some of our dishes before we were done :/
The crab curry was something different than what I usually order, but it tasted so good. I'm happy I tried it and came out to support a restaurant I've always walked past.

Our friend brought us to this restaurant during our recent visit to NY, and we were taking a much needed break from 99c pizzas :) Wow! The dishes at this place reminded me of those days when I used to visit my friends in Bangkok and they would bring me to these out of the way restaurants where they served totally non-typical Thai food.....that was out-of-this-world delicious! Well, this is one of those such places.

My first impression when arriving at this place was, it looked like a typical older, casual, regular looking Thai restaurant along the street. But when we all entered, I thought to myself, ok, this is not the decor for a typical Thai restaurant....and this is when I became excited to check out their menu. It's actually a decent and spacious sized, nicely decorated, casual ambiance type restaurant....a little more upscale casual than most Thai restaurants I have been to.

As for the menu, everything looked and sounded absolutely amazing! Nothing sounded typically Thai.....more like a chef's nouveau rendition of some of the best Thai style dishes that are hard to find even in Thailand.

So, honestly, we had a late breakfast and weren't all that hungry. We started out ordering just three dishes and we thought that would be enough, but that grew to five dishes shortly after the food started coming out as we were liking what we were seeing and tasting.

So, we ordered the Coconut Crab Curry, Crab Aob Woonsen.....(glass noodles with baked jumbo crab claws and meat), Pork Cheeks....(marinated in fish sauce, served with jeaw sauce), Prawn Karee (basically, prawn curry), Stir Fried Cabbage (with garlic). All these dishes are actually meant to be eaten with rice....and their rice was so perfectly steaming hot, moist, and fluffy....and went so so well with all the curry sauces.

Some of our group thought the curry dishes were a bit salty, but I thought all the dishes were perfectly prepared, the ingredients were incredibly fresh, the flavors and textures were amazingly delicious, and an absolute favorite dish during this meal experience would be hard to pinpont as everything was so good and satisfying. My only issues were that the we were told by our server that the kitchen refused our request to reduce the salt in their cooking, no substitutions whatsoever would be entertained, and that you had to pay extra for the rice ($3 a bowl) and $1.50 for any extra sauces you requested.....like the Prik Nam Plaa, Chili sauce, and Nahm Jim Seafood sauces....all $1.50 extra for each.

Service was ok.....sometimes nice, friendly, and helpful.....other times, she seemed cold, frustrated, and annoyed that we kept calling her attention. Also, the dishes here are not cheap at all, but other than that, food is amazing and not easy to find anywhere else. A must try!!!

Upon stepping into Fish Cheeks on Bond Street, we were immediately greeted by the delightful aromas of the Thai kitchen. This is a rare and promising occurrence in Manhattan, where many restaurants invest heavily in powerful ventilation systems that eliminate any cooking odors, the good with the bad, even in those with open kitchens.

Our group of six, including some who have lived in Thailand for several years, enjoyed a wide array of dishes, all of which were simply outstanding. While savoring our meal, we discovered another remarkable aspect of Fish Cheeks - their food is so authentically Thai that it transports you to Thailand itself.

Our feast included lobster Tom Yum in a flavorful broth (served in a round serving pot heated by a burning candle), steamed Bronzino with Thai herbs in a fragrant broth, served in an oval warming pot, crispy fried Bronzino, noodles with crab, coconut crab curry, flavorful crab fried rice, jasmine rice, satisfying warm sticky rice served in a rattan basket,  Som Tum corn ribs salad, and more. The seafood was exceptionally fresh. The fish was elegantly served in a special Thai oval fish pot, heated with a burning candle at the bottom, lying in an excellent broth, gently warmed by the live fire. The steamed fish was so tender that it practically melted in our mouths, complemented by the excellent warm broth that infused the fish with flavor. We concluded our meal with the sole dessert option available - an ice cream on sticky rice, just as it is traditionally served in Thailand. This delighted our friends who had spent time in Thailand, making them even happier. We all departed  from Fish Cheeks in a good mood.  

I highly recommend this restaurant for an authentic Thai dining experience.

Fish Cheeks is arguably one of the best Thai restaurants I have ever eaten at and I've been to Thailand. I was honestly a little skeptical at first because I hold a high bar for Thai food, but this place did not disappoint. I came here for a team dinner and there were so many things that were ordered, but I wasn't able to try everything because most of the dishes had shellfish in them (I am allergic).

My 3 favorite things were: 
-Corn Salad: Ok hear me out. This salad was so delicious! Sweet corn, spicy chilis, and tossed in this amazing fish sauce! 
-Zobb Wings are a must! Perfectly flavored, crispy, and purely delicious! I could have finished that plate all by myself.
-Steamed Fish is probably the show stopper here. It's hard to get it wrong, but when you get it right, its amazing. And this fish was amazing! I am happy that my team didn't eat a lot of fish so I practically ate the entire thing by myself.

This place is now on my list of places I need to come back to when I am in NYC!

Me and my husband came here for a late night dinner. The food here is so good and flavorful. Once you make reservations here you are seated and served quickly. I got the crab stir fry 10/10 and my husband got the coconut curry crab 10/10.

This place is cute and the chicken wings are some of the best I've ever had. The dry rub on them was just the perfect amount of spicy. The service was also incredible- our waiter was able to recommend some great drink and food options. Giving 4 stars because the pork dish we got tasted gummy and was not my favorite. However, I would come back again if only for the chicken wings.

Felt too pricey for what we got. The portions were small considering how expensive they were. Everything was just a touch too salty. Definitely seemed overpriced for food that didn't blow my mind. But the service was good, attentive waitress. They only have one bathroom which sucked because lines got long. Ambiance was busy and lighting was a bit dim. 

Food really was just meh and I really wanted to like it more.

Has been on my list to go for awhile but never have. Tried it today with some friends. Dishes are expensive for what they were. They are pretty small. Found the menu to be somewhat limited. Would pass on pork belly  very salty. Duck curry and crab friend were okay but definitely not amazing. Overall okay but not something I'd have again!

My favorite was definitely the Zabb Wings. I still think about them and want to go back even just for the wings. Prepare to spend at least $30 per person as plates to share are a bit on the pricer side. My least favorite was the Pork Belly Pad Kaprow because it was too hard to chew. The Coconut Crab Curry was quite spicy and definitely a must try. The Crab Fried Rice and Crab AOB Woonsen were just like any rice and noodle dish, safe options. The Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs was also tasty. Service was quite quick! There is seating outside and inside the restaurant. Make sure to make a reservation, or there will be a long wait.

Food (5/5): Ordered the Thai iced tea which was delicious although steep in price. We also got a bunch of dishes for friend's bday. This included the fried fish, steamed fish, fried chicken, coconut curry, crab fried rice, tiger prawn curry, and sticky rice ice cream. All the dishes were super delicious!

Service (5/5): Food came reasonably fast and the staff were friendly. From the initial greeting to the service we had no issues.

Ambiance (4/5): Solid ambiance with plenty of indoor and outdoor seating. They have wooden chairs that look handcrafted. The roof tiles and some walls were in the design of fish scales. Overall a nicely decorated place with good ambiance.

we got lucky last minute reservation for 3 from  Amex concierge service. Casual ambience with strong fish odor and curry smell as I walked in checking all the tables with colorful dishes and pretty drinks .
Food was amazing. We have crab fried rice, crab curry, mussels with lemongrass and it's amazing lime cilantro sauce , stone crab with vermicelli and finally the best dish : sticky rice rice with pandan ice cream. So good !! Gotta try ! Highly recommended!
Amazing food. We loved everything we ordered- I don't think you can make a wrong choice. And a beautiful neighborhood spot!

Been wanting to try this place for so long! I heard so many good things. Came in with a friend on a Saturday night. It was just two of us and we were seated right away at an indoor table.

5/5 Coconut crab curry - amazing flavor. Wish there was a little more crab chunks but overall such a great tasting dish. Goes so well on top of rice

5/5 Steamed fish with thai herbs - amazing sauce that goes great with rice. The fish was steamed perfectly with so much flavor in each bite. Strong lime and cilantro presence which i love. Only qualm is that it wasnt boneless but thats very common in fish dishes. 

5/5 the only pad thai on the menu - very unique drink! It was pretty well balanced. I could taste most of the ingredients. I thought it might be odd but i actually enjoyed this quite a bit. Still cant believe they used fish sauce in a drink and it worked. I'd come back just to get this again

Great food and drinks. The only issue i had was that our table wobbled a little and that it was too loud to chat properly inside. We spoke loudly even though the table was small and we were right across from each other. Would return for the food though. I would recommend making a reservation if you can. I think we just got lucky walking in that night though there was another table 2 person table open the entire we were there.

We arrived way earlier than out reservations so we had to wait a bit. She said 30 mins but it was 10 min. Service is good and the food was delicious. Highly recommend the fried fish and the crab fried rice. Lots of chunky crab meat and great flavors. The fried fish was fried perfectly and the herbs salad really added a lot of flavors. Only complaint I have is that the crab fried rice came out 10 mins after the fish and chicken dish we ordered. Could've just been a glitch in the kitchen or maybe the fried rice takes longer. But anyways I can't wait to come back and try the other dishes.

Struck out many a time attempting to eat dinner here but lunch reservations were a cinch. I arrived here directly from the pulmonologist with a stack of print outs which included my insurance card. I kindly asked the waitress to make sure things didn't get too spicy here as I didn't want to go back to the hospital so soon. The overall impression was that Fish Cheeks is worthy of the hype with a menu that can be ordered from four or even five times before you feel you've explored it all. Mussels and pork belly were excellent, trout was a bit bland but still tasty.

The food is great. They have various starters and main dishes. The drinks menu has cocktails and mocktails, delicious. Service is great, all the staff is very friendly and attentive. The ambiance is nice, the food was amazing, highly recommend.

If you're looking for flavor, fun, and fiery foods, come to Fish Cheeks and you will NOT be disappointed. There is something so immensely welcoming and homey about the food here (and not just because they're shareable plates). The Zabb Wings have the perfect kick for spice-lovers, and the green curry is loaded with the perfect balance of creamy and savory flavors. You know they're good at what they do (and know it too) when the menu says "no substitutions or modifications".

Probably one of the best thai food i had in a while. Must gets are the thai steamed fish and the wings. The wings are prob the best i ever. The fry and spice are spot on. The fish hella hits too, cooked in a tom yum liked sauce taht was previously steamed. Cheer!
Been there twice from out of town, every dish I have ever tried was good. Will definitely visit again once I'm in NYC again!

Came here with reservations for two around 7:30pm on a Saturday and it was popping. I'd definitely try to book ahead of time. 

There's a variety of table sizes, as well as seats at the bar. Starting off with some minor annoyances, our table was right next to another, and the gap was so small that someone trying to squeeze into that table ended up bumping into my water despite me moving it from the edge.

We were also seated at the table right next to the door, which ended up being a bit of a nuisance. There's a set of curtains that opens from the middle, but people would come through the side, and unwittingly right into our table. Additionally, we could feel the cold breeze from outside throughout our meal. 

Aside from that, we really enjoyed the food. The two of us got the Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce, Crispy Rice Salad & Pork, and Isan Style Grilled Chicken. The first two were spicy, but not in a way that made them any less tasty. The grilled chicken came with two sauces that were nice and tangy, but had great flavor on its own.

Overall we enjoyed our meal, and appreciated the good service, but in the future we would try to avoid the table right by the door.

Finally had the chance to try this place. The crab fried rice is a must! The two sauces that come with it complement it so so well, I needed more. It also came with a lot of crab. We also got the Zabb wings which was well seasoned. I don't recommend the Khua Kling if you cannot do spicy. It was ground short rib so the meat was dry and with the spice I couldn't continue eating it after one bite. The tongue & cheek cocktail is good for anyone who prefers a more fruity light drink but I would say it is still strong.

Great ambiance. DELICIOUS food. Fun happy hour.  We had oysters as an appetizer (so yummy & that sauce they serve it with... delicious). Then had both the duck & crab curry which were  so so yummy! Want to come back & try alll the things! 

*We went for lunch and were lucky to not have a reservation & got sat right away*

Fish cheeks has been on my list for awhile and we finally got a chance to try it. Yeah the food was a 4/5 but the hype around this place made it a 3/5.

It was good but didn't feel special but I'm thinking maybe cos it's overhyped. Expect sort of a little more refined family style dishes. Delicious but nothing out of the ordinary.

We had the pork cheek, chicken wings, prawn curry, steamed fish, crab fried rice, morning glory and a side of sticky rice. The fish, pork and wings were my favorites. The fish was boneless! So good job whoever has to fillet an entire fish back there.

Staff were over attentive. Like they need to clear every dish the moment it's done. Kinda annoying.

I'll probably not be back but Bangkok supper club is on the list

Did takeout from here and although I cannot speak to the service and vibe of the restaurant, I can say that the quality was excellent. The portions were large so it is not ideal for a solo diner, but if you are two people looking for somewhere delicious, this is your place! I already have my reservation to go back and eat in person next time. We ordered the Isan Style Grilled Chicken and Crispy Rice Salad & Pork. The chicken was half of a full chicken and was as tender and juicy as chicken can get. The crispy rice salad was unlike anything I had ever tried before and  I was pleasantly surprised.

wow. A whole experience! We went for happy hour, had to wait a few for a table, and were glad we did. The cocktails were bar none some of the best we have ever had. We ordered oysters and had a few other apps. The manager came over and explained the dishes to us in such detail and with such enthusiasm, I've really never experienced that sort of pride in food/a restaurant. I cannot wait to go back and try more of the menu! Super hip spot.

I usually wait to visit a place twice before reviewing. But this place was phenomenal. Ambiance is laid back and relaxed. Friendly service and flavorful explosions dish after dish. The fried fish was perfection. The curry with the duck breast was also perfectly executed. I left feeling full and satisfied without being weighed down. A hit from start to finish. ENJOY!!!

Everything here was so good. 

The cocktails (get the lychee - all drinks are a good mix of flavorful and strong)

The oysters

The chicken wings 

The glass noodles with crab meat 

The raw shrimp app 

The steamed fish 

Can't go wrong here!

A thai place without pad thai? Yes and you will be thankful for it because there are so many wide variety of options. Every time I go to a Thai restaurant, I get the same dishes, but Fish Cheeks brings me on a new journey.

We got the crab fried rice and steamed fish with thai herbs. They were not stingy with the crab. Every spoonful of rice, was crab. We would pour Prik Nam Pla all over the rice and it would soak up the spices and fish sauce. It is an acidic touch to season the dish even more!

The steamed fish with thai herbs was out of the world. The chili lime broth still makes me water till now. It's acidity is within every flake of the fish. I could not stop eating it with the soup. The fish was so soft and it would melt in our mouths. 

As we approached, end of happy hour, staff made sure we got our last round of drinks. We were also worried about the spice levels but they helped us understand how spicy the meals were using their knowledge on korean food (what I usually eat).

This is a partial review given I had only three dishes. Conclusion is FC is good, but I don't quite understand the hype even if I accept that I probably need a second visit to try different things. The chicken wings are interesting, but I found them too amped with salt and some sort of lime acid powder (possibly a mix of citric and ascorbic acid powder). The crab curry is good, but no, not to die for and the crab content is small relative to the curry. The morning glory was authentic and good; I appreciated the fermented soy beans.
This place is always poppin' with energy from guests and the team. Really delicious food and drinks with a bright fun vibe. Try their happy hour, stay for the full dinner experience.

This place is such a great spot for Thai seafood. The service here is seriously so good and they even refilled my hydroflask with ice! They have really nice outdoor seating but the inside is also decorated very nicely. I'll rate the foods down below.

Manila Clams (3/5) - Honestly, these clams weren't that great. It had good flavor but for the price, it was not that great. 
Oysters (4/5) - They had some fried shallots and some sauces for the oysters which made it super good. I got these for happy hour and probably would've got more if I didn't have the rest of the other items to eat. 
Coconut Crab Curry (4.8/5) - If they had a bigger portion of this for the same price, it would be a 6/5. This is absolutely delicious, it had nice spice and was creamy. I didn't taste much of the crab but it was nice and light with a lot of flavor.
Steamed Fish with Thai herbs (4.7/5) - So damn good. It's like a nice soft fish in a sour soup (Canh Chua for my Vietnamese people). Just so nice, I don't even think there were bones in that either.
Calamari (3/5) - It was okay, but I would never get that again. Such a small portion and that wasn't even the calamari I was expecting. I was expecting some rings and barely tasted any squid.
Thai Tea (5/5) - I would 100% get this if you're here, it just tastes like the classic thai tea flavor. Good tea flavor with the mixture of the milk. I wish they offered refills on this because if they did, I'd be drinking 3 cups of this.

Overall, I think this place deserves a 4/5 stars despite the good food reviews. I just think that their portions are way too small for the amount they're charging. If they keep the prices the same and made the portions just a bit bigger, it would be a 5/5 for me. That's my only critique of this place.

Really great atmosphere, but a little crowded and our table was close to the door so there were a lot of people moving around us. We didn't have a reservation but only had to wait 10-15 minutes for a table for 2. The service was great and they were so accommodating with gluten allergies -- they have a separate gluten free menu and the server was very knowledgeable about which dishes were safe from cross contamination as well. We ordered the Nam Prik Goong Siap appetizer which was really interesting and delicious, the Coconut Crab Curry, and the Rawaaeng Curry. The Coconut Crab Curry was delicious but seriously spicy! Not for the faint of heart. The Rawaaeng Curry was our favorite. We also had the Thai Iced Tea and Coco Bah which were both very yummy and helped with the spice level. The Coco Bah was like a pina colada with orange juice. Definitely would go back to try some of the other dishes, especially the whole steamed branzino and the dessert!

Fish Cheeks is my favorite restaurant in NYC (at least all you need to know is it's rated the highest on my Beli). Their coconut crab curry has the perfect level of spiciness and I love the blend of spices and creaminess in the curry. Their steamed fish with herbs is also delicious, the fish perfectly tender, but refreshing with the herbs and citrus. I would also definitely recommend getting their oysters, especially during Happy Hour, because the sauce they pair with the oysters is amazing. It really elevates the oysters with the tanginess and the oysters are always fresh. Be careful of the khua kling if you have a low spice tolerance; it tasted amazing but our entire party was drinking cups of water to water down the spiciness.

To try multiple dishes at Fish Cheeks, this is a great place to go with friends or a bigger group and to share family style. With how popular this place is, I would recommend getting a reservation, but it is possible to do a walk in. I was lucky enough to get an outside seating for 6 once, but I made sure to get reservations each time I went after.

I heard a lot about this place and was definitely really hype to try it out. I would definitely recommend making a reservation before you go. The service was good and fast. They had a lot of recommendations. They had both outdoor seating and indoor seating. 

1. Crispy Rice Salad and Pork (8/10): This was the best thing we had there. It paired nicely with the cabbage and had really good flavor. However, it was pricy for the amount that you get.
