2. Coconut Crab Curry (7/10): I was really excited for this dish but was disappointed. The portions were small and there was very little crab meat. The flavor was a bit bland but was a nice topping on the rice.
3. Fried Fish with Garden Herb Salad (7/10): Like the other ones the portion is small and it was pretty sour. The pineapple was a nice touch but was not wowed by it. 
4. Tongue and Cheek, Spicy Mango, Panang Negroni (7/10): These drinks were on the stronger side. If you like the taste of alcohol I would recommend but if not these might not be it for you.
5. Pandan Lemongrass Iced Tea, Butterfly Pea Flower Limeade (6/10): These non-alcoholic drinks were underwhelming. They tasted like water and not much else. 
6. Calamari (6/10): I don't remember what this was on the menu but it was no unique and did not stand out. It wasn't bad but it wasn't good.

Walked in on a Monday and got seated immediately at the bar; the service was great and we ordered the crab curry and the crab fried rice. The curry was spicier than I thought but had amazing flavor, and the fried rice was so full of flavor, especially with the green and fish sauce they gave. It is a bit on the pricier end but definitely worth the quality. The only thing is that their menu isn't like typical Thai spots with the classic pad see ew and pad Thai selections.
Solid Thai food! The dishes have some decent spice to it, which is a plus. The steamed fish that comes with all the herbs is really good and packed with flavor.

Great tasty fresh food, service was attentive and friendly also helpful in our decision making (the whole fish was excellent) and the space is charming. We sat at the big round table by the window and we were very comfortable. They were crowded but everyone, staff and diners, looked relaxed.

Fish Cheeks is a place that I've been recommended many times, and I have been once in the past. I went back again earlier this year in 2023 and I feel like the quality has dropped a lot. 

TL;DR: portions are small, but taste is good (honestly not bad, but not amazing)

Ordered:
* Crab Fried Rice
* Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs
* Lobster Plaa

Food: 3/5

Food was not bad, but not amazing. We ordered the lobster plaa, steamed fish, and the crab fried rice.

The crab fried rice was pretty good, but not outstanding. There were many places that I could have gotten as good, if not better, of a crab fried rice from. 

For the steamed fish with thai herbs, I felt that the fish was a bit dry, and the herbs and the broth did not really enhance the flavor of the fish. Additionally, the portion was surprisingly small for a $40 dish. 

The lobster plaa was the best thing we ordered. However, the lobster only came with several bites of meat, which hardly justified the $30 price tag. The lobster was quite tasty, but nothing outstanding. Honestly, I could have gotten much more lobster or a better quality lobster from a seafood restaurant.

Service: 2/5

The waitstaff was not rude, but was pretty insistent on us ordering two appetizers for two people in addition to the two entrees, which we did not listen to. Additionally, the waitress was not very present throughout, and we ran out of water several times, and had to wait a while before being able to flag our waitress down to get more water.


Atmosphere: 4/5

The restaurant is very clean. However, it didn't really have a "date" vibe to it, and it definitely did not seem like we were paying for the atmosphere of the restaurant.


Overall: 3/5

Probably would not come back. This place is very over-priced, and the food is not bad, but not outstanding. Additionally, the portions are surprisingly small.

I wish I could give this place more than five stars! This is definitely the best restaurant I've tried in NYC so far. Everything was SO flavorful. Me and my friend split the chicken wings, crab fried rice, and steamed fish -- I can't even choose a favorite, they were all 11/10. Service was quick, the waiter was happy to answer any questions we had, and the ambiance is super cute both inside and outside. I have a couple friends visiting from out of town next week, and this will be the first place I'll take them to!

Steamed fish okay v
Zabb chicken wings - you Dian gan
Oren karee you Dian xian -
Crab fried rice -x 
Thai iced tea v

First time trying a place that specializes in Thai seafood and it was so so good!!! The fish was sooo tender and flaky and they de-boned it! Also got the crab fried rice, pork jeow, and prawn curry. The pork was sooo tender and the crust was delicious!! Definitely get a side of rice for the curry - the sauce is pretty salty but perfect with rice!

We also decided to try the Thai liquor. I liked the lemon grass chaser way more than the alcohol haha, but it was still fun for the group to try! Highly rec this place!!!

The food was good but portions small for one person. 
We had 4 prawns in the shell and crab fried rice. It was enough for one , barely two people. Bill came to 60

This was the first Thai restaurant ever been to that didn't have any variety of pad Thai, or most the typical Thai dishes.

We were seated outside, which extended into the street. not ideal having cars pass by your table 4 feet away while you eat but whatever.

Waitress kept insisting to get two appetizers. She was borderline obnoxious and argumentative, titled and rude. She waited for my friend to get back and grilled him too. If it wasn't pouring rain we would have just walked away.

Bathroom sink handles were broken it was just continuously blasting hot water

Good food if you're ok overpaying and small portions.

This was truly an awesome place with terrific food and fantastic service!! Clement, our server, recommended excellent dishes and was so kind, sweet and informed that our overall experience was significantly enhanced by her. Go for the happy hour drinks and oysters and the seafood is fresh and tasty. Christina, the manager, checked in on us and made sure everything was going well and then asked to stay for their 7th anniversary party. Cecil totally rocked with the drinks. We completely understand why this restaurant is going so strong after 7 years and look forward to trying out their Supper Club that will soon open. Thanks everyone -- we had a wonderful experience and can't wait to go back!

This place lives up to the hype! Everything was super delicious, the staff was attentive, and the crab fried rice was devoured in minutes. The chicken wings are a must try here! One of my all time favourites.
Really decent happy hour deals with well priced drinks and $1.5 oysters. On the mains, the Tom yum, pork belly, and steamed fish were super good! The Thai chilis added hella heat but was oh so good.

This place brooooo? OH, my gooood. This truly fills a craving in my heart simply because it's just that good good Thai food for real. Please try the fried fish when you got the time.

Peep that double oyster action in the pic

Everything utterly delicious and you get to even buy some seasonings! 

Our waiter Gabe was so kind and informative on what to order.

Make a reservation in advance!

Had a weekday dinner reservation for two people. There was a steady stream of people even during the weekday, so I definitely recommend making a reso. I know this place has a lot of hype - overall I thought it was good and worth checking out. I would come back just for the steamed fish. Also, for those who can't do spicy (like me) there are plenty of options that are clearly marked. 

Ambiance / Service: honestly, nothing too notable, but it's laid back and cozy. Service was great as well. My only qualm is that there were flies buzzing around inside that we had to constantly shoo away from the food. 

Food: I had heard that this place was known for spicy food, so I was a bit worried since I have a horrible spice tolerance. However, food is very clearly marked and there are a lot of options. Family style is the way to go. For two people we ordered the below (it was too much food - should've ordered one less entree):

-Somtum Corn Salad: fresh and light. But nothing notable. I probably wouldn't order again. 

-Crab Fried Rice: delicious. Would 100% order again. It looks super basic in the photo, but it was sooo good. Sometimes fried rice can be pretty bland, but this had such good flavor. 

-Steamed Fish: THIS IS A MUST! I was hesitant at first because I don't love branzino, but you can't go here and not get this dish. It's well worth the $40. Soooo flavorful and so tender. Has a citrusy, tamarind, garlic broth that is delicious. I've never had something like this before. 

-Isan Style Grilled Chicken: chicken was cooked perfectly - charred on the outside, but juicy. However, it was a little bland, especially compared to the fish and rice. The sauces are key. Based on the other entrees we got, I wouldn't order again.

I've visited Fish Cheeks twice at this point. My first visit was ruined by the extremely rude hostess thus I didn't write a review, fearing it might have been bias from that interaction. 

A co-worker suggested we stop by for dinner a couple days ago and I reluctantly agreed. Once again, the hostess gave us really bad attitude when we said we didn't have a reservation. Outlandishly told us the wait for an inside table would be an hour and a half...which luckily ended up only being a 15 minute wait. 

Any ways, let's talk about the food. Just like last time, EVERYTHING is doused in fish sauce. I get the restaurant has the name "FISH" in it but must my grilled chicken  really taste like chicken of the sea? That distinct taste of fish sauce is enjoyable at small doses... when everything is doused in it, it just feels like they're trying to hide the freshness of the ingredients. 

Some of these prices are also pretty outrageous. $40 for a steamed branzino with some lemon grass...who's bothered about that! 

I really wanted to like Fish Cheeks...but this place is just NOT THAT GIRL. If you want Thai food, I recommend going to Thai Villa in union square. At least the hostesses, servers and staff members are polite and happy to serve you. Price point is much more fair in my opinion as well.

Fantastic Thai restaurant in the Village. They specialize in seafood (not a surprise given the name). Everyone should get the coconut crab curry - it's spicy, the seasoning in the curry is spot on and the crab meat is incredibly tender and juicy. We also ordered the somtum corn salad which is basically summer in a bowl, and it's got this amalgamation of all sorts of different flavors and textures (spicy, sour, sweet, crunchy, juicy) that works super well. The cocktails here are delicious too - every drink utilizes southeast Asian flavors to great effect and pairs great with the food. Prices here are on the high side but that seems to be the case with all restaurants these days.
It was really good. The food was great! Very tasty. The service was great and I would definitely go back. I didn't take pictures, but the wings were amazing and the corn salad, yummmmm!!!

~ Lobster Plaa (5/5) ~
It's a refreshing and complex flavoured dish, love it to bits! The portion is surprisingly good, there are a lot of lobster meat, felt like it's more then half of the lobster! The meat is fresh, tender and bouncy. The coconut galangal sauce is very light and citrusy, doesn't overpower the lobster at all. It taste fantastic with Thai basil, garlic, shallot, mint, lemongrass!

~ Prawn Karee (3.5/5) ~
This curry is a bit too watery, but flavour is great though. Curry powder and soft scrambled egg are a match in heaven. The Prawn tasted fresh and bouncy, but perhaps a tad bit overcooked? The shell is a bit difficult to remove. Slightly disappointed in this, it could have been really good.  

Will I be back? Yes
I love a seafood based Thai resto, would love to come back and try other dishes!
Foods were awesome, pig's cheeks and branzino in lime juices are delicious. Great services, ambiance is casual, needs bigger restroom that the only issues.

First time having thai food again in the city after many years and this DID NOT DISAPPOINT. We got the fried fish, the morning glory vegetables and the crab fried rice. There was something just so fresh with the crab, it was really immaculately done. 

The fish dish was amazing; heard the regular fish was even better but I was more than satisfied with the fried version. Stayed crispy the entire meal and the dipping sauce was a great compliment. The perfect bite would be rice on the bottom, morning glory in the middle, then fish on the top. 

Sat outside so can't speak to the ambiance but it looked nice from outside

Too much fish sauce - everything has a slightly similar background taste because of it. Also they were out of Singha beer, sparkling water, bronzino and broiled macherel. The waitress kept waiting until we asked for the dish to say they were out of it, which was annoying. We had the calamari - would not repeat; the crab fried rice - good and would repeat, and the shrimp kampow good, would not repeat. Not sure what all the hype is about. Plus, it is not cheap at all, so not really a causal dinner out. Lastly it was 90 and humid out today, and indoors there was not enough air circulation or air conditioning for a day like today. Would not recommend, and sadly, would not return.

Overpriced but food and service was good. Some dishes too spicy for my guests but overall I liked it a lot. Not much ambiance but it was clean and sort of sterile. Creatively spiced dishes. Seems to have a young crowd but most new places do.

a great place for lunch. i got crab fried rice. it went really well with the green sauce that it came with. it was a good portion- good for sharing up to two people. there was also a good amount of crab in it. service was friendly. seats get filled quickly though, so i recommend making reservations beforehand.
The wait is pretty atrocious ngl but you will come back for the zab wings  I do not recommend sitting outside in the summer unless you want bees munching on your wings too though

Great little gem in Noho area with a Thai flair to seafood. We were able to sit outside on a beautiful summer day and really enjoy this place. Our server was able to quickly recommend a bunch of cocktails to start and some of their more popular dishes.

For drinks we went with the Negroni and the Tongue & Cheek, and they were excellent. We also went with oysters and chicken wings as an appetizer. All plates by the way are meant to be eaten family style. The oysters came with a green sauce as opposed to traditional Tabasco and I liked it better! Chicken wings were marinated well too. 

For the mains we shared the Coconut Crab Curry, Crab fried rice, Steamed Fish with Thai herbs, and the Island Style Grilled Chicken. Let me tell you one thing... the fish was so good we turned one of our friends who is a non-fish eater into a believer. Incredible, really. 

Ended this delicious meal with a sweet Thai Iced Coffee and that was the icing to the cake!

Ordered 3 items and all were inedibly salty.

1. Pork Cheeks - appetizer, thinly sliced pork. Salty and gamey.

2. Scallops - extremely salty. I didn't finish all the scallops, which is saying a lot.

3. Glass noodles with crab - least salty of the three but still salty. Didn't finish either.

Left feedback with the staff but only response was: did you try eating it with rice?

Seems like there are good reviews on fish so maybe I picked the wrong items but I tried 3 things.. I think that's a big enough sample size.

The only positive was the location and good weather.
Food and drinks were amazing 10/10. Visited Manhattan and randomly picked this spot for lunch and it was a great experience.

I had an amazing meal at fish cheeks, such a unique menu and well thought out dishes with excellent service. The coconut crab curry is a must order dish, so silky, creamy and the flavor was incredible the crab was not too overpowering but always present. So yummy soaked in rice! The steamed fish was also a treat, beautiful presentation on a special fish platter and the sauce it was bathed in was so tangy, herbaceous and refreshing packed with flavor you could really taste the cilantro. I also really enjoyed the pork salad as a starter, it was a bit tough to turn the lettuce into wraps but the flavor was amazing so minty and unique, like nothing I've ever tasted before. 
We made it in time for a happy hour so the delicious mango drink was a reasonable $11. Definitely make reservations for fish cheeks as I saw some people turned away with a two hour waiting time estimate by 6 pm. Interior is modern and cozy. Loved the experience here such a great spot in nyc!

I got lump crab fried rice for delivery on DoorDash. From 2 to 5 PM there is a happy hour, that gives a bit of a discount. It's OK. Other Thai restaurants on DoorDash are more generous with amount of crab meat for this dish.

I came here with my friend right when they were opened without making a reservation. Oh my goodness, seafood freaking heaven for me tbh! I got the fan favorite coconut crab curry $30 and happy hour 1/2 dozen bad boy oysters for $9. It was really pretty inside, loving the decor. The staff was very sweet, they gave me a sample to try the coconut curry before getting the real deal. They had three chili spiciest on the side but I wanted to make sure it wasn't going to kill me with the spice,  for me it wasn't spicy at all, so I was able to handle it, but for my friend it was way too spicy for her. They were very accommodating to her allergies. Thank you so much for that. Thank you for asking in the very beginning. Food was excellent, I would definitely come back to try everything else on the menu, but next time I would definitely want to make reservations before coming here bc it does tend to get busier throughout the day and it looks like it's hard to get seating if we came any later than 12pm today.

- best wings in NYC with the lemon pepper taste
- chicken was very moist and delicious - wish it came with rice
- great Thai iced coffee
- excellent pork

Overall, really delicious Thai. Shame there wasn't Pad Thai, but still excellent nonetheless.

Gabe was a great server - thank you!

I'll give it four stars. As the name suggests, this place is heaven for those who love seafood. I am not a big fan of seafood. I came here for NYC dining week. I started by ordering the wings. I have to say the wings were my favorite! And they are also huge. They are definitely not an appetizer. I think you can get full on just the wings alone. I also ordered the Coconut crab. I wasn't a fan of this. I think I would have been better off with the Leng Saeb, which is pork neck coked with different spices. I ended my meal with the ice cream bo lan. I absolutely loved the dessert. 

Overall, four-ish stars.

One of the best restaurants I've been to in a long time.  

My favorites out of what we ordered:

-Steamed Fish (my favorite)
-Prawn Karee
-Oysters (has a nice citrus sauce with fried shallot)

Others in my group also liked:

-Crab fried rice
-Coconut crab curry
-Sauteed cabbage

We also got a round of shots that had a pandan tea chaser.  The chaser completely eliminated any taste of the alcohol instantly.  Good stuff.

Service was amazing. They accommodated 6 adults and 6 young kids. Staff was very friendly.  

I'd come back again (without kids) to really enjoy it.

Multiple friends told me that this is their favorite Thai spot so I had to check this place out. We walked in one evening and was luckily able to snag a spot without a wait. The wait staff was very friendly and super helpful in helping us pick a few dishes. 

The crab curry was my favorite dish of the night! Very flavorful with a slow build of spiciness. It catches up with you later but despite the burn, you keep eating because it is that good! 

Next time, I have to come back hungrier to try more food!

Cozy place but good for groups.

The corn salad, grilled pork cheeks, and prawn kharee are all very good and worth getting.
Excellent food and service! Reservation is highly recommended, otherwise you might have to wait 45 mins during rush hours or even longer.

Good experience, but I think it's a little overhyped. Snagged a last minute reservation for 7:30 on a Saturday night by turning on notifications on Resy. We were seated promptly; they have bar seating, indoor and outdoor dining. The overall ambience is very casual. Our waitress was prompt, polite and gave us suggestions on the most popular dishes were to order. 

We couldn't decide between the calamari and the wings for an app, so we ordered them both! They were my favorite part of the meal. I loved the sauce that was with the calamari. The wings were so crispy and the seasoning had the perfect spice. For entrees, we ordered their famous coconut crab curry and the prawns dish. I enjoyed the curry with the large lumps of crab meat; I do wish they served it with a little more rice. I hated the prawns dish; I would not recommend this to anyone. The flavors were bland and mushy. I'm not sure how prawns are typically served, but I was expecting them to be de-headed and de-shelled and they were not. 

I've definitely had better Thai food at other restaurants. I would most likely come back for happy hour if I'm in the area, but it wasn't good enough to come back again for another full meal.

The wings and calamari are a must! They were absolutely delicious. The seasoning on the wings was so good. I didn't have high expectations but saw everyone ordering them and now I know why.

The calamari was tender and crunchy. 

The crab curry is their signature dish and was very good and the perfect amount of heat. I wish they gave you enough rice to eat all the curry though as the rice is a small portion. If you want more they charge $3.

The prawn dish was the most disappointing. $28 for 3 prawns still in the shell. While everything was good I would not recommend this dish. 

The cocktails are $17 each. 

The space is very casual and we were never rushed. The food came out very fast and hot which I appreciated.

I enjoyed dinner but for the price I do not think I would return.

Decent but overhyped. The space inside is cute and the staff was friendly and knowledgeable. I ordered the chicken wings (good albeit a little hard to eat), the crab curry (average tasting and almost no crab meat), and the fried fish (fish was well fried but not super flavorful and had just undressed leaves on top of it). We also had to wait about 20min to receive our drink order and were almost done eating because there seemed to be only one bartender for the whole restaurant. My husband and I also got nauseous after returning home. 

Overall I just don't think it's worth the hype or the price point.

Worth the hype, even better if you can walk in.

We sat outside since it was super full when we arrived but service and food was on point regardless. The crab fried rice and calamari were some of the I've had in NYC. Would absolutely come here again!

Snatched a last minute reservation at this popular place and was not disappointed at all!  We tried NYC restaurant week menu ($60 pp) consisting of 3 course menu:  appetizer, entree and dessert.   More food than I ever wanted!   I enjoyed crab curry -  tasted more like panang.  Perfect balance of spices and flavor.  Their corn salad was to die for.  Five stars!

Food was very good (we had the curry, chicken wings, prawn karee) but we had it on a very hot day in NY.  I don't recommend that!  I loved the Thai iced coffee!! 

We sat by the door and someone kept Windexing the door next to us which drove a bunch of fumes our way which I found unpleasant. I appreciate the attention to cleanliness but just a heads up that it's rough on the nearby people- particularly on warm days.

Come here and eat this food and have some tasty drinks! Calamari, it's got a nice crunch and crisp and the sauce is liquid love. Wings tasty dry rub that makes you want to keep chowing with a crispy outside and mooooiiiiissssttt inside. The steamed fish... is fire. Like still on fire and super juicy. Make sure you pour the sauce from the fish on some rice and chow down. 
GET THE DRINKS: the pad Thai thing was delicious, martini is a "yes pleaseyyy" and the Negroni was a tasty.
Lastly, Carson was more attentive than my dog in all the best ways. Made sure the food was coursed well and our drinks were refreshed right on time.

Same yourself some time and stop reading other reviews abs just eat here at Fish Cheeks!

Wowowowow this place is phenomenal. I stopped by for lunch and it was one of the best meals that I've had in a long time. It fell during restaurant week and their daily happy hour so I started off with their oysters and spicy mango cocktail which were both fantastic - I loved the accompaniments that came with the oysters. The nam tok pork salad was SO flavorful and I really enjoyed the mix of fresh ingredients and the decent sized portion of protein. 

The coconut crab curry was so comforting on a rainy day like today and packed a punch. Lastly, the pandan ice cream was super tasty and I loved the addition of the sticky rice. Can't wait to come back and try more of their spectacular menu!

My family all came down with food poisoning after having the crab and scallop main dishes as well as the calamari and shrimp appetizer. Brutal sickness.  Not sure which dish was the problem, but we won't be coming back or recommending this place. It wrecked our holiday in New York.

What an amazing little spot!  We stumbled upon this gem walking around in NYC.  Even though it was Saturday evening, we were seated quickly.  They recommend sharing entrees family style, due to their small kitchen.  This worked out great as we were able to try three different entrees.  The crab fried rice was really good and had large chunks of crab in it.  The pork belly was not spicy at all and had a good flavor, but the portion was pretty small for the price.  The crab AOB Woonsen was good and had 2 crab claws and chunks of crab in it.

The drinks were great and the service was amazing . We ordered the crab fried rice , the steamed fish , the oysters, and the pork belly . The one thing I would back for is the steamed whole fish and the mango with sticky rice . The cherry on top was that they de-boned the fish . The crab rice was simple and the pork belly although cooked to perfection was a bit salty (I didn't eat it with rice ). I do want to go back and try the prawn and crab curry as well as the wings people rave about .

Fish cheeks was a great restaurant to visit as my first in Manhattan! 

As a group of two, we ordered the zabb wings, prawn karee, and coconut crab curry. Of the three, the prawn karee stood out with its excellent gravy. The Zabb wings are also something I'd definitely order again--they have a distinct white pepper note that I haven't seen many places.

The service was relatively attentive with a few minor hiccups, but given the extreme traffic this place experiences I guess that's to be expected. One recommendation I'd make is to eschew bar seating--there really wasn't enough table space for a super comfortable experience at the bar.

Overall I'd definitely visit again but might save it for a nicer occasion--the meal was a bit pricey and came out to around 50 a person.

This place is awesome, it gets very packed so book a reservation! All the food is family style so you can share with a friend or two. I loved all the dishes I tried out and considering I'm not a big fish person, that is saying a lot. It is important to note that Fish Cheeks has traditional Thai dishes so you won't find any pad thai. I will be revisiting and look forward to trying out the cocktails which look so pretty. They will provide you with your check promptly to ensure the next person can sit.

I've been to fish cheeks two times in the past year.  The first time when I came, I ordered the steamed fish with herbs and the coconut crab curry.  The second time, I ordered the steamed fish, half a dozen oysters, morning glory, and the pork belly dish.  

During my second visit, I noticed the size of the steamed fish has gotten much smaller compared to my first visit.  However, I do appreciate that they help you debone the fish.  The oysters are quite tiny, my boyfriend and I both found the pork belly to be way too hard to even chew.  The coconut curry is super delicious and spicy.  The morning glory was good, but we noticed we mostly got stem of the vegetable, while the party next to us got a good mixture of leafy and stems for the dish.  

However, the service staff here was very attentive despite it being very busy!

Went here with 4 other friends and sat outside on a watm saturday afternoon.

It was happy hour so we got the oysters and cocktails. The oysters were fresh and came with crispy garlic which was a very nice touch. However, some oysters were very very very small. I mean the shell was big but the actual thing was just tiny. (See photo)

We got their most populous items for main course. 
Stemaed fish 4.5/5: very well done. Came in this playe that looked like a fish and was cute. There was a little flame underneath that kept it warm and gave it a unique and pleasant look. The broth was lemony and refreshing and the fish itself was well made. I wouldn't say it is very special but it was definitely good. If you want something healthy, refreshing, and exciting at the same time go for this dish. 

Crab Curry 3/5: It was just fine. Kind of tasted like chicken tikka masala but with crab and a bit of curry. I wasn't too impressed. I mean it tasted good but if u add so mych cream to anything it is gonna taste good. Other than that I think thr spuces were a little off. It was just spicy (which I like) but pther than that not very special.

Crab Fried Rice 3/5: mid fried rice. It was ok idk. It was just fried rice. U can get this anywhere. Do not overpay here. 

Tom Yum Soup: It was way too sour. Howevwr the presentation was nice and there was a lot of interesting seafood in it. In general however the broth was just very very sour. This is not a mild soup. I think it should be more mild and less sour. 

In general, the presentation was creative and the dishes were too. Maybe you should go once to try it and see if you like it but I do not think I will personally be going back.

Sooo good! Everything we ordered for the table was yummy. Whole fish was definitely a show stopper! Chicken wings were good but average compared to everything else. Their pork belly is also a good option. Wait staff was pretty knowledgeable. It gets really crowded inside so we sat outside last time. Outdoor seating is covered and surprisingly well-built unlike most restaurants.

This place has THE BEST THAI FOOD in Manhattan. I was blown away by the coconut crab curry. While their crab fried rice wasn't anything out of the ordinary, in tandem with the coconut crab curry it was such a good decision we made and made the experience out of the world. I would recommend to definitely get those two. The coconut crab curry was indeed spicy but it was a delicious amount of spice to balance with the coconut and sweetness of the crab. Great service too!! We did not have any reservations but since it was just me and another person, we were able to get seated walk-in but definitely wouldn't rely on that if you have a larger party because the place was quite packed.

The fish was flaky, perfectly cooked, and the sauce complimented it so well!! The cocktails were also so yummy, and the happy hour was a good deal! Super cute interior, and the servers were all so kind and sweet. I was taken to this place when visiting a friend in New York, and she said she takes everyone that visits her from out of town, and all of them love it. I can see why!

This place is just really good. I was surprised how much I liked it. I go to thai restaurants in woodside which is next to my apt and i consider those to be elite but i actually thought this place was better. 

We had zabb wings which is like doritos chicken wings and I mean that as a compliment. It was also a big portion for $15 which was really nice given how expensive eating out is now. 10/10. 

The coconut crab curry was great also. I could have done without the crab if it would have made it cheaper because I find crab to be a bit tasteless and bland (everywhere so it's not a reflection of fish cheeks) but the curry was 10/10. They rate it as 3 peppers spicy but that's just to be on the safe side. 3 peppers here isn't 3 peppers at the thai restaurants in woodside. They're probably catering to a different clientele. It's still spicy but it's not painful. Again the portion was pretty big. This place is really meant for sharing so coming with a group is ideal. You'll probably end up tasting a lot of great dishes and it won't be too expensive. 

Anyway, the place was great and I'd come again.

The crab fried rice is excellent. My friend ordered it as a side dish to the meal she cooked and it was so good my husband and I ordered the same dish from another restaurant the next night and it didn't even compare. I haven't eaten at the restaurant yet, but I have high expectations now!

I'm so sad about this place because I was underwhelmed . I feel it's so overhyped . At first glance it's a beautiful place the servers are amazing very sweet and kind . The food now I don't know . The calamari starting out was soooooo good so good. The best calamari one of the best I've had . I also had the green curry . It literally had roasted vegetables corn and chili peppers . It needed more depth . Even some nice crunchy shallots on top . A garnish . It didn't even look appetizing . I was extremely disappointed . The price range doesn't bother me , because it's in soho you're going to pay but for what you're paying for I think it could have had more depth or even different veggies I don't know . Also when the server asked us if we wanted sparkling or tap water . I'm thinking the sparkling water is free , $12 bucks for the sparkling water . The bathroom is very cute . But I think I would maybe come back and try a seafood dish and see what I think . Maybe I don't know . But I was so stoked to try this place and the meal fell flat for me . But our server was extremely sweet and attentive . What's cool though about this spot is you don't have to wait to pay you can pay on the app it's awesome .

Clement was phenomenal! She helped our table order what would be best for our individual palates. The food was amazing and definitely hit the spot. Don't even get me started on the drinks which added to the flavor profile of the meal. Overall a great experience and if you want a knowledgeable, lovely server ask for Clement; she'll get you right. Clement has consistently been the most amiable, honest, and relatable server here.

Absolutely love coming here just for Clement! we come at least once a month and enjoy it every time. We love it and we're going to continue the tradition. We always request Clemene tans she's always been the perfect server for us and caters to every need!

Always so happy here - I had some friends from out of town visiting, but they had so much traffic on the way and was 1 hrs late to the reservation - As I waited with other people, the staff was super attentive and was so sweet. We ordered appetizers as we waited and they were phenomenal. The happy hour oysters and fried wings are delicious and leaving us wanting more! When our full table arrived we had the crab curry, steamed fish, pork neck, morning glory, and calamari and they were all very tasty. The only thing is that if you can't handle spice, it may be a little difficult for children. Would recommend to other people to visit :)

Loved everything about this place and haven't stopped thinking about the food since going two weeks ago.  Getting a reservation can be pretty hard - I set up a notification on Resy and got lucky.  We tried the red curry scallops (amazing), the pork belly bowl (amazing), and the whole branzino (amazing - good for two for sure).  Nothing was overly spicy (and I am sometimes sensitive to jalapeños) but it was all well seasoned.  The drinks sound really strange but tasted like standard cocktails.  The vibe is lively yet cozy.   This is a great place to go with friends or a group - it might be a little loud for a date or parents.  Service wasn't very memorable, the staff was nice but seemed overwhelmed.  
@alex.eats.365
Traveling for work needed to get my thai fix. Saw great reviews on yelp and decided to go here. Ordered fried calamari, carb fried rice, and steamed fish. Exquisite. Muah. So good.

One of my top Thai restaurants in NYC. Cute decor and nice restaurant. Some of my favorite dishes are the steamed fish, oysters, and crab curry. The food has a nice kick and eating their food reminds me of being back in Thailand. Nice authentic flavors, the green chili sauce is amazing. Definitely make reservations prior to coming and get the happy hour oysters!

I hate to say it, but it's overhyped. The food here is definitely good, but it didn't blow my mind away.

We were seated when half our group arrived, in a corner, near the service door. It was really loud in there. The waiter was attentive and took her order promptly.

We tried most of the menu, but the standouts were the crab fried rice, the raw, shrimp appetizer, the whole steamed fish, the pork cheeks, and a softshell crab. Skip the desert, it's simply just ice cream with sticky rice.

When we were paying for our bill, the waiter kept on, trying to upsell us with happy hour. I've never had that happen before, and we were ready to leave.
Worth the hype. Food was great. Standout dishes were the pork cheeks, crab fried rice and wings! No notes. Will go back. Easy payment system via the qr code

Friend made reservations today to try this hype restaurant and I thought it was pretty good. I just came back from Thailand weeks ago and I thought the flavor was pretty similar with more American taste to it. I enjoyed the service and the ambiance!
Delicious, but expensive. It's worth it, don't get me wrong. Try the crab curry and the wings.

I can't believe it's taken me this long to write a review for here... not that my review would make any sort of impact bc this spot is AMAZING and everyone already knows it... if you can't get a reso... go put your name down and grab a drink the standard hotel on Cooper sq (they have tons of seating and it's less than a 5 min walk). I've had both the fried fish and the steamed fish and both are really good but I do prefer the steamed fish. Spicy crab curry is fire in every way possible... spicy delicious hot curry with massive chunks of crab. Crab fried rice is also a fav, I think I've had that every time I've gone. If you're skeptical... Chrissy Teigen used to live on Bond st pre kids and pre la and although she is only half Thai we all know her mom raised her on some legit Thai meals... and fish cheeks was her fav Thai place. The staff is always friendly and the service is great even when you're sitting outside on the street. Love this place.

Came in with high expectations and was not disappointed! First off, the decor was colorful with fun vibes. The hostess and the staff were awesome and made great recommendations. The only hiccup was that we had a party of 10 and didn't make a reservation until a few days in advance so we had to split into 2 groups. NBD though. 

Our group ordered several dishes and family-styled it with the fried calamari, steamed fish, choo chee scallops, crab curry, and crab fried rice. All the dishes were fantastic but my favorites were the crab curry (a generous amount of crab and the perfect amount of heat) and the steamed fish (sooo tangy and umami - just a perfect balance of flavors). The fish did take a little longer to come out compared to the rest of dishes, but well worth the wait. 

Overall amazing seafood in a fun, bright and vibrant atmosphere! Can't wait to come back and try more of their dishes!

Fish Cheeks is an upscale Thai food with delicious and rather ornate dishes, such as the famous steamed fish. I would highly recommend all of their dishes, as well as the drinks; the mocktails are pricey, but at least fancy/complex enough that it isn't just juice masquerading as a cocktail. The only thing keeping it from a 5-star is that the tables are small, the environment can get so loud you can barely hear each other talking, and I received the wrong order (prawn curry instead of crab). However, everything I had was still amazing, and it's worthy of a visit.

Please do yourself a favor -- go to Fish Cheeks, get the steamed fish, and please please take a moment to take it all in. 

The broth is so addicting. So perfectly lime-y and acidic with the deep umami flavor from the fish sauce. It has the perfect amount of spice with fish that is literally so juicy and light, it'll melt in your mouth. And when you come back home and have time to think about what you just experienced, you'll be thinking about when the next time you can go back will be :-)

This honestly may be the best restaurant I've ever tried in nyc to this date. I understand why it's so hard to book a reservation here and why it's such a popular spot. I 1000% recommend the calamari as your appetizer. It's the crispiest, yet still light, and most flavorful calamari I've ever tasted. The Thai basil and cilantro add the perfect boost of richness in flavor. Coconut crab curry was also delicious but it's quite spicy! The seared fish was recommended to us because we couldn't decide on our second dish and I'm so glad we went with it. Again, so many layers of flavor which the jasmine rice amplified even more. Definitely try for a reservation unless you don't mind a long wait.

Solid option for Thai food. If you want to expand your Thai food palette a bit, definitely recommend this place- no pad Thai or drunken noodles here, but in a good way. The Crispy Rice Salad and Pork was a pleasant surprise- nice mix of crunchy and chewy textures and had a nice kick to it. The Isan Style Grilled Chicken was really tasty- definitely recommend that one. Friendly staff too- would come back.

Today I stopped by here by myself after a Whale Watching trip. I ordered Crispy Rice Salad and pork as well as the Coconut Crab Curry

Fish cheeks

Crispy rice salad and pork
REALLY tasty. It's spicy, sweet, salty. It's crispy with good flavor from mint, shallots and garlic. The crispy rice brings a crispy and chewy texture, while the pork is also crispy. Definitely recommend it.

Coconut Crab curry- Very good, ok amount of crab, the curry had good heat, had pretty decent coconut flavor too. Very filling if eaten with all rice.

Overall: All of the food was very good. May come here again, the reservations are kind of tough.

Fish Cheeks has been on my list for ages and finally managed to try it. Pretty place. Lots of seafood options. Food was pretty good, though not the most authentic Thai food out there. Pretty approachable though. 

1. Pork neck: could be better. Sauce could also use a bit more work. I've had better in other places 
2. Raw shrimp: such a hard dish to find in other places but theirs was pretty great. Acidic with lots of citrus. Fresh. 
3. Steamed fish: one of my favorite things to order - theirs was pretty good. 
4. Cabbage: lots of wok hey charred flavor. Pretty good. 

Overall, Fish Cheeks is pretty good. Not the best but definitely will not disappoint especially if you want decent thai food in a nice setting. You won't find thai food with a twist but hey, it's pretty good if you're in the mood for Thai.

This place is tasty!! Vegan options were limited but delicious! The green curry was spicy with deep flavor and assorted interesting vegetables that provided great textures. The corn salad (with vegan dressing) was so fresh and spicy. The omnivores at the table were raving about everything, especially the whole steamed fish, wings, ribs. The service was friendly and speedy. Highly recommend.

Went right at opening for dinner on a Tuesday and we didn't have to wait for two people! The waiter was so friendly and had great recommendations. The crab noodles were decent but not super flavorful, but the calamari was perfect and crispy. We came for happy hour oysters + drinks, which were definitely the highlight. It was a bright, open space that is so welcoming and vibrant. Lives up to the hype!

Arrived on a Wednesday evening with no reservations,  but they were able to seat us. Husband and I just barely caught happy hour. Enough time to get 2 drinks each. They were very tasty. The complimentary shrimp chips were an acquired taste. I liked, but Husband did not. The chicken wings were so good and unique with a strong lime flavor. The pork belly was cooked perfectly,  crispy, but we could have done without the sauce. Lastly the cabbage was absolutely amazing.  This will definitely be on our list any time we visit NYC.

There are many great places for Thai food in the city (including the outer boroughs), but Fish Cheeks has a great combination of excellent food and cocktails, great location, and nice atmosphere.  And they will actually prepare the food spicy!  I have gone alone and with friends, and I have enjoyed the restaurant every time.  When I last visited in mid-May, the menu had a high concentration of (delicious) crab dishes - something to consider for you crab lovers out there.

I always heard about Fish Cheeks but never had the opportunity to go before. I am so glad to have gone there. Who's crazy enough to drive into Manhattan? This girl right here! Luckily, I found parking right when meter parking time was over.

No reservation was made, so it was all based on luck. Thankfully, there was an empty table but the staff said that there was a reservation at a later time so if we were okay with finishing our meal within an hour or so, they can take us in.

Since I came here with my sister and friend, it was no surprise that one of them hates cilantro. Apparently, cilantro tastes like soap to her. Upon hearing about the cilantro, the staff tried to explain that many of the dishes contained cilantro, but it was okay because we were going to order dishes containing cilantro either way. Cilantro haters, beware!

We first started off with drinks! I ordered the Tongue and Cheek, which contains vodka, lychee, lime, hibiscus, aquafaba, and toasted sesame on top. It was quite delicious and not too strong. Light and fruity are just the right words for it.

For food, we ordered Oysters, Prawn Karee, Pork Cheeks, Zabb Wings, Crab Fried Rice, and Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs. The oysters were fresh and not gritty at all. The sauce was a plus! I couldn't help but slather a lot of sauce onto the oyster. helped to The Zabb Wings were full of flavor and packed a lime-y punch as you ate each piece. To get some carbs, we ordered the Crab Fried Rice. The Prawn Karee was a nice addition to everything that we ordered and it went well with the fried rice. 

Would I come here again? Absolutely. It's a nice place to grab dinner with your friends and family and even a date. The interior of the place is modern, with a hint of traditional Thai touches. It's a very chill place to have food and drinks at.

After not eating there for a year, had lunch twice in past 2 weeks, and was very disappointed.

Menu prices were normal, not lunch special, but the portions were ridiculously small. There was a tiny bit of protein, crab the first time, and a plate  filled with sauce. That makes sense if  eating in rural SE Asia, where protein is the flavoring, but not at these prices.

The second time, there was no sauce, just for scallops cut in half.  I forgot to ask them to hold the salt, and it was incredibly salty, as was my friend's.

I had really liked this place last year, but now I won't go back.
This is a tasty treat with good energy and an amazing location. Really recommend the Cocoanut curry

I can understand the hype. Kind of a whack dining crowd at this point but the food was very good. We shared the pork cheeks (delicious but gets very greasy very fast), manila clams (not the freshest honestly...tasted like they'd be sitting out for awhile), steamed fish (omg was this good) and crab fried rice (can't go wrong really). Definitely book in advance although most late night slots are open daily.

Favorite Thai restaurant in the city!!! Service is relatively quick and the food is incredible. Not your typical Thai restaurant - dishes are a bit more unique and full of flavors and textures. I asked for their recommendations and they were so so good. If you're going for the first time, I really recommend getting the steamed fish. I am definitely going back to try the rest of the menu.

I saw this place on tik tok and really wanted to come! My bf is also from Thailand and after looking at the pictures he said it looked very good! We made reservations for 5 on a Tuesday afternoon.

Pork cheeks: i was a bit disappointed by this dish. Usually this dish is served with other veggies and has a lime cilantro flavor. I felt like the pork lacked any flavor and you had to dip it in the sauce in order for it to taste good. 3/5

Steamed fish: this is one of their most popular dish and i highly recommend! The fish is pretty small but the seasoning is so good! They add a ton of cilantro and Thai sour sauce that makes the dish extremely flavorful. 4.5/5

Green curry: this is a vegan curry so it's nice they had options for vegans. My family didn't enjoy this one as much as the crab curry probably because they aren't used to a vegan based milk. 3/5

Coconut crab curry: this is another one of their most popular dish. I highly recommend getting it! We were worried the dish would be too spicy but honestly it was bearable. We probably have a high spice tolerance. Sauce to crab ratio was good too! Pairs well over rice 5/5

Prawn karee: holy cow this was the best dish we got. The prawn to curry ratio was perfect! The flavors were so flavorful and we were so surprised how good this dish tasted. 5/5

Oysters: we came during happy hour so we got the half off oysters which was great! Oysters are on smaller end but very fresh! 4/5

Overall we were pleased with this restaurant. Flavors are very authentic. Make sure to book reservations as this place filled up with for a Thursday afternoon. They have outdoor seating as well!
Crab curry was mid, short ribs was fire, but spicy, everything else was incredible. Zappa wings was a pleasant surprise

This authentic Thai restaurant is tucked away on Bond Street. It took us a couple of weeks to secure a table, although they do welcome walk-ins, I wouldn't count on it.

The place was bustling when we visited on a Saturday night, and we quickly understood why. We were promptly seated at our reserved time, and to our delight, the staff brought us crackers with chili jam to nibble on. It was a thoughtful gesture that earned them an extra star in my book.

The menu is conveniently available as a QR code and is easy to understand. To start, we enjoyed some imported Thai lager and the pork cheek appetizer, which consisted of slices of marinated pork cheek in fish sauce, served with jaew sauce. The dish was full of flavor and perfect for sharing.

Next, we ordered the whole fried fish with garden herb salad and pickled garlic dressing, along with their highly recommended coconut crab curry. Both dishes were truly indulgent and exceeded our expectations.

Overall, our dining experience at Fish Cheeks was exceptional, thanks to their efficient service, delicious food, and fantastic customer service. If you haven't visited this neighborhood gem yet, I highly recommend doing so!

Omg LOVE this place! Their raw bar oysters are the best because of whatever their special house sauce is. We ordered 3 trays because we couldn't get enough and finished it all. The crab gut (?) fried rice is my other go to.  Always look forward to coming here!

Fish Cheeks is a culinary gem nestled in the vibrant streets of New York City. As a seafood enthusiast, I had heard whispers of its exceptional offerings, and my recent visit confirmed that it truly lives up to its reputation. From the moment I stepped foot into the restaurant, I was transported to a coastal paradise, where the flavors of Thailand's seaside delicacies danced harmoniously on my palate.

The ambiance at Fish Cheeks is an impeccable blend of contemporary chic and traditional charm. The intimate setting, adorned with nautical accents and soft lighting, creates an atmosphere that exudes warmth and relaxation. The staff greets you with genuine smiles and guide you through the menu with unparalleled expertise.
Now, let's dive into the culinary journey that unfolded before my eyes. The menu at Fish Cheeks boasts an impressive array of seafood dishes, all meticulously crafted to highlight the freshest ingredients and authentic Thai flavors. The standout feature of Fish Cheeks is their commitment to sourcing locally and sustainably, ensuring a dining experience that not only satisfies the taste buds but also supports responsible practices.

We ordered: 
- 1/2 Dozen Oysters (Happy Hour Pricing)
    - We paid only $9 for half a dozen oysters and it was paired with an excellent asian inspired vinegar sauce 
- Crispy Rice Salad & Pork
    - This was like no other dish I have had before, the pork was cooked to perfection, and it was served with a quarter head of lettuce that we could pull apart 
- Cho Chee Scallop
    - One of the best cooked scallops I have ever had in NYC, the curry that the scallops were cooked in was slightly salty but this was an excellent dish 
- Coconut Crab Curry 
    - This was one of the top dishes that we have had it was very good, the sauce was more panang curry like but like a million times better! 
- Prawn Karee 
    - We got a chef's special that substituted the prawn for soft-shell crab, but this was our least favorite dish that we had ordered, still very good but would not recommend

Overall, Fish Cheeks is a seafood haven that captures the essence of Thai cuisine with finesse and creativity. Its commitment to quality, sustainability, and culinary excellence sets it apart from the crowd. Whether you're a seafood aficionado or simply seeking an unforgettable dining experience, Fish Cheeks will undoubtedly leave you craving more. Prepare to be transported to the shores of Thailand, right in the heart of NYC.

The Branzino is love. Perfect mix of sour, chili, and all the while preserving the fresh flavor of the fish. One of the best meals during our trip. We weren't able to get a reservation so we arrived around 5pm on a Friday, prepared to wait an hour+ but the hostess was able to call us back within 10min!

Food is awesome!  I haven't had a fish that I didn't like! Service is great. Attentive without hovering. 
A+++
Pretty neat Thai place, the fish was the best. I would come back here again. Actually have really been back here two more times haha. You also can't beat the happy hour $11 cocktails!

I truly loved this place. Everything tastes so fresh, the drinks are amazing, the staff is sweet and attentive. It's a pretty casual restaurant in appearance and the food is incredibly thought out and done soooo well.

Came here with my parents for lunch and it was not completely full. We walked in without a reservation for 3 and were seated pretty quickly. Our waitress was great and was able to get us warm water and accommodated some changes after we ordered. We got the crab fried rice, coconut crab curry, steamed fish and the crispy rice salad as well as half a dozen oysters w the happy hour deal ($9) The oysters came out first and they were super duper small, the size of a penny but I liked the sauces and crunchy crisps that came with it.  The flavor of the crispy rice salad was too strong for me and my parents so I do not recommend that. The coconut crab curry was alright and not as spicy as I thought it would be (I would compare it to like a mild spicy dry pot - maybe even less) but I'd pair it with white rice rather than the crab fried rice that we got. I really do not think it should get 3 spice levels on the menu. The crab fried rice was also just fine - tasted like a classic egg fried rice with crab bits but the crab bits could be more fresh bc you could tell that it was frozen crab meat. Steamed fish was 10/10, the fish meat was soft and deboned and was perfectly seasoned. 

Would recommend sharing everything like they say on the menu. I loved the color scheme and decor of the restaurant but the food was overhyped imo and I probably would not come back again.

Hands down one of my favorite Thai places. Solid food every single time I come here. 

- Zabb wings 
- Crab fried rice 
- Pork belly pad kaprow 
- Steamed fish - MUST GET 

Everything is absolutely delicious and has so much flavor. Tons of crab in the crab fried rice. The steamed fish is the star of the show though, this is a must order! Service is always great and the outdoor area is really cute.

Holy spicy Thai. They are not kidding around with the chili pepper ratings. 
Everything here is awesome, just be careful with more than two to three chili peppers in the menu ratings...

Great scene, great good. Highly recommend.

Came to this restaurant upon the recommendation of a friend. We were greeted pleasantly and seated outside. Carson was our server and he was great! 

I had no idea what to expect as I didn't look at the menu beforehand or even know what type of food they served! I was in for a treat! Fish Cheeks offers authentic Thai cuisine.

To start, we tried the calamari and pork--both were delicious! We also got the "She Fell Off The Boat" shot. It was so interesting and it all comes together nicely! 

For mains we did the Coconut Crab Curry, the short rib beef, and whole fish. Everything was delicious! The curry crab and beef were spicy! 

Great food and amazing service! Definitely a great place to dine if you are in New York!
Great casual spot for authentic Thai food - loved the sour spicy steamed fish and the crab curry. Can't go wrong with any of the dishes here!

Visited New York last month with my fiancé and this place was highly recommended - it definitely did not disappoint! Everything we ordered was amazing. It even has a slightly higher rating on google reviews compared to the other Thai restaurant that has a Michelin star. 

We ordered their Zabb chicken wings app, and 1/2 price "happy hour" oysters to start. If you come between 12-6pm their oyster platters are 50% off, what an amazing deal! We got 12 pieces for $18 and it was super refreshing especially with the fried shallots and lime/citrus sauce. The chicken wings were dusted with a chili lime seasoning, crunchy skin on the outside but very juicy on the inside. For our main, we shared the steamed fish with Thai herbs, it was sitting in a cilantro chili lime broth and it complimented the fish so well. We had it with a side of rice and morning glory with garlic side dish. Everything was delicious and reminded us of Thailand when we ate here! 

Service is super friendly and efficient. It gets super busy so I highly recommend making a reservation online. They do reserve a few tables for walk ins but it fills up super fast. We came right when they opened and luckily got a table before the place filled up by 1pm. 

Will definitely come back here when I visit New York again to try their other dishes! Highly recommend.

The food here is absolutely delicious. Came for the Happy Hour Oysters (fresh and amazing toppings!) Stayed for the Steamed Fish (I could eat it every day). My husband got the crab curry and it was sooo good but it could have been a bit bigger considering the cost. Pork cheeks are really tasty.

Love the food here! What really stands out here are the sauces. My god, the flavor is immense. We started with Oysters, that were very good and accompanied with an herby green sauce. The Shrimp in 3 crab sauces, which was also great - and again, my god the sauce was great. The Pork Cheeks were then fantastic and so good. And then for the main courses the Coconut Crab Curry was fantastic - just the right amount of spice and smokiness, and also creamy. We also had the Crab Fried Rice which I couldn't stop eating. This place is great!

They were very busy yet our server took time to explain the menu and was very friendly. The food was refreshing delicious. The specialty cocktails were a perfect match and on par with the food. Already planning my next visit. Can't wait!

Really great meal here.
5/5 ambiance.
5/5 service.
5/5 food.
5/5 value.

Morning glory - delicious, savory, sour, spicy, fresh morning glory.

Cabbage - weakest dish, overboard with the fish sauce, but nice charring and wok hei on the leaves.

Pork cheeks - simple, but amazing. Perfectly tender and the sauce is crack. Lots of lime, shallot, garlic, fish sauce, chilis. Wow.

Steamed branzino - incredible. So fresh. 95% deboned. Lime and cilantro with tons of garlic in this sauce and chilis (not too much). This was just amazing. I love steamed fish and they knocked it put of the park with this one.

The food was delicious, but pretty pricy. Most of the main dishes, priced around $30-40, were small and definitely not entree sized, so you would need to order multiple of these per person. I'd say you should expect to spend $80+ per person to have a full meal here.

This was my 2nd time going to fish cheeks. I loved all the food there. I went to my boyfriend and did a walk-in on a weekday around 6:30pm. Waited 15 mins for outdoor seating (inside was already full). Please make a resy or go earlier if you don't want to wait.

The steamed fish is a must orderrrr!! So good! I also love the crab curry. It comes with 1 rice so we had to order a 2nd bowl. The corn Salad is spicier than the crab curry even though the crab curry is  on the menu but the corn salad is just . Both were still delicious though!

For drinks, must get the tongue + cheek!! Super good!!!
Absolutely delicious food and a very nice and casual atmosphere. Excellent service. Very unique Thai food. Highly recommend.

Incredibly memorable experience at Fish Cheeks. We booked a table for 12 people last night and were graciously welcomed to feast from start to finish. 

Fish Cheeks despite having a small kitchen, is VERY well-equipped for a larger party. Service was prompt and helpful as they guided us through the best dishes on the menu. 

The flavors were bursting in every dish, with each more memorable than the last. Can't wait to return!
Not a very authentic Chinese restaurant, it is more like a Asian and American fusion. If you are here with you friends, it is recommended. But if you are by yourself, try somewhere else

Fish Cheeks is one of my fav restaurants in nyc! I usually get the spicy coconut curry and the crab fried rice but this time I decided to explore the menu. 

There's a big hype around the zabb wings and I can see why people are obsessed it with! So yummy. 

I'd definitely recommend the Crab Aob Woonsen! 

The interior of the restaurant is so cute & the restaurant is always lively!

A reservation is recommended but walk-ins are also accommodated. 

Would I come back? Heck yes!

Came here on a Friday night by myself when I was in town for work, and I got seated at the bar within 15 minutes or so.  I got:
- Fried fish (4/5) - Nicely fried, with a tasty, sweet sauce.
- Morning glory (3.5/5)
- Ice cream bo lan (3.5/5) - The sticky rice was great, but the ice cream to rice ratio was a bit too high
- Drinks (4.5/5) - Both drinks I got - the Soi 38 and The Only Pad Thai on the Menu, were really interesting and quite good

We had a reservation and loved the flavors of this place! Half dozen happy hour oysters which comes with a nice green sauce for $9 from 12-6pm and the steamed fish with lime was delicious! We also had the crab fried rice which went perfectly with the fish! I liked the Thai ice tea and it tasted like it had more of a coconut flavor milk. I would come back here again!
If you have a "white" taste buds but still want to venture to southeastern Asian food, this is safe for you. But if you are Asian or familiar with real Southeastern Asian food, don't bother.

Wow! This place is super yummy and is not your usual Thai place. They won't have pad Thai or pad see ew. (Wish they did.) but so many great dishes that I can't knock them for not serving me the usual noodle dishes.

Pork cheeks so tender and juicy with a bounciness.

Crab noodles were yummy although the crab itself sitting on top could use some sautéing with some alliums.

Chicken wings were crispy and finger lickin good.

Shrimp curry so divine. I could eat that curry sauce over rice all day long.

Tom yum fish was very tender and juicy.

Everything tasted fantastic and I dream of going back. A very unique Thai food experience different from most.

The best thing that we tried on the menu was the steamed while fish. It was well spiced and flavorful and cooked just right. That was truly amazing and would absolutely come back to have that again. I was also recommend the coconut crab curry as well. This is a more upscale and place so the quantity is small to medium so make sure to order appropriately. I would definitely recommend for date night!

Fish cheeks was my FAVORITE meal on my nyc trip. I miss it already. Absolutely incredible food, very cute outdoor seating, and good service. We had the corn salad, Manila clams, and prawn karee. Every dish was to die for. The corn salad was sweet, spicy, crunchy, juicy. I could have dranken the sauce just like that. The Manila clams were also so flavorful but unlike any other clams I've had. Again, in an incredible sauce that I was just eating with rice by the end of the meal. The prawn karee was also amazing. The karee has egg in it which I've never had before, but loved it, different from your yellow, red, green curry sauce. Prawns were cooked perfectly. I regret not going again the next day and trying more dishes, it really was the best.

Loveeee her! I'm surprised to see I haven't reviewed one of my favorite places in the city yet! Fish cheeks has awesome ambiance, awesome food, awesome staff! I love eating here and it's worth the extra work to get a reservartion. I love the herbed fish and the pork belly, the jeaw pork is so succulent and delicious. The prawn karee is always a crowd pleaser, and the crab curry is NOT as spicy as they warn-- try it! I also love their cocktails, especially the "Only Pad Thai on the Menu". Always happy dining here.

Heard about and seen this place on quite a few platform so I was thrilled to happen to be in the area to check it out. I was ready to be blown away but unfortunately maybe I was expecting too much...

They're pretty busy even on a random afternoon. We did get seated immediately but in the "no service" zone in the corner of the restaurant where nobody would come to us for 30+ minutes...We also found hair in our food.

The above negatives aside, I do think that this place does make legit Thai seafood. Their menu specializes in that. We got the Scallop Choo Chee and it got great spice and herbs. As a Thai person, I can approve of that. Their Tounge and Cheek drink was also very delicious. The lychee came through well and the drink overall was very refreshing.

Although we had troubles during our visit, after we're able to get somebody attention, they did remake our dish and compensated the dish which we appreciated.

So, all in all, I think this is a decent spot for good food, just maybe need to work on the service a bit. They do have a great happy hour deal on drinks and food though.
Two star for food, good and only okay not good enough to compensate for the outrages price... will not go again and don't recommend

Lives up to the hype! Everything I've had here is on another level in terms of taste. Although you do need to know what to order to get the right balance since most dishes are packed with flavor.

I would recommend:
- Pork slices appetizer
- Oysters if happy hour 
- Steamed fish is a must try! Sour and spicy, and the fish is already deboned. Their best dish by far.
- Prawn curry. Savory and goes well with rice.
- Tom yum soup. Lots of seafood and the soup is delicious. Just don't order with only the steamed fish since both dishes are sour.

I watched a few plates of the steamed fish go by but my waiter highly recommended the fried fish, what a mistake. Too breaded and too fried, dry and tasteless even though surrounded by herbs and flavors. Then I watched another 10 steamed fish dishes go by me with jealously. 

I even ordered a shrimp dish to go because I was so unsatisfied.  I think it was the Kraab which was much more flavorful, but a little bit salty and too oily.  

My friends love this place I'll give it one more try with them, so I know the better things to order.

The ambience is lovely, but disappointed that my waitress recommended so strongly what a few people later told me was their least favorite diah

The place was lively and the decors looked bright and lovely. We tried oysters (the fried shallot was so interesting), crab fried rice (yummy and solid) and steam fish (delicious!!). I would recommend this spot!
Tom tom soup was so delicious. very Fresh seafood. The coconut curry was also good just very spicy!! Would love to come back and try more of the menu

heard so many good things about this restaurant and it did not disappoint! all the food was so flavorful and balanced, but a bit pricey bc it seems to be a slightly upscale thai restaurant. would rec coming here with 3+ people to try different dishes

we happened to come during happy hour, so we got a dozen oysters for $18 and cocktails for $11 each. the sauce and fried garlic condiments made the oysters so delicious and unique that I literally want to eat oysters like this forever. I liked the only pad thai on the menu cocktail more than the tongue and cheek just because the tangy flavor was so unique and well-balanced.

the zabb wings were so crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, and each wing was huge. the coconut crab curry was also really good, but I wish there was more meat or substance to go with the amount of sauce. since the curry was so rich, I liked how the crab aob woonsen was lighter, with thin noodles and sizable pieces of crab. 

the ice cream bo lan dessert was just good, but our ice cream was pretty melted upon arrival, probably bc the sticky rice is warm. I wish the jackfruit pieces were larger bc I found myself digging through the ice cream to find the tiny pieces

Food was delicious! I was in New York for the weekend and just happened upon this spot. Their cocktail menu was impressive, and the wings are a must! Service was great and they make it easy by allowing you to pay via QR code at the table. I also recommend the coconut crab curry- delicious!!!

A love letter to Fish Cheeks ~

I've heard everyone + their mom rave about this place, and I concur -- this was probably some of the best Thai food I've ever had! I came here with 4 others for lunch last Sunday (we'd made a reservation around a week prior), and we all loved our experience, from the service to the food. 

To start, we shared a dozen oysters ($18; part of their happy hour deal, which runs from 12-6 all week). These were some of the freshest oysters I've tasted -- it also came with a green sauce that was sooo flavorful and complemented the oysters extremely well. We also ordered the Zabb Wings ($15 for four large pieces), whose exterior was perfectly fried and whose seasoning was simultaneously spicy and sweet. 

For our mains, we shared the coconut crab curry ($30), prawn karee ($28), and steamed fish ($40), all of which were delightful. The coconut crab curry came with sizable chunks of crab; the prawn karee was unique and contained silky scrambled eggs; the steamed fish (branzino) was SO tender and dressed with a chili sauce that tasted clean yet packed a punch. 

We ended up paying around $35 pp -- not cheap, but definitely not bad considering the quality of the food and the fact that we were full for hours thereafter. 

....and that ends my glowing review on Fish Cheeks. A must-try when you're in New York -- I'll be back.

Great Thai food with great ambiance - I made reservations a week in advance but it wasn't super busy when I went. I ordered the crab curry and prawn with egg dish which were both super packed with flavor. The crab curry is SPICY -- I wasn't able to finish it because it was too spicy for me. However, the menu did say this had 3 chili signs next to it so I'm not sure why I thought it wasn't spicy! LOL

The prawn with egg was my favorite dish and paired perfectly with rice. The prawns was really easy to eat since the shell came out super easily! The restaurant is also very aesthetic and makes for great pictures.

I've seen this spot recommended on Tik Tok consistently over the last month, and this place definitely lived up to expectations! We were able to grab a table for two on an early Sunday afternoon with no reservations. This trendy spot is absolutely beautiful inside, and the flavors of the dishes we had match the stunning ambiance. We tried:

- Green Curry: One of the few vegetarian/vegan friendly items on the menu. The vegetables rotate by season, and the flavor and heartiness of the dish make it a perfect dish to share.
- Crab Fried Rice: Probably my favorite of the two dishes we tried. They truly didn't skip out on the "crab" part of the dish. The umaminess imparted by the sauce left us wanting to order a second helping!

Overall, highly recommend Fish Cheeks for a lovely brunch or dinner in the East Village. I'll be back!
My favorite restaurant in NYC!!!!! Especially the fish in the sour broth!!!! As well as the Tom yum soup... so good!!!

If I could give this place a sixth star, I would have! It's arguably some of the best thai food in Manhattan which is a high honor. The flavor profiles of every dish were so balanced and rich at the same time. The aesthetic of the restaurant is very nice and bright. I was able to find a reservation for 8 people 2 days before Saturday, so it's not too hard to get a spot too. The idea seems more to share all the plates and order a lot because the portions are not that big. 

We ordered:

Coconut Crab Curry: a must-get! little bit of kick with the spice but just enough to bring out the curry flavors, taste explosion in your mouth!
Oysters: very fresh with some good sauce
Crab Fried Rice: another must-get! probably some of the best fried rice I've ever had, the crab flavor is subtle in this dish, adding the sauces makes it a whole different dish 
Crab Aob Woonsen: the crab itself was very tender, noodles were good but nothing special 
Vegan Green Curry: a more subtle curry with a bit more sweetness than spice, very delicious 
Pandan Ice cream: the flavor changed with each bite, really delicious 

I will come back here many times!

Ngl this place made me reevaluate what I rank as 5 stars. THIS PLACE IS UNDENIABLY 5 STARS. 

I ordered:
Bangkok Mule (not my cup of tea but someone I ate with loved it)
1/2 Oysters (toppings and sauce are delicious. Sort of spicy. Unique flavor)
Zabb Wings (citrusy and kind of tart. Crispy texture! Really good.)
Tom Yum (My favorite!! If you love ceviche you're gonna love this. REALLY hit the spot)
Coconut Crab Curry (creamy and excellent. It does get pretty spicy. It creeps up on you and will make you sweat but not overpowering)

Also great service. The waitress checked up on us regularly and was very attentive. 100% will go again.

One of the best meals I've had in a while - excellent and strong flavors in every dish. Came with 4 friends and we ordered the shrimp curry, crab curry, oysters, zabb wings, and steamed fish. The steamed fish was definitely my favorite dish. The sauce it's cooked in is citrusy - I could just eat that sauce with the rice. Seasoning on the zabb wings was all so great. And the sauce that you put on the oysters was so fresh and cut through the briny flavor of oysters. Couldn't recommend this place more. Meal total came out to around $35/person which is great considering how full we were and how good the food was.

I'm a snob when it comes to to Thai. For a Thai place in nyc- this is great for authentic Thai. However, i often have to fish out too many things out of my curry ( lemon grass, shells, bay leaves etc). I also don't like that i cannot change the spice level.

Super cute spot. My favorite was the Tom yum. The seafood and fish in it tasted super fresh. The wings were recommended and they were yummy, very lime-y which I love. The pork cheeks were good too, the dipping sauce that comes with it is delish. The decor was cute and the servers were quick and friendly!

I love the coconut crab curry but it is definitely on the spicy side! We also got the tom yum soup and the 3 crab shrimp. Tom yum soup was good and very flavourful and the shrimp as well (also pretty spicy)

There's happy hour until 6 for cocktails and oysters. Service is pretty good, they checked on us fairly often

Vibes overall are pretty good, went pretty early (5:30) so it was still bright out

Overall very tasty (but spicy) Thai food

Fish Cheeks is one of the more unique Thai restaurants in the city. There were many dishes on the menu that I had not seen before and I was excited to give it a shot. 

I went on a Friday afternoon with a few buddies and we were seated in the outdoor seating area. I got the Green Curry with had some very unique vegetables and an incredible flavor. The service was very quick and the ambiance was great.

Honestly lives up to the hype. Basically all of the seafood is cooked to perfection and packed with funky and spicy flavor. Calamari was amazing, crab curry had surprising complexity, the clams were great, as were the drinks. Honestly everything was fantastic here. Even the complimentary shrimp chips were served with a shockingly addicting sambal. Only disappointment were the size of the oysters which reads to me more of a sourcing problem than anything else, their fried shallots worked great as a topping and the nam jim was great as an alternative to a mignonette. Even the damn sauteed cabbage was packed with flavor, certainly the best nearly plain cabbage I've ever had.

I went to to this long running NoHo staple with one of my usual groups last December. From what I can remember, the service was friendly but pretty fast and getting us to order because there's a ton of people who go here and they didn't feel pushy. For drinks, I went with the "Thank You Kha" listed as "aromatic + tart + complex" with El Dorado 3-year rum, coconut, galangal, ginger, lemongrass, makrut lime, and chili oil drops witch like all their other specialty cocktails was $17. This had a good mix of fruit and spice and there was a definite light heat at the end. Overall, I liked it a lot. 

They gave us some shrimp crackers to munch on while waiting which came with I believe a roasted chili dip which had a nice umami. Soon arriving was our only appetizer, the Crispy Rice Salad & Pork, with crushed coconut crispy rice tossed with sour pork, mint, chili, saw leaves, lime & ginger and served with peanuts. This is an Isan specialty and is one of my favorite Thai Dishes. It could have used a bit more of the Lao sausage and overall it could have been a bit more sour but it was still fine. At $16, this was pretty reasonably priced though a bit blander compared to other spots though I'm mostly comparing it to Isan specialty spots like Zabb PuTawn and several spots in Queens. 

The other pork dish we got was the Pork Belly Pad Krapow for $28 with crispy pork belly stir-fried with holy basil, garlic, and chili and served with rice.
