The pork belly was very tender with a good crisp on the outside and there was a touch of heat. A bit pricey for the portion size but it is NoHo.

Best of the meat dishes was the Khua Kling, a Southern style dry curry made with wok roasted short rib, market lime leaf, lemongrass, red finger chili, bitter beans and also served with rice. This is listed with 4 chilies on the menu and it indeed was quite spicy though there was a lot of flavor otherwise. The beef was short rib was cooked down wonderfully. While I've had better; such as at Mayree which is a southern Thai restaurant; this was still very good and it would be good option for someone who doesn't mind a strong kick and for some reason or another wants to avoid fish.

The first fish dish was the Tom Yum, a lemongrass soup with mixed seafood, cremini mushroom, bird's eye chili, galangal, market lime leaf, half and half, and chili jam. Tom Yum; in this case Tom Yum Goong due to the seafood; is a soup that I know quite well but I really couldn't have much of this due to my allergies. Mixed seafood in Thai restaurants almost always uses squid so all I tried was a bit of the broth making sure there were no tentacles. The broth had a good sourness but not too much and the people who had the seafood inside appeared to enjoy it. It was large and definitely shareable for a group and pretty reasonable at $27.

Their Coconut Crab Curry; a southern style curry with crab meat, house-made curry paste, betel leaf, makrut lime leaf and served with rice has been their most famous dish for a while. The sauce had a good kick though not as much as I expected for three chilies. There could have been a bit more crab but the pieces in there had a good natural sweetness and this is just one of those dishes that works perfectly with rice. Overall it was delicious and worth it for $30. 

The food overall is pricey but it is NoHo. The staff was friendly and the food was overall solid. I would definitely stick with the southern side of the menu and go to other restaurants if you're craving the northern part of Thailand (and especially Isan.) Low 4 though I definitely prefer their new restaurant Kru a lot more.

I had high hopes since I've seen it rated as one of the top Thai restaurants in nyc. I can admit the pork cheeks we got were tender, but nothing else really stood out. Crab fried rice was standard, oysters were ok (but this as my first time topping them with fish sauce/chimichurri-like sauce), and portions are smaller for the price.

I never give 5 stars. I am sorry if this is coming off too strong to you, but it is my humble experience. This was my first time here, guided to this peak via someone who highly and rather aggressively recommended it.

*across all dishes (we had the oysters, corn salad, fried chicken wings, and steamed fish with herbs), what stood out most and was the throughline was the FLAVOR. The kind that's light, texturally balanced, and also just so yummy you could eat it forever yet be COMPLETELY satisfied within a few bites of every new dish.
*from the plates, the tiny electric candles they bring out for dinner service, to the entire interior design, it's cohesive and lovely.
*the way the food looks wasn't to overcompensate for a lack of confidence or quality in taste or ingredients, the food came first which I feel like is so rare, so acknowledgement 

The entire meal was spent PUMPED. 
Cheesin'.
Lookin up :')))))

We sat at the bar and took advantage of their happy hour. The service at the bar was friendly and attentive. The decor was nice and simple (not that busy) and it was a much more quieter vibe given that it was still before prime dinner time.  

The cocktails were delicious. The first two we tried were Thank You Kha and Tongue & Cheek. I ordered The Only Pad Thai On The Menu which was very funky - not sure I'd order it again but it was worth trying. 

Food wise I suggest their Zabb Wings and Fried Fish. Both was so flavorful.

Not sure if this is one of my fave Thai spots in NYC but then again I haven't tried a lot in the city. I would say I'd prefer Thai Diner for its more expansive menu and upbeat energy.

I've heard so many good things about this restaurant and I am so glad to try it. I went during HH and ordered two drinks. Totally forgot the name of it, but the customer service was great. I didn't like one of the drinks we ordered, and they were happy to make a new one for us. Throughout the night, they were checking in to make sure everything was great. Loved it!! 

Food wise- everything was very flavorful and definitely on the saltier side. Definitely recommend eating rice with any of the dishes. We ordered clams and I mixed the clam sauce with rice and that was a fireworks of flavor. My favorite part was the oysters!! They were small, buttery and sweet -- the flavor many of us are looking for. Can't wait to go again.

I've heard great things about this spot and I'm happy to say it lived up to the hype. First of all, the service is very attentive and happy to answer any and all of our questions. There was never a moment where I was frustratedly waiting or searching for a waitress. We sat outside so I can't speak for how it was indoors but it looked pretty full, which makes sense given its reputation. They have a happy hour (and I was told it extends to the weekend as well) and some mocktails as well. I appreciated the fact that a mocktail was mentioned without having to inquire. I went tried the Coco Bah which was a Thai take on a piña colada (just not frozen) with a little spice kick to it; highly recommend. We also had complementary prawn chips + spicy shrimp dip which was a good touch. My friend and I shared the crab fried rice and Crab Aob Woonsen. Both were delicious and the accompanying sauces provided a great blend of flavor and spice. Lastly, we split the Pandan Ice cream which was a really unique and lightly sweet but not overpowering dessert. I'm big on flavor and this place definitely delivered. Highly, highly recommend this spot.

I came here with my girlfriend during happy hour on Sunday. This place was amazing and quality was fantastic. The drinks and the happy hour deal was dope and the bartender was was extremely friendly.

I will definitely be coming back to try out their main course dishes because they look so delicious !

Completely 100% honest, the best Thai food I've had in my life! I've heard about this spot for ages and finally snagged a reservation for a late lunch. The coconut crab curry and fried fish with garden herb salad were incredibly flavorful. Unexpectedly, the biggest hit was the pork cheeks, which were so tender and juicy! The presentation was also so beautiful and vibrant mix of fruit and herbs and seafood. Already scheming when I can come back next time

Delicious--absolutely lives up to the hype. Friendly, attentive service. Bright and airy dining area. Went for an early bird dinner and restaurant was full. Had steamed fish, crab curry and shrimp ceviche app. Friend and I practically licked our plates clean.

One of the best Thai restaurants in the city. The food and the service is outstanding. Each dish is unique and something you won't find in another Thai restaurant. 

We got the wings, the corn salad, the crab curry, the fried fish, the scallops, the crab fried rice, and oysters and each dish is amazing. 

If you want something different for your palate than the regular Thai restaurant Fish Cheeks is the place to be.

Overall I enjoyed my dinner at Fish Cheeks. The service was great, the drinks were creative and the food was good. However, the price point is a bit steep so I would probably only come back on special occasions.

The standout dishes were definitely the grilled pork cheeks as they melted in your mouth the minute you bit into it. 

I also really enjoyed the coconut crab curry but found that the spice level was pretty inconsistent. This time we had it, it wasn't spicy at all. But I've had the chance to try their curry at a different time and it was extremely spicy.

we ordered the zaab wings, coconut curry & the fried fish with garden herb salad. 
zaab wings - while these weren't the juiciest wings ever, they were by far one of the most flavorful. they were simultaneously sweet, tangy and spicy. 
coconut crab curry - they told us this curry takes five hours to cook and you can definitely taste it in both the tenderness and the flavor of the curry! even though it's noted as being one of their spicier dishes, i would say it's not too bad as the spice doesn't hit you immediately, but rather builds up. 
fried fish with garden herb salad - this blew me away. i was not expecting to love it as much as i did!! the fried fish was perfectly balanced with the salad which had mint, scallions, pineapple, cashews etc. and i feel like there was a little fish sauce as well? the acidity and brightness of the salad really balanced the fried fish without overpowering or detracting from the fish itself. this dish is partially deboned so if you're not used to picking out bones, just be wary!!! 
we also ordered the thai iced coffee (which i thought was too sweet) and the pandan ice cream - i would say you can pass on these two. 

the service was great and we were lucky enough to get a seat without reservations! the waiter was super attentive and helpful with recommendations. the space is quite large and lively and casual! would recommend for a casual brunch with friends :) overall i'm definitely looking forward to coming back and also bringing my friends so i can selfishly try more dishes too!!

Came here for a Sunday lunch; it's such a cute spot with delicious food!

We ordered the happy hour oysters to start--oysters were fresh, and the sauce was flavorful and tangy. It's a pretty good deal so I would highly recommend ordering if you're able to come during their happy hour times.

In addition, we had the grilled pork cheeks, crab aob woonsen, and the corn salad (gotta get your veggies in)! Veggies were tossed in a vinaigrette that was light and refreshing, but still tangy. Pork cheeks were flavorful and tender, but I think my favorite was the crab. The dish doesn't come with a ton of crab meat, if that's what you're looking for, but the crab flavor really does come through in the noodles, which I enjoyed. It also came with some more of the green sauce that came with the oysters, but honestly I think the noodles were already flavorful enough to where I actually preferred without the sauce!

Overall definitely recommend this place!

Absolutely love this place , when you walk in and sit down it's just a breathe of fresh air  the food is full of flavor and freshness which is why I like it so much , it was recommended by my fellow foodie Rob . Such a good place after work or for a nice lunch/ dinner date . They also have a good happy hour if you can catch it .

Fish Cheeks is the place to go for high end tapas. I hadn't tried many of these dishes before, but this restaurant was the perfect way to introduce myself to tasty new foods. Portions were just right, and they were great to share with a group of people.
Amazing food, my only complaint is that portions are tiny and prices are high, I usually have to spend $100+ without alcohol to be full here.

Spent some time in New York this past weekend and stumbled into this gem. This place got recommended a few times, and we were in the neighborhood, so we decided to give it a try. We managed to sneak in before the the end of happy hour, and boy are we glad we did. $9 for 1/2 dozen oysters and $11 dollar cocktails (that's basically free). We ordered a couple of entrees with our drinks, but the star of the show was by far the Calamari. The Calamari was for sure the best dish I've had in the past year; perfectly cooked with cilantro, pickled garlic, chilis, and a tamarind and fish sauce glaze. Everything else was delicious and unique as well. If I lived in NY, this place would definitely be in the regular rotation.

Had a dinner with my friend who hasn't seen each other for 7years. We ordered the fried fish and pork cheeks kinda like port belly) so tender! and Crab fried rice which tastes so savory! They all tastes satiated! I'd love to come again! The service is nice as well. Ambience is cosy.

Best food I've had all year. The oysters with green sauce was amazing. I wish I could take the sauce w me everywhere. We had the steamed fish, crab curry, prawn curry and crab fried rice. I couldn't decide which was my favorite. Every time I took a bite of something the food tasted better and better.

crab fried rice is my go-to. The sesame cocktail and fish sauce cocktail are surprisingly so good. The only flaw is the wait for the restroom is ridiculously long. Maybe they should add another toilet.

This place is not worth the price, even for happy hour.

We made a reservation for 5pm happy hour on a Thursday night. We ordered 4 drinks ($44), pork cheeks ($17), coconut crab curry ($30), and one other thing I can't remember because I started writing this review months ago and just decided to finish it. All I remember about this dinner is that was overpriced, there were barely any vegetables in the already over priced dishes, and finally our waiter put on an overly excited fake waiter voice that was frankly condescending and annoying. 

There are plenty of more authentic options in town that taste better and have better value.

This is my 3rd time coming to this restaurant and it never disappoints, I ordered the steamed fish with Thai herbs, zabb wings and 3 dozen oysters. The subtle kick from the chili lime wings is always amazing, the fresh oysters with the fried shallots and green salsa are the perfect combo and fish is great too, def alil spicy tho with the red peppers so just make sure to not eat that if you don't like spice. For the drink I ordered the pandan lemongrass iced tea, it wasn't my favorite but I wanted to branch out a-little bit, I love the ambiance and service. My friends also got some drinks and extra dishes that I didn't fry but they all enjoyed it. I do have to say though since the last time I was here the prices have gone up but I guess that's not surprising. Also it was for my birthday so they brought out 3 ice creams for the table. Only downside I have to say is that they didn't ask if we wanted that many but it was a nice gesture. and they put the ice cream on the bill and auto charged 20% gratuity and NY tax so it definitely is a little pricey~ bill came out to about 460 dollars. But other than that great food and great service

Had made reservations, something I'd highly recommend. This place gets super busy and for a reason. We had made reso's for a table of 5 and got a very comfortable window seating on a fairly cold Saturday lunch day.

Staff was friendly and welcoming and we got started off with some drinks which included very delicious iced teas.

For appetizers we ordered Pakboong Fai Dang ($12) and Sautéed Cabbage ($10) - both being extremely delicious with the cabbage having a slight edge with a nice garlic kick to it.

For mains I got the vegan Green Curry ($23) which was amazingly flavorful and a perfect touch of spice. The roasted seasonal veggies were excellent and in plenty and the potatoes and cauliflower were cooked to perfection. This dish is good to share - the coconut milk curry eventually gets to you.

Service was quick and food arrives within 20 minutes of ordering. Noise levels were on the lower end and the overall ambiance and setup of the place was very warm. Will definitely visit again!

THE STEAMED FISH - chefs kiss. I would come here just to eat that. Had the pork cheek appetizer, also very good. The waiter warned us about the spiciness of crab curry, but my friend said it was "going to be okay". Let me tell you, I was not okay. It was way too spicy for me (I have low tolerance), at one point it just tasted like pain. Even my friend who has a higher spice tolerance was sweating. Doesn't mean it wasn't good! Just not for me.

100% will continue to be a patron and hope to come back with a larger group so we can try more things at once.

Food: 5/5
Service: 4.5/5
Ambiance: 4.5/5

Fish cheeks is the most reservation I've made in 2022. My Resy could prove it. I love every food I've tried here, and the cocktails are fun, innovative, and of course delicious.
My favorite cocktail is tounge and cheek but all the other ones are great as well. 

I repeated so many orders, and to name a few, my favorites are:

1. Oysters: the mixture of fried onion and the sauce are amazing. The crunchiness, the herb from the sauce and the saltiness was the perfect combo.

2. Steamed whole fish: it has a very fresh flavor that you usually don't get in seafood. 

3. Pork cheeks: if you don't like fatty pork, this is a must try!

Overall, this place has the perfect casual setting for food and drinks!

This used to be our #1 favorite restaurant in NYC. We ate here several times a year and always brought out-of-town guests. Sadly the last three visits have been very disappointing. Today was the worst. So bad, that I think this may be our last visit. The chicken wings which were one of our favorite dishes was mediocre at best, the chicken was SO DRY, it tasted like cardboard covered in limey spice, must have been previously frozen (?). 

The VERY EXPENSIVE crab curry, was nothing like it had been the previous years when we first started eating here. Today there were only a few disappointing specks of crab and the sauce was so overly spicey it was barely palatable. Same for the crab fried rice, I don't think I found one crab, (it was $30, for basically, rice with egg & side of sauce)  

In the past, those two dishes were out of this world! full of chunks of crab and the dishes were incredibly delicious.

WHY can't restaurants stay consistent?? why start cutting corners while charging the same?? You lost me as a loyal customer. VERY SAD!

Honestly I do not understand the hype. The menu is overpriced and the portions are small- I rather much go to Elmhurst and get an authentic meal. Even happy hour is pricey, although the tongue and cheek cocktail is quite good. I went to celebrate my birthday and still felt a little hungry even though we ordered a lot of dishes.

Awesome food and service! Vinny, our server, was attentive, very friendly and let us know about the dishes on the menu. 
This place has the best calamari. The flavors are awesome. Sweet, slightly spicy and cook perfectly. 
Crab fried rice is a must. Full of crab flavor. And you must try the side sauce with it (nice, citrusy). 
Prawn Karee was delicious. Get rice on the side to lap up that sauce. You get 3 prawns with the dish. 
Steam fish was our favorite. They de-bone most of the fish, put it back together and cook it to perfection. Great citrus flavor. You actually can't tell it's fish. Super yummy
Came here during happy hour and got multiple glasses of wine.  
Fantastic service by the whole team here. Our water glasses were always full. They cleared our glasses and dishes as we finished. And they constantly checked up on us.

Really disappointing experience here. The food was good, that is true. However, two things really spoiled the evening for us.

1. We asked the waiter what the special was, and he strongly recommended the tiger shrimps special. However, it was actually a single tiger shrimp, for $28. When it came to the table, I actually laughed at the portion being served to our party of 6. We felt misled by the waiter, and ended up ordering a second just so everyone could have a taste. However, the two pieces of shrimp were not worth the $56 (this was also pre-tax!).

2. At the end when we received the check, the waiter handed the POS system to me to pay, and the tip options were 15%/20%/25%. He didn't indicate that a 20% gratuity was already applied since we were a party of 6. I had to ask to double check and he actually seemed upset that I asked. It felt like he was hoping we would add 20% on top of the 20% that was included. Overall this behavior felt very scummy and soured the overall experience.

I've been here before a few times so really disappointed by this experience and will not be coming again.

Expect long waits on weekends and holidays--I'd make reservations ahead! Restaurant had a nice ambiance. The server was friendly and helpful in explaining the menu. The coconut crab curry was creamy and had a slight kick to it so don't be intimidated by the spicy level on the menu. The fried fish was cooked perfectly though I wish they sauced it better since it was on the bottom. Overall good first time experience.

When I was in the area to pick up food for the plane ride. This spot caught my eye. I saw John legend visit here 5 years ago, so I'm like let me check it out too. 
.
It was warned this thai place is not your typical thai food like pad thai. It's more unique and twist on the cooking. So I'm like I must come try if it's not the regular thai food. 
.
What caught my attention was steamed 
Branzino seabass. It is a salt water fish. It was filet and barely bones. There is fish skin which I don't like and had to scrape it off but it was easy. There were no fish scales which was a plus at least. 
.
The presentation was good. It had a good broth to it. All I needed was a bowl of jasmine rice. Loved all the thai herbs, basil, lemongrass, lime, thai chili. The fish was cooked perfectly. I couldn't help it but keep on scooping the sauce on the fish and over my rice with all the fresh herbs. 
.
It was worth the price tag they charged. 40 bucks. The fish is expensive, also around 15.99 a Lb when I did a brief research.  if you love fish or want to try something new, I highly recommend it.  
.
Also they have happy hour from noon to 6pm. I took advantage and order the specialty cocktails which was the lychee flavor one. The server suggested that will go good with the fish. It sure did paired well. The specialty cocktail was 11 bucks vs 17 which I had the night before at some speakeasy bar. So it was a good deal in new york for a specialty cocktail. 
.
Overall it hit the spot and will be back to try other dishes.i left with satisfaction, different, and a good experience. Hope this helps and thanks for reading! Have a yelptastic day!
This is a great spot, packed on a weekend.  Service was friendly and fast.  The curry was very tasty but extremely spicy!  I can do spice but this one was too much.

If you enjoy sour and Thai spices/herb try the steamed fish! It comes so quick too and apparently they prepare it all the time so we don't have to wait the whole time for the fish to steam from the beginning. The soup is delicious with fresh and tender fish. We also got zabb wings (big pieces), the out side seasoning is good, not super sour and salty enough but the inside need more marination/flavoring. We also got happy hour oyster, they are ok and small sizes. This isn't a typical American Thai restaurant and def try it if you are tired of getting pad Thai all the time!

Came here for dinner on a Friday night with a friend - make reservations. We ordered the wings and pork cheeks for appetizers. Shared the fried fish salad and crab fried rice. The wings were spiced perfectly and the cheeks were so juicy and tender. The crab rice was delicious and the fried fish was so refreshing.

Could. Not. Say. Better. Things. 

This restaurant has impressed from beer/wine/cocktail list to a couple of sneaky amazing desserts and everything in between. Service included.

Favorites have included the pork cheeks, crab fried rice and curry, wings, pork crispy salad, prawn karee, I'm running out of things to complement. Except I'm not - the whole menu has delighted. 

The environment feels lighthearted and fun - and it isn't your corner store Thai spot. This is next level.

Worth the wait and it will continue to be in the rotation. Looking forward to Fish Cheeks continuing to evolve.

I'm so happy this place expanded.  It's way more spacious and your more likely to get a seat if you get there before peak hours. They make the best Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs.  The BEST whole fish I've had, ever.  If you like fish just order it.  It's so delicious. We also ordered the Som Tom Salad and Manila Clams which were also tasty add ons.  Will be back!

By far my favorite restaurant in NYC! Every dish is amazing! I specifically love the steam fish! Very fresh and tasty! Fried chicken is super juicy and crispy. Crab fried rice is also very yummy! Haven't tried their fried fish, will do on my next visit.

author.name: Iron A.
author.location: Lower East Side, New York, NY

reviews.review:
One of my favorite spots in NYC! Everything is so fresh and delicious. Would definitely recommend making a reservation in advance if you can to avoid a wait or go either for a late lunch/early dinner. 

The zapp wings and coconut crab curry were my two favorite menu items and can't be missed. Just a heads up -- the coconut curry is VERY spicy (but delicious!) The corn salad is also a great refreshing side. 

Overall great / trendy spot for Thai food!

The food was definitely not the best in all Thai restaurants in NYC, the review was good and some friends recommended, but when I finally got chance to try it, I was disappointed. However, the Happy Hour oyster was great! $18/dozen is much better than those $1 oysters. The waiter was nice and very attentive, I spilled beer and broke the glass, I got a new beer right away, free of charge :) 
The food was really just okay, I came here for the raw shrimp, I was very disappointed, it didn't taste like the one at Somtum Der. Other dishes were just average nothing special.

I truly wish there was an option for extra well done wings. The flavor was amazing but my stomach turned as soon as I saw the pink. It's a bustling place so, in order to turn tables over quickly, they bring the food out quickly! Which is great except when we are taking about undercooked chicken. It's a popular place and the aromas were divine. The fried rice was divine!

Okay so... trust me when I say this has been my FAVORITE eating experience in New York City thus far. Don't expect your typical Thai dishes (like pad thai, pad see ew, etc.), because Fish Cheeks is such an innovative Thai restaurant that has a lot of fun playing with Thai flavors throughout its dishes. 

Honestly, huge shoutout to one of my childhood friends for hosting his birthday dinner here. I wouldn't have been able to try so much of the menu if it hadn't been for the fact that he literally ordered half the menu for the party. You can probably tell that we ate so much based on the number of pictures I have attached to this post (sorry for the blurriness in half of them... I was too excited). I'll list my favorites because otherwise there would be too much to go through: 

- Coconut Crab Curry: the dish that everyone raves about here. There's a good reason why. So creamy, with big chunks of crab... omg. The spice didn't impact me but I could definitely tell there was a kick. Beware if you don't have as good of a spice tolerance. 
- Dungeness Crab: okay, usually I'm quite skeptical of dishes that look this good because my assumption is that it's merely for the aesthetic. But WOW, I also loved the creaminess in this crab dish, but there was SO. MUCH. CRAB. They really didn't skimp with this one. Just. wow. 
- Grilled Pork Cheek: This is the perfect dish if you want something meaty on your table. I'm a big fan of fatty meat cuts generally, but this pork cheek was the perfect balance between fat and meat. I was really surprised that I liked this dish as much as I did. 
- Pandan Ice Cream: I am a HUGE fan of anything and everything pandan. I loved the use of Southeast Asian flavors and fruits to make such a light, refreshing end of the meal. Definitely reminded me of my childhood growing up as a Southeast Asian kid. 

Loved the pandan juice that came with our party shots in the beginning. What a fun way to start the meal. I also had two cocktails: Tongue & Cheek and Spicy Mango. Both were delightful, fruity, and very alcoholic -- just the way I like my cocktails. 

I could write about this place forever but for your sake, I'll simply impart this last piece of wisdom: GO TO FISH CHEEKS!

The first thai restaurant that I really enjoyed.
The crab fried rice is worth the $27. Don't even doubt it. The fried fish or whatever its called and the isan style chicken are also amazing!!  

Add that in with the somewhat recent indoor expansion or dining on Bond St in the summer with a spicy marg or a thai iced tea & this place lives up to the hype! 

They are no longer on uber eats, but you can call
The restaurant to do pick up orders!
My new favorite restaurant in NYC - highly recommend crab curry and the pork belly. Amazing flavors and great drinks (Thai ice tea is really good). Will be trying to come back asap

I can sum this up quickly. The food was tasty. If you like spice its for you. If you dont like spice like me there is something on the menu for you too. Everything I had was fresh and taste wonderful. You need a card to reserve. When I arrived at first sight i wondered why i needed a card for a small quaint spot but the food, service, and ambiance was exceptional and they obviously know their worth. It fills up fast and there was a line of people waiting to get it.
We visited for restaurant week and was so impressed we will definitely be back for their regular menu. 
We had curry crab
Wings- they are huge
Corn salad
Mixed seafood- cant remember the name but came in light broth. It was suggested because my first choice may be too spicy.
Cheesecake. 
Not one complaint. Everything gets an A

We went to fish cheeks for RW this week. All the indoor seating reservations after 6pm were taken, so we did the 5:30 seating which turned out to be a pretty good hack. It was still happy hour! Not only that, but they let us place a second happy hour order before 6pm and hold it until we were ready for our drinks later in the coursing.  Everything we ordered really was excellent. One word of caution, the Tom Yum was extremely spicy! The Miang Pla starter was amazing - it was like a flavor bomb in my mouth, lighting up different parts of the roof of my mouth as I was consuming it. Definitely a worthy way to spend an evening during RW!

Have been meaning to check this restaurant out -- despite the heavy rain it was still packed! Full party is needed for your reservation to be seated, once everyone arrived we were seated immediately. Service was amazing and our water was filled frequently. 

We ordered one small plate, three large plates, and one side for three people.

Favorites from the menu were the Manila Clams (no photo unfortunately), Crab Aob Woonsen, and Sautéed Cabbage. The sauce with the clams was super tasty and the flavor of the noodles with the crab was good. Unfortunately I felt the mackerel was a bit lacking in terms of how it was cooked + the flavor profile. The prawn was tasty but only had three pieces in the dish.

Overall a nice place to visit with a group of friends! Might be a bit loud/crowded for a date.

Delicious and authentic Thai food! They have daily happy hour (12-6pm)! We ordered:

1) A dozen oysters and it was very fresh. It came with a refreshing green spice sauce and deep fried onions. 
2) The calamari was also delicious, it came with a thickened sweet sauce
3) Thai herb fish that is tangy and boneless! Must try and a very popular dish here
4) Prawn Kare which isn't spicy. Came with 3 huge prawns. It had an eggy, white, curry sauce. I really enjoyed this dish!
5) Crab aob woonsen was yummy. It is glass noodles and the sauce was soaked up in the noodles! Flavorful with small bits of crab meat. I would recommend ordering this too! 
6) coconut crab curry is spicy! The curry was creamy. There are not that many pieces of crab. Popular dish if you can handle the spice! Must order rice with this!
7) Pork belly kaw prow (not pictured) was a great addition on top of all the seafood. The meat was tender and cooked well! 
8) Pandan ice cream was good and helped off set the heat

Service was good and the restaurant is beautiful and lively! I would recommend making a reservation!

This was some of the best Thai food I've had in the city (and I've had a lot). The unique, seafood-influenced menu is definitely a highlight. We ordered some of the more popular items: the coconut crab curry, crab fried rice, and Zaab wings. The curry was perfectly creamy, and the crab was beautifully tender. It was definitely very spicy though, so a warning to those who might not enjoy intense spice. The crab fried rice was the best crab fried rice I've had in the city. The rice was light yet bursting with flavor. The Zaab wings also blew me away. The seasoning was salty, tangy, and spicy all at once, and the chicken was just the right amount of chewy. This place is also known for its cocktails, so my boyfriend and I ordered the Manao Mao (Thai rum with lime bitters and palm sugar) and the Phea Tec (gin and tonic with pear liqueur). My boyfriend also surprised me by ordering the Ya Dong party shots before I arrived. They were made of Thai street liquor and chased with pickled fruit and pandan iced tea. All the drinks were excellent, and the party shots made our experience even better. Also, the service was amazing. Our waitress kept checking in on us, and our food came out fast even though the restaurant was really busy. I would recommend this spot to anybody looking for mindblowing Thai seafood and unique cocktails.

This was a mediocre Thai food experience. The food was decent, but nothing stood out as really memorable. The best dishes that we got were the zabb chicken and the pork belly. 

The service was also questionable. I had made a reservation, and they still made me wait more than half an hour for my table. Might have just been an especially busy night, but it was not a fun experience.

There are lots of Thai places around the area that were tastier, cheaper, and had a better ambience. I don't think I could recommend this place to anyone in good conscience.

Serivce was rushed and came off as rude, maybe because it was busy and the staff was inexperienced.  Food was better but not something to die for and come back to.  There was also a billing issue which had to be dealt with but was subsequently resolved.

I have heard so many great things about this restaurant so of course I had to stop by and try some of their dishes. I ordered the market oysters, Manilla clams with sweet basil, coconut crab curry, and steamed fish with Thai herbs.

The oysters were small but sweet and came with a lime fish sauce concoction. They offer these for happy hour as well at half price. For the price of the coconut crab curry, I think the crab portion was a bit small but the sauce was delicious and had a good kick to it. The steamed fish with herbs was a favorite and the sauce was tangy, sweet, and salty all at the same time. The fish portion again was pretty small but it was well worth a try. 

I would definitely come back for oyster happy hour and when I want to splurge on Thai food!

Came here for a late Sunday lunch with my gf and was lucky enough to catch their Happy Hour, which has very expansive hours. We weren't really looking for drinks but we did interest ourselves in their discounted Happy Hour oysters. The sauce and crispy onions both went great with the oysters, which tasted quite fresh. 

Crab Aob Woosen: 4.5/5. The noodles in here were super delicious since they were soaked in the sauce. The crab pieces were really tasty, but there wasn't that much of them.

Grilled Pork Cheeks: 5/5. The grilled pork cheeks were my favorite part of the meal. If you like pieces of meat that's a bit fatty but isn't overdoing it, this is definitely a must-order!

Corn Salad: 4/5. I'm not usually a big proponent of getting salads at restaurants, but I'll make some exceptions when the ingredients are unique, and the end result is delicious. This was certainly the case here! The corn was so good, and the slight spicy kick definitely was a plus.

I've been wanting to check out this place for a while and so finally my friends and I decided to stop by. We dropped by on a Tuesday night ~6:30 and the place was packed! We didn't have reservations but they still seated us outdoors (which btw was pretty warm for a cold winter evening). 

My friends ordered the fried rice I believe. I got the crab curry. While my friends seemed to have enjoyed their food, I did think the crab curry was a bit too spicy. I have a pretty high spice tolerance but I felt that the spice level was to a point of discomfort - like I wasn't able to enjoy my food fully. It is also a little on the pricier side when it comes to restaurants.

Overall, great vibes and ambiance, staff is friendly, but food could have been a little better. Maybe I'll return just to give it another try and check out different items on the menu

Everything that we had was bursting with authentic flavor - and heat!! The spicy indicators on the menu are spot on. Luckily, the iced Thai milk tea was delicious and helped cut that heat :) we had a late reservation on a weeknight and noticed it stayed pretty busy until closing. Overall a great experience!

This place is truly a gem. The food is light and healthy but so flavorful. I am so happy I gave it a shot the service was special. I got the steamed fish and I was pleasantly surprised by how delish it was and the presentation makes it even better. I will be back!

Zabb Wings (4.5/5) - $15 
The Zabb Wings were seasoned with a nice tangy flavor and a good balance of salty and sweet. The wings were huge and the skin was crispy and thin. 

Oyster (4/5)  - $18 
The oyster was really fresh and delicious. Affordable during happy hour. 

Steam fish with Thai Herbs (5/5) - $40 
The Steam fish with Thai Herbs was so good. I highly recommend this dish if you like its citrusy taste. The fish was so tender and the bones were already picked out which made eating it so much easier. It had just the right amount of citrus. 

Extra
The service was nice but very busy so not as attentive 
Food came very quickly 
The seating are a bit tight

3.5 stars is more accurate, 3 would not be fair. A highly anticipated visit that took us a while to curate. I so wanted to be amazed at the food and setting.
A bit of disorganization on the line at 3:20 pm, even with reservations and then newcomers asking about the process, any open seats etc. While people are waiting, they could be enjoying their first drink, but bar seats are for dining so we were asked to wait on line for our table.. the profits of allowing customers to have a quick cocktail at the small bar and then be ushered to their table has to be greater than having folks occupy those seats for an hour or more. Drinks-seats-drinks-seats..over and over $$$$.
Lots of busy staff, the hostess serving drinks, took a while to order ours. 
(Thai Old Fashioned for Lee, Phea Tec for me)
Unfortunately we finished a dozen oysters and the food was arriving by the time our well made cocktails finally arrived. Very gracious staff despite the awkward flow in service..
The oysters, pristine and delicious, were served with fried shallots and a nam jim dressing, a refreshing slurry of coriander, garlic & bird's eye chilli  and a more sophisticated garnish than cocktail sauce & a lemon.
We shared 2 dishes that were very good but not ones that would inspire our return : The Coconut Crab Curry, rich & not enough heat and the Crab Aob Woosen, glass noodles which are my favorite with precious lumps of perfect crabmeat.
I was really glad that I finally made it down to Fish Cheeks, and encourage you to give it a try, reservations a must...but for me, on to other similar spots in the area.

Most things were amazing. Food was so good. Drinks taste good. Atmosphere was amazing and all the staff but the front check in person was great. When we first arrived we were greeted with a not so friendly person with a long ponytail. Sat us at the table right in front of the door. We asked to be seated at another table and that's where we received more attitude. Finally another lady came over and asked if we wanted another table. We moved over and had amazing service with ren/rin. Again food was amazing.

Food was amazing. My sister me I came here on a whim. There were a lot of people I side so we knew the food would be good. It did not disappoint. Food had great spice and the drinks were amazing. Try it!

I have been dining and ordering takeout from Fish Cheeks regularly ever since it opened a few years ago. I am glad to see that they appear to be doing well (as they've expanded to 2x the space) though sadly the quality has declined a bit 

To start with food, here are some of my faves:
- Crab fried rice (easily the best in the city, beating Thai Diner which is the new Uncle Boons, which had the OG crab fried rice)
- Shrimp in 3 sauces - very flavorful and inventive raw shrimp dish
- Pork cheeks
- Pork belly krakow, though the last time I dined there (this week), the accompanying rice was soggy. A big no no for an Asian restaurant 

Service here has always been a bit absent minded, which is fine for your regular Chinese joint but disappointing for a hip place like this one. Though I've always been disappointed/ slightly annoyed by how bad the hostess/host is. They take a really long time to come to you at the door, even though you're standing right outside and can see them just chatting away with the other staff

All in, come here as it's a "buzzy" Thai restaurant but you're probably better off ordering off of Caviar

Somehow not as good as I remember, but the wings were amazing as were the drinks. 

-Drinks: highly highly recommend the tongue and cheek. It was so delicious and refreshing, fruity, all without being too sweet.

-Zaab Wings: favorite dish of the night. The wings were not too deeply fried or very breaded at all, and had a nice lemony flavor that really gave the wings a kick. The meat was extremely juice and complemented the strong flavors well.

-Crab Woonsen: I love these types of noodles, but without the sauce on the side, I found these noodles to be a bit dry and stuck together. Def need the sauce

-Coconut crab curry: the crab meat didn't taste very fresh at all, and the spiciness overpowers the actual flavor of the coconut curry. I wish it was a bit more flavorful and fragrant, but it was nice in small doses with the delicious jasmine rice.

-Steamed fish: the flavors were amazing. Fish was nice and tender, but not as soft as it could have been. The flavor was so unique though, but a bit sharp

Nice. For its price should deliver more than what's good to great dishes they serve .  

I will go back for the food when the prices don't bother me

This is a fabulous restaurant!  Our family went the week before Christmas and tried many items on the menu.  All were just delicious!  The layers of flavor just mouthwatering.  My favorite was the steamed fish and the chicken wings.  The drinks are very creative and equally great.   Our server, Tiffany, was wonderful and attentive, even though it was very busy.  Do yourself a favor when you want a great meal of creative Thai food!
One of the best meals in NYC!!! Welcoming staff, delicious food, and some exotic dishes that i've seen nowhere else.

Looking for great Thai restaurant in the city? Yup, you have come to the right place! Just last year alone, I may have come to Fish Cheeks close to 10 times and I don't even live or work nearby so it was quite a commute there, but it was all worth it! 

What I love here: Coconut Crab Curry, Crab Fried Rice, Goong Ob Woonsen, Tom Yum and something basil (not sure it was pork or beef but it was GOOD!) 

Make a reservation before you go if possible as we once had to sit outside in a cold day so it wasn't so pleasant. Sitting by the bar wasn't so bad though. 

Some dishes are totally enough to share like Tom Yum and Curry -  You can def order a couple things and extra rice!

Came here for dinner at 9pm (was the only time we could get a reservation for), and was definitely worth the wait. 

We ordered 4 main dishes and 2 appetizers for 4 people and that was a good portion size for all of us. We got the crab curry, corn salad, calamari, steamed fish, and the pork belly. My personal favorite was the crab curry and the calamari! I liked both because even though they were common Thai food items, each of them tasted really unique and way better than what you would typically expect from it. 

The inside of the restaurant was cute, but nothing particularly unexpected or different than any other nice fusion restaurant. Overall did really like the food and would recommend this place for anyone looking for some modern Asian food that is a little nicer than usual
Amazing food! Unique from Amy other Thai place I've gone to before. Highly recommend!

I went here on a date and I was really impressed with the food, the fun decor and the service. It's city Thai food so the price is on the higher side but that is to be expected since city rent is higher. Overall, I enjoyed my meal, I thought the atmosphere was great for a date, the meal as a whole was good. I would easily revisit. 

The food:

Crab Fried Rice- Crab, rice, egg. scallion, cilantro, cucumber served with nam jim seafood & prik nam pla. Ok I think fried rice is kind of kid's dish but wow the one here was made really well. It was the best dish of the day. The texture and flavor was perfect and there was a good amount of crab with nice fluffy eggs. This is a must get. This tastes exactly how the good restaurants in Thailand make it. 

Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs- Whole Branzino, chili, lime, cilantro, culantro, in a cilantro lime broth. This was the only restaurant I am aware of that serves this dish in NYC, in Thai the name translate to fish steamed in lime. I get this in Thailand all the time and I love how citrusy and assertive it is. The version here, while still good, wasn't as assertive but still a good version to try. I thought the sauce had a good citrus flavor and I enjoyed the cook on the fish, I also liked how they served it in a traditional metal fish severing dish with a flame on the bottom.

Grilled Pork Cheeks- Marinated in fish sauce served with Jeaw sauce. I was really expecting to love this dish since it has always been a winner everywhere I have had it but the cheek came off a bit gamey and I was kinda surprised how it was lacking in the silky and fatty department. I would skip this a try something else.

The smell when you first walk in is a little off putting. We came for a quick bite and drink before our dinner reservations. The sauce with the oysters were different but tasted very good. I've never had crispy onions with oysters and although it's different because you must chew a little longer I was not disappointed. The liquor alcoholic drink was good, wine was okay. Rice was also tasty!

Solid 5/5 Thai fusion restaurant. The oysters and clams are great. My favorite dish is their coconut crab curry -- so so spicy but so so good!! I tried their steamed fish for the first time recently and was blown away. The cilantro lime broth was so flavorful.. I'm salivating thinking about it. 

Their service is always wonderful. Plenty of seating inside, but it does get packed during peak hours. I suggest making a reservation on RESY!

Arrived here for food around 3:45pm. We didn't have a reservation. The hostess said it is an hour wait. We gave them my contact number. Surprisingly it was only a 10 min wait. We ordered fried calamari to share. It was crunchy and very flavorful. My friend ordered coconut crab curry and it came with jasmine rice. She thoroughly enjoyed it. I ordered isan chicken. It was very juicy and flavorful. Huge! But needed to order rice with it. Too salty to eat on its own. The service was good. Next time I would like to try their fish. 

FYI: They have only 1 restroom for such a large restaurant with two dining sections and one bar. You will be on the line waiting for sure.

EATS: Fried fish, Calamari, Pakboong Fai Dang, Zabb wings, Coconut Crab Curry
Soooo good! The best thai food I've ever had. Dare I say even better than the thai I've had in Thailand. The food was cooked to perfection, the flavors were bright and distinct. Going back to order the whole menu next time!

After trying (and failing) many times to get a dinner reservation, my boyfriend and I decided to just stop by as a walk-in on a Friday night to see if we could get a table. I think we ended up waiting around 45 mins or so, which wasn't too bad. This was in the summer too, so we were able to chill in their waiting area outside the restaurant.

Once we got inside, we ordered the:

- Somtum corn salad (5/5): Super light and refreshing - I could eat this every day!
- Steamed fish with thai herbs (5/5): Perfectly steamed (and deboned!) and beautifully presented. The branzino was so soft and juicy, and paired well with the cilantro lime broth. Must get!
- Crab fried rice (5/5): Must get as well! Super tasty dish that comes with sizable chunks of crab.

FYI: You're given complimentary shrimp chips to start, which were light, airy, and crispy!

Highly recommend if you're looking for solid Thai food with decent portions. Service was great too - quick and attentive!
Eating with more people is merrier because you can share more dishes and also need to note that their oysters are elite!

Came here for a happy hour lunch. Overall, the food is good. However, it's vastly overpriced. We (2) shared the following:

- Half dozen oysters: Oysters were good quality and fresh, but very small. The accompaniments (fried shallots and a cilantro-lime-garlic sauce) are unique but really overwhelm the delicate taste of the oysters (even in tiny quantities). I really love oysters and would go elsewhere next time I'm craving them. 3/5

-Crab coconut curry:  This dish was pretty disappointing in my opinion. It's quite small with about 3 tablespoons of crab meat and a ton of curry sauce. I couldn't even taste the crab. 2/5

-Steamed fish: This was my favorite item and I thought it was very well done. 5/5

Experience: Typical NYC dining experience--tables crowded together. However, food came out quickly and wait staff were great. One additional gripe:  even if you have a reservation, they make you stand in line OUTSIDE of the restaurant to "check you in". We waited 5-10 minutes past our reservation time to be seated, which I found to be off-putting. 3/5

One of the neighborhood all time favorite, even though there has been many Thai spots opening in the city that has their own characteristic. Fish Cheeks set the trend.

Crab Vermicelli simple yet delicious.

Lobster Salad refreshing and delicious.

Wok Stir Fry Short Rib extremely spicy, 4 spice sign not joking.

Everything else as delicious but I wish I had two stomach to eat since Crab Curry, Prawn Karee, Fish, ... Etc all comes with great flavor yet heavier. It's meant to eat with rice, so so stuffed!

Cocktails were delicious as well.
Happy Hour was great.

Came here for lunch yesterday and everything was delicious! I strongly suggest making a reservation. We tried walking in actually a week or so ago and they weren't able to accommodate a party of 4, only parties of 2 at the bar.

As for the food here's what we got:

- Happy hour dozen of oysters (5/5): were so fresh and delicious. The sauce it comes with enhances the freshness and I could've crushed more tbh. 
- Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce (5/5): shrimp was very fresh and the sauce also enhanced the shrimp & tasted amazing. Easily one of my top dishes. 
- Coconut Crab Curry (5/5): warning. There's a reason why they even warn you when you order this. It's VERY spicy, but if you can handle spicy, it's bomb. I love that the curry is so flavorful and the consistency isn't too thin nor too thick, it was perfect. I would order again if it was so spicy. My tongue was numb haha. 
- Steamed Fish (5/5): loved that it's deboned. The fish was steamed perfectly, the meat was very soft, and each bite was full of flavor. 
-  Crab Aob Woonsen (4/5): this one was pretty tasty, but didn't stand out like the other dishes. If I were to nitpick, it feels like the crab meat was just thrown in there and quickly assembled.  I feel like it has potential to shine more. 

Overall, I'd highly recommend coming here! I think there's a reason why it's so popular and it's so warranted.

Love this place!!! I first heard about them at an event called Plate by Plate held by Project by Project and wanted to eat in. They did not disappoint! 

Our favorite was the Crab Coconut Curry. Just a warning - it does have a kick. With every bite, I probably needed a glass of water but I wouldn't stop eating it because it was so good. Our second favorite was the steamed fish. It was so smooth/fresh and great flavor. 

The staff was very attentive. My water was constantly filled (which I needed) and they answer every question we had with a smile. I would definitely come back!

really love the steamed fish with thai herbs and lemon. The food here is very tasty and light meaning super healthy and refreshing. The service was excellent and the atmosphere was very nice ! The ingredients were all fresh

This is one of the best Thai spots I've ever been to. You won't find many traditional dishes on the menu - and by traditional, I mean things like regular curries, spring rolls, and pad thai. While those menu items always delicious, Fish Cheeks captures Thai flavors in a whole new way, in a much different set of dishes.

It was really hard to choose, but we did two starters and two entrees. The sour pork crispy rice salad is an absolute must, and while we really enjoyed the pork cheek, I would probably try another seafood forward app next time, just for variety.

The crab curry is THE dish to get, the flavors are incredible and we couldn't get enough of it. I also highly recommend the fried fish. The crispy, flaky fish paired really well with the herb salad that came with it.

I understand why this reservation was so hard to come by. We'll definitely be back.

Really good food and I think a very versatile choice for all occasions - neither super casual nor formal. Steamed fish was the highlight, very tender and fresh and easy to eat as it came deboned. The flavor of the herb broth is quite sour though, so perhaps not for everyone. Pork cheeks were delicious and not too fatty as this type of dish can sometimes be. I wasn't the biggest fan of the coconut crab curry as it had a bit of a play-doh taste, not sure if it was due to the coconut or the chili used. Cocktails were solid, if not that memorable.

Fish Cheeks is a must if you love seafood and Thai food. Definitely make reservations weeks out for a larger party because they do get busy. Our server was very nice and attentive. If you make it in time, definitely take advantage of happy hour! Get their oysters and delicious drinks.

For a larger party, we basically ordered a bunch of stuff and shared everything. For our starters, we got grilled octopus and zabb wings. I think the grilled octopus was a seasonal special, so I'm not sure if they still have it available. It was good, but it was pretty expensive for one skewer. The zabb wings were so delicious; perfectly fried and seasoned. For the main dishes, we got crab fried rice, coconut crab curry, prawn karee, steamed fish, and fried fish. The crab fried rice is a great base to eat with all the other dishes. There was so much crab lumps in there, it was perfect. The coconut crab curry was also so delicious with a bunch of crab lumps. It was a great pairing when you drizzle it on top of the fried rice. The prawn karee was, again, another great mix of eggs, veggies, and shrimp. A little disappointing that they only gave 3 prawns, but they were big and tender. We had to try both types of fish they offered. I think I preferred the steam fish because the meat was still tender and juicy while the fried dish was on the drier side. 

Fish Cheeks has a great ambiance where you can enjoy a meal with a large group of people. Everyone was happy by the end of the meal and definitely stuffed. Totally worth it!
I was very excited. ... but then.... Food is super salty . always need a rsvp . The Thai iced tea was great . Everything else was ok at best. Servers are everywhere you can't get their attention. ..

We got a reservation after eyeing this place for a few months and it was so worth it! We got the pork cheeks, the coconut crab curry, steamed fish, and sauteed cabbage. Everything was so so good. 

On top of the delicious food, our server Tiffany was awesome!! She was so bubbly and kind- she even helped us move our plates and dishes around to take the best foodie pics possible! Definitely recommend asking for her. She helped make our experience an 11/10!
Insanely good! Thai food elevated and was delicious, and we'll priced. Highly recommend!

Went here for my birthday dinner!! Great service, our waitress was so kind and helpful, wish we were able to get her name. Overall I would come back, try new dishes but get the calamari each time (ugh it was so good). Okay here's the breakdown:

Steamed Fish [$40] - delicious, but very very strong broth, which my group loved. The tamarind really kicks you in the back of the throat. It's comparable to a more intense version of sinigang, if you're familiar with Filipino food. The presentation was very nice too. We noticed multiple tables ordered this dish.

Isan Chicken [$28] - I'm biased because I'm not a huge chicken fan, but I thought it was slightly dry and just ok, my group liked it! 

Calamari [$16] - you have to get this!! definitely our table's favorite dish, everyone's eyes kinda widened a bit whenever we had our first bite. Calamari is usually all the same but this was different so it took us by surprise. It does have a slight spice to it fyi but nothing crazy

Oysters (not pictured) [$18] - we came during happy hour so we got a dozen/$18 and we loved it!! depends on preference tho, but our group loves raw seafood

Tongue and Cheek Cocktail [$11] - happy hour price! I asked our waitress to recommend a drink that doesn't taste too much like alcohol, and she recommended this but unfortunately it tasted like perfume to me. I'd try a different cocktail next time.

I can definitely see why this place is such a hot spot for Thai food. Its very authentic and not overly priced. 

Not pictured but we absolutely all loved the Pandan ice cream. A big big fan of pandan, I've never had ice cream like that. It wasn't overly sweet and didn't taste like artificial flavor. 

The fish, similar to others, was my favorite savory dish as it was well steamed and very flavorful. 

We ordered the curry and tom yom soup as well. All were fine but the ultimate mind blown dish was actually the ice cream!!

A revelatory meal. Everything thing we had was impeccably cooked and full of flavor. The Zabb (Thai for delicious) fried chicken was seasoned with keffir lime leaves and had an incredible balance of salty, sweet, and tangy flavors on a thin, crispy skin. I couldn't ask for anything more in a fried chicken wing.

Our next favorite was the steamed fish, so tender and full of flavor. The crab fried rice was also very good, especially with the accompanying sauces.

A lovely night out. Can't wait to see what they will do next!

Fish cheeks has phenomenal Thai food. Very much enjoyed the coconut crab curry, although it is quite spicy. Worked for me but not everyone at our table could handle the spice we also got the pork salad which was delicious. I felt as though it was more spicy than the curry so just a fair warning. Both dishes were fantastic and the service was great too! Would love to come here again :)

Incredible. Food is spicy, but PACKED with flavor. We had the cured shrimp (app) and lobster plaa, both were really good. Grilled Mackerel was also really good, but a tiny bit dry. Dessert was kinda disappointing - just a regular ice cream despite the elaborate description. Nonetheless, we loved it and will be going back to try other things on the menu, particularly the whole fish and the crab dishes.
The absolute best crab fried rice in NYC. I always tell everyone I know that like Thai food to go to the cheeks lol

The best Thai food in NYC.

If you can eat spicy, get the coconut crab curry.
Steamed fish is herby and sour. Morning glory tastes exactly the same as back in Asia.

Highly recommend! Make reservation if you can as they're always busy.

Very accommodating and kind staff with Great recommendations. If you enjoy spicy foods, make sure to get the coconut crab curry. Despite the heat, there's a ton of flavor! 

The clams were delicious as well!

Reserved brunch for 4 girls on Saturday afternoon (2PM). It was pretty packed when we got there so I was glad we had a resy.

It was happy hour so cocktails were $11 and they were delish! 

For food, we ordered crab fried rice, Tom yom, steamed whole fish, prawn karee, and green curry.

Everything was so flavorful and yummy. Our favorite was the steamed fish - it was bright, herbaceous, and the fish was soo moist. The prawn karee was amazing as well - the sauce was bomb!

Was so excited to try this place, heard great things about it! Didn't take any pics because I just wanted to try everything and let me tell you, it did not disappoint. The chicken wings were my favorite thing on the menu! The crab curry was very good but spicier than expected. Had to take multiple breaks. The prawn karee was amazing!! Really happy we got it. Our waitress was very helpful and recommended great options!

Great service from Quin who knows the menu and enthusiastic.  Food was fresh and flavorful.  We dined family style.  

Seafood soup had flavor galore, not overpowering, just really good. Crab and rice side dish was so light and tasty, maybe the best thing we tried. Chicken wings, curry and shrimp was excellent.  All the seafood was high quality and fresh. Cocktails and French white wine were complimentary to flavorful food. 

Should have been a 5/5.  Easy to get to that, get a professional host.  I never understand why good restaurants put amateurs to interact with their customers and management is not aware of how they interact. Leaves a bad impression.  Luckily for Fish Cheeks, Quin our server was excellent and turned things around.

Loved the crab fried rice here as well as the vermicelli noodles/crab aob woonsen (not pictured here since I took a video). The beef short rib(?) with the four spicy signs wasn't that spicy but I wasn't a fan of the taste. Would highly recommend the first two dishes though! The waiter was also super friendly and attentive. Had a good time :)

My husband and I visited here on Black Friday around 4:45 for dinner (we had 5 pm res, highly recommend you make a reservation as this place is packed at all times it seems!). I didn't realize I had made a reservation for outdoors, I was worried that it would be chilly, but the heat lamp situation with the plastic zip covers had as snug as a bug outside despite the wind and chill!! 
For starters, my husband and I had the zabb wings and we were misled by the powder rub on the wings. We weren't expecting much, but the flavour that these wings packed was exceptional! Looks are truly deceiving! They were cooked to perfection 
For mains, we got the cilantro lime steamed branzino and the prawn karee, and were just obsessed. Each bite was better than the last, and serving sizes were absolute perfection for the two of us and our baby! The seafood was cooked so beautiful and the presentation was immaculate!

I'll definitely be back to try more things off their menu!!

Also huge plus for clean and large bathroom, they have a large table top kind of contraction you can use for baby changing if needed :)

This was the best meal I've had in New York while visiting! I've heard about fish cheeks from YouTube vlogs and decided to try it out. My friend and I got super lucky and were able to snatch a table without a reservation. 

We opted for the pork cheeks, steamed fish, and coconut crab curry. Each dish was amazing. The steamed fish is a must order - the sauce was so flavorful! The curry was not as spicy as I expected but extremely yummy. 

100% recommend!

Solid Thai spot in SoHo! I've been here a few times and I usually get the steamed fish, this time I got the crab fried rice and I thought it was fine, I'm probably not going to order it again next time. The pork cheeks are also a favorite and whenever I see morning glory veggies on the menu, I always get it!

I do like the ambiance in the restaurant but with how some of the tables are set up (right by entrance and kinda in middle of the walkway) I have to sometimes request to see further in as I'm not a fan of sitting in walking traffic.

Come to Fish Cheeks and I guarantee you will have one of the most distinct, fun, and memorable Thai meals you have had in a long time. The menu here changes often as its owners pride themselves on experimenting with new flavors and ingredients to fully showcase the spectrum of cuisines that Thailand has to offer. My boyfriend and I chose to dine here because we were tired of always choosing the typical noodle and curry dishes at Thai restaurants. The funky interior set the mood for the bold flavors we would soon encounter. We ordered the Grilled Pork Cheeks, Coconut Crab Curry, and Zaab wings. We paired our meals with the Manao Manao and Bond Street Villain. Since we went during their Happy Hour (daily, from 12-6PM), cocoktails were only $11. The Manao Manao had more of a zesty, refreshing flavor while the Bond Street Villain was more savory. Among our dishes, we liked the Coconut Crab Curry. However, it was so spicy that it was difficult to eat more than a few bites without needing a reprieve. The curry was so creamy, fragrant and packed with flavored, that eat bite baits you to ignore the heat and eat more. It was unlike any other curry I've had before. The other dishes didn't leave as much of an impression. The Zaab wings were good although the meat on the wings was a little dry. The Grilled Pork Cheeks were another great choice to escape the heat of the curry. The pork belly cubes were so fatty and crispy, a great indulgent pairing to rice. The fish sauce and sweet chili flavors balanced out well.

Fish Cheeks is a great spot for those looking to venture into more inventine Thai cuisines.

2/5 for the food. The 3 start are mainly for service.
I don't know where to start, but here we go.
The crab meat curry is super tasty. Like I finish the entire curry and the rice that came along. But the portions are .... Speechless. My girlfriend literally uses the spoon and tries to scoop how many drops of curry are in that bowl.. and the amount of crab meat that's in there... even more disappointing. There goes 30 bucks.

Next, we got the grilled pork cheeks. Pretty good. Fatty meat and the amount of fatty are balanced very well. It's a juicy piece of meat. And the portions size is alright. Better than curry. Can you believe the appetizer portion is 2 times more compared to the main dish?

And lastly, the fish.. it's presented very well. You have the taste of lime and salty, which you can tell it's good Thai food. BUT... after like half way through. The taste feels so salty and sour toward the end. Maybe the heavy seasoning is on the bottom? 

Ok. Drinks. One of the cocktails was super amazing. 
- tongue & cheek 
This cocktail was amazing. It is very fruity, and you taste the alcohol, but not overly heavy. 

Over all, a good experience. I just can't believe I blew $160 on 3 dishes and 2 drinks. The portion size is just ridiculous. This place is worth a try, but It's overrated. I am sure you can enjoy some amazing Thai food without breaking your bank.

This place is flat out amazing. Had the Prawn Karee with a side of rice. Everything was A+ the side of rice mixed with the dish and sauce made it all come together. My only regret was having to peel the shell off the prawns myself but that is a small price to pay. Can't wait to go back and try something else.

Im lost for words and can only say this. The food is very, very, very spicy but oh my so very yummy. If you don't die from gastro-intestinal issues you won't regret coming here for the superb flavors they dish out. Overall yes the hours of wait time are actually worth it and you should stick around.

Actually one of my favorite restaurants in nyc, i always recommend visiting friends and family to come here. The wait time is long, so i highly highly recommend getting a reservation (they fill up fast!). The food is stellar and I adore the flavors. I'm not typically the biggest fan of thai food, as I find that sometimes it is too "heavy" for me (pad thai, drunken noodles, curries..). But fish cheeks manages to make thai food light and fresh, authentic, yet very interesting. There is a key focus on seafood (hence its name) and they offer many varieties, including the crab curry and the steamed lemongrass fish. The fish is seriously amazing. It reminds me of the steamed fish that is served in chinese restaurants, but with lemongrass, fish sauce, and some spice. The fish is high quality, and the bones come apart in one piece with the rest of the fish's skeleton. Eating the sauce from the fish with the rice, i never felt happier. Another outstanding dish are the appetizers, the pork cheeks. It's paired with this amazing sauce (tart) that I also drank by the spoonful. The meat is succuluent and juicy. 

No where makes food quite like fish cheeks, PLEASE COME HERE

Excellent and authentic Thai food.

We got the oysters and fried chicken wings for starters. 

The oysters come with a seafood sauce and fried onions on the side. Gently push the oyster meat to the side with a spoon and top it with the sauce and fried onions. They go really well together!

Fried chicken was very good! No sauce needed - the dry rub does all the work. It's tangy & spicy and although the wings are fried, it doesn't feel too heavy. Each order has four large pieces.

The steamed fish is packed with flavour from the herbs but it's not overpowering - you still get to taste the fish. 

The prawn curry is so tasteful and has a thick gravy. The prawns are not chewy - i.e. cooked just right.

The crab curry is also excellent but quite spicy. 

Overall, an incredible culinary experience. I'd recommend getting a reservation though because the place is always packed.

Love love Fish Cheeks. The food is so tasty and they have a good variety. Their crispy pork is the perfect balance of sweet, savory, crunchy and tender. Worth it to eat an early dinner if you don't have a reservation.

Came here on a weekday with a 5pm indoor reservation - turns out we could've comfortably done an outdoor reservation too, since they have a nicely heated and enclosed outdoor area. 

The food came with complimentary shrimp chips to start which were nice and crispy, not too oily either. We ordered a "snack" plate and one of their sharing plates for 2 of us, which was enough food. I would've loved to end the meal with dessert, but they didn't have any when we were there which was a bit disappointing. Here's what we thought of the two dishes: 

Pork cheeks - so tasty and the meat was nice and tender, not too fatty. The sauce that came with the dish was perfect for the fish cheeks and I loved the added crunch on top 

Prawn karee - also super tasty! The scrambled egg component with the sauces was scrumptious and it paired really nicely with a side of rice. I wish it came with rice instead of having to order that separately, but otherwise I don't have any other complaints for this dish 

Overall a great experience!!

A solid Thai restaurant with both indoor and outdoor seating :)

The pork cheeks were SO good! 4/5!! Simultaneously crisp and tender, and paired beautifully with the sauce they gave us.

The coconut crab curry was fine - 3/5. Exactly what you would expect curry to taste like but with crab in it instead lol

An overall 3.5, rounding up to 4.

Fishcheeeeeeks. Great name, great concept. The service and waiter were amazing. Everything was quick and we got amazing recommendations. We sat in the outside tables, so not as lively as inside but was warm and fun. As for the food: it was delectable but not crazy. Eating pork cheeks was a fun concept but it wasn't anything mind blowing. Same with the crab curry, it tasted just like any ordinary curry. The fish was amazing and the shrimp too! Not tryna be harsh, but if you're looking for Thai: try another place. If you're looking for the idea of getting an exclusive res with lil shareable plates: come here

Have had this place on my list for quite some time and was glad I finally got to try it.

We got the coconut crab curry, Tom yum soup, and crispy rice salad. The curry was super spicy, make sure you can handle your spice if you get it. The Tom yum was a very big portion and had an abundance of seafood in it. I kind of wish they didn't have a mini fire burning at the bottom of the soup. My favorite dish was the rice salad, which can be best described as lettuce wraps, and had lots of different flavor profiles in one. I would come back just for that dish. 

The staff was very helpful throughout our meal.
One of my favorite in the city. Cannot go wrong with anything. If I had the option of no wait times I would be here every night. Manager if you read this can I please get a table for 2 for Friday

My friends and I walked up to the restaurant expecting to be placed on a long waitlist on a Saturday mid-afternoon (2pm-ish). But to our surprise, we got seated fairly quickly. There were still a decent amount of people inside, but wasn't super crowded.

We all decided to do family style and share a bunch of dishes to try everything out. We ordered pork cheeks as an appetizer and Coconut curry and Crab Fried Rice as a shared entree.

PORK CHEEKS
This meat was very smooth/soft. If I had to compare it, it almost has the taste & texture of pork belly in a way - almost melts away in your mouth. I was honestly hesitant of trying it at first because of the name "cheek", but I was pleasantly surprised. I ended up grabbing more than one piece. 

COCONUT CRAB CURRY
Although I didn't really taste the crab portion of it, we all really enjoyed every spoonful. The curry is a staple at all Thai restaurants, but this particular one tasted very smooth, creamy and delicious. 

CRAB FRIED RICE
It tasted exactly how I imagined. Traditional fried rice with few crab pieces inside. The fried rice taste pretty similar to other restaurants, but they add their own unique sauces on the side. My favorite part was trying the rice with the different sauces. It definitely added an extra kick to it. 

First impression: It is definitely on the higher price range for thai food. Most of the actual entree dishes range from $27-40. The size of the dishes aren't the biggest either. One "shareable" Kub Khao plate is probably enough for 2 people (3 non-hungry people max). Thus for me personally, it wasn't 5/5. With that said... I still did believe they deserve 4/5 because I did feel the quality & presentation of the food was quite superior to some restaurants. While eating, it appeared to me that they were using quality ingredients. It tasted rich and of the dishes I did try, they were delicious. So despite the hefty price tag for an entree, I did appreciate the food overall. And I'm glad that I did try it once.

I've eaten here and gotten takeout multiple times.  I could eat the crab fried rice for days! The chicken is so good and anything with prawn was amazing! Also the service is super attentive and understanding and great!

**Looking back at my 2019 review, I think the waiter underestimated my friend and I - the fish is so good that it would definitely be perfect for the both of us.**

It's understandable why Fish Cheeks is so hard to get a reservation for. Having been here in 2019 September, I clearly remember how every dish we ordered back them was memorable. Flash forward to 2022 and I still feel the same way. 

Between 4 people, we ordered the shrimp in 3 crab sauce, coconut crab curry, crab fried rice and of course, the steamed fish. It's hard to pick out a favourite when everything is top-notch, but I think the texture of the shrimp in 3 crab sauce stood out to me. The tang of spicy hits you a few seconds after a few bites and it is utterly refreshing and cooling. Do note that the coconut crab curry is quite spicy - we thought one bowl of rice sufficed but ended up ordering another. Wait for it to cool down a bit so it's not too hot, making it spicier.

For the fish, which we saw almost every table order, it was a great alternative to the direct spiciness of the other dishes. The pickled vegetables in there were a highlight for sure, and the tender fish went great with the fried rice. 

Would genuinely love to be back and try their vast menu offerings, though it'd be difficult because I would also want to order all that I had this time around too!

One of the best happy hour deals for delicious cocktails. And also one of the most authentic and delicious Thai places in the city. 

In regards to cocktails, I've had all of them and they're all delicious and unique. There's one with chili oil and another with fish sauce. Honestly you can't go wrong and it's $11 at happy hour. 

For food, I highly recommend the PORK CHEEKS as an appetizer. It's like a barbecued pork but much more tender and the dipping sauce really elevates this dish. The ZAAB WINGS are also a great starter; it's the perfect crisp and flavor. 

For main entrees, the COCONUT CRAB CURRY is fantastic but be warned, it is very spicy!! Even with the very first bite, you'll feel the heat. If you can't handle spice, I'd recommend the STEAMED FISH. The herbs mix well with the fish and it's superb. Eat this slowly because there are bones but it's worth it. I've also tried their crab fried rice and crab aob woosen. Not as mind blowing as the other two dishes, but it's still solid and great for those who need something without spice.

Honestly, I think everything on the menu is fantastic. They've perfected their dishes and drinks and I highly recommend this place!

Fish Cheeks always hits the spot. Food is consistently delicious. Drinks are unique and fun. Recommend the drink Tongue in Cheek. Spicy crab curry and the whole steamed fish are my go to for entrees. This from someone who typically avoids fish on the bone. The spice level on the crab curry is also appreciated. It is delicious and spicy for someone who grew up eating spicy Asian food. The portions are also good. Dessert was pandan ice cream but nothing special. Couldn't really taste pandan. Not a must have. Tad pricy but worth it. Two people with a drink and an entree each cost about ~75 each with tax and tip.

Went here to celebrate a wedding in the family and it was pretty disappointing. We've been before, and had really enjoyed the food, especially the fried fish with herbs. That dish was still good, but the crab woonsen was ridiculously, inedibly oversalted and other dishes were just fine. Next time we'll just go to Elmhurt for places like Khao Kang or Saranrom.

For the food alone, I would give this restaurant a glowing review. Each dish we ordered was so diverse in flavor and I loved the emphasis on seafood. Presentation was beautiful. I want to come back so that I can try the entire menu. 

However, it doesn't get a raving 5/5 rating for me because the service was very distasteful. Our waitress seemed very nice and welcoming in the beginning, but as the meal went on, she proceeded to treat us with disrespect and a rude attitude. Not sure where that switch flipped because our group was very respectful...
