Example 1 of many other rude remarks: we tried to help her clear the table at the end by moving our plates towards her and she responded in an extremely annoyed manner to "just leave it alone".  My friends are all people who try to treat servers and service workers with respect, and I was thrown off by the lack of reciprocation from our server's end.

That being said, I thought the food was wonderful. We started with the grilled pork cheeks and also ordered the coconut crab curry, pad cha, crab fried rice, and steamed fish (of course). The crab fried rice was one of our favorites. The mint sauce that comes with it is sooo tasty drizzled over the fried rice. I also personally loved the coconut crab curry, which was the perfect blend of creaminess and spiciness. We couldn't come and not order the famous steamed fish dish, and I loved the citrusy flavors and herbs on top of the fish. I appreciated that it was all deboned and wasn't that oily either. 

Overall delicious meal but was very disappointed after the service we received.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in the city. It has amazing seafood, asian fusion dishes. Their fish dish is amazing and crab fried rice is my favorite. Glass noodle dish was my least favorite. 
Make sure you make a reservation!

Came back for a 2nd time one year later and I am glad to say my thoughts on this place did not change. The service and the food stayed consistent. 

I tried the steamed fish this time around and although a little expensive, it was delicious! I liked the fact that the fish is deboned, which makes it a lot easier to eat.

Fish Cheeks has been on my bookmarked list for a while. It's really hard to get a dinner reservation but the hostess was kind enough to squeeze me and my friend on a busy Monday night. The menu is extensive and I wanted to try everything. Initially I wanted to order the coconut crab curry but everyone kept telling me it was really spicy. I have a very low spice tolerance so we decided to share the steamed fish with Thai herbs and the crab fried rice. They were both very flavorful and I can see what's the hype with this place. It really lived up to my expectations and I would love to come again for lunch or happy hour!

Heard a lot of hype about this place and finally got to try it out. The food was overall good, but I do think it is a little over-hyped. The pork belly pad krapow and prawn karee were both really great. The pork belly was really crispy and flavorful, and the prawn karee had a unique umami flavor that tasted almost like ramen, although there were only three prawns. The crab fried rice was good, although nothing special, and we thought the coconut crab curry was overpowered by spice, as we couldn't really taste any other flavors in it. The prices are also pretty high, especially for the serving sizes.

Fantastic Thai place! Must order the coconut crab curry and the prawns with glass noodles. Definitely hard to get a reservation here, but it's worth it if you can wait for a table.  Can't wait to go back here and try more dishes.
Omg so so tasty- the fried chicken and vegetarian curry are highlights.  Corn salad is also excellent although I wish it were vegetarian still.

Amazing amazing amazing! I decided to check out this spot during happy hour so I ended up sitting at the bar. I started off with 1/2 dozen of oysters and they were so amazing, I had to get another 1/2 dozen. The nam jim sauce and fried shallots complimented the oysters perfectly. Probably the best oysters I've had! Can't wait to go back and dine with a group to try a lot of things off the menu with the family style serving they recommend.

Note You can't ask for items to be less spicy. The crab fried rice was okay. Their signature fish with basil was amazing. The chicken wings are a must. The curry was creamy as well and their other chicken dish was marvelous.

author.name: M H.
author.location: Central City, Salt Lake City, UT

reviews.review: Food was delicious! The grilled pork cheeks ($17) is a must-try. The famous coconut crab curry ($30) was another delicious option. We also had the grilled Spanish mackerel ($27) and sauteed cabbage ($10). They take their spice pretty seriously here, so be prepared! As for the drinks, we tried the Tongue & Cheek, Nam Gin Martini, Manao Mao, and Bond Street Villains ($17 each, $11 during happy hour) and all were tasty and decently strong. We came without reservations in between meal rushes (~3pm) and had a very short wait for a table of 2. The only downside was the long wait times for our food and drinks; we weren't in a rush, but definitely expect long wait times in between your dishes, especially if you come at peak hours. We also had to wait for our side of rice for so long that our curry got cold while waiting. The table next to ours actually couldn't wait any longer for one of their dishes and just had it taken off their order instead.

Easy 5 stars. People have been hyping this place up since I first moved to NY a year ago and Fish Cheeks did not disappoint.

Made a reservation for a party of 6 weeks in advance - this might just be the perfect party size for this spot. Plates aren't big so we were able to order most of the menu with everyone getting 2 (small) servings of each. Literally everything was great- there was nothing that any of us thought 'ehh we could have done without it.' 

Spice levels weren't a joke but this place isn't as spicy as Ugly Baby so don't be afraid!

Standout dishes for me were the steamed fish and the coconut crab curry (I don't even care for Thai curries!). Other callouts from the group were the short rib, corn salad and the sauces that came with the oysters!
Love the atypical selection of Thai sea food dishes and cocktails. The steam sea bass was the best dish of the meal. Definitely a fan now and will come back

fish cheeks really delivers with its punchy flavors. i had a great meal here and would love to come back to try other things on their menu!

MARKET OYSTERS: these were on the smaller side and very neutral in flavor, neither briny or sweet. the accompaniments were unique and very yummy -- we kept using them long after the oysters were finished.

COCONUT CRAB CURRY: the curry's spice level literally knocked me out -- i wasn't expecting it to hit as hard as it did, and i was definitely struggling through the beginning of the meal. even with the spice factor, i thought the curry was absolutely delicious and couldn't stop eating more. it was super flavorful and the crab pieces were fantastic, although there definitely could've been more -- given the name of the dish, i was expecting crab to be a more prominent and better integrated.

STEAMED FISH: recommended by our server, this dish stood out for its broth -- it was super tangy and umami, and it added a lot of flavor to the super tender fish. overall, i really enjoyed it, despite it being cilantro-forward -- spoken as someone who has the "cilantro tastes like soap" gene : ) my only note is that the fish broth tasted identical to the sauce pairing for the oysters, so there was a little more flavor redundancy throughout the meal than i would have liked. 

BOND STREET VILLIANS: this drink was very fun, both in terms of taste and presentation. it was different from the tropical/coconut-y rum cocktails i'm used to and definitely lived up to its menu description -- its sweet and savory profile was satisfying and complemented our meal super well!

Would definitely recommend this place for Thai food lovers. The spicy margarita was delicious... we had the wings, coconut curry, tilefish and dungeoness crab. my favorites were the wings (perfectly crispy, super umami dry rub with citrus?, and the coconut curry. Wouldn't say the coconut curry is super shareable (I'd eat it by myself easily lol) but it was soooo flavorful and spicy. I had to drink sips of water in between lol. The tilefish sauce was good too and so was the dungenous crab (mp $125). Service was fantastic - I can't remember his name but he was super nice and knowledgeable.

Not gonna lie, I initially wanted to come to this restaurant because the name intrigued me. And hey, any reason is good enough as an excuse to get me to go here again! 

We went during happy hour on a weekday which was a great move: not that hard to get a res for 2 and the drink and oysters deals are worth it.

Oysters: got half a dozen for $9 (compared to the usual $17)! they were perfectly briney and paired well with the spicy green sauce and fried onion it came with

Tongue & Cheek: solid "fruity, playful, light" drink as they described! Also liked the black sesame garnish on too

Soi 38: such a unique flavor! my friend ordered this so I will be getting this next time myself :)

Grilled Pork Cheeks: Ah its namesake - a bit misleading since they are pork with fish sauce on the side, but no real complaints because they tasted great

Coconut Crab Curry: SO good! I'm surprised when restaurants label their spice levels accurately so this delivered the kick I wanted in addition to the creamy goodness and plenty of crab meat chunks

Now THIS is a Thai seafood restaurant!! I had heard SO many good things from friends who had a good experience, and I had to make a resy when visiting the city this weekend. I thought lunch menu prices could be cheaper so scored a 12PM lunch resy (but lunch and dinner are the same price haha;;). The hostess seated us right away, and I LOVED the ambiance. Beautiful interior AND exterior. All of the servers that we interacted with were super kind and explained everything thoroughly. We ordered the pork jowl app and shared the fan favorite, coconut crab curry. It was definitely 3 spice level, and I wish we were able to adjust the spiciness. If it was one less spice level, it would've been perfect. Even though it was a bit too spicy for me, I still enjoyed it. Food was absolutely DELICIOUS, and we will definitely be back!!!

I'm that person who's always salivating over what other people ordered (we want what we don't have right?!). If you're like me, then this place is for you because all the dishes here are meant to be shared. 

For our table of 6, we started with 6 oysters, wings, and clams. The wings were definitely the winner -- huge pieces with bomb spices! For entrees, our server recommended 5-6 dishes so we ordered the crab curry, crab fried rice, tom yum soup, steamed fish, and pork belly. The tom yum soup (so many ingredients!) and the steamed fish (the spicy, sour broth is to die for. I kept scooping some to eat with white rice) were my favorite. My whole table found the crab curry to be extremely spicy and the pork belly was too crispy  (like reallllllyyyy crispy to the point where I initially thought I was biting on bone instead of the skin).

Overall, the food was delicious and I would come back to try the rest of the menu.

One of my FAVORITE restaurants!! I literally bring everyone I know here. My only regret is that I live in Jersey so it's not an easy trip. This was the first restaurant that I tried oysters and I've become obsessed ever since. They're so fresh and I love that they serve it with fried shallots. Their grilled Spanish mackerel was so rich and flavorful. I also love their Zabb wings and they are crab fried rice *chefs kiss. The staff is also really nice and generally quite quick with their service. Last but not least they have a happy hour and the oysters are half off & the drinks are discounted. Enjoy!!
This is authentic Thai food. It hasn't been Americanized. So, if you want honest Thai food, full of spice and tang, without so much sugar, make your way to Fish Cheeks.

I came to this restaurant because a YouTuber of mine came here and posted this place on IG stating it was the BEST Thai food she ever had anywhere. I had to try it because I'm always on the hunt for a new Thai restaurant to try. I went with my friend and we had the crab lobster rice, pork, and the fried chicken wings. I would say my favorite was the crab lobster rice it was BOMB. Everything else was okay. Was it the best Thai food for me? I wouldn't say so I'm still on the hunt for it. But I definitely would recommend for people to try this place out. The service was good, the staff were attentive. My friend loved her spicy drink and my drink wasn't bad as well. Mine wasn't too strong. All in all doesn't hurt to try.

My new fav Thai place in the city! Just loved my experience here, the vibe, the cocktails, the food = 5 stars. We sat outside so can't comment on the interior vibe but even outside you can feel the cool, laid back, friendly mood they were throwing down. Everything was good but the standout was the steamed fish - I dreamt about that fish the next morning. Can't wait to go back!

Food: 9/10
Value: 9/10
Service: 9/10
Vibe: 8/10

The food alone is worth a 5 star review. But equally impressive was the service. All the staff was awesome and always observant to anything we needed. Gotta shout out our hostess Rin who was especially great.

STOP RIGHT HERE!!!
Read  this review and RUN to this place!

One of the best places ever! GET THE WINGS. The spices on those wings are fire!! Also the prawn karee was amazing! Not to mention everything else on the menu is either amazing or amazing looking. YOU CAN NOT GO WRONG HERE!

The place has outdoor seating and the entire atmosphere was very nice. Service was really good. 
I do not have a single bad things to say about this place.

So..... what are we waiting for.... RUN!

enjoy!

There is not a thing that I would not have on their menu. 
Thought provoking Thai flavors that do not disappoint. Reserve ahead, don't miss out, educated service.
Food is delicious but extremely expensive. The clientele consists of groups of younger people (who must also be relatively wealthy) that make a lot of noise.

Fish cheeks has been on my list for quite some time and I'm so happy I finally got to eat here. All the food we ordered left no traces of any left overs. Everything was full of flavor and perfectly cooked to perfection. 

Already planning my next visit to come back and trying some other things on the menu! Plus we missed happy hour so I'll be sure to make it next time.

Returned for dinner and tried a few new things. Spicy mango cocktail was great. My friend and I then shared:

+ Pork belly pad krapow - incredible, the best thing we ordered 
+ Fried fish with garden herb salad - also awesome 
+ Somtum corn salad - great 
+ Pakboong fai dang (wok fried morning glory) - not my favorite, but still good 

Definitely will be back again and again!

Very popular on a Friday night ! Without reservations, expect to wait around 60-90 minutes for a table. 

We ordered many popular dishes like the zabb wings and the coconut crab curry. 
Overall , food was done well, very tender and definitely caution if you can't handle spicy well !! The coconut crab curry definitely hit harder on the spicy meter than expected.
Favorite dish was the wings -- the seasoning on it was fantastic ; and they also sell this seasoning so that you can use it at home as well! (Great purchase!) 

Giving it a 5 for the service as well, even on a busy Friday, the staff accommodated a table change and were friendly and informative throughout the night.
waited half hour to seat 3of us in a small table that only can fit 2 dishes max. Ask if they can combine the empty table and they refuse to combine for us.

Great atmosphere and service! The steamed fish was our favorite, and I would definitely get it again. The sauce on the fish was acidic, spicy, and addicting. The crab in the crab curry was really soft, but the curry itself was nothing special.

We went for a friend's birthday and the waiter said he had a "surprise" and brought dessert. He said it was free but then later charged us for it, we didn't even want dessert so we asked them to take it off and they brought out the manager to argue that it was our fault. Also saw the manager yelling at another diner later in the night. Food was okay but the staff is combative and unprofessional. Telling everyone i know and never coming back

So delicious!!!! Rin was such a pleasant server too. Sat outside on a beautiful day and it was a perfect lunch. Coconut crab was spicy but at my max threshold and delicious. Manila clams also delicious and oysters perfectly petit. Will def be back.

This place was bustling in the afternoon when I came and it definitely was for a reason! 
Fortunately I read the reviews and made a reservation. Unfortunately, we ran over 15 minutes late (the allotted time they'd hold the table), and had to wait for a while before a new one opened.
We decided to come during happy hour to try the $1 oysters, but they seemed to have upped the price. Either way, the oysters were still scrumptious with the sauce. We also followed the suggestions on Yelp and got the Pork Cheek and Steamed Fish! Those were for sure the best items of those we ordered. The pork cheek had the perfect chewy consistency and wasn't gamey at all. The soup/sauce the Steamed Fish was stewing in provided a very refreshing citrus taste, coupled with the savory fish and toppings, made it a perfect dish overall. I think the crab fried rice was alright (nothing special tbh) and the Prawn Aob Woosen was also ok). The cocktails were very fun though! My favorites were the Kushiro Bloom and Tongue and Cheek.
Also, I must say, the service was exceptional. We would have ordered more, but we had allergies in our group, and our server was very accommodating (to the point of even writing a list of what we could and couldn't get-- maybe that's a standard in the area, but if you read my reviews I've had my share of more than bad experiences, so I'm very appreciative of the concern)
I think the only downside of this restaurant would be that it's a little pricey, but I wouldn't say the prices are too absurd either. Nonetheless, I would recommend this place to friends for sure!

Spicy means spicy!! We got two of their spiciest dishes and flavor was great but good golly, I was dying hahaha that's all on me. 3 stars because I think it's overpriced - especially their coconut crab curry. There is soooo little crab in there, it's almost offensive. Of the pieces that were in there, they were more like shreds of crab than anything. Sigh.

Amazing. So glad we were just two and were able to walk up and get a table. We were visiting quickly so hadn't made reservations anywhere. It was about to rain so we took a chance on a half covered table because we really wanted to try this place. So many flavors I didn't know what to chose. Went with the Coconut Crab Curry (no joke spicy), but that was a flavor I'd been missing in my life for awhile. I am still craving it and will be reduced to trying to make something 1/3 as good at home. We also had the Prawn Aob Woosen on the servers recommendation. I don't do spicy and this was a great option for me. I wish we could go back soon.

One of the best places I've ever seen in NY.
We found the place by Google maps and it was an amazing restaurant with top vegetarian & fish dishes .
Highly recommended !

Bomb dot com! Our bartender RAY-RAY gave me and my girls great dishes recommendations and made my first time experience amazing! The food was so delicious and spicy, just how I like it! I would totally come back!

Had the best time sitting at the bar. Ray ray  our bartender was so much fun!  He made the best drinks and recommended the best dishes.  Food was so delish. Even better with our eye candy chef Ross.  Totally recommend this place.

Fish cheeks is always a solid place for Thai food. My 2 favorite items on their menu is their oysters and pork cheek. The pork cheek is succulent and the sauce is just the perfect pairing. I also got the prawn woosen that is not pictured and the Khua Kling to go. My entire meal was enjoyable but oh man the Khua kling was such a fail. I brought it home for my fiancé and it was inedible. Extremely saltyyyyyyyyyy even with rice. My fiancé said his felt like it was burning from how salty the dish was.

At first, we wanted to make a reservation for happy hour (all week 12-3:15pm & 5-6pm) because there were many comments recommending it, but there were no more options on the website with our time preference. We came to Fish Cheeks at 12pm when they opened on a Sunday and were seated right away.
We ordered Oysters, Zabb Wings, Grilled Pork Cheeks, and Crab Fried Rice. The happy hour oysters were shockingly tiny, so it's good that we paid the happy hour price (1 dozen for $18); however, the side green sauce and garlic crisps pair nicely with raw oysters. The dry rub chicken wings ($15) started off with a light flavor, but the more I ate the more the flavor came out and I enjoyed the lemony zing and slight heat. There was a good portion of tender pork slices ($17) provided, which paired nicely with the sauce. 
The crab fried rice ($27) was the most flavorful and came with a side of green sauce and a red pepper sauce but was a little too salty for my liking.
Although the food tasted good, I feel like the flavors started tasting all the same for each dish, and there was nothing that stood out to us.

I sent my friend a text after he recommended this, "I don't want to sound crazy but this was one of the best meals I've had in a while." It truly was and make it a point to try as many good restaurants when visiting NYC. As others have mentioned, the food was outstanding - flavorful and fresh.

I had the Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce and Crispy Rice Salad & Pork. I like spicy dishes and both had a good kick. I partnered this with a glass of their orange wine, which was refreshing and light to partner with the seafood. I'm so glad I went here and cannot wait to be back to try out more items with friends.

Another bonus? This area has amazing shops nearby so you can easily walk around before or after a great meal.

Got a seat at the bar with no reservation and was met by the bartender Ray who offered us amazing recommendations and delicious drinks. He walked us through ingredients and also delicious tips to better enjoy the food. Was an amazing experience and was able to communicate to him with ease about our meal. This guy is dope and I will be happy to see him again soon!

We had the crispy rice and beef appetizer which was spectacular. The oysters for the happy hour is an incredible deal. I could have two dozen oysters easily. Love the way they prep them. The seats at the bar are very very uncomfortable. Hardwood. Ugh. The mixed drinks are interesting but very weak. Bartender was a nice guy though. The red wine was nothing to write home about. The crab Curry special is truly phenomenal. Spicy and fabulous. Definitely a repeat order. It would be nice if it had a bit more crap me. Put the flavor of the carry is great. I would definitely get an extra bowl of fries. The only reason for four stars as opposed to five is the drinks and the bar seats.

TLDR; come if you're a fan of seafood (they also have non-seafood dishes) and Thai flavors! Service was great and food was so flavorful. Make sure to order lots and share family-style for the ultimate experience!

Amazing spot for Thai seafood! I made reservations about a month in advance (basically when reservations opened online) for a party of 7 on a Sunday night. There's both indoor and outdoor seating but we opted for indoor seating since it was a hot summer night. However, it still wasn't cool enough inside. There's also only one bathroom, and there was always at least 2-3 people waiting for it. Our waitress was nice and attentive throughout the meal and the food came out fairly quick!

They offer happy hour all week long from 5-6PM so we just made the cut off and definitely took advantage of that! We got many drinks and a dozen oysters. The oysters were unique since it came with a sauce that had a nice kick and fried shallots. They weren't huge but tasted fresh.

Our group shared everything family-style, which was honestly the best way to enjoy the food since we got to try a variety of different dishes. 
- Zabb Wings: fried perfectly with a dry rub of chili lime seasoning. It reminded me of the lime tortilla chips haha, but in a good way!
- Grilled Octopus: perfectly cooked and tender but not worth $28 for just one skewer. 
- Crab Fried Rice: get this to pair with all the other dishes. It's flavorful on its own and has lumps of crab in it but I enjoyed it as a base for our other dishes since everything was so flavorful.
- Coconut Crab Curry: highly recommend! So fragrant and creamy with chunks of crab. Definitely has a kick to it but so delicious.
- Fried Fish: meat was a bit dry but fried really well on the outside and was a decent size as well. The herb salad that it was topped with was a great pairing.
- Steamed Fish: I preferred this one over the fried fish. The meat was so tender and the fish was deboned! It comes over a small fire that keeps it bubbling in its cilantro lime broth.
- Prawn Karee: sauce had a mix of eggs and other veggies that were a great combination and super flavorful. Definitely loved pairing the sauce with rice. It comes with only 3 pieces of prawns but they were cooked to tender perfection.

Highly recommend coming with a larger group of people to try more dishes! We all enjoyed the meal and were stuffed by the end but the company was definitely the highlight. If you make it in time for happy hour, make sure to take advantage of those drink prices! Food prices are a bit on the higher end but they do a great job on making sure each dish is flavorful.

This spot is a must-try if you love seafood. The fish was so delicious and fresh!

To start, we got the wings and the corn salad. The wings were crispy and had this delicious dry-rub on them. They didn't even need sauce. The corn salad was very fresh and a good companion to the wings. 

We shared the steamed fish with thai herbs and the coconut crab curry. The steamed fish was different than anything I've ever had. The flavors were light and fresh and the fish was super flakey and tender. Probably my favorite thing we got! The crab curry was also delicious and had a serious kick. It's a great choice if you can handle spicy foods. 

The food came out quick, and service was great, and you can pay by yourself at the table which I thought was brilliant as there's no waiting to leave if you're in a rush. A great restaurant to bring visitors to.

An iconic Thai restaurant in the East Village for a reason, Fish Cheeks does not disappoint, from the creamy coconut crab curry, to their tropical cocktails and their Ovaltine and egg yolk covered ice cream. Be sure to do this place family style

Absolutely incredible!! For someone that doesn't like spicy food or Thai food, this was a revelation! Get the coconut crab curry, the crab fried rice and munch on the shrimp crackers. The cocktails are on point too!! 

Was hoping to try to mango dessert but they were sold out :( 

Must visit if you're in New York.

Do yourself a favor and come to fish cheeks. I felt like I traveled back to Thailand with all that flavor exploding in my mouth. Happy hour is 5-6 so make sure you don't miss that bc we did  If we could, we would've ordered everything, but we had a show to catch so we had to inhale everything within an hour. We settled with some oysters and clams. Then came the steamed fish, morning glory, prawns, and this tile fish dish. Everything was boooooommmmmmmb, but if I had to pick one I loved the prawns. Make sure you ask for a straw bc you'll want every last drop of the sauce. Can't wait to go back and eat my heart out...just be careful with the hot chili peppers. They might look like tiny and cute, but they'll light butthole on fire the next morning. Speaking of fire, staff there were all super friendly and attentive.

Great vibes, food, and service!
We enjoyed the oysters for happy hour, as well as the crab curry and Thai iced tea. The crab curry was spicyyyy...but good! Oysters were not too sweet and not too salty. The Thai iced tea was delish! 

Overall a cute place with good food and great vibes.
Absolutely amazing!!! Spicy but we love spicy so wasn't a problem. Cannot recommend enough. The whole fish is incredible

Don't come here for the Tom Yum, but come for other dishes. I felt it was okay, some good dishes some very meh. But my friend felt this was one of the best meals she's had in the city so. 

Tom Yum is way too salty but the wings and coconut crab curry (very spicy) saved the day. 

Service was meh. We ordered a dish we were warned was very spicy and then they left us alone without water for so long.
Excellent service and food. Zabb wings was my least favorite mainly because it was a little too salty for me. Everything else was delicious and fresh.

10/10  From the Hostess, to the servers, the kitchen staff, and most importantly the food!!! Zabb Wings, Manila Clams, Pork Belly Krapow, and the Steam Fish - everything was delicious and on point! We enjoyed every bit of it. so Thank you, we enjoyed the experience!

We came here for restaurant week and were more than satisfied with the food and the service. The portions were good and the flavors were great. You get great value for the food.

The appetizers stood out. Especially the Zabb Wings. The seasonings that they use were amazing! Most of the seasoning and sauces used in the dishes were delicious. The entries didn't stand out but they were still 5/5. Just weren't as unique in contrast to the appetizers.

The branding of the place is on point! I would definitely recommend it!

In the heart of NYC, Fish Cheeks is an excellent Thai restaurant. Great service and wonderful ambience make it really enjoyable to be in there, and the food came by very fast. The appetizers were delicious, and there were a wide variety of entrees to choose from. Awesome cuisine and very varied food options, but the biggest issue was the prices. Other than that, it really was very good, with some of the most flavorful Thai I've ever tried.

Absolutely phenomenal food. The lobster plaa is one of those dishes that I'll think about and come back for every once in awhile. I loved it so much. The coconut crab curry was also wonderful. The grilled Spanish mackerel was great, though I wouldn't put it in my must order list. I'm glad I tried the zabb wings and they were super good, but I'm excited to try something new next time. The nam gin martini was the best martini I've ever had!

Def not a fan...this meal was all around disappointing. The pork jowl wasn't bad just meh. The wings were ok, kinda taste like lemon pepper chicken wings very tangy. The curry crab, which came highly recommended was unbearably spicy. Spicy to the point where your mouth is on fire, ears hurt and eyes/nose are watering and it doesn't even taste good.

I came here during lunch because I heard pretty great things from Yelp and others! We accidentally ordered the still water, which ended up being $10 -- typically restaurants will let you know which water option will cost extra so it just caught me off guard that they didn't provide that warning. But that was our mistake though so nothing on the restaurant for that. We ordered the oysters to start, which were pretty good!! They were a little small for the price, but they tasted super fresh and the provided seafood sauce was amazing! We also got the Zabb wings, which were alright! The portion was pretty small ($15 for 6 small wings) but I did enjoy the tangy, sour flavor. The main dish we got, however, was superrrr disappointing. We got the Prawn Aob Woosen, but it was extremely salty. There wasn't much flavor other than fishiness. Don't get me wrong, my group loves seafood, but the dish kind of just tasted like salt water/ocean. I think the food just didn't taste super authentic to me, which was kind of what they advertise to be so it was a let down. I honestly think there are a ton of Thai restaurants that are much better all over NYC, and since this one has such a high price point with small portions and lacking flavor, I would not recommend this spot.

Wow! We had a delicious lunch at Fish Cheeks while we were in New York City. There is seating both inside and outside the restaurant when you arrive. We opted to sit inside even though the outdoor seats looked nice. I like the atmosphere of the restaurant because of how thoughtfully it was constructed inside. The Soi 38, which is essentially an old fashioned with a "thai" theme and contains bourbon, selected fruity brine, branca menta, black cardamom, and white peppercorn, was the first drink we ordered. The Soi 38 was fantastic, and all cocktails are $11 at happy hour (weekdays from 12 pm to 3:15 pm and 5 pm to 6 pm).

We then ordered the crab fried rice, and it was unbelievably delicious! This dish was made outstanding by the Dungeness crab in the fried rice. Finally, we tried the coconut crab curry, which was so extremely spicy that it immediately caused my nose to start running and made me want to reach for a cup of water. The curry was so hot that my lips were burning, yet I absolutely couldn't set this food down. I'm excited to visit Fish Cheeks in the future and can't wait for our upcoming trip to New York City.

A great meal that I will definitely come back for. Had to make a reservation in advance for a group of four, but typically you can find openings. They have outdoor and indoor seatings during the summer. We sat outdoors and while it was nice because the street was pretty quiet and not many cars were going through, there were a lot of flies and even a dead roach on the structure we sat on which was a huge turn off for the food. However that is Mother Nature and not the restaurants fault, so I am not considering it as part of my review. 

Food here was extremely flavorful and service was amazing. We ordered the coconut crab curry (way spicier than anticipated - be aware!) crab fried rice, the grilled branzino, a chicken wings, and even the vegetables. There's not one dish I would've skipped. The table comes with complimentary fried crackers when you sit down which I could eat ten plates of. We wanted to order the mango sticky rice for dessert but they unfortunately sold out of early. All dishes are mostly for family style and would come here with a group is you can share as many dishes as possible!

Wow just wow! I absolutely loved this place.
It was my first time at this establishment and we ordered the Manila clams , the glass noodles, and coconut crab curry.
The Manila clams aren't in my pictures because frankly I was starving and finished it before I even had the thought of snapping a quick picture ! My only complaint: most of the clams weren't purged properly and had a lot sand. Flavors were rlly good though so I give it 3.5/5

Prawn Aob Woosen ; The noodles were sooo good. As a huge noodle aficionado, this was like heaven to me. I loved the tiger prawns; they were cooked well and juicy. The noodles were full of flavor as well. I feared it would be a little too dry but it was actually fine! My mouth is watering writing this haha 5/5

The coconut crab curry was also so so good. There were actual chunks of crab which tasted super fresh and mixed in well with the comforting yet spicy curry. I liked that they mixed coconut cream in so it was less spicy. 5/5

Overall definitely recommend trying this place out!

I had an out of body experience at this place!!! So amazing. Went at 5:00 and got sat right away. Happy hour oysters 1 dozen for $18 and $6 beers can't go wrong with that!! The oysters came with an incredible sauce that elevated them immensely. Ordered the steamed fish and coconut crab curry and both were DELICIOUS. Love the atmosphere of this place and the service was great. Definitely will come again when I'm back in NY!

I have heard great things about this place and reviews looked amazing. We had to go back home quickly so we ordered to-go. We ordered the crab fried rice and the wings. I was very disappointed with the crab fried rice (attached photo). For $27 (plus tax), the portion and presentation was underwhelming. I understand that crab is more expensive and it is higher quality but I wish there was more crab and maybe some more ingredients that make it worth the price. The wings were amazing though 5/5 so that is why I rate it 3/5.

Ooooh my goodness 10/10/10.  Food was so on point.  Service was superb.  Lucky we had no wait on  a Saturday at 1pm.  Ordered the pork cheeks, steamed fish, crab fried rice, and oysters.  All was above and beyond.  Definitely my favorite Thai place in the city.

came by during happy hour for $18/doz oysters. they had shallots and a unique green sauce that went really well together. the oysters were good but pretty small, I would probably only get them during happy hour times (usually $34/doz). We also ordered the coconut crab curry and steamed fish. Both dishes were on the spicy/tangy side, so I would only recommend it if you enjoy spice! I loved both dishes -- will definitely be back!!

OK I have now been to fish cheeks 3x and loved it every time, so I'm finally writing a review of everything I've gotten to eat. It's a long one.

APPETIZERS: 
Grilled pork cheeks - these are the single most delicious things I've ever eaten. If you go here, and you don't order these, you are wrong, and I am judging you (unless you have dietary restrictions and don't/can't eat pork, in which case it's fine). They are so TENDER it's like eating meat butter, and the sauce is so delicious that we literally drink it. 

Crispy rice salad & pork - DELICIOUS, just the right amount of spicy, so many fun textures. I just had this last night and I want it again like, right now.

Manila clams with sweet basil - 0/10 would not order again. The only disappointing thing on the menu. Not because they're not delicious - they are SO good - but because we paid $18 for 5 tiny tiny clams. That is absolutely absurd and was wildly irritating, but I was having such a nice time it didn't matter too much. The sauce is also divine. But not worth the money.

Zarb wings - the lemongrass powder they use on these is the kind of thing you will lick off of your fingers. I was a little skeptical of dry wings and I was proven wrong (though I wish they came with a dipping sauce just because that would be fun). They are so crunchy and delicious, and the taste is absolutely magical. 

Somtum corn salad - it's fine! It's not super exciting, but if you need a vegetable it is there.

ENTREES:
Coconut crab curry - I do think this is worth the hype. It is SO spicy it will have tears rolling down your face, but you won't be able to stop eating. I love the creamy curry and the juicy crab. I wish there was slightly more crab, because it's kind of like, a soup where you have to find crab meat sometimes? But all in all it is delicious. 

Khua Kling - omg, I tried this for the first time last night and was totally blown away. The meat is so juicy and the spice is incredible. I thought they did a really good job of balancing a ton of flavor with the four-chili-pepper spice rating. 

Grilled king mackerel - to be honest, this wasn't my personal favorite thing. I wasn't really getting any of the fish sauce caramel/sweet and sour dressing. To me it was a little boring. However, I was in the total minority, because everyone else at the table thought it was amazing, so I have to concede that I'm probably just wrong. The fish was perfectly cooked in terms of texture.

Steamed fish with Thai herbs - Having tried this, and also having tried the mackerel above, I really prefer the steamed fish with herbs! It's so juicy and flavorful and brothy and phenomenal. I love the medley of flavors and how well they blend on your tongue with the fish that is just flaking apart as you eat it because it's so soft and steamed so nicely. 

DRINKS:
Thank You Kha - I keep on trying other drinks that are not the thank you kha, and they're great, but then I regret not getting the thank you kha. Every time.  Have also tried the Soi 38, the Panang Negroni, and the Nam Gin Martini, and they are all delicious! But just get the Thank You Kha. It's the best drink on the menu by a long shot. 

DESSERT:
I get the mango sticky rice every time. I know there are other things and they look great, but I am a fiend for a mango sticky rice and theirs is perfect. The rice is the ideal salty/sweet/sticky and the mango is so soft and juicy. 

SERVICE/VIBES:
I have really never had a bad experience here. Our servers are always so kind, friendly, and fun. Last night, we had Clement (I hope I'm getting their name right) and they were amazing. When. I was eating the crispy rice salad last night, I was so over-enthused that I accidentally ate an entire dried chili pepper. Safe to say my tongue was burning. Clement very kindly brought me a literal shot glass of milk, as well as several cups of ice cubes, so that I could keep enjoying spicy food without totally dying. They were super nice and their service was exemplary. Also, every person working there is so friendly and wonderful and ready to help you out. I love the vibes here, it's such a great time. 

ALTOGETHER:
I know some dishes are a miss, but I cannot help myself from giving Fish Cheeks 5 stars, because almost everything is like, the most delicious thing I've ever tried. This restaurant is so fun, the atmosphere is loud but not too loud and beyond wonderful, the food is great, the spice is out of this world, and the service is amazing. Sorry this was such a long review!
From the lemonade to the crab curry, a surprise and delicious. Light, airy vibe with superb service. Great happy hour oyster special too!!!

OMG DELICIOUS!!!!! Had reservations for Friday at 5pm, which I completely recommend if you can get there that early because there's a Happy Hour from 5-6PM ($9 half dozen oysters, $11 cocktails, $10 wine). I absolutely loved everything I ate here and am still craving those Zabb wings since I've left. Service is also super nice and attentive. 

Here's what we ordered:
- Oysters: Super fresh. I loved that they were the smaller oysters vs large blue points. They were mild and clean. I would caution (similar to other people) not to add too much of the green sauce because it will completely overpower the mild, clean taste of the oyster. BUT SAVE IT FOR THE WINGS!!!
- Zabb wings: DROOL WORTHY. They were savory umami with a little zest from the makrut leaves and lemongrass. Not oily to touch, but still super crispy and moist on the insider. Definitely takes skills to make well. Make sure to dip the wings into the GREEN SAUCE from the oysters!
- Coconut Crab Curry: Really creamy and good chunks of crab meat. A little kick. Not the most memorable, but it is still a really good dish.
- Khua Kling: This is SPICYYY. I definitely still loved it and it was so so good. It was savory and delicious. I may have looked like I was dying, but I still wanted just one more piece. Our server did suggest to order something a little less spicy, given the crab curry also has a kick, and I admit I did not listen, but no regret! Painful, but still delicious.
- Pandan ice cream with coconut and taro: It is mild and nothing mind blowing, but definitely needed something to calm down my tongue after I ate 5 too many pieces of Khua Kling. 

Cocktails: 
- Spicy Mango: Wish they put a salt rim to make it like a margarita. Refreshing, not too sweet, and a little kick at the end
- Panang Negroni: Strong on the campari and vermouth. But if you like a negroni, it's good! 
- Soi 38: This was interesting. Can't put my finger on it, but it was very unique. A little pandan scent, but not sweet. 

Overall, I LOVED Fish Cheeks. I'm so happy our friend recommended us to try it. It was not gimmicky or catered for IG influencers. It was unique and delicious and I can't wait to come back soon!

This place never misses. I've come on two occasions with two different people, and everyone (myself included) agree that this place offers the best Thai food we've had..!

Every single dish I've ordered here was always soo good, and I want to go back until I've tried most things in the menu.

The broth with the steamed fish was full of flavor from the herbs and lime juice, and the occasional piece of thai chili added a great kick of spice too. We ordered a side of white rice to have with the broth, which I highly recommend! It had a bed of cabbage underneath the fish as well.

The prawn aob woosen exceeded expectations too--it came with an acidic and herbal green sauce that you pour over the dish. The celery leaf on top added a really nice refreshing flavor.

I had no expectations for the ice cream dessert, but the toppings (mango, coconut flesh, and something nugget-shaped and chewy) made it a nice finish to the meal. Nothing amazing, but good, and I'm curious to see how it compares to the mango sticky rice.

It was a really hot day, and I do wish the inside was cooler--it felt like pretty much the same temperature as outside. It was also a little louder than I would've preferred, but the food definitely made up for it.

The ambiance is really nice but the AC was kinda too weak and we were sweating since it was so hot out.
Amazing food and would def come back! 

We started off with the market oysters which were really fresh and came with a delicious spicy sauce
Market oyster - 9/10

Crispy rice salad and pork !! -10/10 !
This was my favorite! The pork was so crispy and the sauce was so good. I def recc this ! 

Prawn aob woosen - 7.5/10
It was very good sweet glass noodles with three huge prawns but barely any pork belly ( more like 2 small pieces) we had four people so kinda sad there was only three prawns. The prawns were really good tho with the spicy green sauce that they gave with the oyster. 

Tile fish pad cha ! - 9/10
Another one of my favorites because the fish was cooked so well and tender. The sauce was really good and the greens that came with it paired really nicely with the tenderness of the fish. Just wished the portion was a bit more.

Mango sticky rice !! amazing, heavenly, the best I've had - 10/10 !!! Must get !  The coconut milk with it omggg and the mango was so soft and sweet and the rice was just amazing

Not pictured: Pandan lemongrass ice tea -4/10
Didn't taste like much, more like watered down pandan syrup, no lemongrass taste... I don't recc

Food was good but the service was mediocre. The area my party and I were seated in had no AC and we were given lukewarm water on a day that was over 90 degrees. Aside from that, staff just seated us and told us the menu was on the QR code on the table and moved on to the next table. That being said, DEFINITELY go during happy hour (between 5-6 for the evenings) for the oysters. They were ok and they came with a nice complimenting sauce along with small fried prawns to put on the oysters (both on the side)! $18 for a dozen oysters during happy hour. Crab fried rice was great, pork cheeks, and the Zabb wings were good. Highly recommend the pork cheeks! The sauce on the side definitely elevated the taste. The sautéed cabbage was also great but it's definitely something you could make at home. Would definitely come back during a cooler season but the atmosphere and food were great!

I think compared to soothr, this place is more authentic than fusion. Every dish here reminds me of the food I had on my Thailand trip which is very nostalgic. The proportion is pretty big and satisfying. The only reason why I misused one point is because some dishes were a bit too salty for my liking. Here's what me and my friend ordered:
- fried chicken wings: this was my friend's favorite because the lemongrass powder they use is definitely magical (they sell it in the house too). The wings were very crunchy, juicy, and perfectly cooked.
- morning glory: if you ever visit Thailand, you'll realize they have this on almost every menu. surprisingly, this was the star of the night as it was even better than the ones I've tried in Thailand. The red thing they put in the sauce is a game changer and super flavorful. Will definitely order this again next time.
- Crab curry: this was probably my least favorite dish because it was quite spicy and you can't adjust the spicy level. The crab tasted a bit dry like chicken so I'll probably get the crab fried rice next time.
- fried fish: SOOOO YUMMY. This was my first time eating fried fish where you can eat the bones. 
- mango sticky rice: they made the sticky rice a bit salty which is actually how they do it in Thailand. Overall very authentic.

As a huge fan of Thai food, I will definitely be coming back here to try their crab fried rice!

Server were not just amazing but went beyond to make sure that I'm 100% satisfied with my food. 
Although they changed back to sliced beef but the paste was a little overwhelming compared to before. Maybe light on the paste? Just a suggestion. I truly love the ugly baby khua Kling but so way more better than Wayla. Since that I'm not traveling to bk, fish cheeks still serve the best khua kling in Manhattan. 
Steam fish is a little salty and I had it with bass before. So, I think the branzino tasted too "muddy" for my liking plus the cost the lower than bass. However, server came to check on me & explained the two types of fish they used. 
Oyster with Nam jim sauce always my craving. Must try if you haven't! 
Just because Cory was super attentive, I will always be your number fan when comes to Thai food. 
Thank you for staying strong through the pandemic!
Best Thai place in manhattan! I love the dishes here. Everyone item has unique flavors and packs a punch. Don't miss out. You must go here.

I highly recommend the Grilled King Mackerel (not pictured because we scarfed it down too fast). It's not as picturesque popular as the Steamed Fish, but Mackerel's got balance with the tender smokey, savory char fish and the tangy sweet mango salad - perfect Summer dish.

I've ordered standby classics Coconut Crab Curry and Sautéed Cabbage 6-10 times as this point. Always yummy!
we had a huge group so we got a bunch of things family style! servers were hella nice and efficient, and the food was all really good. also, the drinks were pretty

This is the best meal I've had in NY in a while. Everything we ordered was excellent. For appetizers, the corn salad was so deliciously refreshing and memorable, and the Manila clams came in this amazing broth you just want to drink from the bowl. For entrees, we had the steamed whole fish, which also came with an incredible broth. The fish was nice and light and cooked to perfection. The crab curry was pretty spicy but so worth it and probably one of the best curries i've ever had. If you're bothered by spice, you may want to steer clear of this one or order extra rice.

The cocktails were also fantastic. We had the Spicy Mango, which was my favorite and not too spicy (just take out the chili pepper when you reach your preferred spice level); the Taengmo Fizz which has a nice tartness to it and just enough sweetness; and the Kushiro Bloom which is a nice light refreshing cocktail that goes down easy on a hot summer day.

Love love love the food! This restaurant was on my list to check out and I'm so glad that we did as the food was so good and the staff was super friendly. I recommend going for lunch as it gets super crowded at night.

Def check out the crab fried rice along with prawn karee.

My favorites were the manila clams and green curry. They both had great flavor and spice. The clams were well cleaned and weren't sandy at all, so you could really enjoy them. The grilled king mackerel was on the dryer side, but the sauce made up for it a little. Crab fried rice was solid. Portions were on the smaller side (especially for the prices), but food was good overall.

Was lucky to land a last minute seating on a Saturday afternoon. The food is unique and tasty. We had the following items - in order of my personal preference:

(1) Coconut Crab Curry - The curry is thick, creamy and spicy with generous amount of crab meat. This is the dish that I will be going back for.

(2) Prawn aob Woosen - I am not a seafood fan, but actually loved the seafood flavor in this dish - it has the umami of the seafood flavor without the fishiness. The prawns were fresh and great with the glass noodles.

(3) Steamed Fish - The fish is fresh and the meat was silky smooth and delicate.

(4) Zabb wings - Perfectly fried and the seasoning powder is decent. The breading was light and crunchy and the meat still had some juice. The flavor reminds me of potato chips seasoning. A bit salty for my taste.

(5) Special: Pork Belly - This dish did not stand out in this awesome meal and a bit too crispy for my taste.

Was in the area and wanted to find somewhere for dinner, had been wanting to try this place for awhile. 

The two hostesses (two young women) were both so friendly and helpful so it was a great first impression. We initially put our names down to eat inside at the bar but then one of the hostesses flagged us down as we walked away and mentioned that an outside table opened up so we took that- and were essentially seated right away (around 8 on a Sunday night) 

I'll just get right to the pros and cons overall: 

PROS: 
- kind and helpful front of house hostesses 
- friendly staff overall 
- food was delicious (we got the prawn karee which I highly highly recommend and the khua kling) 

CONS:
- expensive 
- took forever to get water refills 
- wait service was slow/not as attentive as I would have liked 

But I would definitely come back and try it out again- would love to see how it is inside as well

Probably my favorite thai restaurant in NYC. Everything you get here is full of flavor and complexity, but a little different from your usual thai restaurant. The crab curry and the fishes are the stars of the menu, but the side of wok fried cabbage is sneakily one of the best things on the menu. The cocktails are all interesting and delicious.

Was so excited to come here with reserving a table two weeks in advance!

We enjoyed the oysters for happy hour (the Thai chili sauce was a perfect complement!) and ordered a side (morning glory) and three mains. 

The steamed fish was the star of the show - soo soft and the sauce/soup was flavorful, which paired nicely with rice. If you can't handle/don't like spice, would recommend to pass on the coconut crab curry - but it was delicious and addicting!

I don't get this place. Maybe we ordered everything wrong. Oysters are a good deal during happy hour for sure and they were decent. Pork cheeks were not bad either. We ordered today's special a lobster dish and it was too pungent. The short ribs dish was extremely salty. I think it was the most salty short ribs dish I've ever had in my life. The coconut crab curry was extremely spicy. I love spicy food but this is too much to the point that the spicy flavor felt unnatural. Maybe my friend and I just have a different taste from everyone else but I wouldn't recommend this place. Service was good though! Btw we ended up spending $100 each (1 drink each) and didn't even feel full at all

Food 10/10
A place that is nearly impossible to get a reservation at, I finally got to try it with a reservation that was at around 930pm. We ordered fried chicken, curry, and steamed fish. The steamed fish still lives in my head rent free almost every single day. Such a flavorful spicy broth, paired with beautifully tender fish, the spices they added to this were really different from how I usually eat steamed fish, so it was a really pleasant yet surprising experience. The fried chicken is really solid, and the curry, despite people's recommendations, actually wasn't the star of the show. 

Atmosphere 8/10
Super cute and funky colors. I felt like as if the tables were really close to each other, but that's just nyc space I guess. 

Service 8/10
I remember things took a while, but then again, it was getting quite late so I don't blame them.

Wings: flavorful,. Dry rub

Steamed fish: doesn't come with rice. I thought it would. Looks like some fish soup. Anyway, flavor was good but fish was fishy. It's not like mackerel fishy but fishy and earthy (subtle dirt like taste like beets). There were several bones big and small. It was good but prob wouldn't get it again. Should've gotten the fried fish but this seemed diff and saw so many good reviews.

Service was okay. I tried to get the servers attention a few times. Asked another server for hot sauce/Thai chilies and he never came back so had to ask our server. They gave us the liquid red pepper sauce and another chili thing with garlic and fish sauce. I love the Thai chilies in the vinegar but I haven't seen that anywhere in nyc or nj :( anyway, food was okay... maybe we ordered the wrong things.

I'm in my 3rd month since moving to NYC and Fish Cheeks is my first 5-star review. Was able to snag a quick reservation off resy. 

What we tried- 

Tongue & Cheek: Love that they describe the drinks in the menu. This was listed as "fruity - playful - light". Very accurate! 

Kushiro Bloom: Clean finish. Both drinks didn't taste like alcohol but got a good buzz after 1 drink. 

Market Oysters (pictured): 
I'm from Seattle, WA. I know good oysters. These came with a green sauce that was absolutely delightful. You could put that sauce on a shoe and it'd be delicious. Tart, garlic-y & spicy. Love it! Oysters on their own were ok. 

Grilled Pork Cheeks:
Good! They were fatty and flavorful. The sauce was good too. 

Coconut Crab Curry:
Beware, I'm Asian and grew up with spice and this def packed a punch! A bit on the sweeter side but nice consistency and pieces of crab were yummy. 

Prawn Karee:
SO GOOD. Love the gravy/sauce it's served in. Good meaty prawns. Must order if you go!

Pakboong Fai Dang:
Tender morning glory with great garlic flavor. The perfect side! 

Mango Sticky Rice:
Perfect way to end this meal. Sweet mango, creamy/sticky coconut rice that is both sweet and salty. So yummy. 

Service was great, attentive without being in your face. Cute atmosphere, would be a great place to start your night. Highly recommend Fish Cheeks!

We were lucky enough to grab a table for Juneteenth during lunch. Their happy hour drinks price is reasonable for NY standard. The drinks were great, very tropical and refreshing. They definitely took inspiration from Thai flavors.

The food- if you like cilantro then you will love Fish Cheeks. 

Highly recommend the steam fish here as the fish is very tender and melts in your mouth.

If you come during happy hour, I highly recommend getting the dozen oysters. The cilantro sauce goes really well with the oysters.

Don't get me wrong- I love their food but they get chintzier and chintzier when trying to save a dollar. The $30 entree doesn't come with rice when you order it to go. Every time I order the cabbage, the portion- already smaller than what you get when you sit down at the restaurant- gets smaller and smaller. I'm going to have to restart my search for Prawn Karee elsewhere.

Fantastic dinner!! We shared the pork cheeks, fried chicken wings, crab curry (spicy!), whole fish and the corn salad. Everything was so delicious! We're visiting from California and this was recommended to us for a meal. So glad we were able to enjoy!

Favorite Thai restaurant in NY! Can't say enough good things about this place. The food is delicious, service is good, restaurant interior is cute too! 

Food: 
Steamed fish - 100000/10 HIGHLY RECOMMEND! The dish is so soft and the flavor is so unique and delicious 
Coconut crab curry - 10/10 so good! Ask for it spicy 
Crab fried rice - 10/10

when the first bite was so amazing you're too stunned to speak

they offer a variety of thai dishes i've never tried before & everything was so delicious! the staff and our server, Rin, was incredibly sweet! 

- pork cheeks - you MUST get this cause holy crap this was so juicy and an explosion of flavor! i could eat this alone for the rest of my life and be happy 

- isan styled grilled chicken - loved the seasoning on this chicken and it was so soft & perfectly cooked! they give you a variety of different cuts too! 

- coconut crab curry - they said this was a fan favorite and i can understand; im weak so i thought this was pretty spicy 

- steamed fish with thai herbs - if you like a cilantro & lime broth, this was super tasty; the fish was de-boned so that was a plus! also look how cute the fish shaped dish was

(ig: @missrubo)

Quality Thai seafood restaurant with delicate potions packing Thai spice flavors and high prices. They recommend ordering multiple dishes per person. Most people would probably need at least 1.5 dishes to be relatively satisfied. Food was amazing. Staff was nice and kept checking on us, but food came slowly. It was also insanely hot outside in the unshaded portion. Seating inside is much better. They take reservations and are very busy. The wait was 45 minutes maybe half an hour after they opened for lunch. Food wasn't very filling and if we went to get tacos and cookies afterwards, I won't tell. 

@ coconut crab curry (9/10) - best thing I had all night. Maybe I got all the crab, but it was very full of crab and the coconut curry was mildly spicy and very creamy. Too bad there wasn't too much of it, and my friend complained they didn't get much crab. I'll order this on a date and enjoy this tiny delicious meal. 

@ oysters (6/10) - got a dozen during happy hour, not sold individually for happy hour any more. The oysters were on the small side and very delicate, deliciously fresh with the fried onion and spicy sauce. We made sure to get to them before the sun sucked them off their half shells!

@ whole fish (6/10) - very impressive presentation, overall delicious juicy fish, but not worth the money or hype, they removed some of the bones, but be careful if you're not used to it 

@ marinated raw shrimp appetizer (8/10) - most interesting item, I liked the sushi-like texture of the raw shrimp cooked in ceviche-like juices

tl;dr delicious Thai seafood, expensive, small portions, takes reservations, very popular and busy, inside seating much better in the summer, crab curry!
Amazing Thai in nyc. Pretty casual and service was a little curt but overall well worth the food.

Fish Cheek is has good food and the interior is cute tropical theme. Came around opening and there was already a lot of people dining in. The service is also decent. However, I am docking of a star because I do feel that the dishes are overpriced and the serving size is small. 

Would I consider this the best Thai place? Probably not, but it's a very respectable Thai place assuming you're willing pay the steep price tag. You should head into Queens for the best and more affordable Thai food. Elmhurst and Woodside are good places to start at. If you're in or near flushing, you should definitely try "When in Bangkok" and "Kin'd"

Happy hour oysters are a dozen for $18, super good deal! The green sauce that comes with it is sooo good (I think there's fish sauce in it). This place was packed for lunch but we luckily waited 15 min.

We stopped here for a quick lunch and the food was pretty good! 

We sat outside near the host stand. The service was very mediocre- the server didn't check on us and we had to wave her down numerous time before she could come to us. We were given 1 bowl of rice even though we ordered two entrees and one side dish.. We had to wave down our server so many times before we could get another bowl of rice.. :( 

The crab curry was flavorful but definitely not worth the price. The water spinach was very yummy and I would definitely come back just to eat it again! The Spanish mackerel topped with mangoes was very refreshing. :)

As someone who has traveled to Thailand, the flavors of the steamed fish was the closet I've gotten to tasting the same flavors as in Thailand! Great ambiance too. I didn't find the curry super authentic, it lacked some flavor, but everything else I got was very yummy.

Please try this place at least twice and make sure to reserve before going. Their cocktails are something I look forward to after a long day from work. Get their fried fish special! You can never go wrong with their Karee and wings too!

Really delicious and cute restaurant. You need a res! We had the crab fried rice and grilled fish. Both were lovely, though my favorites were the coconut crab curry and steamed fish from a previous visit. Don't miss out on the oysters either!

this is hands down one of the best authentic thai restaurants in the city! even though their prices are on the higher side and their portions are quite small, i'm so glad that we decided to give this place a try! the flavors in their dishes are something i've never had before, so it was a great dining experience!

- notes -
both cash and card are accepted!

- atmosphere -
the inside of this restaurant isn't that large. the tables are relatively close to each other but the restaurant was really attractive! it's a great place to take some family members or friends. it may not seem very "fancy" looking, but the quality of the food definitely matches a higher-end restaurant. 

- overall experience -
we came on a sunday afternoon at around 12:00 and the restaurant was packed. we had a really large group of 9 people so we called the restaurant in advance to make a reservation; you can also make a reservation through resy for smaller groups. when we gave them our name, we were seated right away and didn't have to wait long before our orders were taken. our dishes did take around 30 minutes to come out since we did order almost everything on the menu! i will say that their portions are on the smaller side, so they do recommend ordering multiple dishes to share! the quality of all of their dishes were absolutely amazing, but i can't say that they were all worth the price. so, i'll do my individual reviews of the dishes mostly based on taste rather than price. 

- recommendations -
highly recommend that you must try their coconut crab curry, crab fried rice, and prawn aob woosen!

2/26/22
-coconut crab curry: this is one of their most well-known dishes and i can definitely understand why. it's a southern-style curry with crab meat curry paste, betel leaf, and makrut lime leaf with a small side bowl of rice! my spice tolerance is very low so this tasted extremely spicy to me. however, it was truly so so flavorful! you can really taste the crab and coconut which is why this was one of my favorite dishes from the meal. it was $30 for a relatively small portion. (4.5/5)
-crab fried rice: this is also one of the more popular dishes, which has crab, rice, egg, scallion, cilantro, and cucumber served with nam jim seafood sauce and a traditional thai sauce. the amount of crab was fair for the price of $27 and every bite had so much flavor! it's a good option for kids who may not like the taste of seafood in large portions. (4.5/5)
-market oysters: they sell oysters at $3 per oyster, $17 per half dozen, or $34 per dozen. we decided to get the dozen since we had a lot of people, and they were pretty large in size! the flavor of oysters is not for everyone, but it did taste fresh and high in quality. on the side, they also served it with a nam jim seafood sauce and fried shallots. (4/5)
-grilled pork cheeks: this dish came with grilled pork cheeks marinated in fish sauce and served with jeaw sauce. it was really flavorful and cooked just the right amount! an order comes with around 5 slides of pork cheeks for $17. (4/5)
-isan style grilled chicken: this dish comes with half a chicken marinated with thai herbs, with jeaw sauce and sweet chili sauce on the side. this was also cooked perfectly and had lots of flavor in every bite! it's probably the dish that's worth its money the most since the amount of chicken you get is pretty fair for $28. (4/5)
-pakboong fai dang: this side comes with wok-fried morning glory vegetables, garlic, thai bird's eye chili, and soybean. the vegetables did seem a bit too oily for my liking, but they had a pretty good flavor. it was nothing special, but the portion was pretty fair for $12. would recommend getting this if you're looking to fit in some more veggies into your meal. (3.5/5)
-prawn aob woosen: this dish was one of my personal favorites! it comes with three large baked prawns on top of glass noodles, cilantro, and celery leaves. the flavor of the prawns really seeps into the noodles, which was personally my favorite part of the dish. the noodles were cooked perfectly and held onto the sauce well too. although i wished that they had more prawns since the price was $27, i was really glad that we ordered this. (5/5)
-steamed fish with thai herbs: this dish is a steamed whole fish with chili, lime, and cilantro in a cilantro lime broth! i personally didn't really like this just because i'm not a big fan of herby and lime flavors, but it was a table favorite from everyone else. the fish tasted really fresh and it was cooked just the right amount too. it didn't taste spicy at all to me since i didn't try too much of it. unfortunately, the whole fish wasn't that big, even though the price was $38. (3/5)
I felt it was quite overrated. The dishes lacked that extra something, nice and fresh but also nothing special.

Get. A. Reservation. Fish Cheeks is truly that good and the line is down the block easily an hour before they open. A fantastic place for happy hour - even though I didn't end up getting a beverage, they all looked really good and I hope to return to get the full experience. The pop chips with the chili sauce is such a colorful touch to start but the oysters and the pork cheek really stole the show. The shrimp with crab sauce dish was SO spicy but I was insanely into it. Very herbaceous and absolutely sumptuous. The pork cheek was such a tender counter balance and it was a great recommendation from our server. The oysters were amazing, no shocker there, and were so light and fresh with lots of sauces to add on top. No surprise I want to come back for a deeper experience, but definitely the best Thai food in Soho and a very uncommon experience.
Delicious and authentic! Had the whole fish, crab curry, oysters here and every dish was on point. Would come again!

Mediocre food that's comparable to your average American neighborhood Thai restaurant in with a few poorly executed dishes that are harder to find. The fish on steam boat was bland and tasteless, and the crab curry lacked any other flavor apart from spice. The drinks were decent. Maitre'd was rude and unpleasant to deal with.

Drinks and food were great. Food took a little long but our server Emma was super sweet and brought us out a complimentary ceviche while we waited. The bartender, manager and host were all really nice and everything was delicious!

Fish Cheeks shows you the world beyond your usual pad thai.

Resy's are available, but we were able to get seated through walk ins. The table we had was fortunately round (we love dim sum family vibes) and was also near top to bottom windows to offer that natural lighting. 

The Happy Hour Dozen Oysters ($18) were delicious! I've had bigger ones, but I definitely found these sweeter and way more enjoyable! I would go back for these alone.

For apps, we got the Pork Cheeks ($17) and Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce ($15). The Pork Cheeks weren't very memorable but the raw Shrimp on the other hand! The flavor in the tangy sauce of the lime juice, chili, and whatever else drenched in, infused right into the Shrimp! Highly recommend that.

The Khua Kling ($27), which was a 4 pepper dish, was insanely spicy for my tolerance, hell no!! But the Coconut Crab Curry ($30) was right up my alley. It is a fan favorite for a reason thanks to the creaminess of the sauce and small crab meat pieces being a perfect pairing to the accompanying rice bowl.

The Crab Fried Rice ($27) was sweeter than your average fried rice because hello, crab. The star stunner herself, the Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs ($38) was a whole fish presented beautifully and deboned! I've never had my fish in such a tangy cilantro lime sauce before, it was delicious! And yes, we did not forget to eat the fish cheeks. 

As indicated by the prices, the restaurant emphasizes on the sharing of dishes. Come with big money and a group and you will feel transported to wonderful Thai flavors that'll have your tongue tingling for more.

4/5 for menu options and vibe. 1/5 for the happy hour "oysters". The oysters are not "fresh". The waiter says they are pre shucked out every morning. But they are prepping them... as in empty shells + a bucket full of oyster meat.. that is not fresh, yo. It's giving canned oysters. Soooo yeah just a heads up in case y'all try to order up mad oysters only to find out they not as fresh. :)

Quite simply one of the best Thai food spots in the area. I would say this place is second to Soothr which is only about 10 minutes away. Fish Cheeks also offers a slightly different menu, one that I think is a bit closer to what you'd actually eat while visiting Thailand. 

The outdoor space is a nice touch and the ambiance is lively with the scent of Thai chili's, lemongrass and fish sauce.... initiate mouth salivating....

Here are some of the highlights from my last visit:

Starters
- Zabb Wings :: fantastic way to start the meal, nice blend of spice, perfectly moist chicken and a zest of lime

- Crispy Rice Salad & Pork :: I found this dish to be very similar to a Laab salad.. spicy... crunchy but not as savory as I would've liked

- Manila Clams & Sweet Basil :: one of my faves and definitely an item you should order

- Grilled Pork Cheeks :: I wouldn't put this as one of my top 5 of the night, but you genuinely can't go wrong with tender pork bites with a slight tinge of spice

Entrees
- Coconut Crab Curry :: if you like spicy of the spiciest.. this is the dish for you. Packed with flavor and a delayed spicy punch that'll knock you backwards for a second

- Crab Fried Rice :: less spice is sometimes nice and in this occasion it was much needed, I truly enjoyed this dish and found it to be simple but flavorful

- Fried Fish with Herb Garden Salad :: not too over the top fried and pairs nicely with the salad provided. Spicy but not over the top

- Isan Style Grilled Chicken :: YASSS .. this reminded me of all those incredible outdoor stalls in Thailand, nicely grilled extremely flavorful and spice is provided on the side to make it as you wish.. damn good

For drinks, I also recommended the Spicy Mango .. hits the spot and has a nice balance of spice and sweetness

Phenomenal food! Spicy, light and fresh. I don't know another Thai restaurant like it in the States. The people who work their are always kind and thoughtful. The crab curry is always a winner but everything I have ordered there has been top notch.

Disappointing. Yes, labor is hard to find everywhere, but the service on this visit was so bad. Drinks arrived 45 minutes after we sat down and after the food was being served. Waiters disappeared for a long time. And the food was so so. Two dishes too spicy despite telling them our tolerance was medium. Oysters no lemon. They'd run out of sticky rice pudding. Very average experience. Won't go back. I'd go instead to Thai diner.

Best thai food near SoHo. 

Walk in for lunch on weekend should be fine. But it's always better to reserve a spot especiafor dinner. 

Menu highlight:
Thai coffee/ ice tea are great
Happy hour oyster is a steal 
Whole fish is a must have - light taste and super refreshing

Price:
$120 pre tax pre service fee
Easily one of my top preferred restaurants in the city. Creative and delicious food (and idyllic location) without being pretentious.

author.name: Megan T.
author.location: Upper West Side, New York, NY

reviews.review: I dined here with 3 other people and we ordered multiple drinks during happy hour and two items from every category. some we doubled like the crab fried rice, and the oysters!  from the pork cheeks to the whole steamed fish, everything was fantastic!!   even the corn salad! i think we had two of those too!!   a definite must have are the glass noodles. I'm not sure what the sauce is but there's so much umami!  I would highly recommend dining here and remember to make reservations first!

This place is absolutely incredible. Amazing balance of flavors and some dishes I've just never experienced before. The crispy rice salad and the prawns in their green sauce were standout favorites. The crab fried rice was impressively flavorful.

Huge respect to a Thai place that doesn't have the stuff everyone would expect of a Thai place - pad kee mao, pad thai, etc.. 

We'll definitely be back.

I didn't take any pictures but we tried several of their dishes as there were six of us. Everything we had was amazing especially the wings and the service was equally as good! I will definitely be back when I visit NYC again. You will not regret choosing this place!!!

I absolutely love this place! I always go with my dog and they make sure i have a seat as well as offer my dog a bowl of water on the warmer days as well. The staff is amazing and the waitress always gives me great drink options. During the summer they also have frozen drinks that taste amazing as well. The chicken wing flavor is to die for and the oysters are great but the toppings they give you for them really make them unforgettable! great restaurant and i will definitely be back all summer long for their happy hour oysters
Sooo good ! Everything was so good ! I am def going back . Only thing I would say is they need more mango sticky rice ! They ran out I was disappointed but def will go back !

Great Thai food and highly enjoyable but be warned some dishes are very spicy. Not average spicy but several levels above (and this is coming from a couple that at least thought we had a high spicy tolerance). Overall though absolutely delicious and would rank as one of the best Thai meals we've had in NYC.

Heard great things about this place for a long time and was glad to finally check it out. I came on a warm summer afternoon and sat outside. We both had the spicy mango cocktail which was really good. To eat we had a crab curry dish and a fish dish as well which were both phenomenal. Can't wait to come back

As many others have commented, the food here is really wonderful.  This isn't your typical pad thai joint by any means.  All the food is fresh, flavorful and plated beautifully.  

Only complaint is that they have just 1 restroom, so there's always a long wait.

Bro... so damn good. First off, our server was legit (Corey), very enthusiastic and knew the menu very well, and a super nice guy. The food comes out very fast. I recommend coming here with at least 2-3 people so you can get a bunch of different plates. The raw shrimp was delicious, as were the raw oysters (they serve it with this green sauce and crunchy shallots, like they do in Thailand, SO GOOD). The steamed fish is so flavorful and tender, I definitely recommend. The coconut crab curry was also very flavorful but light as well. The mango sweet rice is ridiculously tasty (make sure to ask for it in the beginning so they reserve a plate for you). If you like Thai food this is the place to try next, it will definitely not disappoint. Love, Cris.

Honestly, I was very excited to come here but I felt a little underwhelmed. On the bright side, the thai iced tea was AMAZING. The food is not the traditional Thai food you would typically see at other Thai spots in the city. It's focused on fish dishes which is great but it just didn't do it for me especially with the high price point. Food also took forever to come out and service was nothing special.
