Definitely lives up to the hype. The coconut crab curry and corn salad and pandan ice cream were wins. I found the first two just a bit too spicy to truly enjoy it. Had to order some Thai tea with its milkiness to balance out the fire. Outdoor seating is so nice. They have their own impressive retractable roof! The kaffir lime flavor comes through and it's so good. The wings weren't super special. Meaty but a dry rub and less herbs than I thought. Crab fried rice is also good, as a standard.

(4.5)

There are a ton of incredible Thai spots in the city, but Fish Cheeks is probably my favorite of them all. More broadly, it makes a very, very strong case as one of the top restaurants in New York.

The menu doesn't have many of the usual items you'd expect to see at a Thai restaurant (no pad thai or drunken noodles here), but instead a slate of unique, creative dishes packed with a ton of flavor. My time-tested favorites here are the zabb wings, crab curry, and kua kling. The wings are perfectly tangy and lightly salted, a lime-citrus combo executed to delicious perfection. The crab curry and kua kling are VERY HOT, but if you're into spice, they're absolute musts. The only dish I've had here that I'd skip in the future was the green curry. It's a meat and fish eater's destination, for sure; vegetarians don't have much to work with here.

The cocktails are also excellent, and they have pretty generous happy hour deals, including $11 drinks (and wine / beer discounts, too) for much of weekend brunch!

The service here is prompt and attentive, which is a plus, but they try to turn over tables quickly. If you're looking to hang out with a group and have a leisurely, drawn-out meal, this might not be the best choice.

Sidenote: I've also ordered takeout from here before, and the quality has been equally fantastic.

Truly outstanding on all levels. 

Service: the place is absolutely packed every night, and yet the service is overwhelmingly strong and calm, like they're somehow never in the weeds. It's a very well run operation and the front of the house reflects this through and through. 

Food: Extremely delightful. Out of this world with flavors and presentation too. Seriously, just INSANELY good. One of the strongest restaurants in the area 
PS specifically - I had pork cheeks and a crispy rice salad to start, and I'd highly recommend both before your meal. 

Ambience: clean and classy little spot that's expanding in size (they were building out the restaurant into the next place when I was there, tho you wouldn't even know that either). Always a good scene inside and as mentioned, the place is jumping every night. 

Really, a truly lovely restaurant, one of manhattan's best spots.

This has been my favorite restaurant in NYC since 2017. I should have written this review years ago, but now I can really and truly say it's a great experience every single time. The temperature, texture, flavors of each dish I've had are *chef's kiss*. From the Prawn Aob Woosen (delicious glass noodles with a depth of flavor that is indescribable with my limited vocabulary and 3 giant prawns that are so tender I literally cry), to the properly spicy coconut crab curry (tender, would make y'all weak spicy ppl cry with the way it builds), to my absolute favorite oysters in the whole city featuring bright nam jim sauce and fried shallots), I come here time and time again. The cocktails are absolutely delicious with extremely pretty presentation. This time I was served by Rin, who was literally the sweetest human, taught me how to make prik nam pa at home (literally heading to H Mart after this for the ingredients). She was so attentive and patient with all of my questions. I didn't have a reservation, but somehow Jaci (also lovely) got me seated in 30 minutes on the hottest day in NYC so far, so you know it was PACKED. I had a long doctor's appointment and a hard week, so this level of attention, care and accommodation was exactly what I needed. Will be coming here for as long as they're open (ideally forever!!!!). Thank y'all for the exceptional service and food through the solo dinners, stood up dates, friend reunions and more to come. Love y'all! And pls tell me where you got the fish lights, they're so cool!!!

Paid $30 for grilled chicken that came out fully pink on the inside and cold. I told the waiter my chicken was pink on the inside and he laughed, said nothing and walked away.  Not sure if he was being rude or just didn't even know. Will not be coming back.

Grilled pork cheek is pretty nice, I like the tamarind sauce go with it. 
Kuhn kling is super spicy, order with caution.

Fish Cheeks is one of those restaurants where, if you have money to burn because it's NY, then why not? Went in with high expectations and was disappointed at a high price point. 

3/5* service: for an upscale place, the staff does the bare minimum here. We were promptly seated and told to reference the QR code. No one offered to explain the menu or ask if we have questions (we overheard another waitress explain to the adjacent table that one of the menu items was discontinued so they have 3 specials instead!). No one checked in on the meal after food arrived. 

Rounding up to a 3 because, after we proactively told them about our curry tasting bitter, they realized the chef messed up and removed it from our bill. 

2/5 coconut crab curry: doesn't live up to the hype at all. Or maybe because they over reduced ours so it tasted bitter (which the chef later acknowledged). For the price, you're better off at any other Thai place. 

3/5 prawn karee: large prawns but was one note. Came out lukewarm. You also only get 3 prawns for $28, so I hope you're in a small group. 

5/5 steamed fish: this is the one dish that lived up to the hype. If you're a fan of lime, the flavors are divine and the fish is so tender. Be careful of bones as you get closer to the fish's head. My mom's obsessed and tried to find the recipe online afterwards!

Love the food here! Definitely need to get a reservation a week or two in advance. The oysters are small here but the sauces that comes with them are unique and yummy. The crab curry was spicy but I couldn't stop eating it! The fried chicken wings were a bit salty but I still enjoyed it. My boyfriend loves the steamed fish with Thai herbs! A must try food experience
Beautiful Zab Zab wings and amazing entrees. We are the thousandth review, so congratulations Fish Cheeks on making phenomenal food for 1000 content eaters.

Fish cheeks was so good and authentic! They serve very flavorful Thai food concentration on seafood so we went during happy hour! We made reservations because I wanted to sit indoors and get all the feels and vibes of the place. Also I'm happy we ended up making reservations because the day we went it was pouring outside. 

When we first got their we immediately got sat. 

We ordered the pork cheeks which we saw on someone else's table and thought of the pork shoulder we get at our fave Thai spot in sf and said we had to get it! We specifically had gone because it was happy hour so we ordered the happy hour oysters. It came with a green sauce that was spicy but so flavorful! Fortunately the crab fried rice we ordered also came with a side of that green sauce as well as a red pepper, garlic sauce that had a kick to it but more than anything really tasty. & for drinks we got a tongue and cheek cocktail with black sesame that was really refreshing and not too sweet as well as a Leo lager beer. 

We wanted to order the famous coconut crab curry but when we asked the waitress how spicy it was, she said really spicy so we passed because we can't that much spicy especially if someone who is Thai is telling us it's spicy. Maybe one day I'll have the courage to try it, but I will definitely be back to try other items on the menu.

Tapas style small portions. I think it's good for 2 people if 3-4 should double up your food. Best thing I liked was the glass noodles. Worst was the crab curry. Crab meat was small chunks from a can. The curry was labeled spicy but it was SO SPICY that it over powers the actually dish and crabmeat. It was just heat. The flavor was covered by the spice. I had to wash the chunks of crabmeat in the water to eat it because I felt bad wasting it since I could barely eat it. I can eat spicy but holy sht it was spicy! Oysters was super small. Couldn't even taste the oyster because it was tiny lol. I left couldn't taste my mouth and still hungry.

Unique menu with lots of well made fusion dishes. It's a great spot for a group of people to share dishes. The drinks are tasty too. The outside seating is covered and has heaters for when it gets cold. We also saw Quandale Dingle while eating there! Small world. Would highly recommend.

As a Thai American, I definitely look for authenticity. It's nice to see at least some staff who are Thai. The seafood based restaurant is unique and I loved the concept. We didn't have a reservation but lucked out and got one for 7pm on a Friday. I asked to be notified on Resy and got a text a few hours before dinner time that they could make it work. Service was quick. Food and drinks were yummy. Got the spicy mango and  gin fizz. I LOVED the gin fizz. Very unique tastes. Go during happy hour so you can try more of their unique drinks. For food, got the crab curry (spicy!) and prawn woonsen. Sticky rice and mango for dessert of course. The paying process was super easy to do on your own with QR code. Something new I've never tried before. Cramped space but it's nyc! The staff were great. Even offered soda water when I stained my top haha. All in all, would come back again!

Probably the best Thai in post Covid era. I have been long disappointed in the Thai fusion hype among those instagram food bloggers. 
Although I am no expert in Thai food, i think the tradition Thai food should be appreciated more than just offering pad Thai, coconut rice n their dessert. In fact, the geological position of Thailand can always tell you how good they can cook seafood using their expertise in spice, herb etc. 
we had zing wing n fish. ( order their best seller or their daily special). 
It is just epic delicious. 
The zing wing is like fried chicken but batter is thinner. Within that thin batter, the texture is immersed with sour n spice n sweet flavor. We just can't stop eating. 
But the fish is just the star of the whole thing. First, take a sip of the soup, it is sour at first bite but then somehow you are driven to have another sip n next you will find yourself still having it. And the fish is just fresh. Had been growing up near the coast La area, I doubt many restaurants in nyc can provide such good quality of fish. 
Overall: a must visit if you are long for thai food. As I said, all you got will be epic.

My only regret is not coming here with more people so I could try more dishes!  Wife and I ordered the coconut curry crab and the steamed fish with Thai herbs.  Both were AMAZING and had such great flavor profiles.  The curry was SPICY and at the very top of my spice level.  I wonder if they can bring it down just a notch.  The fish was a real treat!  They manage to get most of the bones out and the herbs really compliment the dish.  Mango sticky rice for dessert was also amazing (might have to order two desserts next time).  Inside is nothing fancy but the food was delicious.

I visited here during happy hour on Saturday. I highly recommend to make a reservation and you must try this place if you like Thai food!! I loved every single meals I tried. They are really flavorful, complicated yet perfectly come together. Also, don't forget to try their cocktails!!
The crab curry is amazing. I had it a year ago and still dream about that taste. Looking forward to trying something else
Best Thai food I've had in the city! Everything was incredible especially the crab curry and the cocktails. Being on Bond St doesn't hurt either!

So incredibly good, the restaurant was packed on a busy Saturday night and we were lucky enough to have a reservation secured nearly a month before. You'll need one, as we heard a party try to walk in shortly after only to be told they were in for a nice two hour wait.

The restaurant itself isn't huge, but they make good use of the space they have along with a nice looking outdoor area. We sat inside, but the enclosure looked clean and sturdy. Wait staff was incredibly attentive, provided useful suggestions and paced the meal perfectly. They even let us know unprompted that Happy Hour was about to end, and let us preorder a drink at Happy Hour prices that they kept at the bar until we had finished our first! Incredibly nice and much appreciated. 

The food is why you're here and it does not disappoint in any way. We were afraid doing a double order of crab dishes (the crab fried rice and the crab curry) would be too much crustacean, but no sir it was not - it was exactly the right amount and I would have gone back for round two if there was any space left in my stomach. Prices are reasonable all things considered (NoHo reasonable is probably about the same price range as the rest of the country - sans California's - Michelin Star options, but you know what you're getting yourself into) and I left ready to plan my next visit back so if you can find a table, I suggest you take it!

Have heard amazing things about their Thai Herb Branzino and this immediately became a crowd pleaser  Don't miss their desserts too!!! Pictured: Coconut icecream topped w coconut flakes, jackfruit & Mango sticky rice (the crispy rice topping adds such a great texture  

Their Thai green chili complement the oysters so well! Personally feel like the salad is quite salty to eat alone.

I absolutely love this place! I went with three other friends on Sunday afternoon for lunch, and we got three main dishes for the table. We got Steamed Fish, Coconut Crab Curry, and Crab Fried Rice. My personal favorite is the steamed fish because the herbs and seasoning was on point and the fish was soft but still could feel the texture. Crab fried rice was also great, seasoned thoroughly, and the two sauces on the side paired well with the rice. Coconut crab curry was still good, but it had a little bit of tanginess, which was sort of unexpected, not that I disliked it. For drinks, I got Tongue & Cheeks for myself; two of them got Thai Iced Tea, which you cannot go wrong with; and another got Cabaret. Speaking for myself, I liked my drink--it was refreshing and sweet just the right amount. I would definitely go back here for more happy hour deals and to try different dishes. I highly recommend!
Pretty good food, but what the hell are these prices? Like $30 for fried rice? I get that some of the dishes are elevated, and they do taste good, but it's not worth the crazy pricetag.

This restaurant is small; the table set up feels tight so be sure you come with peeps you like to be around.  We had a party of 6. Highly recommend making reservations ahead of time. 

I'm not a fan of Thai Ice Tea - the majority of Thai / Vietnamese restaurants make this drink way too sweet and thick.  I decided to try it here and I FRIGGEN LOVED IT! I wanted to order another! Their alcoholic signature drinks were also a hit - visually pleasing; you will not be disappointed in what they have to offer.

Please note that this spot is known as a Thai restaurant specializing in seafood dishes.  Don't come here thinking you can order traditional Thai dishes like Pad Thai or Yellow Curry Chicken.  Our group had a couple of picky eaters and one was allergic to shellfish and eggs.  Thankfully our server was exceptionally knowledgeable about the menu and the ingredients used in their dishes.  She was truly a Godsend! 

Because of our limitations, we only ordered a couple of things - 

grilled pork cheeks 
sum tum corn salad
and 2 fish dishes - fried fish with garden herb salad and steamed fish with Thai herbs

The pork cheek dish was bland on its own. Adding the dipping sauce made it much more flavorful.  

The corn salad - OMG, it slapped me silly!  I wasn't expecting it to be that good!

Both fish dishes were cooked to perfection! Even our picky eaters who kept scraping off the herbs on their piece of fish couldn't deny how tasty it was. (Don't scrape the herbs, it enhances the flavors!)

For dessert, we ordered the sticky mango rice and coconut ice cream. Unfortunately, the sticky mango rice was a bit of a disappointment - I wasn't a fan of the saltiness that was in the milk/cream and the mango was more tart than sweet. Stick to the coconut ice cream filled with jackfruit and fresh coconut!

What made this an even more epic night was seeing Trevor Noah dining a few tables away from us. AND LEMME TELL YOU, his nose-side profile is so so cute!! What a way to end our last night in NYC =) Thank you Fish Cheeks!

P.S.  Love their merch - "Cheeky" =)

We made a reservation through resy. After arrived at fish cheeks for dinner, the hostess informed that our table is ready, she sits us right away. Our server is very nice, friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. We ended up order 4 dozens of oysters, crap meat curry, prawn curry, grilled pork, streamed fish, wings (best wing I ever had), fried fish with herbs and do not forget to order their ice cream with mixed fruit and mango sticky rice that came out perfectly in every bite. This is the best Thai restaurant in NYC hands down. Couldn't get enough of it. Definitely be back very very soon!

Zabb Wings: 4.5 stars
great spice mix

Yum Goong: 3.5 stars
Large shrimp. Usually more sauce and more flavourful, today bland

She-Crab Lon: 4 stars
Fried fish sticky rice is too salty cured. 

Fried Snapper: 4.5 stars


Aob Woon Sen: 3 stars
mushrooms. Noodles weird sweet flavour

Came here on a Sunday afternoon. The restaurant was crowded but did not have a wait. The inside space is a little tight and was unable to accommodate my double stroller. However, the hostess and restaurant staff were very accommodating with the outside space and even offered us some blankets in case we get cold :)

We ordered a dozen oysters, the clams, morning glory vegetables and crab fried rice. The food was VERY good. The oysters and the dipping sauce that came with it was our favorite and we could have easily ordered another dozen between the two of us. The clams, although on the smaller side, was so good, almost wanted to drink the sauce!

Definitely coming back!

If you're a fan of Thai food, Fish Cheeks is an absolute must try! To start the meal, you get a bowl of shrimp chips that you can dip in their chili jam which on it's own is incredibly delicious. I could see myself using a plethora of chips or crackers for this dip - wish they sold it separately. I'm a big wings guy so I couldn't pass up their dry rub Zabb Wings. They pack an insane blast of flavor, both sweet and sour. Next up I tried the Grilled Pork Cheeks which were extremely tender with a nice bit of acidity and heat. For my main, I had the Spicy Beef and when the waitress warned us about the spice level, I didn't take it too seriously because I have a high tolerance for spice but wow that was spicy. It's not for the faint at heart but nonetheless it was quite tasty. I'll absolutely be back ASAP to try their various curries.

This place is great! We started with the Crispy Rice Salad & Pork which had a nice amount of spice. And then we ordered and split the Crab Fried Rice and the Green Curry. Both were excellent and the service was very good as well.

Got the pork cheek and steamed fish to go, and OMG it was delicious! So tender, great flavors, and sauces. I felt like I was home, it tasted so authentic. This is a highly recommended restaurant and I am planning on coming back to try more cuisines.

The Happy Hour drinks are soooo good. The bartenders are truly so talented. The flavors of the drinks are unlike any I've had before.

The happy hour oyster deal is also great. Best oysters I've had (havent had many to be fair). 

The pork cheeks were lackluster. The chicken wings were flavorful.

Me and my friend went to have lunch here on a Sunday, the food we had were amazing and the server that assisted us was very nice and friendly! Tips for people that would like to visit this place, it would be best to reserve ahead, we were there at 1pm but was lucky that we got a counter seat, I would definitely revisit and this time with reservation!

Fish cheeks, you are so delicious and unique. I've had the best steamed fish of my life here. And the best oysters. Everything I had here was so good. It's also very refreshing to eat at a Thai restaurant that serves such unique dishes. Can't wait for my next visit.

Their iconic crab and curry dish at $30 would be worth it if there were an ample amount of crab--but there is not. And the taste of what little crab there is, is overwhelmed by a spicy sauce. 
 
The steamed fish was bland. 

With so many really good, reasonable Thai restaurants I do not  understand why this place is so famous.

If you are allergic to imitation crab, confirm that all the crab here is authentic. I could not tell because of the overwhelming sauce but I assume it must be.

If I was asked what I want for my last meal before I die, it would be everything from Fish Cheeks!   Everything was soooo good.  Not only the food but the service too.    Can't say enough on how accommodating everyone was. My daughter and I couldn't decide what to order cause we wanted everything so we ordered enough to feed a party of four.  I should have wore stretchy pants.  Love this place and will definitely be back.  We had the pork cheeks, wings (omg the best!), the curry, the fried rice (who knew fried rice can taste like that!!) and the steamed fish with herbs.   Oh, and a couple of happy hour wines.  Great price for nyc.  If you were thinking of going, stop thinking and just go.  You won't regret it.

I had visited fish cheeks years ago for a birthday dinner and remembered I definitely wanted to come back for the steamed fish and it did not disappoint. We came on a Friday night at 5:15pm and did not have a reservation. We put down our name and waited for about an hour. Would recommend getting a reservation before going. 
We ordered steam fish, crab curry and morning glory. The crab curry is really spicy and might not be the best option for someone with low spice tolerance. It's flavor was really good tho. My favorite has to be the morning glory. Not sure what they use to cook it but it's so good!

Came on a recommendation from several. Showed up during HH, unplanned, but pleasantly surprised. Took this opportunity to try out their signature cocktails. Our favorites were Thank You Kha, Pandan Gin, and the Tongue&Cheek. Normally $17, but during HH, they are $11.

Food wise, it was delicious. Crab fried rice was good, and so were the sauces they served it with. I wish they served it with more, but we just asked and they brought it. The coconut curry is spicy! But still super yummy.

It's just a little bit expensive - definitely more of a treat yourself. It's intended to be a family style place though. But each entree is almost $30.

Staff is friendly! Make a reservation early though. They seem super popular, and it's hard to get a good dinnertime reservation.

We have been here for years. The food is always the best of the best. Can't find better Thai food in city. 

What we really like: 
Oysters with fried shallots and a type of special sauce
Clams with sweet basil 
Crab fried rice 
Prawn Karee
Tom Yum soup 
Steamed fish with Thai herbs 
Green Curry 

The fragrance and texture of each dish is handled to perfection.

Went here a few weeks ago on a mild winter day. Even though it was nice outside, they offered us blankets & hot tea. The food was SO authentic, I come from Queens where the Thai food is super special and authentic, so this really hit home. Get the whole steamed fish, you will not be disappointed.

Coconut crab curry! Trust them when they say it's 3 curry signs. It is HOT! But so fragrant and tasty!!! The crab fried rice is also amazing. I LOVED the shrimp in 3 crab sauce (appetizer) and the prawn karee!!! LOVEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!!!!!!!!

Very fresh seafood. The oysters are good
But the best part is their sauces
The steamed whole fish was my favorite dish and it was just AMAZING! Perfect balance of sour sweet, spicy and so so fresh. It was a master piece

I ordered the coconut crab curry and the prawn karee. Both were very delicious, and luckily the prawn karee balanced out the spiciness of the crab curry. I appreciated the pleasant, unpretentious service. However, the portion size is too small for the price point.

- 10 stars
- grilled fish with herbs is delicious
- coconut crab curry is delicious, it is spicy tho
- make that resey
- impeccable service 
- good wings
- great oysters 
- self pay at the table,  is a perfect idea
- tequila drinks were all tasty
- I did not like the rum drinks
- fun soundtrack

My husband and I came to New York from Georgia for our honeymoon to eat all the eats and found this place from watching one of our favorite YouTubers The Fung Bros. Out of the of week long stay, and eating at 11 different places, Fish Cheeks was our most favorite place. 

We ordered the following:

Market Oysters - I am Thai and I am ashamed that I never thought to eat oysters this way but I never want to eat oysters any other way ever again. 

Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce - Similar flavor profile to the oysters, so delicious. 

SomTum Corn Salad - the flavor on this salad was a little too mild for me, but I love the use of corn instead of the traditional papaya salad since the corn added sweetness to the dish. 

Coconut Crab Curry - They did not skimp on the crab or spice in this dish at all! So much flavor, so much spice. Soooo good. 

Pakboong Fai Dang - This is my absolute most favorite vegetable to eat and cooked in the best way ever. I was so happy they served this here. This needs to be served at all Thai restaurants. 

We saw other tables around us get shrimp crackers (not the fry looking one but they colorful abstract shaped ones) so we asked if we could get it too, as it came with tamarind dip (I think). So that was an awesome addition because I love cooking those up and eating them at home all the time! 

We also ordered the Ya Dong Party shots which tasted like medicine chased pandan iced tea - another favorite of mine (since my mom used to make me pandan iced tea all the time). I also ordered the spicy mango, which I think was good but my mouth was already on fire from all the Nam Jim and coconut crab curry, I couldn't tell if the drink was spicy or not but the drink itself tasted good but not something that was amazing. 

I am extremely sad that we don't have a place like this in Georgia... might just have to open one up myself. But I'm the mean time, I guess I'll be making these dishes at home! Especially the oysters! 

Great job to the Chef for bringing out some of the best parts of Thai food to America. You have made this Thai person very proud!

Service 5/5
Food 5/5
Ambiance 5/5

Probably one of the best restaurants I have had an opportunity to eat at during my visit to NY this past week. 

Staff were exceptional! Our table never had dirty plates sitting around, water always full, and they always made sure to ask how we were doing. 

I highly recommend steamed fish with Thai herbs and coconut crab curry. It had flavors that I had never tasted in a traditional Thai restaurant. Made me really ponder how they were able to create such unique flavors! I'm definitely going to crave this spot!

Ambiance/Atmosphere was lively as it was a packed house but a little bit cramped to my liking. But what do you expect in New York? Lol.

Highly highly recommend this place to everyone visiting or living in NY.

I wanted to try this restaurant on my visit to NY because a friend recommended it. We got to the restaurant and were told it would be a 1 hour wait for a party of 8. After a while, the host was able to check us in earlier by splitting us into two tables. They seated 4 of us while 4 of us remained outside. After 45 minutes, we were told by another male staff member there was a miscommunication and they didn't have a table for the 4 of us still waiting. When I asked about an empty table that had just been cleared, he was very rude and yelled at me that the table was for reservations made a month ahead. He then asked us to sit at the bar, at this point we didn't care anymore, it was really cold outside, and we just wanted to eat because the first 4 people in our group were almost done with their meal already. Sitting at the bar was not what we expected and wasn't enjoyable for our group. It's hard to eat family style while sitting at a bar. After we finished our meal, the empty table that was being held for a reservation was still empty. 

In terms of the food, we ordered 8 dishes and only the crab curry stood out. Everything else was just ok. At least it wasn't as bad as the service we received!

After hearing many great reviews about the restaurant, I finally was able to go try it with my friends over a weekend. My friends and I were not able to make a reservation in time so we arrived around 2pm hoping that there would not be too many people. Luckily upon arrived, we waiting for approximately 20 mins before being seated at the bar.

Our server let us know how to use the contactless menu and payment system and came back in to take our order when we were ready. In the end, we decided to order the crab fried rice, grilled pork cheeks, zabb wings, and tiger prawn karee. The crab fried rice and tiger prawn karee were delicious and not too heavy. The zabb wings were nice & crispy according to my friends because it was a bit too spicy for me to try to eat everything. The pork cheeks were grilled nicely with a thin layer of crispy skin. 

Overall, the food here is good and I would come back to try the other dishes available during off peak hours.

Wow! Strange name but the food is amazing, can't recommend enough. The wings were probably
My favorite but everything was great. Little hard to get a res so plan ahead!

All our dishes tasted fresh and very flavorful. My only wish was that it wasn't so spicy! And you can't change the spice level, I think because it's already been prepared that way or at least for my entree maybe since it was curry. Admittedly, I did choose a 3 pepper level dish, but even the 1 pepper level dish felt spicier than the average. It's almost a shame because the flavors are great but you're so busy trying to survive the heat that you can't fully enjoy it. Will come back to try their non spicy dishes next time. 

What we ordered:
- Corn salad
- Spicy Coconut Crab Curry
- Grilled Branzino (highly recommend)

The atmosphere was cute, the staff are nice and efficient, and the food is ok.

The thing is, the food is fine, but for the price, I would've expected something a little better or more interesting. I think I might've had too high expectations based on the Yelp reviews.

This is one of the places where if I'm in the neighborhood and I'm hungry, I'd go here--but I wouldn't go out of my way to find it.

Tasty Thai

Tried a few Thai places, so I didn't expect much here. Walking in, I really liked the interior light decor and, while the wait was a little long, the food was amazing. Every dish was different than anything I've had before, so I was definitely surprised. 

We ordered the Coconut Crab Curry (large chucks of crab, AMAZING CURRY!), Khua Kling (super spicy beef cuts), Steamed Fish w/ Thai Herbs (super tender, refreshing, my favorite), and the oysters (not bad). While elevated Southeast Asian cuisine doesn't always work, Fish Cheeks delivered--will be back to try more!

The food here is SO DELICIOUS and they do not disappoint with spiciness. Came here during happy hour for the oysters (dozen $18) which are super fresh and delicious, then ordered shrimp in 3 crab sauce as an appetizer bc I love raw shrimp dishes. So on point, it was very spicy even with my spice tolerance which I don't find at a lot of other restaurants. We also ordered Crab aob woosen and coconut crab curry - portions looked kinda small but it filled me up bc it was so spicy. Both were tasty but I liked the coconut crab curry more bc it was less generic. For dessert we got Coconut ice cream with egg yolk and ovaltine powder - at first I was like meh, it's just coconut ice cream which I can get anywhere but it turned out to be very special. The texture is insane and the hardened egg yolk goes so well with it. The food here is pricey so I wouldn't come here often but once in a while it's such a delicious treat!

They have some outdoor seating kinda in booths - heater isn't super strong but it's sufficient. Service was amazing too!

We celebrated my friend's bday here and then I brought my husband here again. The food is exquisite with the staff being so welcoming and accommodating. I've tried the chicken wings, the Crab curry, crab fried rice and the fish with Thai herbs. All are so delicious especially if you enjoy lime flavors.
A little bit on the pricier side but def worth it for those meals that you would prefer to be memorable.

5 stars for the thai food on the menu, please skip the oysters. The fried shallots were not super fresh, and the sauce pairing was weak, and the oysters were just average on the freshness scale.

Now onto the food. 

I'm convinced this is the best crab curry in the city. Slightly spicy but with just the perfect amount of spice, the crab curry (5/5) has well-rounded flavors and a generous serving of seafood. At $30, it's a bit pricey but you get what you paid for

Pork Cheeks (5/5): The pork cheeks here has changed my mind about cuts of pork. I place this on par or above pork belly. The sauce pairing was exceptional as well, bringing out the light flavor of the pork cheek itself. 

Overall definitely worth. Happy hour drinks are standard for a thai establishment and nothing to die for

So here's the thing, I was reluctant to come here. In fact I had an attitude at the fact that I was being taken here to eat. Like, WHY would you bring me here. Whyyyyy?!!! *insert rolling eyes, pouty lips and trying to hide my attitude while speaking*

A Sunday, I'm craving seafood. Came across this place, read the reviews and still was like no. Couldn't find another place & ended up here. Was told the wait was 90mins, yes 90 real mins (and that was to sit at the bar) Fine. Immediately stared walking around looking for another place to eat - your girl was hungry. 20 mins later, received a text "your table is ready at the bar". A miracle. So in their defense, the restaurant is small. I was also happy I sat at he bar because the tables are rather close to each other. 

The bartender, AMAZING, don't know his name but he was nice & fun, just good vibes. On to the food...the chicken wings has the major seasoning groups lol. A little bit of salt, spicy, sweet - very good. Next up, crab rice, no need to say anything else. Light, fluffy, crabby, so good and the accompanying two sauces made it taste better. Now, the star of the show, the herb steamed fish. *chefs kiss* A whole fish, NO bones, sitting in a broth of different herbs while being kept nice & toasty by a little fire underneath the dish it's served in. ANDDDDD when you add the fish herb sauce to the rice, it took the rice to another level!!! I wish I could buy a bottle of the herbed broth - so amazingly good. 

Because nothing is perfect, I did not like the portion sizes. The food is served family style & a little more food would be greatly appreciated because there's no way more than 2 people could share that rice or fish. 

Can't wait to return to try the pork cheeks, I'm a fan of it already & I haven't tried it yet!

Food and bar staff were great. The wings hit all flavor sensations. Crab rice was also good, but I wish it was a larger portion, I could have eaten it by myself. The sauce of the steamed fish was delicious.

This is always on my list to go to whenever I visit NYC. Honestly, I'd still come back, always! Even though this most recent time I went, my favorite dish was not cooked up to par (Prawn Karee, shrimp was definitely over cooked where the meat tasted like frozen prawn and soggy, not what I'd expect in a $28-30 dollar dish with only prawns that should be the key and most important part to cook carefully). Other than that, everything else was good as usual, especially happy hour oysters 
Have to get side of rice with this dish , it is a must if you want to enjoy the karee/scrambled egg with something like rice to help balance out the tastes well :)

Came here a few weeks ago right when they opened for dinner. Had a struggle at the door when the woman who was checking vaccine cards, said that my husband's vaccinations were not valid because they were expired. We were so confused. Turns out she was looking at one of the vaccine labels on his card, which included the vaccine lot # and exp date for the particular dose he had received. Had to explain to her what the label exp date meant. We are low key people and felt embarrassed holding up the line. I think she understood at the end but it was awkward. Service was otherwise fine inside the restaurant. The oysters were ok. The steamed fish was great, but it was a small fish for the price.

It was good, but I think it's a little overhyped. 

We got the fried zabb wings, pork cheeks, coconut crab curry, spicy beef dish, and coconut ice cream. The apps were really good. The chicken wings were very flavorful and crispy. The pork cheeks were tender versions of chasiu or chinese bbq pork. The coconut crab curry was so spicy. Beware of the spicy labels on the menu because it was indeed 3 chili signs of spice level. I couldn't finish it because it was so spicy. I think I drank the most water I've ever drunk at a restaurant lol. The ice cream was fine, nothing special. 

I'd get the zabb wings and try other dishes if I came back.

fantastic experience, from the interior to the food to the service! 

the food: i got the oysters, clams, beef entree, and (not pictured) crab fried rice. wowow the oysters were amazing, i wish i had gotten a dozen, the sauce and fried shallot combo is unbelievable. everything was so perfectly seasoned, packed with flavor - my favorite was the oysters but the clams came a close second. the beef is spicy btw! 

the interior: fish themed everywhere, very cozy and warm. 

service: very attentive and kind workers, always kept my hot water filled!

Phenomenal! The crab fried rice is a staple and must try! Never had a dish so flavorful. Also the prawn karee is rich with flavor. Zabb wings were great as well as the manila clams for appetizers. However they are a nice to try and less of a staple. Not sure if the drinks are worth $8 because they're not memorable. Definitely will come again!
FOOD WAS SOOO DELISH! Def coming back for that steam fish. I typically don't care for Tom Yum soup but it was so good here too.

Came here because I heard good things about it and it did not disappoint! We got the fish special and it was definitely interesting and flavorful. I really like their pork appetizer... Simple with just the right amount of salt!

It's amazing.  the crab fried rice is so worth it.
I think every was great. Would come back for more! Drools

The crab curry rice was really good too!
I personally have issues w curry (spice induced diarrhea) not the restaurant fault, only my body doesn't work well with spices. Hahaha

I love Thai food and so I get very excited to try a new Thai place any chance I get! 

My friend made relatively last minute reservations so we ended up having to sit outside for 2pm lunch on a Saturday. It was 18 degrees that day and despite their heating lamps, it was still quite cold however it wasn't terrible. 

For appetizer we started off with the pork cheeks. I HIGHLY recommend you get this, it was absolutely delicious. Perfect amount of fattiness, it was so good. The sauce it comes with was really good too! 

Next we had the crab fried rice and the steamed fish. The steamed fish was so soft and moist with excellent flavors of lime, garlic, and cilantro. It paired really well with some crab fried rice. We also got the crab curry, and the waitress warned us that it would be spicy however we underestimated her. It was actually REALLY spicy that I couldn't enjoy it too much. I felt the burn down to my stomach. 

They had happy hour until the end of their lunch service which was 5 pm. We ended up drinking a bunch of cocktails all of which were good! 

I would come back here to try other items off their menu!

Stopped in for restaurant week and we were quickly seated despite being 10 min late for our reservation. Nice trendy ambiance, poor acoustics so you'll just hear everyone else yelling around you and not the person across from you lol. We decided to go with the restaurant week menu and tried the mussels, crispy rice salad, branzino, coconut crab curry, and sticky rice dessert. Everything was flavorful and good though the crab curry didn't really live up to the hype. It was pretty spicy which overwhelmed the dish and crab chunks were few. The crispy rice salad and sticky rice dessert were both really good and delicious!

I rarely write reviews but I had to because I didn't see enough praise for the corn salad appetizer in the first page of reviews. That salad is amazing, with the pork cheeks? The best. Both of those dishes are refreshing and delicate. The coconut crab curry is great; I enjoy the spice level, although ours did taste a bit bitter for some reason. Regardless, I appreciate when things are actually spicy. Crab fried rice was so good; fluffy, crab in every bite, and perfectly seasoned.

This is my preferred spot over another very popular Thai restaurant on the LES. I can't wait to try to the steamed fish dish next.

Came here with a friend for restaurant week dinner in Feb 2022 and was so amazed by all the interesting flavors of the dishes! My favorites were the Zabb Wings, Crispy Rice Salad & Pork, and Ping Gnob Plaa. The Zabb Wings have a sour, tangy taste that just works so well with the crispy fried outer shell. I've never had anything like it before, but it was amazing. The Crispy Rice Salad & Pork was also really refreshing, the whole dish has pretty strong, distinct flavors but again really good. It's pretty sour and salty, but goes great with the cabbage. The Ping Gnob Plaa was super good, loved the curry taste and the fish meat itself was really juicy. Both of the desserts were the cherry on top. The texture of the Coconut Ice Cream is a little thicker, but still super creamy. And then the Black Sticky Rice with Young Meat and Longan was interesting since the coconut meat is actually salted and the rice came out very warm. Overall, Fish Cheeks knows how to mix unconventional flavors together in a way that gives you a unique experience for your palate unlike anywhere else!

This was my first time here and it was such a nice surprise. We went there during happy hour (5-6pm/ all week), we ordered half a dozen oysters and some wine to start. The oysters were very fresh, it came with fried shallot and Thai Nam Jim seafood dipping sauce. We ordered two entrees: coconut crab curry and steamed fish with herbs. I'm not a huge fan of Thai curry, but I actually like this dish. It's spicier than what you expected but in a good way. The crab meat is cooked perfectly as well. My favorite dish of the night had to be the steamed fish with herbs, it just had a good combo of sourness and spiciness. The fish meat was fresh and tender, very flavorful. The sauce they made was just amazing. I would totally go back just for the steamed fish. 
The restaurant is very busy so definitely make a reservation before you go. They also have outdoor seating area as well with heat lamps installed.

Solid restaurant, I noticed they had a lot of people on their staff which is great. From hostess, bus boys, waiters/waitresses, managers. The zabb wings were great (they were a dry rubbed type) if you like that, the pig cheeks were delicious! They were fatty and full of flavor. The crab fried rice was also good but pretty standard. The drinks are strong!! And it's great that they have happy hour!! Even on the weekends!!

Definitely get a reservation since it's a popular spot! My friend and I went for dinner and shared several dishes: coconut crab curry and the steamed fish with and extra order of rice. The curry dish was definitely spicy, so be prepared! the steam fish was the best part, soooo flavorful!

we came here and ordered steamed fish and crab curry. The steamed fish is not too bad, with fire to keep it boiling. The crab curry was a disappointment. The curry tasted too raw and too strong that it covered the taste of the crab. you may not tell what you are eating with the strong taste of curry. Both dishes were both too sour which made only the first bite interesting but following not harmonious.

Cute establishment. Very flavourful. Oysters, clams, waterspinach, wings, the cilantro lime fish is all a must. Homemade ice cream...delish
Price is high, portions are small. Good service. Location is a lil out of the way. Mos def one of the better thai restaurants in nyc.

The ambiance and decor are great, as is the service, but the food is severely overhyped. I swung by Fish Cheeks yesterday evening with a friend without realizing it's Restaurant Week. We were able to share one order of the restaurant week offering ($59 only, which is actually a good deal split between two people) but they required us to order another main dish (~$30)--still cheaper than ordering two restaurant week options and ending up with too much food! My friend and I opted for the chicken wings, the crab fried rice, the coconut crab curry, and the coconut ice cream. Here are my thoughts:

* Chicken wings: kinda whatever. I'm not a chicken wing person and found these to be unmemorable. 
* Crab fried rice: very tasty, big fan of this. But this is a hard dish to mess up, and at $30, it's a bit more expensive than other NY. Thai staples (namely Glur + Thai Villa)
* Coconut crab curry. Incredibly memorable in the absolute worst of ways. Yes, you read that right. In my opinion the waiters should give diners a warning upon ordering this dish because the spice level is frankly quite dangerous. I am not a fan of spicy food but I can handle mild spice (which is better than many!); that said, this dish made me physically ill. I literally had to run to the restroom mid-meal because it made me sick. The first flavors that hit your palate are delicious but a millisecond later you'll feel like you're in danger. Tongue in flames, spitting fire, almost gasping for air. We had to ask our waitress for some yogurt (which they do not have, but she was kind enough to serve us a Thai iced tea to help us out). Even with that though, we couldn't handle it and had to box the rest. I genuinely thought that perhaps accompanied by some Greek yogurt it would be okay, but I was sorely mistaken. I had to stop eating the leftovers entirely because I once again started to feel queasy. I am even developing a headache now. Some may think I'm being melodramatic but I promise you I am not. This dish is seriously no joke and coming from a person who can handle at least some degree of spice, this is saying something! I implore Fish Cheeks to start notifying diners about this, or at least providing some sort of spice level option because I think this dish has incredible potential sans the ridiculous spice level. And if anyone from Fish Cheeks is reading this, please let me know if you ever take this advice as I'd love to come back, give this dish another try, and update my review!
Coconut ice cream: I was shocked by how much I loved this. I am not an ice cream person but this blew my mind. Coconut pieces, egg yolk, and ovaltine--who'd have thought!? Love it. Would order this even on its own if I'm ever around.

I didn't try any drinks yesterday but their menu is fascinating with lots of seemingly delicious options. 

So, in summary, the coconut crab curry ruined the night for me. I really hope the restaurant team will take my recommendation into consideration though because I truly believe I'd order from + dine at Fish Cheeks fairly regularly if the spice could be adjusted down here. I just can't let myself eat that curry dish again in its current state because I've already suffered enough GI problems as a result. That said, I really appreciate the attentive service and I love the ambiance. Their happy hour sounds like an incredible deal ($11 cocktails, heavily discounted oysters) so that sounds like a safer bet for me moving forward.

I'm really torn on how to rate Fish Cheeks. I have been wanting to try this place for ages, and I don't know how much I actually enjoyed it, but I also think I don't know enough about this style of authentic Thai food to judge. So I'll just share my impressions!

Ambience: the inside is adorable. We ate outside. Outdoor seating is sectioned off by plexiglass, comfortable benches, warm heaters overhead, and you're offered blankets. Couldn't be more comfortable even on a frigid day.

Service: a little patchy. I got the sense they were short-staffed, i waited about 10 minutes at reception to be able to get our (reserved) table, and at one point we basically had to chase the server down in desperate need of water. They also kept trying to clear plates we were still eating from, which was a little frustrating. But everyone was very gracious and kind! 

The important thing, though, is the food! 

Drinks: We shared the first drink on the menu (has hibiscus, black sesame, etc). Super beautiful and very yummy! Neither of us are big drinkers but I can tell this would be a fun cocktail spot.  We also later ordered a thai iced tea out of sheer spice desperation, which was basically extortion at $8 but also delicious. 

Apps: We had the clams with Thai basil and the zabb wings. The clams themselves were too fishy for my taste. Some were tasty, but I got some that were just so intensely briny and ocean-y that I couldn't get them down. They were also rubbery in texture. The curry they were in, though, was exquisite. I could have drunk it, and I did. The zabb wings were so delicious. Perfectly cooked, tender meat, and that seasoning blend was just incredible! However I do want to note that one of the wings wasn't cleaned properly--I found a few pinfeathers in mine! I also couldn't get the server's attention to let her know, and then someone else came and cleared the table. We also got a complimentary snack of shrimp chips (yummy, crunchy) and a sadly tiny portion of delicious chili jam to dip them in--I wish there'd been more of this tasty stuff!

For our main, we split the famous crab curry. I get the sense from reading other reviews that the spice level on this dish may vary from time to time. My companion and I (who are both very adventurous eaters) agreed this was the single spiciest dish either of us had eaten, spicy enough that it caused some pretty serious physical pain to eat it. I wish they'd toned it down, 
because it was also maybe the most delicious curry I've ever eaten, and I kept eating more even though it was making me cry! The crab portion was generous, but honestly the protein was an afterthought for me--it was all about that flavorful, perfectly creamy sauce. 

My companion talked me into dessert, and we split the coconut sundae. It was very tasty, though I found the inclusion of an egg yolk a little peculiar and not very appetizing. The ice cream itself was lovely.

We came during restaurant week, but did not order off that menu--I'll note that the restaurant week special is not much of a savings at Fish Cheeks, which is unfortunately the case at an increasing number of restaurants. Our bill came to about $60 each including tax and tip. 

All in all, it's hard for me to say what I think of this restaurant! Certainly, the flavors were superb, but there were also a couple of missteps that surprised me at this price point. Overall, though, it was definitely a really unique experience and great fun to try a new combination of flavors and ingredients.

I have been to many different Thai restaurants and I will say the experience at Fish Cheeks is a different one. Most of the food on the menu are pretty spicy so if you are someone that do not like spicy food, I would stay far, far away. I do like the Zabb wings. I find the wings to be a good combination of salty and spicy at the same time.  The crab fried rice is delicious as well. That is probably the only entree on the menu that is not spicy and super filling. I would definitely say you can share it amongst two or three people.  The Coconut Crab Curry is another great entree. It is definitely spicy but another good spicy.  I actually came to this restaurant with a bunch of friends and I was sharing my curry entree. Fair warning - you might want to order an additional order of curry entree if you end up liking this dish. My friend ended up eating all the crab out of the dish!
Flavor full food and lively atmosphere with well paired light drinks. Would go back to try different items!

Wowowowowow. Came here for restaurant week 2022 and it did not disappoint. (Dinner restaurant week price $60/person).

We came one hour after they opened and it was PACKED. Only available seating was at the bar and it was still a great experience and we were well taken care of.

****I would suggest that you have a high tolerance for spice. From someone who loves spicy food, I did find myself drinking more water than usual hahah. 
****I noticed that lemongrass is a key ingredient in most of their food. It has a strong flavor. If you don't like lemongrass, I wouldn't come here. 

5/5 Complimentary app--shrimp chips with some crab meat on top. Tangy and good! Only available for restaurant week.

7/5 Zabb wings. All I'm going to say is that I think this is the best wings I ever had at a restaurant. Just get it. No questions!! 

4/5 Mussels. Chef's special ONLY for restaurant week. Sweet and sour. The broth was nice and salty. I wish I asked them not to clear it away so I can have it with my rice 8)

4/5 coconut crab curry. What they are known for. So.....on the restaurant week menu, it didn't state the spice level and we ordered it based on the bartenders recommendation. my poor husband was having some difficulties.... (He doesn't have a high tolerance for spicy food). He did say it was good though. The flavor was smoky as well. I would have liked to see more crab but it's a great dish with rice. 

3/5 ping gnob plaa. I appreciated how there weren't any bones. Lemongrass is quite strong in this dish. I thought it was okay. Nothing too outstanding in this dish. 

10/10 Now the STAR DISHES from this place imo were the desserts. I'm not too good with sweets but the desserts just had the perfect amount of sweetness.
Both the coconut icecream and the black sticky rice is worth ordering. I think those two desserts paired very nicely with each other. The black sticky rice is a warm dessert btw! 

I would definitely come back here again.

The grilled pork cheeks are divine. I will order these everytime I'm here. They are perfectly fatty and tender, and that Jeaw sauce added a punch of acidity and fish sauce-goodness. This dish is the perfect appetizer or complement to your beer/cocktail/life.

Oysters with nam jim sauce was amazing. Another flavor blast.

Fantastic happy hour deals everyday on cocktails, beer, and oysters from12-3:15 PM and 5-6PM.

They give complementary shrimp chips + dip, which were excellent.

My friend and I came by on a Friday night for dinner. We couldn't snag a reservation on resy since they book up soo fast but we were willing to wait. We got lucky and they squeezed us in after 20~ mins for indoor seating, yay! The seating was definitely a little tight though, probably because they're so popular rn and it was a weekend, lol.

We heard such good things about so many dishes that we didn't know where to start. We decided on half a dozen oysters to start, the pork cheeks, coconut crab curry and prawn aob woosen which comes with glass noodles. And omg, not one dish disappointed! The oysters come with this cilantro sauce with a kick and fried shallots and it paired SOOO well. Unlike anything I had before. I also heard they are the first Thai restaurant to serve oysters so this is a must. I would come back just to order 2 dozens for myself. The pork cheeks were really tender and came with a great sauce also. The coconut crab curry was spicy but packed with flavor, crab and super creamy. Prawn aob woosen was also good- paired well with the garlicky glass noodles.

So refreshing to see a new and different Thai restaurant in the city- I can't wait to come back and try more dishes!

This place never disappoints!!! This is definitely one of my favorite Thai restaurant and I love it so much. I always tell my friends that we have to go here if they haven't yet. The crab curry is so delicious WOW. So flavorful and perfect. The crab rice looks simple but very addicting to eat. I would go during HH because they have really good deals, like $9 for half a dozen of oysters and $11 drinks (normally $17!)

Probably my favorite Thai spot in the city!

A lot of their dishes are on the spicy side, and even as someone who can take and enjoy lots of spice, it was a lot. But it didn't take away from the flavor or anything. 

We went during lunch and got oysters as part of their happy hour. There were crispy toppings given to put on top and it was a nice texture combination with the oysters. 

The coconut crab curry was also great - super creamy and leaned more toward the coconut flavor which chunks of crab in it. 

The steamed fish is also a must whenever I come! It's deboned and cooked so well. The soupy part is a nice touch and I also love the pickled vegetables that come with it. I took my friend who was visiting the city here and he absolutely loved the fish as well. 

The interior is also super pretty and has a cute ambiance. We usually go for lunch and walk in without a problem.

Visited here the other day and ordered the pork, the crab fried rice, the half dozen oysters, and the tom yum soup. All were very delicious but considering the price, I was expecting larger portions. The restaurant is being COVID conscious by checking vaccine cards and the service was friendly.

Ehh.  Mixed feelings about here. 

Came without a reservation on a Tuesday night during Restaurant week winter 2022.  Hostess was kind and was able to sit me inside.  

Both inside and the outside shelter eating area are nice ! Inside you'll be sitting close to your neighbors but it's not cramped. 

Waiter was friendly and came over quickly with fresh cold water from a metal pitcher and the rest. week menu. I opted out of it bc I wasn't too hungry for a 3 course meal they were offering at 59 bucks. 

It was happy hour! So I got a drink and oysters for starters. 

The drink was a spicy mango margarita. I was disappointed. It was boring and no salt rim. 

The oysters didn't taste that fresh. And I wasn't a fan of the garlic chips nor the mignonette they served with it.  It was too overpowering for oysters but maybe bc it helps bc I don't think these were the best quality oysters. They were 1.5 each so the price was right. 

I ordered the famous crab curry. As I was waiting for it I've noticed all around me , free shrimp chips with a dip were given to patrons. None for me though! Is it bc I was dining solo I wondered. There goes another star. 

The crab curry was delicious! Very spicy so beware. I loved it nevertheless.  However , it's a small portion for a 30 dollar dish. 

I was eyeing this place for a while and I was sadly disappointed.

Absolutely cannot wait to return to try the other dishes!

Oysters for $1.5 for HH, they are on the thinner ends of the scale so you get another of meat there but the sauce and fried shallots give it a nice refreshing flavor than the common sauces.

Zabb Wings - nice flavorful crunch on the outside with tender and moist meat underneath, would def order this again!

Grilled pork cheeks - the sauce, amazing. It paired so well with the perfectly ratio of meat and fat.

Manila clams - a good dish but the table wouldn't miss it if it wasn't there..

Coconut crab curry - this is your go to if you're into a coconut curry, it had plenty of crab!! Definitely order this and if you can handle your spice.

Prawn karee - I'm drooling just thinking about this one. The prawns were so juicy and plumpy! Sauce was on another level and innovative in a way for throwing eggs into it. Highly recommend.

Khua Kling - be ready for your next visit on the toilet, the spice is wild on this one.. but flavors? Top notch, was it worth the bathroom visit? I'd say so

Coconut ice cream - YES YES YES, we kept ordering more and more til we literally almost got kicked out, jk oops

Can't wait to come back!

This place is so good but so expensive. :( The coconut crab curry is delicious (spicy so beware). The crab fried rice was amazing but is like $33. It comes with a side of sauces to really amplify the flavor. The pork cheek is so soft and fatty. I've ordered it twice. I've also rebought their signature zabb seasoning and have it as a home spice now. I pour it on my eggs and popcorn lol.

Wow this place is amazing. Would definitely come again. Not pictured are the chicken wings but they were a hit!! None of the items were super oily. Everything was every fresh and flavorful! Highly recommend and would come again when I'm in the city.

Good vibes, good food, good service. Not the greatest thai restaurant in NYC, but it was still very nice.

My friend and I went on a busy saturday night without a reservation, and luckily enough, we got a seat at the bar just when we walked in. Don't try your luck, though, because the wait can be hours long.

We split the basil clams and coconut crab curry. Both were really yummy and had a nice spiciness to them--the curry was one of their most popular dishes and was a bit spicier, nothing overpowering though. The clams were a "snack" size but were tastier than the curry, in my opinion. I just wish the curry was bigger given its price--$30 for one bowl with a side of rice--as well as its advertisement as a "shareable" dish.... Either don't come here super hungry, or plan on having a "shareable" plate by yourself.

We also got the 2 for $20 "She Fell Off the Boat" shots. It came with two vodka shots infused with their medicine block herbs (nice and floral), as well as some pickled mango and pan dan tea as a chaser. These were great, and I'd highly recommend!! Note: if you're looking for a more elegant cocktail, the "Tongue In Cheek" was super popular.

By far my favorite Thai place in the city. It's very different from any other Thai restaurant I've been to as they specialize in very fresh fish and seafood. The fish is the star of the show!! The restaurant is also very cozy with a nice ambiance. 

You have to get the grilled Branzino, the sauce they pair it with is to die for.

I don't even remember how many times I have been here.
Never disappoint me and my friends 
Foods, drinks and wait staff....
A bit pricy compared to other Thai restaurants in the city but it has its own perks 
Everything is perfectly done. 
I would recommend to try Grilled Pork Cheeks and Crab Fried Rice.

I haven't given a 5 stars on Yelp in a long time, and Fish Cheeks is highly deserving of this! I want to take all my friends and family here so we can order even more things to try :D

The star of the meal would be the fish, but before we get into that, you absolutely must get the oysters and the grilled pork cheeks. Happy hour pricing for the oysters is such a great deal too, $9 for 6! While the oysters were deliciously fresh, it's the side green sauce and fried shallots combination with the oysters that really brings out a spicy and refreshing slurp that will leave you wanting more orders (which is what we ended up doing!). 

Grilled pork cheeks ($17) is a perfect balance of meat to fat that the mouth feel wasn't greasy, but melty and tender enough that you're soon picking up the next pieces. For an appetizer, it's a good portion too, as I was definitely expecting only four pieces or so. Nice sear on them, with a spicy/sour sauce on the side that I didn't use much as the protein itself had a lot of flavor already. Yummm

Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs ($38): the best fish I've had in awhile! I love that it's deboned (there was still some on the side but that's fine) so it was such a smooth eating process without having to worry about accidentally choking. The fish itself is soo soft too. The soup that it's in is a bit like pickled cabbage fish in that it's sour, but it's very refreshing with all the herbs. It's served with the flame underneath it to keep it hot during the entire meal as well. Next time, I would definitely order either a crab fried rice or rice side dish to go with the fish, as towards the end, the soup did get a little too sour for my usual tastes, so some carbs would go well with that. But flavor and taste wise, absolutely delicious. 

Highly recommend!

It was so cold in the restaurant that I had to put my coat and scarf on. Not a pleasant dining experience. Food was also mediocre. I had the corn salad and green curry. Have had much better at hole-in-the-wall thai places. I had been excited to eat here but will not come back.

Loved the seafood options! The shrimp in 3 crab sauce was amazingly good. The citrus and chili really go well together. I could easily eat multiple servings of it. The coconut crab curry and crab fried rice was well recommended as the fan favorites. They both had generous lumps of crab but flavor wise was quite standard. The whole fish steamed fish was by far the best part of our meal there. Just the presentation was very impressive and the fish is so fresh and well cooked. The citrus flavors work really well in everything. Will be returning!

My No1 favorite Thai Food restaurant in NYC. Never been disappointed. Ordered Tom Yum Soup, Chicken wings, Crab Fried Rice.  
Service was friendly and efficient. Love it.
The best coconut crab curry ever. I recommended to my friend, he's literally spitting fire rn. I think he's okay tho. The pork cheek and steamed fish were all very delish.

Make reservations online ahead of time because wait times otherwise are long and it can be hard to get a table. 

Fish cheeks lived up to the hype and I loved every dish my table of 4 tried. The cocktails were also great! It was a pricey meal (over $100 pp including drinks, tax and tip) but the food was worth it!

Great food! Always consistent, been here 4 times now. Recently had the branzino wrapped in banana leaf, crab curry, shrimp in 3 sauce and the morning glory. The branzino and morning glory were my favorite.

Good service and food, but small portions and expensive prices. 

Had to take off 1 star right away for the dinky small portion of prawn aob woonsen they give you. You can't really split this dish between more than 2-3 people it's ridiculous.. just give us 30% more noodles man it's cheap to do. For charging $27 price we should get a decent amount of noodles. 

Other portions are okay but still rely on getting u full with rice. 

Also, why is the thai iced tea and coffee so expensive? $8? Whaat is going on? Stop this madness there's no justification.

Just had dinner here last night and it truly exceeded my expectations!! Highly recommend getting a reservation during happy hour from 5-6pm, you can get a half dozen oysters for $9 and discounted drinks.

Fish Cheeks' Thai cuisine is so unique, and I love all the fish decor. Even the bathroom sink handles are fish shaped!

Jenna was our server and she was AMAZING, extremely attentive and so friendly. We started with a half dozen oysters, just $9 during Happy Hour. It was so fresh and flavorful that we had to get another round. For drinks, we got cocktails ($11), the Tongue & Cheek which is lychee flavored and the Pandan Gin Fizz (my boyfriend accidentally called it Pandan Gizz when ordering lol). We loved both drinks.

For entrees, we got the popular Steamed Fish & Coconut Crab Curry. The Steamed Fish really knocked it out of the park for me. The Thai herbs made it so tangy and the fish was so soft, delicious, and juicy. They serve it to you with a little fire underneath to keep it hot for your entire meal. Don't miss out on the fish! The Coconut Crab Curry was too spicy for me to eat (my spice tolerance is low, so FYI to others if you can't handle spice, I wouldn't order this) but it was still very good; rich, creamy, but you can still taste the sweet crab flavor. I can't wait to come back and bring others to try this place!

Absolutely do NOT come here if you cannot handle your spicy food. I normally can handle my Indian curries at 2-stars, sometimes 3, without an issue. 

The curry we tried had my friend and I sniffling out the door with our tongues on fire, desperate for any solace we could find (which did not come in the form of the $10 Thai iced tea they offered, much to my despair). 

Unfortunately, this is the type of restaurant that you must practice for before you go. Otherwise, you'll make it about 5 spoonfuls in before you leave with a pounding head and a mouth that regrets every decision you made in the last five minutes. 

The clams were good, but nothing special IMHO.

I've been wanting to come here for a long time and I finally got to go yesterday with one of my best friends. The place is small so we opted for sitting at the bar. We enjoyed the jelly sauce that came with the complimentary shrimp chips. It was sweet with a lot of flavor. I had done my research on this place so I knew I wanted to try the Coconut Crab Curry. Skeptically, we ordered one coconut crab curry because the menu said it is shareable but me and her like to eat so we were just hoping it would be enough. It looked small initially but it is in fact shareable we just ordered an extra bowl of rice. It was so creamy and spicy I just wish there was more crab. I also ordered a Thai ice tea that was delicious. I definitely want to come back and try the Steam Fish With Thai Herbs or the Prawn Karee. I'll probably also order a coconut crab curry to go for myself lol

Love it  
You beat all Thai food from Los Angeles.
I also enjoyed the cocktail here  def would come again!

Had a great meal here! Came with a group of 4, we were seated promptly with our reservation, it's a bit tight seating with the tables all super close together but still comfortable! We had a few different things to try and everything was really good! Worth noting that everything is pretty spicy so something with multiple chilis next to them should be noted! The drinks were awesome and I would order every dish again! Our server was also very nice and helpful.

The food was obviously wonderful here, but we walked away most excited about Fish Cheeks' cocktail program. Tried four among us and all were good, most were excellent. My personal favorite was the Thank You Kha (white rum, coconut, galangal, ginger, lemongrass, makrut lime, and chili oil drops). It had a rather complex and completely unique floral/herbal flavor profile and was very well balanced. Also enjoyed the Spicy Mango with tequila, mango, lime, and Thai bird's eye chili, which had a certain richness to it that was faintly reminiscent of a mango lassi and had this complementary tropical fruitiness and spiciness. 

The oysters were notable for their nam
Jin seafood sauce, which is a bit like a mignonette sauce but has a fish sauce note.

We split two main courses: the crab fried rice and rainbow trout pad cha. The fried rice had a very light but pleasant flavor and also came with two sauces, including the nam jin. The rainbow trout (fillet trout, habanero chili, acacia leaf, green bean, ginger root, basil and green peppercorn served with rice) dish was spicy, slightly sour, and had a light sweetness. The sauce is mildly addictive. 

A note about the spice levels here: the menu includes the spice level of each item, from 0 - 3 chili peppers. The trout had one chili and I found it pretty spicy. The table beside us ordered something with 3 chilis and they couldn't finish it and seemed to be in pain. So take care.

I came here with a work group of 7. We ordered all the appetizers and a majority of the entrees. All family style. It was fantastic. Group consensus was that everything we had was a 10/10. I will definitely return. My favorite dish was the chicken.

This was hands down one of my favorite meals during my last visit to New York! My friend and I stopped by for lunch on a Monday around 12:30 pm and the place was pretty packed. They have happy hour from 12-3:15 pm daily so we definitely took advantage of their oyster specials which are $18 for a dozen.  We started off with a dozen oysters, grilled pork cheeks, pakboong fai dang (morning glory), and their coconut crab curry.  The oysters come with their nam jim seafood sauce and fried shallots and were AMAZING! Oysters were super fresh and the sauce and shallots were such an amazing combo.  We couldn't get enough of it!  Next, the grilled pork cheeks came out and we were blown away with how tender and perfect these pieces of pork cheeks were.  It came with jeaw sauce and it was the ultimate flavor combination with the pork cheeks. So so good!  The morning glory was also really tasty and was great to eat with our meal.  Finally, our coconut crab curry came out and it was absolutey divine.  It had nice chunks of crab in the curry and the flavors were on point.  We ended up ordering an extra dozen oysters because it was so delicious.
I wish I could've came here one more time to eat during my trip but we didn't have the time. This is definitely one of my top restaurants in NY and I can't wait to make a trip back just so I can come visit Fish Cheeks again.

Super disappointing. Although this review is for the delivery from Fish Cheeks, it was underwhelming if you see the pictures below for its crab curry. It came about half full in a tiny container with tiny pieces of crab and a box of rice. It was as if someone just threw in some leftover crab pieces into a curry without any other ingredients. For $30 + delivery? Would definitely go somewhere else.

We have dined here twice and ordered takeouts three times since we moved to this neighborhood. The food is absolutely amazing. The pork cheeks and the crab fried rice are our favorites. The curry is spot on. No wonder it is such a popular restaurant. The first time we came here, we were lucky enough to get a table for 2 outdoors because we came right before 5 pm on a weekday. Reservation is highly recommended.

My only complaint is about picking up takeouts. Unfortunately, this restaurant doesn't seem to have a good system in place for picking up takeouts. On all three occasions, there was only one host/hostess outside, and that person was understandably busy dealing with all the patrons waiting to be seated. No one seemed to be paying attention to those waiting for takeouts. My third time picking up my order, which was this evening, was my worse experience so far. 

This evening I arrived at the restaurant at around 6:55 pm, five minutes after Postmates showed that the order was ready. I informed the host that I came here to pick up my order and gave him my name. After a quick trip indoors, he told me "they" would check on it. Two deliverymen came and talked to a different person at the restaurant. They were able to pick up their orders right away. I figured maybe mine wasn't done yet despite Postmates saying otherwise, so I patiently waited for ten minutes.

After ten minutes, I asked the same host again to check on my order. I got the same answer, except this time he didn't even bother to go inside and check. I was confused to say the very least. He just stood at his stand as if he had nothing to do with all of this. Through the open front door, I watched other staff come and go, yet no one seemed to be checking on my order at all. 

At one point, three more deliverymen arrived. After getting the same "they would check on it" answer from this host, they waited with me for a couple of minutes. It was at this point that they decided to take matters into their own hands. They stormed into the restaurant, one after another, with gigantic backpacks on their back. Now that finally got the restaurant's attention, and after kicking out the deliverymen, someone quickly came outside with four or five orders. I briefly thought about doing the same, but foolishly decided against doing so because I didn't want to cause any more chaos on a busy evening.

Ten more minutes passed. I realized I had to be more proactive. I got a hold of a waitress walking by the door and asked her to check on my order. She asked for my name, and for the third time I gave my name. Within a minute, there it was. My precious crab curry. I understood, right at that moment, it had been sitting on the shelf the entire time. I had been talking to a guy who decided he was too good to be the one picking it up for me.

TLDR please don't ignore those customers picking up their takeout orders. Thanks.
the drinks were really good. food was ok, kind of bland. I guess that's why they give you a bunch of sauces.

We've been back twice and can't wait to go back again! Great vibes, good drinks, and the food is awesome. A bit pricey for Thai food but make it a date night and it's totally worth it!

Our favorites are the wings (MUST), oysters, and the whole fish!

I organized a lunch hangout for my classmates here, and it was a great time for everyone! The reservations teams was very easy to coordinate with via email. I would highly recommend coming here for the food, the service, and the overall ambiance.
One of my Top 5 favorite restaurants in NYC. Food is amazing, from the steamed fish to the wings. Everything is so flavorful. Customer service is great.

Fish Cheeks is not all hype. Everything we ordered was DELICIOUS! The chicken wings were extremely flavorful, the crab curry was so good but a bit too spicy. We loved the whole fish. I can't wait to go back.

Came here for the happy hour oysters with my bf and his sister last weekend! She raved about the oysters and the delicious fried shallot topping so I knew we had to try it. She was correct! I LOVED the fried shallot and had never had this on a raw oyster before. They don't use the regular cocktail sauce, but this was even better. We got two dozen to share but ended to getting one more dozen hahah. 

We didn't try any of their other dishes, but I do want to come back to try their fish dishes! And of course get more oysters!

5/5!!

The oysters are a must try. The sauce they have for it is amazing. However, they did use this same sauce in many of their dishes (same sauce for the raw shrimp) thus it did become a bit repetitive. 

The cocktails were good. Everything is a bit on the pricier NY typical price range. 

The curry is not memorable to me; I can't remember it at all. I'd order the crab fried rice again. The fish was good but again - very similar flavors of the oyster/raw shrimp. 

I'd go back but probably not order mult dishes with the same sauce.

3.5 stars for me. I enjoyed this place a lot before reservations became so hard to come by and oysters were 1 dollar per for happy hour. Times have changed however and they're becoming Hollywood. Either way that doesn't take away from the quality of both food and drinks they offer.
