tl;dr: Highly recommend you come with a large group (or be prepared for leftovers) as the flavour profile of each entree is slightly unbalanced on its own but creates a delicious harmony when paired with other dishes. And get the pork cheeks.

My friend brought me here as this is one of her favorite places for Thai food in Manhattan. We made reservations for 5:45pm on a Wednesday--right at the end of their happy hour so we got their cocktails and oysters. Oysters were alright, and their cocktails are pretty strong. The tongue & cheek was probably my favorite.

To start we also ordered the pork cheeks and the zabb wings. The pork cheeks were so flavourful, and somehow both soft and crispy--for sure a must-order. I also really liked the lime-forward flavour in the zabb wings, but in general I'm not a fan of dry rub wings and found myself wanting a dip on the side.

The entrees are called kub khao (plates to share), and I can see why. We got the coconut crab curry, crab fried rice, and steamed fish. Each dish leaned heavily towards one flavour: the curry was super spicy, the fried rice was salty, and the steamed fish was very sour from all the lime. Independently I probably would've found each of them to be too overpowering, but eating all 3 together created more of a balance and had me appreciating the aspects of each individual dish more. The one exception would probably be the rice which I still found to be too salty--I ended up mixing it with some plain white rice to make it more palatable. Also a warning that I thought I had a high spice tolerance, but that crab curry really put me and my stomach through it--order at your own risk.

Throughout our visit service was friendly and prompt, and despite ordering so much and the place being busy, our dishes came out quick. Definitely hope to come again!

best thai food i had in the city goes to...

..FISH CHEEKS..!

visited on a sunday night, and had originally called in expecting to wait an hour, but after getting to the restaurant, our party of 3 was super swiftly seated!

their cocktails were particularly delicious--i had the pandan one and it had a subtle taste of pandan to show face without being overpowering.

the steamed fish in the wrapping and the pan was sooooo good..although the sauce that comes with it might come off a little overpowering.

tom yum soup was also super yummy and flavorful. was a fan favorite within my party!

also had the crab curry, tasty as well. i liked the fact that they weren't shy with the spicy levels when we ordered it. my only gripe is that i wish it came with more rice.

great service, nice ambience, and wasn't too cold despite not sitting with a heat lamp next to us.

i don't typically gravitate towards going out for thai, but when in the city won't hesitate to swing by fish cheeks any chance i can moving forward.

Coconut Crab Curry was SPICY AF. I can handle spice, and even this was spicy for me. My other two companions felt the same way. 

Everything else was great. The prawns with vermicelli was my favorite. The portion, however, was underwhelming- it's enough for a few bites each when shared with 3 people. 

Husband really loved the Tom Yum soup. 

We all like the crab fried rice. 

Morning glory dish was yum too! 

My only complaint is that the coconut crab curry was SPICY AF and I feel the waitress should have mentioned it to us. When I complained about it, she dismissed my complaint and said that it had two chili signs next to it on the menu. 

Just beware when ordering that crab curry. 

The Thai Iced Teas are $8 here. I'm from LA, and I'm not used the seeing $8 Thai Iced Tea ever lol. That is all.

first time here, great service

food: 
fried rice was great
steam fish was really good
prawns karee was creamy

When we ate there with my friends we requested for outdoor sitting and we were attended to very promptly . Superb food!! We ordered Steamed Branzino and it was fantastic! Aside from delicious fresh fish the presentation was also superb! The crab fried rice , sweet corn salad were all delectable and generous servings! Will be sure to dine back with some friends soon!

Great authentic Thai flavor. Limited menu but recommend all of the appetizers. The pork jowl, chicken wings and crispy rice were all great. Fried fish just like in Thailand and the crab fried rice was better.

Rating the vegetarian food only! We ordered takeout from here and I ordered the corn salad and the green curry. Sadly, these were the only two vegetarian options. Corn salad was good, nothing mind blowing, but it was refreshing. There was a kick to it from the Thai red chilis that I liked. The dressing was a sweet but tangy vinaigrette, which paired well with the corn. 

For my entree I got the green curry. Spice level was higher than I expected for no extra spice being added, which I appreciated. The vegetables added to the curry were a major miss for me. First, they seemed pretty random - broccoli, cauliflower, squash and eggplant. Second, they were all undercooked too!! It seemed like they just threw raw veggies into the curry. Also, there was no protein option for vegetarians. The curry itself was tasty, it was the vegetables and lack of protein where I have deduct from my rating on.
Love the food especially the crab fried rice and fried fish..  It looks like a hole in the wall but the food is excellent.

This Thai place has very unique and flavorful dishes at a high price point. We ordered pork cheeks to start, and they were quite yummy and fatty crispy! The prawn karee and coconut crab curry were my favorite and had amazing rich seafood flavors. The crab fried rice was kinda standard, but still tasted really good and came with fish sauce and a sour pesto-y sauce. Finally, the steamed fish (not pictured) was cooked so tenderly and had an acidic flavor that was both soothing and delicious. I highly recommend family-style to try as many of their amazing flavorful dishes as possible!

4.5/5

My favorite restaurant in NYC!!! I've been going here since I was still in school. It always brings me the best memories. Everything tastes exquisitely amazing. If it's your first time, you will be pleasantly surprised by the little twists in some of the dishes you are familiar with, but also satisfied with the classic favors that are still in there. Just realized all these years I've never wrote a review about them so here I am. Please don't miss it!

Fish Cheeks is a Seafood- Focused Thai Food Establishment in the NOHO Section of Manhattan. Fish Cheeks gets 4.5 Stars as it served to be a place that provided a good dining experience. According to their website, they create a modern approach to Thai Dishes and that is evident throughout the various dishes that are on their menu. 

The three of us decided to meet up at Fish Cheeks last month on a Friday Evening after work for dinner. Fish Cheeks has both Indoor and Outdoor Dining  and we showed our Vaccine Cards in order to enjoy Indoor Dining. Fish Cheeks has casual yet chic decor that includes table-sized candles, cool lighting fixtures and floral patterned wallpaper in the bathroom facilities. Fish Cheeks also has a "Merch" Menu where one can purchase a signature shirt, sweater, tote, beanie, special seasoning, etc. 

We were looking forward to eating here as one of us craved + raved about the food from their previous dining experiences at Fish Cheeks. Fish Cheeks has interesting dishes that can be prepared mild, medium, spicy, etc.  We Ordered The Following:

FOOD -
KIIN LEN (Plates to Snack On) -
Grilled Pork Cheeks - Grilled Pork marinated in Fish Saucer + served with Jeaw Sauce. 

KUB KHAO (Plates to Share) - 
Crab Fried Rice - Crab, Rice, Egg, Scallion, Cilantro, + Cucumber served w/ Nam Jim Seafood + prik nam pla. This one was one of my favorite dishes. 

Coconut Crab Curry- Southern Style Gravy w/ Crab Meat, housemade Curry Paste + Betel Leaves served w/ Rice.

Grilled Branzino - GRrilled Fish Seasoned w/ Sea Salt + served with Cashew Garlic Sauce. This was one of my favorite dishes. 

COCKTAILS-
Tongue + Cheek Cocktail - Vodka, Lychee, Hibiscus, Aquafaba + Toasted Black Sesame.

Pandan Gin Fizz Cocktail - Oandan Infused Gin, Lemon, Lemongrass, Aquafaba + Singha Soda. 

Great Tasting Well-prepared Food + Cocktails! We talked about how good everything tasted throughout the entire meal. We even contemplated ordering more food and I also considered getting Crab Fried Rice in a To-Go Bag-lol. My favorites were the Crab Fried Rice + Grilled Branzino and I would definitely order those item again.  The Grilled Branzino + Crab Fried Rice deemd to be a nice pairing +  complimentary dishes to one another. Fish Cheeks serves nice Family-Style Plates w/ nicely shared-sized portions + good cocktails in a cool atmosphere. 

Fish Cheeks Information- 
Instagram- @fishcheeksnyc
Website-www.fishcheeksnyc.com
Email - info@Fishcheeksnyc.com
Hours of Operation- Monday - Thursday 12pm-3:15om (Lunch Service) + 5pm-10:15pm (Dinner Service). Friday - Sunday 12pm-3:15pm (Lunch Service) + 5pm-11:15pm (Dinner Service). Once can make reservations via Resy. There js Happy Hour every day from 12pm-3:15pm and from 5pm-6pm.

The food ended up being fairly costly, but I think it was definitely worth it and would love to come again. We ordered quite a bit of food - the crab fried rice, the steamed fish, the tom yum, the coconut crab curry, the crispy rice salad and zabb wings. The zabb wings were very unique and flavorful; the outside is salted with some seasoning that tastes really moreish. The crispy rice salad was also fairly interesting. The coconut curry was great, although it was quite spicy. It was a kind of spice that hits later and not immediately, and leaves the back of your throat feeling quite hot. The perfect solution to this is to order a thai iced tea, which was REALLY good. I never really get side drinks at restaurants but this is something I would probably get again if I came. It tasted amazing and was the perfect complement to the curry. I thought the steamed fish was ok but I'm just not the biggest fan of steamed fishes in general - it was really tender though. The meal came out to be quite pricey but I think it was worth it and would come again!

Absolutely excellent food. Dare I say- best Thai food I have had? 

We got the Zaab wings as an appetizer, which was crispy, perfectly cooked and very flavorful! I didn't expect to enjoy a drier wing so much but it was great. The seasonings were perfect. 10/10

For the main course we had:
- Crab Coconut Curry. Overall pretty flavorful! 9/10
-Kua Kling, which is a stir fried dry beef curry. The spice level was crazy and I can handle my spice. Even though it was quite spicy the flavors were excellent, just make sure to get yourself a lot of water/thai tea to help with the spice! 10/10. If you can't handle spice, skip this dish. 
- Tom Yum. Delicious and a nice break from the very spicy Kua Kling. This dish has a mix of seafood including mussels, fish, and prawn. The Tom yum was creamy and perfectly sour. 10/10.

For dessert, we had an ice cream which was also great.

Overall I couldn't recommend this place enough. It's not cheap but I promise you that your tastebuds will thank you.

Table of 3. Normal go-to is steamed fish but decided to try fried and it was well worth the try. Satisfying and well done.
Crab curry was a bit weak compared to expectations given that it was highly recommended. Spicy. Saltier dish, but that's expected for curry.
Morning glory has a kick but very satisfying and a great accompaniment to the fish.
Coconut ice cream and pumpkin custard desserts were loved by the table. Pumpkin custard was warm and comforting. Coconut ice cream with Ovaltine was fun and delightful.

I'm a big fan and thai food and have tried my fair share of Thai food in the city. Fish cheeks really stand out among all of them. We tried their oysters, zabb wings, coconut crab curry and steamed fish. Looking at the names they seemed quite ordinary but the taste was nothing but.
Oysters: we went for happy hour so they were $1 each (might have been $2, can't remember). I've only had oysters with tabasco before but here they use a mix of thai flavors. They were easily the best oysters I've had. Do yourself a favor and try those fresh oysters with their sauce!
Zabb wings: crispy, lightly breaded, and seasoned to perfection. The wings were the perfect size. The middle of the wings were not as bland as most other places.
Coconut crab curry: they give you a generous amount of crab meat. The curry itself was not overpowering or too heavy. Mix it with rice and thank me later.
Steamed fish: I just really really love thai flavors. This was the first time I tried steamed fish with thai spices and seasoning and now I want it every day. The perfect balance of salty sweet and umami. Really complements the fresh fish. 
Solid 5/5 in presentation and taste of food, and service. 10/10 would return over and over again!

Delicious, delicious food! One of the more authentic Thai places in Manhattan and was pleasantly surprised by the abundance of flavor and the fact that they were not shy about spiciness! Actually reminded me of food in Thailand. Khua kling was so tasty (but definitely more than a tad on the spicy side), and came with tons of beef. Coconut crab curry was also delicious and the curry sauce was amazing, but they were a bit skimpy on the crabmeat. The rainbow trout pad cha was also very good, the broth was gingery and flavorful, was the least spicy out of the 3 dishes. The drinks were great as well. Flavors were great and didn't give us a tiny amount like some other places, which justified the $17 a drink. Negroni was perfect and strong. Pandan gin fizz was mellow and just slightly sweet. Our waitress was great as well, brought me half a glass of Thai iced tea free of charge when the spiciness was too much (eventually ordered my own glass, hint: do not eat the green peppercorns). Overall excellent place, wish the crabmeat curry had more crabmeat, but the quality of food and drink made up for it.

Fantastic Thai food. The oysters are a must have. The sauce is well balanced with heat, spiciness and savory. The crab fried rice, crab curry and Bronzino were all phenomenal too. Service was both friendly and informative. Clean bathroom, but today there was always a line. I would return in a heart beat. The  oysters also were at an insanely good happy hour price. Give it a try!

Been eating at this restaurant on and off for a while.  My first impression, pre-pandemic was this IS a great place and I did return w family and friends who all agreed it was great!  During the pandemic my family an I had dinner there and it was so-so not up to par with pre-pandemic food.  This is where I will tell you to eat there and support this place!  My family and I went there again on Sunday 10-24-21 to celebrate my father-in-laws 93rd birthday. The food was great, the service was exceptional but most of all my father in law loved it he ate almost the whole order or crab fried rice and steamed fish!

So yes this is a hidden gem on Bond Street

Came here with Alexis and Wendy and I had a delicious good time!! The place is very cute and casual.  We had to show proof of vaccination to enter. The service was good and quick.

I started with the pork cheek and it was so tender and tasty.  I'm mean it was succulent and divine.  Then we shared curry crab, crab fried and a whole fish. All the crab dishes were wonderful. Both the curry and fried rice were filled with lump crab meat not scattered little piece, these were my favorites.  They also have wonderful signatures drink I mean these we very tasty and good ratio of alcohol to flavorings.

I recommend this place if your every in the area and you want delicious Thai seafood!

The hype is real!! We snagged a reservation at the last possible second and was so grateful. We came on a Wednesday evening and ate to our hearts content.

My brother, his girlfriend, and myself were seated inside in the heart of the action. We ordered the fried chicken, the crab fried rice, the crab curry, and the fish. Definitely get the fish. I am usually too intimidated by a whole fish but they debone it for you and make it very easy/accessible to eat. I ended up eating a bit of the Fish Cheeks which is supposed to give you good luck (?) but did not have much of a distinct taste. My absolutely favorite was the crab curry. It was so savory, rich, salty, hearty, and just intensely flavorful. There was a great amount of crab as well. The fish was definitely delicious, tender, and salty with the sauce that it was served with. The fried chicken was crispy, had a bit of a spicy kick, and packed a huge umami punch. The crab fried rice was the only thing not super memorable, but to be honest it was probably because I slathered the rice in the curry for a two pack crab punch.

The interior is fun and a bit whimsical with the colors. There is enough seating inside but the only downside is that there is only one bathroom. The waitstaff is super friendly and helpful in clarifying each dish. I would strongly recommend coming here and making a reservation beforehand, but probably make the reservation WAY beforehand because they are rightfully booked!

This place si super busy. Either come when they first open and rsvp prior. I made a rsvp for 2 for dinner and 530 and was able to sit right away. Out waiter was super sweet. She went on details whats on the menu. Also there is happy hours between 5-6 for their cocktail menu and oyster (11 dollars). Best to come around this time to try out their cocktail menu. We had pork cheeks, crab curry, oyster, crab fried rice. Everything is delicious 
. Also tried thier off menu chicken. Nothing too special. Remind me ofCosco chicken lol. But def a great place for thai food with chill atmosphere and friendly service

Food was inventive and delicious. Cocktails were well balanced. Staff was warm and engaging. The decor was sexy and playful. Great place to go on a Saturday night or during the week. My new favorite restaurant in Manhattan.

Wooooow. After following them on IG for a while, I finally got to eat here and it completely blew my mind. We ordered almost everything on the menu and our expectations were surpassed. My only comment is that the coconut crab curry had a slight bitterness to it but still delicious. Thank you to our servers who were also incredible and friendly.

Fish cheeks tops all the Thai restaurants I've been to in NYC! The flavors are incredible and you simply won't be able to order many of these dishes in another generic Thai restaurant. Truly, I'm a picky eater but everything is perfect. 

The zabb chicken wings has it all: a dry rub with some sourness and packed with some heat. It's my ONE favorite chickens wings in all of NY.

The entrees are quite impressive too. I'd recommend prawn karee with its thick garlic sauce. But you can't go wrong with po tak (which had so much seafood packed in sour and spicy broth) and crab fried rice (a classic that didn't fail).

We made reservations far in advance, although it seems there were lots of bar walk-ins. 

Everything we ordered was delicious-- pork cheek, po tak soup, crab curry and the fried snapper. 

Our waitress was not the most friendly, so that's how good the food was! Beware of spice.. and half of us had to rush to the bathroom soon after. The iron stomachs did not
Another lucky day for us. Walked in without reservation and got a table outside. Was able to catch the daily happy hour (5-6pm), a dozen of oysters for $18 and specialty cocktail for $11 each.
Pretty good thai for Manhattan, but still a tier below Jackson Heights. The coconut crab curry was the best thing we tried, although the salad on the fried fish was also pretty good!

Came by for lunch and got a couple drinks and plates to share. My favorite was the zabb wings which were v crispy and well seasoned ! I loved the lime flavor that came through. The spicy mango drink was fun and fruity with a nice kick to it but a little too much in combination w the other spicy dishes we got. I really wanted to like the coconut crab curry but it was too spicy for me. I generally consider myself pretty good at handling spice esp when it adds to the flavor of a dish but in this case felt it was overwhelming and we weren't able to finish it. Service was attentive but towards the end felt like they were pushing us to leave despite the fact that we hadn't been there for that long and there were plenty of empty tables. Overall thought the food was pretty good, but not sure if I'd come back again soon.
Food was okay. I thought the oysters could have been fresher, although the condiments were good.

11/10 for food, service and all around a good time

Food was cooked perfectly, and thats coming from someone who can't handle spice and yet still wanted more because the food tasted so good. The flavor combinations of everything was delicious and those wings are a MUST- sweet, spicy and a perfect crunch! The Potak is good if you like fish sauce smell/taste, similar to Tom Yum in terms of flavor and smell. The coconut crab curry was a hit or miss with our group but if you like peanuts and crab, this is perfect for you - it is spicy though! The desserts were done well and with such skill. The pumpkin custard was an actual pumpkin that you could eat whole and the strings on top were candied egg yolk! 

Go check out Fish Cheeks!

The happy hour here is $11 of any cocktail which is a steal, however the drinks have extremely odd flavors combos, most of the food on the menu is over priced, over hyped & waaaaay too spicy (as a brown woman spice is my birthright) & these dishes were obnoxious. Over hyped. & def not a fan, wouldn't recommend when there are so many other, better Thai food options around

Refreshingly good Thai food that with a different menu from the average Thai restaurant. They have some fun and unique cocktails as well.

My favorite dish by far was the Grilled Pork Cheeks, but the Coconut Crab Curry was great as well. The Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs was good too, but be prepared to deal with some bones since it is a whole fish.
Great food and great service! Love this place. Both fried rice options are delicious, as are the prawns and chicken wings

Get the pork cheeks for some cheeky fun, tasty meaty, having you wondering why we dont eat more cheeks in this country. The crab curry was FIRE and delicious. Shrimp on noodles was another favorite of the night. With a table of four, you can basically order the whole menu

We went here at 12pm Sunday and booked reservations just to be safe, after seeing some people waiting a few hours for a table during dinner time. It's also beneficial to go here for lunch as they have happy hour for oysters and drinks at a discount. 

We got the Somtum Corn Salad and half dozen oysters to start. The corn salad has great sauce that is slightly spicy yet refreshing. The oysters have accompaniments that are more unique and Thai-inspired versus the stereotypical horseradish etc. I greatly prefer these accompaniments honestly, especially the fried shallots which gave nice flavor but did not mask the fresh oyster flavor. It also converted my friend to loving oysters.

Then, we got the popular coconut crab curry and steamed fish. Coconut crab curry features huge chunks of crab meat and the sauce is quite spicy. The rice is not a lot for the amount of curry they give, which is alright because the dish is what matters most. Steamed fish is pretty good with lots of lime and Thai spices. 

Service here is solid with consistent replacements of empty water jugs. The meal can get pricey really really fast so just be careful, but it's mostly worth it as the seafood is very fresh and a Thai friend vouched for this place so it's legit.

Every dish was so good, packed with so much flavor!! Recommend the crab curry, grilled pork cheeks, and branzino, that green sauce is amazing!! Can't beat the happy hour too, $1.50 oysters and $11 cocktails which is everyday! Can't wait to try the rest of the menu!

I've been dying to try this place and I even set up my reservation about 2 weeks out. Today I finally got to dine in and was very disappointed with the service. Don't get me wrong, the food was good but the service made the overall experience unpleasant. 

I got seated at the table that's right next to the bathroom even with the reservation which is the worst table in the restaurant. It's already gross eating next to the bathroom but there is only one bathroom in the whole restaurant so people were lining up to use the bathroom right next to our table. Line full of people right next to me while trying to eat was extremely uncomfortable and chaotic. I'm not sure if this is because the restaurant is pretty small but it's a pretty bad layout and I was really hoping to get a better table than that with a reservation. 

Next we had a server who was very awkward and unprofessional. She took our order and came back in like 5 mins asking us what we want to order. Maybe she forgot that we ordered, so we remind her that we already ordered and she looked confused but moved on. 

We ordered 2 mains and 2 sides and our table was really small to hold everything so we finish 2 dishes first and asked the server to remove them so we can make some room on the table. I think she was confused on which dishes to remove so we point and make it very clear which ones we want to remove and which ones we are still working on. Instead she removed 3 dishes, including the one that we were still eating... We tried to say something but she pulled them off so quickly and walked off immediately. I can overlook other mistakes but this one was crucial. 

At the end, we asked the server for a check and they had one of those portable check system that they print at the table. The server stood so close to me when I was paying, staring at the screen. They should always give customers some room when they are paying or at least try to small talk so it's not awkward... instead she literally watched me the whole time without saying anything and made me feel extremely uncomfortable. 

I've been in the service industry myself so I empathize with the servers but the service was unfortunately way below average. While the food is good, that alone is difficult to justify the overall price and tips.

Amazing all around. The wings are bursting with flavors and was really juicy. The branzino was also steamed and with the sauce really done right. My friend got the crab curry (spicy) which was also very delicious. I can't handle spicy so I may have wanted that toned down a bit. Deff go during happy hour, will be back to try other things!

Nestled on the corner of Bond St, is this bustling Thai bistro with a menu centered around seafood but don't let that stop you from ordering the meat. The Chicken Wings were some of the best I've had in the city with a dehydrated lemon zest and the little kick of chili creating a perfect layer of seasoning on the very tender wing. 

The Crab Fried hits the spot, but the most ordered dish, the Coconut Crab Curry were lacking in Crab meat and laid on the way spicier side than expected but was still delicious. 

The desserts were solid 4 stars - we got the Pandan Cake and the Ice cream with Egg Yolk and Ovomaltine. The cocktails were also great!
Best dinner after a while definitely worth to try , I don't always write a review but this place worth to put time

I am literally obsessed with this spot. You might have to wait a while but this is the best spot for happy hour oysters in nyc hands down! I love the green sauce. The coconut curry recipe may have changed since I went pre-covid but it's still creamy and has that hint of spiciness. The crab fried rice is AMAZING. The branzino was pretty good when I tried it too! 10/10 would recommend this place - everyone I took here fell in love with the food!

This review is a bit old but hopefully still relevant!

I do not like spicy food that much... But when I say this place is so good that I will go through the pain of the spice just to eat it... I hope it means a lot lol

The special appetizer sounded and was amazing! It was raw hamachi topped with a sweetish sauce with fresh vegetables on top! It wasn't spicy and was super fresh! 

The pork cheeks are a MUST order, they're super tender and just jam packed full of flavor! Sauce is a bit spicy but not too bad :) really brings out the flavors in the pork cheeks!

Raw Shrimp with a spicy seafood sauce. This was a dish I couldn't stop eating even though my mouth couldn't hand it !! I tried picking out as much chili and seeds as I could but it was so delicious!! The seafood sauce had a kick to it but it works well with the raw shrimp which was plump, soft and kinds chewy. I would totally come back for this dish!! So GOOOOOD!

The crab fried rice is probably one of the best I've ever had! Lots of crab huge meat and perfectly cooked fried rice! A nice carb on the side that isnt spicy to balance out all the flavors (imo)

I love this place !!!! Totally would recommend and would come back for that raw shrimp dish

I ordered the prawn curry and the only beef dish there. The portions are garbage. They told us it was shareable and that was a joke. The prawn curry came with 3 prawns and the beef dish was funky bowl of ground beef. We paid 100 bucks for two dishes and a side of rice and some bottled water. Don't come here. All the other top thai restaurants in NYC severely outclass this restaurant in every way. Service was great though so I tipped decently and they got another star from that.

Overpriced and overrated

Given the very positive review on The Infatuation I navigated my way to Fish Cheeks yesterday.

5pm on the dot. I didn't want to stay 2 hours in line....  The place is nice they placed tables and chairs outside with some distance.

The menu was pretty limited and seemed strong on the drinks.  I got their Som Tum Corn that is corn based with no papaya

It was nicely flavored but could be more generous.

For the main I got the Vegetarian  Green Curry, the only green curry option on the dish.  It also was  Ok flavored but could be more generous.

They do not ask for how spicy or not you want your food and it's pretty mild 

All in all. I had a better Thai food in the city for much less.

We walked in for lunch and didn't have to wait. 

Coconut crab curry - crab was shelled and it was creamy. Paired well with the rice.
Fried fish - the herbs, salad, and the sauce was amazing! The fried fish was perfectly crisped yet still juicy and mixed with the salad was splendid. This was the highlight and I absolutely would return just for this. 

This Thai restaurant doesn't really have all your traditional noodle dishes but instead has a wide variety of different seafood options. Refreshing change and worth a visit!

I went on a date with my fiance & we got there right when they opened at 5PM & since it was just me and him, we got seated inside, right away! The restaurant is so adorable -- It had a very cute and colorful ambiance!

We started off with appetizers -- raw oysters, crispy rice salad & pork, & grilled pork cheeks. The grilled pork cheeks were SOOO good! -- They were easily my favorite app! They were very juicy & had the perfect balance of lean & fatty meat!  The raw oysters were very delicious as well, when paired with their green sauce & crispy onion flakes that came with it, however some of the oysters were kinda small :( The crispy rice salad & pork was very flavorful but a tad spicy, but delicious nonetheless :)

For our entrees, we ordered tiger prawns karee, coconut crab curry & the crab fried rice. The tiger prawns karee was also very flavorful and MUST definitely eat with rice, since it's very saucy & can be a tad salty on its own. The crab fried rice was very aromatic & had big chunks of crab, which is just what i like to see :) The coconut crab curry is a bestseller & there is a reason why! It's freaking delicious! But beware, the spice is a sneaky one! It starts off sweet from the coconut but then the spice will slowly creep so be prepared! 

I would definitely come back & recommend to a friend!

2.5+

this place doesn't make sense to me. lots of hot people and asians frequent it, yet i forever leave this place semi-unsatisfied. 

staff are gen z as hell aka they have a job but 'fuck capitalism so i won't actually do my job' vibes. 

sticky tables

one bathroom

hot air

spicy ass food

limited variety

$5 cokes

aint me

Very authentic Thai food that reminds me of Thailand! Fresh ingredients, local seasoning, and tasty dishes! Highly recommend the steamed fish and the coconut curry dish. 

Lovely settings both indoor and outdoor. Efficient staff and fast service.

Fish Cheeks is probably my favorite restaurant. They have amazing authentic Thai flavors that contribute to an amazing dining experience. Loved the crab curry (spicy af though), fried fish, and grilled pork cheeks. It is a little pricey and not in my budget for a frequent meal, but the flavors are worth the money for an occasional treat. This place is ALWAYS packed because of how delicious it is. Make a reservation if you can because it is well worth it.

Charging for hot sauce at a Thai restaurant ? That's like charging for sand when entering the desert. The ignorant persistence of the server on this issue reflected poorly on the establishment, despite the bus boys, chef and kitchen staff doing their best to prepare meals in a timely fashion. Shame on her.

I'm going to second Picky M's review below and say that although the food is among the best in New York, the service, especially as it relates to the hosting, is terrible.

I've never felt compelled to write a review anywhere until today's lunch experience that effectively ruined my day. The hostess waited until we were nearly sat to tell us we had an hour at the table - having never given us a choice before - which ultimately led to the waitress rushing us through the rest of the service. That same rush though didn't apply to the food with entrees being delivered not long before the waitress told us we had to give up our table.

All this to say that it's great the restaurant is busy, and certainly deserved when it comes to the food, but there is a tactful way to turn tables and the front-of-house staff here is woefully unaware of it.

Sub-par restaurant catering to spoiled NYU kids that think they have a worldly palate.  The menu looks amazing, but be forewarned, the fish is not "fresh", the flavors are mediocre, and the dinnerware is dirty.  Our table was sticky, the "Zabb Wings" were dried out, the grilled pork cheeks were flavorless, and the Prawn Aob Woosen tasted like leftovers from a streetcart.  How this restaurant justifies $30+ entrees blows my mind.  Fish cheeks... send your management back to the chalk board because you guys need help.

Fish Cheeks Ratings: 4.1/5

Food: 4.5/5 - The pork cheeks was phenomenal, 100% blew my mind away. It has the perfect ratio of fat and lean meat, aka the richness of a pork belly, but with less fatty meat, literally the best thing ever. The texture was tender, delightful, and each bite was so wonderful; it's so good that you can't stop eating it. It was sliced thin, marinated in fish sauce, crisped and charred on the edges, but the pork cheeks itself is moist, juicy, and rich in flavors. We ordered the crab fried rice. It has simple ingredients, but tasty. The rice was chewy and al dente, not soggy or hard, literally the best CARBS I have eaten in a long time. Make sure to add the nam Jim and prik nam sauce to the rice. It added so many tastes to it: sweet, spicy, and sour, and it just worked out perfectly together. The steam fish with Thai herbs wasn't that impressive. It is a whole stripe bass cooked in chili, lime, and mint in a cilantro lime sauce. Fish meat was soft, melts in your mouth, tasted exactly like it was fresh out of the sea. I just think the cilantro lime broth did not impress me that much. Thought it was average, I'd say skip the steam fish. 

Ambiance: 4.25/5 - Located near SOHO. The outdoor seating is so pretty, and it's really hard to miss it. The outdoor patio is in some sort of a fish scale design and decorated in bright colors. The indoor decor is nice, small (limited seats), and intimate, with a full cocktail bar and bar seating. You can also see the kitchen in the back. 

Price: 3.75/5 - We ordered one appetizer and two plates to share. The pork cheeks is $17, the crab fried rice is $27, and the steam fish is $38, so total around $110 after tax and tips. I would say portion sizes are small, and shared among the three of us, we were definitely not full afterwards. This is on the more expensive side for sure, but the food and quality was good, so that somewhat makes up for it. 

Service: 4/5 - Staffs are attentive with their service and knowledgeable with the food items on the menu. Our server provided us recommendations and some popular items. Team was pretty cohesive and detail-oriented, felt welcomed and overall had a lovely experience. 

BLUF: Probably one of the most authentic Thai restaurant and a must visit in NYC for anyone that loves Thai food. Please get the pork cheeks and the crab fried rice, just do it seriously. There's good happy hour deals especially for oysters and drinks too.

After hitting some golf balls at the pier with a girl friend, we went here for Happy Hour which turned into a four hour hangout and catch up moment. They have an all week happy hour of drinks and $18 oysters/ dozen so as soon as we sat down, we each ordered a dozen to get it going. We drank up our first oysters so we got another dozen while we waited for the actual food to come out. Then we got a whole bunch of drinks and I even pulled some strings to get a glass of wine when the bar was closed until dinner time. 

The oysters are very special here. They serve them with a chimichurri like moment with garlic chips. Ladies/ gents, if you are on a date, make sure he/ she/ they have some garlic chips too because your breath will reek! However, do we care? You kind of need that crunch to offset the slimy, salty elixir that is not necessary but makes it so much better. 

Our actual meal, because oysters are more of snack than meal, was the shrimp glass noodles and crab curry. My girl friend and I both shared. She loved it. I thought it was good, but it was definitely  too sweet. Hindsight, some lime would have made the dishes a lot better. I so recommend the glass noodles. Seems they used to make it with crab once upon a time, but now it is shrimp. Would have liked the crab better, but it is a preference and there was crab in the curry. 

I forget the drink I got, but the first one was a mango and bird's eye chili moment. I wasn't a fan of it because the mango nectar they used made the drink viscous and my personal preference in a cocktail is strong, fresh, and not too sweet. My friend got some drink that looked like a dragonfruit. Pink with black seeds. I think they were trying to mimic a dragonfruit, but it was delicious. So the rest of my five drinks were that. Think it was called Tongue and Cheek. Vodka based and just so refreshing. I can drink a pitcher of it on my rooftop laying in the sun. 

This place is very good and it is one of very few places where I would so want to go again. I am actually looking for a reason to go very soon! Try not to make plans after this moment only because this place makes you want to stay for hours and drink up a tab. I had a last minute date and boy was I not in the right state of mind to be on a date. I recommend going during happy hour, which I think is 12-4 pm? Drinks are $5 cheaper and oysters are $18 a dozen compared to $34. If you plan on going after happy hour, make sure your company is paying ;) (kidding!).

The food was incredible, but the service was awful. We arrived at 7:25 pm for a 7:30 pm reservation, and were asked to wait five minutes while our table was being prepared. It wasn't until 8:05 pm that we were finally seated. We had ordered a round of drinks, which took several minutes to be delivered, and we were missing a drink. Moreover, when the drink was finally delivered to the table, it was spilled all over one of the patrons. The restaurant didn't even bring another drink to replace the spilled drink. As a big group, we split the bill on two cards, both of which were charged twice when they should have been charged once. As much as I love thefood ambience, the service was a disaster and I don't believe I'll be dining here again.

My friend and I came here to try this Thai place. It was a great idea because the food was not only delicious but fantastic! We had Pria as our waitress. Good job!  We had oysters to start. It was not bad, but oysters were too small, although the condiment was delicious. Then I ordered Prawn Karee that was so yummy! My friend ordered Vegan Green Curry, and that was great too. The place looks nice from the outside and better from the inside. It looks upscale and hip at the same time. Whatever the case is, the food is outstanding! I must say that the best karee comes from here. I'll order this again.

I went to fish cheeks for lunch with my family this past Sunday. The food was alright but the service we received was amazing!!! The hostess was an absolute joy and put up with a myriad of annoying questions from my parents! So sweet and kind, hope she's having a lovely day.

Liked this spot but wasn't as blown away as I thought I might be. Tried the Tongue in Cheek cocktail which was stellar - very fruity flavor and the foam is delicious, and then did the Pork Cheeks as a starter - a absolutely incredible like everyone says with the meat all fatty and crispy, and then I had the prawn wooden - I liked it but the prawns weren't cleaned that well and all the glass noodles got stuck together in a clump. We also tried the khua kling beef dish which was very spicy and not super flavorful outside of the extreme spice

Food was good
Waiter service was good 
But host need more training.
Was very rude and didn't have any common sense.
2 dishes just comes out, host come to my table says: 
I'm give you a head up, that you have to leave in 5 mins before the next rsvp arrive? 
First off, she should have looked at the table and see if we were done eating. Second she need to be more friendly and less rude. What an idiot the host was. If they were only gonna rush us and only give us 5 mins to eat 2 dish that just got served  to table they should have told us before we even ordered. 
First time here and prob wouldn't come back unless I'd really had to. There are so many other good thai places to eat in the city why would anyone come back to a rude ass host service. ( * note I still left more then 20% tips )

The food at Fish Cheeks was phenomenal. But reader, be warned: the Kua Kling packs heat like an oven door.

We ordered the Zaab wings, the Pakboong Fai Dang, the Coconut Crab Curry, and the Khua Kling.

Someone else described the Zaab wings as 'Thai dorito-style.' They are coated with a savory and citrusy dry rub. Now, dry-rub wings can be dangerous. If the chicken is overcooked, the dish becomes unbearably dry; you really want some kind of a sticky wet sauce to compensate (like blue cheese or ranch). And the Zaab wings arrive unaccompanied. That's bold. But they absolutely pulled off the solo mission. They were exquisitely juicy and tender.

The Pakboong Fai Dang was stellar. Truly a must order. It's garlicky, aromatic, and packed with classic Thai flavors.

The Coconut Crab Curry was creamy, rich, and not overly fishy, but still tasted crabby. I'd definitely order it again.

Last, the Kua Kling. Spiceheads, rejoice; all others, be wary. The Kua Kling will tingle the roof of your mouth and dampen your hairline.

My wife and I had to order an emergency glass of thai iced tea (also delicious) to soothe our tongues. We are no strangers to spice. We almost always order our food "thai spicy." But the Kua Kling is potent. The three pepper symbols on the menu almost don't do it justice.

Overall, the off the menu stuff was fine. The service was pretty standard. And I'll admit, the décor inside is not particularly chic or trendy. I think it's fair to call it 'no frills.'

But so long as you are simply looking for tasty Thai food, you will find it here in abundance.

WOW. This place so deserves its 5 stars. It IS expensive & portions are small, I wish I was rich just so I could eat this all the time! 

Tongue & cheek - 5/5. ordered with gin instead because I love gin. 
Pandan gin fizz - 4/5. Solid gin fizz. 
Manao mao - 2.5/5. Didn't like this blend of flavors. 

Oysters - $1.50 at HH, get them!! Comes with a spicy nam jim sauce and crispy onions

Grilled pork cheeks - 4.5/5. Tender meat, a bit overly salty. Not a 5/5, because I have couple japanese izakaya places that edge it out with their grilled yuzu pork cheeks. But still so good and definitely worth getting. It also has the most meat per $ spend on the menu I think. So add it just to bulk up some protein in your meal here!

Coconut crab curry - 5/5. Wow there's a reason this is the most popular. This IS spicy, so be warned. Comes with rice to sop up the delicious curry sauce. Small but reasonable portion of delicious crab meat. 

Prawn Karee - 5/5. Honestly, I might like this even more than the crab curry! Only thing it's missing is spice, so I just add some of the crab curry sauce and mix it in :) The curry here is just SO flavorful and an umami bomb. Shrimps are shell & head on (but the head is trimmed). Comes with 3 large shrimps.

Crab fried rice - 3/5. Good, but nothing too special. Can get at other thai places, so don't waste your time here on this. 

Steamed fish with thai herbs - 5/5. Fantastic, still lots of flavor, but a lighter dish to balance out the curries. It's bright and delicious with super soft flesh. 

HH is fantastic with excellent oysters and steal on cocktails ($11)

Service is a bit hit and miss. One lady made us wait 20 minutes for our reservation (despite having multiple tables open), and when a bunch of parties accumulated behind us, she then proceeded to sit a bunch of us at once. And other people actually got their orders taken and food delivered before us! (We were 100% ready to order given we had already waited 20 minutes). Food does take a while to come. Our first waiter was nice but a bit clueless. The second was great and food was ordered and delivered seamlessly. The first waiter actually had the gall to bring us out a bowl of rice (which we paid extra for) that was clearly scraped from the bottom with clumps and dried out grains (a far cry from the beautiful bowl that came just 15 minutes prior). Anyway, they're super busy likely due to the increased capacity from the outdoor area, so I mostly understand. And the food will keep me coming! Just make a reservation on Resy if you can, and be patient.

If you're looking for original Thai food, this place is not! After searching on the website and reading all reviews so we decided to go here. Since we saw the menu there were a little dishes and mostly expensive. The server was not Thai, when we asked for the details she couldn't explain what it was! We ended up order papaya salad, she said no papaya but used corn instead! The taste was only sweet, there was only corn, tomatoes, and beans for $15! Another dish was shrimp curry, only 3 shrimps and the taste was too salt! cost $26. After disappointed for these 2 menus, we decided to go another restaurant nearby which was cheaper and tasty than here. We would not come back!

I don't usually opt for Thai, but Fish Cheeks has been on my list for quite some time! Couldn't get a reservation so I stopped by to see if there was availability for walk-in... they put me down on their list and had us seated within the hour! 

Luckily made it for the oyster happy hour which is offered all week from 12-3:15pm and 5-6pm. Oysters were super fresh and served with a Thai infused mignonette sauce. For cocktails, we ordered the tongue & cheek which was light, refreshing, foamy, and garnished with black sesame seeds! For entrees, we split the fan favorite coconut crab curry and the prawn aob woosen. The coconut crab curry was delicious but my tongue hurt from the level of spice... my tongue was actually numb and my nose running throughout the entire meal. Good, but proceed with caution if you can't handle your spice.. even the sticky rice won't neutralize the situation. The dish was also a bit shy of crab... felt like we were mostly served coconut curry without much protein. As for the prawn aob woosen.. this was the fan favorite for me!! Loved the glass noodles and the flavor contributions from the cilantro root and celery leaves. 

All the dishes were unique! Fish cheeks knows what they're doing with respect to seafood. Would recommend, especially for those that love their Thai cuisine! Suggest making a reservation and maybe coming with a larger party size to share more dishes from the extensive & fun menu.

We promptly sat down.  Our server was great.  Their Happy Hour Specials are worth checking out.  This is Thai Food with a twist.  And we loved their Spicy  Mango Cocktail ‼

Festive and loud atmosphere.  I was there with my Wife for an overdue Date Night but there were Large Groups and Families with Kids also.  I noticed Bar Seating also.

Credit Cards only.

Very good Thai restaurant. The fish is awesome. Oysters too. I ll go back next visit. 
Service is fast and good

Came here for my birthday with friends and I died and went to Thai and seafood heaven. This place is worth the hype and long wait if you don't have a reservation. But it is so good. I dream about this meal. We decided to start with the oysters and they were the best I've ever had. For mains we had to get the coconut crab curry, the fried fish, veggie green curry, crab fried rice and the corn and beans. Everything was so good and I will be back again!
This place has the best Thai food in Lower Manhattan! The crab fried rice is to die for

Fish Cheeks is my favorite Thai place in NYC. I've only been here twice, but from my first visit I've been compelled to order the wings and corn salad to start. The wings are seasoned in this sweet, salty, sour, spicy seasoning that they sell in a bottle, and are freshly fried! The corn salad is very refreshing and so different from anything you could order anywhere else!

During my last visit, I ordered the whole fried fish and a prawn dish with glass noodles - both were really good and I appreciated that the fish was deboned and a pretty substantial portion. Although the prawn dish was good, I couldn't help but feel that the serving size was a bit underwhelming for the price. 

I am always recommending Fish Cheeks to others when they want a Thai food recommendation, with the added note that they do not make pad thai. However, I don't see that as a flaw and will come back again for sure.

Perhaps the best Thai restaurant in NYC! Everything was meticulous and super flavorful. Even with the hostess being slow and unprofessional, I HAVE to give this restaurant five stars. Came here on a Sunday evening, turns out they still had happy hour (it's all week from 5pm -7pm; oysters, beers , cocktails). Got the oysters, crab curry, steamed fish, and morning glory. Everything was AH-MAZING! The extra bonus? Their mango sticky rice was REALLY good! But please skip the other desserts, they were way too sweet.

Came here for a birthday, was really easy to share plates. We tried a bit of everything. The green curry was great, but spicier than I was expecting. The corn salad and the crispy rice were really great. We also got oysters and pork cheek which were pretty standard.

Our waitress was Very friendly and helpful In recommending portion size / popular dishes for our group, and recommended nice cocktails to enjoy. The interior was a bit noisy/ small so I might try to eat outdoors next time!

Hands down the best thai food I ever had!! Chicken wings cooked to perfection which has an unique flavor of spicy, salty, sour, and crispy all in 1 bite. I loved the coconut crab curry and the steamed fish with thai herbs, must get these two items you will not regret it!!! The coconut crab curry is so flavorful and rich with the right amount of spice!

TLDR, Fish Cheeks is a must visit for anyone looking for delicious and deeply personal take on Thai cuisine. Everyone at the restaurant demonstrated a deep commitment and artistic attention to making the dining experience enjoyable for the guest. The Spicy Mango Cocktail, Grilled Pork Cheeks, and Prawn Karee are all great! A little pricey and hard to get a table, but well worth the price and wait for admission! Details below:

Fish Cheeks is a restaurant unencumbered by the preconceived notions of its cuisine. As many reviewers have already noted, if you're looking for the familiarity of standard Thai fare (Pad Thai, Drunken Noodles, Lard Na), you're likely to be disappointed. If you're instead looking for food that is unapologetically personal and clearly rooted in a rich cultural heritage, then Fish Cheeks is right up your alley.

Getting a table was the most challenging part of the experience for me; the line for a table at 6 PM on a Saturday was two hours long, and next weekend's dinner reservations (before 9 PM) were all taken. All promising signs of a great restaurant to be sure, but if you want to enjoy a meal at Fish Cheeks, then you'd best have a plan. Booking far in advance on Resy (2-3 weeks out), avoiding Friday and weekend nights, or having oodles of patience are your best chances.

But once you get your table, you're in for a great meal. The staff was super attentive and knowledgeable. Within 2 minutes of sitting down, our server (I can't remember her name but she was amazing) was at our table with a long list of specials and recommendations, with menu details and insights coming from both the wait staff and kitchen. It was clear, right then and there, that everyone in the restaurant was invested in every aspect of our experience as guests.

We ordered the Spicy Mango Cocktail, Grilled Pork Cheeks, the Prawn Karee, and a side of white rice.

The cocktail was really well-balanced. Oftentimes, spicy cocktails either pack too much or not enough punch, but this rendition got just enough heat from the Thai birds eye chili to cut the mouth-watering tropical fruitiness of the mango. All of this, paired with a smooth and unassuming tequila, made for a refreshing compliment to the meal.

The grilled pork cheeks were really stars of the show. If you've ever wished you could have the richness of pork belly with a leaner and less fatty meat, then this dish is the answer to your wish. The pork cheeks were just right in every way; thin and tender but not lacking bite, crisped and charred on the edges but still juicy, fatty and rich without being greasy or heavy. The meat on its own would have been great, but Fish Cheeks takes it a step further, adding freshness with a few sprigs of cilantro garnish (removable if that's not your thing) and some acidic heat with a Jeaw sauce that doesn't overpower the meat. It's a dish that is greater than the sum of its parts.

The prawn karee was the finisher to our meal, and it was a worthy bookend even if it didn't quite reach the lofty heights of the pork cheeks. The prawns themselves were fresh and cooked to a tender and juicy state, a perfect canvas for the effervescent sauce they swam in. The sauce was tasty yet also a bit confusing; so many tastes--curry, sweet jam, spicy chili, rich egg--competed for attention. Don't get me wrong; all of the flavors worked together, but each bite was a sensory overload that really required rice or prawn as a counter-balance.

Overall, the meal was great! Fish Cheeks is definitely a little pricey and the portions aren't huge, but you get what you pay for in terms of quality. Everyone associated with the restaurant seems to be fully invested in communicating, conflicting, and compromising with each other in order to deliver a cohesive, detail-oriented (even the rice was deliciously fragrant and airy), and personal meal to their guests. Would highly recommend you make a plan to try it out; it's well worth the wait.

I think this is as authentic as you can get for Thai cuisine. Recommended by a friend, I have had this spot bookmarked for the longest time and just happened to be in the area with my gf looking for a lunch spot.

The staff members were pretty accommodating as we got a table inside that was in the middle of the dining area and was able to switch seats with another table that just cleared against the wall. They were able to give some recommendations based off of what was popular. We started off with drinks, including a Leo Lager Beer at HH pricing ($6) and Thai Iced Coffee ($8), delicious if I may add.

For entrees, we ordered the Rainbow Trout Pad Cha ($27) and the Coconut Crab Curry ($30). The Coconut Crab Curry had two peppers next to it on the menu and they were not messing around when it comes to spicy. I love spicy, but I underestimated how spicy it could have been. The crab meats is what makes it all worth it and taking a spoonful of the curry and dumping it onto the bowl of rice. The Rainbow Trout dish is unique I don't think you can find at many Thai restaurant. Carefully filleted as much as possible, although you may encounter some bones, so you've been warned. Seasoned very well with myriad of spices and obviously it was delicious.

We ended our meal with Mango Sticky Rice ($13). I think it tastes better without the coconut cream?, but regardless, one of the greatest ways to end a meal. You get that natural sweetness from the mango combined with the sticky rice to add to the flavor (and coconut if you choose to do that).

I have only lived in NYC for a couple months. Almost all of my meals have been incredible. This one was top 3 EASY. May be numero uno. Anyway. It's not your standard pad thai joint. These are classy meals fam. We got the steamed fish and the prawn karee. IDK about yall but steamed fish does not jump off the page to me, but thank zeus for my girlfriend because it was fire flames you guys. Fire flames. Then the star of the show was the prawn karee. Holy crustaceans the sauce this was in was the most exceptional mixture of tangy, spicy, and savory. I would drink that thick slurry if not for my already tenuous status as a sane person. Would have loved for that prawn to have been peeled already as I used 5 napkins for the job, but it was a small price to pay for possibly my favorite dish in NY to date. 
Staff was also high quality.

So I really wanted to love this place. The menu looked great, photos of the decor were cute, and it just looked like an overall cool spot in the city. 

I'll start by saying the spot is cute. Indoor decor was really nice, small, intimate. But... they only have one bathroom. Might sound like I'm being nit-picky but for such a popular place on a crowded evening when drinks are flowing.... It's annoying to stand in a small restaurant waiting in line for a single bathroom.

As for food & drinks. The happy hour is a really good deal. The oysters were good and I had this Spicy Mango drink (wasn't spicy at all) that was pretty tasty. Food - I was disappointed. For the price per plate I was expecting a burst of Thai flavor and spices. I ordered the crab fried rice and it couldn't survive without the two side sauces in came with. I thought the portions would be big, but one entree and appetizer is not enough for a party of two so again - not really understanding the price point. Maybe it's because they're seafood dishes? idk. 

Overall, I'd go back for happy hour, but not the food.

One of my favorite restaurants I tried in New York. The dishes were unique, fresh, light, and delicious. Love their sauce and broths. Did not like their alcohol though and probably not worth the price.

Market oysters: oysters were good, but the highlight was the sauce
Crispy rice salad with Pork: good texture and nice flavors
Grilled Pork cheeks: one of my favorite dish here. Great sauce that accompanies it. 
Steamed fish with Thai herbs: light, fresh, and thinking about the flavors makes me salivate. Get the coconut rice to eat this with. 
Pandan Gin Fizz: good pandan flavor but I wish it was sweeter
Ice cream bolan: raw egg added an unique texture along with the ovaltine dusted on top

Ambience: beautiful decor and even the outdoor stalls they tied in with the same vibe. Sanitizers available. 

Wait: seemed busy on a week night. But I did see a group walk up and get seated outdoors without too long of a wait. Still recommend reserving

Price: expensive but worth the flavors. I don't think you can find a place with similar food for a cheaper price. Drinks aren't worth it in my opinion

COVID precaution: sanitizers available and outdoor seating as well

I think this place was popularized by Chrissy Teigen (pre-cancel). 

It is such a cute spot for a casual first date if you like Thai and spiiiiiiicy.

Ive been here several times. My favorite dishes are the coconut crab curry, whole steamed fish, and pork cheeks. I know the zabb wings are also extremely popular. 

Dishes are served family style for the most part so go with a group of friends or a big appetite. There's something for everyone, pescatarians and carnivores!

Beautiful restaurant. Highly professional and kind staff. The artisan cocktails were well done and tasty. We had the Thai sliced fish as a main course. Well it was tasty, it needed something more. The rest of the food was just fantastic. It's definitely worth a try.

Came here on a Sunday and had one of the most delicious meals I've had in the past year. Oysters were sweet savory fresh cold with a bright sour sauce and savory fried shallot that added texture and even more umami. The pork checks were juicy beautifully cooked glistening with a crusted filled with maillard goodness and a salty cilantro herbed fish sauce to accompany and mix with the glistening fat. The shrimp we ordered had an amazing sauce that tasted of crab brains in the best way. 5 stars way up enough to want to drag friends over

However when coming back for happy hour I brought new friends and I'm sorry to say the consistency was not there. Oysters were similar and good but perhaps since it wasn't the first time anymore the wow factor was not there. Pork cheeks seemed under crisped and a bit soft. Steamed fish was undercooked in the middle so we had half steamed half ceviche fish. And shrimp sauce didn't have the flavors. Kudos to the waiter who brought out beers one by one for us you were the real mvp as the food also took a while to come 

Would try again but on the weekend where I had such an incredible time

Fish Cheeks is an excellent Southeast Asian spot restaurant with great food, even better drinks, and cool happy hour! 

Food: Food is best family style. For small plates, I'd recommend the pork cheeks and the raw shrimp. For large plates, the steamed fish and the crab curry are both delicious. The crab curry was surprisingly very spicy for me, so order carefully! 

Drinks: the cocktails are all very creative and delicious. They are $11 on happy hour, which is a steal. My personal favorite is Tongue & Cheek, though it's one of the less creative ones on the menu. 

Ambience: It's clean and cute. Great place to come with friends, with a date, or with parents. 

Convenience/service: Takes reservations, though they are often hard to come by. Nice service as well. 

Value for money: My only caveat is that it's slightly expensive for what you get - $15-20 for small plates, $30-40 for large plates.
The crab fried rice and Zab chicken wings were phenomenal!! Always nice to dine on Bond st. As well. Fantastic ambiance.

reviews.review:
A great Thai spot. It's not like your typical Thai spot where you get your pad Thai,  drunken noodles, etc. Seems like this place focuses more on Thai-inspired seafood dishes which I think is unique. 

The steamed fish is really good and the soup it's marinated in is very flavorful. The oysters are yummy and come with two dipping sauces. And the green is solid as well. This place gets busy quick so either make a reservation in advance or come as soon as they open!

We've been to Fish Cheeks a few times and it was always interesting. It's not a service oriented restaurant possibly because they are pretty busy. The menu is rather limited especially if you're looking for veggie options and there's very no room for accommodations. It's definitely pricey for Thai food but some stuff is yummy including the steamed fish and corn salad.

I was thrilled to try this place out. As someone who lives in the southern part of Thailand for many years, seeing authentic list of dishes in their menu strikes me that their food would certainly be delicioso! And I was right! Most dishes that we ordered tasted delicious and authentic. We sat outdoor, which was nice. It was a cool summer day. But there's a downturn of sitting outside -- you can get a bad service. 

The reason I gave only three stars was because of their poor services. It took them forever to greet us, let alone took our order. One of the servers work as if he hates the job. I asked for " prik numpla", which is a typical thai condiment that you can get if you're at any authentic Thai restaurants. Normally you would eat it with rice and giant prawn, or anything. I know that prik numpla takes time to make so I was waiting patiently. But it took forever! 


I went inside and kindly remind the same server again. He abruptly answered me with an upsetting tone, " It's coming..." I felt as if he can add " you annoying biotch" to the sentence he would. And that's where my great feeling for this place went downhill. He could have responded nicely. After we finished our meal, we're sitting there, glance blankly at our server and other servers, none of them seem to care. Only one of the lady who seems to be the manager paid attention to us. 

I want to like the place, but their service makes me not wanting to return.

I think this restaurant is heavily overhyped, especially after hearing so many great things about it. We came for dinner on a Friday evening, and despite having a reservation, we still had to wait 20 minutes with no apology. The service was super frazzled, and there were three items on our bill that we didn't order. The drinks that we ordered upon sitting down didn't arrive until halfway through our meal. The food wasn't that good, and for what it was, it was massively overhyped. We got the prawn aub woosen and the crab curry. If I wanted a clay pot vermicelli type dish, which is what the prawn aub woosen was, I'd have gone to Chinatown, where almost every restaurant would've executed it better and more cheaply. The prawns were soft and not bouncy at all, so we could tell they weren't fresh. There were also only three prawns. As for the crab curry, it was not terrible, but beware that it is very VERY spicy. Paisley in Tribeca does a much better crab curry. It's also noisy as all hell inside, and the line for the restroom consistently had 6 people in it throughout the course of the night. We spent over $100 for two entrees and two cocktails.
Fish cheeks is definitely worth all the hype. Their tom yong soup and noodles are so good. Worth multiple visits.

One of the top restaurants in NYC hands down. Must order items are the oysters, morning glory veggies, crab fried rice, and the steamed fish. Pork jowl is amazing too. The prices are so reasonable for the quality of food and service.

This was an extremity overhyped restaurant, come if you're ready to spend over $60 per guest for lunch. Quality is 4/5, portion is 2/5. We were a table of 4. We ordered the HH oysters (4/5), steam fish (4/5), aob woosen (2/5), pork cheek (3/5), and crab fried rice (3/5); that's five dishes and we left the place feeling half full. Our waitress also took our water away for almost an hour. We came here per Yelp and it was a huge letdown after going to Thai Villa the day before. Lastly, they charged us for a Thai tea ($10 after tax) that we never ordered.

Come here for happy hour and get the oysters, so fresh and a unique sauce to go on top that you cannot get anywhere else but here! The drinks are fabulous and unique. The mains, clams are back on the menu - hooray! Add a side of rice bc the clam sauce is amazing is a dish all by itself. Then we had the steamed fish, crab fried rice and crab curry...it was a lot but soooo delicious we ate it all! Love this spot!

I came here for the 3rd time with friends and this time, I had the coconut curry, zaab wings, and pork cheeks. They were, of course, amazing and mouth watering as usual!

Recently I have been on an oyster craving but I have never tried Thai raw oysters so I was nervous that I wouldn't like it... BUT I LOVE IT MORE THAN THE AMERICAN ONE! They were clean of debris inside and outside, fresh, had no fishy smell, and were very refreshing. My friend and I started with a half dozen but then later ordered a full dozen, knowing fully well that we need to come back for more! On top of that, it was happy hour and 1/2 dozen was $9 and full dozen was $18!! Compared to my experience at Williamsburg and their $1 oysters the day prior, Fish Cheeks was godsend. I will neverrrrrrrrr go to Williamsburg for their $1 oysters no matter how desperate I am. I'll only going to be Fish Cheeks now

*takeout only*

Incredible flavors--I've had a lot of green curries and this is absolutely the best I've ever had, hands down. And it was vegan 

We also got the morning glory, the fish wrapped in banana leaf, zabb wings.

Visited on a weekday for lunch with high expectations after reading through the reviews but sad to say my girlfriends and I left hungry and disappointed. We reserved for indoor dining but asked to be seated outside instead because there was no AC inside (it was around 90 something degrees and was cooler to sit outside). It took us about 20 minutes just to be greeted by our server. Oysters and the salad came out first and we had to remind them that we had ordered drinks for them to come out. The oysters weren't anything to write home about and the crispy rice salad with sour pork was SO SALTY! I get that the raw pieces of cabbage are supposed to mellow out the flavor but my god, the shock when I first put it in my mouth. Also, the crab curry didn't have much crab meat for the price they charge and was a bit too ginger-y for me (personal taste) instead of it being more coconut-y. The best dish was the fried fish, hands down; perfectly crisp and flavorful. We each had our own bowls of jasmine rice, which was also perfectly done. Unfortunately I probably won't be returning due to the underwhelming service and the food.

Market Oysters - 5/5
Coconut Crab Curry - 5/5
Crab Fried Rice - 5/5

Came in for happy hour. Oysters are $1.50 each. Sold by the half or full dozen. They are amazing. The fried shallots and nam jim seafood sauce really up the flavor. The coconut crab curry is buttery deliciousness. It's got a fair amount of heat, so be warned. The crab fried rice is what dreams are made of. Everything about it is perfect.

Delightfully tasteful Thai joint. I don't think I need to go into too much details but all the dishes were solid. Most of them had sauces unique to each plate that had my tastebuds singing. That crab fried rice was absolutely perfect. Had a blast with the curry too. 

The only dish that I felt were a little more flat were the fried fish and the sautéed cabbage. The pakboong fai dung (morning glory) we had could have been more fresh too.

I'd come here again 110%.

So, Fish Cheeks has been on my list for quite some time. I finally got to go last month with a friend who has been before. She spoke highly of it, and I was super excited to try it! The environment alone, gives loving vibes. All of the staff, from the front of house servers, to back of house cooks/chefs, all gelled so well, and it made for a smooth-running service. I enjoyed the decor a lot, and the feel it offers. We made a reservation and were seated right away. 

We arrived as they opened (the time of the resy), so had plenty of time for happy hour! We both were eyeing the same cocktails, so each started off with the, "Thank you Kha". First off, this drink was stunning! It was soooo pretty! The chili oil drops added color to it, aside from it's already whimsical presentation. It tasted super smooth and rich from the coconut. I thoroughly enjoyed it! The second cocktail I got, was the Mano mao. It was a nice, refreshing spiced rum drink, with limes, and palm sugar. It was done very well, and strong! 

Ok, for the food, we started off with the Zabb wings, which were absolutely DISRESPECTFUL! This chili lime flavor on these crisply fried wings will have you ADDICTED, hear?! Like, for real. Trust me. These wings were some of the best I've had in the city, and I could eat them by the dozen, don't test me! Tuh! Next, we ordered a dozen of their oysters, which were beyond fresh! They must have JUST scooped them up out of the water because they were FRESH! No fish smell at all, with the right amount of meaty texture. We also ordered the crab fried rice....omg. I took a forkful of this, and it took me on a flavor journey. Just the amount of flavor they were able to develop in this rice still blows my mind. It was loaded with fresh, lumpy crab meat. We shared this dish but honestly.....I could've eaten it all to myself, and wanted to! Lol. We also shared the coconut crab curry which was just divine. It was so creamy and loaded with flavor and crab! We each poured some over  rice and went to WERK! I will say, if you can't handle the heat, then stay out the curry! Lol. No, seriously, she spicy! I mean, I could handle her, but I almost didn't make it lol. It was so delicious, that I wouldn't have ever stopped eating until it was fully finished. 

Fish Cheeks is a must try. This is AUTHENTIC, genuine, loving food with the real flavors of Thailand. I will be a regular here for sure. I've already gone a second time lol!
Delicious food & great service! All the foods are on the spicier side (very few not spicy dishes). Recommend reserving on Resy to avoid a wait. Will go back!
Been here several times. Always been an amazing experience. The oysters and crab curry are must gets. And the ovaltine ice cream!

The Thai foood from fish cheeks is one of the best in New York City (I have tried at least most major thai places in midtown/downtown )they do have one of the best. It is a pricey restaurant but they do service high quality food and good cocktails.

Dinner was overall really good! The flavors definitely hit the sweet, sour, spicy, and bitter spectrum. 

Grilled Pork Cheeks: MUST MUST HAVE! The pork is cooked to perfection and the meat glistens! The fat to meat ratio is also really well balanced. Crunch on the inside, juicy on the outside. The sauce drizzled on top really sealed the deal. 

Fried Fish: The fish is fried to perfection, not too fried/greasy, but not soggy either. The herb salad was def a good balance. Def. a must try! 

Crab Fried Rice: The fried rice was good. I'd probably not go for this dish again because it was just a regular fried rice, with crab meat. I'd def. try out the curry next time. 

A place to def. try out! The vibes were great as well. Def. hit them up for happy hour!

the best Thai seafood restaurant in NYC. We loved crab fried rice, crab curry and steamed fish. The food was just liked we had in Thailand. The flavor and the spiciness were perfect . Service was excellent. Will go back there again when we come back to NYC.

This is hands down my favorite restaurant in the city. I come here all the time and we probably do order the same things but I could never get enough. From the sauce served with the oyster and raw shrimp, to the amazing tomyum seasoning on their wings, they're all so addicting. Love that the soup comes in the little hotpot thing and I think we've tried almost the whole menu at this point. The food flavor just feels so authentic and I will always recommend people here.

This may be one of the best meals I have ever eaten!
Every single thing we ordered was so intentionally and expertly prepared.

Typically, it can be hard to secure a table for dinner at FC, but we stopped by for lunch on a random Thursday and got a table right away.

Turns out, every week day lunch time is HAPPY HOUR, where specialty cocktails are $11 and oysters are $1.50 a piece.

We picked out a cocktail, ordered 6 oysters, the pork cheek, a steamed fish, 6 more oysters, and finally, a coconut ice cream for dessert

First, the oysters were INCREDIBLE.  I was going to take a pass, but the garlic/cilantro and fried onion topping was a game changer.  I live in Maine and these were the BEST oysters I have ever had!

The pork cheek was in-your-dreams tender and came with an excellent tamarind sauce

The steamed fish was beyond!  It came in a dish with a heating element below which kept the sauce bubbling.  It was cooked in the most delicious lemongrass, garlic and chili sauce, it was SO SO good.  Pro tip: definitely ask for rice on the side, you will not necessarily want, but NEED this!

I was really on the fence about dessert, but we decided to share.  The made in house coconut ice cream drizzled with a sweet egg yolk sauce was everything you might imagine it would be.

THANK YOU Fish Cheeks!
We're back at the apartment and STILL talking about our lunch today!

There is no doubt the food was good, but I was kind of disappointed in seeing how they prepared to set up the tables.  There was a man wrapping the forks and spoons in napkins.  The man touched the head of the fork and the head of the spoon with his hands.  I waited tables for several years and that is something you don't do.  You should NOT be touching the part of the utensils that the customer puts in their mouths.  Disgusting.

Came here for lunch happy hour oysters.

I'll start with the good, the pork cheeks and chicken wing appetizers were great. The wings had a nice spice to them. 

The tongue and cheek cocktail tasted ok but it's weird to have sesames floating in it (looks over functionality). The pandan fizz was better.

The oysters weren't cold and the sauce it came with was oily which isn't really something you want with oysters. Also the fried garlic chips should never be served with oysters if you ask me. They have some work to do with those.
honestly just okay! got really expensive water here $10 on accident because i thought it was free! but we got the curry and it was just okay
Incredible food and drinks, but a bit on the pricier side. Be prepared to sweat as their dishes don't shy on the heat. Cocktails were great

Fish cheeks is my favorite restaurant in all of NYC. good luck getting a reservation here though. I always book a month ahead in advance. There is absolutely nothing there that is mediocre. Everything is EXCELLENT. The HH deal is fantastic (all cocktails discounted AND $1 oysters???), the wings are incredibly tender juicy but packed with zingy flavor, all of the whole fish options are incredibly home-y and comforting. I wish they would expand and have more seating (and add another restroom since a line tends to queue up), but I'm so so so glad they made it through COVID closures.

I am so mad at myself for discovering this gem after moving out of NY. This easily would be one of my favorite restaurants in NY. It's a tiny place, but they have outdoor seating that could fit our party of 10. 

Let's talk about the food.
