Grilled Pork Cheeks: MUST HAVE! These cheeks are the best cheeks I've ever had! It's a good amount to share with two or three people, but I could probably eat two just by myself. 

Zabb Wings: MUST HAVE! The seasoning is crack! Which they sell btw. It's cooked to perfection. Crunchy on the inside, juicy on the outside. Yum!!! Get it. 

Crab Fried Rice: it was good. I'd probably get it again cause I'm a sucker for crab fried rice, but it's not a must-have. Friendly reminder, GET THE CHEEKS.

Steamed Branzino: it was interesting. Lol the flavor was on the sour side, but it was good. I liked it, but I would try the grilled one next time. 

Coconut Crab Curry: IT'S SPICY! I'd say at a level 4 out of 5. I couldn't even eat more than two spoons of it. I wouldn't get it again. 

I'm so sad I wouldn't be able to eat here again until I go back to NY the next time. So go eat there for me!!! 

YOU MUST GO HERE!
Great Thai place I frequent with my husband. I love the crab glass noodles and lime chili wings. He is a big fan of the prawns in egg sauce - goes great with rice. Friendly service.

I rarely visit the same restaurant in twice in 3 months, but this one is a place really satisfying all your needs in the summer. Even though you are not a spicy lover, you still have enough favors and options to enjoy the food. Specially the fusion style cocktails really open your mind to try something new. 

The crab curry is the only one I feel too spicy, others are friendly for anyone.

LOVED Fish Cheeks! Came for the first time on a Friday at 5, right when they opened, since we didn't make a reservation in time. We were able to get a table outside. Their outdoor dining setup is super cute, and very spacious. I like how the street was closed down. We ordered the crab fried rice, that day's ceviche special, pakboong fai dang, rainbow trout pad cha, and yum hed yaang. It was all AMAZING, there are no words for how amazing this dinner was. I loved the sauces that came with the fried rice, and the ceviche was so fresh. It was a bit expensive, but I say it was completely worth it. I've never had thai food this good before. I would 100% recommend you come to eat at Fish Cheeks.

So delicious here!! Everything we ordered was bursting with flavors. Excellent service. 
There was a cabbage dish, it was so simple yet so delicious, I absolutely loved it. The fried chicken skin was crunchy with a little kick to it. 
The side sauces for the apps and some dishes are so yummy. It sauce compliment each dish so well. 
We ordered fried fish, steamed fish, shrimp, crab fried rice, crab woon sen, oysters, chicken wings, curry (curry was VERY Spicy!!) thai tea, thai coffee, lemonade, sweet mango rice. 
This place is a must visit if you're in town.

After trying 5 times to get a reservation I finally managed to snag one and it was def worth the wait. The pork cheeks are to die for and was my favorite dish. I probably could've ordered another plate of it because it was so good. We also ordered the steamed fish and coconut crab curry and they were both really good. The steamed fish was zesty and flavorful and the coconut crab curry had the perfect amount of spice. I'm absolutely coming back to try the rest of the menu. Make sure you make a reservation though because even for a weekday lunch it seemed pretty packed!

One of THE BEST Thai food restaurants in NYC. The food is so fresh & seafood focused, but you must order the Zabb wings too. Everything is incredible! 

We ordered:
Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs 
Zabb Wings
Happy Hour Oysters ($18/dozen)

Outdoor seating is super cute too. Bonus that I've spot a celeb there or walking by every time I've gone haha (last time it was Liev Schreiber)!

Fish Cheeks is a Thai fusion restaurant and definitely one of the most flavorful ones that I've tried. 

Although their meals are almost double what normal restaurants charge, it's well worth it for the taste. They even have a happy hour to get cheaper oysters and cocktails which is always a plus!

Highly recommend if you are into Thai food. Be warned, the curry is spicy!

This was a great experience! Oysters were fresh and a wonderful deal during happy hour. The raw shrimp was slightly fishy tasting, which gives me qualms when eating raw seafood about its freshness, but they seemed to have cleaned it well. The pork cheeks were crispy and its sauce complemented it well. Lastly, one of their most popular items, the steamed fish, was light, meaty, and flavorful. We loved the sauce, and certainly tried not to waste any of it by spooning it onto our fish and eating it with our rice (I'd say you'll probably want to get this if you get the fish). Prices are a little steep, but it's great to come at least once as Fish Cheeks provides a unique experience compared to other Thai restaurants that focus on the classic pad thai/see ew/etc dishes. Staff was very sociable and considerate, and when we arrived right at opening there was already a long line. I'd suggest making a reservation beforehand, although my party was seated rather quickly. I enjoyed Fish Cheeks and look forward to my next visit!

Came here for dinner on a Saturday. Fortunately at 5 pm they take walk ins. While waiting on line, I even had a celebrity sighting...Liev Schreiber! 

Now onto the food...my party of 3 shared 2 dozen oysters, the pork cheeks, the hamachi ceviche, the Thai steamed fish, and a side of morning glory. I also ordered the Pandan Gin Fizz. All in all the food was very good. The oysters were a bit on the smaller size (maybe not oyster season?) and the steamed fish was very flavorful and de-boned! 

The service was exceptional and every now and then you see the fire from the flambé in the kitchen which was fun! 

Only downside is there is only one bathroom :( which can take quite a while considering both indoor and outdoor dining at capacity, but c'est la vie. Recommend for everyone to try. Would like to try more of the crabby stuff next time!

Saw this spot on Yelp, the named spoke to me.. pulled up, had a 15 min wait. Came back, the waitress sat us down. We sat in one of those lil cubbies in he cut. Surprisingly wasn't that bad, preferred it to sitting in the middle of the street. Anyway. Ordered apps, entrees and a dessert. The dessert was the only that wasn't A1. The fried fish was delicious, the crab curry was pretty as well. The pork cheek appetizer was prolly the best thing I got tho. The drinks weren't bad either.

everything is amazing !! pls try the thai iced coffee!! the shareable entrees really are shareable!! the zabs wings are so flavorful & good if you don't like getting messy with wings! they were able to sit us down ten minutes earlier than our reservation!!

This was the worst dining experience I've ever had. We called before we arrived since we were getting there late. The woman on the phone said as long as we sat down by 11 we'd be good to go. We sat down at 10:55 and I placed my order, which they put in, but my friend had to use the restroom so she put her order in at 11:02. They rejected the order and legitimately scolded us for ordering 2 minutes past 11. So they gave me my order, but told my friend tough luck. It was so unprofessional and rude. I've never been treated so poorly by restaurant staff. Definitely do not recommend!

Had the most wonderful dining experience at Fish Cheeks. The food was delicious, drinks were fun and service was great. 
Our group of 6 came hungry and we pretty much ordered everything on the menu. No regrets! 
All the dishes were super flavorful with just the right amount of spice.
Highly recommend the oysters, shrimp in crab sauce, crab curry and crab rice. We also had a wonderful morning glory side dish (sorry forgot to take a pic!) 
Fave cocktails was the Thank you Kha.
Can't wait to come back and more of the deliciousness!

The cocktails have the spotlight here; let. me. tell. you!!!
Super unique - I had the cheek & tongue and it was so sweet and fruity ahh! Loved it. Was very curious about the pandan one as well - wish I could have tried both! Go during happy hour when the price drops from I think it was $17 to $11 a cocktail! 

Food here I already knew was going to be amazing. I can't handle spice personally but my fiancé ordered the crab curry and although it burned my stomach after just 2 bites.... it was worth it.

LOVED the grilled branzino; the sauce was perfect, it was cooked perfectly; it was just perfect.

Would highly recommend and definitely would go back.
Delicious Thai seafood dishes with refreshing flavors. A bit on the pricier side compared to other Thai restaurants but each of the dishes is very thoughtful.

Came here for a dinner date on a Sunday around 7:30 and we had to wait an hour! The weather was nice so we did end up walking around which got us hungry for our meal! 

We ordered two appetizers- the zabb wings and the pork cheeks. The wings were delicious but so spicy that I couldnt eat more than 1. The pork cheeks on the other hand was delicious- it was tender, and the the sauce that came with it was also very delicious- we finished this dish pretty quickly. 

For the mains, we ordered the Crab Fried Rice, Tiger Prawn Karee and Crab Aob Woosen. 

First, we had the tiger prawn karee- The curry, egg sauce was so freaking tasty! This dish comes with just 3 prawns so if you are here with a big group, be prepared to order multiple of this dish! 

Then we had the Crab Aob Woosen which was glass noodles with crab meat cooked in a sweet sauce but with a heavy cilantro taste. Though I dont usually like cilantro or the taste of cilantro, I still thought this tasted pretty good- I love glass noodles in general! This dish is good to share with 2-3 people max, I think. 

Last, we had the crab fried rice- we had this with the curry egg sauce from the prawns and OMG. If I wasn't as full as I was, I would eat all the rice but I was pretty full. The rice itself was pretty tasty but the sauce with the rice- no words. 

We also got two drinks- a pandan drink and a butterfly pea limeade (i think). Both were pretty interesting but I think water would've sufficed for the meal. 

Overall, the dishes were all pretty good and we enjoyed our time there. Definitely recommend!

I generally don't write restaurant reviews but really feel compelled to write this one I as I fell sick after eating at this place. On my first visit this Saturday afternoon, we had ordered crab curry, mussels and some fish and something wasn't quite right with one of those items. 

Second reason for poor rating is their dog policy. The restaurant allows dogs and we had one on the table next to us. The dog was smelly and had his hair flying all over on our table. To me the entire experience was off-putting because of the dog's smell and hair. I have never seen a dog being allowed to a NYC restaurant ever. 

I don't know what caused me to fall sick so badly but I have to blame it either the food or on the dog. I am still not fully recovered but want others to read this review so that they can benefit from it.
This place is so good!  Just the portion is a bit small but I will come back.

Best Thai food in nyc. Hands down. Flavorful, insanely creative, and all around scrumptious. Get their crab curry, prawns, mussels and steamed fish - you will not be disappointed. Top it off with their refreshing coconut ice cream for dessert and you can go home ultra satisfied.

What an incredible lunch with my wife yesterday this restaurant is amazing, I have been in the restaurant industry for 25 years,the service was wonderful very friendly and accommodating and they were very busy, the food was spectacular!!!! Their wine list is awesome,This is what we had!!


Zabb Wings
Fried chicken wings with chili, lime, mint

Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce
Lightly cured raw shrimp with lime juice, fish sauce, slice garlic, Bird's eye chili, mint, bitter melon

Crab fried rice
Crab, rice, egg, scallion, cilantro, cucumber served with Nam Jim Seafood & Prik Nam Plaa

Tiger Prawn Karee
Stir fried with curry powder, scramble egg, scallion, onion, micro celery, roasted chili jam

Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs
Whole Branzino, chili, lime, mint, culantro in cilantro lime broth

Very pretty and colorful outdoor and indoor setup. Went here for lunch on a weekday and it was poppin' at around 2 pm. The smell of delicious Thai cooking enticed us even more. Our waitress (a young woman with short, wavy black hair) was excellent and very knowledgeable about the menu. For appetizers, we ordered the Zabb wings to share. The crab fried rice, coconut crab curry, and pad cha stole the show. The sticky mango rice was unique- it had a jasmine tea taste to it. Ordered a bunch of drinks for the table. Loved the tongue & cheek cocktail so much that I downed 2 rounds of it (happy hour, baby!). The burst of flavors in every dish at Fish Cheeks make it stand out above the rest. Check this place out- you won't regret it.

Wow. This place is absolutely amazing! All the food that we ordered was so good, and definitely something I would come back to and already craving again. 

For appetizers we ordered the chicken wings, corn salad, and oysters. The oysters were fresh, and had an amazing sauce on the side that paired excellently with the oysters. The corn salad was light and had a nice light dressing like a vinaigrette that was super tasty and refreshing, and the chicken wings were cooked well, moist, with a bit of a kick and had some tang to it as well which was a nice touch. 

For the main entree's, we had the coconut crab curry, crab noodles, and a fish dish I can't remember the name of, but were all amazing! The coconut crab curry was nice and creamy but also had a nice level of spice to it. The crab noodles were amazing, and the fish was a pleasant surprise as it was cooked in banana leaf and cooked in a sauce that was so amazing. 

For dessert we had the mango sticky rice along with coconut ice cream
The steamed fish was extremely good, would recommend if you like a nice tender fish w rare bones (if any) and phenomenal flavors.
Amazing restaurant and service. Highly recommend. Big on the spice, good options, cute outdoor setup. Definitely worth adding to your list

Been here so many times and I love every dish!!!!! Highly recommend steamed whole fish & The shrimp in 3 crab sauce! Love love love! Crab coconut curry, grilled pork cheeks, Zane wings are also nice... it's now one of my favorite restaurants in NYC.

Wow, this was an amazing meal. We came here around 5:30PM on a Sunday - it was rainy and we got a table indoors right away.

We got the pork cheeks, steamed fish, and the tiger prawn karee. Other reviews have complained about portion size, but these 3 dishes satisfied the two of us. All 3 were excellent, and I would get the first two again.

Pork cheeks are more tender than pork belly, and with the sauce, provides a succulent taste. The steamed fish has a very flavorful, limey broth, and comes with a warmer to keep the dish hot! I'm a big sucker for my dishes being kept hot. The tiger prawn karee comes with 4 prawns and has more of a nuttier flavor with eggs in it.

We didn't get rice with these dishes, but certainly would be nice to have it with these dishes if you need

Make reservations ahead of time on Resy! Fish Cheeks curates an impressive menu that still imparts the comfort of Thai home-cooked dishes. 


4/5 Rainbow trout: love the heat and fragrance from a combo of chilis, lemongrass, basil, and green peppercorns. 

Unexpectedly, their jasmine rice was pretty damn delicious: fluffy, fragant, and enhances the dishes so well! Highly recommended as a side!

This is the spot to hit up for Thai food in the city. 

They have the best drinks for the girls night out and their food is delicious. The portions are on the smaller side, but it's great it allows you to try more of their delicious food. 

We ordered the fried fish- so great and crispy, perfectly done and white meat was tender so succulent  doesn't have the strong fishy taste which I love. 

Ordered the Zabb wings- perfect amount of spice and deliciousness 

Crab meet noodles - these were on the dried saucy side, and could of been a lot better if it was less dried. Nevertheless we gobbled it up.

What a gem! Had such an amazing meal here tonight that I'm writing a review right after getting home.

The raw oysters came with a sauce that was delish, although it was really good on its own. LOVED the pork cheeks. Don't think I've ever had it before but it was so tender that I was able to cut it with a spoon. For our entrees, had the crab curry which was really flavorful but a little too spicy for my taste. Lastly, the star of the show was the steamed fish! Still thinking about it now... the meat tastes so fresh and melts in your mouth. Better than many I've had in Thailand... 

Some tips: getting a reservation could be tough, especially same day. I recommend coming a few hours early to put down your name and walk around the neighborhood. They also have oyster / adult beverage happy hour from 12-3:30 and 5-6pm daily!

Cute on the inside for dining. Been wanting to come here for a while but it's usually booked.

Wings were amazing. So flavorful and 6 wings are actually full wings so it's more like 12 to a serving.

The steamed fish presentation was nice. It comes on an aluminum plate w fire under. It was a bit too salty and the flavors are a big combined.

The crab rice was good but it was lacking a bit of flavor as well. It was more on the bland side and the rice was also a bit too salty.

Overall I liked the wings the best. The meals are shared portions so my friend and I bought thought the same. Not sure if I would order the fish dish and the rice again unless they adjust the salt.

No beer!  They serve only Thai beer, which is nice in theory, but say they can't get it these days.  Really?  Some of us like beer, Thai or otherwise.  How about you go to a local deli and pick up a six pack of Bud or even some nice local brews?  I asked whether I could do that myself and got no real answer.  

The food was decent.
Good and interesting food. Not giving five star because I always just feel it could have been better.

Redemption update. I am now a fan of this place after I had a chance to try more of their menu and not just the super lemongrassy fish. Very flavorful and punchy. Honestly their apps may be better than the entrees - def get the zabb wings and grilled pork cheeks. Portion size of the appetizers are actually on the larger side so better if more ppl. Entree wise, they were all decent. I personally liked the coconut crab curry and crab fried rice the best. Friends really liked the crab glass noodles, which I enjoyed as well but did not think was particularly special. The Ping Gnob Pla tasted a little strange - I think the fish was just too earthy. Oh and avoid the steamed fish with Thai herbs if you do not like lemongrass and cilantro. That fish is a big r i p in my book.

I am absolutely obsessed with Fish Cheeks. I usually find any reason to make a reservation here: my birthday, a friend's birthday, girl's night, ANYTHING. 

What I order:

oysters - their take on oysters is so addicting. There is this spicy fish sauce that they give & fried shallots and I'm telling you once you have one, you'll be back for more. 

Coconut crab curry + crab fried rice - the reason I listed these together is because the crab curry actually comes with plain white rice but I like to order the crab fried rice and have it with the crab curry instead of regular Jasmine rice (you'll thank me later). 

steamed fish - this fish is so so good. The fish is always cooked to perfection & the meat is always so soft and full of flavor. 

Zaab wings - okay these wings are not for the faint of heart. From the first bite, it's a flavor explosion & carries a kick. 

Pork cheeks - I've never had pork cheek until I tried it here a few weeks ago. The meat is so tender & the serving is huge!! Would definitely order this appetizer again. 

Crab aob woonsen - This noodle dish is good but I dont think I would order it again. There was no "wow" factor for me & the portion was actually pretty small. 

Corn salad - I love this salad, it's so refreshing and I've actually never had a salad like this anywhere else. 

Cocktails - I always get the spicy mango and I LOVE it. Please try this if you enjoy spicy margaritas.

This is one of those restaurants I can eat at over and over again. 

The crab curry is creamy and delicious. 

Their raw shrimp with thai chilly sauce is to die for. 

I always get a steamed fish. It's very big so be ready for eating. 

Food is great ambiance is clean and lux. Service is fast and friendly. I can not get enough. Come here !

In the mood for oysters we came across Fish Cheeks and their $1.50 happy hour oysters. We arrived shortly after opening and had to deal with a hostess struggling to find a table (in an empty restaurant).

They finally managed to find us a little table in the corner. We didn't pay too much mind to this thinking that maybe they were booked out and the other parties had yet to show up. Fast forward 60 minutes the restaurant was still half empty at the very least. 

We started off with a dozen oysters (after all that's what we were here for). Oyster at Fish Cheeks are served without typical accompaniments instead served with fried garlic crisps and a spicy green sauce. Unfortunately, the sauce was just overwhelming and the wait staff were far from accommodating. They were hesitant to bring out even something as simple as lemon slices, instead arguing that their sauce had hints of lime.  Would have appreciated if the menu advertised their unique take on something so traditional. 

After the oysters we ordered the dry rubbed wings, Maitake mushrooms and crab fried rice. Wings were salty and didn't really make an impression beyond that. Mushrooms were supposed to be grilled but were served cold on a plate of greens and an overwhelming amount of lime juice. The crab fired rice was okay but at that point we were looking forward to leaving more than trying anything more.  

Over all, the restaurant was a pass. Will not come back and don't recommend.

Came here with no reservations. It was a 40min wait. The host offered us an option of sitting inside at a smaller table instead of waiting. We gladly accepted due to the weather. ASK WHAT THE SPECIALTY DISH AND COCKTAIL IS. Not sure how often they change it but it was a great recommendation. Wish I could remember what the starter was called but it had very delicious oyster mushrooms. The dishes are made family style so sharing is caring. Had the Tom Yum and Crab Fried Rice. Great pairing. Possibly the best Thai food Ive had. For drinks, try the Pandan Gin Fizz, its cute lol.

Feel conflicted because to be honest the flavor of the fish was very good, but the price is quite high for the amount of food and I don't think the flavors are THAT good to justify the price. The steamed fish really is as good as it looks, with some spiciness from the peppers that isn't overwhelming and citrus from the lime. There are lots of strong flavors that go well together and the meat is very soft. They say they try their best to get rid of the bones, which I genuinely believe because it's hard, but there was quite a number of bones and scales, more than I expected and made it a little difficult to eat. The curry was actually a little underwhelming; it was smaller than we expected and wasn't memorable to me. It comes with one bowl of white rice.  For 2 people they recommend 2 appetizers and 2 entrees - we only got 2 entrees, I do wish we got another appetizer but none of them were really standing out to us.

Great Thai spot! Came on a Thursday during happy hour with a reservation for 5pm. When we arrived there were several tables open, but by the time all the tables were taken. Started off with half a dozen oysters which I thought were great. I normally don't really like oysters, but they were served with some fried shallots and some sorta cilantro sauce which I thought was delicious.

My friend and I shared the Crab Aob Woonsen, which was pretty good. My favorite was the Coconut Crab Curry though. The curry is pretty spicy but the flavor is incredible. I ended up slathering the curry over the noodles from the aob woonsen cause it was so good.

I ended up ordering two drinks throughout our dinner: the Tongue & Cheek and the Pandan Gin Fizz. Both were great but I think I liked the latter a bit more. The drinks are pretty strong too, I had a nice buzz afterwards.

I think the only complaint that I have is that the dishes are a bit on the smaller size. Even with all the food we ordered I wasn't all that full afterwards. Regardless, the food here was incredible and the overall experience was great. Would definitely recommend!

I loved Fish Cheeks! Came on a Friday night and still had to wait about an hour so I recommend making reservations if possible. We shared two appetizers and two entrees between three people and this was more than enough! Our waitress said the mussels were her favorite dish so we decided to get that; however, it was just alright. The pineapples were a good add though. The pork cheeks were my favorite dish of the night. So crunchy yet tender. The steamed fish with thai herbs and crab coconut curry were also delicious! Service was attentive as well. Only taking a star off because it's pretty pricy for Thai food but definitely worth the try!
Above par on food quality.  The crab dish is amazing with a generous helping of crab in there.  I tend to go here every other month.
Always have a good experience dining with Fish Cheeks. Everything is always well seasoned and cooked. Fish Cheeks never disappoints, even when we order take out.

Amazing spot for Thai seafood! Every dish was a perfect blend of spices, flavors, and textures.

We shared 7 appetizers + dishes among the five of us:

Pork cheeks- extremely succulent and juicy with a perfectly seasoned sear.

Zabb wings- nice and thin, crisp crust. Tangy and spicy dry seasoning, but not overly zesty. Meat was tender. Well balanced.

Grilled Branzino - Amazing sauce and perfectly cooked fish. Delicious red curry paste rounded off with Kaffir leaves and coconut cream.

Kunamoto oysters - Served with green dipping sauce (nam jim) and fried onions. Good, but not really worth $3 a piece. Try during happy hour instead.

Crab fried rice  - So good! Fragrant, simple dish. Elegantly fried. Good sized chunks of crab.

Tiger prawn karee - Amazing sauce. Slightly on the saltier side, but the egg curry would be great to mix together with some white rice.

Morning glory - Perfectly cooked with the right amount of garlic and  umami seasoning. We eat this often in Myanmar and this dish brought back many memories.

Service was great. Ambiance 5/5 (their outdoor seating is cute too). Sanitizer at every table. I look forward to coming back!

Fish Cheeks is one of my favorites restaurants in the city. The dishes are just so good. My favorites have been the fried fish and shrimp dishes. Though, you simply can't go wrong with any of the seafood options and I challenge you to try as many as possible. Their cocktails are also unique and delicious. The bright vibe matches the happiness you'll feel during your meal. Definitely a must try.

Not impressed. Considering the price point, I'd say I am disappointed.  Fried water cress was the best dish. It was cooked to perfection. 

The flavoring of the curry was out of balance, and tasted a bit bitter, perhaps with too much clove and cardamom. The crab mung bean noodle basically used a typical Chinese/Taiwanese cooking technique to cook a dish in a way less successful than what I can find in a Chinese restaurant.(the green sauce they provide was a stand out)

This place has an awesome happy hour! Come for the drink and oysters specials, stay for the delicious food! 11$ house cocktails and discounted oysters on the half shell complete with fried crispy shallots and spicy sauce. I could eat a million of these they are so good. On top of that the wait staff is so helpful and let us order that extra drink as happy hour was ending. So nice of them! The zabb wings are tangy, sweet and a dash of heat. Paired nicely with the crab fried rice which had a light mild flavor. The grilled branzino was fresh and hot. Can't wait to come back and try more things on the menu!

This is one of my top 3 restaurants in NYC. It's the place you want to bring out-of-towners or anyone for that matter to impress them.  They are super consistent with the quality, presentation, and taste of food every single time I come here. I always get the crab curry, crab fried rice, OYSTERS, and STEAMED FISH. Listen to everyone when they say get the fish. It's phenomenal. I don't know how else to say it. The mint, cilantro, garlic, red Thai chili, lemon and fish sauce are the perfect sauce on this fish. You'll want to drink it. All the crab dishes have very big chunks of crab. Andddd don't get me started on the oysters. The Nam Jim seafood sauce and fried crispy shallots make this an oyster you'll never forget. All the flavors tie in beautifully with each dish. I can't stop thinking about the food when I'm done.

Without a doubt, Fish Cheek's coconut crab curry is one of the best things I've ever eaten. This dish will have me coming back to Noho for as long as they will be serving it up. 

Located on a quiet Bond Street, Fish Cheek's fresh and inviting interior alludes to the quality of the meal you're about to sit down to. The waitstaff is super friendly, and take pride in their depth of knowledge about the menu's offerings.

We started with the Zabb wings, a tasty and tangy appetizer to open up the meal. There's about 4 wings per plate, so don't be afraid to order 2!

Now for the pièce de résistance. I kid you not, I've had dreams about the coconut crab curry from Fish Cheek's. It's perfectly seasoned - somewhere between being a little spicy, and a little sweet. The delicious crab morsels are like hidden gems when digging into this dish. Served with a side of rice, my modus operandi is to actually dump all of the rice into the bowl of curry and tuck into what I know will be the best thing I will eat all weekend.

Make no mistake, Fish Cheek's does a lot of dishes extremely well. But it will be the coconut crab curry that will keep you coming back every single time. Hats off to the chef!

I was so excited to come here but the experience as a whole was lackluster. NYC just opened indoor dining back up so one would expect restaurants to elevate their indoor spaces to invite their guests back in. Nope. Their ambiance was so bland. The waiter recited the specials so fast that we couldn't really understand him so we just ordered off menu because we didn't want to be rude and make him repeat it... but wish he had pushed the chicken special a little harder because our neighbors who received it raved about it. I ordered one app and two entrees and asked the waiter if that was enough and he suggested a side which I accepted. This was definitely not enough food for the two of us - wish we got that chicken special too! What a missed opportunity.

Poached shrimp appetizer - very thick sweet coconut that overpowered the whole dish. There was no citrus to brighten it up. It was ok. 

Fried fish with fresh herbs was a tiny little guy. The fish sauce/lime juice ran a little sweet but fresh herbs were nice. The fish entrees here are so expensive for what it is. Not impressed. Felt robbed for receiving such a small fish for $35!! Insane SoHo pricing for something deep fried & they don't specify what kind of fish it is... 

Crab coconut curry - I can't believe we paid this much money for this. The thick curry is sweet and very spicy with just a tiny bit of crab. I'm not sure why this is a fan favorite but I was so disappointed. $25... I can't shake my head enough. 

The side of cabbage - another rip off. They didn't cut it into small pieces so you get these large leaves with nothing to cut since their cutlery set doesn't include a knife (just spoon & fork). It was a small portion for the price of cabbage that you had to savagely rip apart with your bare hands or eat like you're Stitch from Lilo & Stitch (not pretty). 

Overall, sad, super hyped up place with no ambiance or star quality. Maybe it's just because of the pandemic but won't be returning.

What on earth? I consider myself an avid Thai eater in New York and I've had this place bookmarked for a while so finally decided to order it tonight. Absolutely awful. My boyfriend and I got the Kua Kling ($25), the coconut crab curry ($25) and the wings ($13) and ended up throwing half the food away. 

The wings were good but a little undercooked so I found myself carefully biting into the chicken to avoid raw parts. The flavor was delicious, however, and it was a shame that they weren't cooked better. 

The kua kling was good with a nice kick, but dry and lacking in flavor. I've had much better versions of the same dish. Portion size was good though.

The crab curry was rancid. This was the one dish that we both took one bit of and spit out. My boyfriend said it tasted like his wet dog smelled. It literally tasted like poison to me, just absolutely awful. 

Expensive for the portions and very bad food overall. Would not order again.

Came here for my birthday in the covid-dining-era, 2/2021. 

We were a group of 7 and had reservations for indoor dining. 
We had the best time. Drinks were strong and delicious and the food was out of this world!

Everyone had the best gastronomical experience as we basically tried everything on the menu. Everything was THAT good that we kept the food flowing. Can't go wrong here with whatever you order. 

We all left happy and with a full belly!

They are sooo good. The fish is amazing perfectly seasoned. Be warned, this is actually spicy so if you can't handle the spice don't come in. It's so annoying to hear people say don't make it spicy. It's a Thai restaurant! It's like a vegetarian going to a butcher shop asking to hold the meat.

Some takeout in Fish cheeks.
Amazing Thai cuisine.
Highly recommend tiger prawn karee.

I died and woke up in Thailand! 

Been dying to make it and finally showed up no matter if it was cold and outside. Anyhow the weather is turning and indoors is back! This is a bit older while it was only outside dining with heaters.

I don't wish to ramble, I just need to say this is the only authentic Thai restaurant I have come across after 20 years in NYC. Try the chicken wings for sure, you will be amazed.

Saw many mouth watering photos ad on Instagram and 4 stars on Yelp we decided to come and give it a try.  

The place was packaged both outdoor and in door in a Sunday evening.  Need advance reservation for us party of 4.  We were seated inside but we were all holding on to our Jackets since it's freezing inside, I was told they've already turned the heat to the highest, since the entrance door is open for the server to bring out the food that's why it's cold.

We ordered a hot alcohol drink to keep us warm.  it was way too strong and not to the normal standard.  We ordered zabb wings, fried crispy fish skin, coconut crab curry, grilled pork cheeks, tiger prawn Kareen, EVERYTHING tasted extremely SALTY! It's like pouring salt on top on every dishes.

After we leave the restaurant walked outside, the temperature outside was even warmer then inside.  Overall it was a disappointment.  Our first and will be last time here.

I had my fair share of Thai food. I expected more from Fish Cheeks. Many of the entrees are just too salty. There's a difference between flavorful or just a load of salt. Crab meat curry, chicken skin and the fish was all too salty. Prawn Karee was the best of everything in my eyes. Additional the place was freezing cold indoor. We asked to turn up the heat but they said it was at the highest. We felt the temperature was no different than sitting outside (45 degrees).  Thanks but don't think I'll return anytime soon.

Everything we ordered was delicious! Each dish was packed full of flavor. Our favorites were the coconut curry with crab and the fried chicken skins. They were a 10/10. The rest were 9/10! Very rare that every single dish is amazing when eating out but it seriously was. Will be back for sure.

Went back with a larger group about 2.5 months post my last visit in order to try more items. What can I say? This is quickly becoming one of my favorite restaurants in New York City. The food is perfect - each dish better than the last - and the cocktails are insane (I love you, @cheeky green). Between the five of us we had the zabb wings and the pork cheeks for appetizers, and had the steamed fish, coconut crab curry, tiger prawn karee, crab fried rice, and green curry for our mains. We shared everything and everything was fantastic. Only thing I would skip is the green curry - still great but pretty typical and I think their specialities are so much better.

I'm already excited for my next visit, and am so glad this place is around. A million stars!

Probably one of my favorite restaurants in the city. I've come on multiple occasions and they never fail. The staff is all very attentive, clean, and polite. The food, believe it or not I think they deserve a Michelin over uncle boons. Crab fried rice.. A must with every dish.. Just mix it in and amazing combination of flavors. Coconut crab curry, Pork cheeks, Morning glory and oyster.. My go to's here I don't come often enough or with enough people to order everything on the menu but one day I'm going to. 
Whenever anyone asks for a recommendation. This place is always the first that comes out of my mouth.

Overall decent thai place I stumbled upon looking for great seafood in the city. We had coconut curry crab, branzino with thai herbs, and curry branzino in banana leaf. For drinks we had pandan lemongrass tea, thai tea, butterfly pea limeade. 
Curry crab: the idea of it sound great however its extremely spicy almost to spicy to bare. We asked for them to make it mild and instead it taste lkke they made it spicer which eas very unfortunate as ee ended up having to try and add coconut cream to it to dial it down and still didnt work so kind of a waste.
Branzino with thai herbs: this was not a favorite at all. The fish was cooked lightly so 1 level above raw. The flavors did not mix well and it had a very fishy taste. We ended up trying to use some of the flavor from the curry crab to liven it up but it eneded up tasting like a spicy mess so tossed that too.
Finally the curey branzino in the banana leaf. Now this was the all star dish of the experience. It was delicious perfect seasonings and overall great dish this was the only dish enjoyed. And made up the 3 stars given
Lastly the drinks
Thai tea- was good your typical thai tea
Pandan lemongrass- great! Unique drink that was delcious be aware if you never had pandan with be a bit of a shock as its a strong flavor mixed with lemongrass which is strong but enjoyable
Butterfly pea limeade just taste like regular limeade that happen to be purple.

Have been here more than a couple dozen times. Food is always consistently fantastic. Steamed fish, shrimp in 3 crab sauce, and grilled pork cheeks are a must. Love the garnishes & sauce that comes with the oysters. All the drinks r great too. Think I've tried everything here; can't go wrong with anything on the menu.
I now understand why some reviews say bad customer service. The manager was very rude and we were not happy about the experience at all. Not coming back.

Fish Cheeks is a punny name with some great merchandise. Located on Bond street next to fame Italian/Mediterranean restaurant Il Buco / the lively outdoor coloring and aesthetic for fish cheeks will surely catch you eye & the aroma of the steamed fish will catch your nose. 

Went here on a Monday night with a few friends. They do have a table time limit right now for covid but I never once felt rushed or in a need to hurry along. 

But let's get to it: 
- large outdoor booths with great heat 
- quick service with water and drink orders 
- got the Thai iced tea and asked for light milk which they were able to accommodate however they didn't fill the glass all the way up. For $8 (!!!) for Thai iced tea I would of loved to have a full glass 
- whole steam fish was good...but I was probably most disappointed in this as it looked and smelled so good but it was very bony. VERY. I read many reviews saying it was deboned but perhaps that's not the case. 
- the crab fried rice and the accompanying sauces were a highlight 
- the tiger prawns although delicious only comes with 3 so be prepared for that if ordered for the table, etc 
- it's good....I maybe didn't have a great first experience so I'm still going with 4 stars and I will probably go back in the future. But I need to see more.

Open for indoor and outdoor dining during winter '21. Big dividers between each table indoors- somehow the business manages to keep a really palatable aesthetic. We decided to stop by for happy hour, as we don't like to splurge on such pricey options for actual dinner.
$6 beers (Singha, Chang, Tiger), $10 cocktails. My husband enjoyed his Thai Old Fashioned. 
The curry sauce of the mussels was delicious! But the mussels themselves were not 18 bucks delicious. 
It's a fun splurge in an upscale neighborhood!

Maybe I ordered badly. Came here for the restaurant week special, a vegetarian green curry. I wasn't a huge fan of the selection of vegetables they used. Normally, I'm used to seeing broccoli, eggplant, peppers and the like. But they used cauliflower (not a fan) and root vegetables. I know they were trying to be different but I would have preferred the more popular ingredients. The curry itself was yummy and I'd be interested to try something else from them, though it is on the expensive side when compared to some other popular places.

Overall: 3.5/5

Came here for Sunday lunch and made reservations a few days in advance for indoor dining. It was still a bit chilly inside, staff wore masks, tables separated by dividers, but no temp check on arrival. We (2 ppl) got the Coconut Crab Curry, Zabb Wings, and Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce. 

Zabb Wings - awesome flavor, would get again. 
Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce - spicy and tasty, would get again, good for those that like raw seafood. 
Coconut Crab Curry - the crab was delicious and there was a considerable amount given. Also came with a bowl of rice, kind of small to split between 2 people. The curry and flavor were good, but not great. It seemed like it was lacking something. I would not get again. 

Service started out pretty good, I liked my server, but got kind of weird at the end. I think it might've just been a matter of miscommunication, but I asked for an extra bowl of rice right when we got the curry cause I knew we'd need more and this was to the person who brought out our food. We waited maybe 10-15 minutes for the extra bowl of rice and finally decided to ask again, this time to our server, because by now we had been done with the first bowl. Then waited another 5 minutes and then asked how long the rice would be, he seemed surprised that it hadn't been brought out yet and then brought a steaming bowl of rice immediately. Then the check showed 2 extra bowls of rice which was corrected to 1, but still not a great experience...

Omg - literally the best Thai food I've eaten outside of Thailand. Please get the Zabb wings - they look dry but they are juicy inside - layers of spices that leap around your mouth. We also got the crab rice and crab curry - both exquisite and super flavorful. The tiger prawns, short ribs and steamed fish were all delicious and unique. Don't sleep on the veggie side dish of morning glory - so so good. This is not the place for you if you're intimidated by spices and chilli. The chef obviously knows his way around Thai ingredients and truly celebrates them in every dish. I'm going back again very soon!

Came back to Fish Cheeks a year after my first time here and everything still holds up! Still remains as one of my favorite restaurants!

Dined here last night for a Valentine's Day dinner date with my bf, made a reservation for 5pm in the main dining room on Resy as soon as it was announced that indoor dining was opening up again. They have outdoor seating options available as well. Outdoor/indoor seating availability is listed on the app. $25 cancellation fee per person if you're a no show or cancel after 5:30pm on the day before your reservation. 

Service: 5/5 - We were driving there and running 10 minutes late so we called ahead and the hostess was very accommodating. Upon arrival, they checked our temperature and were seated inside a few mins later. All tables (indoor and outdoor) are separated with dividers with hand sanitizer at every table. All staff are wearing masks and following Covid protocols. Our waiter, Christopher, was attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable on all the dishes and drinks. Although the restaurant was super busy, we never felt forgotten about or rushed. 

Food: 5/5 - Happy Hour is from 12pm-6pm. $11 cocktails, $10 wine and $6 beer. Was especially looking forward to the $1.50 oysters but sadly they're not serving oysters at the moment. My bf got red wine and I got the Cheeky Green, which tasted like a mojito but still good nonetheless. All dishes are meant to be shared, it's family style. We loved every dish we ordered. I thought we'd have leftovers but it was so good, we killed everything! For apps, we ordered the Zabb Wings and Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce. The seasoning on the wings is so simple yet unlike any other chicken wings you've had before, crispy and flavorful. The raw shrimp is super refreshing and flavorful, the 3 crab sauce adds a nice kick. For main dishes, we ordered the Fried Fish with Garden Herb Salad, Coconut Crab Curry, and the Crab Fried Rice. Fish was fried just right, soft and tender on the inside, lightly fried and crispy on the outside, accompanied with lots of herbs, ginger, chili, and a pickled garlic dressing. So much going on but it all works together so well. Coconut crab curry came with jasmine rice and a generous amount of crab. Simple curry, it's literally just curry and crabmeat but super packed with flavor. Crab fried rice was amazing as well. Also had a generous amount of crab, came with sauces on the side. We mixed in the sauces, took the rice to another level. Also ordered a Hot Toddy and the Thai Breaker cocktail later on, both tasty and great. 

Ambiance: 4.5/5 - My first time here was back in February 2020, and I remember it being really warm and cozy. The lights were dim and the ambiance then felt more relaxed and intimate. This time, all the lights were on, you know that feeling when you're one of the last customers still in the restaurant and they're trying to close up so they turn on the lights and stop the music and it begins to get uncomfortable? That's how I felt haha. And although we were seated inside, it was still pretty cold. I had to keep my jacket on and I still felt like I wasn't wearing enough. But I do understand with indoor dining having been reopened just days ago, many restaurants are having to adjust once again and honestly just trying to stay afloat in this pandemic, not everything can be perfect but overall I'm super happy with my experience dining here yet again. It was my bf's first time here and he absolutely loved everything!

Still so excellent.  Came here for lunch today around noon on Monday.  Sat outside in a small separate booth for 2 with no reservation.  There were outdoor heaters that kept us more than cozy.

Got my favorite dish of all time- Crab AOB Woonsen.  This dish unfortunately isn't available for delivery.  It is so good in person.  Glass noodles covered in sweet savory sauce paired with delicious firm chunks of blue crab and the delicious tangy spicy salty green seafood sauce.  It's amazing!

We also got some grilled branzino- a moist fillet covered in a spicy red curry sauce with peanuts (I think).  Was so delicious, too.

I got the butterfly pea limeade- perfectly cut through the richness of the dishes.

The Thai chicken wings was delicious! It came with a great amount of wings in a box. The chicken was very crispy and the flavor of it had an amazing aroma. The level of spiciness in the coconut crab curry was just right. I'm definitely coming back again to try out their other dishes.

-happy hour oyster deal is the BOMB. their accompanying lil fried shallots and green herb sauce makes me sad that the norm is horseradish/lemon. would go again just for them! they're a tad on the small size but that just makes them perfect for any oyster first-timers !!
-took up yelps recommendation of the crab curry; totally delivered, so rich and creamy, ample amount of crab. nice amount of spice.
-skip the desert, interesting concepts but fell short on flavor, was just nondescript
-no pad thai or drunken noodles though if that's what your looking for hahaha

Hands down the best Thai food I've had in NYC! So authentic and delicious - every bite was packed with flavor. I came with my friends for happy hour. We all started off with drinks and I got a spicy mango while my friends got a spiked Thai iced tea after our waiter recommend it (it's not part of happy hour but worth every penny). We ordered zab wings, pork cheek, steamed mussels, crab coconut curry, crab fried rice, morning glory (not pictured), and the steamed branzino (not pictured). This meal came out to $260 with tax and tips for the 4 of us. My top 3 favorites was the crab fried rice, pork cheek, and zab wings. I think I could eat the crab fried rice everyday for the rest of my life, it was THAT good. Highly recommend and worth the hype. Also, great outdoor dining space - it was really warm!

They have a great outdoor setup with heaters and separators between the dining tables. The colorful roof tiling and cobblestone block gives the restaurant a great  ambiance for casual dining.

Ordered:
- Crab Curry ($25), comes with jasmine rice: this curry is a must try! If you love spicy food, this will be an instant hit because it sure brings the heat! (If you can't handle spice, I would skip this.) There's quite a decent amount of crab meat in the curry too. Super rich and creamy, but not overbearing sweet from the coconut milk. 
- Zabb Wings ($13): very limey and acidic. If you're a huge fan of lemon pepper, this is for you. Personally, I don't gravitate towards those flavors.
- Nam Jin Seafood Sauce ($15 for a bottle): great dipping sauce for seafood and even for nachos and tacos to be honest. In a sense, it's similar to a green salsa but with Thai flavors, do wish it had more green chilis and was spicier though.
My go to Thai restaurant! My favorite things to order are the wings, corn salad, seafood soup, crab fried rice, steamed branzino, and morning glory! I mean everything is just so so good!

Ordered here TWICE for restaurant week 

Not sure if they changed their menu or they ran out but manila clam with rice was not available the second time around. Both times I got the tom yum seafood with rice. Third option was vegan green curry with rice. Appreciate how they give three options. 
It also comes with a drink, sodas, Thai tea, Thai coffee, or lemongrass pandan tea 

Tom Yum Seafood 
This is the best tom yum I've ever had. All other places are too watery and/or skimpy in seafood. Here it's sweet and sour and spicy and savory all in one, sooo flavorful!!! I can easily eat all the rice with this. The rice is on the drier side but that works perfectly well for absorbing soup. 
They give a lot of high quality seafood, ofc not the best best best but way better than many places. The mussels are big and plentiful (4?). The fish chunks are big and fresh. The shrimps are big and plentiful (2?). (For comparison, I ordered a paella the same day and that had much smaller and lower quality seafood).

 I got the lemongrass pandan tea the first time and Thai tea the second time. I like how they come in a sealed bottle that can be recapped. 
The lemongrass pandan tea is yellow in color. It has a faint pandan flavor. The lemongrass dominates but not in a refreshing way. It awfully has the massage oil vibe. Interesting stuff not my thing. 
Thai tea is the iconic milky orange one!!! It's the second best thai tea I've ever had. They don't put ice in the bottle so it's not diluted, well considering it's meant to be super sweet. I drank some and added milk. Even after adding a lot, the tea flavor still came through. The first place thai tea is slightly better because there's an aftertaste while Fish Cheeks one doesn't. 

Anyway this was good enough for me to go again. The things I got impressed me. I'm happy to try other things outside of the restaurant week menu.

This is a fantastic Thai place! When Americans think of Thai food, I bet that they think of carb heavy pad Thai, drunken noodles, generic curry and Thai ice-tea (the last of which is awesome by the way if done right). However, this place offers flavors that are more aligned with the real deal in Asia, and farther away from the mainstream Thai food in North America as we know it.

I ordered several very flavorful dishes for sharing. My favorite dish by far is the steamed fish - the fish was served with various Asian spices and came with a small burner underneath it to keep the fish warm - definitely worth having when eating outdoor at sub 30 degree temperature. The grilled pork neck is a popular dish in Thai restaurants, and this place's version didn't disappoint. The manila clams were tasty but I wouldn't say it could beat the fish in a one-on-one contest. Finally, the raw shrimp - normally I wouldn't order it due to hygienic concerns, was well worth it. The wonderful blend of sweet, sour and spicy flavors from the spices and the freshness of the shrimp was a worthwhile experience.

What I would NOT recommend is getting the cocktail. Perhaps I am just not a cocktail person in general, but I was sold by the waitress to have one after making a mulled wine at home the other night - I just wanted to see how my mixed drink compared to those that I had to pay like $15 for. The verdict is - stick with my fat jar of mulled wine at home. For Thai food, the Chang or Singha beer is my go-to beverage accompaniment, or the good old Thai ice-tea as I already mentioned above.

Made a reservation for this afternoon and man, this place definitely lives up to the hype! Ordered the favorite coconut crab curry, pork cheek, grilled branzino, and a few cocktails. I wanted more of everything. Definitely can't wait to come back and try the Zabb wings, scallops, and more. Outdoor dining could be a little more weather resistant but the food makes up for everything. Good service too.
Amazing food! So freaking tasty and fantastic service. Get the steamed fish especially!

My girlfriend took me to Fish Cheeks for a birthday lunch the other day, and I was super excited.  We made our reservation, were seated, and began our feast.  The food was exceptional, the raw shrimp and pork cheek appetizers were flavorful and delicious, and the crab curry was so good neither of us could stop eating it.  After washing it all down with a couple of Leo beers, we were pretty happy.  We would have enjoyed the grilled branzino a bit more, however, had it not been for the slow, rude, and overall absence of service midway through our meal. 

After getting our appetizers and crab curry, we were expecting our fish to quickly follow (as everything else had).  This was not the case.  We sat with no attention from the wait staff, abandoned, for at least thirty minutes.  Eventually, I asked our waiter where our food was, and he was immediately rude and defensive, saying that the fish took at least 15-20 minutes to make.  This would have been a good excuse if we hadn't been waiting for thirty minutes already.  About ten minutes later, he came back and explained there had been a mixup (no other explanation given), and that our fish would be coming. In another 20 minutes, it finally came.  At no point was there any kind of apology or even acknowledgement that the dish had taken almost an hour to reach our table.  

I find it hard to believe that in a confined space with other tables getting their orders, nobody from the waitstaff thought to check in on us! Not to mention the fact that there were plenty of people waiting to be seated, and we were taking up valuable real estate waiting for our food.  Of course, once the fish was finally brought out, it was only a matter of minutes between that and being handed the check.  Again, no apology, no acknowledgement, and overall rudeness.

I don't care how many reviews a restaurant has, or how posh the neighborhood is, or how authentic your cuisine is supposed to be, or how one of the waiters assured us that he really was from Thailand so the food had to be good.  Bad service is bad service.  I loved the food, I really did, but based on how we were treated, I don't know if I'll be back!  Nice way to treat a guy on his birthday, Fish Cheeks!

Reservations east on RESY (yes they hold deposit in case you don't show up); they do not take reservations via telephone day off; both covered and uncovered outdoor seating; strong standing heat lamps (I was not cold!), Service was friendly and attentive. Safety and spacing protocols in place.

Now let's get to the food....the appetizer pork cheek were cut thin and appeared larger than an appetizer (easy for 2 to share), and the BEST crab fried rice I've had in a long time. I'm lightweight obsessed with the crab fried rice!!!

******EDIT FOR 1/15/2021*******
So I know it's only been a day, but I am so obsessed with the crab fried rice I ordered it for delivery last night. I also got the Zabb Wings. The wings flavor was a dry rub....it was like a punch of flavor...not too spicy, I can taste a little sweet but limey zang to it. I inhaled them.

I ordered the crab fried rice again and yes, it was STILL as delicious as it was the day prior!

Picked up some take out after hearing about this place from a friend and the food was incredible. I picked up the zabb wings as an appetizer and the crab fried rice entree. Both were very flavorful and I loved the zesty-ness of the wings and trying the different sauces that came with the crab fried rice (which also did not disappoint in the amount of crab included!) 

I definitely want to come back and stay for a sit down meal since the decor and ambiance look very nice, even if its outdoor dining only. The location is peaceful, right off of the wide cobblestone streets of NoHo.

I normally write reviews so that I know what to return to/not visit again. But at this point, writing a Fish Cheeks review is a formality. Everyone knows it is some of the most delicious, flavorful, rich, and consistent food out there. I honestly can't wait to try everything on their menu.

Last time we ordered FC is over new years eve, when a close couple came to surprise us with a visit. We were all starving, and they had recently moved out of NYC and were craving some great Thai food. Well, it really isn't a question of where to go- we ordered fish cheeks and everyone was absolutely blown away. The Crab Fried rice is incredible, the crisp, juicy wings are AMAZING, pork cheeks are delicious, and the crab curry is rich and overwhelmingly addictive. 

If you are a fan of flavor, give this place a shot!
Worth outdoor dining in this cold winter. Be careful though, you may end up keep placing new orders that your wallet will be empty and you have to go to gym

10/10 would recommend! Not only is the name eye catching, the food is also incredible! I ordered the Somtum Corn Salad, Zabb Wings, Crab Fried Rice, the Tiger Prawn Karee, Pakboong Fai, the ice cream Sunday with egg, and the sesame balls in ginger. For drinks I got the seasonal special mulled wine and the cocktail they have. Was considering ordering the khua kling but was steered away by the server as being VERY spicy. The service was incredible and we adored our server - she was incredibly helpful and actually designed some of the seasonal drinks!

The standouts - The zabb wings have crack in them I'm convinced!! They have the tiniest punch to them and the lime on them just compliments the food really well. Will be dreaming about these wings for awhile. The corn salad exceed my expectations ten-fold! Wouldn't have really expected much from it but it was light and really flavorful. They said they make it fresh to order which is lovely! The ice cream sundae with the egg was insane. Usually not that big into ice cream but it was topped with Ovaltine and had a duck yolk mixed with sugar in it. SO YUMMY don't get thrown off by the yolk since it hardens when in contact with the cold ice cream. 

The good - the crab fried rice was super yummy just very simple! The sauces they had with elevated the rice so much and the dish had really generous chunks of crab! Would order again for sure it just was a little simple! The tiger prawns were also great and well done, just not really a big prawn person to begin with so they were good just not for me! The drinks were alright nothing special. The mulled wine had a little too much spice for me.  

The bad - the sesame balls in ginger were really not good. I think you probably could get better versions of that in an Asian grocery store that's been premise and frozen. :(

The atmosphere - the tables are heated! There are probably like 8 tables outside - 4 in a little tented cute area and 4 uncovered. If you can get a table in the tent definitely do because it is significantly warmer. Came at like 7/8 and it had 4 tables uncovered open.

The outdoor dining area was nice. There was a heater and they gave me a blanket when I asked for one which was so nice. The food was great, small portions and pricey but overall worth it. The curry is soooo spicy just a heads up

Brrr, it's cold as ice sitting in a tent during CoVID on 12/26/20 and we are hoping to enjoy our lunch. Bathroom is cute!! More after we eat!
We ordered shrimp in 3 crab sauce for an appetizer. Amazing melange of flavor with a lot of spicy pepper flakes. Normally I don't like spicy food but it was FREEZING out so I didn't mind having my insides warmed up a tad! Lol   We also ordered Po Tak which is a delicious lemongrass soup with shrimp, mussels and squid which we shared. The waitstaff was very nice and they all wore masks. We also had the tiger prawn karee which wasn't as spicy. It was a very light late lunch and we all enjoyed it very much!! We will be back!!

I really really really wanted to like this place however it was sadly mediocre. The food looked very pretty and the dining experience was very aesthetic however the flavor was just not there. Everything kind of had the same taste to it and I was very bland. The drinks were really good, the lemonade was amazing so if you want to go to a place to get some good cocktails I would go here but if you're looking for food I would try someplace else there's a lot better places in the Bowery.

Since Uncle Boons closed (RIP), Fish Cheeks is my go to for great Thai.  So it was surprising, I had such a negative experience last night.  

I've been there a few times since COVID (incl the week before) and they have a great covered booth setup with overhead heat lamps (in the Patio section) and never had issues. In Resy, I specifically booked this "Patio" section as opposed to the other seating option, the "Sidewalk" section which are uncovered tables w pretty weak, standing heat lamps.  I came 5m early for my reservation and was told by the hostess that they can't give me the covered section right now, but to sit in the uncovered and when the booth opens we would get it.  Waited patiently, order drinks and apps, and I turned my head for a minute and it's the same waitress giving our booth away to a party who came after me, didn't have a Patio reservation, but I guess complained more than I did about moving.  At this point, after probably getting frostbite eating their delicious wings and pork cheeks...the cold was unbearable and we decided to pack our dinner to go.   Bust of a night and I didn't make a good impression with my dining companion. 

The manager gave a half hearted apology, did not offer to comp anything or even discount our dinner, even though what was supposed to be a nice Friday night dinner downtown ended up me traveling 40m for takeout.  And the Steamed Fish I had ordered for dinner (which is one my fav dishes at FC) is not a dish which travels well. The manager brought us a round of drinks as we were leaving and to be fair did try to bring in another ineffective heat lamp, but at that point I couldn't feel my nose so we left.  

This is the first bad experience I've had here, so will call it an outlier because of these exceptional circumstances.  Still the best Thai in Manhattan and I will definitely be back. But my advice is to definitely call and confirm your Patio reservation beforehand or you may end up wasting your night and risking hypothermia.  I gave an extra star because the food and servers were top notch. I think the hostess and manager just had a bad night.

YES. 

the steamed branzino and coconut crab curry are to die for. their martinis are BIG and the pig ears are delicious. praying this place doesn't get closed due to covid

Hands down the best meal I've had in New York. 
The steamed fish was so soft and flavorful and did not have a fishy after taste. 
I came here for happy hour oysters and they were fire. It came with a lemony topping and fried shallots crisps for only 1.50 each. 
I also got seafood Tom yum which was also delicious. The soup was good to share between two people, to each have two small bowls.

This was outstanding. We came and sat at a well-distanced table outside of their enclosure and got the sumtum corn salad, fried chicken skins (special), shrimp in 3 crab sauce, crab curry, and the crab aob woosen. I really loved everything, although my wife wasn't crazy about the shrimp because it was a little bit too herby for her (and she hates cilantro). I'd also be open to subbing out the woosen next time, and maybe the corn salad, just in order to try more things, but the zabb chicken skins and crab curry were absolute must-reorders. I'll be dreaming of that crab curry in particular -- it would be hard to make this much better.

COVID-19 outdoor dining review: after walking by Fish Cheeks and seeing their beautiful setup out on the cobblestones of Bond St, I was determined to come back and eat here. Ended up going for a small group dinner a few weeks ago, and I was even more impressed than I was when I came last year! Despite the pandemic, this restaurant has remained insanely popular, so definitely plan to come by a bit early and put your name down. My group of five arrived around 5:15PM on a Sunday, and we were seated after a brief 15 minute wait. They have a spacious, distanced outdoor dining area lit up with twinkly lights, and Bond St is largely undisturbed by traffic, so it's a great al fresco dining situation. 

We started with a round of Spicy Mango cocktails and ordered the zabb wings, yum pla salid, coconut crab curry, steamed fish with Thai herbs, khua kling, crab fried rice, sautéed morning glory, and a special with crab and glass noodles to share (we eat a lot). Everything was outstanding and all the flavors paired so well together: favorites were the wings (crispy with great flavor), the coconut crab curry, crab fried rice (HUGE chunks of crab), morning glory, and the steamed fish. I was really impressed by the fish in particular, as steamed white fish doesn't usually do it for me, but this was so light and delicious, and a great counterpart to some of the heavier dishes we ordered. For dessert, we got the coconut ice cream sundae and this banana-flavored sticky rice. Major props to our server for insisting we get the sticky rice, which was unassuming looking but AMAZING. I'm still craving it! I also love that right before happy hour ended, he went around to every table and asked if they wanted another round of drinks (we did, the Spicy Mango was delicious). 

Also, as a follow up to my previous review, I now own one of their sweatshirts in a pretty sage green color. The only size they had left was XL, but I was unfazed: very glad I went for it, as it is extraordinarily warm and soft, but the fit is also slightly structured? It's a very chic oversized look, is what I'm saying. BUY THE MERCH.

We got delivery, it came fast, everything tasted good. Even the rice was prepared well, slightly sticky but not a glutinous ball. The crab curry was rich and spicy, the veggie green curry was larger and less intense. We got a super fresh corn salad too. Everything we ordered is worth ordering again next time.

The food here is so authentic and the staff is very accommodating. I accidentally arrived 30 minutes before my reservation and was able to get seated immediately outside. It was getting cold even with the heat lamps so the staff were very accommodating with moving us inside and honoring that my reservation was initially made for indoors. 

Appetizers: shrimp in 3 crab sauce, Zabb wings and grilled pork cheeks. All were delicious! My favorite was the shrimp because it was very unique and all the flavors went together perfectly. 

Entrees: coconut crab curry (comes with side of white rice) but we also ordered crab fried rice as extra. Curry was delicious and had lots of crab! The steamed fish was the star though. It was so tender and flavorful and loved eating the broth with the rice to soak up all the goodness. 

Go here for authentic Thai seafood! But be warned you won't find pad thai or drunken noodles on the menu.

So good! The wings are a dry rub but so interesting and different! The coconut crab curry and tiger prawn karee are great. The crab fried rice could be improved with crab fat included to make it less dry. Overall great!

The food here was unexpectedly amazingly delicious! It's a more modern take on Thai food and the flavors were on point with great variety and taste.

My favorite was the fish which was cooked in this lime broth which was just amazing, flavorful and just well made. The crab curry was good as well and also very tasty but the fish was definitely the highlight.

Absolutely, hands down, the best Thai food I have eaten in the US. 

I ordered the coconut crab curry and the fried crab rice. I spent some time in Asia, and I can honestly tell you that I felt I was eating authentic food in Thailand. Next time I'm going to eat fried fish.

I will be back in NYC in December for two weeks, and I will be eating here a lot.  If ever in NYC, do not miss out on Fish Cheeks!

Got to sit indoors and temperatures were taken.

Spicy Mango Cocktail- love the spicy kick from the chili

Grilled Pork Cheeks- who knew there was so much tasty meat on the cheeks?! 

Steamed Fish- whole fish was DEBONED! 

Coconut Crab Curry- my favorite dish. Flavorful and I kept pouring the sauce over the rice. Extra yummy!

Crab Fried Rice- large amounts of crabs, good portion

Would definitely come back again!
I will give four stars because I'm thai and I would say that the presentation are good the food some of them taste authentic but some of them less authentic.

I've heard great things about this restaurant and it's been on my list for some time. I finally had a chance to go with my friends and I would have to say it's now my favorite Thai restaurant. Every single dish was so flavorful! I would highly recommend the chicken wings, pork cheeks, steamed fish, crab woonsen and crab curry!
The outdoor seating is packed with people sitting back to back without any barrier between them. This doesn't meet my level comfort for safe social distancing between unrelated parties.

I highly recommend this place. Authentic Thai food that is not Americanized. Had a great waitress that made the experience worth it. On top of all the dishes in the tops we also had Crab Aob Woosen, which was absolutely phenomenal. I Highly recommend this place. It's a must check out place in this area.

This place has a small  and limited menu with dishes made up of mostly seafood. I chose to dabble a bit and tried their grilled cuttlefish! It was unique in taste and honestly delicious, i don't think another place could have made it better. the atmosphere was relics and invited and the service was just ok-- a bit slow.

My friend brought me here for lunch on a Saturday. Let me tell you now! Just go with money and an empty stomach. I wanted to try a few things but we got full. This place is truly an experience. I love Thai food but they took it to another level. I felt like I was in Thailand which I've been to before. 

I had the Somtum Corn Salad as an appetizer and the the Grilled branzino. It was soooooo good. The spices and herbs they used complimented the branzino in the perfect way. 

I had a glass of prosecco and their Butterfly Pea Flower Limeade which was amazing. 

I can't wait to go back!

This place is truly a gem I can't believe we only just discovered. We had obviously heard about fish cheeks for a while now and any place with reservations this hard to get in New York City, is usually worth the hype. Fish cheeks lived up to the rumors and how! I don't want to go too much into detail because it's making me drool just thinking of it. We had a dried fish appetizer and the pork cheeks to start with. The coconut crab curry and steamed fish with Thai herbs from mains. A spicy mango drink and their version of the hot toddy to wash it all down. What a spectacular meal. Service was on point too. Can't wait to go back.

This review is for outdoor dining during the pandemic. Really great set up outside with tons of ample seating as they're located a quiet street right off Bowery. 

The outdoor dining decor is very true to the fish cheeks vibe so it's very chic. My boyfriend and I started off with the spicy mango and Thai old fashioned drinks. For food, we got the morning glory veggie dish, steamed fish with Thai herbs, and the crab noodle dish. All very delicious and packed with flavors! The steamed fish was savory, yet refreshing as there's a strong citrus lime flavor. The morning glory veggies were cooked well and great with the spicy kick! Great chunks of crab in the noodle dish. 

This place never disappoints! I love spicy food and fish cheeks always tests my threshold.

I've been back a few times since my last 3-star review, which was docked a star for service rather than the quality of the food.

The food remains top notch! I haven't been able to come back for happy hour oysters and drinks but I've been back during covid for outdoor dining twice now. 

The chicken wings are perfectly fried and seasoned. The crab fried rice is so simple but delicious. The crab curry is unique and flavorful. The prawns are very well done as well! 

Not sure if it was available pre-COVID as I lived uptown, but they now deliver to where I live downtown.

Went to fish cheeks to lunch on a Saturday. Got the happy hour oysters, pork cheeks, coconut crab curry, steamed fish, and morning glory on the side. I liked the sauce and fried shallots that came with the oyster, they were very refreshing. Pork cheeks were okay, but not my favorite. The coconut crab curry is popular for a reason, the curry itself is moderately spicy and they give a generous amount of crab meat. I loved the the sauce and herbs that was steamed with the fish, added a herby flavor and the fish itself was very tender as well.

[PRE-COVID REVIEW]

My friends and I stumbled onto this place after attending a NYFW event nearby. We didn't wait long but then again it was closer to 9pm. We ordered the *steamed fish*. My god. It was super delicious. It was so juicy and flavorful. The flavors all worked in tandem and it is a MUST-HAVE! I'm not a seafood eater but I genuinely enjoyed eating this along with the other dishes. 

The atmosphere is fun, colorful, and moody all at the same time at night. I really do need to revisit this place because I haven't been here since COVID happened but it was extremely delicious and I am glad that they are still in business. I'm coming back, y'all.

Not traditional Thai food but the food is amazing. Ordered steamed fish and crab curry. Even though we waited for an hour to be seated cause it's pretty popular. Ingredients are fresh. We both loved it!! Would love to come back to try other dishes.
Omg DELICIOUS.  Great (very spread out) seating.  The street is shut down so no cars zooming by.

Drove in from New Jersey for this place on Sunday! I did not know what to expect and was blown away by my experience! To start off I had the pork cheeks, pomela salad and a Thai old-fashioned. The flavor profile for everything was amazing. For dinner I had the Tiger prawns and Steamed fish with Thai herbs. Both of the dishes were amazing the bursts of flavor from the fist bite to the last did not disappoint. Unfortunately I forgot the name of the dessert I had but it had jackfruit and tasted like I was eating a bowl of Fruity Pebbles!!

We were gifted a Take our dinner from here and we haven't eaten here since the one time when they first opened only because we thought it was extremely spicy but to our surprise our dinner was excellent this time with only the right amount of spiciness...we enjoyed it so much that we went back for take out again two weeks later and it was very good too except for one issue which was the crab curry that had very little crab in it!

Fish Cheeks is now easily one of my favorite Thai restaurants in the city. This place does NOT cater at all to Americanized versions of Thai cuisine. There are no pad thai, pad see ew, drunken noodle on the menu. Instead, Fish Cheeks focuses on Thai family-style seafood dishes.

Coconut Crab Curry - As someone who's not really a fan of Thai curry, I only ordered this because of the overwhelming positive reception from Yelp and Pete Wells. They were undeniably correct. The curry was rich thanks to the coconut milk, with a gingery, almost spicy, flavor. There was also a very generous amount of crab chunks. I will definitely be back again soon to try this and also the crab fried rice. 

Pork Cheeks - This appetizer reminded me most of pork belly, but even the lean parts were extremely tender and rich. The fried garlic bits and chili fish sauce dip was also an amazing accompaniment. 

There's happy hour before 6 pm, and some of us ordered $1.5 oysters and spicy mango cocktails.

Fish Cheeks' hospitality easily bumps this place up to 5 stars. We came here for our friend's birthday, and our waiter went above and beyond to make sure we were happy with our meal and helped serve our pre-bought cupcakes post-dinner. 

During COVID, our hostess took our temperatures before she escorted us to our seats. The entire street was closed down on the weekend, so Fish Cheeks really leveraged that to have a spacious layout for each table.

To nobody's surprise, this is another 5-star review for Fish Cheeks. Honestly, I'm just mad I didn't prioritize coming here earlier. My first visit was a couple of weeks ago, then a quick second visit followed roughly a week later. Nowadays, the question of "should we go to fish cheeks again?" is in the regular rotation of say-whatever weekend pondering. 

I am absolutely, head-over-heels obsessed with the steamed fish; the spicy-limey-cilantro-y broth with the delicate, deboned branzino is the best flavor bomb. The oyster accoutrements are also a revelation; bonus win for oyster happy hour from 12-6PM on most days.
