We ordered the curry crab, wings and crab fried rice. Everything delicious. A bit stingy with the crab in the coconut curry crab entree. We did inquire about this and was told it's all weighed and we were not being shorted. We tried! Lol however the crab in the crab fried rice was plentiful. 
Our total was about 100.00 with a beer and a cocktail. The spicy mango cocktail was delicious. I must say I had it without the spice (which can be done) and was recommended by our waitress. She was very pleasant and knowledgeable on the menu. We did not have desert but the coconut ice cream sound appetizing! I would definitely return to this restaurant in the spring.

My partner in munch and I surprisingly enjoyed our quick trip to Fish Cheeks- although the name initially made me think that the restaurant would be smelly..  We grabbed drinks and munched on the wings. I wish they were cooked a bit longer- they seemed like they weren't quite ready. Otherwise, a nice time!!

I have been meaning to write this review for a while. This is one of my favorite places to eat at when I am back in town. Every dish is on point and the service is always stellar. Great for date night or catching up with friends. If they don't have reservations you can always try and catch a seat at the bar. 

Highlights: 
-Oysters Thai Style:Amazing complex flavors and a great way to start the meal
-Coconut Crab Curry: This is my go to have yet to go to dinner here and not order it. Great flavor and perfectly spiced 
-Crab Aob Woosen: Honestly I love most of the crab dishes. This sticks out as it is a more unique style of thai noodles I haven't had before
-Thai Old Fashioned: Great spin on the classic 
-Happy hour is a great option here

Came in for a 7pm reservation and we were seated immediately. Kate was our server and she ran over to let us know that we had about two minutes before Happy Hour ended and she could get our order in-Score!!! We got the fresh oysters and the sauce was delicious.  Ive been on the hunt for a Thai-style steamed fish dish that I've only had in Asia. I was so excited when I saw it on Fish Cheeks menu and it did not disappoint. It was super tender, deboned, and the citrus sauce was perfect. In fact, everything we had was so amazing!!! This place was packed and there's good reason for it.

The food at Fish Cheeks is delicious and the decor is bright and beachy - I'll definitely be going back!

I have had similar versions of many of the dishes we tried at Fish Cheeks, but somehow, they did it better! To begin, they bring you complementary prawn crackers - these are addictive and I would nearly go back for these alone!

We also ordered the steamed fish in thai herbs (pictured). This dish surprised me in such a good way! Sometimes I worry steamed dishes will lack flavor in exchange for being "healthy" but this dish had both! The broth was light but sweet, acidic and full of flavor.

We also ordered the green curry which was slightly spicy and filled with delicious vegetables. This is the type of vegan dish that non-vegans would eat.

The decor is super cute and makes you feel like you're not even in NYC anymore. The chairs are a rainbow of colors and the beach theme is carried out even in the light fixtures. Fish Cheeks is definitely staying on my list until I can go back and try more!

Fantastic Thai restaurant that I had the pleasure of trying last week! My friend recommended this place as he heard great reviews and was able to get a coveted 7:30 reservation through Resy. 

The restaurant is super cute, though it is on the smaller side. I saw the remainder of the happy hour crowd as we headed to our table, and it definitely seems like a popular place for drinks and food! Our server was great and took our orders for drinks and food very quickly. 

We ordered the steamed fish, the crab/noodle dish, and the morning glory. Everything was unreal and incredibly well done. The flavor of everything was on point, and I loved the uniqueness of the dishes. My favorite as definitely the crab dish, the spice of the morning glory side went especially well with this one!

Everything on their menu looks really great, especially if you're a seafood fan. Definitely will be back to try more!

Fish Cheeks has been the most trendy place for happy hours and Thai recently among friends and we finally got a chance to try after our 3rd time visit. 

We highly recommend to make your reservation ahead or come right after they open. We were there at 5:15pm on a Friday night and there were only 3 tables for 2 left at that time. 

Their service was energetic, attentive and friendly. We really enjoyed the causal and relaxed ambiance there. 

Firstly, the staff served the complimentary shrimp chip with matched sauce. We ordered grilled pork cheeks as our appetizer, the pork cheek was well grilled, tender and tasty, definitely a must order. 

Our entrees were Crab Aob Woonsen and Coconut crab curry, both dish were extremely delicious and addictive. We also love their Pak Boong Fai Dang, fried morning glory with fish sauce, which was the best match with rice.

Seems like a pretty popular restaurant as there are quite a few guests waiting on a Thursday night. I got the famous crab curry- too spicy that I couldn't even hold my tears. The Thai tea helped a little bit though. The pork cheeks were good compared to the curry; I'd give one more star for that. Also it's quite noisy as everyone was talking real loud. Guess I was just having too many expectations.

Definitely worth the hype! Make your reservation ahead of time (note: Resy requires you to put a credit card down when reserve your table) Our reservations were for 12 (right when they open) and a line was already forming outside. Plan ahead!  11/10 would recommend the chicken wing appetizers

Great service  
Strong drinks 
Flavorful dishes 

I will definitely be back!

Came here once with a friend. Both our meals were outstanding. We sat at the bar, and the bartender was nice and made good drink recommendations for her as she was sure what she wanted to drink. She loved the mussels and herbs. The hat frai fried chicken and the fried rice were both phenomenal. I loved the whimsical decor, with the bar tiles that look like fish scales and the multi colored chairs; the place really has a nice feel to it.

Came here last year for my birthday dinner with a large group of 12 and came back again recently because I remembered how much we all loved it so much! For a table of more than 10 people, usually servers can't handle and keep up with their service for such a large group but I remembered for my birthday the service was relatively swift and soo accommodating! The food is packeddd with pungent flavors!

Pork cheeks (jowl) were BOMB!! Tiger prawn and crab fried rice was everyone's favorite that everyone fought over for. The crab fried rice had plenty jumbo lump of crab meat. Their coconut curry flavor is sooo on point, we even doused it on top of our rice and almost everything. Tiger prawns were also flavorful and huge. Everything pretty much was very spot on. Careful though, some dishes are super spicy. This & Uncle Boon's are def my top two favorite Thai restaurant to eat in New York. Very authentic and both are not the typical Thai spots that serves pad thai... no pad thai's on their menu!

After coming back from my honeymoon in Thailand, I've been on the hunt for some legit Thai food. Fish Cheeks nails it with its rich flavors and unwillingness to shy away from spice.

Reservations were relatively easy to get - I set a Resy alert for a Saturday night dinner slot and was able to snag a 7pm reservation a week in advance. They were also super accommodating over the phone when we were running 20-25 minutes late, and were very friendly about it when we did finally arrive.

The atmosphere is LOUD and tables are quite close together, but if you're dining with just one partner, holding a conversation is still very doable and somehow feels more intimate.

My husband and I shared three dishes:
- Yam Khai Plaa (the special of the night) which was similar to a som tam (green papaya salad), but instead of green papaya as the crunchy base, it had fish roe mixed with dried shrimp and herbs. I loved the texture of the fish roe (similar to a crunchy quinoa) and how punchy the flavor was. They do not shy away from fish sauce, lime juice, or chilis!
- Tiger Prawn Karee, which came with three medium-sized pieces of prawn (would not go as far as calling them giant) in a bed of saucy scrambled eggs. This only had a hint of spice, but overall was pretty mild and good to mix with rice. Don't forget the suck out the flavor in the prawn head!
- Coconut Crab Curry, which is probably their most popular dish. This was SPICY but was totally bearable. It's the kind of spicy that makes you instantly take another large spoonful/bite, because it hurts more to just let your mouth sit idle. There's a generous amount of soft chunks of crab. For $24 including rice, this is not a bad deal at all.

Definitely give this place a try if you want to give your taste buds a challenge and a treat.

This is one of my favorite Thai restaurants in NYC. The dishes here are so different than what you'd find at most Thai restaurants. The steamed fish with herbs is my go to dish here. I also love the corn salad -- it's so fresh and light. Excited to keep trying new things on their menu.

I came here after watching a food documentary that mentioned this place. When you walk in the aroma of food hit you and I mean it's just amazing. I recommend coming for lunch because in the evening this place is packed and RSVP is about a two week wait. I basically tasted the whole menu lol. Flavors, texture and creativity this place is special!

I have come here about three times and every time it's delicious! Also, courteous service and very accommodating to large parties. Back to food, always have to order the zaab wings and oysters. You know I would take a star away just because they won't tell me what's their seasoning is for the wings and oyster sauce. But it's okay, I understand they want to keep the masses coming back. The other dishes are great, although they can get spicy, but like I said the wings and oysters are the best. During their happy hour it's an even better deal!

Located right in NoHo my friend from NY recommend this spot. Also on of Chrissy Tiegens fav Thai spots. My friend and I shared some cocktails, grilled pork cheeks, zabb wings, coconut crab curry with a side of greens. This was plenty of food for 2 people. The craft cocktails were delicious. The pork cheeks were cooked and cut perfectly. The right amount of salt and each bite was packed with flavor. The zabb wings are a must order. They came out piping hot. The Thai chilis, lime and mint added some great flavor. The coconut crab curry is a must order if you love seafood and curry. Rich Southern style broth with a little heat. A fan favorite and the crab was plentiful. Fish cheeks is a really small location, but they do feature seats for large parties. Service here is great and the food comes out quickly. It's best to make reservations prior. If you want authentic Thai this is your place

Yummmm. Doesn't really get better than this.

Had three of the raw oysters- $1 each during happy hour. A little too much of the seawater taste to me but I enjoyed the toppings. 

The morning glory was delicious. Spiced well and fresh. Also had the steamed fish with herbs. I don't know what crack they put in the sauce but this stuff is so. good. The fish wasn't overcooked. I could order and eat four more bowls of rice just to get the sauce all in it. The pork cheek was tender with a mildly crispy exterior and the sauce on the side was so flavorful. 

It's different from most Thai places in the city and I would go back here again and again to try the whole menu and eat everything all over again once I've tried everything. 

My only qualm is that I wish the portions were a little bigger. Also, save yourself the wait time and make a reservation beforehand. Enjoy.

Thai food has never tasted any better. I am pretty basic when it comes to Thai food. I always get Pad Thai, but Fish Cheeks forces you to try something else since they don't offer Pad Thai and I am glad they did. We ordered the set of 3 and damn it was worth it. 

Food:  5/5: flavors on flavors topped with more flavors. The fish was delicious. The wings were scrumptious. The crab or lobster curry was yummy. The other curry with shrimp and vegetables was fantastic. The clams were okay. The pork was meh. We had to order more rice since the food is a little spicy and you cannot adjust the heat. 

NOTE: They don't adjust the heat/spice level which  is fine for me but more of a concern for my sister. She still enjoyed it but she used a lot more rice

Ambiance: 4/5: nice spot for a date or dinner with friends/family. 

Service: 2/5: our waiter was fine but when I asked the manager if they can make the food less spicy she (the manager) was quite rude and said "it's not spicy to me"......great well I am not asking you what you think, I am stating to you it is spicy. You can just say everything is prepared beforehand since it takes a long time to cook. My sister has a medical issue and cannot handle extremely spicy food. A simple sorry we cannot adjust the temperature would have sufficed. 

Price: 4/5: more or less reasonable for the quality and quantity of the food.

I will come back since it is one of the best Thai food spots I have been to.

We were here for the steamed fish. For some reason I found it hard to find a Thai restaurant in town that has steamed fish. After a few years I was luckily to find that on fish cheeks menu. They didn't disappointed me with a very fresh fish and really good seasoning. We almost ate everything including its flavorful fish soup. (Like a Bowl of Rice I think) the other dishes were really good too. We loved the crab coconut curry. I'd definitely recommend to order the oysters if you come at Happy Hour. They use different seasonings for oyster and I think it's really worth a try! The only fish that we weren't that happy with was the crab aob woonsen- we think it was too expensive compare to the amount of food we got- bowl mostly with glass noodle and little crab meat. But overall it was a great experience!!!

Make sure to make a reservation in advance because this place is no joke. I've never been here and seen an available table. 

The food is incredible. A friend from Thailand recommended this place as one of his top Thai spots in the city. Their wings are without a doubt the best wings and I would recommend dining early (5-7pm) in order to take part in their happy hour deals. The $1 oysters are the best because their additions to the oysters make them delicious. 

If you love spice, this is the place to go because they don't mess around. I completely underestimated the spice levels on their dishes. We tried the Somtum Corn Salad, refreshing with a kick, and the fan favorite, the Coconut Crab Curry. My friends and I were fighting over the last scoop of curry. Same thing with the last wing from the Zabb Wings order. We also split the Crab Aob Woonsen, which was obviously delicious and not too heavy as a noodle dish.

On top of the cozy ambiance and delicious food, the staff is always spectacular, speedy and helpful.

Fish Cheeks has been on my must-visit list for quite some time and I was finally able to venture out to try! 

The restaurant is medium-sized and from what I witnessed, very busy, so it would be a good idea to come with no more than a party of 5-6 and with a reservation made. It was the perfect marriage of traditional dishes and a trendy atmosphere. The servers were all very inviting and made sure we were satisfied throughout our meal.

The happy hour drinks we ordered were the Spicy Mango marg and the Thai Breaker. Both were very tasty cocktails but I'd have to say the Spicy Mango was the one to break the tie, having both a refreshing taste and zesty kick. Definitely stop by for their happy hour, which happens everyday 12-3:30 and 5-7 PM, and try for yourself, for only $10!

Every dish we ordered had a punch of sour tang that should be guaranteed when dining Thai: (There were 4 of us)

Po Tak ($25): This was a clear lemongrass seafood soup, containing pollock, shrimp, mussel, squid, oysters, mushrooms, and an array of spices. They did not skimp on taste or seafood!

Coconut Crab Curry ($24): The crab meat was both bountiful and tender and the curry had the perfect balance of pungency and sourness. I can definitely see why this is labeled as a fan favorite! (This dish comes with rice).

Manila clams ($24): Stir fried in a sweet basil sauce and chili jam, this dish was able to cater to both your savory and sweet cravings. A great dish amidst all of the sour!

Steamed fish ($35): So how could you come to Fish cheeks and not get a whole fish... They have other whole fish options (fried or grilled) but we opted for steamed and the meat was fall-off-the-bone tender. The refreshing cilantro lime broth it was swimming in was a refreshing balance alongside the Crab Curry and Manilla clams. 

Overall, my favorite dishes would be the coconut crab curry and the steamed fish. Fish cheeks is designed to enjoy family style, so bring your family, bring your friends, as I highly recommend this delicious restaurant!

This place was a gem. Found it via random search for Thai food (while in downtown Brooklyn), despite being located in the city we made the drive over.
No reservations were available online but when we arrived the wait was estimated to be 45mins. The bar also has a waitlist btw.

We ended up walking to the Bowery Hotel for drinks while we wait for the text that our table was ready.

The menu had quite a few tasty options but we narrowed it down to 2 Entrees and an Appetizer. 
Our waiter did let us know that Happy Hour was still in effect, so we ordered Oysters as well.

Oyster- It came with this fantastic spicy sauce and these small crunchy things. The oysters themselves were quite small. They were $1 each but the size was more like $0.50 each.

Coconut Crab Curry- This was a delicious. Slightly spicy and slightly sweet. Perfection.

Steamed Whole Bass- The sauce it came with was excellent, and not overpowering for the fish. Good amount of fish present. We ordered an extra side of rice because I don't think this came with rice.

Steamed cabbage- Not much vegetable options that i noted. Waitress said this was a popular item. I ate it pretty fast so I must have liked it. 

Coconut Ice cream- They only have 1 dessert apparently. By the time this came i was overly stuffed but yet I was able to devour 1 scoop. There were shavings of gelatinous coconut present. 

Overall I enjoyed my meal and was impressed. 
Make reservations to avoid the wait.

Very cute restaurant with delicious food. Not a huge overwhelming menu which I like. The staff is very friendly. This restaurant is quiet enough to have a conversation. Bathroom is big and clean. Can't say one bad thing. I will happily return.

This is one of those places that thinks being trendy means dimming the lights, making the tables really close together and raising the prices on small portions.

We ordered the coconut crab curry, khua kling, manila clams and steamed fish. There's no doubt that the food was really delicious but one can't help but imagine that this wasn't the most authentic Thai food one's ever had. We were warned that the khua kling was the spiciest item on the menu, but it wasn't bad at all. For many dishes, the rice came separate.

Overall, it was a nice dinner but not necessarily an establishment that was a must-try.
Ate here.  Loved it!  All the flavors are so tasty. My favorite dish was the fish. It was sooooo good.

Easily of the top 3 Thai restaurants in the city on my list. No wonder the hype is here. My party and I arrived without any reservations and there was an hour wait for walk-ins at 5 P.M. Luckily we still had time to take advantage of the happy hour deals until 7. 

For happy hour, we took advantage of their $1 oysters. They tasted extremely fresh, thoroughly cleansed and paired really well with the fried shallots and the nam jim seafood sauce. We also had an order of the Zabb wings (5/5) which had a delicious concoction of spicy and citrusy flavors. 

The coconut crab curry was easily my favorite (5/5). The sweet coconut milk aroma immediately hit me as soon as the dish was laid down on the table. They also didn't skimp out on the crab meat as there was a lot buried underneath all the delicious curry. The crab fried rice (4.5/5) also had a decent amount of crab meat. 

The tiger prawn karee was also really mouth-watering. There were 3 tiger prawns the size of a grown man's palm. This came submerged in a stir fry curry powder sauce with scrambled egg, onions and chilis. I enjoy sucking the curry out from the prawns and especially from the head. The sauce from this dish and the curry from the coconut crab both went extremely well with jasmine rice. We even ordered extra bowls of rice to soak up the excess curry so none of it went to waste. 

We later ended up ordering the grilled pork cheeks (4/5) because we didn't want to miss out on it and regret not ordering it. The pork cheeks come marinated in fish sauce and served with Jeaw dipping sauce. It tasted smokey and reminded me of Chinese cha siu. 

Overall, my party and I enjoyed our first visit here at Fish Cheeks. The servers were really nice and the food was beyond phenomenal. I can't wait to come back in the near future to try out their other offerings. I especially look forward to trying out their coconut ice cream since there are raving reviews about it.
Fish cheeks. Your food is amazing, but did you really charge me $24 for this much curry? SMH.

I rarely find a restaurant to be as good as the hype, but Fish Cheeks is it! A Thai restaurant with unique, fresh, seafood offerings for those who want to go beyond the typical pad Thai fare (which FYI is not even on the menu).  Larger dishes are meant for family style sharing, although in general, the portions run on the small side. Everything we ordered was delicious- corn salad, pomelo salad, fried fish, steamed fish, crab curry.  It is a restaurant that truly brings something new to the table with its use of seafood in unexpected combos (ex. Pomelo and fried fish). Prices can get to be on the higher side (we spent about $40-50/person), but we're a family that eats large portions and the price was worth it!

Based on my personal rating system at the bottom, would have to give this place 4 instead of a 5, but it was pretty close.

Have had this place recommended by a couple of people, one of whom said it was the best Thai place he's ever eaten at.  It's not a typical Thai place - you won't see the typical noodle dishes you'd see from your down the street Thai restaurant in nyc.  

Came for happy hour - got their $1 oysters and $5 Leo beer from their menu.  Nice to see a pricey restaurant still offer happy hour deals.  Though like any other appetizer, basically a secret way to add to your total bill, but I digress.  Oysters were decent and kind of unique - they give you the spicy lemony chili Thai sauce as well as mini fried shrimp as toppings.

Had the Fried Fish (Raindbow Trout) $35 and Crab Ao Wonsan (glass noodles with crab) $24.   We're used to see red snapper at Thai places like wondee Siam, so was interested to see how the trout would be fried in this style; it was pretty good, pleasantly surprised, meat juicy.  The accompanying chili sauce was also very good.  One critique - would be nice if rice would come complementary with the fish; we asked for a side, we knew it would cost extra ($3) which we were okay with, but still.  At $35 a fish plate, I think a bowl of rice could come free with it.

It kind of hurt knowing we were paying $24 for glass noodles which we could get at say Ktown for only $6.  It was very good, had a unique saucey taste to it, might be one of the best glass noodles I've ever had, but is it worth that much more?

I can see why this place is popular, especially amongst celebrities.  Although I think the food is very very good, don't know if it's so much better than other very good Thai places (Wondee Siam, Pure Thai Cookhouse, Top Thai) to justify paying ~50% more the price for.  Definitely worth a try once, just don't know if I can afford the place on my budget to frequent it regularly.


FYI here is my yelp rating system

5=worth a trip, something you'll crave
4=worth getting if you're already in the area
3=only worth it if it's free/discounted, not worth paying full price
2=would not even eat it if free, waste of stomach space
1=the place should shut down

Overall,The service is fast and welcoming,The food is absolutely delicious.and ambiance is great and spectacular.
I got the corn salad.It was very refreshing and tasty.l had coconut crab curry.lt was quite spicy but l loved it very much.highly recommend if you like to have a great time.

One of the best meals I've ever had in New York City! The staff make you feel like family, the space is colorful yet tasteful, and the food and drinks are simply delectable. Plus, they have a stellar happy hour till 7pm with $1 oysters and $10 cocktails (on top of discounted wine and beer). 

This spot is a popular one so be sure to make a reservation! We booked a day in advance for 3 people and there was just a 5pm and 9pm spot left. 

What we got: 
- Thai Breaker cocktail: might I say this was one of the best cocktails I've ever had?! It included Thai tea and coconut and all the ingredients were mixed perfectful. 
- $1 oysters: standard and delicious. 
- Pork cheek: so flavorful and juicy. 
- Wings: tasty, spicy, and crispy. Out of all the items we got, this one we probably could've done without since our order was more than enough despite them being yummy. 
- Pomelo salad: really refreshing and light! 
- Pukboong fai dang (spinach): One of my favorite dishes! Possessed a ton of flavor and made me want to keep eating greens! 
- Glass noodles dish: My favorite dish of the night (could've had the entire thing to myself). The noodles were so flavorful and the crab was meaty and cooked perfectly. 
- Curry fish in banana leaf: Flavor was ok, but slightly too spicy for our group. 
- Coconut ice cream: UNREAL. So much coconut and the soft serve just melted in my mouth. Perfectly creamy. 

Can't recommend this spot enough.

A very popular spot for happy hour, make sure you get reservations cause this place is poppin.

Oysters for a buck each? Hell yes. And not to mention the toppings they give you of seafood sauce and deep fried shallots are top tier. The shallots provide a nice crunchy texture and the sauce is spicy and citrusy, both compliment the oysters very well. 

Drinks were also top notch, the thai breaker is a really interesting bourbon drink with thai tea and pineapple juice, highly recommend.

We got the got the khua kling and the crab ao woonsen. The khua kling was actually pretty hot, and it was spiced pretty well there was alot going on in that dish.

The happy hour deal and the quality of this place is so fantastic and will have me returning again.
Their coconut crab curry is legit. I always expect some waiting time here. but it is worth it. And people I bring here always loved the food. It's a cute date place too.

This is not your typical Thai restaurant with pad thai/drunken noodles dishes but there are unique dishes that are definitely worth trying. I've been here a few times for dinner and absolutely love this place. 

Oysters are $1 each during happy hour and tastes much better with the green sauce and fried shallots. 

Coconut crab curry is probably the best dish on the menu but beware it is quite spicy. The dish did not look very impressive but there is generous amount of crab meat. 

Crab woonseen is relatively small but noodles really soak up the flavor for the dish and is a great non-spicy option alternative on the menu. The portion size for this is pretty small and probably would not have this as a sharing dish. 

Overall, Fish Cheeks is very unique and different from most Thai restaurants with a variety of different flavor profiles. The service was also great and I cannot wait to come back!

Fish cheeks is one of my favorite restaurant right away.The service was great.Awesome food especially pork cheeks it was tender and yummm also the cocktail,spicy mango,was excellent.highly recommended  :))

Fish cheeks is a nice spot to dine but get crowded very fast.any way l waited about 20 minutes after that l was seated by the prompt hostess.l started with pork cheeks.lt was well roasted and very delicious.Then l ordered crab curry Wow!!it  was valuable dish.can't wait to come back.

I went to fish Cheeks for dinner with my friends.we both started with the cocktails- spicy mango It was very refreshing.The great balance;not too sweet and not too strong but just sufficient liquor that lt creeps up on you.Then we had the crab aob woonsen.lt smelled very good and also tasted so tender and delicious.another dish that we got was steamed fish.lt was very fantastic.pretty recommended.

Fish Cheeks brings thai food up to another level with it's seafood specialty. Reservations are a must or else you'd be waiting hours just to get a table at this busy and oh so popular location. I recommend coming with at least 3-4 people so that you are guaranteed to try at least 3-4 dishes, because why not! 

I would absolutely recommend getting the coconut crab curry. They don't skimp on the crab and the curry sauce is fantastic over rice. Make sure you do order bowls of rice for the table to soak up all that goodness. The manilla clams were also great, although the portions are a little bit on the smaller size. They offer a whole steamed fish that comes very aesthetically pleasing in its fish shaped dish and I would also recommend this because it just tastes so hearty. Lastly, we ordered their Po Tak lemongrass soup. If you're a fan of something similar to sweet and sour soup, then this will be right down your alley. It's filled with plenty of seafood and super comforting to consume. 

Moving on to drinks, my friends ordered the spicy mango while I had the Thai Breaker. If you're a fan of something more fruity, I would recommend the mango because you can't really taste the alcohol so it's dangerous yet delicious. If you're into a stronger drink, you'd definitely be able to taste the bourbon in the Thai Breaker, it's not bad, but I enjoyed my friends drink more! 

Overall, I honestly don't think you can go wrong with anything that you order here. Fish Cheeks is designed to be eaten family style, so make sure you come with good company!

Saturday night 9 pm.Walked in and no hostess for 10-15 min.  When we walked in there were already 2 empty tables. During our wait for the hostess two more tables got empty. Anyway. There was a group of 3 and a pick up in front of us. When the first group asked the hostess for a table of 3 she said she had none and when they asked her if they could squeeze into a table for two she said that it's not possible unless they were a group of two. First group left. When it was our turn I asked her for a table of two and she said she didn't had anything and it would be 1 hour wait. When I pointed out 4 empty tables she said they were for people who had reservations. Maybe she thought I didn't heard the conversation with the previous  group because the place was pretty loud. Long story short, make a reservation before you come otherwise they will lie to your face.

Such a great period time at fish cheeks.My wife tried to persuade me to have Thai food several time  and l decided to get some at this place.So we started with the pork cheeks.lt was very tasty.Then we got the coconut crab curry and steamed fish .Both tasted delicious.will come back to try something different.

This place definitely changes my prejudice against Thai food in NYC!! I love Thai food for its exuberant spices and flavors, but always all Thai places I visited never made truly spicy Thai dishes and replaced the spices with SALT. But omg, Fish Cheeks was so different! Everything I ordered took me straight to heaven.

We as a party of 5 came at 2:30pm for lunch the day after Thanksgiving and the restaurant was packed. Luckily, we reserved a spot through Resy (I initially only did it for the formality- I didn't expect this place to be so busy at lunch). This is a cute little restaurant in NoHo with awesome lunch deals! Maybe that's why people were here for, so definitely reserve your table before coming here. 
 We ordered 15 oysters, which was only $1 each. The oysters were so fresh and were served with fried shallots and the special green Thai sauce. I love the green chilli dipping sauce but I never had it with oyster. This was so ingenious! We had the grilled pork cheeks for starter and it was another stellar dish. The pork cheek had a perfect balance of lean and fatty meat, grilled to imperfection, and coated with a sweet honey layer. The dip for this one was also excellent!! Fish Cheeks really nailed it with their dips. 

For the mains, we had the famous coconut crab curry, Tiger Prawn Karee, and Potak. Everything was damn delicious. I can't believe I was obsessed with everything we ordered. The coconut crab curry didn't look aesthetic on photos but the taste made up for it! Incredible curry soup, generous chunks of crab meat. It was kinda spicy but I couldn't stop getting more rice to eat with the curry alone. So flavorful and unique! The Potak was a sour seafood soup with squids, fish, and prawns. It's a hearty addition to the dryer dishes we had. I also loved it. Last but not least, we had the prawn karee as recommended by the staff here. It's stir -fry shrimp with scrambled egg. The tiger prawn was huge and fresh, but I loved the sauce even more. The scrambled egg sauce was so tasty! It had so many flavors to it: curry powder, coconut, chili. I could order this one separately to eat with rice if they had it. 

I almost forgot, their Thai tea was bomb as well! I intended not to order it since I want to remove lactose from my diet, but I saw my friends' and I knew I had to have it. The Thai milk tea was beautiful, only lightly sweetened, very creamy, and served in large portion! It's worth the price! 

I will always come back to this place since it's so close to school. The price is higher than other Thai restaurants but FishCheek focuses on seafood, which generally costs more than other meats anyway. For the quality in ingredients and amazing flavors, it's worth paying a little more.Definitely come at lunch to take advantage of their amazing $1 oyster lunch deal.

Such a great period time at fish cheeks.My wife tried to persuade me to have Thai food several time  and l decided to get some at this place.So we started with the pork cheeks.lt was very tasty.Then we got the coconut crab curry and steamed fish .Both tasted delicious.will come back to try something different.
Love this place.we went there last night.Food was extremely delicious especially coconut crab curry and crab aob woonsen.highly recommended.

Not your typical Thai food here. It's 1 of the few Thai restaurants that do not have Pad Thai on the menu. But going in knowing this, it's got to be unique.

The best dish on the menu is the coconut crab curry. I don't have a photo of it because it was basically demolished once it hit the table. I put it over both the fried rice and white rice, it's pretty spicy, yet undeniably delicious. The curry is very smooth and tasty, but could use a little more crab meat. I'd order this every time if I was prepared to sweat a little each time I eat it. 

The crab fried rice is a great plate to share with someone and can be enough for 1 person with a big appetite. It's totally worth it and has a lot of crab meat mixed in. 

The manilla clams were delicious, but it's on the smaller side of dishes. It could almost be mistaken for an appetizer. Overall it had an awesome flavor from the chili jam, just needed a bigger portion of everything.

The Crab Woonsen is about the same size and hence has the same portion size issue as the clams. The pork belly gave the dish a nice touch of flavor, otherwise it wouldn't have had that much flavor aside from the cilantro root. There defnitely could have been a ton more glass noodles and crab meat. This dish I would not consider it to be sharable. 

Overall, Fish Cheeks makes your mouth water with unique flavor profiles and curry dishes that have true Thai inspiration. Make time to visit, but be careful which dishes you order. Otherwise you'll end up ordering a few more than you originally estimated.
Fish Cheeks is probably the best Thai restaurant in NYC.Colorful decor,nice ambiance and Food was fantastic especially steamed fish lt was soft and juicy.ln addition don't miss coconut ice-cream!!yum

Pretty love this spot.The service was so prompt and professional.
Food - pork cheeks was so tender. 
            - Zaab wing was crispy and tasty.
             - coconut crab curry was creamy and yummy. 
Definitely coming back.
The First time here l have to say"lt is really pretty good spot" l had the pork cheeks and crab meat fried rice as the same time.lt was very delicious.will come back for try something different.

I went to Fish Cheeks around 7:30 pm without a reservation. The wait was around 2 hours for a party of 2.

The restaurant is quite small and they really pack you in - to get into our seat we had to move our table and move extremely cautiously to not numb items on our neighbor's table.

We ordered the coconut crab curry and glass noodles with crab. The coconut crab curry was incredible and would highly recommend. The Glass noodles were also good but definitely need to side sauce they give you. We tried without at first and both thought they were a bit bland. Food comes out very quickly (within 15 minutes) after you order.

Overall, would recommend but expect a wait if you go without a reservation. If you prefer not being close to other parties around you, maybe not a great place as it is nearly unavoidable.

Let the fabulous time flow at Fish cheeks.l went there together with my coworkers.we ordered pork cheeks and coconut crab curry.Both taste very yummy.The stuff was very friendly and hospitality.definitely come back.

Definitely in my top 3 favorite spots in NYC,Fish Cheeks is likely to do everything right now.The food was fantastic.l got the sliced pork cheeks OMG!! It was tender and very tasty.also l had the steamed fish.lt was awesome.l was so sad.l didn't have any room for coconut ice cream.so l will come back for sure.

The food is incredible. I love it. Nice decoration.
Fish is the best here it is the new way for Thai food. Very good reputation. And the drink is so good. Last thing is the service that I have to say. You deserved 5 stars from me. Everyone so nice and friendly. I am so impressed and will be back for sure.

I heard a lot of good things here, tom yum koong, and seafood . The reason why im here because i love seafood dishes and the seafood sauce.
I had a whole fish on top with sauce ( spicy) which is super incredible tatse. The stuff are friendly and professional . The bar is so cozy. I spoke with a bartender,, he had a lot of knowledge. I love it.
I will surely go back to support this restaurant .

A cute place in a very hip neighborhood but way overpriced ($70 lunch for 2 people with no alcohol ?!). Have you not heard of a lunch menu? Service was rough and indifferent AND their Health Dept "C" rating poster was not displayed anywhere. But my fish soup was amazingly tasty. Beware.
Fabulous food and good date atmosphere! This place is always popping and popular so be sure to make a reservation! The steam fish and the coconut curry are absolutely amazing, def recommend!

This is hands down one of the best dinning experiences. Sunday night, no line, empty enough to pay more attention to the details...
GET THE CRAB CURRY...the truth...
Say no more, go out if you're up for a flavorful experience I highly recommend this place.

A bit pricey if your get drinks so wallet gear up.

I was so sad when Pok Pok in Brooklyn closed. There goes my favorite Thai restaurant in the city. Then along comes fish cheeks. Their food is delicious!! Although they do focus more on seafood, which is also a plus.

My favorite things were the pomelo salad. It's amazing and light, seasoned with herbs and crunch onions and garlic bits. It's such a refreshing dish and perfect light appetizer. The fried fish, wish is their most popular dish, is my favorite thing. It's crispy and crunch but not oily. The fish sauce topping sauce is wonderful and goes so well the fish. I enjoyed it immensely and strong suggest you try it as well! The Crab Aob Woosen is my second favorite entree. Although I wish they gave you more portions cus I could it eat it all in 3 bites. The favors is full but not overpowering. I was not a huge fan of the crab curry, it wish the curry itself was thick and less liquid-y. 

Overall my experience was incredible. I definitely recommend it to thai and seafood lovers. Just make sure you make a reservation on resy! It was a 2 hr wait on a Friday night!

I heard a lot about this restaurant. All the review are good. My friend are the regulars customer here. they love the food and service. I just heard about it until today.
Yeah!!! Finally I'm here. First I had a tumyum koong soup is so good. and I ordered classic cocktails I had old fashioned my husband ordered martini ... wow so good . We came here because we have heard a lot about fish that so fresh... I expirinced a nice service from here very impressed. Now I'm looking to find the restaurant to have a small party to my family birthday. This is gonna the best thanksgiving party for my family this year.

Mainly here is the seafood.... The fish is so good no no I must say super good haha... I had a seafood sauce with fish .. My favorite is tomyum , crispy whole fish with seafood sauce..I am actually bring all friend to party here, they said wow the taste is so similar from thailand... I am so glad that my friend love this restaurant. We opened 2 bottles of white wine .. Cant you imagine how good it was!!! spicy thai seafood + white wine.... Cant say no
More... Next time will bring my boyfriend who loves spicy food and im sure He will love it.

What a good thing in soho--- finally i found out the best thai resturant with all fresh seafood in the heart of city. Whole fish was sooo good . When i ask for seafood sauce , cant ask for more ,,, TWICE that i asked, i know is a little bit too much but cant help... it was soooo good ... all stuffs hostess bartender and server are all friendly .Next time I will try to sitting at the bar. I feel like cozy spot to sit down. Love the vibes . Recommend for dating or party stuffs ... love the song too .... fun!!!

Long wait but delicious food. Almost every dish we ordered was spicy. Be sure that you're able to handle spiciness before coming here. Most of the tables are reservations only but they allow walk ins so chances are you will be seated at the bar. Walk in wait was about 2 hours for a party of 3 on a Friday night. Staff was all very polite and attentive even when the restaurant was very busy. Not much seating for groups because the seatings are very close together. Also, I like to admire how the food comes out and see all the colors on the dishes. Kinda wish it was a bit brighter in the restaurant because it was too dim to see my food.

We ordered:
Zaab wings
Oysters
Grilled Branzino
Coconut crab curry
Manila Clams

My favorite dish was the grilled branzino. It was wrapped in curried banana leaf. Mostly deboned but there were a bit of bones and scale in it when I had it. The zaab wings was crispy, juicy, lemony and spicy all at the same time. One of our favs. Overall the flavors of every dish was very pretty authentic and close to what I had in Thailand.

Finally got a chance to come here and eat.  We sat down right away and was greeted by the friendly hostess.  space is cozy but has that nice open kitchen feeling. Ordered  the guava smash cocktail and the mango sticky rice cocktail.  Both drinks were refreshing and you can taste the fresh basil in the guava smash.  

we ordered the fried  chicken , branzino, pakboong fai dang and i have to be honest here; ive been to a lot of Thai restaurants in NyC and this place tastes like home.  the sauces that accompanies each dish is Thai authentic.  come here and you will eat like you were in Thailand.  definitely coming back to try the rest of the menu.

Food was tasty but disappointed that they've downsized their portions!  We also had to wait a really long time and eventually was told they kicked a table out to seat us (but we were never given anything for the wait).  We ordered their famous coconut crab curry, which had so little crab meat in it - I've been here and ordered this dish before and it had SO much more crab meat so I am disappointed they're downsizing (presumably to save ingredient costs).

What an absolute delight... Brace yourselffor a fantastic flavorful and spicy treat.. the taste of which will linger for days to come.

I can't think of one flaw in everything we ordered (except maybe some dishes were priced a bit on the higher side).

We had an hour long wait (almost an hour) the host was very helpful and courteous so it was an easy wait. 
First of all I loved my cocktail- Gin with coconut water and black flower pea tea. You know bar tender knows his/ her  job well when they can make a gin based cocktail enjoyable.

Now let's start with the food. Warning: be ready to experience hightened level of spices and burst of multiple flavors in your mouth, all at once.

Coconut crab curry was my favorite, the soft crab meat with spicy curry (mellowed down and thickened with coconut milk). The flavor and aroma was enough to send you into a food coma. Don't forget to order a side of steamed rice with it. 

Po Tak soup was filled with cilantro and sea food (shrimps, calamari, fish etc).The warm tangy soup was delicious, a true savior on this cold winter night. 

Beef sirloin was the spiciest dish on the menu, loved the juicy beef with flavors oozing out of every bite.

Oh I cannot not mention the dessert of the day: it was coconut ice cream with coconut flakes and papaya. Let me risk it by saying perhaps it's the best Ice cream dessert I have had in a long long time. It was difficult to put my spoon down. 

Last but not the least their restroom was very well maintained; clean and fresh. And that is why this place qualifies for five stars.

Excellent  food, good ambience, warm staff, innovative cocktails and well maintained rest room. 
Surely recommended.

This is hands down my favorite Thai restaurant -- in NYC. We ordered the Set 2 menu to share which included: 1) the chicken wings 2) corn salad 3) fried fish 4) crab curry 5) clams. This is a lot of food for 2 people so come hungry, it's worth the price. 

We enjoyed all of the dishes except for the corn salad which was mediocre. The curry, clams and fish were packed with flavor! The chicken wings are good, but the fish dishes were the true stars of our meal. 

I would have given it 5 stars, but it took a very long time for snacks part of the set to come out and our waiter wasn't the most attentive. Maybe 45 min until we received the snacks. We still will come back though as the food is definitely worth the wait!
Went there during happy hour and oyster was only 1$ each! Had a dozen oysters, spicy mango cocktail and fried noodles and all of them were YUMMY! Will definitely go back again

Fish Cheeks kept popping up on my "Suggested places to eat" on Yelp and I am ETERNALLY grateful Yelp has figured out the correct algorithm to lead me to Fish Cheeks and/or have Fish Cheeks's ads keep pushing its way through Yelp because I am l i v i n g for this restaurant. 

My fiancé and I came here on a Saturday around 12PM. We had reserved for 2 to eat here, but because we came during opening hours, I don't think it would have been necessary per se. However, if you come even 20 minutes later than the opening time, you'll be waiting outside the restaurant, enviously watching other happy customers devour delicious and homey Thai food. 

To kickstart our feast, we started off with the oysters. Happy hour goes on from 12 PM-3:30PM and 5-7PM, so dollar oysters hit all around our table. There is only 1 type of oysters, but they are flavored very well. Crunchy onion pieces garnishing the oyster as well as a lime/citrusy flavor that smacks your palate immediately once you gulp your oyster down. We ordered 4 in the beginning and loved them so much, we closed our feast with yet another 4 oysters. 

My entree ended up being the grilled pork cheeks with fish sauce on the side. Pretty self-explanatory, pretty simple, pretty much a classic. Our table was blessed with a mountain of pork chops that were unobnoxiously fatty. Tender, savory, and delicious. Eating this with white rice will help neutralize this heavily umami-like dish (or just take it all in). It's technically a "shared plate"/appetizer but I think it can be large enough to be an entree.

My fiancé's entree was the coconut crab curry. If you're a fan of curry, you will LOVE this dish. If you're not - doesn't matter. I'm not usually a fan of curry, but this dish has converted me to one! Fish Cheeks rates their food from 0 - 3 peppers indicating spiciness level. This has 2 peppers, so it's pretty spicy. It will definitely make a lot of people sweat up a storm, but the heat is worth it! Excellently creamy and plentiful in crab, this was such a joy to eat. Also eaten with rice to help neutralize the spiciness, but if you live for the spicy thrill, eat it without rice. 

Fish Cheeks is one of the best Thai restaurants I have ever tried! Eating here was a wonderful experience and even just remembering the food brings both a smile to my face and some drool out of my mouth. This place is a MUST.

This place is amazing! Almost every single dish was phenomenal. While it is a little pricey, the food is worth the price. As an appetizer they served us some air popped chips to start and a sauce (I forget the name but SO GOOD). We ordered the pork cheeks as a starter and my friend was a huge fan of these. I am not a huge meat eater and found them a little "meaty" for my liking, but personal preference. For our entree we got the crab curry which was PHENOMENAL amazing spice content, rich, creamy, served with white rice - PERFECT for a cold dat. Along with our entree we added the Pak Boong Fai Dang, and WOW it was amazing - garlicky, some spice, really hit the spot with the curry. I ordered the Limeaid as my beverage, it was sour and not sweet at all - exactly what I wanted. My friend ordered the butterfly effect cocktail which he thought was a bit too tarte and strong for him, but the waiter was nice enough to switch it for the spicy mango drink - which was amazing.

This place is busy and a bit tough to get a table if you don't get there right when they open (which we did) or have a reservation for later in the night. We got there at 5 on the dot and got seated. Happy hour from 5-7 was great and the $10 cocktails were delicious- as was everything else on this menu that we tried. We opted for the $105 (total) tasting menu (called Set 1) for 2 people and it was PLENTY of food for 2. This seems like the best deal as the food is mostly for sharing and prices ranges from $10-$30 for each dish. We also got 3 oysters to start and wish we got more. The crab fried rice was literally the fluffiest rice I have ever tasted. The grapefruit salad in the beginning seems like an odd dish, but completely works. There was also a pork loin dish, a noodle dish with crab, and a spicy soup. Everything was to share and I could not recommend this place more. To note despite being busy, our server was really nice and attentive.

I wanted to come here for my birthday and needed to make a reservation for 5. It was a little bit of an ordeal. They emailed me a credit card authorization form that I had to fill out and send back. But otherwise the food is great! My favorite was the spicy beef and the fried fish. The beef was so spicy but I couldn't help myself and kept eating it. The drinks are a little weak and not worth it.

Unbelievably delicious food. Like... HOW is this possible!?

Some tips: check out their happy hour times and make a reservation. If it's your first time, consider checking out the "sets" that the chef has put together to get the full experience. The price is for the set, not per person! We did the set 1.

*Oysters (3/5): a little too spicy and covered up the oyster too much
*Grilled pork cheeks (5/5): tender and juicy pork with a spicy tangy sauce
*Pomelo salad (5/5): the perfect fresh plate we needed to prep ourselves for the meal to come. it was tart, spicy, and oh so good.
*Po Tak (5/5): holy moly - SO good. also, so spicy. but so many layers of flavor
*Crab fried rice (5/5): fantastic, soft, delicious fried rice with chunks of crab
*Crab aob woonsen (2/5): a letdown after everything else - it was pretty mediocre. Just some sweet salty glass noodles with a few chunks of crab and pork belly. not the best dish!

Overall this was the best thai food I've consumed and I can't wait to return everytime I'm in NYC!

I'm the type of person who has 100 restaurants on their "to try" list and refuses to go back to a restaurant because I want to keep checking off new ones. But I can confidently say I can't wait to go back to Fish Cheeks! The interior is cute and colorful and they have a fun variety of cocktails. Mostly spins on classics if i remember correctly but still delicious!

Food-wise, we got pork cheeks, the steamed fish, happy hour oysters (we came at 5:30), coconut crab curry, and chicken wings split between 4 people and it was the perfect amount. We had room for the coconut ice cream dessert which was fantastic as well! Food was presented beautifully although I failed to take any because i was so excited to dig in :)

This was by far the best meal we had in New York. We were lucky enough to walk in without a reservation and got seated right away around 6pm on a Thursday. The service was really friendly and our server was knowledgable and gave excellent suggestions. We knew they had to turn the table so we ordered quickly and the food and drinks came out right away. Drinks were EXCELLENT! I had the Cheeky Green and my husband had the Thai Old Fashioned. Food was unreal, Pork Cheeks!!! Outrageously good, the corn salad, crab sob woonsen and beef tartar were also amazing. The pork cheeks and crab were our favorites tho. For dessert the coconut ice cream was delicious - creamy and so so rich. We loved every bit of our experience and can't wait to come back!

HAPPY HOUR until 7pm?!! $1 OYSTERS?!?! DISCOUNT COCKTAILS?!! Sign me up please! 

Came here at exactly 5:30pm, without reservations, and was seated immediately. The crowd started picking up shortly after, so I felt like I hit the jackpot getting a table for two without a wait. (Thank you Restaurant Gods!!) We had Corey as our waiter, and he was the best! He knew everything about the menu, and gave us a lot of helpful suggestions based on our spice preferences. He was super attentive, and I loved his positive attitude. We were made aware they had a table with reservations for 7:30pm, but they did not rush us at all, and I really appreciate restaurants like Fish Cheeks, whose staff are so sophisticated and organized at time managing that they make every customer feel taken care of and ensure they all leave with a great dining experience. 

In terms of food, we ordered oysters during happy hour, and a few drinks. I had the "Drunk in Love" which had rose sangria, watermelon juice, and ginger essence. It came with a candied orange slice, and the drink itself tasted like a subtle lychee martini. I enjoyed the drink a lot, but if you're someone who prefers their drink slightly on the stronger side, I wouldn't recommend this. For our appetizers we ordered their Zabb Wings, and Grilled Pork Cheeks. I really enjoyed the Pork Cheeks, but it kind of reminded me of a chewier version of "char siu" (bbq pork in Chinese). I liked it because of its chewy texture, however I couldn't justify spending $15 for the small portion, however it is something I am glad I got to try despite the price for the portion! The Zabb Wings were a miss for me. The order comes with four pieces of fried chicken wings coated with chili, lime and mint. It is a dry rub, and I found it to be quite salty and very spicy. I believe it was meant to be sweet and savory at the same time, but I found it more on the saltier side. I would definitely pass on this next time. 

For our main dishes we ordered the Coconut Crab Curry, as well as the Tiger Prawn Karee. The Coconut Crab Curry is a fan favorite, but also on a spice level of two chili peppers, so people watch out if you can't handle spice (or have thai iced tea ready for you, and tissue ready for your tears/runny nose). I had a bite from my friend, who ordered the Coconut Crab Curry and I couldn't handle. Don't get me wrong, the crab curry was pretty flavorful, but then the spice kicked me in the face, and I was downing water for the next 5 minutes, so I decided to focus on the Tiger Prawn Karee, which I LOVED. The dish goes very well with rice, and I am actually quite surprised this dish doesn't come with rice on its own since it costs $27. I had to order a side of rice for an extra $3, unfortunately, but I'll have to admit it was worth it! This dish had no spice level, and ate with a very well balanced sweet and savory note. Overall, I had a great experience at Fish Cheeks, and I can't wait to come back and try the rest of the menu! I would have to admit they are slightly on the more expensive side for Thai food, but it is definitely worth every penny.

This is a great place because of all the factors combined - it's in a great location, interiors are uplifting, food is fresh and very tasty.

You'll often find a crowd outside waiting - I went here on a hot summer day, late lunch/early dinner time. I like eating at this time in general in NY so you can avoid lines/crowds/etc.

Atmosphere: it'll always feel like a hip seaside Thai town, I just love the decor. Simple and sweet and non-pretentious.

Food: we had a myriad of seafood options, I can't even begin to name, but they were all fresh. The steamed fish was the highlight and came in an appetizing display - perched high on a dish, soaked in sauce. 

From an authenticity standpoint, don't expect dense Thai flavor - there are other places for that kick in the face tongue jerking kind of Thai although you can make anything spicy here if you want to induce sweat pellets. 

This was a delightful meal.

I have been many thai restaurants in New York but i would said this is the hidden gem restaurant. First there is no PadThai!! I was lil bit upset because this is Thai restaurant. Well i open my mind to try something eles. I had Crab curry which is to die for. And Oyster are so fresh and ofcause happy hour for those. I would recommend for who want to get new experience in Thai restaurant. I would come back again.
I don't even like chicken wings and I couldn't get enough of these. The curry was incredible, great service, fun atmosphere, will be back.

The food here is soo flavorful, expensive but tasty. I love the clean minimalist decor has a Japanese feel to it. It was difficult to get a reservation 2 days in advance but i managed to get a 5pm table. We got some complimentary prawn crackers to start. My friend and I ordered the coconut crab curry.
I was under the impression that this was soup but it was a sauce that went amazing with the rice. I would def recommend this especially if you're ordering any kind of meat- it will compliment the meat really well. We also ordered the branzino ($35) I thought this was too pricey but it was super tender, the portion was just enough for too. The sauce that came on top of it was super spicy and savory- go for this if you like spice but I wish I got the sauce on the side as it was slathered in sauce( for a good reason though).
We decided to balance it with a vegetable dish and opted for the pakboon fai dang. It just went well with our meal- has a seaweed kind of texture.  My friend got the king prawn to go and claimed it was the best out of the things we ordered but I did not get to try it. 

They only have one item on the dessert menu (coconut ice-cream)which I hope changes in the future. I will definitely be back!

Fish Cheeks serves delicious, seafood-forward Thai food!

Crab, fish, and shrimp are heavily featured on the menu. We started with the grilled pork cheeks which had great flavor and a tender but chewy texture. We split the coconut crab curry and tiger prawn karee after. The coconut crab curry is spicy and smooth - almost like a bisque with chunks of crab in it. Very good, but not as good as the tiger prawn karee. The prawns were large and the flavor packed a punch. Fish Cheeks also has happy hour every day featuring $1 oysters! 

Definitely one of the best Thai places in Manhattan. It's fun and casual, and great for groups. Can't wait to come back and try more of the menu!

This was my second time and last night took friends for their first time, and Fish Cheeks never disappoints. The food and staff are amazing.

Chris our waiter was attentive and informative on the menu. Coming from a customer service industry I thought it right to acknowledge great customer service.

My friends were still talking about the food the next day. Zabb wings,$1 oysters, and crab curry a must. Trust me when I say, I will recommend your restaurant to my friends and family.

Thanks again for an enjoyable night until the next time!!!!

This place is pretty awesome. Been for lunch and two dinners. I don't eat a lot of rice, but the crab-fried rice was awesome. Steamed fish was awesome. The pork cheeps were the favorite. Cocktails were so-so, nothing too amazing, but I'm not expecting special cocktails at a Thai restaurant.

My first meal was with two others, and we ordered a lot: multiple sides, mains, and each had a cocktail. With a good tip I paid $240, and we had left-overs to enjoy for lunch the next day.

Oh my god. So good. So so so good. My favorite Thai spot in the city for sure! 

Came here and luckily snagged two spots at the bar. This place gets crowded and even though I had to dine at the bar it was so worth it. Their happy hour is quite fantastic, cocktails are amazing and the $1 oysters are served with two amazing sauces that make it so very special. My boyfriend and I ate two dozen and honestly we wanted to order more but we had to apply some self control and stop ourselves. 

Since we sat at the bar, our bartender was our server and she was so awesome. I didn't get her name but she was very helpful with explaining the cocktail menu to me. She was busy making drinks and taking orders the entire time I was there but still managed to be so sweet and lovely to everyone. I ended up trying Drunk In Love and the Spicy mango (yes I know two cocktails just for myself!!) and they were both fantastic. The lovely bartender even omitted the spicy part of the rim for me and I highly appreciate her accommodating to my taste buds. In terms of food we got the prawn karee and grilled Branzino. Both fantastic but I highly highly recommend the prawn karee and maybe a few extra bowls of rice- My boyfriend and I definitely wiped that plate clean of the delicious sauce! 

Just writing this review makes me miss my meal there, I cannot wait for my next visit here!

This restaurant is fantastic and I only wish it weren't so hard to get a reservation! It's upscale, modern Thai food with a heavy seafood/fish emphasis (hence the name). I shared a bunch of dishes with a friend and they were all delicious, and I'm just waiting for a chance to head back!
Delicious seafood Thai restaurant in downtown Manhattan, lovely place love the decoration, love the tests love everything, love love.

One of the most delicious meals I've ever had! The food was so incredibly well seasoned, i mean they managed to make something as simple as corn, tomatoes, and green beans taste like heaven! I was so close to ordering another one for myself hehe 

Their pork cheeks were also to die for! You have to, have to, try them!! The prawns were also very good but next time I would switch things up and try a different plate as they all sounded amazing.

Stopped by on a Friday and they were all booked but luckily we snatched the last 2 bar seats. Recommend calling ahead to make a reservation unless you don't mind waiting for a place at the bar if they're all booked.

Wow. I had this place four days ago and I'm stilling thinking about it. It is so incredible and I'm so sad I don't live in New York. Fish Cheeks is truly the best and most memorable Thai food I have ever had. Dish after dish, they surprised us and each dish we had, had the perfect amount of spice. Beyond the food, we got reservations for 2 pretty easily and the service was great! 10 / 10 would recommend to ANYONE. Love that it's not the typical Pad Thai ordeal (still love that too though). I wish we could try everything on the menu but below is what we got. There isn't a standout dish because they're all delicious. 

Appetizers:
Market Oysters
- so fresh and delicious with fried shallots and nam jim seafood- can't have oysters any other way now, UGH!
Zabb Wings
- Wowwow. I am actually one to be against ordering wings at an Asian restaurant but these wings blew me away. No sauce needed because they seasoned and crusted to perfection. Not too bready. Hell. Ya. 

Main Courses:
Coconut Crab Curry
- Great flavor and, again, perfect amount of spice. 
Crab Aob Woonsen
- Incredible noodles with an amazing sauce; crab is a great add-on to this dish. So traditional! Love.
Crab Fried Rice
- People can really get fried rice wrong but definitely not Fish Cheeks. This is also a must-have!

The food, drinks and service are exceptional. We had the chicken wings, my advice is to give them a second to cool down and have water handy because the spice sneaks up on you. We also had the curry crab, pork belly and noodles and the shrimp all of which we loved. What a great spot!

This place is SO good! I order from here all the time on Caviar but since they have such a good happy hour deal, I decided to go in person. I LOVE Nahm in Bangkok, where the chefs trained at, and the food here does not disappoint

Agreed with the reviewer below that the oysters weren't memorable, but for $1 I'd take them. Everything else on the menu is amazing. 

Strongly recommend:
- Grilled pork cheeks (on the fattier side so buyers beware)
- Steak tartare appetizer
- Fried fish
- Crab fried rice
- Crab noodle thingy (aong sen?)

The crab curry is good but could be a little heavy. They were out of the tenderloin but I can't wait to try those! 

Cocktails were ok. I think the spicy mango is better than the Thai old fashioned, which was a bit too sweet for me

Ambiance is good, but less so than Wayan, which is super chic

This Amazing food overall - I ordered curry, pork, and oysters and thoroughly enjoyed each dish. Adding on great service and a laid-back ambience, Fish Cheeks won its place in my heart as my favorite Thai restaurant by far in NYC.
The food and service was amazing. Very authentic Thai flavors in both traditional and more creative dishes. Make a reservation if you don't want to wait over an hour and half for dinner.

I came here for the first time for summer 2019 restaurant week with 3 other friends. I had heard great things about it from other people previously. 

There is a set sharing menu all year round, so you don't have to wait for restaurant week to share a few delicious dishes with friends. 

I really enjoyed my meal.  Three of us ordered a variety from the restaurant week menu and shared.  The other person doesn't eat seafood so she ordered different items that were not in the prix fixe. 

NOTES: most of the food is spicy. Most of the food has seafood in it. 

I would not recommend coming here in a group where anyone does not like or cannot have anything spicy or if someone does not like or cannot have seafood.  Or worse - anyone with a seafood allergy.  

There are some veg/vegan options but not many. There are maybe a couple items that are not spicy but even "mild" spicy can be too much for someone who does not like spicy food.

I go here pretty much every second week. Once I even went twice in a week. Fish cheeks have some of the most flavorful and interesting Thai dishes in town. Their portions are massive and comes relatively quickly. The bartender and waiters are also really nice! Slightly dark at night and very lively. It's a good place for date night albeit its a bit hard to talk.

Having been here twice, once with a small group and last night in a large party I'd give Fish Cheeks a solid 3.5. The first time I thought the food was average. The happy hr oysters were mediocre but hey for $1 I can't complain. Skip the bland beef tartare. Last night with 10 people, we tried most of the menu. My favorites (in order of preference) were the grilled branzino with peanut sauce (order this over the fried or steamed fish), chicken wings, crab fried rice, crab curry, corn salad, and pork cheeks. My gfs loved the crab noodles but I forgot to use the green dipping sauce. The coconut ice cream with jackfruit was a delightful way to wrap up a great meal. The bill was $67/person with ample food and one drink each which makes it (sadly) reasonably priced in a sea of overpriced manhattan restaurants. Cute place for a fun night with friends! Not hurrying back but happy to dine here again. It's packed so make your resy.

My niece and I went for restaurant week. So I have only been here once but why wait to say something nice. Pro tip: Don't even bother without a reservation. Tiny space but loved the bright decor.  Food was amazing. Decent sized entrees, super helpful and friendly staff(I love enthusiastic recommendations!) but, super tight inside seating. Another reviewer (Dawn Q) said it was reminiscent of a southeast asian eatery- what a lovely sentiment. I will try to think of it that way next time because I will be back.

The dollar oysters (from CAN) were forgettable but the cocktails were not. I fell in love with my spicy mango... that was channeling sticky mango rice, I think... but was a cold slushy perfect dessert in a glass that has complex notes and good liquor while still keeping you on diet track. Beautiful. And his Thai old fashion was certainly different and he thoroughly enjoyed it. 

Attention to detail and accoutrement is key. Decor, plateware, sauces even the shrimp chip table starter was so smart. Now let's get the meat. 

We shared the crab fried rice and the shrimp curry in a bowl with an amazing assortment of veggies and starfruit. The crab fried rice was perfect golden fluffy and simple. But littered with chunks of crabmeat. Yes. That is a good thing you did there FC. And that curry! I'm sorry I may be butchering a most elaborate name for this dish (on the mid-bottom right of the menu) but I most certainly wouldn't skimp on description. A gorgeous soft turmeric coat that is almost butter rich and round filled a bowl of select shrimp meat and topped with bits of shallot and a bit a citrus. White Napa, long beans, skinless stalks of cucumber, mango, starfruit completed with basil and mint surrounded this curry for dipping or wrapping and dousing. 

We did both of course and were unanimous that this dish should come with a bowl of white rice it was so so flavorful. Course we had our fried rice and used that. Needless to say we did all but lick both plates clean. 

Holy heck, FC i get the hype. You deserve it and more. I can't wait to be back to try more thoughtfully and uniquely concocted dishes. Props to the petite manager with super style and great bedside manners in explaining every question we had as well.

I was so excited to try Fish Cheeks after hearing it toted as a trendy new casual-upscale Thai place in downtown NYC. We can always use more places like this! The restaurant itself evokes the feel of a Southeast asian eatery with tables packed closely together, lovely wooden basket lights hanging from a high ceiling, and a colorful, bright interior. We made reservations in advance which I would highly recommend as this place gets packed. 

Unfortunately, we missed the happy hour which goes from 5-7pm. We arrived early, but were informed that since our reservation was at 7pm we would not be allowed to order drinks before that time. I was pretty surprised considering there is a bar that you would think would be available to customers who are waiting for their table. The whole thing was kind of surprising and disappointing. 

Once we were finally seated and then (finally) allowed to order drinks and we chose the spicy mango and the butterfly effect. The spicy mango was a hit but I would stay away from the butterfly effect which has a pretty unpleasant flavor. Luckily, things improved once we ordered the food. A word of warning that this is a VERY seafood heavy menu. We decided to try the grilled pork cheeks, grilled branzino, and the vegan green curry. The grilled pork cheeks were very juicy and flavorful strips, perfect for a meat eater looking for a more decadent appetizer. We were very leased with the mains as well. The grilled branzino comes wrapped in foil and when opened revealed a perfectly cooked piece of white fish accompanied by a lovely peanut sauce. Additionally, the vegan curry was very well done - with vegetables including broccoli and eggplant simmered in a flavorful thai basil and red finger chili curry. This was both light and filling at the same time. We were very pleased. 

Overall, despite a rocky start with the happy hour, we had a very nice time and thought that the food really met the mark. I would recommend coming with a small group due to the tight space and making a reservation, but it's definitely worth a try!

You can tell that they used high quality ingredients and the food was good but nothing special. Is it worth $25 per entree? Probably not. There was nothing wrong with this place but I don't think it's worth the wait so definitely make a reservation if you want to eat here. The waiter told us that the food is "Thai spicy" meaning spicier than normal, but honestly none of it was spicy and I had to ask for hot sauce! The food was mostly sweet and salty. Definitely get the wings though.

Love this place so much that I came back twice in a week. A must for seafood lovers! I recommend Set 2 and it's great for 2 or even 3 people. You should get a reservation, otherwise wait until 10 pm to get seated!

Food: 2/5
Is it me or is the food subpar now? I think the best thing we ordered were the oysters. It came with friend shallots and a green sauce. Very tasty and only $1 during HH! Would definitely recommend! The crab with glass noodles were very very very dry and lacked flavor. Definitely not worth the $25 price. The presentation was nice but easily duplicable at home. Nothing special. The crab curry was also mediocre. It was packed with spice which I somewhat enjoyed but it sort of tasted like melted peanut butter and chili.

Did I order wrong?

Service: 5/5
Our waitress was super nice and attentive. She was such a dear!

Ambiance: 3/5
Cute and cozy. This place is called Fishcheek so expect fish/scales decor everywhere. There's only one toilet for the establishment. Expect a super long wait for the bathroom.

Absolutely amazing.  Having limited meal times available during our trip to NYC, I wanted to make sure that the stops on our culinary itinerary were well chosen, and this one absolutely did not disappoint.  We made reservations for a weekday at 12:30.  While there were some empty tables, it started rounding up so definitely did not hurt to have those reservations.  

We shared the tiger prawn karee (curry with scrambled eggs and prawns (which were 3 giant prawns with head-on)), the coconut crab curry, and the somtum corn salad.  Yes, I know, how dare we go with two curry dishes.  But, the descriptions were amazing and I don't regret it one bit!

It was all delectable - five stars for each individual dish and yes, something you write home about.   So, so very flavorful and each dish was memorable in its own way.  The crab curry was panang based (I believe) so was nuttier than the prawn curry.  The corn salad was fish sauced based so had the wonderful earthy and tanginess that one would expect of Southeast Asian cuisine.  The prawns in the curry were monstrous.

The Drunk in Love drink was wonderful as well.  Very fragrant and I'm always a sucker for watermelon juice and rose, so this really was the perfect pairing for me.

Service was fantastic.  Friendly, prompt, reliable.

Everything was great.  This first lunch stop for our NYC trip this year did not disappoint.  I highly recommend it to locals and tourists alike.

Absolutely love the food here. They take Thai and give it a fushion twist and t works! I'm usually not a fan of fushion restaurants as they never get it right. They also know how to kick up the spice here! I'm a big fan of spicy too. They just hit all the wants! Can't wait to revisit!

Made our way here on a Sunday afternoon and found 5 open tables to a surprise. Came with my wife and son so it was a relief to find it fairly empty. We ordered as soon as we sat as we know our son needs to eat right away before he gets not hungry but hAngry. After about 35 minutes, still no $1 oysters or cocktails to start. We saw the bartender making drinks for everyone at the bar first and finally got our drinks after we made it known to the waiter. 45 minutes later still no food and everyone that came after us had already gotten their food. At this point, my son was impatient and was crying nonstop. We finally got our oysters, steak tartare and pork cheeks. Oysters were tiny.  Steak tartare was dry and saltier than we would've liked with a strong lime aftertaste. Pork cheeks were tender with a great jaew sauce. At this point, we were rushing to finish our food to leave but had to wait another 20 minutes for our crab curry. Table in front of us got their crab curry dish before us and they arrived after us. No apology whatsoever for the delay but instead the server says, "yes of course, it's on the way". Seriously? When? Next year? Service took so long that people who arrived after us finished their meal before we did. Was the food good? Yea. But not worth the price point and delay of service.

Probably the best thai food i ever had so far in NYC. 

We came in around 1:30pm on Saturday. The hostess put us on the waitlist and told us to wait for 15 min for table for 2. But actually waited for 20-25 min. 

Happy hour is until 3 pm so we got the oysters for $1 each. Small but really delicious. Different from the oysters i usually have, it's served with some crackers and the sauce was thai-style sweet chilli flavored. Amazing taste!!

We also got the po tak, a traditional thai soup with seafood. Grilled branzino, tastes great even without the sweet chilli garlic sauce. And pak boong fai dang, a veggie dish, tastes good too. We will come back to try more of their drinks as well.
Excellent food & service! Delicious chicken wings and crab fried rice! I will definitely go back to try the other menu items.

Best Thai food I've ever experienced in my life! Get ready for spice! I could eat all the oysters in the restaurant, they're so delicious.
