The coconut curry crab is one of my faves as well as the steamed whole fish. I go every time I'm in the city, this last time I went 4 days out of the 7 I was there. Can't wait to go back

I've only been to Fish Cheeks once but loved it. And will be back to try more things. Service is impeccable and I only had 2 things: the oysters and the pork cheeks.

Pork Cheeks are to die for. Must have.

Raw Oysters were fresh but I didn't like the sauce. The sauce was delicious with fried shallot or garlic chips to top. But I wasn't used it. It was quite strong too so overpowered the oyster flavor. I prefer great oysters with mignonette and cocktail sauce. The oysters themselves are fresh, on the salty side, and a bit small and flavorless. They are $1 each though during happy hour so a great place to get your fix if needed.

Happy Hour is during lunch and dinnertime so that's always nice!

TLDR: Thai seafood restaurant on Bond Street. Good groups both large and small. Very tasty but make sure you reserve. A bit on the pricier side.

So we've been going to Fish Cheeks for a bit now and it is a place we enjoy going to. It is kind of a new school Asian restaurant but I definitely dig the concept here. While they do offer some non-seafood items, the seafood is most definitely the star.

The menu changes during the seasons but some of the staple dishes seem to stay like the crab curry, the pork cheeks, the morning glory.

Our favorites though are the Crab Curry, Lobster Ka Ree (or whatever protein it is), Pakboong Fai Dang (stir-fried spicy greens, so so so good!). The crab curry is saucy with a generous amount of crab while the ka ree is that dry stir-fried goodness. Try the mango sticky rice if they have it! If you're not sure what to get, they do set meals where they have your dinner built out with appetizers, entrees, etc.

Everything just has so much flavor, the spice has some real heat and its a bit different than the standard Thai fare available. Great place to catch up with some friends and great food. Make a reservation a couple days in advance because the place does get crowded.

If you love raw, spicy, and layer of flavors, and don't mind strong and aromatic food, you are in for a treat here. 

A cute spot, bright, and charming, the small menu from chefs Chat Suansilphong and his brother Ohm, who used to work at the Michelin Starred Nahm in Bangkok, Thailand, now running this still a hot spot as of 2019! 

Grilled PORK CHEEKS - Compart Duroc pork cheeks marinated in fish sauce served with Jeaw sauce, nom! 


Po Tak - Clear lemongrass soup, Pollock, shrimp, mussel,
squid, Oyster mushroom, Bird's eye chili, galangal, basil, Makrut lime leaf. Sweet, sour, and spicy but solidly good.

Manila clams with sweet basil, Stir fried with scallion, roasted chili jam, sweet basil, garlic. Small portion but super tasty.

Crab Aob woonsen, Baked crab meat, thinly sliced pork belly, glass noodle, cilantro roots & celery leaves. Lighter clear noodle dish, good.

Steamed fish with thai herbs, Whole Striped bass, chili, lime, mint, culantro in cilantro lime broth. Light and bright dish, very good dish to share.

Don't forget they have HAPPY HOUR everyday 12-3.30 pm, 5-7 pm for $1 oyster, $5 beer, $8 wine and $10 House cocktails.

We can't wait to come back!!

this place is one of the cutest finds!! My boyfriend and I came here because they had Happy Hour & $1 oysters but this restaurant has way more than just that! 

As many has said, interior is super bright and vibrant; all of the servers wore bright colored tropical shirts and they were friendly & attentive! Our server explained the menu to us and we really enjoyed our time there because of him.

For drinks, I had the Drunk in Love which is a watermelon cocktail & it was so refreshing and not too sweet. We ordered oysters & the blue crab coconut curry to share. The oysters were fresh but are a little smaller then other places we've been too but it comes with a side of green chili which is absolute delicious! The blue crab coconut curry was so flavorful & I definitely recommend! It is spicy but it's a very unique spicy; it will hit you in a subtle manner as initially it doesn't taste that spicy.

I will definitely be back to try out their other dishes!

Fish Cheeks offers the best of Thai food with high quality dishes and professional yet personable service. The prices fall in the high range with each dish costing $15+. The menu is quite small and limited but they offer some tasty dishes like steamed fish, crab fried rice, oysters, and their famous pork cheeks. 

Pork Cheeks: 5/5 I don't think I've ever had such a tender slice of pork. Usually pork is a bit tough, chewy, and dry. Fish Cheeks has absolutely perfected their pork cheeks. The meat is extremely tender and with the small cuts of fat, it basically just melts in your mouth. The sear gives it a nice smoky flavor. If this came over a bed over rice (that wasn't $3 a bowl), I would surely order that. The serving size was surprisingly large as well. 

Chicken wings: 5/5 These were fabulous- super crispy exterior with a grainy outer texture. The wings have a slight sweet component (think of the Wingstop seasoning). The chicken meat is juicy and well executed. 

Clams: 5/5 The clams were highly recommended by Mike Chen so I just HAD to try them. We aren't huge fans of clams but these were quite tasty. The sauce was savory with a nice kick. Top it off the fried rice and you're golden. Be careful- the bell peppers are actually really spicy. 

Crab fried rice: 4/5 Don't get me wrong, the crab fried rice is everything you look for in fried rice. Good seasoning, moist rice, a hint of sweetness from the crab. However, I could not justify spending $28 on a plate of fried rice. As much as I LOVE fried rice, I would skip this next time to make room for another dish. 

Our experience at Fish Cheeks certainly stands out from all of the restaurants we enjoyed during our stay in New York. The bill for 2 of us which included 4 items came out to be $100 including tip. When you make a reservation, you do have to put in your credit card info so plan accordingly or cancel on time!

This meal left me quite speechless and as my friends would say "Holy sh*tz, the only time you're ever speechless is when you got laryngitis!".  

Yup. That. Freaking. Good.

We came on a Monday night thinking it will be a little less crowded; but WOW, this place fills up fast once they open their door at 5pm. Luckily we made a reservation and made sure to show up on-time. They are generous, giving patrons an extra 15 mins buffer for your "late" friend but alas, if you have one of those perpetually late friend - then you best leave 'em!  

Intimate, cozy and so boutique like setting; with an open kitchen towards the back and a bar serving up some mighty yummy mixers.

We made a reservation (highly recommended for party of 4 & less); no wait.  3 girls, 2 starters, 2 drinks, 1 juice, and 4 entrees.  Total bill $60 each; perfect portion meal. 

Crab curry; plentiful of blue crab meat, 200% flavor and packs heat! Signature crab fried rice, on its own, it's mild but combine with that freaking addicting green sauce - "BOOM".  Had the Tiger Prawns w/ egg sauce - must eat with rice, it is absolutely amazing. Also got the morning glory, it's ok, good veggie addition to our entrees.  Oysters were fresh and so good with the fried shallots & green sauce (epically good). And the cannot-miss grilled pork cheeks - Yo! I can eat this all day!! No joke.  Get 2 servings!!!   We girls absolutely DID NOT dine like ladies, we came to EAT!  

We left very full, happy and already planning a return. 

#amazingexperience #girlsnightout #SOHO

Heard really good things about Fish Cheeks, so with my craving for $1 oyster happy hour, I was sold. First things first, oysters = AMAZING! The green sauce and fried shallot crunchies to add on top, rather than the usual cocktail sauce or horseradish, make it one of the best combinations I've had to date and really makes Fish Cheeks stand out serving something so simple. I would come here just for like 5 dozen of these.

Zabb wings were served hot and the dry rub was slightly sour and spicy. Good if you're in the mood for wings; could pass if you're looking for something more substantial.

Coconut crab curry was a hit! We didn't think it was spicy - if you can't handle spice, you will think it is. The flavors were good, creamy and there were decent chunks of crab meat. I normally don't like to eat a lot of rice, but here, I needed it to sop up all the curry, short of licking the bowl clean.

As for cocktails, Thai old-fashioned was ok, not as strong as other places and the Thai breaker was pretty good, though I'm not really a fan of coconut flakes.

I recommend coming here for happy hour specials. Totally worth it, and you can add other things. I'll be back!

The food is good. I really enjoyed their happy hour oysters more so because of the sauce that came with the food. All the items we ordered were well seasoned (a touch on the salty side for the po tak). The one I didn't like was the vegan green curry because it was surprisingly bland. I ordered tiger prawn curry to-go and it was great as well. I would come back again.

This is one review I could not wait to write. This is a gem of a restaurant that deserves all its accolades, from its ambience to service to food. Everything was perfect, but the food really shines. It's one of those places that you want to try everything on the menu. Make a reservation, you'll need it. The place was packed 15 min after opening its doors.

Thai tea - A bit bitter and acidic, may have been over seeped, this I would pass.

$1 HH Oysters - from 1230-345 and 5-7 everyday, they offer $1 oysters (usually sold for $3) with a spicy and tangy chimichurri sauce and fried shallots. Today they were kind of on the small side, no meat at all. 

Beef tartare - It's reminiscent of the raw beef dish I love from a hole in the wall thai restaurant I use to go to in San Diego. Really good flavor, spicy, herbaceous because of the basil, good meaty texture.

Prawns with Egg Curry - SUPERSTAR. The tiger prawns were chargrilled to a T. The meat kept it's bouncy texture, the head custard was intact, and the sauce... oh my god the sauce was out of this world. The curry was made with scrambled egg and the entire sauce tasted like shrimp head butter. It was divine. I only wish it was spicier.. Which brings me to:

Crab curry - Insanely spicy, but it was perfect when mixed with the shrimp curry sauce. The flavor needed work and I wish there were more ingredients, but it was still a good dish overall. 

Steamed sea bass with herbs - Flakey fish bathed in lime juice, fish sauce, and lots of basil. Fish was cooked perfectly and deboned (except the tail, belly, and head). It was a good dish to pair with the heavier curries.

Coconut ice cream - NEED. Seemingly simple, but I promise you that you need to finish the meal with this. It's the creamiest ice cream I've ever had. The jack fruit and palm fruit make it a thai affair. In love.

My date made me promise that we wouldn't repeat any restaurants in NY, but this might have to be an exception.I

Fish Cheeks is on the pricier side, but it's hard to argue with the quality of their ingredients and cooking. They really have their flavors downpat. This was one of those rare experiences where all the dishes were varying degrees of wonderful.

We received a small dish of shrimp crackers and a thickened, milder gochujang/shrimp paste to start. I usually see these crackers with crispy chicken at Cantonese banquets, so this was a fun and nostalgic surprise.

Market oysters - I capitalized on the $1 Gulf Coast oysters for their 5-7 happy hour. These were decently plump and quite nice with the nam jim seafood sauce (a bright, spicy, sour green Thai sauce with lime juice, fish sauce, cilantro, garlic, and chilis) and crispy shallots. Although I've never had anything crunchy to go with my oysters, the combo actually worked really well. I did miss the cocktail sauce, but not nearly as much as I expected to.

Crispy garlic branzino with fish sauce - I enjoyed the light and crispy exterior, and the branzino was cooked well. It was a bit bland on its own, but once I dipped or let it seep into the fish sauce it became a winner.

Crab fried rice - We really ordered this more as a bougie starch base for the branzino. These days I'm more hesitant about getting crab fried rice because the flavors are too mild for me, and that was also true for this one. But it came with that nam jim sauce again, which added a lot of great flavor and enhanced the taste of the crab. The rice was also pretty fluffy, and we were pleasantly surprised by the amount of crab.

Coconut crab curry - This was our most anticipated dish of the night and it didn't disappoint. As with the fried rice, there were so many chunks of crab meat. They didn't skimp at all. It was creamy, very spicy, and best to split, because it tasted too same-y after a while. The portion of rice was pretty small, so we ate this with the crab fried rice as well. Crab on crab is the best kind of meal.

Manila clams with sweet basil - So flavorful and a nice balance to the spicier crab curry. I loved scooping the sauce, bell peppers, and garlic onto my rice and just eating that.

They also have some tasty sounding cocktails. My friend got the Sticky Rice with rum, coconut cream, and rice milk. It was sweet and milky, almost like a dessert in drink form.

Note: They regularly change parts of the menu, so a few of these dishes might not appear in the current iteration. But you can't really go wrong with anything that's on offer.

Don't judge this place by it's strange name. It is a restaurant filled with bold colors and flavors. The food was so good that we came here twice during our one week vacation in NYC. Make sure to make a reservation or coming during a weekday lunch because it gets busyyyy

Try:
- Happy hour and grab some $1 oysters. Oh man the crunch of the garlic flakes with the sour sauce.
- Zabb wings - has a nice sour kick, comes out piping hot and is low key spicy.
- Crab fried rice - one of the best I've ever had 
-  Tiger Prawn Karee - a great mix of curry with egg (??) with giant prawns
- Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs - delicious, sour and fragrant. almost like a tom yum soup

Skip: 
- Coconut crab curry - sorta had this peanut flavor that I didn't really enjoy. I thought that the prawns were better
- Grilled pork cheeks- good, but there are so many other delicious things to fill your belly with
- Fried fish - not as crispy as I thought it was going to be :/ 
- Coconut ice cream - because I like my ice cream creamy... 


Overall, a delicious authentic thai restaurant with great flavor that I haven't had in awhile. Oh yeah... and end the night with some mango sticky rice.

We came here on a Tuesday and it was an hour wait for a party for two. Please make sure you do yourself a favor and make a reservation before coming. They have $1 oysters until 7pm, we didn't get to make happy hour so I cannot rate it. 

We ordered two cocktails, pork cheeks, the lump crab coconut curry, crab fried rice and fried fish. I would really recommend the pork cheeks because it is really tender and comes with a tangy sweet chili dipping sauce. The curry was really spicy but goes really good with rice and it is super rich with coconut milk. The fish was and flaky and amazing.  The crab rice is not bad but tastes less flavorful after having everything else we ordered.

Overall, I would recommend this price although it is pricey. Everything came out to be about $162 with gratuity.
I sat at the bar and ordered the steamed fish and a Singha. Delicious. Can't believe I ate the whole thing, but it was that good.

Fish Cheeks is an upscale Thai restaurant that delivers the wonderful flavors of authentic Thai cuisine, with some reimagination. The venue is rather small, so the wait can be long if you don't make a reservation. We ordered the Coconut Crab Curry and the Tiger Prawn Karee, with a side of Pakboong Fai Dang and Happy Hour Oysters. For a party of four, this was just enough to be satiated, but most may think that the serving sizes are small. Most dishes are quite spicy, even the dishes without the chili sign have a very mild level of spice. Two chili signs definitely will get you sweating. To counter the spice, we ordered some Watermelon Juice, which is a nice change to the usual Thai Ice Tea that we order. The waitstaff is great - friendly and quick. Ambience is chill, though due to the venue being on the small side, it can get loud...but that's also the best part of this restaurant's ambience. On the menu, there is a Chef's Selection prix fixe style menu, which I'd like to try next time.

The flavors in each dish were bold and overall truly exquisite!! I was most intrigued by the coconut crab curry--the crab was very fresh and its fluffy texture paired perfectly with the creaminess of the curry. Although it was a little spicy, a subtle hint of coconut really sealed the deal. 

This is the perrrfect spot for a summer weekend brunch (happy hour!!!) There's such a fun and vibrant ambience as soon you enter with a really welcoming staff. Highly recommend!

If you come here, you will absolutely love the food. They have a gluten free menu that I ate off and it was great. You must have the pork cheek! Everyone loves the crab curry and its everything everyone says it is. I have issues with spicy, but if you love spice you will not want to eat anything else. I instead had the pawn lon. It was so delicate and mild but so full of flavor. it comes with veggies and just so very nice. Please come and come for happy hour to have a nice drink with your meal.
Great service and great all day happy hour. Portion sizes are huge so you can share. Highly recommend, especially on a rainy day.

Honestly i would give this a 3.5 * and i really do hope yelp introduce the half star soon .

the place itself is cool but not somewhere you want to spend your evening - something about it just says eat and leave .


the food itself is pretty good but honestly the crab curry lacks crab  - like seriously where is the crab ?

the fragrant fish is quality but again on the slightly pricey side but probably paying extra for the fragrance !

In a nutshell overall yes but i still prefer Thai Villa ( not the line or wait )

It was a wonderful evening that started in a very distasteful way! I came in on a Sunday night at 9:00 PM and requested a table for one. The hostess then proceeded to pressure me to to sit at the bar. I had a looonggg day and just wanted a lovely dinner to start my week off right. I wanted a table. Despite the restaurant having less than 5 full tables, the hostess sat me on a table right next to the bathroom! Well, actually between the bathroom and the food service area and kinda dark. The other couple behind me was an interracial couple. Apparently after a few minutes the hostess felt bad and offered to move me tables. At this second encounter she was truly gracious. Just do it right the first time hostess and you don't need a do over and you won't almost ruin someone's night! I took off a star for the ungracious hostess. 

Now on to the substance of the night....
Not only was the food delicious, the servers were really, really knowledgable, efficient, and passionate.  It was really an evening of deliciousness and theatre! I highly recommend this place! I had the steamed fish! Devine! I ate ALL of it!!! For my appetizer I had the pig cheeks! It was absolutely delicious! I chased that that down with a light white wine and a coconut martini! What a night! Delicious! My server who I will name once I remember was wonderful! 

The best Thai food I have ever had and one of the best meals I have ever had, hands down! Wow! I will return!

Honestly the best Thai food I have ever had.  I had the green curry and it did not disappoint.  We also had the happy hour oysters and beer specials.  The restaurant is clean and very cute.  We had a great server.  We went at lunch and had a reservation.  I would recommend to anyone!

My gf and I come every time we're in New York. EVERY TIME. Food and cocktails are great! Definitely get the coconut curry if it's your first time. 

Pro Tip: Wait times around dinner can get pretty long without a reservation so come for Happy hour which is 12-7pm. $10 cocktails and $1 oysters. Perfect for a Saturday lunch.

Fish cheeks! Oh how I love you... just the thought of you makes my tummy rumble in hunger. This place is nothing short of delish!  The decor is cute and comfortable, the service is always stellar-literally no complaints. It's fun to watch the chefs banging dishes out in the open kitchen, it's like dinner and a show. The curry crab, crab fried rice, fried chicken, and sliced pork are my jams at this sweet little joint that has definitely won my heart. Should definitely join the ranks of a NYC dining staple; don't ever change.

Finally decided to post a review after my third five star experience here last night. I honestly do not have enough positive things to say about this place. Every time I've been here the service has been impeccable, the food outstanding, the drinks just right. 

Last night my party of three devoured:
- Coconut Crab Curry 
- Crab Aob Woonsen 
- Crab Fried Rice
- Fried Fish (you can literally eat the entire thing: bones, tail, head...)
- Zabb Wings
- Corn Salad
- Shrimp Sao Nahm

Already looking for another excuse to go back.

Bruh, the food at Fish Cheeks is so damn good. They are very much worth the hype. The flavors are bold when they need to be, delicate when they need to be, and so well balanced. It was as good if not better than my favorite meals in Thailand. 

The restaurant is bigger than I expected. Probably seats about 50 and every seat was full on a Wednesday night. Its bright and colorful during the day but all their lighting is really warm so at night it looks way more chic. 

But that star is the food. Omg. I ordered the tasting menu that supposed to feed 2 that definitely could feed 3 lol. Everything is served up family style. The zabb wings are sour and low key spicy. The corn salad is milder that some I've had in the past and I loved it. It had really clean flavors and was a nice counter balance to the wings. 

For the main course we had the crab curry, crab fried rice and the fried fix. The curry was good, they dont skimp on the crab, its listed as spicy but the coconut milk helps cool it down.
The crab fried rice was so surprising. It was sour lol. Ive never had fried rice like that and I loved it!
The fried rice pair perfectly with the fried fish. It has just enough of that lime flavor in the rice that would replicate the lemon or lime you might drizzle on fish. The fish was *deboned* (yayyyy) so you can just dig in. It has to be the most exquisitely fried fish I have ever had. It was so crispy. The skin was like a potato chip. 

Everything was good and I had enough for breakfast in the morning.

Service was truly horrible!! 
Food was good. but we got seated at the bar in between a woman who was holding a baby on her lap and a couple. We could barely even pick up our water glasses easily because we were crammed between both of these parties. I then went up to the hostess stand asking them how long the wait would be for a actual table - they said 30 minutes, we decided to wait. We wait the 30 minutes, then our table becomes available and they seat as at the exact same seats at the bar?? The woman with the baby had left but we could have just stayed if we knew we were going to wait 30 minutes to get the same exact seats? Still very confused by this. Also, had to ask multiple times for our water to be refilled and for the oyster chips in order to get them. Really not sure how this restaurant is successful with such horrible service.

I really wanted to love this place but I left feeling quite underwhelmed.*

The space is small but decorated nicely. The best thing I ate was the the oysters (the fried shallots and sauce were excellent additions). The Zabb Wings were mediocre, the shrimp appetizer was okay and the crab dish with pork belly was bland.

I will say they have a great happy hour everyday (12:30-3:30 and 5-7) that includes $1 Oysters, $5 beer and $10 cocktails. I would come back for happy hour but I would pass on a full meal.

*I came for restaurant week so maybe it wasn't a true representation of the food.
Amazing place with interesting food. Will say that sometimes the food is a little salty, but it's not a big deal and I always come back
For the best flavorful broth and fish, come to Fish Cheeks. So, so, so good. Service excellent and vibe so hip and fun.

One of the most memorable meals I've had in NY. Coconut crab curry and the tiger prawn karee are absolute musts. The corn salad and grilled pork cheeks were also stellar! I love that this is Thai food but not with the usual pad Thai / curry dishes we're generally used to. 

This isn't the type of food you can eat every day, but that's because everything is so incredibly flavorful and absolutely delicious. Come ready to experience a meal that's spicy, savory, tangy, and sweet all together.

Everything we ordered was incredibly flavorful and we were so impressed. Not your typical Thai menu, which made it even more fun. Close seating quarters, but they do take reservations. Friendly and resourceful staff. Definitely recommend this for a fun night out as a date or with friends. Plan to order and share!
The steamed fish and pork cheeks were great.  The staff was really nice and my boyfriend and I have a great time

Every morsel of this fare was perfect.  Best wings I have ever eaten and I don't even like wings.  It's packed and loud though, so don't expect tranquility.  Expect your lip to be flipped by amazing fresh food. Recommend the Shrimp Sao Namh, the Corn Salad, Zapp Wings (!!!), and Coconut Ice Cream!  Even the Vegan Green Curry (while fairly predictable) was delicious.

Made reservation the night before and got a table around 6 pm on a Friday night. The restaurant is small and packed when we arrived, so definitely go early if you do not want to wait.

We got a dozen oyster ($1 each, great deal), corn salad, grilled pork cheeks and coconut crab curry, the portions are a bit small. The corn salad was very refreshing, the pork cheek is okay, the crab curry was too spicy to my taste, and I am very good with spicy food! So be careful if you do not handle spicy food very well. 

Overall the experience was good, the restaurant is nice, but the flavor is not really up to my expectation.

Wow. Came here for restaurant week. It was absolutely amazing. 

Corn salad - fire 
Tiger prawn whatever it is called - Fuego
Ice cream dessert - so freaking good. 


Will be back!

Came here for lunch on a weekday. The place was empty to my surprise! My family and I splurged on a spread of dishes, and while they were all 10/10, my favorite was the crab curry. So spicy and sooooo crabby.

Amazing food and fun decor. Came here on a Sunday night with bae and waited about 15min for a table. 
Food: 
- Market oysters: the oysters were fresh and the sauce was to die for, best oyster dipping sauce I've ever had 
- Grilled pork cheeks: super tender and flavorful
- Coconut crab curry: absolutely delicious. I could bathe in this curry sauce 
- Steamed fish with Thai herbs: light and fragrant with lots of fresh herbs, feels healthy but still taste good 

All in all, a fantastic dining experience that makes me want to come back for more ASAP

Yes yes yes!  Everything was so delicious. I have no trouble believing it's Chrissy Teigen's favorite Thai restaurant. I love pad Thai but this is not street food Thai food. It's elegant, adventurous, and flavorful. We got set #3 and it was perfect for 4 people. The Thai chicken wings are ridiculous. Perfectly fried, with some kind of lime and chili seasoning in the batter. Crab curry was wonderful, spicy with lots of crab meat. Prawn salad had good flavors of sweet, fish sauce, onions, pineapple. Beef cheeks were tender and smokey. The grilled brazino was super tender and had a bomb peanut sauce. Prawn curry was good, not spicy as crab curry. We substituted the fried fish with herb salad bc they were out of mussels and it was 10/10. I would eat here every week if I lived closer!

Seriously the best Thai food I've had stateside. Incredibly complex layering of flavors - something out of my dream.

Started with a round of Prosecco to warm the stomach then we dove into some Pig Cheeks (no Fish Cheeks here LOL), slices very thin and tender, with some incredible sauce.

The Manila clams were to die for - perfectly tender with that out of this world flavor: this one is a must-order. 

The Coconut Crab Curry, while super flavorful needs more crab meat. Crab fried rice has large chunks of moist, fresh crabmeat, and has that perfect aroma (of my childhood).

The Tiger Prawn Karee is another must-order (3 pcs per dish), so hard to find these sizes cooked so well. A real treat.

The Masterpiece: Steam Fish with Thai hers - set in it's own cooking vessel, impeccably prepared and BONELESS! What a concept. You can go full in without fear.

They have happy hour 5-7 so the Singha is priced reasonably, so are the cocktails.

And - our serve Cory was so helpfully cool, composed and entertaining, we're looking forward to seeing him again.

Go if you can.

Came in for a sunday lunch, and was blown away! 
Not only was the food amazing but our server was extremely attentive and she was super personable and made excellent recommendations! Loved the $1 oysters, steamed fish was phenomenal and the cocktails were tasty and beautiful! Definitely will be returning- and we hope Kate will be there to take excellent care of us again!

Romantic date spot. A little pricey with small portions but its quality food with great flavor. Wish their zaab wings came in counts of 20. I could eat those all day. Good service. I dropped a utensil and they immediately replaced it without me having to ask. Dinged a star because a bowl of rice is $3 and it's the cheap kind.

Really great atmosphere! Hosts and other dining assistants are friendly and welcoming. My usual go-to order consists of the coconut crab curry and pork cheeks! This time around I tried the zabb wings. The seasoning mixture they used was both  flavorsome and unique. We also got the crab fried rice which was average. Nothing to really rave about except it's a pretty standard fried rice dish that wasn't disappointing nor amazing enough for me to reorder next time. They have fantastic happy hour specials but during the last two times I've been here, at least one person has gotten a stomachache from the oysters. I would most likely skip out on the oysters next time and stick with the cooked menu. If you're daring, feel free to get the oysters! The green sauce and friend shallots really make the oysters very palatable.
The food here is phenomenal. We loved every dish that we ordered. Note the famous crab curry is pretty spicy so unless you can handle spice, I would ask for mild. Otherwise it was delicious!

Fish Cheeks is a seafood-focused Thai restaurant on 55 Bond Street in Manhattan's NoHo neighborhood. The menu isn't particularly adventurous or long but it's quite varied, thoughtful and there is sufficient variety to satisfy everyone, including vegetarian and non-spicy dishes.

We couldn't get a reservation but decided to take a chance and go anyway. It worked out perfectly with bar seats since is was right after happy hour was over.

Our bartender was very friendly and attentive. We got a few things from the menu since everything looked so good!!

Appetizer - 

-Market Oysters
-Grilled Pork Cheeks

Main -

-Coconut Crab Curry - is spicy and amazing with big flaky chunks of crabmeat
-Pakboong (side) - was also very delicious
-Crab Fried Rice - yummy!! 
-Khua Kling - went very well with crab fried rice

 Thumbs up!!! We will definitely be back

As much as I like the food served here, I think a lot of things here are a little over priced and over salted. I would say get the crab fried rice but maybe avoid the three chili sign dishes on the menu because you won't be able to taste anything after having that dish. Love the Thai flavors but expect to pay quite a lot for a pretty affordable cuisine.

If I ever move back to NYC, honestly, I would eat here every other weekend. Because this shizz is THE bomb (dot) com. I promise, one meal here and you'll be seriously considering making a move to NYC. I was in town with a friend and we were browsing the shops in the area. I absolutely love the fact that ACNE and Goop is on the same block. We got the chicken wings, oysters, coconut crab curry, and rice. Oh and two beers, because if you eat spicy food, it's always best to drink a beer with it. You definitely should family style this because portions were good enough for us two. 
Chicken wings and oysters were good but what blew my mind was the coconut crab curry. Oh my god. I've never had anything that amazing, that just makes such an impression on my memories. It's also authentic Thai food - like that woman on 90 day fiancee says, it 's bu** hole spicy. I added the asterisks to emphasize how spicy it's gonna get. It's not like we ordered extra spicy either, just medium. However, I do want to say it was an enjoyable kind of spicy. And oh so flavorful! Creamy and rich and all these other descriptive words for delicious things. I couldn't stop eating and my mouth couldn't stop burning. Good thing I ordered a Singha with it. Next time I come back, I might just eat here every night!

I was coming in from out of town and booked my reservation ( confirmed on resy) almost a month in advance for a busy Friday night.
My friends and I arrived on time only to be told my reservation had been cancelled?! I showed them my email with confirmation and no cancellation record . They claimed they didn't cancel it...they said they couldn't seat us , I was livid !! So despite booking way in advance and there was an error, clearly on their part , they would not rectify it . I think they cancelled( maybe from overbooking their restaurant) but just wouldn't admit it !!This is customer service 101, I'm highly disappointed in the way they handled their wrong doing...so just a warning even if you have a reservation you might not be able to eat here!

Incredible food and experience getting weekend lunch at Fish Cheeks. It's a Thai seafood restaurant that is very energetic and upbeat. Not a place to come for pad thai (I think they even have a sign stating that they don't serve pad thai LOL). The branzino was brilliantly cooked and absolutely falling apart on the plate, which made for a great meal. Also the coconut crab curry was super creamy and packed with tons and tons of spice. I would highly recommend the coconut crab curry and also for anyone looking to visit to make sure they had a reservation as this place is growing in popularity and lines are a common occurrence. Loved it here!!!
Got the zaab wings and Manila clams for restaurant week. Delicious food and good service

Yassssss! I love fried chicken wings so much that I've probably tried at least 15+ restaurants' fried chicken wings so far and these zabb wings rank high on my rating scale! They came out so crispy, hot, and juicy; they were seasoned so well...I'm salivating again just thinking about them. The green vegan curry...oh baby! It was just the right consistency of a classic, smooth, green curry with the perfect balance of richness and lightness and a satisfying amount of tender, fresh vegetables. The curry was accompanied with fluffy, white jasmine rice! Mmmm! The whole steamed sea bass with thai herbs was beautifully presented in a fish-shaped pan. The fish itself had a mellow flavor that complimented the punchy broth. The garlic pakboong fai dang made eating greens easy. All in all, this meal felt like (if not actually) a very nutritious, healthy (except for the fried chicken wings) and delicious meal. I will be back!

The Vegan Green Curry was good. The Pakboog Fai Dang was great. The Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs was amazing. But HOLY CRAP, the Zabb Wings were out-of-this-world delicious! One bite into them and you could tell they were cooked with the perfect amount of heat. Add in super crispy skin, a little sweetness from the grains of sugar sprinkled on, and lip numbing chili spice, and you've got the best wings I've had so far in my 2.5 years in NYC. So ono!

Came here for restaurant week dinner- overall very tasty and everything was well executed, just not my favorite type of food compared to some more elevated fine dining spots at the same price point for restaurant week, hence the four stars instead of five.

Started with free chips and a sweet chili dip thing, then for apps we got the shrimp sao Nahm. It was very light and fragrant and acidic at the same time, shrimp tasted fresh. 

For entrees we shared the tiger prawn karee and the potak which I think is the way to go if you like diversity of food. I definitely preferred the tiger prawn karee- it was flavorful with three plump prawns and not very spicy which I liked. The potak was this suuuper strong, fragrant and spicy broth with seafood and mushrooms and lemongrass sticks inside. Amazingly flavorful but I started by drinking the broth and after a few sips my throat was on fire, definitely not meant to be drunk like soup unless you've got insane spice tolerance. I have fairly low spice tolerance so it wasn't my fave. 

Finally dessert was the ice cream, nice and refreshing. Overall a good experience. Also service was great, super attentive and quick with everything (I think partially because there was another party coming soon after us, but we liked the efficiency :))

Been here a few times to check for the HH oysters. The green sauce is sooo addicting.. Love how everything always taste fresh.. Pork cheeks to grill fish or crab curry. All delicious  can't go wrong. 

My only complaint is the place is small so you gotta wait by the bathroom which isn't  always ideal when your about to eat because the only have ONE stall. 

I suggested making RSVP because the so sell out

Wow! This place is amazing, from the food to the decor to the service. I first discovered this place during restaurant week last year and have been back multiple times since. I highly recommend the crab curry (watch out - it's spicy!) and wings. They also have an amazing happy hour on drinks and $1 oysters. Definitely one of the best restaurants I've been to in NYC.
Delicious!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! will be returning again for seconds or thirds or fourths :)

Wow! This place took me by surprise. I'm usually picky when it comes to Thai food since I grew up eating homemade Thai food, but Fish Cheeks exceeded my expectations. Hands down one of the top Thai restaurants I'd recommend in NYC. 

The taste was authentic and had all of the wonderful flavors Thai food has to offer. We had the crab curry and the steamed fished. Both were perfect to eat with white rice and enough to share between the two of us. 

We had reservations on a Sunday evening. The place was packed, so highly recommend making reservations in advance. Can't wait to go back and trying the other dishes.

If you love seafood and a mouthful of delicious flavors/spices, this is your spot!

Thai food and cocktails? I couldn't ask for anymore! From the design of the restaurant to the food, this place is a must. 
The natural lighting in this place during the day is perfect for taking pictures LOL. The booth tables are lined up along the wall and made out of wood with a cushion on them - that gave the place an authentic vibe. 
I had the crab curry. It was very spicy, definitely good for opening up the airways. It comes with a bowl of rice and taste so delicious. There was an abundance of crab pieces so you won't be skimped. I really love that this place had an authentic and extensive list of cocktails. My cocktail was purple and looked so pretty! This place values its aesthetics and I appreciated it a lot.

This is my favorite Thai place so far in nyc

I love the crab curry with rice - my go to (sometimes I order this to go after an eat in meal)
The steamed fish is amazing
The happy hour oysters are good 

You have to eat in with someone or in a group so you can try more dishes.  So far I have been here for couple times, still delicious as usual. 
You have to make a reservation if not you have to wait on the weekends.

Highly recommend this place :)

This place was an adventure for your mouth and eyes - almost like an orgy sensory overload! The menu has a la carte and chef menu sets of dishes - both equally delicious and tough to decide on!! We got set 2 because WE WANTED THE AMAZING GOD LIKE WINGS!!! But be prepared to feel like you died and gone to thai food heaven!! The flavors are so authentic that you can close your eyes and easily pretend to be in Bangkok or Chiang Mai! I really dont know how some restaurants can do this and others just simply cannot!!!!

So back to the food - we added the prawns which were just heavenly!! The wings came next and were just the right amount of spicy and sweet - all the heat at this restaurant is flavorful heat - not that bullshit hot sauce heat!! Spiciness has a purpose here and the chefs know their shit! The fish, crab, and clams blew my socks off! They were all such different flavor profiles on the menu! But my favorite was the the crab with the vermicelli noodles! Oh my god!! If you love crab! Please get this for your mouth!!

For dessert - my stomach exploded and we got the coconut ice cream! Oh my lordy!!!! Real coconut -- i died twice in this restaurant! Bravo chefs! Bravo

I loved everything about this place!  Tucked away on a side street in Soho, this place was hopping on a Friday afternoon.  I had made a 2pm reservation via the resy app and when we arrived the majority of the place was full.  My friend and I lingered and chatted after our meal and even though they had closed to prep for the evening they weren't pushy or shoving us out the door.  They have a happy hour menu in the afternoon, $1 oysters and a variety of cocktails to choose from. 

We started with the chicken wings.  The spice level on these hits you afterwards, my lips were tingling!! The fry on the wings is light, doesn't overtake the chicken with coating and you can taste the spicy chili with the pop of lime.  For our mains we had the coconut crab curry and the crab fried rice.  Both were amazing.  They bring you a side of rice for the curry, but by the end i was putting it right on top of the crab fried rice, i could have just slurped it up! 

To cool my mouth down we got the coconut ice cream ( no picture, dug right in!). It's the perfect end to the meal, refreshing and great palate cleanser.

I will definitely be back and tick thru the rest of the menu here, given my first taste, this place will get a repeat visit!

I should have done a review a long time ago on this restaurant!!! I would love to say the food is horrible because I want to keep this hidden gem to myself but the food is ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC. I have gone here at least 20 times and the food is amazing and always consistent. The only thing is I wish the bring the can't calamari back it was so delicious .

An absolute gem located in SoHo off the busy streets of shops! My friend and I put in our names for a table for two. The hostess at the front was very friendly and attentive and even recognized us when we went to sit out front -- our table was ready sooner than he thought and he got us seated much sooner than we expected. Wait for 2 at 6:30pm on a Thursday was initially about 30min.

The aesthetic of the place is lively - just enough light, great fish accents, fun lamps and colorful chairs. The place is pretty tight, so be prepared to do that New York thing and cram yourself in a little.

We ordered two entrees (they recommend sharing all dishes): the Crab Aab Woonsen - a glass noodle dish with crab meat, sliced pork belly and garlic based sauce, Fried Fish (Bangkok style) with spicy curry. The Woonsen was delicious - excellent noodles, plenty of crab and about five pieces of fork - full flavor in every bite. The Fish was being cooked a little differently that night with a thai spicy salad instead of a rice curry. We didn't mind and were treated to a perfectly crisped, whole, fish that was moist and full of flavor. The salad was spicy so my friend ate it. We ate everything. It was so GOOD and fresh.

We asked for water and got a tap bottle for our table and great metal cups. Service was attentive and my nut allergy posed no problem for the kitchen. We would go back. You should visit if you've never been!

I followed the hype but honestly I have no idea how this place has such high reviews??? The service was okay but food was extremely salty and pricy. Me and my friend ordered a dozen oyster and 2beers from the happy hours menu, and we also ordered 2appetizers and 2entrees from regular menu, we spent like $180 in total (including 15% tips), based on the portion of food, definitely not worth the price. Not coming back for sure, and please avoid this place.

Wonderful service, nice, bright, colorful setting and amazingly delicious gourmet food come together for a very nice meal, in a city where there are many Thai and Asian restaurants on every corner, this one stands out.

We had 8 in our party and the service from the entire staff was excellent. Very attentive and always available with brights smiles. 

From the appetizers ( Raw oysters, fried Thai style wings, shrimp ceviche, beef tartare, tiger prawn, corn salads) to the main dishes ( beef sirloin, grilled fish, various curries, crab fried rice, Tom Yum soups and more ) each creation was bursting with flavor and spice level to your taste.

Whether you are looking for traditional Thai dishes, Thai fusion or just want a wonderful tasting meal with great service, I highly recommend you check out Fish Cheeks...it is a foodie's dream! Yummy!! "

This is my new favorite restaurant of all time. It was the closest to true Thai food we had in Thailand together last summer. So many friends have recommended this place, so I took my boyfriend here for our date night. He and I LOVED every dish! 

1. Steamed fish with Thai herbs was our favorite dish by far. How was it so delicious?! 5/5 
2. Coconut crab curry was by recommendation from our waiter - she said it's their most popular dish. It was good, but a little spicy for my liking and a bit too creamy. 4/5
3. Tiger Prawn Karee was the most popular when I was reading reviews on yelp, but we thought it wasn't great. The prawns were good but the curry egg mixture wasn't to die for. 3/5

The old fashioned is GREAT! If you get there in time for their happy hour (5-7pm), definitely get it! Only $10

I hope to be back here very soon :)

Nice place, great play list of music and good food.. I came here for happy hour around 2:30 pm had $1 oysters some Sauvignon blanc and the crab curry dish.. the crab curry was awesome definitely packed some heat to it! Service was prompt and courteous would recommend.

Hands down ! I'm Thai and this place is the best Thai Restaurant in NYC. Came here for lunch with a group of friends. We tried almost everything. Food was absolutely amazing ! The staffs were so friendly and helpful. We can't wait to go back !!
Most bang for your buck Malaysian fare I've ever come across. Rice will make any Asian cry from happiness.
Amazing! Ate here twice in one week and will probably come back a third. Food is amazing and bartender/new best friend Phoon is the best!!!!

Delicious! My husband and I would love to go back to try the other foods. 
We were able to get a reservation by calling despite open table saying there were no tables 1 week out. We went on a Saturday around 6pm and it was busy all throughout the meal. It's a fun open atmosphere with great drinks for happy hour. Our least favorite dish was the oysters. The fried onion and sauce were great but the oysters themselves didn't taste fresh and looked pre-shucked. 
The rest of our meal was fabulous. We got the pork cheeks and wings, both of which were delicious. The wings were my favorite. The lime flavor and crunch was perfect. For entrees we ordered the crab curry, crab noodles, and king prawns. Out of the three we really enjoyed the prawns and noodles. I think they out-shined the curry. Although the curry came loaded with crab meat, the other two dishes were so different and flavorful that the crab curry kinda got overshadowed for us. Will def be back for the wings and to try the other entrees.

Fish cheeks is incredible.  It's an odd name for a thai and Japanese fusion spot, but their cuisine is superb. 

PROS:  The raw oysters are $1 during happy hour and come with roasted shallots and a delightful sauce for dressing each one.  

The crab curry was rich and spicy... and it is hands down the best take on crab I've had in my life.  I wanted to slurp the bowl at the end.  It comes with rice too.

The prawn dish was easily 5 stars.  Rich with egg and spices,  with 3 large prawns to feast upon. 

The corn salad was sweet and spicy,  but all around refreshing.  A perfect summer dish.  

The pork cheek was perfectly roasted,  with just enough fat on it to melt in your mouth with each bite. 

The grand finale.. coconut ice cream.  Wow. I didn't think I'd have room for it,  but one bite and I couldn't let it go to waste. 

CONS:   Reservations pretty much required,  unless you want to wait 2 hours.  It gets jammed QUICKLY.  The tables can be tight,  so you'll feel like you're part of your neighbor's table and party of everyone's conversation.  That's not so great.  

One restroom... although it's nice,  it's not enough to accommodate the people that Fish Cheeks can hold.  There was a constant line.

OVERALL:  I'd give it 6 stars if I could.   I was utterly impressed.
Best Thai ever.  The happy hour is an amazing deal.

Have been here several times over the years and the coconut crab curry continues to be one of the best Asian-inspired dishes in the city. The crab fried rice and steamed fish are both definitely worth trying, though not every dish on the menu is of equivalent quality in my opinion. The cocktails are also inventive and serve as great complements to the food. Just get the crab curry and go from there!

I love this place!!! No Pad Thai for me every again!! The food is so authentic. I have never had a bad meal here. The space is modern and fun! The drinks definitely complete the Thai theme with a Thai basil twist of a Moscow Mule - really smooth and refreshing. My favorite dish is their side dish of sautéed cabbage - so simple but the umami flavor, probably a mix of fish sauce and other hidden addictive flavors, really hits the spot. The whole fish is also quite the experience every ounce of the fish can and should be eaten. :)

Another cool happy hour spot we went to on our New York trip. I believe when we went here, they only took reservations, so make sure that you book in advance! We mainly came here for the $1 oysters and a few other things to snack on before we had dinner later on in the evening. We ordered a couple drinks and beers as well. When the oysters came, they were pretty good sized and tasted pretty good. Comparing it to the oysters I had at Domo Domo, these came in second. Still good, but I preferred the $1 oysters over at Domo Domo better!

The chicken wings at Fish Cheeks were crispy and delicious. Nice crisp and flavor on the exterior of the wing, with the juicy meat on the interior. I think we ordered another order of wings right after we finished the first order! I'd definitely recommend this spot as it is really popular!

I'm usually down for the hole in the wall Asian food and always dislike the fancy looking places that would do the same food but dress it up in both plate and price.  This place is different.  

Happy hour oysters was awesome since it's $1 each.  I could have easily went for 20.  Their sauce was clean with the right mixture.  The pork cheek was awesome, you need to eat it right away while it's warm because once it cools down, the juicy fat won't taste the same.  

Both the curry crab and clam was just insanely good.  Without knowing I was finishing the rice because it taste so good with the sauce.  

The fry fish with orange curry was the least favorite.  It's something you have to eat quickly because the crispy fish soak up all the soup and become blah.   It was also the most expensive out of the other two dishes.  I won't order this again.  

The price matches the quality of the food.  Will come again!
$1 happy hour oysters, delicious drinks, large portions, meant to be shared.  girlfriends and i shared a bunch of desserts and they were all very delicious

Would have been 5 stars if there wasn't oil all over the chair I sat on! Really good Southeast Asian influenced food. Haven't had steamed fish like that since Malaysia. The fish is citrusy with lots of lime, cilantro, chili peppers, and fish sauce ($34). Eat it with the crab fried rice ($26) and spoon the sauce over the rice for a totally delicious and resourceful hack. They have complimentary chips on the table that comes with this sweet chili jam and it's literally the best chili jam that can be eaten with anything. The prices are a bit higher than a 2 dollar sign spot but it truly is good and I would not hesitate to come back.

Went here recently and everything was fantastic and full-flavored. For appetizers, the pork cheeks were delicious and juicy; the $1 oysters were great, too, although they didn't have much of the brine in the shell. Loved the accompaniments for the oysters though!

We all shared the coconut crab curry, crab fried rice, cabbage, and grilled branzino. The crab fried rice blew me away with the large chunks of crab and the taste--it was better than I expected. The coconut crab curry was spicy and salty and nuanced, a perfect pairing with the rice it came with. The cabbage was heavy on the fish sauce (as a lover of fish sauce, this is a good thing!) and the grilled branzino with sea beans was a hearty portion for sharing with a sweet and savory peanut sauce on the side. 

Cocktails were delicious as well and service was great. I'd recommend this spot for anyone who's into flavorful seafood dishes.

Was craving oysters and came here. They have a different take as far as dressing the oyster but it was really good. Sometimes I like more of a ocean-y taste with my oysters and theirs don't have that but it was excellent

This place was super delicious. I loved how small and quaint the place was. The foods seemed really fresh. I went with a group of 4. We made a reservation like 2 days before. Which was awesome because i thought they would be fully booked on a Friday. But we got lucky i guess. All around amazing !!

We got there at 8 on Friday night and was lucky to get a table without making a reservation. We had to try the steam fish and pork cheeks. We complimented these dishes with stir fry morning glory.
The appetizer pork cheeks was so tender and juicy. Dipping it in the sauce gave it a nice flavor.
The steam fish was done to perfection. The lime, garlic, cilantro mixed herbs gave a wonderful taste to the steamed fish. Unfortunately, the morning glory was too spicy for my daughter, so I had to volunteer :) to finish this dish. It would be nice if they would have ask us the level of spiciness that we can handle. Anyway, it's an above average Thai restaurant with a good service.

This place is so adorable.

The meal started off with a complimentary bowl of shrimp chips and a side of chilli paste. The chilli paste was so tasty!

Happy Hour Oysters- These were the best oysters I've ever had. The sauce and fried garlic flakes on them separated them from other oysters I've had so far. ($1 each)

Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs- This fish arrived bubbling in a cute plate shaped like a fish. It was so flavorful. They deboned most of the fish, but watch out for tiny bones! ($34)

Crab Fried Rice- Very delicious. ($26)

I definitely recommend the oysters and Crab Fried Rice.

Nothing too, too Thai about the restaurant. A nice, little, modern space. 
Only one bathroom, which seems to always be an issue here.

The Shrimp Sao Nahm was a delicious salad. But quite small for $15 a pop. Sweet, crisp, refreshing, especially next to our next dish. I wish we got the two together at the same time.

The Coconut Crab Curry was DELICIOUS. Rich broth, but not too heavy. Very spicy, very hot. So enjoyable. And great sticky rice to accompany.

Should Thai beers cost $8 a pop? They're super cheap there. But we're not there. So, alas...

Prices aside, size aside, waits aside, the place is great. But those shan't be forgotten.

This place has great Thai food in a city that really doesn't have many great Thai restaurants that have any kind of scene (not counting Uncle Boon's, which has a great, albeit noisy, scene).

My group of 3 enjoyed pork cheeks, steamed fish, and prawns - all really tasty and fairly reasonable priced. Service was pretty good, too.

Note that they will not seat you unless your whole party is there. For us, that meant that even though they did not give our table away, we ended up ordering drinks and appetizers elsewhere when we would have been super happy to have done it at Fish Cheeks instead!

Loved this place!  You need reservations or you have to wait which we did.  But the food was worth the wait!

Crab fried rice is yummy.
Crab curry which is amazing and spicy- yes bringing the heat!


Can't wait to go back and try more food!

Beautiful place and very delicious food!  

I came here on Saturday for dinner, didn't have rsvp and wait time was over 1hr but the friendly host offer bar seating which actually work out perfectly for us.

Menu it's small but great options - no the typical Thai dishes which I personally found very refreshing; we ordered the oysters - so amazing! The signature Coconut crab Curry and the Po Tak and was so good! Simple and fresh ingredients but so full of flavors and tasty! I'm so happy I found the place, I'm coming back for sure!!
I can recommend for all your guys food here is so good, very tasty, yummy and fresh. Staffs was so nice. The atmosphere in the restaurant very cozy.

So good! I didn't know what most of the dishes were prior to ordering but they were all delicious! Coconut crab was probably my favorite. 

They are not joking around when they say spicy so keep that in mind when you order. 

One major con is that there is only 1 bathroom. So you need to mentally strategize when to use the bathroom with the least wait time. Another semi con is the price- be prepared to spend over $50/person here (with 1 drink). 

It's busy even on a weekday so I would recommend making a reservation if you can. 

I will definitely return!

This is ONE OF MY BEST ALL TIME FAVORITE RESTAURANT!!!! 

Everytime I visit New York even just for a few days I make sure to come in at least once or twice! 

I absolute love this restaurant very much!! The place has a urban chic vibe which is always perfect for date night! They often have different dish on different days, the staff is always always informative to what's new on the menu. I always order drinks there I personally like all their drinks. 

I love their pork cheeks and fish!! The portion is perfect to share as family style dining. I love the way everything taste.

Overall, the food was great! There were a lot wonderful flavors and options to choose from. I will say if you order a spicy dish, it. is. spicy! Take caution. Orange Curry fried fish dish was just ok. The best dish was the appetizer dish, Pork Cheeks. They were so tender and full of flavor. The meat was tough. Can not wait to come back to try other dishes and desserts.
Best Thai food in NYC. Hands down the most authentic flavors of Thailand after coming back from an amazing trip there.
I'm Thai and I can say that this place has the most authentic Thai food I have ever tried in NYC. Go for it!

I wouldn't bother trying to eat here without a reservation.

We showed up at 6:15 on a Thursday night and were given a 1.5 hour wait time - it's a popular place, fine. We went to a bar for drinks and showed up an hour and a half later, and were told the wait would be at least *another hour* but there weren't any guarantees that we'd be seated. And yeah, they never seated us - and never even sent a text message to update us on the wait time or anything. The lack of communication was the most frustrating. I wish they'd just been up front with us when we first showed up, rather than wasting our time.

Excellent from start to finish. The coconut crab curry was, perhaps, the most delicious curry dish I ever tasted. I would have liked more crab in the dish, but it was satisfying nonetheless. The tiger prawn karee is a must have. The prawns are large and tender and left in their shells which are edible. The prawns are swimming in a delicious concoction of curry, chili paste and scrambled eggs. The vegan  green curry was good.  I would not order it again, but my wife loved it. We also ordered the cabbage and wok fried morning glory which were both delicious and different. I highly recommend this restaurant.

I cannot wait to come back! I had a delicious dinner here last Friday and it was all about flavor and spice - not the typical pad thai/pad see ewe dishes (which are also delicious), but exciting things that you definitely need to try. 

Oysters (5/5): for happy hour, these small $1 oysters were perfectly fine until you add that magic green sauce and fried shallots - then they're amazing. 

Goi Nuaa (5/5): even the beef tartare is spicy! But in a good way, especially with tangy fish sauce and crispy plantain chips. 

Fried fish with sour orange curry (5/5): completely caught off guard with a whole fish curled up in a pot of soup, but this ended up being one of my favorites! The skin retains some of its crispiness even in the soup, and the meat is super flaky and tender. I couldn't stop drinking the soup itself - it has this addictive sweet/sour/salty perfectly balanced flavor. It's also a less spicy option.

Coconut Crab Curry (4.5/5): doesn't look that impressive when it arrives, but it delivers on all flavor notes AND there are generous chunks of crab meat! 8/10 on spice - even though it was slightly painful I couldn't stop pouring that onto my rice. 

Crab Cob Woonsen (4/5): I've never quite tasted a flavor profile like this, and the noodles really soak up the intense sauce. It leans a bit smoky and hoisin-saucy. Another good less spicy option.

Khua Kling (3.5/5): how much spice can you handle? This teetered on the edge of enjoyably and painfully spicy. I found the beef too chewy. It is a large portion and my other friends really loved this with rice. 

Pakboong Fai Dang (5/5): I could eat a whole side of this morning glory on my own. It has a distinct "wok" smoky flavor that is so good. But careful, even THIS was spicy! 

Mango sticky rice (5/5): I'm still thinking about this... so simple but so delicious! The light syrup glaze is so fragrant and a bit savory, nothing at this restaurant is one-note on flavor, even dessert.

Coconut ice cream (5/5): 2 scoops of heavenly cooling relief, a well-deserved reward after all the spice. A few slivers of coconut and mango jelly on top just as an extra bonus.

TLDR: Get out of your comfort zone and be prepared for a very delicious, very spicy meal. Everything is flavorful, and all different flavor profiles! Service was great, but next time I will ask them to course it out. Almost all of the dishes came at once and it was overwhelming. Ambiance is lively, fun, and exciting, just like the food.

Came here for lunch and I am in love. Adorable decor, friendly staff and great food. I had to try the fan favorite- coconut crab curry and they did not disappoint! I would recommend it to anyone who isnt sensitive with spice (the dish lives up to the two peppers) $5 beer special and $1 oysters during happy hour! I will definitely be back.

Coconut crab curry- $24 bucks but worth every buck!

Felt so lucky to find this delicious Thai food place!

* * * EXPERIENCE * * *
Friday afternoon at roughly 1:30pm it was still all packed, only a couple bar seats left. The menu was not big, yet all of them looked so good just reading the descriptions and fellow Yelpers pictures. I knew beforehand morning glory was a must, and decided to throw in the crab curry which seems to be many's favorite.

* * * FOOD * * *
Coconut Crab Curry: A
The coconut flavor was strong, it's pretty spicy and mixing it with rice was heavenly especially the sweet coconut helped add a balance. The crab meat was cut into big pieces and tasted very fresh. 

Pakboong Fai Dang (Morning Glory): A
Lots of "wok hei" there which is a must for good morning glory, it looked very salty but actually not, very garlic-y, and there was a hint of sweetness too, such a balanced vegetable dish.

They seem to be switching out some items on the menu once in a while, I hope they will still have the sour orange curry fried fish next time I visit!

I came here for lunch with a small group on a Sunday. We were able to make a reservation online one day in advance. We ordered the coconut crab curry, grilled branzino, crab fried rice, tiger prawn karee, pakboong fai dang (wok fried morning glory), and sotum corn salad.  
Favorites
- Crab curry - this was by far the best dish we ordered. The curry was flavorful with just the right amount of spicy. The crab was smooth, fresh, and plentiful. Smother your rice with this curry! 
-Tiger prawn karee - this dish is also a must order. It consists of tiger prawns cooked in a scrambled egg curry like sauce. You may need request a seconds on the rice to soak up all this delicious sauce. 
-Grilled branzino - whole grilled branzino served with a chili garlic peanut sauce. The fish was cooked perfectly and deboned for easy eating.  

Other dishes we ordered included the wok fried morning glory - beware it is very spicy, crab fried rice - perfectly cooked and plenty of crab, and corn salad - fresh corn cut from the cob mixed with other veggies that reminded me of the papaya salad flavors. 

All in all everything was delicious and I would definitely come back. Don't expect your typical Thai street food prices though. This is a more done up version of Thai food.

Visiting my cousin in NYC and she wanted to try this place. I gotta say this is the best Thai restaurant I've eat EVER!! And no I'm not kidding. The food is that good. We had the $150 3 person meal set but you can order individual dishes as well. Let's start with the list from my least favorite: 

Prawn Lon - prawn meat in curry sauce and veggies. You put the veggies on a piece of cabbage and scoop the curry on it. I was surprised that they have the Asian star fruit. 
Shrimp Sao Nahm - this is kinda like ceviche with shrimp and mango. The sauce is a bit sweet and refreshing.
Zabb Wings - good fried chicken wings with a bit chili power and the dip sauce gives it a bit more flavor.
Crab Curry - can never go wrong with curry but with crab meat. A bit spicy which made it all better.
Pork Cheeks
Grill Brazino Fish - I'm not a fan of steamed fish but this was amazing. It's steamed inside foil wraps on top of a grill. The whole fish was deboned and filled with sea beans. The meat was very soft and the dipping sauce has an awesome kick. All the flavors worked well for this fish and dip.
Tiger Prawn Karee - my most favorite dish is this huge prawns with the garlic sauce. Prawns are fresh, crispy and drowned that garlic sauce. Can't describe how good the sauce is but I pour it in the rice and eat that by itself once the prawns are gone.

All the dishes are great but I had to list them by order of favorite so people would know.

All the dishes are great but I had to list them by order of favorite so people would know.

Delicious food!  Favorite Thai restaurant in the city.  Highly recommend the steamed fish and grilled pork cheeks.

Would not recommend this restaurant for large parties though, especially for dinner.  Reservation is done via email and a google doc (don't understand why it can't be done via phone or via a more secured payment method).  Mandatory 20% tip added for our party of 6, which is understandable, but a bit rude for them to ask as to leave the moment we paid.  Not a good place to linger, drink, chat after entrees/desserts.

Two of my top 5 favorite food groupings in one restaurant: Thai and seafood. 

Was on a one week trip to NYC and was staying in the hip part of the Lower East Side. Stumbled upon this restaurant via Yelp right after having drinks down the street at Angel's Share. I have to say, Fish Cheeks did not disappoint.

I would recommend going with a group of friends so you can share.

Was only able to try the steamed fish and the crab curry and I could easily eat those two dishes on a weekly basis. 

The crab curry was by far one of the best dishes I've ever had. Sweet, spicy, creamy, paired with rice. Just delicious. 

The steamed fish had a kick and was deliciously citrus-y. 

I honestly cannot wait to come back to Fish Cheeks and try more of the food options

I'm so conflicted writing this review. I REALLY wanted to like this place. We had a bad experience and management totally justified it by covering our check. Pork cheeks are amazing. Tartare is very spicy! Our visit was cut short due to problems at the restaurant. We unfortunately can't give a full review.

Came here for a late lunch with my friend--it was mother's day so it was quite  popping but we were still able to get a table in 30 min. 

I liked the flavors here a lot---we got the crab curry, sea bass, and oysters (happy hour!). It is thai-inspired I think--the sea bass was steam/cooked in a wonderful lime and chili/lemongrass broth and was very tender. We drank up the broth as soup afterwards. For us, the highlight was definitely the crab curry. It was decently spicy but dang, there was a LOT of crab--piles of it really. You can really get a good curry to rice to crab ratio going on with each bite. 

The prices were reasonable for the fresh and whole seafood and the drinks/cocktails were pretty good/strong as well. We will definitely be back to try the branzino and other dishes someday!

The food here is amazing. We ordered the whole steamed fish, crab fried rice, and the crab curry which were all phenomenal. We wouldn't reorder any of the cocktails, but only ordered from the happy hour list. The oysters were paired with unique sauces and were delicious and well priced for HH. Reviews on the chicken wings were mixed, since not everyone loved dry rubs.

Stopped by for happy hour on a Tuesday early evening - their happy hour is every day, 12 to 3:45 PM and 5-7 PM and has awesome drink deals. Beer for $5, wine for $8, and cocktails for $10. To top it off they also have $1 oysters at this time.
I'm a big fan of seafood so I went in on the oysters- they came with a Thai inspired sauce and topped off with fried onions. They were fresh and delicious- I would highly recommend. $10 for a cocktail was a great price point, but I felt the quality was lacking- more so felt like a spiked soda rather than a specially prepared cocktail. 
I'll definitely be back for the oysters but may opt for wine or beer instead of a cocktail next time. Warning! It's a really seafood heavy place and smells like it too. It didn't bother me, but my s/o who doesn't eat seafood tagged along and couldn't stay for long.

The food at Fish Cheeks was terrific. We had the chefs choice for 3 and enjoyed everything other than crab curry which was just ok. The highlights are the zabb wings, tiger prawn karee, and shrimp sao nahm. No complaints about the food. However, as I was looking up the menu when we got home to learn the names of best dishes, I realized we didn't actually get the prawn lon. The missing dish was a bummer on an otherwise fantastic experience.

Don't know what the hype is about. Food was so freaking salty I think my insides are now preserved for the next 50 years. Spicy was not even spicy. The prices for each dish were literally not worth it unless you like to splurge on tiny portions that are meant to be "shared". If this was my first time eating Thai I would definitely not eat it again. What a true disappointment. You're better off going somewhere else for Thai food.

Came here on a Friday night w a reservation . But they don't seat you until the whole party arrives, which is ok. There's a bench outside the restaurant which you can chill while waiting . 
 So three of us ordered 2 appetizers, the mango shrimp, and the pork cheek. They are both delicious- but all of us voted the mango shrimp as our favorite. It's refreshing and you could taste the mango in the sauce that comes w it. 
 For the entrees- we had the fried fish in orangey curry, crab cob Wonsan, and the pok tak soup w seafood in it- we originally wanted the Tom yum soup but the waitress was telling us this would b the closest to it because they don't have Tom yum soup. 
 They were alll delicious!! The soup is spicy and I could taste the lemongrass in it! And the fish- it's one of my friends and my favorite among the three! The only thing I m not sure is about the curry - the orange taste has overwhelmed the curry we didn't taste much curry flavor at all. But still it tastes sooo much, the fish was fresh. You can taste the crunchy even the fish is soaked in the sauce! 
 For the crab cob wonsen- it was delicious as well . But it's not outstanding so it's not our favorite but don't get me wrong - it's yummy. 
 We also ordered the dessert- had the coconut ice cream with jackfruit as topping and the mango sticky rice.  I would say, don't come here for dessert- it's not worth it. Coconut ice cream is nothing special. And the mango sticky rice- it has slices of mango and the sticky rice with the sugary sweet syrup as topping of the rice. I was expecting the syrup has a taste of mango but it didn't - kind of disappointing. 
 Overall I still give this place a 5 star rating. And will b back for more!

Actually so good!

I passed by this restaurant before and thought it was just another one of those cute interior but bland Asian cuisine (you know the aesthetic over taste type) - but it's not! It's really good!

I think you usually need reservations but we came right when it opened and was seated when the full party was present.

For food we ordered the pig cheeks (highly recommend) and the steamed whole fish (not pictured). Definitely get those two! The more meh dishes were the prawns (literally just 3 prawns and barely anything else) and the noodles were ok. Thai tea was a little sweet for me but decent. Mango sticky rice was good but portion was small.

What really stood out (other than the fish and pork cheeks, I'm just going to type this out again for emphasis), is the waiter service. He was super friendly and enthusiastic on describing the dishes to us. Thanks for that! :)

Wow, this place did not disappoint. Both times I've been, I had pork belly as an appetizer and steamed fish and crab curry as mains. The pork belly is tender and has such a clean taste, pairs well with the sauce. I usually find steamed fish to be boring, but the presentation (in a fish-shaped dish!) is so creative, and the spice and lime and cilantro really kick up the flavor. The crab curry is divine. LOVE the decor here - the fish lamps are so much fun! Make sure to check out the bathroom, too. Even that is beautifully decorated. Staff are friendly and helpful with the menu. A+

Really, a fantastic and fun experience. The service was fast, friendly, and informative, and the food was alive and delicious in a way that few places are. 

The pork cheeks are absolutely a must, and the crab curry is mind-bendingly spicy and delicious. The fried fish gets better and better as it absorbs the broth. Drinking prosecco while gorging on fiery, delicious thai food is an awesome way to spend an evening.

The wings were very good, but I've had better Thai-style chicken wings, where the skin was saltier and crisper. That said, I've also had much worse, almost all the time. Cocktails are great, and the raw oysters are delicious too, and a deal at $1 during happy hour (which goes until 7). 

All in all, we had a great time and will be back.

A friend of mine was in town and had found this restaurant in her search for a place for us to meet for dinner. I had high expectations for this place reading all the rave reviews (though sadly, the place failed to meet those expectations even though it was still very good).

The aesthetics of the restaurant are super cute. We sat at the bar, which was cozy but comfortable. There was no wait around 6:00 PM on a Monday night and didn't really get crowded until closer to 7:00.

Everything on the menu looked delicious, but the prices aren't exactly cheap, so we settled on getting three things - a dozen oysters, the beef tartare (Goi Nuaa), and the Coconut Crab Curry. We both also ordered a cocktail ($10 at Happy Hour) - the Blank Slate and the Butterfly Effect.

- Cocktails (5/5): The drinks were really nice. I had specifically asked the bartender which of the options were sweeter, and he helped me pick out the Blank Slate. It was very easy to drink and a nice complement to the meal.

- Oysters (5/5): I'd give this a 10/5 if I could. The oysters tasted very fresh, and the green sauce that it was served with was superb. 

- Beef Tartare (3/5): I'm always a little nervous to eat raw meat, but the texture of this made me forget that that was what I was eating. The chili on this really built up in spice the more you ate of it, but it was yummy and flavorful. The beef could have been a bit fattier or moist ... it tasted very dry by the end. Plantain chips were also a nice touch, though my friend actually preferred eating it with the complimentary fried chips.

- Coconut Crab Curry (2.5/5): I was expecting this dish to blow my mind ... except that it didn't. The flavors were alright, very creamy and spicy. However, it didn't really taste all that special, and if I were to return, I would definitely not be reordering.

Also, when we arrived, we weren't offered the complimentary fried chips. I'm not sure if it's something that you have to ask for, but I had to (since I saw that everyone else had a bowl on their table). All in all, I would really give this place 3.5 stars, but the $1 oysters and drinks helped to bump up my rating. :) Definitely try to go for Happy Hour if you can!
I fell in love with the calamari and am now heartbroken that they've taken it off the menu. Please bring it back!! The drinks are delicious and happy hour is a great deal.

Amazing spot! During my first visit here, my friend and I ordered the coconut crab curry, crab fried rice, and the steamed bass with Thai herbs to share. The fish was delicious and flavorful! The curry was spicy enough to enjoy, and the crab fried rice was good. 

We came during their happy hour, which is also when they open. The food was phenomenal and their drinks were really good. I enjoyed their mango drink but not really their watermelon spritz, because there was little to no prosecco in it. 

Our waiter was incredibly knowledgeable and didn't need to look at the menu once or check with the kitchen to answer any of our questions, which made me feel that he's tried everything on the menu and was giving us his honest opinion! The oysters were also amazing ($1 during HH).
