My most recent visit was on 4/12, and I pretty much ordered the same thing (see pics). I'm giving Fish Cheeks 5 stars because the service is great, the inside is bright and spacious, and the food is always phenomenal.

Best meal in NYC! Service was fast and food was so  good! We got the lobster curry and steamed fish. We came for happy hour so oysters were $1 each. The sauce and fried onions was the perfect combo. Ugh, so good I wish I was eating it right now. We loved it so much we came twice in 3 days. Can't wait to come back again!

If you're contemplating coming here just stop. GO! Your tastebuds will thank you, I promise.

If you love oysters, take advantage of their happy hour which is 12-7 with a small break in between I believe. They come with a delicious chimichurri sauce and fried shallots. Absolutely amazing.... I had 10!

Coconut crab curry is to die for. SUPER spicy though - even for someone who enjoys spicy food. I also had the crab fried rice... very tasty.

Our waitress was very nice and attentive.

My only complaint is that the place gets super cramped when it's busy. In order for my boyfriend and I to exit our seats, we had to ask the couple next to us to move their table over. But, the food so was so damn good that I didn't even care that much.

Definitely would love to come back and try their other menu options!!

Fried fish with sour orange curry: Bangkok style curry, crispy whole fish, krachai, napa cabbage, morning glory, sunflower sprouts, served with rice ⁣
Coconut Crab Curry: Southern style curry with crab meat, house-made curry paste and sea beans, served with rice⁣
⁣
I *think* this is supposed to be an authentic Thai place but I wouldn't know because I don't know Thai food. The flavours were all really strong and defined, so not really my type but it was a nice change in style. Definitely preferred the fried fish orange curry better than the coconut crab because it was slightly sweet (and I like fried fish) and SUPER spicy even with only one pepper. Crab curry had 2 peppers but wasn't as spicy. However, the crab was cooked very well whereas the fish was just slightly overcooked. ⁣

Overall the place was okay and I would like to try the steamed fish, crab aob wooden, or Khua Kling next time⁣

Finally a place that know how to treat a Branzino correctly !!!
Yes , not far from there Il buco alimentari used to do it but unfortunately not anymore.
Full fish deboned with no gimmicks or complicated sauces (they do serve it with peanut sauce on the side ,but not for me :)
Everyone who loves fish will get his money worth double and triple time!
I Started with zabb wings , spicy and delicious .
Great service and real comfortable and cosy space .
I always order the crab fried rice (best in NYC) and the crab curry (also the best in NYC). This place wins hands down for crab dishes.

The food is prepared fresh & packed with flavor, however the portions are small so I would probably rate this place on a $$$ scale rather than $$.
That aside, unique flavors & dishes, and amazing drinks. It's a smaller place so make a reservation and come in a group to try out all the dishes.

Came here for a friend's birthday dinner. And so glad I did. We pretty much got everything on the menu to try. Everything was great. The flavors were wonderful. The drinks are amazing. The waiter was nice. All in all a great experience. Would definitely recommend to friends. 

Some of my favorites include:
-coconut curry - the flavors in this are so intense it was unbelievably good. It is very spicy so beware. 
-crab fried rice - big fat chunks of crab in there. Put the coconut curry over this and it's bomb
-tiger prawns - so amazing you don't want to share. Each order comes with 3 pieces so make sure u order enough for the table. Trust me, no ones gonna want to share after the first bite.

I'm too Type A to wait 90 minutes for a table to "Break Bread" any where on the planet. 
That being said and I'm in The Bowery district of New York on a Saturday night at 8:00, I don't have a lot of choices going on here. So, my wife parked my butt at the Lobby Bar of the Bowery Hotel across the street from Fish Cheeks (where there was a 90 minute wait) and told me to slowly sip my beer and people watch and behave myself.

Guess what, it worked!  The text came from the restaurant saying our table was ready; and.....Oh Boy, was this worth the wait. 

I'm sort of a Thai food affecianado after years and years of flying to Thailand on business and eating this cuisine hundreds of times in The Motherland.

Fish Cheeks was just down right terrific, authentic and delicious. Everything was great:
*The Zaab fried chicken wings were super
*The Pomelo Salad was spicy as all get out but the tastes going on here along with the burn taking place was a treat
*The Crab Fried Rice was the best I've ever had, and I've had it all over the world
*The Pork Cheeks were served with a fish stock sauce that just worked in every possible way
*The Tiger Prawn Karee was by far my favorite dish. This one will keep bringing me back here for a long (long) time.

What else can I say about a place that just floored me? Not a whole lot, other than I highly recommend Fish Cheeks to all that will hear.

Cuisine: 6
Service: 7
Decor: 7
Value: 6
Overall: 6

Let's be honest, it's a Thai restaurant in downtown Manhattan. If you want truly authentic Thai food for a decent price, go to Woodside, Queens. Take a trip out there and try Ayada Thai, Sripraphai, Playground, and many more. However, if you're simply looking for some Thai cuisine that taste good and don't care about money, then this could be the place for you.

The space is long and narrow, with a bar in the back of the restaurant where the open kitchen is. The aromas of different Thai spices permeate the room. Everything was decent but nothing was special. The crab curry did have the largest lump crab meat I have ever seen, however the curry was so salty that I needed lots of water. Another dish was tasty, but a bit lost since it's spicier than anything I had in Bangkok. If they can fix up some of these problems, I would love to try those dishes again.

Colorful, fun decor. Friendly staff. Came here for the $1 oyster happy hour, which they have every day. I realize $1 oysters may be a loss leader but their oysters struck me as especially plain compared to similar happy hours I've enjoyed elsewhere.

Highly recommend coming with a crew so you can try an assortment of dishes. The fam got the set menu for 3 ($150) so we didn't have to think much about what to order cause we were HUNgry.

Apps - would get all of these again:

1. Zabb wings - I love wings, but I prefer wings with a dry rub vs. saucy (unpopular opinion amongst my friend group) so this was amaz imo. Spicy, salty, tangy. Drool. Don't be surprised to find me alone in a corner somewhere downing/hoarding 4 orders, at min., of these one day.
2. Grilled pork cheeks - super succulent, super generous portion, super good. Came with it's own sauce but we actually used the sauce from the pomelo salad too. 
3. Pomelo salad - flavor bomb with the sauce and crunchy dry aged fish + the sweetness of the pomelo was refreshing. I love pomelo but also side note, have you ever bought a pomelo and peeled it to find like almost nothing lol. It's a crapshoot, or maybe idk how to pick pomelos. Not that this was a problem here. This was great.

Entrees:

4. Coconut curry crab - creamy and spicy, yum, but wish there was more crab.
5. Crab fried rice - was supposed to be tiger prawn karee, but it wasn't available, sadness. Fried rice isn't usually something I order, however, I guess it was a good sub cause we ended up eating it with the curry and prawn Lon. Tho the sauces the rice came with added great flavor to the rice in addition to the sweetness from the crab meat. 
6. Prawn lon - also really yum, I liked the fresh vegetables on the side too. Cleanses the palate.
7. Grilled Branzino - this was cooked really well, the fish seemed really fresh. Paired with a peanut sauce. 

Also had the Thai iced coffee. Great for calming down the spice level when needed. 

I think I overused the word sauce in this review but would 10/10 drink shots of them cause they're so good and add great flavor to the dishes. But like acid reflux so maybe not. Or maybe after popping an antacid idk.

Will I come back to try the other offerings on the menu? 
Yis.

Amazing and authentic Thai food. Quick and delicious. Make sure to place a reservation as the restaurant fill up fast and has limited space. Luckily the bar was available and offers the full menu. Guillermo the bartender was very friendly and helpful. Can recommend the ouster happy hour for lunch, the Branzino, pomelo salad and the wings, especially paired with a Plantation Rum Old Fashioned with chocolate bitters. Went very well with the spices of the wings.

some of the best thai i have ever had and thats wild because i eat so much thai its kind of weird. anywho, everything here is pretty dang spicy so dont say i didnt warn you. happy hour is also a bargain if youre one of those people who can actually leave work at a decent hour you should try to go. couple gripes: i dont need to know that in two hours a party of 12 is coming in. dont rush me for no reason. secondly, plastic plates? cmon thats lame. had to knock this place a lil to bring it down to human level.

From entering the restaurant to receiving the check, everything was great. The host, bartender and our server were very warm and welcoming, and made us feel welcomed. Even though my group took forever to order our food and drinks, our sever was very patient and friendly. 

My cocktail, the Butterfly Effect, was fantastic and really beautiful. We ordered the happy hour $1 oysters to start and they were so good! Surprised by the quality. 

We ordered family style because there were too many things we all wanted to try. Ended up ordering the the Khua Kling, Tiger Prawn Karee, crab fried rice and vegan creek curry. All delicious, with portions big enough to satisfy 4 people. Topped the meal off with the desert (only one option, but it's a good one), the homemade coconut ice cream with fruit - delicious!

Totally in love with this place and will definitely be back during my next visit to New York!
Food was superb, Best Thai food in NYC, Fishcheeks have their own characters, can not find from somewhere else. So, high recommend for this place!!!!
Not worth the price.. disappointed! Food was okay and  the service was good :) not gonna come back for sure.

Best Thai I've had in the city. Been here twice and got the same thing both times, most places in NoHo are overpriced. This one was amazing. I love how everything has coconut in it. Get the crab fried rice it's amazing

Excellent food!

I went with a group of 4 at 5pm without a reservation and we were seated right away. 

We ordered a dozen of oyster ($1 for happy hour) pretty good deal! They served it with green sauce instead of cocktail sauce or mignonette. We also shared set 2 which came with Zabb wings, pomelo salad and pork cheeks. The wings was my favorite. As for the entree, we all decided that crub curry was the star of the meal. Big chunk of crab meat swimming in a very flavorful homemade curry sauce (be carful it is spicy) the service was also fast, friendly, and attentive. I would definitely be back!

This place is so yum! I came here with my girlfriends for a Sunday brunch/lunch and it was a 45 minute wait. They let us wait at the bar so it wasn't too bad, and time passed by relatively quickly.

The restaurant has cute, colorful decor with lots of sunlight. The four of us were seated comfortably in a corner and got right to ordering. They have $1 HH oysters everyday during lunch so my girlfriends jumped right on that (meanwhile I'm not really a huge oyster fan). They said the oysters, though a bit small, were super fresh and they liked the fried onions to top it with. As a table, we ordered grill pork cheeks (app), khua kling (spicy beef), and two coconut crab curries. While the waitress was taking our order, she warned us that everything we ordered is spicy -- she emphasized *Thai spicy* and we said that it was fine. Boyyyy was she not kidding. I thought the coconut crab curry was the perfect amount of spice, but the khua kling was actually super spicy!

The coconut crab curry is DELISH. Perfect amount of coconut and crab with a slight kick. There's no surprise why it's the most popular entree. The khua kling was also very good -- the combination of lemongrass and chili with tender beef created a flavorful dish with some serious heat. Two of my friends and I were fine until we had the khua kling...everything after that tasted 10x spicier. My other friend (with a high spice tolerance) found it all to be delicious, not affected by the spiciness. Even though I was sweating halfway through my meal, I will willingly and gladly do it all again.

Service was good, food was delicious, and I'm more than likely to come back and try other menu items! Also, heads up: cards only, no cash!

I don't even know where to start... The glass noodles with crab was sooooo good,
as was the steamed fish with Thai herbs! (Avoid the head, too many bones).  The crab curry was very good too, but not as good as the other two.  Serious flavor explosion!  We waited 15 minutes for our reservation and they comped a drink and gave us a dessert of coconut ice cream with jackfruit- also delicious!! Such a generous thing to do.  The staff and food are amazing, wish I could come back every week (day) ;).  No cash, only cards, that's a first- but better than the reverse .

One of my favorite meals in New York for sure. Came here for lunch with my boyfriend a little after 1 on Monday. The restaurant is cute and clean and was about half full. It was happy hour which was a nice surprise. We ordered a couple oysters ($1 on HH), the wings, corn salad, and the coconut crab curry. The small dishes arrived first and they were all bright and beautiful. The corn salad was full of color and flavor. It was spicy but balanced well with the sweet corn. The wings were also very good. I prefer wings with a dry rub so these were perfect. The wings were seasoned well and also very spicy.... they were addicting! The oyster was probably my favorite bite. My boyfriend and I love thai flavors - fish sauce, lime, cilantro, thai chilies so we were a big fan of this dish. The oyster was seasoned well and had fried shallots on top for a little texture. The crab curry came last and it was so flavorful and homey. It had huge chunks of crab and came with a bowl of rice. All in all, everything was delicious! My boyfriend and I wanted to try other dishes but knew we wouldn't be able to finish. Will for sure be back to try some of the fish dishes and get some more oysters!

This place had been on my list of places to try so I came here on a Monday evening with my friend. We were promptly seated by the bar with no wait which was nice. We had 7 minutes before happy hour ended so we got a couple oysters for $1. The oysters were ok. The sauce that was paired with it was delicious. The complimentary shrimp chip was a nice snack. We were there at 7 and the waitress told us there were several dishes they were out of. She literally pointed to half the menu so our options were limited. We got the pork cheeks which was the best thing we had. The zaab wings were disappointing. Remember the MAMA tom yum instant noodle packages where you would pour the sauce in the noodles and eat it like chips. The rub tasted like that and MSG. I'm not saying it's bad, but for upscale restaurant, could of been better. The coconut crab curry was very disspointing. For close to #30, there was curry, small chunks of crab meat and nothing else. What happened to the veggies? Service was also very slow with 2 servers running the whole place.

Came here twice in one week, so you know this place is yum. 

Definitely get the Zabb Wings. The dry rub coated fried wings had the right amount of saltiness, sweetness, and spiciness. It will for sure excite your taste buds. It was so good I asked if they sold the dry rub in jars. Unfortunately they do not, but if they did, I'd be the first to buy it. 

The Somtum Corn salad was not bad. The corn was super sweet and refreshing. 

The Coconut Crab Curry was delicious. I was surprisingly impressed because I never really liked curry enough to order a whole dish. When this dish came, it didn't look like there was crab. I was expecting crab pieces with the shell. After mixing the curry, there were chunks of crab meat on the bottom. Super delicious crab meat, but I wish there was more. I even had to order an extra side of rice to eat the curry with. 

Fried Porgy with Thai Garden Herbs was fun to eat. It was like a scavenger hunt getting to the fish meat covered in chilies, nuts, herbs, and greens while avoiding the bones. The sauce was light and refreshing. It had super small pieces of lime and what I think were mango pieces. I thought that the sauce was lacking acidity for me but it was still good. I would pass on this the next time I go. 

I was actually disappointed by the Crab Fried Rice. I thought it was bland. It didn't have wok flavor. It came with 2 sauces and it made the fried rice taste better. I really think that the fried rice should taste good on their own, without sauce. Pass, even though I love crab meat and fried rice. (I'd suggest going to Uncle Boons for Crab Fried Rice).

I really wanted to like the Manila Clams with Sweet Basil, but I felt that it was a small order and was missing sauce. I'd like to give this a second try, especially because I love seafood. 

I was super duper impressed with the Tiger Prawn Karee. I would simply describe this dish Tiger Prawn curry and scrambled eggs- a simple dish, but Fish Cheeks does it right! These are huge Tiger prawns served head-on. Too bad, there's only 3 of them to a dish. I want more! This by far is one of my favorite dishes here.

Pakboong Fai Dang is also an essential dish to order, wok fried morning glory. The first time I had it here, the wok flavor was on point, the second time not so much. It is still worth getting every time. I could just pour the sauce over rice and call it a day.

Market Oysters is a hit or miss. I've only come during happy hour and this is important to note. The first time, the oysters were acceptable in size for $1 each. The second time, I feel like I was duped. I wouldn't even count some as whole oysters. It was like I was being served premie oysters. Let's just say size may vary for a buck each.

Overall, food was good. Ambiance was nice. Wait staff was on point. 

TL;DR: Must get the wings, coconut crab curry, tiger prawn curry. Still come for happy hour $1 oysters even though size may vary.

Walked in on a whim and now I think it's one of my new favorite restaurants in NYC!! I've never had "real" Thai food so I really wasn't expecting much. Everything we tried was so delicious and fresh. I will definitely be back!

After paying $40/person just for food, we realized that the only thing we could really eat was oysters.  Everything we ordered burned our mouth including Crab Curry and left most of them after a few bytes.  We left the restaurant kind of hungry.  The menu had no warning about how hot the food were.

The food and wait staff are both A+! I am so happy I ate here! I don't know what to say except that I love this place. My husband and I split the pre fixe and we got appetizers of hot wings and a corn salad. The hot wings were good but not a plate revelation (skip worthy). The corn salad was AMAZING. I have never eaten anything like it before and I am still thinking about it. The chillis and corn and green beans just perfectly balanced off each other in synchrony. Then the soup course ... wow that lemongrass fish soup was so flavorful! With huge chunks of fish and mushrooms. And the lemongrass flavor just accented everything perfectly! Then the next course was crab fried rice ...WOW! The flavors just popped and the crab simply accented the dish perfectly. Then the final part, the curried sea bass. I was so full by this point but I HAD to eat the sea bass. It just was phenomenal and the curry PERFECTLY complimented the fish that melted in my mouth. I definitely want to try more fishes next time. I had such a great experience! Also the spicy mango cocktail was terrific. I am worried about reviewing this place because it might make it too popular to come here going forward!

I work down the street and I'm here at least once a week. Spicy food upsets my stomach but this is worth it. 

I've never had a bad experience here. The food is consistently great, servers are attentive, and the drinks are nice and strong. I always order the oysters (the nam jim seafood sauce is crack), crab fried rice, coconut crab curry, and the coconut ice cream for dessert. Their dishes are meant for sharing, and are in generous portions. The coconut crab curry is not for spice beginners and is Asian-level spicy. You've been warned.

My friend from Thailand took me here - it's his go-to restaurant and I get why! This is by far the best Thai experience I had in the United States. We shared the steamed fish and Goong Aob Woonsen (glass noodle with shrimp) and they were both phenomenal. If it weren't for my friend I wouldn't have been able to discover this restaurant. 

It's a bit above my usual price range so I probably won't be here as often as I want to, but I cannot wait to go back.

Food was great but the service was slow and they did not listen to dietary restrictions. The first round of drinks came after the appetizers. It generally took 20-30min to get each round of drinks. After expressing our concerns with the manager, he did almost nothing for us despite our dissatisfaction.

Edible kick boxing 
What a night I endured at the colorful yet hidden site in NoHo ; collected yet bountiful is the best way to describe my first experience at Fish Cheeks. After a cold blistering day , the flavors FC provided definitely fueled the fire in the commute home. Coinciding with my analogy above ; everything down to the freshly made limeade had a beautiful hit to it. I'm not one for spoilers but I'll definitely tell anyone what I ordered and also highly suggest for the first timer.  Limeade , Oysters x4 , zabbwings!!!, coconut crab curry and their beautiful eye opening/goosebump inducing approach at morning glory.  Story time over, Also get the coffee before you leave.

Now the name does not scream anything authentic at all about this place, but I must say, it has to have been one of the best Thai food experiences I have had in quite a long time!  This place had that distinct taste that you can't find a lot in the US, but this place had it!  It's so hard to explain, if you know, you just know.  

You must get the crab curry!  Right?  Crab curry?  I have never had such a thing so I was very intrigued to try it, especially Thai-style curry!  We also got the Pakboong fai dang, which is wok-stir-fried green and it is amazing.  A dish as simple as this and yet to flavorful, my first bite, I was hooked!  Highly recommend!  

Now my experience here was actually kind of a disappointment.  I had ordered Seabass curry, but instead we got a branzino.  The waiter saw and knew he made a mistake and took the fish back.  We waited about 30 minutes for the seabass to arrive and to our disappointment yet again, the fish was undercooked and still raw, and was taken back again.  Well by this time, it would have taken another 30-45 minutes to get this fish again, and we decided to just cancel the order.  Because of this mistake, we were offered a few other dishes, dessert, a round of drinks and a discounted price from the check.  Now that's amazing customer service!  

Even with my misfortunate experience, based solely on the food quality and taste, and their excellent service, I will definitely come here and dine again and also recommend to many friends who want a good Thai food meal!  Can't wait till I get to taste that yummy crab curry again!
Just take my money. Please! Some of the BEST Thai food I've eaten in the states. Highly recommend the branzino, crab curry, and morning glories!

Man oh man! I'm so delighted I came to this place. Cute spot. Love the decor in this establishment. So cute! I came to try the fish in Thai spices . Also the curry crab dip . Whew ! DELICIOUS! Just the right spice. Service I have no complaints everyone was polite and persistent about making sure we were good and satisfied with our order. Desert was to die for. Jackfruit ice cream, wow never tasted anything like it! More than satisfied with Fish cheeks! I'll be returning for sure!

Fish Cheeks handsdown is one the best, most unique Thai restaurants in the city. When you hear "Thai," you expect Pad Thai and drunken noodles, but Fish Cheeks is a culinary experience above and beyond. Every time I come to fish cheeks, I get the Chef's Selections Set. At around $45 a person, it's definitely on the pricey side of dinners, but it's WORTH IT. The Chef's selections sets are 1000% worth the price for the amount of food you get, and you get to try so many different things on the menu! The Crab Curry is pretty darn spicy, but it is DELICIOUS. The Zabb Wings are uniquely flavored, crispy and juicy. The grilled pork cheeks are also to die for. Go to Fish Cheeks, you won't regret it.

(1) Clam with curry and basil (2) crab curry. The 2 Thai dishes I haven't had in more than 2 years. Both were amazing. No PadThai here lol (too common).

If they can make omelette as an option to go with curry will make it really nice. The place can get filled pretty quick so you need to make reservation. 

Great place and atmosphere.
Delicious Thai food, definitely try the oysters in Thai style. The food is delicious.
So, so good.  Everything we ordered was amazing!  Calamari, steamed fish, crab curry and sautéed morning glory won't disappoint.  Reservations are a must.  Can't wait to go back!

Favorite thai place in the city! Let's start with this place is super hip and they have happy hours where they serve one dollar oysters and half priced drinks. Their food is amazing and one of the most authentic Thai cuisines in the city. The coconut crab curry is legit spicy. Like really really spicy!!! So please don't order it if you can't handle your spice haha the steamed sea bass is amazing and I loveeeee their crab fried rice. Get the shrimp with vermicelli clay pot omgggg soooo delish!!!!

Absolutely amazing food. So flavorful!!! I would come here every time I visit NYC  the steamed fish was the best steamed fish I've ever had. Pomelo salad perfectly compliments every dish with a hint of sweet and tangy. Love it

Very casual place with happy color chairs and white walls.  This is my 3rd time here since they opened maybe 3 years ago now?? More??

I still like the place.  My favorite now is the oysters with the cilantro garlic sauce you put on top.

The mild grilled pork cheeks goes well with their fish sauce based spicy dip. 

The crab meat has a lot of sauce than crab but it is very good.

I love the shrimp salad - it has about 6 pieces of large shrimp and a dressing that's indescribably good.  Mild.

It's a go to place.  Good food!

I love this place!!! I had marked this place for a year, and I finally tried it. I found this place one day after shopping in soho, this place and the name are pretty interesting.

You better reserve the place before coming. Otherwise you will sit near kitchen or at the bar.

Decoration: I love this restaurant's decoration! You see "fish" everywhere. The bathroom is very clean with flower wall paper, and fish faucet. They also have a candle lighted in the bathroom.

Food: $1 oyster with their special sauce is super good!!! Recommend!

Well, each dish is not very big... so you may need to order two or three for a group of two. 

Fried chicken is good as appetizer. Tom yum goong is spicy, and not as good as I expected. Crab curry is very good. Shrimp and noodle is so good.
We ordered the set 1 which came with shrimp, calamari, clams, coconut crab curry, and noodles. Huge amount of food and each dish was exceptional

Made a reservation for 2 at 6pm in a Wednesday night, but the restaurant was only about half full. By the time we left around 7:30/8, it was completely full, including the small bar.

Water and complimentary shrimp chips with a small dish of thick, spicy-ish dipping sauce were brought to our table immediately.

Happy hour from 5-7pm included discounted drinks and $1 oysters.

We drank ($10 hh price, $14 regular):
Guava Smash - A
Spicy Mango - A

We ate:
Coconut Crab Curry - A (slightly spicy but not painful spicy)
Goong Aob Woonsen - B- (The ingredients didn't meld together into a unified dish. It came with some green sauce for the shrimp and pork belly, but that didn't wow us.)

I've heard so many great things about Fish Cheeks so I was really happy to have snagged a reservation for a party of 7 on a Wednesday evening. (BTW, definitely call them directly if you're trying to book a large-ish party...they didn't have an opening when I tried online). They have great service and are super accommodating. 

Now, onto the food. Here are some pro's: 
- Menu has plenty of options for meat eaters, fish lovers, and even vegans (clearly marked). Was pleasantly surprised considering the name of the restaurant. Overall, a well rounded menu with very differently spiced and flavored foods. 
- Steamed fish was excellent and the plating was super cute 
- Tasty vegan corn salad 
- Great toppings on the ice cream
- Cute decor - fish themed lights, what a nice touch!

Here's why I gave it a 3: 
- Portions are really small for the price point. Our waiter was kind enough to warn us about the portion size but still, I was expecting more than a little bowl of curry for #23 (I'm looking at you, coconut crab curry) 
- Some of the dishes were rather forgettable. The fried rice seemed okay and the beef, while very spicy (In a good way) was not anything I would rush to return to. 
- Minor gripe, but they ran out of duck by 7:30. 

Simply put, the price point for size of entree turned me off... perhaps there's too much hype.

Super-super duper. I came here by happenstance on early in the afternoon on New Year's Day; I hadn't been in the neighborhood in a few months and walked down Bond St. intending to go to Mile End. But it has closed, so I took a look at Fish Cheeks next door. It wasn't too crowded, so I had a seat at the bar and ordered the Phlaa Salmon and the Manila Clams. OMG.

The salmon has such a robust flavor profile (citrus, chili, a hint of mint) and the clams have an incredible garlicky-milk broth. I soaked the latter up with white rice. I hear that the coconut crab curry is their signature, and perhaps I will try it on my return trip. But I'll be dreaming for some time about those two dishes I just had, so it will be a tough call. 

An incredible meal to kick off 2019.

Visited Fish Cheek for the second time and there were some tweaks to the winter menu. Be warned the three chili symbol is not for the faint of the heart and I can attest that they are some of spicest Thai dishes that I've ever tried. In particular, Khua Kling, which means stir fry in Thai, is the mother lode of all spicy dishes. Some might find them too spicy, but this is the type of food I crave. Po Tak is another one of my favorite this time. Extremely herby and aromatic, perfect for the season.

Came here for a friends birthday dinner.  Ambiance made the restaurant seem really cozy.  

No noodles here, which you might expect at a Thai restaurant, but even so, the menu is fantastic.

I have heard great things about the oysters and will have to have some next time i am in the area.

We had the Coconut Crab Curry, Corn Salad, the Fried Fish with Thai Garden Herbs, Sauteed Cabbage, and a few other items.

Everything was super fresh, super flavorful, and extremely delicious.  We were also with someone who had a shellfish allergy, and the staff was wonderful about accommodating this with the non-shellfish dishes we ordered.  They even let us know when we originally ordered a couple of small items that we did not think had shellfish in them did.  Our server checked with the chef and came right over to let us know that certain things they used in the dish would have shellfish  and recommended something else. This is really appreciated and not something you see at every restaurant.

Was not too expensive, service was fantastic, and the portions were decent sized!

I highly recommend Fish Cheeks to anyone in the area! I know I would certainly enjoy coming back.

Came here because of a friends suggestion and I cannot rave enough. The food was great (some dishes are on the spicy side but not intolerable, but they do indicate which ones on menu). 
Drinks: we had the yummy sticky rice cocktails, which were sweet and not too strong and the cheeky mule which was a little too strong for my taste but not bad. 
 Appetizer: we had the calamari which was different than expected but very delicious none the less.
 Dinner: we had the crab fried rice, the duck confit hungley curry, and the mussels and herbs, all of which I highly recommend. The place was pretty packed so make sure you have a reservation.

I finally tried the fish cheeks after hearing rave reviews from my friends who are regulars. It's a cute little spot with a cozy inviting atmosphere. The food is fragrant with fish sauce smells lingering in the air.

The best things here according to my friends are
The coconut crab curry and the morning glory. They were very good but my favorite is the steamed  fish (bass). I also enjoyed the crab fried rice.

Instead of fish cheeks we ate pork cheeks which were alright. The food is flavorful and sticks to you for a while. Fair warning if you plan on going out after a meal like this.

We went during the daily HH which is a good deal. $1 oysters and $5 beers.

A must try: chicken wings!! Really good and special taste. The crab curry is good too. I'm not a fan of the squid since it's too sweet with too much syrup on them. All in all, a good restaurant deserve visit.
Hands down the best Thai food in NYC, if not the US!! Favorites are pork cheeks, crab curry, fried snapper, crab fried rice and corn salad.

I made a reservation through Resy and I called the day of my reservation to confirm and they tell me it was cancelled through Resy and they had no available seats for the night. To my surprise I wasnt aware and super annoyed because I received a text message from Resy to confirm my reservation which I did, but they say somehow in the system it was "cancelled". I never got a cancellation from Resy nor the restaurant. They were not helpful at all and I believe I spoke to the manager as well and she didn't try to accommodate.  Seriously - customer service is part of your job and should at-least try to accommodate when it wasn't the customers fault and it was something with their system. Terrible and really ruined my plans.

I followed the hype and decided to give this place a try. Walked 10 mins from SoHo. Was extremely disappointed. 

The signature dish, Crab Curry Coconut, contains awkwardly little crab meat, little vegetables, but high on MSG and curry powder. That's not how reputable Thai curry works. 

The koong aob woonsen (shrimp glass noodle) is the worst I've had in Thailand, Thai Town (Los Angeles), or any surviving Thai restaurants. Don't take my words on the taste, as this can easily be observed on the pictures, wherein the shrimps are so awkwardly (again) minuscule. 

$1 oyster for happy hour are fine. The complimentary fried chips/chili dipped are fine as well. 

I would say, this place might be good for alcohol, as can be seen by the many customers happily getting the mixed drinks. However, in terms of the quality, value, authenticity of the dishes, it definitely requires a lot more work.

It is very Thai, much less adjusted for American taste. So when they say something is spicy, it is REAL spicy. 

We follow other people suggestion and order the wings, crab fried rice, Tom yum soup and the veggie side. All very good. The portion is a bit smaller than expected given the price. But the soup has a bunch of seafood in it. The quality of the material they use are very good. Service is also great. I just look around and someone who is not designated my server come and ask if I need any service. I would suggest to make reservation.

This might be my favorite restaurant in NYC right now (high praise I know). I came here with a group of 5, so we were able to try a bunch of dishes.

- Happy hour oysters
- Zabb wings
- Grilled pork cheeks
- Coconut crab
- Fried snapper
- Crab fried rice
- Goong aob woonsen
- Pakboong fai dang

If I were to talk about each of these, this review would turn into an essay, so I'll focus on my favorites.

The zabb wings were AMAZING. These dry rub fried chicken wings were perfectly crispy and had a nice kick of spice. This appetizer definitely started the meal strong.

The next appetizer of grilled pork cheeks kept the bar high. The meat was both tender and flavorful.

While the main courses didn't impress me quite as much as the appetizers, they were still great. In particular, I enjoyed the goong aob woonsen.

We decided to order a side pakboong fai dang so we could have some greens in our meal. I didn't expect much out of this dish, but I actually loved this. It's always nice when veggies taste good :D

I always come here with friends for the dinner. It's really awesome authentic Thai foods in the city. We had such a great time and enjoyed the food so much. Especially, staffs were very friendly and accommodating. 

We ordered one dozen of happy hour oysters which were fresh and came with tasty spicy green sauce. 

Everything was so great. We will definitely get back again.

I would rate this at 3.5 stars, my friends who absolutely love this restaurant took me here. Maybe in my head I had it overhyped a little, it was great...but was it the best Thai food that I have ever eaten? Probably not. Tried the fried snapper, crab curry and steamed fish. I think I liked the fried snapper the best of the 3 dishes.

A true five star experience!! I'm quite familiar with Thai food (traveled there a few times and lived for a month) and surprisingly this is the first time i try it in NYC. But i'm glad i found the right spot to start! Instead of authentic, I would describe this place as an upgraded Thai. The coconut curry crab is a must-try, as opposed to a whole crab, it came in pieces of crab meat in a bowl of curry. Much easier for westerners (or anyone who's not an expert at eating crabs) to devour, the portion looks small on the eyes but it's actually enough for two people to pair with rice. I LOVE how they keep the original spicy level and they DONT tone it down. I think it shows confidence and integrity in their food. I would personally prefer a whole crab, because other than the getting hands dirty part, I think the whole crab might be slightly more tasty and fishy, which would balance out the spiciness, right now the curry is a bit overpowering, though it's still delicious. We also got the wings and the pork butt, both are very delicious! My bf is freakishly scared of touching food and he was using his hands to eat the wings, that's how good they are. No batter, no dipping, just pure goodness  Their menu is not lengthy as most Thai restaurants but i guess it's easier for people to choose from and they can also focus on what they excel. Another highlight is the service. Our waiter is very knowledgeable, efficient, friendly and professional, probably enthusiastic about food as we are too. He deserves every tips he made and I hope the restaurant is paying him well.

I'm not entirely sure what authentic Thai food is supposed to taste like, but several people who have visited Thailand told me this is the spot to go to for quality Thai food in NYC, and they were so right! 

They serve some shrimp crackers in the beginning which was cool, I haven't had those in so long! They were your standard chips you can get at the supermarket. 

As for our real appetizers, we started off with the calamari and pork cheeks. I've actually never had pork cheeks until then and it was so tender. For our main dishes we got the coconut crab curry and the steamed fish with Thai herbs. I was so excited when I saw that the steamed fish came out in the heated dish that they do in Asia and it was the whole fish. I would highly recommend this place, great quality food.

We came here in a chilly Tuesday night and was promptly seated before my reservation. My girlfriend wasn't there yet but they didn't make me wait for my full party. Off to a great start. 

We started with shrimp crackers and green sauce. The shrimp crackers were nothing special but the shrimp paste that came with it was delicious. 

We ordered the happy hour oysters which came with ridiculously good green sauce. So garlicky and amazing. We also ordered the zabb wings, coconut crab curry, hungley curry, and pakboong fair daeng.

The crab curry is spicy and amazing. The pakboong was also very delicious. We will definitely be back. Well worth the price and none of the wait.

Cool vibe, tiny tables, not enough flavor 

Maybe the menu writer is just too good at making all the dishes sound amazing but what we ordered did not live up to its descriptions. Flavors are lacking in mostly every dish which is pretty crazy given we ordered curry and this is a Thai restaurant. Perhaps my expectations were too high or we didn't order the right dishes or maybe the saltiness had masked everything else but for the price point - this definitely isn't something worth coming back for.

With Chrissy Teigen's endorsement as her favorite Thai restaurant in New York, it's difficult not to have high standards for this place. Fortunately, Fish Cheeks lived up to the hype. 
Interior is very adorable, with brightly colored decor, making it look like a beach-side eatery. 
I've been here a few times now, and both times Fish Cheeks delivered delicious cuisine. I have a high tolerance for spicy food, and across several dishes ordered, Fish Cheeks had me sweating and reaching for tissues. 
Something not to be missed is the oyster happy hour - $1 for oysters between 5-7pm, which is an unbeatable deal. A great thing about the restaurant is that they have dishes not usually found on other Thai restaurant menus. Standout dish here is the crab curry, rich, creamy, spicy, and satisfying. 
Service is very friendly, but a minor slipup occurred when they forgot to bring us complimentary prawn crackers at the beginning of the meal, watched others around us receive them, and have to ask for ours later on. Otherwise, this restaurant is great and would recommend to anyone looking for a unique Thai meal.

This restaurant is pretty authentic according to my Thai friends I ate with. The food was really delicious at an ok price.  The only thing that didn't make it a 5 star experience was the waiter.  He was not that friendly and didn't do much (we asked other waiters for favors).  Overall, I would go again. Definitely recommend for authentic tasting Thai food.

lady bartender is badass
chef man works hard
crab cherry with two pepper signs will burn your stomach
calamari appetizer remains dessert like
It delicious
i had a good time per usual and wonder what three pepper sign tastes like
its pretty hot, no kidding
A solid Thai place to go to. Food was great, but a tad salty. Lovely ambiance and my go to when around the neighborhood.
Authentic Thai food. Different than other 99% Thai restaurants you could find in America. Recommend the collection menu, can try a variety of authentic Thai at one time.

Let me start on the deserved note... W-O-W!!! Unpretentious ambience yet very pleasant to anybody's visual senses with superbly delicious seafood and a fun drink menu. Let me repeat that...DELICIOUS food!! This is a place to keep in your favorites' list for as long as life perdures. I cannot wait to go back!!! :)

My wife and I went here tonight and it is delicious.  My favorite dish was the steamed fish.  I highly recommend it.  We started off with the chicken wings as an app and had the coconut crab curry and the steamed fish for our mains.  I think this is the best Thai I've had in a while.

Also we dined early because it was harder to get reservations.  It was happy hour!  A glass of wine for 8 and a beer for 5.  One dollar oysters!! This place was really solid.  

They have an open kitchen.  Everything is clean.  I definitely will be back.  Worth a visit!

One of my favorite places in the city for authentic Thai! Small little cozy place. Some of my favorite dishes include the pork belly, crab fried rice and the whole cilantro lime fish! Lots of flavor and deliciousness! :)

Loved the food here. We ate the fried snapper with garden herbs ( to die for) Po tak and the grilled Branzino. The fish was amazingly fresh and the flavors were so good. One of my most favorite restaurants in nyc.

Lovely place
Good food
Small dishes
Like their Thai tea

Seems famous for their seafood, but honestly there were not so much seafood in the dish...which made me feel the price was a little high
Three girls spent $40+ per person

I really liked it here! My friend and I dropped in after boxing class upstairs (Box+Flow studios) on a Sunday right when they opened at noon. 

We didn't have reservations but because we got there as soon as they opened they sat us right away. It didn't get super crowded but a lot of people filed in shortly after. 

The ambience here is very bright and fairly quiet even with lots of people inside. It's colorful and boaty. 

The food seems to be a modern twist on Thai food with of course a big focus on seafood. We got the $1 oysters happy hour deal, calamari, and the HH $5 beers!

Oysters were great. I loved the sauce they came with + the crunchy fried garlic. I've never had my oysters with fried garlic before. The soft + crunchy combo is great. 


The calamari comes in deep fried balls covered in a tamarind sauce. They initially looked like chicken tenders or fried chicken ball/nuggets so we thought they had brought us the wrong thing. But now I want all my calamari in this easy bite shape.

We only ordered from the apps menu. It looked like the entrees were meant to be tapas style shared between two people. 

I definitely want to come back and try their main dishes.

This place is above and beyond. Every dish was spot on delicious not to mention the excellent service. We were a group of 5 and ordered a whole bunch of dishes. Appetizers: sumtom corn salad, zabb wings, phlaa salmon, yum goong. Mains: crab fried Rice, steamed fish with Thai herbs, khua kling, sautéed cabbage
Our stomachs were happy and were in total food coma bliss. 

This place was a random find and what a treasure it is!!! Already making plans to get back there and try the other dishes!

This meal was absolutely incredible and THE most authentic Thai experience I've had in New York. My husband and I had our honeymoon in Thailand and this meal brought us right back. Everything was absolutely perfect, from the atmosphere to the service (Corey-- you rock!) to the food. Overall, this was worth every penny and we had an amazingly wonderful time. 10/10 for Fish Cheeks!!!!!!

Stopped by this place on a Wednesday night since I was in the mood for some Thai food and heard great stuff about this place. Unfortunately, because we hadn't made reservation (place gets booked fast)  and walked in, the waiter was able to find us a table but had to leave in an hour and half. 
The place has a nice vibe to it including the decoration. Waiters are super friendly and accommodating. Although the menu is limited, it has great options. I will definitely return to try other food options.

Gaeng Tai Pla is one of my absolute favorite dishes, it's Southern Thai influenced by Southern Indian, it's typically amazingly overwhelming with flavor, because it's made with fermented fish innards, it's typically loaded with paprika & shrimp paste & turmeric & galangal & lemongrass & kaffir lime & garlic & shallots, it's very salty and very peppery, you can smell it a mile away, and it's spectacular. Some recipes even load it up with vegetables. But the version I had here tonight was disappointing; it certainly packed a lot of heat, but the flavor was very muted, and the vegetables were very skimpy. If they're going to serve this dish, I wish they'd do it all the way, this felt very safe & was too expensive. 

We also ordered the Khua Kling, which was much better, much more faithful to the spirit of the dish, but once again I felt it was a bit too expensive.

I will return again and again for the amazing Oyster Happy Hour, and I will continue ordering new entrees here & there; I have high hopes, because the cooks are definitely risk takers, but I wish they'd stick to their guns a bit more with less compromise.

Food was awesome, ambiance was great, service was even better. We had the pork cheeks, crab fried rice, coconut curry & coconut ice cream- all was amazing.

I highly recommend!
Done take out a couple times from here.  It is really amazing.  They have a rice with crab dish that is to die for (and it is pretty good for delivery).

If you like seafood, and spicy food this is a great place to come to. This place definitely has an authentic thai taste to it. Every dish I ordered was really flavorful and super spicy espically the raw salmon dish, and the crab coconut curry. The wings were really good, and so were the clams. Definitely great place to go to, and their happy hour and 1 dollar oyster are a great deal.

Incredible food and fun presentation! We were lucky to snag a few seats at the bar on a busy Friday night and had great service for a full dinner and drinks. The bartender was helpful recommending dishes to us which included oysters, Yum Goong, Steamed Fish, and a side of Pakboong fai dang. We were really impressed by all the dishes but I was most impressed by the side dish Pakboong fai dang which is wok fried morning glory. It was so delicious even on its own and had a nice spice to it. The second favorite was the Steamed Fish entree which came on a platter still cooking in front of us. I'm already planning to go back for happy hour oysters and to work my way through the menu.

Wow! Delicious!
A rainy evening in NYC and was craving some comfort food. Decided to stay in and order delivery. Was not disappointed! Absolutely fantastic.
Ordered the coconut crab curry and the corn salad. At first was surprised by the small portion of the curry but in the end was relieved because the curry was so rich and tasty it was definitely enough for one person. 
Can't wait to go back to try what else this hot spot has to offer.

I discovered fish cheeks through Chrissy Teigen as it was one of her favorite Thai restaurants in NYC! She poked fun that this Thai restaurant doesn't serve the standard Pad Thai fare. 

I was pleasantly delighted at our food spread. So delicious and plenty left over for next day's lunch. 

Some favorites were the coconut crab curry, crispy friend branzino and mussels. I hear great things about their happy hour and I'm eager to try more dishes!

Love this place. The Tom Yum soup was mouthwatering and so flavorful. The fish entree's presentation was really nice. The bartender was very nice and attentive as well. I would highly recommend this place if you're looking for an excellent Thai restaurant in the East Village. It gets very busy so I would suggest  you make a reservation in advance, but they also have a bar which is first come, first serve basis. I would definitely dine here again if I am in the area. I think if you like spice, Tom Yum soup is definitely a must! The crab fried rice is great too as well as their oysters. They put their special sauce on the oysters, so it gives it a punch of flavor and tasty.
Best Thai food everrrr! My favorite is the steamed fish with thai herbs. It is extremely tasty and flavorful.

This place was a winner. We sat at the bar because it was packed that night but it still felt like a nice atmosphere to eat and the bartender was incredibly helpful in advising us what to order.  The coconut curry was very spicy but so tasty. We also got a rice dish which was great and combined perfectly with the curry. It reminded me of dishes I had in Thailand. I definitely plan to return.

Had the chicken wings, pork cheeks, shrimp in 3 sauces, crab curry, crab fried rice, the soup, steamed fish and the mango sticky rice. Every dish was very good. The crab curry is very spicy though. The service was fantastic as well. Definitely plan on coming again.
Very nice service. Super flavorful dish and clean. Crab soup is very salty and little bit of crab.

It was a beautiful end of the summer Wednesday night. Fish Cheeks is the best place in my opinion to get Thai seafood in NYC.

To be honest, everything we ordered here was amazing!!!! I love Steamed fish with Thai herbs, Seafood Pad Cha was great and i also ordered Grilled Branzino.

Fish Cheeks is a great ambiance, food, service!!

Came here a few times. Every time I came here with kids the girl host and the gentlemen always looking so upset. If your so unhappy please don't work in a environment where you have to deal with people. 

Food is amazing here but it's a bit too salty. Potions are very small. Love the oysters, fried calamari, steamed fish, mussels, and pork cheeks was all good! 

I recommend if your coming here don't bring any kids. They will have a upset face.
Everything is fantastic. From the fried snapper to the pork to the chicken wings. Not traditional Thai but it was modern innovative Thai which is the best.

The mango sticky rice is heavenly 
The whole fish was packed with flavor - lemongrass, crispy onions, cashews. If nothing else, stop in and have the sticky rice for dessert!!

If you love seafood and bold flavors, this is the place for you! 
TLDR: Go between 12-4pm or 5-7pm for the $1 oysters! And get the pork cheeks! 

My friend and I came for restaurant week and there were no more slots for a reservation so we decided to just walk in. I got there around 5:20pm on a Friday afternoon and the wait was about 1.5 hours. Try to make a reservation if you can! Or be prepared to wait. 

We ended up making it in before 7pm and started off with $1 oysters. I think what I liked best about these weren't the oysters themselves but the condiments they served with them, which wasn't your traditional cocktail sauce and lemon. Instead it was some sort of cilantro sauce with crispy garlic chips. The zesty, sort of spicy, refreshing cilantro is what made it so special.

We ordered the shrimp in 3 crab sauce, the pork cheeks, the coconut crab curry, the grilled branzino, the mango sticky rice, and the coconut icecream. 

Shrimp in 3 crab sauce: the sauce itself was bomb! lime, chili, mint. yum. The raw shrimp however was very gooey and became sticky the more you chewed it. Wasn't a huge fan of the texture.

Pork Cheeks: So tender, loved the flavor of the char and crispy skin

Grilled Branzino: Again, the garlic peanut sauce was the standout aspect of this dish

Coconut Crab Curry: Definitely packed a punch. Very spicy. Wish there were more chunks of crab in here

Mango with sticky rice: Pretty standard and solid, can't go wrong here.

Coconut Icecream: Very refreshing, not your usual artificial coconut flavor.

I'd definitely come back to try their lobster and their zabb wings which looked good!

Fish Cheeks has a small storefront on Bond St that serves up authentic Thai food with no mercy in the spice department: this is a compliment! There is daily happy hour including drinks and $1 oysters from 12-4pm and 5-7pm that is also available at the sit down tables, not just the bar. 

Vegan and vegetarian options also available. My favorites include: favorites included the chicken wings, coconut crab curry, pork cheeks, spicy mango cocktail, and the branzino.

The menu is divided for a family style meal for groups of two, three and more. Not in a sharing mood? Just order ala cart instead.

We visited during Restaurant Week and ordered from their special menu. But first, we started with some happy hour $1 oysters, which were about what you should expect from happy hour $1 oysters. Satisfactory.

Spicy mango cocktail was fantastic. 

We had the 3 shrimp sauce appetizer--which came with sliced little red peppers and it packed a punch. But in a tasty and good way. Pork cheeks were okay. Tasty, but overpowered by the rest of our food. 

The Branzini entree was good, but not memorable. The Coconut Crab meat Curry? More please. Except, if we'd have had any more we probably wouldn't be feeling our tongues until the weekend. It was one of the most flavorful, interesting dishes I've had in some time. Worth going back for. 

Interesting low-key atmosphere, but very friendly and competent service. Highly recommend.

LAST FRIDAY, I made a reservation for four people for today.  Around 15 minutes before my reservation, I received a text reminding me and saying they'd hold my table for 15 minutes.  We arrived on time and the hostess told us that they were overbooked due to a glitch in the reservation system and that we would need to wait for 1.5 hours.  Meanwhile there were several empty tables.  Granted they had just opened a half-hour before and a lot of those were probably reserved but when we responded with a resounding "No", the hostess was nonplussed.  She didn't apologize or care in the slightest.  So we took our business elsewhere and plan on keeping it that way.

My friend and I did a walk in, and we were seated at the bar. I'm giving three stars because the food is actually very good. However, the bartender that was serving us did not give us much accommodation. He pretty much ignored us the whole meal, and when I tired to ask him for cocktail recommendations, he just simply told us everything is good, which is not a good answer.

The food is nothing particular. Never talk to the bartender who has weird long greasy hair. I've never met anyone so rude like him. He's rude to your face. We give him our check first and he straight up ignored us and took the one right next to us. Very salty and unfriendly and snobby to be honest. Bad service over all.

Really good food! We ordered the steamed fish, mushrooms with glass noddle and crab curry. Everything was tasty, especially the fish and the mushroom. They also have the $1 oyster happy hour which was fantastic!
My only complaint is that the portion was small. The service and the atmosphere were good.

I was dreaming about this place long before I set foot inside! I made a reservation for 2 on a hot and humid Friday night. We came a bit early but they seated us immediately. This place is small and loud. So if you can't handle loud meals, still come. It's that's good. We ordered the short rib massaman curry ($25) and the crab fried rice ($24). We wanted to also order the Manila clams ($19) but they were sold out for the night! I was physically upset about this. I'll get it next time! The food was bomb, the service was bomb, the dessert was heavenly. We got the coconut ice cream($9). All of this was more than enough for 2 people, although I wish I had a larger appetite because the table next to us ordered the entire menu and I was very very jealous. I'll be back! I already made a res for those clams...

Completely and utterly obsessed with this place! The ambiance was nice, the waitress was extremely helpful and friendly, and not to mention the food has to be hands down the best, most authentic Thai food I have had. We got the shrimp in 3 crab sauce, curry crab, calamari, and the mango sweet sticky rice. 

The shrimp dish was tasty but not a huge fan of raw food so I am a little bias. The calamari was more like sweet popcorn chicken batter which was a unique and interesting taste. The curry crab was by far my favor. It was a little on the spicier side but very flavorful. Can't wait to come back to try more dishes!!

A real great deal for happy hour oysters! I believe there's only one type of oysters but the House made condiments that goes with it makes up for all that. The food was really tasty as well even though a little pricey but totally worth it!

Fantastic happy hour oysters, with a Thai twist.  Their spicy green sauce and frizzled shallots made the bivalves sing.  Also, noncheesy, super cheerful fish scale themed decor! A girlfriend who lives in the nabe recently introduced me to this lovely place, and I'm already plotting my return.

The food was uniformly amazing, and the set menu (we had #2) is a great deal. 

But the restaurant is deafening. My phone's SPL meter measured 94 dB - after 1 hour at 95 dB you can suffer permanent hearing loss.

Awesome food. I think this place is better than Uncle Boons but it's a similarish concept with more traditional menu and ambiance. Best for a group so you can order the whole menu (like seriously). Portions are big so in a group you could eat here for under $50 pp but yes it's the hated shared plates concept. We went with 4 and ordered 7 things by getting a set and adding a dish, and it was too many. The chicken wings were whatever but the short rib massamun and fried snapper were upsettingly delicious and big portioned. I wish they had roti but I'm really nitpicking now, this place is good.  I don't even want to give it five because I want to still get a table here.

Cory was our waiter and he's one of the nicest and most passionate I've seen.
We ordered the #2 set which was $45/person and it was great. Friendly reminder, it could be quite spicy.
Four stars for the food, one extra star for the service. It was a worthwhile dining experience.

Happy hour here is amazing! I stumbled upon this place while waiting for an opening at Mermaid Inn. There was essentially no wait time for a table for two, so my friend and I decided to eat here instead. 

Since both of us had fairly big lunches, we opted for $1 oysters and drinks. These were some of the freshest oysters I've had in a while. The Thai-inspired toppings were also a nice touch. 

When the time came to select a drink, I decided to go with the coconut / rum cocktail. Highly recommend! Overall, I had a 10/10 experience and will be back to try the entrees sometime soon.

Dang Fish Cheeks, you're literally making my cheeks blow up like goldfish next day with all that sodium in you. Despite the popularity of Fish Cheeks, I found everything to be very salty, so much so that I was busy quenching my thirst with watermelon juice and water throughout the entire meal.

BEST/
Happy Hour Oysters - at $1 a pop, these babies were fresh and delicious, especially when drizzled with the nam jim sauce and crispy shallots. I could eat 2 dozen by myself!
Fried Snapper with Crispy Herbs - a whole fish is fried and then drenched in a thick and viscous sauce. The fish was nice and juicy but my favorite part about it was probably the crispy herb + cashew mix. The sauce was reminiscent of Shanghainese style and was perfect when served over a bowl of white rice!

OKAY/
Grilled Pork Cheeks - thinly sliced, not too fatty. 

NEHHHH/
Coconut Crab Curry - looked promising but was a bit bitter tasting. I don't know, maybe I'm just biased towards my green and red curries.
Po Taksoup - this soup would have been a seafood lover's dream with its assortment of shrimp, fish, scallop, and squid. It was wonderfully fragrant, had the perfect amount of heat, BUT holy smokes... the salt level was next level. Had the sodium been less, way way less, this dish would have been pretty spectacular (think refreshing, savory ocean concoction).
Their Crab Coconut curry is one of the best Thai curry I have tasted! Has a bit of a kick though if your spice tolerance is low. Gets busy during lunchtime

This review is only for oysters and drinks. Came here for their $1 per oyster happy hour and $10 cocktails and everything was delicious and fresh. Great service as well. Make reservations on their website ahead of time to save yourself a wait.

There's a flavor explosion in my mouth! Not one bad entrée. So, I'll start with the $1 oysters happy hour served with fried shallots and a Thai herb vinaigrette sauce. Wow! No way I can go back to cocktail sauce again, even with fresh horseradish. 

The wings are so yummy. A little pricey (3 wings for $13) yes, but so good. The pork jowls (don't freakout) also yummy. They sprinkle this magic dust on it that taste like a mix of salty, citrus and mild sweet. So good. 

We also had a spicy seafood entree. It had 2 chili peppers next to it as a spice level indicator, and is one of the spiciest dish on the menu. Yes, it was spicy even for us and we aren't spice babies. We like a little kick. Despite the spice, I could not stop eating the dish because the flavor was so delicious. The fresh green peppercorns added such a dimension of flavor. 

Lastly, we had the short rib in curry coconut milk sauce. Good, but a little too heavy for me. I can definitely see myself getting more into this dish during the colder months. 

Happy hour boost $10 cocktails. Nothing wrong there either. My favorite is the Thai Old Fashion. 

All I can say is go and enjoy.

Really wanted to like this place but overall just an average place. Sat at the bar and had an app and entree. The app (wings) was great. But that was the only positive thing. Firstly the bartender gives me bill right after I finish ordering before any of the food gets there. Rude. Second, the entree (whole fish with some sorta mix) had great presentation but left much to be desired. Third, the bartender asked me how my food was at the end and when I was honest to him about how great the app was but how disappointing the entree was, he offered nothing. Any classy restaurant in NYC with reputable chef would have offered either a discount or dessert or just an apology. But nothing. With food and service being mediocre, it's safe to say I won't be returning.

Food was Great and Right Up My Alley with the Spice! I had the Seafood Pad Cha and Coconut Crab Curry!!!!! The only downside was not being able to substitute for brown rice and shrimp fried rice. The Fresh Squeeze Limeade was refreshing. Very upbeat for happy hour.
Food was perfect. Service was exceptional...thanks Corey. Will highly recommend it and I will be back

Spicy and and little pricy, but delicious. They have a very very very good happy hour deal - dollar oysters with a tasty Thai spin and $10 creative, quality cocktails. The service was attentive (especially important when you need your water constantly refilled from the spicy dishes!). The decor of the place is colorful and trendy, with authentic music playing in the background. It wasn't too packed when we went around 5:30pm, but started filling up shortly thereafter. Thankfully, they take reservations.

We ordered the oysters, sticky rice cocktail, short rib curry, steamed fish, morning glory vegetables, and mango sticky rice. The $1 oysters were so good with the sauce, although there was gritty sand in a few of the oysters. The sticky rice cocktail was strong and well made. The short rib curry with rice is a good-sized portion for one person if paired with at least one other appetizer. The meat is very tender and the sweet potatoes were a nice addition, however I felt that the curry could have been less salty. The fish and the morning glory, each marked with one chili sign on the menu, were definitely spicy (even for someone who has a higher tolerance), but so tasty if you're into those type of flavors. The mango sticky rice is a must-try - the sticky rice is cooked to perfection and the mango is fresh and sweet. Including tax and tip, our meal was a bit over $60 per person.

My one complaint is that there were several large flies that constantly flew around our table, landing on us, our table, the utensils on the empty table next to ours, and trying to get to our food. One landed on me and I hit it, and it ended up dying on my plate (very disgusting) - I wish we didn't have to constantly fight off flies during dinner!

Cute thai spot. We got there around 6:30 on Thur night and was already more than half filled. Tables turn fairly quickly and had no problem getting a table for 2. HH is until 7pm and includes raw oysters (delicious with shallots) for $1, cocktails for $10, wine for $8, beer for $5. The Watermelon s
Spritz was refreshing but the Guava Smash was my favorite. We ordered the Fried Calamari and Coconut Crab Curry (had small pieces of king crab mixed in). The curry is spicy so watch out. I will definitely come back for the raw oysters and try the other dishes!

Happy hour $1 oysters with a really good Thai green sauce that tastes like a chimi churri. Incredibly good on the oysters. Grilled branzino was so fresh and clean tasting that I stopped using the sweet peanut chili sauce that came with it because I just wanted to enjoy the fish itself. The venue itself is very fun, not stuffy at all. Colorful and open. Great place for a casual date. Very impressive.

Took advantage of their awesome happy hour! It's everyday from 12-4 then again 5-7. We came here around 645 and was able to order dozen oysters and two house cocktails 

There are lots of places that do $1 oysters but I really liked Fish Cheeks for their unique sauce. Oysters came with chimichuri like green sauce that tasted cilantro / garlicy- very savory and just went really well with oyster. The fried shallot (I think...) was also great and added nice texture to oysters 

Now for drinks - they were $10 bucks for house cocktails (normally $14). So many delicious options that I had hard time choosing!! We ended up going with sticky rice and guava drink - both were great. Not too sweat with enough  alcohol which makes the deal better! 

Free shrimp crackers also was great :)


Definitely will be coming back

Came here for dinner a few weeks ago and the food was spectacular! I loved all the appetizers we tried. I loved all the entrees we tried. Everything was delicious, and plated so beautifully. Not only did we eat with our mouths, we ate with our eyes. I recommend making a reservation. Enjoy!

Wow, Fish Cheeks is such a little gem on Bond Street. The atmosphere is very vibrant yet relaxed with plenty of table seating and a considerable sized bar in the back. Dining here is ideal for groups because their menu is essentially made up of small shareable plates. Nice wine selection and the mixed drinks that were coming out looked AMAZE -- I'll leave those for my next trip here. Thai iced tea also looked like a must try. We tried the fried snapper, calamari, watercress, crab fried rice, pork cheek (x2 because we liked it so much), clams, and capped it all off with mango sticky rice (duh). The flavors altogether were superb -- ranging from sweet to savory to spicy. The mango sticky rice was worth getting but I've had better and the plating itself was subpar (legit looked like slice salmon next to a bland bed of rice). The clams were a little lackluster because the "meat" had fallen out of most of them & grainy residue was leftover (but still ate & enjoyed). Overall, great restaurant, great waitstaff, great experience.

Really enjoyed my meal here last night - we ordered the preset for 3 people which included the corn salad, wings, and cheeks to start. After the appetizers, we had the soup, branzino, crab curry, and crab fried rice (as a replacement to the clams since they were out). 

Be prepared for some heat in these dishes, but if you don't mind, it'll be an amazing meal full of flavor. Would love to come back and try some of their cocktails!

When you walk into Fish Cheeks, the restaurant decor and vibes transform you out of the NYC cold. They have happy hour till 7, with $1 oysters and discount wine, beer and cocktails. The food is interesting and creative - this is not your typical thai place, you will not see pad thai. Excellent vibes, really fun atmosphere. The food is delicious, and spicy level can be high. If you are not a fan of spicy food, ask for mild
The food is well seasoned and drinks are very good. I think many would find the place overpriced but since the times I've been the food has been very good so the price is acceptable to me.

Was recommended this place by a friend and Fish Cheeks did not disappoint. I highly suggest their Chef's selection - you get to try a variety of dishes and its a lot of food. This is by far the best authetic Thai I've had

Can't believe I haven't visited this gem since it's been open for almost two years! The ambiance is very chill and the interior is cute yet simple. Service was impeccable with our waiter being perhaps, TOO nice, double-checking that everything was okay with us. Went here for Sunday lunch and it wasn't busy at all (surprising! thought it would be quite packed). I'd say definitely get the PORK CHEEKS (that dipping sauce is the perf combination of spicy and sour) and the MASSAMUN CURRY  (short rib was so tender). Oysters didn't seem as fresh but comes with a selection of thai sauces to mix with so could be worth a try during happy hour. A good variety of cocktails and lets just say they are STRONG.

Came across this place on a whim, and instantly fell in love with it! 

Booked a table for 2 as an early dinner prior to going to the cinema, and even at 6pm the place was heaving! Always a good sign. First thing that caught my attention upon being seated was the vibrancy of the interior. Everything is bright, airy and just overtly cool.

Service was also great, they were quick, efficient and also took time to explain some of their more rambunctious dishes.

Foodwise we got a selection of Oysters to share ($1 on Happy hour), a beef short rib massuman curry, a Shrimp/Scallop salad, Thai Green Curry and Crab Fried Rice...while all of it was amazing, the stand out for me was the Crab Fried Rice - it comes with a cilantro based sauce and spicy fish sauce, and if you give those a whizz through the dish you will not be disappointed! Truly the rice was light, fluffy, and zesty with that great sweet crabby flavor.

My only criticism of the place was that I was not a fan of the cocktails. And that's not to say they were bad, they just didn't quite meet my taste - while all the ingredients seemed to be things I enjoy, there just seemed to be something a little off about them. 

But Please, do not let that overshadow the food - cannot recommend this place enough. Great for a date or catch up with friends!

Best Thai place I've been to so far. Don't get me wrong, I love the americanized thai food, but fish cheeks know how to bring out fresh clean dishes that arnt overwhelming with flavors. True balance.

Pro
- oyster happy hours! The oysters were super fresh! We got a dozen and wanted to order more
- we got this dish. Seafood pad cha. A little bit of kick, but was great. Also got crab fried rice with the dish. Its a must!!! Please go eat it
- all their drinks were super refreshing and yummy
- talk about cute inteior
- the servers were super busy, but were still attentive.

Con
- nothing. Literally loved the whole restaurant!

Ambience:4+ Dinner:5+ Service:4 Value:5 Return:5

*Needing to upgrade my rating here after a nice but no comparison to this fabulous Thai restaurant I tried over the weekend. The food above all is what matters; with food alone, Fish Cheeks is a TRUE 5!

OMG, what a gem!  Reservation made for a late dinner on a Thursday evening.  Cold it was out but quickly warmed up I was as soon as I walked in.  

Crowded and a lively scene was still in place at 9pm in a very dark yet cozy room. Scooting some other guests aside, we were then seated at our spot. 

Enticing aroma and delicious were each and every dish. "Pork Cheeks", "Yum Goong", "Steam Fish", and, "Earl Grey Panna Cotta" being my favorites.  Yet, notable also was their signature "Coconut Crab Curry" which was decidedly my table's favorite.

Happy I was as I left the table, already dreaming of what I would try here at FC when I'm in NoHo next.

CHEERS!

What a great spot. Really good vibes. Everyone was so pleasant to interact with and the food was spot-on. We had some seafood dishes and curries.

I'm not a Thai cuisine gourmand unlike some of the other reviewers, so can't speak to the authenticity, but it was really damn good. 

The food came out at peak flavor, temperature and was quick. We made reservations online and were seated immediately even as the place was popping with all the bar seats taken as well.

Good value play, relaxing atmosphere, great location and friendly staff, what more does one need in life?

My daughter loves Thai and I wanted to one up her experiences with the Thai food we get at home. Fish Cheeks was fantastic. The waiter was attentive and gave many suggestions as well as asking about any allergies. I follow one of their chefs on Instagram and she gave me many suggestions too. My daughter has not stopped talking about the Thai Iced Coffee. 

For our meal we shared crab fried rice (I had to order a side of jasmine rice for my teenager before he ate all of the crab fried rice),  Po Tak soup with big chunks of seafood in a spicy broth, corn salad (a complementary off the menu dish) and the coconut crab curry. I really wanted the pork cheeks but my kids (ages 14 and 19, I wouldn't bring children) were not as adventuresome as I thought they'd be. 

Happy hour is 7 days a week and the drink and oyster specials are a great price. 

Can't wait to go back and try other dishes!
A really fun place with great food and service to match it. Don't be too ambitious on the spicy options!

So happy I finally made it to Fish Cheeks! We walked in around 9:30 PM on a Saturday and were seated immediately. We both weren't that hungry so ordered two apps and one main - the grilled pork cheeks, shrimp in 3 crab sauce, and seafood pad cha. I liked all three dishes, but my boyfriend and I especially enjoyed the pork cheeks. They were so juicy and tender we were staring longingly at the couple next to us who left quite a bit in their plates. The flavors of the pad cha were also delicious and the scallop was very fresh. I must come back for oyster happy hour!

Happy hour oysters are omg delish. $1. And it comes with a spicy green sauce and fried garlic toppings. 

I wish the "shareables" were actually shareable. Instead the dishes were small in portion and quite hefty on the price. However, must say the food is tasty. Had crab fried rice one night and the seafood pad cha another time. Both were good. The seafood pad cha is spicy and it does not come with any rice or noodles. 

First time I went, they gave complimentary chips. But the second time they didn't and we saw other tables get it :( 

The decor and atmosphere is vibrant. Love the colors and layout. Open window during the summer time. Cute place overall.

Happy hour is every day 12-4, 5-7. $1 oysters and drink specials.

Went here with a bunch of my friends for lunch! Everything about the food was amazing! The pork cheeks are so good that we had to get it again before we left. The crab curry was so delicious and not so spicy at all. The chicken wings were not bad. I would seriously recommend this place to my friends and return again.

Warning: "This is a no pad thai zone"

Everything from the drinks to the food is delicious here. To start off our meal, we got oysters which are $1 during happy hour. The oysters were fresh and were not too slimy nor briny. The oysters did not come with your traditional cocktail sauce -- it came with crunchy onions and a fish sauce-based sauce that had lime and cilantro.
