As untraditional as it sounds, the combination is great and highly addictive. The sauce had a nice sweet and salty flavor, and the onions added a crunchy texture that balanced out the texture of the oyster.

As I previously mentioned, Fish Cheeks is really a no pad thai zone. In other words, the menu is going to offer Thai dishes that you don't often come across. I find the menu a breath of fresh air and a nice break from popular Thai dishes we all know and love. 

I recommend trying anything and everything here. I don't think you can go wrong. However, we tried the...
1. yum so-o (pomelo salad, so refreshing and a great appetizer to start the meal)
2. pok tak (lemongrass soup - so flavorful and spicy. Fragrant and has a nice hot/sour taste)
3. fried rice with crab (so simple but so good)
4. manila clams (really like the sauce that comes with this dish)
5. short rib curry (on the heavier side but the meat was so tender)
6. grilled pork cheeks (popular dish and a must, imo)

Get the fried snapper and wings.  Great Thai fusion flavors--I don't think it's the most authentic Thai.  The fish is an adventure in whole body eating with different regions of flavors and accoutrements.  The citrus on the wings is subtle but magical.  The short rib massaman curry is revelatory but the coconut crab curry is merely good.  Try out the cocktails, virgin and otherwise.

Adorable interior; loved the relaxed vibe and colors. The fishing baskets over the lights and the hanging greens on the wall are all nice details that add to the feeling of escapism as soon as you walk inside. 
We came around 8:30 PM for dinner, and the music was insanely loud, we had to yell across our tiny table to make any conversation. All staff were extremely nice, and we always appreciate when our waiter has honest recommendations about the menu. 

We went with the set 1 to try most of the menu for a reasonable price. All portions are full-size, which is a great value. We also got an extra seafood stirfry and crab coconut curry. The texture of the curry was unlike any I have ever had. Extremely smooth, rich, flavorful, and all components shined equally (nothing overpowered the other). 
Everything was delicious and so well done. The flavors really showcase Thai food that is not just the same ol' pad Thai that the American palate is used to. The calamari had a wonderfully crunchy and sweet coating. Pork cheek with homemade chili sauce was delectable. Mushroom noodles were infused with so much flavor to each bite. 

Beware - the dishes described as "spicy" on the menu are truly spicy. Sometimes at other restaurants, when it says "spicy" on the menu, I barely detect any heat at all. But that is not the case here. Be prepared, and I am telling you this as someone who can handle a good amount of spice.

Mango sticky rice was a nice way to end a spicy meal :) 

Tl;dr:  try this place! It's spicy! Get the Set!

Cute decor! A nice place to try something new - good for small groups, can order an assortment of dishes and try everything family-style. 

Finally a different kind of Thai cuisine! Not your average Americanized pad thai joint. This is Seafood Thai, with intense Asian flavors and creative dishes.

I've been twice in two weeks and some of my favorites are the crab fried rice, whole branzino (they take out the bones for you!), pork cheeks, and pomelo appetizer. Don't forget to pour all the appropriate sauces on each dish.

Great date night spot! Managed to grab a reservation on Thursday for dinner on Friday after eyeing up the menu and instantly thinking 'I need to go here'.

My BF and I went for the set menu 2 which literally had everything we were thinking about ordering... clearly we have good taste. This consisted of:

Appetizer
Zabb wings: I'm not the biggest meat on the bone lover but these were really crispy and had a great sweet and spicy flavor. Finger lickin' good!

Yum Goon: okay so I LOVE cilantro.... it makes every dish better. Fact. So this for me just hit the spot. Perfectly seasoned, super fresh taste. 

Entree:
Short rib massaman curry: As you would expect/hope the meat was just falling apart. For me this one was better in smaller portions as it was quite rich in flavor leaving more room for the next dish...

Crab fried rice: *insert mouth watering emoji*. This dish was AMAZING. It's served with a chilli and fish sauce and a cilantro based sauce. These two poured all over it give this light, fishy yet punchy spice flavor. It's SO GOOD. This works week served with some of the best dish...

Seafood Pad Cha: not for the faint hearted. This stir fry is spiiiiicy.  A beautiful bowl of thick, squishy scallops, squid and shrimp with chunky eggplant. Delicious!!!

I appreciate this review is long but people need to know how good this place is!!!!

Cute exterior with the scales.
I came into this restaurant not expecting too much, but as soon as the food came, I was in awe. I enjoyed each and every dish that my group ordered. The items that stood out the most was the pork cheeks. Juicy and sweet slices of pork. The curry was pretty tasty and even my friends whom don't really eat spicy things enjoyed it. The things on the menu were all pretty self-explanatory.
What I want to say is that I really enjoyed the food here and look forward to bringing some other friends to try it too!
This is the kind of Thai restaurant you would find in Bangkok. Tastes like home without compromising modern Thainess.

I was impressed. This place is really good and I enjoyed all of the dishes I had. My friend Yuxi invited me to dinner here and...

Set 3 -- worth it. Every dish was great. 
Make sure to add an order of the calamari to it too. 
Coconut ice cream for dessert.

Looking forward to coming back!

what drew my attention to the restaurant is the name. One day I was walking around the area and I saw "Fish cheeks" and thought that's cute I'm going to try this restaurant one day!

i came here for valentines day dinner and it was perfect spot. It was a chill place yet still cute and romantic. No cheesy prefix menu meals- although they do have a prefix meal, I will talk about more later.

the complimentary dish they give out are crab chips and dip. it was soo tasty and their hot sauce was fire! 

we ordered the chefs selection set one and it was 45 per person and there was soo much food! it was family style as plate after plate comes out. the curry and lemongrass soup was "thai spicy" which means extremely spicy, but it still tasty. the pork cheeks was divine -i didn't expect it be so tender and flavorful. the calmarai was fried so crispy and accompanied with the sweet sauce it reminded me of sesame chicken. 

and at the end, they gave us complimentary chocolate cake for valentines day. it was the perfect ending to a perfect meal! I want to come back again and bring my family here to try out more dishes.

We were served complimentary shrimp chips, which were AMAZING and then ordered a couple of dollar oysters (for their 5-7pm happy hour).

My friend and I shared the short rib curry and it was INCREDIBLE. We didn't arrive starving, but I'm very full and satisfied.

I love this colorful restaurant nestling in Noho! It has such a cute name & the decor reminds me of the vibrancy of Thailand w/ the nostalgic decor of a home.

This is a great place for groups. Good for special occasions, casual gatherings & even for the little kiddies! Service was on point; staff is friendly.

And the food!!! All the right textures & flavors were there. From sweet to spicy, soft to crunchy, all these dishes were perfect for a family style meal.

I would come back for a special occasion. Worth every bite!

Came at 6 on a Saturday, Sat at the bar and started with a dozen oysters which were fresh and good. Then had the calamari, fried snapper and crab rice. Everything was tasty, heat levels reasonable but we played it safe after getting destroyed at other Thai places recently. The service however left something to be desired,. I'll definitely go back especially during happy hour

The food here is very well prepared, much better than the average Thai place in NYC. Their emphasis on seafood is a welcome departure. The sauces are superbly flavored, and be prepared for some heat with complex variation. The food at Fish Cheeks is of the quality of what one is served in a very good restaurant in Thailand.

I love, love, love this place. It does have its quirks - all dishes are more home-style and definitely splittable. 

Their dishes have a lot of heat, but it's not mind-numbingly spicy. It's purposeful, and it really doesn't overpower the taste. The coconut crab curry is so, so good, it's hard for me to move past it. However, the other dishes have always been amazing (they rotate). The Shrimp Pad Cha was a really interesting spin, and it tasted pretty good. The ambiance is cozy but fun (if that makes sense?) and the waiters and bartenders have always been great.

Prices really scary until you realize everything is geared to be shared. We ate the stringbeans, rice and streamed fish. All were delicious, the fish was fresh and fragrant. They came by with an order of the chicken wings when they felt the fish was taking too long to be prepared, for their standards. Classy!!

I've been wanting to try out this place for a while and finally had the chance to visit and I was not disappointed. Fish Cheeks is a Thai seafood restaurant, and although I'm not the biggest seafood person, I do love crab. But I was hesitant about ordering the crab dishes because I wasn't sure how much they would skimp out on the crab meat. I went for it anyways and my friend and I ordered the crab fried rice and the crab curry. Both pretty much blew my mind. It was overflowing with crab meat. I also wasn't expecting too much with the fried rice, but there was just something about it where I couldn't stop eating it. The curry was also probably one of the best curries that I've tasted. But fair warning, it is quite spicy. It's got a kick to it and if you have a sensitive stomach, I'd stay away from it. Even though there was not much in the curry besides the broth and the crab meat, I didn't mind it one bit because it was just that delicious. 

One down side is that this place is quite pricey but I guess that's because of the high price of seafood in general and being located in the city so I can't hate on that too much. I am definitely planning my next visit to this place, I'm a fan!

OMG, this place is sooo good! 
My NY friends recommended this place so of course I googled it.  Yes, a ot of celebs frequent this restaurant so I wasn't sure if it's all hype or if they really do serve outstanding food.  so glad we came. 
We ordered the crab fried rice, chicken curry, beef curry, fried calamari, spicy chicken sings and pork cheeks.  Everything was delicious especially the pork cheeks.  The sauces the entrees came with were all outstanding.  Just enough spice so not overpowering.  The flavors worked so well together.  I can't believe we got such good food and pay reasonable pricing for it.  Will definitely return.

I came here on a Tuesday during happy hour and shared half a dozen oysters alongside Set 2 of the Chefs' selection.

Pros:

The ambiance was cozy. We sat at the bar and the staff was nice, attentive, regardless of it being busy.

The $1 oysters were worth the value. Don't forget to use the chili lime sauce as well as the shallots.

The set has strong elements of the light fresh coconut texture if you enjoy the flavor.

Cons:

The Yum Goong had an excess of cilantro, culantro, and betel leaves on the plate to the portion of shrimp (5-6). This isn't so much a con as it is over portioning.

Zabb wings were over seasoned in my opinion.

Crab fried rice was generous in portion as well. Could serve 3-5 people.

4 1/2 stars. There is a sign at Fish Cheeks that says "this is a Pad Thai Free Zone". Indeed, this is not your typical Thai menu. I am not sure if this is "authentic" Thai, but the high quality ingredients, and unique combinations make Fish Cheeks unlike any other Thai restaurant I have visited. 
13 year old and I actually stumbled upon Fish Cheeks on our way to another place for lunch. We perused the menu and were intrigued. Plus, they had a happy hour special from 12-4 with $1 oysters so we were "in".  

The place looks pretty unassuming and was mostly empty when we arrived.   We were asked if we had a reservation. We did not but  were seated immediately. We started with half a dozen oysters and then ordered half a dozen more. The oysters were fresh but most were minuscule. Yes, they were $1 but I have had $1 oyster specials elsewhere that were nice, plump oysters. 

I had read in other Yelp reviews that the portions were quite small so 13 year old and I feasted with the oysters, a starter and two mains to share. The Calamari was not just Fried Calamari. These were huge crispy Calamari in a sweet tamarind and fish sauce glaze. Could not get enough of that glaze and lapped up any extra!  
We could not resist ordering two curries because they both sounded so good!  Our favorite hands down was the Short Rib Masaman Curry. Made with grass fed short rib, sweet potato, and peanuts, this dish was perfection. The meat was fall off the bone soft. The potato also had a buttery texture with natural sweetness. And putting it all together with that savory sauce... Mmmmm, so succulent and delicious! The Crab Curry was very good:  Lots of Crab and definitely on the spicy side!

Yes, I did look at the menu before we went in, but I guess I had not noticed the prices. The starters are $13-$15 and the mains are $22-$34. Our lunch for two was over $100. I believe what you get is worth it.  Still, I would still like to see some type of lunch special to make this exceptional Thai restaurant more affordable and accessible. 

Now with Yelp, the places we go to are usually researched, investigated, argued about, and carefully chosen. So nice to stumble upon a place for a change and love it!

This place is amazing. The drinks are well prepared, the fish is very delicious and the spice that they infuse is perfect. It reminds me of home cooked Thai cuisine. To anyone who will go here please have the steamed fish with mint.

We decided to come here after having a few drinks at a bar close by . The wait was about 20 mins which was not bad for a Friday night. The ambience is really nice and intimate. It would be great for a date not so much for big parties. Our waitress was pleasant  and attentive and took our orders right away. I Ordered the stir fry sea food which was spicy and flavorful. My friends got the porky Cheeks and the clams which came in some sort of curry sauce. Both were also very delicious. At the end of the meal we realized they completely forgot one of our friends full order. she sat with us for the entire meal only to be told at the end that there was some sort of mistake in the kitchen which was disappointing. All in all the food that I tasted was absolutely delicious

Hands down the best Thai food I've had in New York and maybe in North America. There's no pad Thai here only fresh, delicious, authentic seafood and stir-frys. We had the whole steamed fish, crab fried rice (a must have), mushrooms, and clams. We were really hungry so we finished everything. I would suggest coming here in parties of 2-4. The pace of the service is just right. We didn't feel like they were rushing us or taking too long. The restaurant is always busy but not overbearingly crowded. I recommend making a reservation before coming. 
I have a feeling I'll be coming here a lot from now on.

I've been to Fish Cheeks three times now and each experience has consolidated my belief that this is the superior Thai restaurant New York has to offer. Forget Uncle Boons or Thai Villa, this is where you want to bring your next dinner-buddy. 

I like the well-lit welcoming space that is not too big, so it feels homey somewhat. The crowd can get pretty rowdy which is a good thing I think. People have fun here is the point. 

The Shrimp in three crabs sauce is a must, you should order it every time you go and you should go more often just to order it. They change the rest of their menu regularly so there will always be some excitement.

Pork cheeks is probably the only meat item I've had here but so worth it. Juicy, tender.

I've also had:
1. The coconut crab curry - insanely spicy, so only order it if you can take the heat. Honestly it was so spicy I hardly remember anything else about it. (Big chunks of crab!)

2. Manilla clams with sweet basil - totally on point, classic comfort food in my family. The clams were super fresh. 

3. Steamed fish - very generous portion, we could not finish it because we had ordered another entree. Very clean flavors but nothing very memorable.

4. Seafood Pad cha - one of my favorites, the scallops on top are always perfectly soft, the sauce is probably the best and be prepared to dunk everything else in it.

5. They used to have a non-vegan version of their aob woon senn with shrimps, that was delicious and a good non-spicy option for that friend who cannot eat spicy food.

Finally, the cocktails are very well mixed. 

Run run here. I personally look forward to come back again and again.

This is the cutest and fairly priced Thai food in the NOHO area! It has not been open very long (maybe half a year or so?) - it took over the old French restaurant on Bond Street called Le Philosophe. Now the space is brightly decorated with colorful chairs and also a colorful bar whose tiles mimic those of fish scales. The lighting is beautiful, looking somewhat like  upside-down rattan woven baskets, it provides a cheery and casual ambiance which the name of the restaurant exudes as well. 

I came here with a girlfriend on my last trip back to NYC on a weeknight and it was busy! Good thing we made reservations a couple of days in advance! We came for a 6:30 reservation which gave us a half hour for Happy Hour specials! They have HH every day from 12-4pm and 5-7pm! 


HH Menu:
House cocktails + Oysters 
We started with a couple of spicy margaritas for $10 and 2 dozen HH oysters for $1 each. The oysters were east coast from Massachusetts (my favorite, east side represent!) that came with fried shallots and spicy nan jim sauce!! I have never had oysters with any sauce other than the usual cocktail with horseradish, Tabasco, and mignonette so this Thai chili sauce opened up a whole new world to me! IT WAS SO DAMN DELICIOUS and the fried shallots gave it that extra flavor without overpowering the sweetness of the oysters. Definitely a must-have especially when they are only $1 a piece at HH!!!! 

Appetizer:
Pork Cheeks
After the HH specials, we shared the pork cheeks appetizer. This is definitely a must - it comes with quite a lot of slices of tender grilled pork that you dip in jeaw sauce - another thai chili dipping sauce that consists of fish sauce - SO GOOD.

Entrees:
Crispy Garlic Branzino + Seafood Pad Cha 
The Branzino was HEAVENLY especially if you like garlic and fish with sweet soy sauce!! It's so simple but booked so well .... it's a hot and crispy fish swimming in delicious sauce. The fish is split in half so no flipping it to find some more meat which makes it very easy to share. The seafood pad cha had a bit of heat and has great scallops, shrimp and squid in it - perfect to go with a bowl of white rice! 

I will definitely be coming back here next time I am in NYC to try the rest of the items on the menu! I heard the crab fried rice & coconut curry crab is awesome so next on my list!

Ambience: The restaurant has a nice quirky feel to it. 

Appetizer: The calamari was really good. the pork cheeks were underwhelming.  

Main Course: 
- Crab Curry really had no flavor, it was just very hot with pepper. 
- Crab Fried Rice: was okay, but didn't blow me away 
- Fried Snapper: really good, but the snapper was small. 

Over all, this place was just okay for the price, I would check it out if you just want to experience Thai food, but wouldn't go out of your way. There are cheaper places that are just as good.

Review for August 2017. Reservations made on Resy. 

We got here at the tail-end of happy hour and took advantage of the $1 oysters and cocktails. They weren't great oysters, but hey they are $1. Also got shrimp chips as a free app.

We got the Chef's Selection Set 2, which has changed from its current menu. 
- Calamari: Lightly breaded, fried, sweet and a little spicy.
- Prince Edward Island Mussels & Herbs: eh, the most underwhelming dish.
- Crispy Garlic Branzino with Fish Sauce: It was ok, not something I would order again.
- Coconut Crab Curry: very fragrant and perfect with rice. It's also pretty spicy. I would love to try it again. This bowl goes a long way with rice.
- Pakboong Fai Dang watercress: Yummy veggies. Went well with the other dishes.
- Muu Waan pork belly: Sweet, really small portion size.

Overall, the portion sizes are pretty small and you have to want the set menu (no changes/substitutions). If I were to return, I would go a la carte and not get the sweet savory dishes.

The place is cute and the food is good, but the portions are small.

For 5 people we ordered:
crispy calamari 
dozen oysters 
coconut crab curry 
po tak (lemongrass soup) 
steamed fish 
crab fried rice 
aob woon senn (shitake mushrooms and glass noodles) 
string bean and pork crackling.

You would think that 5 dishes from the plates to share section and 3 appetizers would be enough right? It wasn't though and my group was still hungry after the meal.

As for the food, the crispy calamari is a must. The lemongrass soup was very flavorful but only for those who can handle the spice! The steamed fish and crab fried rice were also delicious and I would highly recommend those. You could do without the glass noodles and string beans.

All in all, the food was decent, but I'm not sure it was worth the steep price tag.

FOOD: Five Stars
AMBIANCE: Four Stars
HAPPY HOUR MENU: FIVE FREAKING STARS! 
OVERALL: 5/5

I discovered Fish Cheeks a few months ago through a friend and I have become obsessed with their menu ever since. 

The first time I visited the establishment, I enjoyed their $1 oysters during happy hour. They're not tiny oysters, either. The oysters come with a spicy green sauce and some sort of toasted nut, which paired together are heavenly. No need to add hot sauce or lemon on your oysters. I tend to get oysters every time I go. 

Now, my favorite dishes, based on both visits include:

- Calamari - The calamari is coated in a sticky honey sauce that is amazing on top of the crunchy coating. 
- Short Rib Massaman Curry - The short ribs are cooked for over 12-hours and literally are the tastiest short ribs ever! I'm not a big meat eater, but I would go back for that dish time & time again.
- Po Tak Soup - The po tak soup is a hearty soup full of seafood & is extremely tasty. It's served in a dish with a fire at the heart of it, which keeps the dish warm for a while. 

In terms of happy hour, you can't go wrong with any of their cocktails, but I'm a fan of their wine offerings. 

Would I go back to Fish Cheeks? Absolutely! HANDS DOWN!

This place is so nice! My friend and I were seated in a corner so we finally received some privacy... something I haven't had much of since dining here in NY lol. The waitress that we had was so friendly and attentive. We didn't have to wait very long for anything and we tried quite a few things on their menu. The steamed fish and calamari were phenomenal! We also tried the massaman curry which I wasn't too fond of, but my friend really enjoyed it. The meat was so tender and looked delicious! Sadly, I'm not really a curry fan. The drinks were great and the desserts were OUT OF THIS WORLD!!! Their mango sticky rice was SO DELICIOUS, and they have the BEST ice cream I have ever tasted in my life!!!!! My mouth waters just thinking about it.... if I were you I would start with dessert and then move on to the rest of your dinner lol.

I was definitely impressed with the food here. And i am not easily impressed. My fiancé and I ordered the raw shrimp (goong chae nam pla), short rib massaman curry, zaab wings, fried calamari, oysters, pork cheeks, and the sauteed stringbeans with pork cracklings. I enjoyed all of the dishes. However for me the nam jim seafood was definitely on the sour side for me. The two dishes that highly stood out to me was the massaman curry and fried calamari. Honestly i didnt think i would like the calamari because of the tamarind sauce. But it was not sweet. The sauce was light as well as the batter. And it was still crunchy. I will definitely go back here. 


However i would not give a 4 star for the lacking service. Our server lets just say did not meet up to the food standards.

Came here on a busy Thursday night with a reservation (definitely make a reservation). If you're a party of two, I recommend requesting to not get seated towards the back near the bar because 1) this place is small, and the bar area is very cramped 2) the two-person tables towards the back are near the bathroom, so like no thank you. 

The food was pretty mouth-watering to say the least. I got the steamed fish (bass) with Thai herbs off of their GLUTEN-FREE menu, yes, they have an entire menu of gluten-free options. If you like Thai food and are GF and are not allergic to shellfish, you have to try this place, like right now. 

They don't have a dessert menu as they only have one dessert option, coconut ice cream. Definitely try it, it's delicious.

I love this place. If you're looking for a cheaper option, come for happy hour ($1 oysters, discounted drinks)!  If you're looking to shell out a little more money, do one of the sets! We got to try so many different dishes for $45. My favorites were the coconut crab curry and the crispy garlic branzino. The interior is adorable. I will definitely be coming back.

I've been here twice, once on a date and another with a group of people. Both were on busy Saturday nights. The crab fried rice is amazing, as well as the crab curry. If you love Thai iced tea, you HAVE to try the cocktail. It's out of this world.

It's my first time to know what real Thai food tastes like. Their dishes are authentic, with nothing 'pad thai' or 'kee mao'. The taste as well as the spiciness is beyond my expectation. The service is great and drink is good. I wouldn't give it a 5 star because it's too pricy. We spent 90+$ at last only for two main dishes and an appetizer. Another tip is to make reservation.
Excellent design and appealing indoor environment. The food is flavorful with tasty dipping sauces. A bit on the pricey side.
Food was good! Service was nice! But portions and price prevent this from being a regular/recommended spot. $24 for a small portion of crab fried rice...!? Oy.

LOVE Fish Cheeks! Besides Uncle Boon's I didn't think there were any truly worthy Thai places in NYC but this restaurant proved me wrong. For starters, the space is great and location couldn't have been better - easily accessible, yet tucked away from hustle and bustle of busy Soho. Bright and spacious yet somehow cozy, with an open kitchen. Great fast and very friendly service, and the food.....the food was fantastic. Deceptively simple yet amazing crab curry, fantastic spicy wings, delicious pork jowl (very generously portioned), the list goes on and on. During the happy hour, there are very well priced beers, wine and cocktails. I highly recommend Fish Cheeks to anyone and everyone to try at least once.

This place was better than expected.  The food was super spicy and they didn't give warnings for the white folks. Respect.

The coconut crab curry and crab fried rice were both delicious. I like crab, sue me. They were also generous with the crab meat which was fresh, sweet, and delicious.

There's also plenty of seating by Manhattan standards.

Did I mention that the food was spicy? Delicious?

This is the cutest looking Thai restaurant with a menu full of the most authentic and spicy dishes. When I say Thai, if you are expecting to eat Pad Thai, you can stop reading this review and find another restaurant to satisfy your hunger. This place is legit.

Here are their happy hour (12-4pm & 5-7pm) specials:
$1 oysters
$5 beers
$8 wine
$10 cocktails 

We started with $1 oysters. We ordered 6 oysters to be on the safe side because oysters are usually hit or miss and I am not too big a fan of oysters to still power through them if they turn out to be bad. I was wrong and they were plump and delicious. They came with fried shallots and a sauce similar to chimichurri verde. We devoured them along with our shrimp chips that comes on the house.

Ordered the Zabb wings next, 9 small wings seasoned to perfection. They're spicy so keep water and a napkin handy. 

Our entrée was the Coconut Crab Curry, their most famous dish along with coconut fried rice. This dish was AMAZING. They weren't stingy on the crab content. The sauce is, again going with the same theme here but, spicy. We literally licked our bowl, left no trace of that orange curry sauce anywhere.

We wanted mango sticky rice but they only serve it in the summer. We finished with the Kaffir Lime Pie, which as our server put it, is a mix between a key lime pie and cheesecake. My only complaint about this dessert was that it was too small.

Great ambiance in a great location, well lit restaurant which I appreciate.

The first thing you'll notice on the menu is that there's no pad Thai (pleasantly surprising). 

The sliced pork cheek is to die for....it was super succulent and juicy. Great start to a meal.

They have a delicious assortment of fishes and curries. I recommend the Crispy Garlic Branzino with as well as the Grilled Porgy.

The only thing is I left hungry ... so maybe order an entree and a half per person.
Everything was delicious, but the waitress service was attitude to us. My boyfriend and I very happy about the food.

I went on Saturday with my husband to get happy hour oysters. We didnt have a reservation but we went there at 5 so it was empty. We ordered two dozens of oysters were great. He got happy hour cocktail  (for get what kind) and I got thai ice tea. The oysters were good but servers weren't friendly. We weren't hungry for other food so we want to go back for their thai food.

I first found out about Fish Cheeks when I saw Chrissy Teigen post a Snapchat story on it. Then, I saw that one of my friends went there for dinner and she mentioned that they have $1 oysters during happy hour, so it was a done deal.

Four of my friends and I went for dinner with a 6 pm reservation on a Friday night. Happy hour is from 12-4, then 5-7, and this will get you $5 beers, $8 wines, $10 cocktails, and of course, the $1 oysters. Now these aren't your typical sad and skinny NYC oysters. These oyster are plump, and they are served with this green mignonette, which reminded me of a chimichurri sauce. Each of us ate at least a dozen, it was just that good.

For food, we decided to order a bunch of plates and share, since there were multiple dishes that we each wanted to try. Here's what we ordered:

Coconut crab curry - this was probably the best of the bunch. It had the perfect spice level, and they give a good amount of crab chunks.
Short rib massaman curry - not too memorable.
Grilled pork cheeks - good, but I felt like i was just eating thinly-sliced pork loin.
Seafood pad cha - this was so spicy but it was so good! I couldn't eat a lot of it because my tongue was on fire but if you like spicy foods and seafood, definitely get this dish.
Shrimp ceviche - the first shrimp I bit into was definitely a shrimp that had been dead for a while. It was mushy and unpleasant. I tried a second piece, which was much better.
String beans  - basic
Clams - again, basic and not too memorable

All in all, I had a great meal. I'll be back for some happy hour oysters and to to try some of their other dishes. Fish Cheeks is probably the most seemingly authentic Thai restaurant that I've been to. They do not serve Pad Thai here. I love Pad Thai but most restaurants tend to butcher it. It's become so commonplace that not many Thai places can make it well. I like that Fish Cheeks doesn't serve typical Americanized Thai food, and sticks to their unique dishes. Can't wait for my next meal here!

It's been a while since I've been compelled to write a review (hence why I lost my Elite status).

I dined here and the food was great. We ordered the set for 3 plus the order of crab fried rice and most of the food was on point. My only gripe would have to be the odd host experience. I had a reservation but my party ran late due to subway issues, fine. I was the first one there about 5 minutes late and the hostess explained that I can get seated once one more person comes; fine. My wife showed up next, albeit 15 minutes later. We walk in and we're told we can't be seated now unless we're going to start ordering the foods; annoyed. But my friends were late so we finally relented. I get that they're busy and respect it 100% but don't flip flop on customers please.

And now, back to the food.

The set included wings, pork cheek and pomelo to start and crab curry, tom yum soup, clams and branzino.

Wings - well cooked, tangy and spicy but also slightly salty, but good.
Pork cheeks - well flavored and juicy
Pomelo - we really didn't know what it was but I ended up really liking it. It's vegan and tasted like some sort of seafood salad, but pomelo is a grapefruit-like fruit we learned today and it was nice and refreshing.
Crab curry - and two pepper signs to highlight the spice level. The curry had the sweetness of the coconut hide its spice until you had too much in your mouth with full of (spice) regret. It was really good though.
Soup - it had an amazing kick to it and all the seafood ingredients were chunky and cooked just right.
Branzino - tied for one of my favorites of the night. Cooked very well and perfectly flavored.
Clams - nothing to write home about here unfortunately. 

As an added bonus (and really because we had. 4th), we ordered the crab fried rice which was great. You can taste actual chunks of delicious crab which was a treat.

Finally, instead of finding a dessert place elsewhere, we ordered the two items on the menu: key lime pie and coconut ice cream. We all shared and dig into the ice cream first and it was so effin good! After devouring that, the group tried the key lime pie and it was good but just did not compare to the first. As a result, 2 of our party put their spoons down and did not even continue. Oh well, more for me!

Overall, a very solid night. Would I come back? Probably not because it's not necessarily a "regular" spot in my opinion plus there are way too many other great restaurants to try in NYC and I don't have enough time.

Would I recommend this to someone: HELL YES.

Sat at the shittiest table possible! To be fair we didn't make reservations but I've been wanting to try this place! So it was no big deal at all. My point is, that even by sitting in the WORST table ever. I'm telling you, THE WORST. Table for two all the way in the back. My back was up against the kitchen door swinging in and out as the servers went through to serve food. 

It was delicious! Our server was awesome, very nice. The food came out at a great pace. We tried 3 cocktails, Thailand in Winter, their version of a Manhattan and the Spicy Mango. Happy hour deal $10 for cocktails until 7PM. ALL FLAVORFUL and really tasty. 

We also had $1 oysters with our cocktails. The green sauce on top was a twist from what we normally have with oysters. 

For our mains we shared the seafood soup served in a traditional pot that looked like a volcano. We also had the curry with beef short ribs. The flavors were so authentic! KEY WORD AUTHENTIC! 


For dessert we had the coconut ice cream with jack fruit. Just so damn good I could bathe in it for days. Def will be back! Def will make reservations to avoid THE WORST TABLE EVER. I only emphasize "the worst table ever" bc despite that,the over all experience surpassed the crappy seating. And the food, drinks and service was top notch!

Just get the crab fried rice. You'll thank me later. No peeling, lots of meat and a green sauce and plenty of fresh cilantro!

The charred cabbage with Thai dressing is gorgeous too!

Great cocktails too. The Thai Old Fashioned made with Thai rum is my favorite.

Definitely recommend this restaurant. Interesting interior and really quality food and drinks. Portion sizes extremely generous for NYC fine dining experience--price is reasonable and service impeccable

Number 1 Thai place in the city. Definitely a must go. Highly recommend the lemongrass fish stew and the coconut crab curry. The cocktails are well worth it as well. Best wishes for Fish Cheeks restaurant

There are not many restaurants that I can say I've ate at twice for dinner in less than 4 days. TWICE! Fish Cheeks has never been on my radar and most people would say they've heard about it because it's highly recommended by Chrissy Teigen. As for me, I found out about this spot because my friends decided to meet up for dinner one night and it sounded "cool" cause pad thai was not on the menu (haha)! I was drawn in by their happy hour menu ($1 oysters, $5 beers, $8 wines, and $10 cocktails). Let me just say, their $1 oysters are the best I've ever had! It comes with fried shallots and some tangy green sauce that gives dollar oysters a completely different twist from all the other joints in NYC. I proudly ate about 3 dozen the first night and I want to say about 2 dozen the second night. As I'm typing this, I'm having flashbacks of the delicious oysters (haha!). 

As for the food, we can break it down into three categories: appetizers, entrees, and desserts. Appetizers: the pork cheeks! They are lean, but not dry and the spicy, tangy sauce it comes with is amazing. Entree: coconut crab curry! This is pretty spicy for what it is, but if you're into panang curry or any yellow curry, you'd love this dish! There's A LOT of crab once you mix the curry. If you're not into spicy at all, I think the dish would taste just as spectacular if it was not spicy (ask if that's an option). Desserts: I think they said it was seasonal, but on both nights I had the coconut ice cream with mango and jelly slices. I would highly recommend getting this if it's on the menu because it's fresh! Great coconut flavor, but not super heavy like a gelato which I loved. I could seriously eat bowls of this and the crab curry!

Really solid food here, especially the $1 oyster special - SO WORTH IT. This is going to be on list of happy hour spots to frequent for sure. I enjoyed everything we ordered, although much of the dishes were quite spicy, and normally, i can't handle spice, but the dishes were worth fighting through the pain. Here's what we ordered and shared amongst a group of 5:

Market oysters ($1 before 7) which came with fried shallots and this green sauce was was SO GOOD. as someone in my group pointed out, it's ALMOST like a chimichurri sauce. the fried shallots were also a nice complementary touch. We ordered 7 dozen for 5 people LOL.

Shrimp in 3 crabs sauce ($13) - OMG as a lover of shrimp, i can attest to this. it's not cooked, so sort of like a cerviche tasting dish and it was spicy!! a must try if you love shrimp.

Grilled pork cheeks ($15) - again, really good. perfectly cooked and the exterior had a really nice flavor. 

Coconut crab curry ($23) UM, amazeballs, and i normally don't even love curry! the coconut accentuated the flavors and it was SPICY so beware. so good mixed with rice. 

Manila clam with sweet basil ($19) - very good, but spicy! a tad pricy. 

String beans - this was my least favorite dish and wasn't really impressive. you can skip this. 

Most of us ordered a cocktail/wine. Drinks were just OK. We also ordered the coconut ice cream which closed out the meal very well as a dessert!

Came here for girls' night on a freezing Thursday night. I called a day prior to make a reservation for a table of 5 for 6:30pm, which is required for large groups. Groups of four or less can book via their online reservation site/app. We ended being a group of four. There was a decent amount of people, when we got there around 6ish despite the cold temps. It's a cute place, but not that big. The kitchen is open. 

Anyways, I did not heard about this place from Chrissy Teigen, like most people did. I stumbled upon this place on Yelp, I believe. I really wanted to try it because of the seafood selection, but didn't realized it was a Thai restaurant. But either way, Chrissy, you failed us all. This place was a disappointment. 

The four of us decided to get the set for 3. We asked the waitress if it was ok, even though it was meant to be shared with 3 people. The set came with 3 appetizers, 3 entrees, and a soup. We also ordered the calamari and a dozen oysters. Oysters are $1 each during happy hour. The oysters were probably the best part of the meal. Loved the sauce they gave. It was some sort of green sauce... maybe pesto with lemon? It was different from the usual red sauce they give you. The calamari was sweet, and I'm not a fan of mixing sweet with savory. But it was not bad. I guess it's the Thai version of calamari. 

First appetizer was a pomelo salad with coconut juice? I did not like it but i came to appreciate it throughout the meal, because it helped balance out the strong flavors. Next appetizer was chicken wings with lemon. This came second fav after the oysters. It was a bit on the too sour side but I did not mind it as much. We also had some pork slices. My friends all said it tasted like viet pork chop. I'm not a fan of pork so I did not care for the dish. 

The lemongrass soup came afterwards. The flavors were too strong. Way too sour and i can feel the spice burn the back of my throat as I swallow. First few sips were good but after awhile, it's too much. And this is coming from someone who loves sour and spicy food. 

The crab curry came next. The crab flavor really came through and they were generous with the crab meat. It was a bit on the sweet and creamy end... too much coconut milk. I know Thai curry is more on the sweet end. I prefer spicy curry more. But it wasn't a bad dish. The set also comes with a bowl of rice to share. Keep in mind, they only give you one bowl of rice. Extra charge for more. Clams were next. I love clams and it's pretty hard to mess up a clam dish for me... but that is exactly what they did. That dish was wayyyy tooooo salty to consume, and I had 1/4 of a bowl of rice to eat it with. Hence how the pomelo salad came in handy throughout the meal. Last dish was a grilled fish. I love fish but this tastes like Chinese salty fish. Again, too salty. 

We were all disappointed after the meal. I wouldn't mind trying something else on the menu if I ever come back but I don't think I'd go out of my way to come eat here.

As other Yelpers have said, this place gained some hype after Chrissy Teigen sang her praises. Woman knows her food. 

Went to Fish Cheeks for a second time last night, ordered all new dishes that I hadn't ordered the first time, and had just as great of an experience. It's a very seafood heavy menu, with many flavor combos that have you going "What IS that?!" (in a good way). The She-Crab Lon was the highlight for me, especially since it was served with an array of vegetables that were new to my clearly unworldly palate. We also had the Grilled Branzino which was flaky, tender and delicious. The sauce had a sweet chili flavor, which I wasn't expecting, but it was delicious nonetheless. 

My only complaint is that I think the service needs to step it up a notch. Perhaps they expect their clientele to be well-versed on their cuisine, but I generally like a dish that has a small soup bowl, a large side of various assorted vegetable and a weird looking hash brown on the side to be explained. What is it all and how does the chef recommend that I eat it?  The server told us he recommended that we order rice with it AFTER we had already order, the food had been served and I had to swivel my head for a while to attempt to get someone's attention to explain the dish. Not super helpful. 

Unexplained dishes aside, I will certainly be back for the amazing and differentiated flavor combinations and fun vibe.

$1 dollar oysters during happy hour are a joy. Spicy, tangy and a little crunch thing on each. You wouldn't think the crunch thing would be good, but it was lovely. For five bucks I had a big smile on my face. If I don't edit this due to severe food poisoning, I encourage you to go for it. Service from waitress could have been a little more attentive/nice, but pretty standard service from entitled NYC waitresses/artists. Hostess was nicer.

The night before dining, we were only able to secure a table for 4 for Saturday 6pm - everything else was booked solid.  Upon arriving, the restaurant was fairly empty (unlike the 2 hour wait at Uncle B).  The place did get busy throughout our meal.

Staff was great.  Very helpful, attentive, and not pushy.  I wish more restaurants carried such staff.

Unfortunately the food was inconsistent and missed the mark altogether.   We shared an order of the:
- fried chicken wings appetizer (which they gave us a 2nd order as the 1st was partially undercooked - and they were just ok in flavor)
- coconut crab curry (very spicy, very flavorful)
- crispy branzino (seemed to be missing garnish and flavor)
- she-crab lon (solid flavor but small portion compared to everything else?)
- vegan curry (flat in taste, huge portion)
- durian ice cream (very good, big portion)
- kaffir lime cheesecake (tasty, but nothing to write home about)

In terms of price, this meal felt expensive for the offering.  In comparison to a similar style restaurant in a quiet part of Brooklyn, we paid the same amount for a larger quantity of lower caliber food unfortunately.  

Given all the good Thai offerings opening in the city, it will be hard to return here.

Fish Cheeks is one of those places that don't adjust the spiciness of their dishes because they want it to stay "authentic." But authentic for authentic sake and at the detriment to the diner is not worth it. My friend and I ordered dishes with one, two and three stars and they all varied. The two was more spicy than the three and overall I didnt get to enjoy the flavors as much because they were all so spicy. Hopefully they will get that not everyone can handle it but do want to try the other dishes with higher spice levels. The restaurant itself is cute and very Instagram friendly, and definitely not your cheap grab and go Thai food. Being on Bond St, I guess they have to pay for their rent somehow. What I did love? A sign that says no phat thai.

Fish Cheeks was recommended to me by a random stranger I met while waiting in line for dim sum last week. She apparently was also visiting the city from California and after talking to her long enough to thaw out from the cold, we swapped tips on places to eat. When I mentioned Uncle Boons, she told me about this place, which she had found out about through Chrissie Teigan. It was sImilar to Uncle Boons, but with a focus on seafood. Of course I had to squeeze this into my itinerary now. I wasn't able to make a reservation but luckily was still able to grab seats at the bar one night for dinner. We had the Coconut Crab Curry, Crispy Garlic Branzino with Fish Sauce, Crab Fried Rice, and a few oysters, which were on the happy hour menu. Except for the oysters, which were nothing special, I recommend all of these items! My favorite was probably the crispy branzino. If you've never had fish sauce before, asians use this to make any food taste good. It was delicious, I scraped every last remnant of fish off of the plate. The coconut crab curry comes with a side of rice and was very well balanced with plenty pieces of actual crab meat. Crab fried rice was good, a little on the mild side for me, but this was my sister's favorite. I also had the watermelon spritz which I thought was diluted and can be skipped.

The ambiance inside the restaurant is pretty and trendy. It is VERY cozy and our server at the bar was a bit douchey, but overall good experience. Definitely a must if you're into northern thai food.

Yet again I long for Yelp to add half stars. This really was a 3.5 or 3.8, but I can't bring myself to give a 4. Showed up on a Friday night without a reservation but it was 5:30 so I figured how busy could it be. The place was basically empty but we were told we could only have the tiny two seat table squished between the bar and the pick up area, even tough we explained we had to be out by 6:30 at the latest, and there still were a few empty tables when we were leaving. Drinks were really good and not insanely expensive. We opted for 5 small plates to share, which was a perfect amount of food. Unfortunately, I found the quality to be all over the place. Some of the dishes, such as the raw shrimp, were spectacular. Others, such as the fried chicken, were just fair. And I thought they were a little pricey.  All that being said, I want to go back and try their chef's menu, as many of the mains were quite appealing.

Really amazing food.  the spicy mango cocktail was amazing.  here's what we ordered:
- Coconut Crab Curry (double ordered, amazing)
- Calamari (probably the best calamari I've ever had)
- Crispy Garlic Branzino
- Goong Aob Woon Senn (peppery delicious)
- Shrimp in 3 Crab Sauce (spicy but wonderful)
- Seafood Pad Cha
- Steamed Fish & Yum Goong (Yum goong was great)
- Grilled Pork Cheeks
- Golae Mussels

we were 6 ladies and this was a good amount, erring on the side of probably too much. but everything was great, reasonably priced! this will be added into my restaurant rotation for sure

No Pad Thai Zone. 

I'm a little disappointed in myself for not trying this place earlier when I had first bookmarked it. The food here is unbelievable. Great sauces and great flavors that will tickle your taste buds. 

Happy Hour is everyday 12-4pm, 5-7pm. $10 cocktails, $8 wine, $5 beers  & $1 oysters. The oysters are amazing, freshly shucked with crispy shallots and seafood sauce. The raw shrimp with bird's eye chili was a small appetizer but fulfilled my craving. The grilled pork cheeks with the thai chili sauce is highly recommended. The coconut crab curry was hearty with a handful amount of crab meat. Beware, it's hot spicy. More numbing than your average curry. This curry portion is not as big as the vegan curry and they both are served with a bowl of white jasmine rice. The Manila clams and strings beans were both great additions to my meal as well. I honestly cannot wait to be back to try the rest of the menu. 

 I did not have any alcoholic beverages because I had to go in a hurry but the Thai inspired cocktails looks like they will kick my taste buds. I had lunch here during the afternoon when it was not that busy but I heard that it can get crazy here. The staff member was very sweet, welcoming, and attentive.Take advantage of their website to make an easy reservation and you can visually see their menu online as well.

Were we being treated differently just because we did not make a reservation?

I would totally recommend you come here for happy hour which includes $1 oysters and $5 beers and then call it a night. Anyway, the seafood sauce was a little too salty. You should tone down either salt or fish sauce a tad. Seafood sauce should be tangy and spicy instead.

I don't think I'm their targeted clientele since every item on the menu is very pricey. $22 for a so-called family style curry? So it becomes our burden when their rent is too damn high?

We ordered a family style Coconut Crab Curry which is a deconstructed version of Haw Mok. I thought the taste was just right; however, I don't think they really grasp the concept of family style. How come the dish only comes with one small bowl of rice? Oh and this is the highlight of the meal. When I asked for an extra bowl of rice, the server informed us that there would be $4 extra!!! Was this jasmine rice grown in a gold paddy? -- Oh, I just checked the price on their menu. An extra bowl of rice is only $3. Why did my server tell me $4?

Wow! I really do wish I had disposable income to become a frequent patron here. You can splurge here once, but I guarantee there are better options out there.

Authentic Thai. Great food, ordered Set #1. It would be tough to pick what was my "favorite" of the many plates presented the Tom Yum Pla was perfectly spicy, Noi's Fried Chicken and Goong Abo were amazing. Definitely 5 Stars except for the tables. Too small for two people. We had plates piled on plates. As each dish was delivered the pile grew. Other than that little gripe, good food great service.
Delicious authentic unique fine Thai food. Well priced . Homelike atmosphere. Excellent staff. So glad I wanted to try this cuisine .

Came here for happy hour and dinner with a couple friends. We started with some oysters and cocktails, which were very good. I wasn't a huge fan of the guava smash but the spicy mango was tasty and fruity. 

For our main entrees, we originally ordered the fried branzino, crab curry and the pork cheeks, but after the food came out, the portion for the crab curry was very small for the price so we decided to order another entree. We went with the crab fried rice. The branzino was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. I liked the dish a lot because of its texture but my other friends preferred the crab curry and pork cheeks which were stronger in flavors. The crab fried rice was decent as well and adding the crab curry to the fried rice made it even better.

Overall, good Thai restaurant with unique flavors and dishes though definitely on the pricier side. I also think the food is probably a little more Americanized but still very delicious.

If you love spicy Thai and fresh seafood, this is the place for you. In particular, you'll definitely want to double down on the crab curry. Huge chunks of fresh crab in a flavorful curry that's got a good kick to it. The oysters should also be on your list - instead of coming with your run of the mill mignonette sauce, these fresh oysters come with a delicious Thai dipping sauce (nam jim) and fried shallots. The morning glory/Thai watercress isn't always on the menu - but when it is, it's a must. The leaves are tenderly cooked in a delicious, light savory broth. Noi's fried chicken is also great alternative to seafood if you're looking for some tender, lightly fried chicken. Really haven't had a single thing here that wasn't good. I've only eaten hear on the early side (5/5:30), so I haven't had to deal with the crowding or noise that others complain about -- but seeing as the space is rather tight, I can see how that might be an issue for some.
Food was good. Service was below average for the price point and the level of ambience.

Pros: flavorful dishes! Been here twice and not disappointed. She crab and crab fried rice are a must try!

Cons: it's loud during peak hours and the portions are small.
Went there right on time they open, but it didn't and have to wait 30 mins till it opens. But, they have great food and spicy sauce.

I had a mediocre bunch experience at Fish Cheeks. The menu was limited (perhaps because it was the brunch menu) and it was lacking options. I really enjoyed the tum yong soup and it was the one dish that I felt was rich in flavor. For main course, we ordered crab fried rice, curry, and sautéed cabbage. All were lacking finesse and flavor, especially compared to other Thai restaurants I have been to in the city. Service was also slow. For that reason, even though the vibe at Fish Cheeks was cute, I likely wouldn't return back to the restaurant.

I really tried to enjoy Fish Cheeks. Heard good reviews about it but for some reason the food was not very appetizing. We ordered most of the menu including the fried rice and fish. The food was just bland.

Very solid and delicious Thai place - and I enjoyed that it had more of a seafood focus. Worth coming especially during happy hour to take advantage of their $1 oysters. Delicious cocktail selection and you get a really hefty portion of pork cheeks for an appetizer. Delicious Tom Yum fish soup - pieces were cubed and completely deboned. This place is great to go as a group since the dishes are meant to be shared, though I wish there were more options for those who show up solo.

Delicious food with extremely spotty service. Maybe it was an off night, but it took several attempts to get the waiter's attention for each of the following things: ordering drinks, ordering more drinks, ordering food, asking about our missing dish, asking for more water (the food was spicy!), and asking for the bill. We were a large group that was happy to spend the time catching up, but it did make for a somewhat stressful experience each time time we needed anything at all.

All of the dishes were solid - my favorites were the oysters (garlic sauce is amazing), calamari (crispy and flavorful), and crab curry (loved the heat). The food is good enough to return for, but I'd think twice about coming back because of the service.

Cool restaurant and authentic food (a cheeky sign says "no pad thai zone").  On the two times I came here I had the crab curry, steamed fish and fried fish.  The food is a little pricey but given its central Soho location it was worth it.
Ordered the set menu for 3 plus a crab rice for a group of five and literally every dish was outstanding. My personal favorites were the fish and the crab curry.

Fried calamari (5 stars): crispy, tender, sweet, and funky

Yum goong (5 stars): perfectly tender poached jumbo shrimp mixed with fresh cilantro and crispy shallots

Crab curry (5 stars): actually spicy! Generous portion of perfectly cooked chunks of crab

Pak boong fai dang (4.5 stars): if the portion were larger it would definitely be 5 stars. Fresh and savory, full of nostalgia

Raw shrimp (4 stars): less tender than some other versions we've had in the city, more like a ceviche and probably cooked longer in citrus. Satisfies the craving though

Happy hour every day and totally worth it! Service is lovely, and they open up the windows when the weather is nice

Very disappointed. Ordered the Chef selection #2 and only 1 dish out of the 6 was actually good; the lump crab meat curry (this one it is worth trying though!!). They really need to check the quality of the mussles and be careful not to overcook the fried branzino. We didn't understand the side of thick pork belly in syrup.

Chef selection plus two beers came to a $140 bill. It doesn't make any sense for the quality you are getting. Quantity is good.

Service was nice and attentive although the pace of the plates during dinner felt a bit overwhelming (4 plates at the same time on the table for 2 people)
one of the best thai places i've been to! it's a small restaurant but the service is good and quality of food and drinks is top notched. a very well-rounded restaurant!

OMG! This place is AMAZING! I visited NYC after a trip to Thailand and I was blown away by the offering. Any of the specials they have are thoughtfully prepared and the flavors are to DIE FOR. I still dream of those flavors to this day. If you are visiting NYC, do yourself a favor and come to this restaurant. Try the Specials menu and go with their recommended for group tasting. If you come at happy hour, they have $1 oysters and I could just snack on their oysters all night! 

They have some really interesting and delicious cocktails. If I lived in NYC, I would visit every week and try something new each time. I'm really impressed by their menu and ambiance/decor. Great place for groups and dates!

The food and the bartender are wonderful. The hostess is awful. We went right after work for happy hour & wanted a table. The restaurant was empty & we were told they had reservations for all the tables so we sat @ the bar. We left around 8 & a table right by the bar was empty the whole time. When I asked why we couldn't have sat there bc no one came. She couldn't keep her story straight first they needed the table @ 8. I pointed out that it was 8 - then she said she had a cancellation. It's the little things that will determine whether or not I'd go back no matter how good the food is.

Cool place to hang out with friends after a long work of day.  This restaurant features an open kitchen and offers happy hour $1 oyster deal from 5-7 pm.  The bartender is very friendly.  The decor is hip and homey.  

I highly recommend the coconut crab soup which comes with a side of jasmine white rice. At first glance, the soup does not look spicy at all.  Rather, it is a bright orange color with a little cream in the middle.  It looks pretty plain, but don't be deceived though. With each bite, you can distinctively taste the richness of the soup and the complex umami flavor from the chicken broth and crab meat.  The spiciness is addictive.  The more you drink it, the more you want to reach for a second spoonful of the crab soup.  Amazing.  

My favorite dish of the night is the glass noddle dish.  Usually I like this dish with crab.  This dish is served up with shrimp and sliced pork.  It is a fairly traditional Thai dish. I love the salty and sweet contrasting flavor of this dish.  Although the noodle does not come with any thick sauce, it does not feel dry when you eat it.  

The coconut ice cream is also such a delight, a great way to finish the meal and satisfy that sweet tooth.  

The only complaint I have is that no one checked upon our table for a good hour.  It seems like the restaurant is a bit understaffed.  

Overall, a great Thai restaurant! Worth a try.

aka my new go-to thai spot..

Been here twice with the wife within the past 3 weeks. The staff is attentive when they're busy for dinner just as when they're slow and about to close. Good experiences both times but I just had to remind the waiter about the shrimp crackers the last time I dined there. (Hey man it's free). No issues other than that.

Ordered Set 2 both times and I'm glad to say it's been consistently good.
Set 2 menu includes
Fried calamari: 5/5, craveable comfort food.
Mussels: 3.5/5, decent app.
Fried branzino: 4/5,  salty and crispy.
Braised pork belly: 3/5, good sauce but fatty af
Thai watercress: 5/5 I can eat this by itself and I'll be fine with it
Coconut crab curry: 4.5/5 spicy and meaty af.

Also ordered shrimp in 3 crab sauce not included in the set menu. 
5/5, I'll swim in that.

Time to explore the menu a la carte the next time visit

Very authentic preparation! We ordered the set B for 2 of us. It was plenty of food for two people, and every dish is full of wonderful flavors. Fresh galangal, thai basil, kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass made up the fragrant broth for the mussels. The calamari was superb. The fried branzino, the tide watercress, the blue crab curry and the pork belly - yummmmmmm! Great combination of dishes accompanied with thai rice. 

Almost forgot to mention - they have happy hour 5-7pm: $1 oysters (comes with thai basil pesto/vinegrette and fried shallots), all cocktails are $10. 

In general, this is a great place to develop your taste buds for good, real thai food. Worth a try! Next time I would probably try the glass noodles with the shrimp and pork belly!

Fish Cheeks is a Thai restaurant unlike any other that I have been to. I had to subdue my basic girl tendencies, as this place does not serve your usual Pad Thai or Pad See Ew. I made reservations for dinner on a Saturday night and I was so glad I did, as it was packed. The thai watercress was the dish that I enjoyed most, surprisingly. It was much spicier than we thought, so I had the pleasure of eating most of it as my boyfriend could not handle it. We also ordered the branzino, because we noticed that a lot of people around us did, but I did not like it much. The calamari was exceptional though. We did not make it on time to try their happy hour specials but I would love to in the future.

Delicious. Slightly expensive for a lunch time meal but their happy hour has $1 oysters and they are yum. Highly recommend this place. The food is worth the extra few bucks you might spend on a lunch.

Surpassed my expectations, their crab fried rice is so much better than Uncle Boons, the thai watercress was good but a bit salty, the pork was great as well, im a huge fan of cilantro and they use a lot of cilantro in their dishes but my friend isnt so partial to it and she ended up enjoying the meal regardless.  the portions are small for the price but im a fan and cant wait to come back to try their other dishes
Was a little disappointed. The portions are small. Not the best Thai food I had. They do have a good oyster happy hour til 7pm. I left the restaurant still hungry.

My homegirl, Chrissy Teigan, said that this is the spot to check out. She is right. Located on hip and trendy Bond Street, Fish Cheeks infuses spice and flavor into the NoHo area. It's easily one of the best Thai places in the city. 

The details:
1. Do you want basic pad Thai? Don't come here. Fish Cheeks is more than the basics. Here you're going to find real Thai flavors and dishes that aren't completely Americanized. 
2. That happy hour really adds so much value to the experience. The one dollar oysters, $10 cocktails make every so much better. 
3. That. Coconut. Crab. Curry. It is perfectly aromatic and spicy but grounded in coconut flavor. You must get this. 
4. Its such a chill vibe compared to the surrounding area. 
5. They deliver. TAKE ADVANTAGE of this. 

Fish Cheeks is the place to be. It's a wonderful Thai place that gives off real flavor. It's a must-try in the city.

Phenomenal ! I never wait to eat, I am the prime example for HANGRY. If I have to wait to eat, it just isn't worth it to me. However, this time, I did wait 20 minutes for them to open. They have split hours of operation I believe, and it was bad timing on our part as we stumbled upon this special treat. I guess since my boyfriend was so eager for me to try - I waited. 

Glad I did, I'm learning patience is a virtue. (: I do think this place is pretty pricey, but so worth every penny. Their oysters were so good, I wanted, but knew I couldn't afford more. I forgot where they were from, but the sauces they made with it was what made it so darn good. It left my mouth salvating for more. 

We got a variety of stuff, but my favorite was the crab fried rice. Ugh, I'm drooling thinking about it. Their calamari was nothing special, but that sauce ! I'm a sucker for sauce, and they have perfected theirs ! We also got the coconut crab curry which was mediocre in my opinion, but I'm just not a die hard fan of coconut based curries. (My boyfriend loved it though) I almost forgot their DELICIOUS tom yum soup. Oh man, hands down BEST Tom Yum I've ever had ! 

Definitely recommend this place, just make sure you go when their open. If not, wait. I promise, you won't regret it !

Great coconut crab curry and nam tok pork. Oyster happy hour is fantastic as well. Spicy and not your standard american Thai joint. Lots of flavor and fresh vegetables - definitely worth trying. Will make it a regular.

I had a craving for Thai food, well noodles to be exact, while shopping in soho so my fiancé googled it and Fish Cheeks popped up. I was sold on the photo of the crispy branzino so we hopped in a cab and head over. We called first and there was no wait which was awesome considering we called another restaurant and there was a 2 hour wait for two people which is typical on a Saturday. 

I read over the menu in the cab to get an idea of what to order and the first thing that stood out to me was that they didn't have pad Thai on the menu. Considering my craving for noodles prompted this visit I immediately begin to panic and reconsider but my fiancé convinced me to stay the course and perhaps there would be other options. I am definitely glad we made that decision! Upon arrival the smells coming out of the open kitchen hits you immediately and made me forget I ever wanted pad Thai. We were seated immediately, brought water and the hostess took our bags so we would have space sitting along the Bankhead. It was still happy hour so my fiancé ordered a cocktail and half a dozen $1 oysters and I happily watched (37 weeks preggers so none for me...yet). We went ahead and ordered fried calamari, crispy branzino, and a glass noodle dish with shrimp ginger pork belly (the actual name escapes me). They give you a puffy chip dish with a shrimp/fish paste to snack on while waiting for your food which was so tasty! Gabriel, our server was awesome and kind enough to bring another when my fiancé oysters and cocktail came so I wouldn't feel left out of the dining experience. I also ordered a Thai ice tea which was absolutely delicious! 

Watching other tables food come out was exciting because you can see what your order will look like as well as what you should try next. When the calamari came out it looked amazing but I felt like I could have eaten it by myself so I would suggest ordering more than one appetizer. And considering how amazing it was I regret not getting two! When the entrees came out we had a chance to see the coconut curry crab and we immediately wished we had ordered that as well considering how small the portions are. I normally wouldn't complain about portion sizes and price since it's New York and ultimately you're paying the rent when you think of prices, but when you say family style, it should be enough food to feed a family. I'd say the servings look more like you ordered two meals and shared the dishes to try both. Aside from that, both dishes were amazing but we were still hungry afterwards so ultimately we ordered the curry crab and were so happy we did. It was sooooo good and soooo spicy!!! Full but wanting to explore more we ordered the ice cream for dessert that was filled coconut, jackfruit and condense milk. It was perfect for sharing and just enough for us to be too full, lol! 

Overall my takeaway from this experience is that it's a pad thai free zone that you walk away from feeling satisfied. I strongly recommend this place for large groups as we were surrounded by parties of 4 or more and also it's a good way to explore the whole menu. If you come with one other person order extra apps or a third meal to get your fair share of food since portions are not what you would consider to be "family style".

Very good food! 

Was walking by and noticed the $1 oyster happy hour! Decided to give it a try and it was a great choice. 

The layout is very welcoming - high ceilings; bright colors with a white wall and a nice open kitchen format. Great to hangout with friends. 

But it was the food that really made this visit. The oysters (from MA) were fresh and their mignonette was excellent. I also had the fried chicken with the sweet Thai chili sauce. Was good!! Reminded me of my time in Singapore. For drinks I had a Thai ice tea which was decent. 

Service is not intrusive but quick to respond to requests. 

Price: happy hour was a great deal but I'm not sure if the food is worth the price at other times.

Regardless, a spot I'd recommend

Love this place! Beautiful interior that's trendy and classy. Perfect for out of town guests or a night with friends. I went with my thai friend and she even said that there's things on the menu that no other Thai restaurant has. Food was amazing, I loved the curry

Going to admit that I only heard about this place because of Chrissy Teigen and decided to give it a try because the menu looks amazing and Chrissy Teigen loves food the same way that I love food. 

Had reservations for three at 7:15 but my party and I arrived early and they seated us without any problem at around 6:30. Since we made it in time for happy hour, we started off with 18 of their $1 oysters. The oysters are served with lemon wedges, fried shallots and a green sauce. It's much nicer than the standard cocktail sauce.

The entrees are all listed as 'Thai family-style dishes' but would not consider them family-style portions. My two friends and I ordered the fried branzino and the coconut crab curry, thinking it would be enough but we ended up getting the crab fried rice as well in order to fill us up. 

The fried branzino is served whole, split in half down the center. Be sure to eat the skin and all the little crispy parts - they're the best parts. The coconut crab curry soup is definitely not for those who cannot spicy foods. There were large lumps of crab meat in there but I would've really hoped for a larger portion, given its price. The crab fried rice was definitely my favorite dish of the evening. It seems so simple but it's so good. Warm and fluffy. When you pour the green sauce that it comes with over it, it turns it something amazing and addictive. I would eat an entire bucket of it if I could.

Had an overall great experience at Fish Cheeks. You cannot miss the place with it's colorful exterior. This is a card only restaurant, so don't forget it at home.

Fantastic.  This isn't your ordinary pad thai place.  The food is really great: the fried chicken appetizer, the fried branzino entree, and the crab fried rice were particularly great.
But skip the desserts---they're mediocre at best.

Went there for dinner and not disappointed. Everything is soo yummy,all staff are nice. Great interior,it's gonna be one of my favorite Thai restaurant. Can't wait to go back soon for trying lunch menu. FYI: accept credit/debit card only.
I want to give this a 4.5. Cute place with good service. The vibe is fun and the cocktails are strong! The crab coconut curry is one of the best (and spiciest) things i've ever had.

I had a really nice dinner here! We got the prix fixe menu A and really enjoyed it. I was stoked about the calamari, and the mussels were great even though I am new to eating mussels. I was hoping that the fried branzino would be a little less dry + fried, but I guess that's what the description says it will be. The crab curry really has a crab flavor (in addition to the pieces of crab in it). The watercress was really nice too. 

The atmosphere is a lot of fun. It's a little bit loud but v visually appealing. I was sad that we missed happy hour because it seems like they have good deals. The lunch menu looks a little different from the dinner menu (notably, there are more noodles) so would be excited to explore that as well.

I ordered the steamed fish with Thai herbs. I was pleasantly surprised at how fresh the fish was... extremely flavorful as well.. not heavily doused in spices.... I enjoyed my meal.... I was a little surprised that I had to order rice as a side... I would suggest that the owners include rice with their entrees... other than that I enjoyed my meal.

I don't know how this place got such a high rating. I came here with an expectation given the reviews. I was VERY disappointed.
First of all, their portions are SMALL and OVERPRICED. 
We order one of the specials which is the Crab Cake last night. And they have shells in them.
Their fried chicken was ok, but don't tell me it's deep fried because it was not.
Namtok Pork: If you want to get a few pieces of grill pork and big pieces of cabbage which occupy the whole plate for $14, go for it.
The watercress was ok.
And in general, all the dishes was too salty for my taste. It probably cater to the American crowd. If you want authentic Thai food, don't come here.
Once you have the crab fried rice , you'll crave it.  Was a party of 3 and had more than enough food with the tasting menu for 2 to share. Cool that you get happy hour prices at the table until 7.

Came here with my husband for an early dinner. I love Thai food and we've been to Thai restaurants all over Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Queens. Fish Cheeks is my new favorite and the flavors are super authentic - even better than Queens stalwarts like Ayada. Seafood here is soooo fresh. 5 stars!

Expectations are really a funny thing. 

Mine were exceptionally high partially because Chrissy Teigen (enough said) and because of the amazing photos seen on IG as well as on Yelp. 

A friend and I arrived for lunch on a hot day and it was a relief to walk into this air conditioned and brightly colored space! The interior as well as the bathroom was welcoming and well designed, and the service from beginning to end was impeccable, from a number of different employees. The waiter was well informed and consistently refilling our water as well being available to us, even as the restaurant filled up.

I love that it says 'NO PAD THAI ZONE' on the sign, giving people a chance to try the range of different Thai dishes available instead of defaulting to pad Thai. My friend and I ordered the Senn Lek Tom Yum, thin rice noodles in a lemongrass broth with mussels, shrimps, calamari, and a soft boiled egg ($16) which we loved! This had one chili pepper next to it but no fear, as someone who doesn't take spice well, it was not spicy at all. The seafood was fresh and the broth was heartily delicious, with some sourness adding to the flavor. Would definitely recommend! 

My gripe is with the second dish we ordered, the Kana Moo Krob, pork belly with Chinese broccoli and a fried egg over rice ($14). It did not look like the photos seen on Yelp of this dish, but that wasn't my first thought. My first thought after my first bite was that this dish was SPICY! This dish has no chili peppers next to it but the chili flakes were apparent in the dish. We struggled to eat it but we had been really looking forward to trying the Chinese broccoli, and it was drenched in the soy sauce/chili mix. The pork belly was delicious, but it was way too spicy for a dish that had no indication of spice. On second look, the photo on Yelp showed seafood in addition to pork belly in this dish, so I'm confused as to if they messed up the dish by making it spicy OR by forgetting the seafood. 

Other than the prices being slightly higher than your average Thai place, the only reason I would take extra precaution when coming here is for that hiccup in the dish. 

I definitely will be coming back to try other dishes as well as the oyster happy hour, and I hope for a better experience then! 

Credit card only.

Went at an off hour during the weekend when it was completely empty. Considering we were the only people in the restaurant, thought they would be a little bit more flexible in extending their happy hour a little earlier. Did not grudge. Portions were small but good. Considering the price and how you can get the same quality of Thai food elsewhere, I'm not sure if I would come back. Especially with the subpar service.

Very flavorful and authentic Thai food. The calamari prepared with a tamarind glaze is an absolute must. The curry we ordered had just the right amount of heat in it. If you're looking to be served quickly and eat great food this is the place for you , service and food is very quick even on a busy night. Very satisfied

The best crab fried rice I've ever had. It melted in my mouth. Ask for the Thai bird's eye chillies on the side, so you can make your mouth a burning crater which can only be quenched with more crab fried rice

I like this Thai spot. It's more a mixed fusion style but the food and service was good. I liked the quality of the dishes. I would go back for their happy hour specials, feel free to try it out. Tom Yom Soup is always my favorite!
