A Thai food place with no pad Thai served? I would have to sit down and give a try. Had to admit that sitting inside a place with no AC on a humid hot day was not easy, however nothing could stop me from dining here!

We came in as a group of three, very hungry, so equivalent to a group of four. Seafood lovers would find themselves at home! Crab fried rice was non-skippable - large chunk of crab pieces fit themselves inside the perfectly cooked fried rice, very chewy, nicely seasoned. The Tom Yum Goong soup, unlike other Thai places, was light and refreshing. This was definitely one of the better meals I have enjoyed in the neighborhood.

They also provide the family style tasting menu, serving either 2 or 3 people, 45 dollars pp, very good deal!

I would give this place another try because the flavor combos look interesting and the decor is very cute. 

But the dry noodles I ordered were indeed dry but it had no flavor, and the pieces of crab and pork didn't justify the price.

I enjoyed my visit to Fish Cheeks. I had the crab curry and it definitely packs a nice kick. It was a relaxed vibe, I ate at bar. I liked the decor as well as the music, brought me back to my trip to Thailand many years ago. I look forward to trying more if menu.

Wonderful new addition to Manhattan in a convenient and popular location. It's truly difficult to find and recommend good Thai restaurants in Manhattan. I would surely add this to the list.

You won't find a bread basket at a Thai restaurant but typically there's a complimentary basket of shrimp chips. Usually I've seen this paired with peanut sauce but over here you get a chili paste as dip - nice! (For those who like spicy flavor). Chips are good on their own too for those who cant't or don't want the spice.

Tried the following dishes 

Noi's Fried Chicken Plate
Deep fried chicken with shallot served with sweet chili sauce.
Nothing special (and not bad) - truly just an average snack to nibble on if you want fried chicken 

Namtok Pork Plate
Grilled pork, roasted rice, shallot, scallion, cilantro and chili. Spicy.
Definitely the least favorite. Flavors are there but was a little too saucy/watery for my preference 

Crispy Garlic Branzino with Fish Sauce
Whole branzino and fried garlic with fish sauce broth.
Oh boy this was quite dry. I should've looked at the visual menu first to see this was breaded. Normally i like fried and normally I like breaded and fried but I was expecting something different. It's a meaty dish but the breading was overwhelming. The fish sauce is served on the side and can be added to suit your preference but this was my 2nd least favorite dish.

Goong Aob Woonsen
Baked shrimp, thinly sliced pork belly, glass noodle, cilantro root & celery leaves
Love glass noodles whether they're sauteed, yum (salad), or in this case, baked.

Coconut Crab Curry
Southern style curry, jumbo lump crab meat with mortar and pestle crushed curry paste and betel leaves served with rice. Spicy.
Best dish of the night. Great creamy/milky texture and amazing flavor with generous amounts of crab meat. 

Crispy Pork Belly with Holy Basil
Stringbean, long red chili, garlic.
2nd best dish of the night. Crispy and tasty!

Pak Boong Fai Dang
Thai watercress, bird's eye chili, garlic.
Standard Thai veggie dish executed well. Wish this was available entree size.

This restaurant, as noted on the specials board, is a pad Thai free zone. No need to get disappointed because there are other dishes that represent popular  authentic Thai dishes. Comfortable setting with Thai carabao-style music playing soft enough to remind you of Thailand and to have a conversation 

A diverse selection of beverages is available  alcoholic and non-alcoholic. A spiked Thai iced tea is available and is really strong - subtle on Thai tea flavor and heavy on the whiskey. Watermelon juice is really good. Of course there's Thai beer and Thai iced tea and Thai iced coffee

What a great meal!  We started out with the fried chicken small plate, and the chicken was tasty, tender, and paired well with the sweet chile sauce.  My wife ordered the Crab red curry, which was HOT,  but I couldn't stop taste testing!  I very much enjoyed the goong aob woon senn, which had rice noodles, brisket, and fresh shrimp.  The cocktails are fresh to order and tasty as well.  Highly recommend if you're looking for some Thai that is out of the ordinary and especially delicious.

Love this place! We came in for late dinner on Monday and only got to try a few things but everything was SO delicious. Natalia's suggestions were on point -must try the namtok pork and guava smash! Best Thai I've had in NYC

OVERPRICED and OVERHYPED Thai place ever. 

It says "Family-Style Dishes" but the portion is REALLY small. I thought the price is pricy because of family style. now I am not too sure if they understood the word "family-style."

We ordered coconut crab curry and seafood pad cha which we paid about $50 + tip and taxes. so we ended up paying about $60 for delivery. I was really shocked when they were delivered. I thought we were missing something. I thought they are pricy because of quality, but quality is not good at all. 

Do you ever want to pay $22 for 6 tiny pieces of squid, 2 scallops and 4 shrimps? Lol. and also pay another $22 for "taste-nothing but spicy" curry? 

Either they need to lower their price or improve the quality.

Chrissy Teigen told me to come to Fish Cheeks. No but I'm glad she mentioned it.

Fish Cheeks is not your typical Americanized Thai fare, but definitely a pretty solid interpretation of authentic Thai food. Do come with friends or family, or even both! This is family-style so I recommend ordering a bunch of food so you can taste a bit of everything because honestly, everything was delicious. 

The star for me is the:
Coconut Crab Curry - they use huge chunks of crab meat and am so glad they're not skimpy on it! the curry is spicy but ohsogood. 
I also ordered the calamari, wings, Goong Aob Woon Senn, and the crispy garlic branzino
with fish sauce. I won't go too much into it but the branzino was VERY crispy and dipped with the fish sauce, you can't go wrong! I would however probably skip the goong aob woon senn next time. All the food has huge flavors so I do find it a bit salty but that's generally how some Thai/Viet food is.

Pleasantly surprised by Fish Cheeks as I generally have lower expectations for Thai food in NY.  Came here with a party of 5 and ordered dinner set # 3 (about 8 dishes, $135, suggested for a party of 3) + a couple of other things that we wanted to add. 

The standout dishes for me were the tom yum goong and nam tok pork. The tom yum was as good as any that I have had in Thailand. Large chunks of galangal, flavorful kaffir lime leaves, spicy - you can't go wrong. The nam tok pork was on point too, the flavors in the sauce instantly transporting me back to Thailand. This is what I had sorely missed in NYC for a long time.

There were some other good dishes worth mentioning. The seafood pad cha had a distinct southern Thai flavor with it's sour notes which are usually balanced out by a generous use of chili peppers. Not a dish for every one but I loved it. For something more fatty and decadent, you can't go wrong with crispy pork belly while the fried branzino is a safe choice.

The only item that I was disappointed with was the coconut crab carry.  This is a dish I had almost daily when was in Thailand last. It's usually served with yellow curry but this version was done with a darker curry which overpowered the crab. 

We also got the calamari which wasn't memorable and the batter came off too easily. We did like the mussels however. The mussels are small like Thai mussels though I think these are of better quality and the sauce was excellent.

For sides we got the Thai watercress and sauteed cabbage. Both were great.

If it sounds like we had the whole menu, it's cos we did. It was a lot of food but somehow we managed to finish all of it. I would happily recommend them to anyone who want real Thai food.

No Pad Thai Zone... You won't find any of the standard Thai food here, but what they do have is very flavorful, tasty food. 

The lunch menu is fairly limited compared to dinner. There are various options for either rice or noodle dishes. Ordered one of each. 
Kuay Tiao Phed is a braised duck leg served with egg noodles with a soft boiled egg, garlic, and celery leaves. Duck was nice and tender. The broth had a good spice to it, just the right amount of spice where it's spicy enough, but not too much so you still enjoy the dish. It was just the right balance for me. 
Kana Moo Krob is stir fried crispy pork belly with Chinese broccoli over rice with an egg. Stir fry had shrimp and veggies. Pork belly was tender with a nice crisp skin. 

Both dishes were flavorful. Fish Cheeks was an unplanned meal destination, but so glad we made it in. 

The chef even came over after the meal to introduce himself and asked how the food was. He also asked where we were from and how we had heard about the restaurant. He was genuinely friendly and very nice. I highly recommend Fish Cheeks and wish a return visit could be sooner.

I am excited to find out some excellent Asian foods are delivering to West Village, even though the distance is not close, and Fish Cheeks is one of exciting restaurants.

Crab Fried Rice ($24) 
This fluffy fried rice is packed with crab meat and very appetizing. It comes with its sauce but it is delicious by its own. I can have it all to myself, yum!

Coconut Crab Curry ($22)
Spicy red curry with chunks of crab meat wasn't so exciting as the fried rice. It is because the complex flavor of curry hiding the crab flavor, for me. But the curry sauce is excellent (house made?) and a generous portion of crab meat is definitely satisfying.

HOLY COW! where do I start? As a Thai person this place rules, not your regular Pad thai kind of place. Loved the oyster with the thai spicy sauce. We got the Hat Yai Fried Chicken and steam whole fish in chili lime sauce, it was out of bound. Go there and try it for yourself.
Reservation is recommended if you are going there for dinner.

This is a review of the even by Tasting Collective that we attended. It was a 9-course brunch, created especially for this event. We were excited to try yet another authentic Thai restaurant! 

It was easy to spot with bright, colorful awning in fish scale design. The inside is also very bright and colorful, I really liked the interior. They have colorful chairs that bring out the fun atmosphere, just by looking at them! It is not a large space, but not too small either. Just the right size for a cozy, homey dining.

They have a bar at the back, also with colorful fish scale tiles under the bar counter. Right behind the bar is their kitchen, kind of open kitchen so if you are sitting at the bar or close enough to it, you can see them creating the tasty food right there. They have a sign on the wall that says "NO PAD THAI ZONE" which I thought was awesome.

For this special event, we had Fried Calamari, Namtok Pork, Prince Edward Island Mussels & Herbs, Shrimp Fried Rice, Coconut Crab Curry, Steamed Fish with Thai Herbs, Sautéed Cabbage, Kana Fai Dang, and Thai Tea Panna Cotta for dessert. Everything was so amazingly delicious, it was great!!! Most of them spicy, much spicier than some can take, but so flavorful and addictive... Loved them all! 

This was another very successful event, with amazing food and great people. I enjoyed all the dishes, I would love to go back for more spicy, addictive, super flavorful dishes. Thank you Tasting Collecting for introducing us to another fantastic restaurant!

Went twice to fish cheeks within a month! I'm usually not a big fan of Thai food however this is not the typical Thai restaurants in NYC. First thing you notice is the decor - simple yet elegant and beautiful.  We ordered the 3 people prefix menu that could have fed 5 people! It came with 3 appetizers and about 6 family style entree dishes. I felt like I was at a Thai home. The food was so homey and comforting! Definitely the best Thai food I've had so far in the city. Will be coming back!

Came bc CHRISSY TEIGEN RAVES that this is her favorite Thai place in NY. Just ate here, and can confirm that everything is so flavorful and aromatic and amazing. 

We came at 6:30, and happy hour ends at 7 ($10 for cocktails, $8 wine, and $5 beer). I got the Thai basil cocktail (has vermouth in it), and my friends got the spiked Thai tea, and they DO NOT hesitate with the alcohol. I had two drinks, and already feeling tipsy, so I apologize in advance if this review doesn't make sense (I want to write it before my appreciation for the food deplenishes).

PLEASE get the crab curry!! The flavors and fragrancy of the curry made this the most popular dish between my friends and I. We also ordered 6 dishes (2 appetizers), and we thought it was excessive at first for 4 people, but then we ordered another, and now we've reached the satisfying amount of full(ness).

I recommend this spot 100%! When it says spicy, it means spicy. My friend who couldn't handle spice started sweating uncontrollably and drank all of the water available. Either way, we all enjoyed.

I could say that food here is exactly like how it is cooked and served in Thai restaurants in Thailand. So if you wanna try authentic Thai food, I would strongly recommend this place. Recommended dishes include Kai Tod (fried chicken with garlic and shallot) and Larb Moo.

The food was delicious. My favorite was definitely the calamari. The sauce on it and the texture just everything was perfect. The fried chicken and branzino were great. The grilled pork was good too but on the spicy side but if we're talking about spicy the crab curry had my tongue on fire! Oof I didn't expect it to be so spicy. We had to order a side of rice to recover from the spice. The soup (I forgot the name of it) was just ok to me. So my main winners are the calamari, fried chicken, grilled pork and branzino but I would get like 5 orders of calamari to myself next time.

Amazing food. Very different experience than ANY other Thai restaurant I've ever been to. Crab fried rice was amazing but the star for my evening was the calamari! Such flavor and nothing like the breaded mess one usually receives when ordering this dish. It was delicate and amazing. Superbly presented. Attentive waitress and cordial staff. 

Would recommend to the UNIVERSE! Would give 10 stars if I could.

Went to Fish Cheeks on a Wednesday night. I had a reservation for 6:45 and when I arrived, the host sat me near the kitchen and bar. I requested a less crowded spot and he was kind to reset a table for me in the main dining area.

I ordered the mango sticky rice cocktail. Can't say I was a big fan of it - it had rum, mango purée (I thought that would be the saving grace but could barely taste the mango flavor), and house made rice milk. Next time I think I'll stick with virgin drinks like Thai ice tea.

We ordered a dozen happy hour oysters. They were on the smaller side but for $1 a piece, why not. Got the fried chicken appetizer. It good but wished I ordered the calamari instead. Our main dishes consisted of the steamed fish and crab curry. Both were really spicy and really delicious! I loved the crab curry as it had just the right amount of kick and had some solid lumps of crab meat.

Such a cute new Thai place! Stopped by for lunch today with a friend and we enjoyed what we tried. Note that they only have lunch Friday-Sunday!

My friend got the kuay tiao phed and it was delicious. The Chinese five spice broth was on the sweet side but paired excellently with the 4 hour braised melt in your mouth duck leg. The soft boiled egg was also super delicious! We were pleasantly surprised by the egg noodles because they are like the Cantonese noodles you get in wonton soup! We have never had noodles like these in Thai restaurants, and we loved it!

Our server recommended me to get the pla muk kai kem, which was a rice dish of stir fried squid, salted duck egg, long red chili, and a fried egg on top. She recommended it because it's a pretty unique dish not often served at most Thai places in town! I thought the dish was alright, but she was definitely right that it was unique. The salted duck egg was a little too salty for me and the fried egg was... too fried? If you like squid, get it! For me, I might have liked the other dishes more because I prefer other seafood over squid! That being said, I don't regret having tried this dish. I am definitely interested in coming back to try other things on their lunch menu though, honestly every single thing sounded delicious. Also very interested in their dinner menu, but would definitely have to come back with a bigger group!

Seafood centric Thai place. High quality ingredients and authentic flavors. Wish the menu had more variety for vegetarians and non- seafood eaters. Loved the stir fried seafood entree, and the spicy coconut crab curry.

Kindly erase your memory of pop Thai food, because this isn't reminiscent of any Thai food I had. ..except maybe for the Thai Iced Tea. At past 2pm today, they were still serving lunch which listed a different menu from dinner.  I got a bit worried since it did not have dishes I've set my heart on. So I was relieved when they were able to give us the crispy garlic Branzino - which should never be skipped - and the Noi's Chicken. Both of these weren't in the Lunch Menu. Both, amazing! Thai Crab Fried Rice has such plump crabmeat that it could be a whole meal by itself. Kana Moo Krob is a lunch combo of stir fried broccoli and crispy pork belly. Then we ordered another side of pork belly, just for good measure. But my attention was devoted to Branzino...carefully savoring every crispy bite.  Each dish had its own sauce that added a layer of richer flavour. Crab curry, you're next in our future visit.  Needless to say, we polished off our plates, save for a few spoonfuls of jasmine rice because we weren't saying "no" to Kaffir Key Lime Pie.

Hands down the best Thai food we've had in the city! The food made me feel like we were back in Thailand. It's a unique experience with family style sets. We had four people and ordered the set of 3 and it was plenty of food. Even had left overs. Oh and the shrimp chips were next level. Highly recommend!

If you're into food, you'll 100% be into this place. A Yelp review doesn't do this place justice. So if you're debating between Filipino, Chinese or Thai for a night out in East Village or simply sitting around yelping the 13987591837 options in NYC, stop wasting time and make your next dining experience at Fish Cheeks. 

Foreword: Notably the most hyped restaurant right now, Fish Cheeks brings traditional, authentic Thai cuisine to NYC. The chefs, all from Thailand, are painting a fresh picture to the EV food scene. Unlike any other Thai place in the State, you won't be getting pad thai or tom yum soup here. What you WILL be getting is an incredible experience with attentive, cordial staff (a rare commodity in Manhattan), fresh ingredients, high quality recipes, and even better cocktails to top it all off. 

Ambience: Trendy, modern, but humble. Your food comes in old school, rather inexpensive plates and bowls. Think cutlery from a Chinese market in Flushing. The setting is intimate and provides space for a gathering or cute date. There's also bar seating where you can also dine at! 

Now the most important part.. what to order (take my word on these options): 
-Calamari- No this isn't anything like the breaded crap you get at sports bars
-Namtok Pork- Dive in
-Pakboong Fai Dang (Thai watercress) - A good balance for all the heavier dishes
-Coconut Crab Curry - CHUNKS of crab meat, holla
-Steamed blue fish with Thai herbs - steamed to absolute perfection
-Seafood Pad Cha- No explanation needed
-Thai Ice Tea sorbet - Always leave with a sweet palate

Pro tip: Make a reservation. Perhaps 3 weeks in advance. Come early and chill at the bar and nom on some shrimp crackers + sambal

My mother and I really enjoyed our lunch at Fish Cheeks!
I had the Senn Lek Tom yum. Which featured mussels, shrimp, squid, egg and rice noodles in a lemongrass broth. It was warm and comforting on a chilly afternoon. The portion was so gigantic that I was slightly alarmed when I realized it had disappeared. 
I did feel that there could have been slightly more flavor and a touch less saltiness, but overall eating it was a very joyous occasion that has lingered in my mind. My mom had the Kaprow tale, which brought her immense happiness.  I enjoyed her enjoyment of her meal even more than my own. She also had watermelon juice, which was fresh and hot pink and delicious. 
The restaurant was very ambient and brought us summer vibes. The service was friendly and fast.

Came here for dinner with some friends. We were all very impressed with the food. I like spicy food so for me it was perfect. Other found it slightly spicy but still not overpowering. 

We got the calamari, fried chicken, crab curry, crab fried rice and seafood pad cha. Everything was great. 

Service was prompt and our waitress was very friendly, provided great suggestions and was very knowledgeable.
Decor was very cute and atmosphere was lively. Staff was very nice and helpful. Had the crab fried rice during lunch and it reminded me of my travels in Thailand. Will definitely be back for dinner!

Of all Thai restaurants in NYC this place is my favorite. I am beyond happy once we discovered Fishcheeks. The taste is authentic. I recommend getting pork belly with basil, namtok pork, fried fish, and hat yai chicken. About cocktails: watermelon vodka is great, guava smash is just ok tasted more like mojito. We will have to go back and try different dishes.

This is a new Thai restaurant that recently opened in NoHo. It's so Thai that there's a sign on the wall inside that says, "No, we do not have Pad Thai." It made me chuckle. If you want Pad Thai, go somewhere else; this place is for people that want refined, authentic Thai cuisine.

-- AMBIANCE --
The inside decor is tasteful and simple. There are multiple seating arrangements that can easily be adjusted for bigger crowds. I came here with my sister and a friend around 6 pm (with a reservation) with only another couple dining, but by the time we left it was a packed house full of all types of people.

-- FOOD --
I had the food chosen for me since I didn't really know what to get. Like the Thai eat, we ate family-style. That means you order a bunch of dishes and people try a little from each. I think we got four different dishes between the three of us. Family-style might be a good option to consider if you want to save some money and try different things. If you are unsure what to order, talk to the server and ask for suggestions.

Each dish was divine and unique in taste, with only one was slightly too salty for my taste. Expect your palate to be opened up, and be open to new tastes.

Also, there is no pad thai, as I mentioned already.

-- SERVICE --
I thought our server was perfectly fine. She attended to us as needed and was aware when we needed refills or anything else.

-- SUMMARY --
While relatively pricey, the taste was unique enough to come back here to try more of the menu. Recommended.

4 stars for food, 0 stars for service. I have never been treated more rudely in a restaurant. 

Had a 9PM reservation for 4 last night and was hurried and disrespected at every turn. As soon as we sat down waitress began pressuring us to order and she left before taking everyone's drink orders when we weren't able to order as quickly as she wanted. After we ordered, we heard her giving a much better warmer welcome to the table next to us-- including an intro to specials which we were never told about. Regardless, the food was amazing. We ordered the crab fried rice, crab coconut curry, green curry, & steamed mussels. The crab coconut curry was too spicy for two of the women, but everyone enjoyed & was full. 

The end of our meal was very uncomfortable. The waitress dropped off the check & proceeded to hover around our table waiting for us to add our cards to it. Less than 5 minutes after putting the check down, she came back to say she was confused and wanted to know if the check was ready. I responded & said no and explained we were waiting for two of the women to finish their drinks. We had been seated for under an hour @ this point & thought that was reasonable. She clearly did not as she walked away and started pointing at us while talking to several other servers. I completely understand that it was a busy Friday night & people were waiting, but we just wanted to finished the drinks we had paid for. None of us were that far from being done and we had not been seated for very long. We felt very uncomfortable and unwanted at this point after being treated so poorly throughout the whole experience. We were able to split the check evenly four ways. One of my friends ran to the bathroom before we left, only to be given another rude glare from our waitress. We left as quickly as possible after that (none of us even put our coats on until we were outside).

Having worked in the service industry, I understand that everyone has bad days and this can reflect in the service provided. However, it genuinely felt like our waitress did not like us and did not want to serve us. She seemed to be very polite and warm to other tables, some of whom had been seated before us and were still eating when we left. The food was so so good, but I'm not sure if I'll be back.

I ordered:
calamari- flavorful, you don't even need the sauce
fried chicken- mediocre
crispy branzino with fish sauce- amazingly cooked to perfection

Will return to try other dishes! Oh, skip the drinks unless you don't mind spending $15 for a small glass of cocktail. 

***they don't accept credit cards***

I'm not Thai, but Fish Cheeks seems like pretty authentic Thai (at NYC prices).  The coconut crab curry was our favorite, with big chunks of crab meat and good spice level. The goong aob woon sen (baked shrimp, pork belly, glass noodles) was also good comfort food.  Fried chicken appetizer was only okay though; a bit dry...dipping sauce was good but can get that anywhere.

If you like spicy food, and Thai food fish cheeks is a MUST.

I ate here with my boyfriend and we shared fried calamari, tom Kha soup and the crab curry.

Calamari: delicious, and glazed with a tasty tamarind sauce

Tom kha: sooo amazingly flavorful. Spicy, sour, full of herbs. I really enjoyed this, however, I wish it came in single serving sizes. The soups is something like $22- would be nice if they had a smaller option for $6-8. Also warning: they put dairy milk in this, but I did overhear they are able to omit it per special request.

Crab curry: filled with tasty crab, and comes with a side of perfect chewy warm rice. Definitely definitely get this!

Other notes...
Our server warned us that the spicy food is really really spicy-- I am good with spicy food, but this made me a little nervous. However, the spice level was perfect. It was not "inedibly spicy" at all. So if you're used to spicy food don't let a warning make you second guess yourself! 

Also, I got the "Mango sticky rice" cocktail. At first it was really good, but became weirdly congealed after it sitting for a bit. Maybe not the best choice.

Overall, great experience. The decor is adorable, the food is amazing and they have a really cool sink in the bathroom. 

This place seems to be trending right now, so do yourself a favor and make a reservation! We waited for an hour and still only were able to eat at the bar (nbd! But planning ahead will work in your favor)

Very solid Thai food, and a good stray from the standard Pad Thai offerings. My friends ranted about how much Chrissy Teigen raved about this place on Instagram, and she was right in her opinions about the place. Good job, Chrissy. The inside is pretty casual with wooden tables and colorful plastic chairs, and a small bar in the back. There weren't too many people inside at first, but really filled up around 8pm.

We decided to go for the $45 set menu, which included a fair number of dishes. Favorite of the night was easily the coconut crab curry. I was astounded by how much crab they put, and how well it paired with the coconut curry, and just kept eating it and eating with the jasmine rice. Hoo-wee. With that, everything else was really great too. The nam tok grilled pork had some really intense spicy flavors, the calamari was light and tender, and the fried chicken was crispy and delicious. The crispy branzino was really delicious as well, and I really liked the cut and the filet of the meat. The pakboong fai dang (Thai watercress) was really great, and it made me wish that all my vegetables were cooked like that, with chili and garlic. 

By the end of the meal, we were both full to bursting with food. The value at $45 was pretty good, and I probably would recommend coming with a larger group, and to come hungry. Service was very attentive throughout the meal, and we got our drink refills almost instantly, which was nice, since we were eating some spicier flavors. I know water sort of makes it worse, but at least we had that brief relief from the spiciness from the ice. Everything was nicely paced, so we were able to eat without feeling overwhelmed.

Overall, one of the better Thai restaurants I've tried recently. Tt's really nice to see more and more Thai restaurants that go beyond the normal offerings, and I'll definitely be back to try their other dishes in the future, but will have to include some coconut crab curry with it.

Love Thai food, frequently visit Thailand so I feel that I can critique here.  Excellent calamari, and pak boong.  Authentic Tom Yum Goong but as I prefer Tom Kha Gai I didn't have too much of it.  The crab curry was good but I was expecting a yellow curry for the crab as that is how it is usually served in Phetchaburi, Krabi and Trang.  We all felt the Branzino was more overcooked than crispy though it was still delicious.  Definitely needed more rice.

KenScale: 8.0/10

When I first tried Thai food in college, it was an eye-opening experience. The spice and flavor was nothing like I've had before, definitely different from East Asia I was being used to at that time. The intensity of Thai food that heavily employs cilantro and coconut, however, became an integral part of my eating experience that nowadays I have to get my fix of Thai food at least a couple of times every month; by contrast, and somewhat shockingly, I can go on for at least a couple of months without eating Korean food. I also appreciate that my girlfriend shares the same love for the addictive flavor to Thai cuisine. For our last meal together of the year, we decided to check out Fish Cheeks, a new Thai restaurant from chef brothers who used to work at the famed Nahm in Bangkok before opening this modest space in NoHo. Overall, we enjoyed most of the food from Fish Cheeks.

Fish Cheeks' rather concise menu focuses on a lot of seafood. Generally, I like to have chicken, pork or other meat items in my Thai dishes, but this time I didn't mind because there was no single bad dish we had. Shrimp with lime juice, garlic, chili and mint was quite fresh without any fishy sensation that you may encounter from raw seafood, and the mixture underneath the shrimp was quite intense, in a good way. I really loved the grilled pork accompanied by roasted rice, shallot, scallion, cilantro and chili. This namtok pork salad had very nice balance of flavor (on the more sweet than spicy side) that was simply perfect for an appetizer before proceeding to the main courses. I've had a very high expectation for coconut crab curry, and while the curry meat had nice texture, I wished the curry itself had a bit less seasoning (i.e. it felt a bit saltier than my girlfriend and I had hoped) while focusing more on the spicy side in flavor. On the other hand, I couldn't really find fault with the steamed blue fish with Thai herbs that is placed inside a fish-shaped pot. The fish was not only more or less steamed perfectly for great texture (which got even better over time with the addition to heat underneath the pot), but I also appreciated that the seasoning was kept at minimal level. For dessert, we enjoyed Thai tea panna cotta that was quite delightful without being overly sweet. 

Getting a reservation at Fish Cheeks seems pretty manageable, but the dining space is not that large so might be a good idea to always book in advance. There was nothing too special about the cozy dining space, which was a bit on the louder side than I would've preferred. For casual dates or get-togethers with friends, it will certainly do. There is full bar with Thai-inspired cocktails on the menu to complement your meal. Fish Cheeks offers some very solid Thai seafood options, so if you need that quick fix for Thai food every once in a while like I do, I do recommend checking it out.

Fish cheeks's rising-star restaurant sticks to its concept of using as many local Thai ingredients as possible in dishes that go beyond your average Thai/American cuisine. 

The menu features an array of seafood and full-flavored traditional Thai dish. 

My recommendation : Coconut crab curry.

I'm OK with Tom Yum Goong but it doesn't go beyond my expectation. 

If you are indecisive to pick the dish, go for the set Menu. ( the same size/portion as regular, if you're curious) 


If you wanna go sweet, try Kaffir Lime Pie. It's tangy and delicious but I wish the fragrance of Kaffir could be more intense. Thumb up for this menu anyway. 

Cocktails: now we can talk lol 
My friend and I tried Guavas, Thai Herb ( with coconut water), Mango Sticky rice , Thai Ice Tea. I would say they are inventive! Thump up for Thai Herb for generous liquor.


I recommend this place for exceptional ambience ( rarely seen in Thai places in NYC )and professional staffs. Just the music that I don't understand...

Came here last night for the first time and boy, it did not disappoint. You won't find pad Thai or pad see revere, but you will find the tastes of Thai spices in the unique dishes here. It seems the crab curry soup is a popular dish so we ordered that, along with the tom yum soup and fried chicken to start. Everything was great. Best tom yum soup I've had in the city. The menu is small, making it easy to choose what to order. And the dishes are to share portions. The restaurant itself is dimly lit and vibrant as the restaurant was packed. Service was great and someone was constantly checking up on his but not overbearing. I'm definitely coming back with my husband and will Def recommend this place to others! Yum!

Dined with a friend on Thursday night and we both loved it! Our meal was fabulous! We went with 'set meal number one' for two people and could not have been happier. We enjoyed, among other things, mussels, calamari, crab curry and branzino. Everything was great! The food was wonderfully spiced--that is, hot spicy, but also flavorful and complex. The food at this restaurant is terrific. We will be back.

Great thai food!
Not the place to go if you're looking for pad thai, but if you're willing to try something new and authentic, definitely give this place a shot.

We came here for dinner on a weeknight, and were immediately seated by the window. Simple decor yet very bright and colorful. 

Food here was amazing, however the only downside was that the portions were rather small for a semi-costly price. 
We ordered the calamari, hat yai fried chicken, goong aob woon senn along with 2 orders of the thai iced tea (contains alcohol). The calamari was definitely my favorite, but overall the dishes were good. 

I'm hoping to come back again to try other items on the menu.

So good! 

Admittedly, I didn't know what to expect (a thai place that doesn't serve pad thai? what?? I love pad thai....) but I was very pleasantly surprised. Made reservations prior and upon entering the restaurant, I was hit with the smell of fish sauce and I knew then and there that it would be a good meal. 

My friend and I got dinner on a friday night at 9pm and the place was packed. We shared the fried chicken, crab curry, and steamed blue fish. The fried chicken was decent - crispy dark meat without the bone - but nothing to call home about. The crab curry was also pretty good and had generous amounts of lump crab meat but it was a little too heavy for my liking. The steamed blue fish though...that really blew everything out of the water. GET THIS! The fish was filleted (deboned and all), served on a cute fish-shaped platter, and simmered in this wonderful lime chili pepper sauce, over a flame. Amazing.

Super cute place! We got the pork small plate, which was delicious, as well as the crab fried rice, crab curry, and steamed fish. The curry definitely was on the spicier side, but still super good with big chunks of crab in it. The fried rice was normal, but didn't skimp on the crab either. I thought the steamed fish was okay, yummy but I have a feeling that I would have liked the fried fish - oh well, maybe next time! It's a bit on the pricier than what I usually pay for Thai food, but I would say if you're looking for something other than your typical pad Thai, this is a great place to try it out!

One word: AMAZING!  Ok, that's the end of my review, haha.  I have been on a Southeast Asian food kick lately, in order to satisfy my craving, I've been to a flurry of Thai, Vietnamese and Malaysian restaurants in the last few weeks. Most of them were pretty good, however, one restaurant stood head and shoulders above the rest, which is... drum roll please... Fish Cheeks! 

We ordered three dishes to share and two were spectacular. We tried:

Tom Yum Goong - beautiful soup with a strong flavor profile that consisted of spicy, sour and savory.  Unlike a lot of Thai restaurants in the city, Fish Cheeks does not hold back on its spices, so be warned if you are not a big spicy food person. The soup has just the right amount of creaminess, but still light enough to feel refreshing. There is copious amount of shrimps in the soup and all of which are perfectly cooked.  Last, but not least, I loved the presentation of the dish, which comes in a large hotpot, similar to the hotpots used in Northern China. 

Coconut Crab Curry - another dish that was out of this world.  I was amazed by the generous portion of crabs in this dish, given the fact that it was priced at $22. The big chunks of crabs are seasoned perfectly by the creamy coconut curry.  One thing worth to note, this was also a very spicy dish, definitely not for the faint of heart. 

Crispy Branzino - this dish was gotten a lot of love on Yelp. I don't think this was the best dish. It was actually a bit underwhelming.  The fish is beautifully fried, but extremely bland compared to the other dishes. The accompanied sauce did not do much to enhance the flavor. However, given the spiciness of the other two dishes, it was nice to get a reprieve from the heat. 

Even though we were stuffed from the three entrees, we had to try the dessert. They offered two desserts, Thai Tea Panna Cotta or Kefir Lime Pie. We picked the latter based on our server's recommendation. It was fantastic!! I think that it might have been the highlight of our already amazing dinner. The lime flavor shone through in the pie and had just the right amount of sweetness. I want to buy a box of the pies and eat it for dinner next day. Also have to mention the Thai Iced Coffee, perfect way to end the meal. 

Service was good, attentive without being intrusive. My only feedback is that they brought out all three of our entrees at the same time, which overwhelmed our tiny table. We barely had any room to maneuver.  Moreover, I wish they brought out the soup first, followed by the fish and curry.  Everything came out extremely fast, it would've been great if they spaced out the service.  Overall, those were small qualms for an otherwise great dining experience. I can't wait to come back soon and try the rest of the menu!!

Authentic thai food from a good chef! Not so expensive dishes. Service could be busy at times, don't try Sticky Rice Mango as a cocktail. It was a meh.

I've never tried authentic thai food as I remembered, but their dish is distinguishably different from the normal pad thai. I love coconut crab curry. Even if it didn't look good on photo, it had great fresh ingredients, crab meat, and spicy curry mixing it. That was almost my favorite. Wait, so is Goong Aob Won Senn. The more words you can't pronounce, the more authentic it is, as a rule of thumb. I can have all the rice noodle in that dish! It absorbed all the rich flavors from shrimps and pork belly with great seasoning.

A great place to try some non-typical Thai dishes. For 4 people, we shared the namtok pork as a starter, the coconut crab curry, crab fried rice, and the steamed blue fish. My favorite were the pork starter and the crab curry. The broth in the steamed fish was good but the fish was a bit tough and didn't have much flavor. Portions looked pretty small but everyone was full at the end. Wasn't too crowded on a Sunday at 7pm but I would still recommend making a reservation because the tables fill up quickly. Overall, good service, cute interior, and tasty food but I've definitely had better Thai in the city.

Given the recent feature in the New York Times, one would expect the lights to be on on a Friday night. We had a 9pm reservation and minutes after being seated, the electricity went out. I was told this was not the first time this happened, that it was unclear if/when the lights would come back on, though our orders could be taken...presumably our meal would be cooked in the dark. 

I was hopeful that either the electricity would return and we'd be able to enjoy the highly anticipated crab curry, but the poor communication from both the host and the wait staff forced us to leave. There was no apology and no attempt at having us return. I can't say I'll be giving this "hot and new" spot another chance.

I'll be honest to say I had high expectations for this restaurant. I've been wanting to check this place out for a while. I made a reservation for 9pm on a Friday night, we sat down and immediately they lost all power. Lights out. This did not sound to be the first time either, but there was very little communication about the situation. The door was open too for ventilation (I think) making it too cold to stick around for more than 30min or so. Cold crab curry: makes me crabby...Some apology, reassurance, or free drink/appetizer would've gone a long way. 
Thanks Fish Cheeks: you be blushing :(

PS this is my first review - just felt it was necessary.

My family of 5 arrived just after they opened at 5 on November 27 and placed our order shortly thereafter. The food took long to arrive and none of the dishes were really hot. Food OK but nothing I would go out of my way to have again

The big insult was when I wanted to pay with cash and I was told they only take credit cards. I will never go to a restaurant that tells me I can't pay in cash. I was told it saves them bookkeeping and employee theft. I shouldn't have to concern myself with that.

Furthermore, this policy of credit card only is discriminatory. If I can't, for whatever reason can't get or don't want a credit card and I want some Thai food and I saved up all week cash to buy it and you tell me I can't, you are discriminating against the poor.

Martin Cohen

Had dinner here tonight for the first time.  It was amazing!!!  Probably the best Thai food we've ever had.  We had the crab curry and the blue fish, which were both delicious!  The watercress side was also great.  Friendly service too.  We can't wait to go back.  We highly recommend!

Love at first sight. Atmosphere super nice and staffs are super friendly and helpful.  Star off with super crunchy fried calamari.  Nice 3 flavor sauce.   Everything sound so good on the menu but because its my first time i decided to order the set menu number 2.  It is for 2 ppl and it will cost you 45/pp but it so super worth it.  You will get serve with so much food.  I dont have to talk more about the food coz all the atuff i had are delish.  And i just got back from thailand lastweek !! 



@hungrypoohnyc

My Thai love affair continues, with Fish Cheeks added to the list of places I'd cheat on Andy Ricker with. The food was so impressive, I am willing to dismiss our expressionless server whose tone oscillated between genuine interest and completely flat sarcasm. Her suggestion of the Asian Negroni was perfect. The lack of Campari made it almost refreshing. It complimented the heat of dishes like the Coconut Crab Curry and the Fried Calamari in tamarind chili fish sauce glaze. The table next to us was digging deep in a plate of Hat Yai Fried Chicken in sweet chili sauce, which looked "ridic" and made me wish I hadn't eaten a proper lunch. They aren't kidding when they say come hungry on their website. COME HUNGRY!!!!

This a hidden gem in NYC. Some of the best home style Thai food in Manhattan. Simple, extremely delicious and so close to MTA AND main streets. 
Must try

It wasn't bad but it wasn't great where I would make the effort to go back.

First, the hostess was a very poor communicator. I had to ask multiple times how I can put myself down on the waitlist and got terrible, ineffective responses. Finally, a young man walked up who was much better and had a clue about how to talk to guests. Our waitress was very nice and seemed pretty knowledgeable on the menu.

Bar seats in the back are first come first serve. This seems to be the only option for walk-ins during peak hours. At 7 pm, I was told a table wouldn't be available until 10:30 when the hostess looked at their tablet, so it doesn't seem that they reserve any tables for walk ins. We did end up getting a table because of a no-show reservation.

Food was decent. But the staff who runs the food out didn't explain anything about any of the sauces that come with some dishes. They just set everything down and walk away.

The dishes seem authentic. Dishes are simply plated and almost feel like you're at someone's home. I personally don't mind this but it's interesting for the location. 

Fried chicken small plate - this doesn't have thick, clumpy batter like typical American-style fried chicken. It's crispy, meat wasn't dry, and seasoned with Asian spices. I liked it.

Mussels small plate - mussels were tender and the broth is very light and simple. I liked the simplicity of the broth because you can taste the lemongrass, galangal, and Thai basil. It came with a green sauce that wasn't explained but is tasty. 

Crispy branzino - It's definitely crispy and they remove most of the bones. I love whole fish with the head on. But, my dish came out with just the fried fish on a plate. No garnish, no vegetables, nothing even for sake of presentation. The bowl of fish sauce broth tasted watered down and bland considering it has fish sauce. I used the green sauce from the mussels on the fish instead. Overpriced at $32. I see now from other people's pics that their dish had cilantro & fried garlic bits so clearly mine was not finished properly before it was sent out to the table. But still overpriced even with cilantro. Another table near us ordered the branzino and I don't think they got any garnish either or I would have realized then that mine was incomplete.

My friends had the crab curry and seafood pad cha. I didn't try the curry, but the pad cha was good and very spicy. I did like the complimentary fish chips that come out at the start of the meal and was brought back to my childhood. 

If someone wanted to go here, I'd go back and try other dishes. But I don't know if I'd recommend it or go back on my own based on my visit.

It's super awesome that this thai restaurant does not serve pad thai and your typical thai food options but more "authentic" dishes cooked by thai chefs. I enjoyed the food very much but beware of over-ordering. 

I came with another friend and tried the:
1. fried chicken - it was good nothing too special for $12. I prefer the fried chicken (dark meat) from som tum der more.
2. coconut crab curry that was good - I wouldn't say amazing as I have read in many other yelp reviews but it is good. I thought it was slightly overwhelmingly spicy (and I love spicy). I wish the crab curry had other components other than just crab meat
3. steamed blue fish with kaffir lime and chili - IT was so GOOD. This was definitely the highlight of the meal. It was salty, sour, and spicy at the same time. They also keep a little fire under this dish to maintain the heat. AMAZING!
4. Thai watercress which was good

Overall I had a good experience but it came out to be pretty pricey. The bill was around $95 with tip and tax. 

On the side note, please make a reservation for this restaurant because they're really bad without one. The first time I stopped by without one around 6pm, they said that we should be seated around 7:30. So we went to soho for some shopping while we waited. Around 7:30 we called to ask if we should head back since they haven't called or messaged us. They told us at that point that we would probably have to wait till 9. We weren't sure what we were going to do at this point so we said it was fine. Around 8:45, we called again to wonder if we can get seated soon and they told us we probably won't get seated until late. I wish they would have told us sooner so we would have found another spot to find food. Its just that I know that no matter how busy they were, they definitely had seats they could have saved for us since we were the first ones at the restaurant at 6pm. I wish they can work better on this. We never cancelled our reservation and they never called us afterwards either.

I've gone multiple days in a row simply cause I can't get enough of the crab curry. It's so delicious and SPICY!
And the green sauce!? I would like a vat of that stuff sent to my home, please!
The cocktails are also delicious with a solid wine list.
My super picky, old korean dad came with me and didn't talk once, just scarfed down the fried rice and asked if he could get another order of it....
This is a MUST GO TO place if you want authentic, southern Thai seafood dishes. These people know what they're doing!
And I also appreciate the #NOPADTHAIZONE. Having been to Thailand for a month and exploring it with a local foodie, people don't eat pad thai there!

This place is actually really bright and warm. I was so excited about eating here. And it may be that what we ordered was not their specialty, but we left disappointed and still hungry. We got crab curry and some appetizers. The curry did have a lot of lump crab in it, was spicy, but not particularly flavorful. It didn't taste like there was any salt in it. It was also pretty small. The calamaris tasted like they were sprinkled with sugar, a lot of sugar. I would stay away from those two dishes and try some others if you are planning to go.

Our waiter might have been just awkward, but it really felt like the service was really rude. There are specials on the black board on one side of the restaurant. We didn't know anything about there being specials until after we had ordered and then overheard another waiter tell another table. The people next to us were told that they only had 45 minutes to eat and were rushing through it and also not very happy. They left half of their food on the plate. Because of those things mainly, it was overall unpleasant.

If you go, definitely make a reservation and ask a lot of questions about the menu.

I was here last night and I'm still thinking about the blue fish and prawns we ate. The food and service were excellent. Our serve Natalie was fantastic and offered great suggestions. I will definitely be back, even though their menu is small there are still so many more plates I would love to try.

Wow. Just wow. We sat at the bar and chatted it up with the friendly bartender. She was awesome and made us some killer alcoholic Thai iced teas. She gave us great food recommendations. And the food was mind blowing. Like - after having so much Americanized, mediocre Thai food my whole life, it was SO refreshing tasting something new and exciting in Thai cuisine. They knocked it out of the park with EVERY dish and drink.

Probably one of the most expensive Thai places I've been too. Not complaining but just stating the obvious. The portions were on the smaller end especially since they promote it family style. The interior of the restaurant was cute. I did like the Thai music playing in the background. I was surprised seeing Thai people cooking the food. The service was on point. Although, I did not have reservations I was able to sit at the bar and a full menu was available there. We did just that. To start we got calamari, the calamari was probably one of the best I have had, just wished we would've ordered two, one did not suffice for both of us. Calamari was lightly fried and not full of crust like other places. For our main course, we got the coconut crab curry- this was one of the spiciest I have had but it was so flavorful. It also had huge chunks of crab which I liked. We also got crab fried rice, this dish did not disappoint as well. The Thai iced tea was a bit on the sweeter end at least to my liking. I will be back to try their speciality cocktail drinks. I am intrigued.

Is there anything more bs hipster pretentious than a Thai-food restaurant declaring itself a "No Pad Thai Zone"? The Prime Minister of Thailand declared Pad Thai as a national dish in the 1940s in an effort to unify the country and promote "Thai-ness."  So...

Attitude aside, the restaurant has several issues. Service was very polite and nice but we were seated 25 minutes after our reserved time, had to wait quite a long while after asking for a bowl of steamed rice, and there were technical problems with splitting the check.

Branzino was "highly recommended" but was small, and honestly after a simple deep-fry prep it might as well have been tilapia. Not worth $32. The tom yum was one of the best I've had though, and the crab curry and sea food stir fry also had great flavor. Skip the baked pork belly/shrimp glass noodles dish unless you like plain tasting food (to each their own).

I love Fish Cheeks!! I was born and raised in Thailand and I have to say that they make real Thai food.  Love that  tonight s meal remind me of home. Goong Aob woonsen is spot on.  Coconut crab curry is great !!! Raw shrimp was soooo tasty. As you all know that seafood in NYC might be questionable but you can tell that they use fresh seafood. Also the chef and cooks are THAI !!! I highly recommend if you are looking for super Thai taste. Kob khun krub

Love the no-pad-thai-zone! If you're looking for an authentic Thai experience this place will not disappoint. The crab curry, goong aob woon senn, and branzino are excellent. The depth of flavor in the curry is a standout with generous amount of fresh crab. Goong aob woon senn has a TON of flavor! The simplicity of the fried branzino balanced with a complex sauce is perfection. Great atmosphere for a group of friends or a date. Super cool retro Thai music. A lot of love went into Fish Cheeks and it shows!

This space has changed hands a few times over the past few years (Hung Ry, Le Philosophe...), hopefully fish cheeks is here to stay! Thai seafood, family-style, straight to your soul - great tagline that fits them well :)

Came here on a Saturday night, restaurant was absolutely bustling and packed. Thank god we had a reservation from a while ago or I think the wait would have been a little ridiculous. They seated our party of 4 shortly after everyone arrived. Their decor is super cute, vibrant with colors and fish scale patterns.Once you walk in, you'll be hit with a strong odor of fish sauce, not sure if that's a good thing or bad thing lol. They seem to be able to combine tables to accommodate larger parties, so keep that in mind if you ever want to host a larger birthday dinner or something like that!

Seems like they highly recommend family style, so we ordered the below to share:

Hat Yai's Fried Chicken $12
YUMMM, this was crisp on the outside and super juicy on the inside. The sauce that it came with was also deliciously sweet.

Nam Tok Pork $14
This was a grilled pork dish that came compliments from the chef. This was probably my least favorite, not that it was bad or anything, but I don't think I would have ordered this if I had to pay for it. Pretty flavorful but on the dry side.

Crispy Branzino $32
My fave! Love how they fried it enough to the point where you can almost eat the whole fish including the bones. The fish meat was a great contrast with the crispy skin, super tender!

Coconut Crab Curry $22
This was soooo creamy and rich, you can really taste the coconut flavors as well (not overshadowed by the curry!). They put in a decent amount of crab, so a big thumbs up. This dish is spicy!

Tom Yum Goong $22
This is a huge soup that comes in a mongolian hotpot style pot. Comes with lots of shrimp (cooked perfectly, not overcooked/rubbery) and mushrooms. As with any tomyum soup, it's pretty sour and lemongrassy, so only order if you like that!

Pak Boong Fai Dang $7
Pretty standard watercress dish with just the right amount of spicy/garlic :) A+

Our waitress was awesome, but their service does need to improve overall, especially the people that serve the food to the table (not always the waitress that took our order). Most of the time, they did not bother telling us what the dish was. When he served up the nam tok pork, all he said was that this was compliments from the chef (no dish name), and asked if we had any allergies. We said no, and he promptly left... SUPER ODD.

This is a decently affordable delicious meal - every bite you take is PACKED with flavor and spices. Everything is on the spicy side though, so beware if you don't like spicy food!

*CREDIT CARDS ONLY (pretty rare huh!)
**They do not automatically give you chopsticks, but you can ask for them! Some of the stuff is quite hard to eat with just a fork and spoon...

The name got me so I decided to check out the restaurant. My companion and I ordered the muscles and the fried chicken as appetizers. I'm slightly disappointed at the muscles but it made up for itself in its hot sauce. The fried chicken isn't what you usually picture but this was definitely the highlight of our meal. As for the entree, we requested the vegetable green curry and unbeknownst to us, received something else. We should've known better but because we were hungry, we ate without thinking twice about it. I found the "eggplant" a strange consistency and upon getting the check, I saw the label "crab curry" and it hit the both of us. Good thing I don't get anaphylactic shocks for seafood allergies and was able to go to a nearby pharmacy and purchase some allergy medicine to prevent swelling.

Sadly my first experience may be my last.

Really good Thai food with good drinks.

We stopped by as a party of four on a Thursday evening with a reservation, although we sat at the bar first since they wouldn't seat an incomplete party. We split several dishes as starters, including the fried chicken (pretty good), raw shrimp, calamari, and the pork starters, the latter three of which were outstanding if unfortunately a little on the smaller end. For entrees, we had the crab curry, the porgy, and the seafood pad cha. The crab curry was easily my most favorite, although a little bit on the spicy end; it was still flavorful and had plenty of crab meat. For drinks, they were all quite good, and the mango sticky rice drink was my favorite. I'd definitely recommend coming here for a good (although a bit expensive) Thai meal in the city, especially for the area.

Pretty legit and feels authentic but really over priced and not mind blowing.  The fried chicken appetizer was tasty but the seasoning didn't permeate the meat. Fried branzino was slightly garlicky and most of the flavor came from the fish sauce for dipping. Crab curry was the best with a refreshing amount of heat

Service was spectacular and decor was lovely. Ordered the fried chicken and mussels for starters and the branzino and crab curry for entrees as they were raved about in previous reviews. The amount of crab in the curry was unreal. So many large chunks of it, they were not cheap and I loved every bite. But beware, it is really spicy and I can normally handle spicy. As for the branzino, it was fried well and the sauce that went with it was perfect. Unfortunately an hour after I left, I had the worse tummy ache and it didn't end well. I was stuck to the toilet for quite some time. Maybe I was just unlucky.

Adorable interior decor with their multi colored chairs and basket lights. They have a no pad Thai policy which is pretty impressive considering they are a Thai restaurant. This is the legit stuff. Their menu is just one page but plenty of mouth watering options. We went with the raw shrimp, the mussels for appetizers and to share we had the fried branzino fish, the coconut crab curry and the glass noodles (Goong Aob Woon Senn). The shrimp was delicious I've never actually had raw shrimp before and this was absolutely delicious. The vinegar dressing with the light peppers just made every bite tarty with a light seafood taste with the vinegar cutting out most of the rawness, you just have to get over the texture. The fried garlic branzino was amazing, you do have to watch fro some bones, but I don't know what else to say, its prepared so well, its just yummy. The coconut crab curry was spicy! The coconut flavors a little too heavy for my liking. As for the noodles I just couldn't get enough of it. Was almost tempted to get a second order. 

Overall I just love this place. I would like to come back to try the other items on the menu.

Pretty legit Thai food. The crab curry has some serious kick to it, but beyond that massive pieces of crab meat (no shells) that make it a stand-out compared to what you'd usually find in most crab dishes. The seafood pad na (or however that's spelled) has a great Thai basil flavor. The lightly fried calamari are a good appetizer, much better than your average calamari with 2 inches of dry crust on them. Great laid-back musical score and simple but pleasant ambiance.

My wife and I ate here 2 weekends ago and really enjoyed it. We didn't have reservations and due to the wait had to eat at the bar. Eating at the bar ended up working out nicely because we had a view of the kitchen which I love and there was only 1 bartender and I believe we got preferential treatment. The dishes are meant to be shared and we ordered several plates, all of which were delicious. We started with the Hat Yai fried chicken which was flavorful and unique. The chicken was not breaded and had a very light crispy exterior. If I am being extremely picky, it was a little dry, but the flavors were wonderful. We ordered the crab curry and tom yum goong as our mains. Both dishes were surprisingly spicy, but in a very pleasant way. The curry was my favorite, but the seafood stir fry was also very good. We had food envy when we saw the branzino and porgy go out of the kitchen. We are looking forward to trying those dishes when we next visit.

A lot of high expectations for this place, especially with all the hype. They were fully packed even at 815 on a rainy night on Thursday. We sat in the bar and ordered the red crab curry and fried branzino. It was really loud in the restaurant and hard to hear especially if having a conversation. The bar tender messed up putting in our order which made our food come out really late which was annoying but he was really apologetic and gave us a free pork appetizer which was good. The fried branzino was delicious and its gluten free too. The red curry tasted so fresh and the crab meat was good but you could tell this place is authentic Thai because the curry and pork dish were spicy
 I drank 6 cups of water. It is pricey and not the best ambiance but definitely worth a shot.

It was ok. 

The crab curry tasted like normal every day red curry, but was different because of the lump crab (which, while very good, doesn't really impact the taste of the dish). The fried Branzino was a little dry and lacked any semblance of salt. The fried garlic was also dry and flavorless. The pork appetizer was tasty but I could take it or leave it. 

Over all it was ok, however the price was really too much for the offerings. The "family style" plates are really not family style. I could have eaten the curry and fish myself. We ordered two dishes and an app and I left hungry- and I'm not a large person. The beers are also $8, for really bottom of the barrel choices.

600th review! Knew I had to make it a special one. 

When I saw that Chrissy Teigen and John Legend had hit this place up, claiming it to be their favorite Thai restaurant, I couldn't stop myself from making a reservation online. The process was easy but peak times go quickly, so definitely plan ahead because the place has limited seating. Also - definitely not the place to go if you/your party has seafood allergies as that is 90% of the menu. 

When we arrived, the place was still pretty empty for 6 PM but filled up by the time we left. Overall, the service is REALLY fast - dishes came out very quickly, luckily my boyfriend and I are quick eaters. We were in and out within the hour. The servers are still a bit green, but very friendly and helpful. 

Started off with some cocktails - the spiked Thai Iced Tea and the Mango Sticky Rice martini. Both were REALLY strong. Honestly, we couldn't even finish them. Not sure if that shows how lame we are, or that the drinks could use a bit more balance. It was just a bit overwhelming when paired with our dinner. At $14/each, I would probably pass next time or stick to beer & wine.

Onto the food. We ordered the Namtok Pork small plate as a starter. This had such an amazing kick to it and we gobbled it up quickly. We also got complimentary shrimp chips as a starter - these brought back memories from my childhood when my dad would fry these up as a snack (every Asian knows what these are!). Boyfriend ordered the special: steamed blue fish in lemongrass/chili sauce and I got the crab curry per recommendation of other Yelpers. Wish we could have tried the fried Branzino, but ...another day. The broth accompanying the blue fish was incredible and so flavorful. I was slurping it up while my boyfriend devoured the fish. The crab curry is one of the spiciest I've had, but was loaded with meaty crab pieces and was also packed with so many great flavors. You can definitely taste how fresh the ingredients are and the difference from other Thai places in the city. The portion sizes were perfect for 2 people to share though you could easily add on more family style dishes or small plates to suit a larger party.

Little pricey for a frequent visit, but fits the neighborhood and the quality of the food you will receive. We loved being pushed out of our comfort zone (aka 'no pad thai zone'!) and trying new Thai dishes. Would highly recommend!

Real Thai food, not too sweet and ample heat. The coconut crab curry is the bomb. I also tasted my date's crab fried rice, very good, particularly the nam jim sauce accompanying it. Hat yai fried chicken appetizer with those crunchy fried shallots is also recommended. I look forward to trying everything on the menu upon return visits.

You don't have to go to Thai Town in Elmhurst, Queens anymore for great Thai food. Fish Cheeks has stupendously good Thai food, just be prepared for Manhattan prices -- double what you would pay in the Outer Borough. Heard about this place from a Chrissy Teigen Instagram post and it's as good as she raved about. The small plates are some of the best things on the menu -- hat yai fried chicken and namtok pork salad are superb. For entrees, we had the branzino, crab fried rice and goong aob woon senn, all excellent but the branzino is to die for. Not to mention that they serve real Thai iced coffee.

On our permanent list when in the area. Sauteed watercress was a nice change and went perfectly with the spicy coconut crab curry with big flaky chunks of crabmeat. The un-breaded deep fried whole branzino was steamy and flaky inside and crispy perfect on the outside. Fish Cheeks also has a nice selection of wines by the glass, and the gewurtzstraminer paired with the spicy curry nicely. We'll be back. The restaurant is located between Lafayette and Bowery, not Bowery and 2nd as noted on the address info.

Wow.  Do not come here.  If you invest in stocks this is the definition of a pump n dump.  The food is very basic and overpriced.  If you want good Thai food go to lam larb.   This place deserves no stars and no recognition.  It may know a few people as I saw gale greene there but the true foodies will see right through this scam.  Just don't go unless you want to see sad faces all around.  100% overpriced

When I came to the restaurant I was greeted by a wonderful man named Danny. He made me feel right at home. I believe that it is so important to have a great person to greet the customers that walk in through your door and he was above standard. Great looks and very kind hearted. He is an asset to the company! Definitely recommending this restaurant to friends and family.
This place is amazing. Great service and food. I had the vegetable curry and now I'm addicted. I Love this restaurant, and I will definitely be coming back soon.
Amazing service! Danny was great, recommend it to literally all my friends and family. Will come back in the near future!
Best food in the city! Amazing servers.  My tummy is full and I am happy!! I will recommend to all my friends, and I'll definitely be back! 5 stars but I wish I could give 100!
The service is great and friendly. Tasty dishes that are unapologetic. Im Thai and I love how authentic each dishes are.  Arok mak ka.

Wow! This new restaurant is on FIRE!!! The small plate fried chicken is not breaded or greasy at all with only juicy dark meat and fried shallots.  The coconut crab curry is a must have!  And all the cocktails are delicious.  If you like Thai food search no more! FISH CHEEKS CAN'T BE BEAT!  I can't wait to go back!!!

This place is the best restaurant in noho!! And definitely the best Thai in New York. We ended up ordering most everything on the menu, and nothing was below mind blowing. I would recommend the crab curry, branzino, woon senn, shrimp, calamari, and pad cha. (But that is most of the menu). The place is beautiful, so welcoming, and the servers are so great to talk to.  They have Aesop soap in the bathroom!! I was so impressed, and will be coming here often. Don't know what I did before this restaurant opened.
Food was amazing! Must try the Coconut Curry. Server was very friendly and knowledgeable, will definitely be returning soon!

The search is over ! Thank all the goddess in #Thailand, finally an authentic Thai restaurant in Manhattan! This is my new fave Thai in NYC. Sorry Uncle Boons :P 

My favorite tonight is the cured raw shrimp in crab sauce lime juice with chopped garlic, bird'seye chili and mint. This is prob the first Thai restaurant which I didn't say "make it extra spicy" lol. The dish is def hot but there so much more than just spicy: it has depth and dimensions - sweet, sour, salty and minty. Oh mine!  All flavors are blended seamlessly, balanced and fragrant. I can eat this every day! It goes very well with the off-dry Gewurztraminer i opted for. 

Main, I opted coconut crab curry (southern Thai style). In case you are not familiar with regional Thai cuisines,Southern Thai food tends to be much hotter than Thai food from other regions and being heavily influenced by flavors and spices used in Indonesia and Malaysia, which is intense and pungent. The coconut, so much part of the scenery, is used to its fullness. No exception in this beautiful bowl of goodness - chunks of king crab swimming in the golden color coconut curry with betel leaf (i consider it the equivalent to basil in Italian cooking with milder aroma). It is spicy yet subtly sweet and abundant coconut perfume. The curry paste is made in the traditional way , meaning mortar-and-pestle crushed. I must warn you, one sip of this golden curry, you will never be able to go back to your out-of-the-jar curry. 

All in all, I have a great experience here. From decor to service, and of course, the food. Menu is concise but well curated. Same can be said about the wine list. Cocktails seem interesting too though I prefer wine. 

Def will come back for more.

The food here is amazing, as are the drinks. We loved the namtok pork, the shrimp in 3 crabs sauce, and the crab curry, as well as the side of sauteed cabbage. The branzino was ok, very fried. 

The decor is super cute, very relaxed, feels like a beach restaurant in Thailand. 

My one bone to pick (hopefully they'll fix this, as they're still super new) is that our waiter really rushed us through our dinner. We were there on Saturday, and we were in and out in under an hour, and not by choice. They brought our entrees while our appetizers were still on the table, and then the second we were finished eating put a check on the table, which they then tried to pick up three separate times when we had not yet put a card in since we were still enjoying our drinks. Being that rushed when we were 'out for the night' on a Saturday was pretty annoying.

Next up for Thai Sunday:

New restaurant serving authetic Thai cuisine.
Limited/reasonably priced menu.

Highlight dishes:  Steamed mussels, fried calamari, crab fried rice, and tom yun goong.

Don't be afraid of the chili sign next to the dishes on the menu; The tom yun goong had a chili sign, but it wasn't spicy at all.

Enjoyed the rambutan for dessert. Tasted like they were freshly peeled.

Excellent service.

Recommend.

: 8 calendars

It's only been ten days since Fish Cheeks threw open their doors and it seems they've already found their bearings. My girlfriend and I walked in at 6pm and was able to get seated right away on a Thursday. Once seated, the staff promised an authentic Thai meal and that anything that was marked spicy on the menu would truly be spicy. I am happy to report that they delivered on both. 

Seeing as how Fish Cheeks bills themselves as serving family-style dishes, we ordered the Namtok Pork, Seafood Pad Cha and Coconut Crab Curry to share. All three items were marked spicy and it is here I'll issue a fair warning to those who can't handle spicy food; the Seafood Pad Cha and Coconut Crab Curry were so spicy it brought me back to the stifling streets of Bangkok on a humid Summer day. The food was sweat inducing spicy and I found myself reaching for my Thai iced tea to temper the heat in between bites but as mentioned, the food delivered on the authentic claims as well. The Namtok Pork in particular was bright, funky, savory and full of rich flavor. Bottom line, Fish Cheeks is a cute restaurant that offers truly flavorful Thai food.
Best Thai food in the city! The vibe is great and the food hit the spot! It's in an amazing area, I would highly recommend.

The food was seriously on point. Fresh, hot, spicy, harmony and flavorful. The chef here spent years with the world renowned chef David Thomson at Nahm restaurant in Bangkok. This dinner reminded me the time I was at Namh as well as other delicious restaurants in Thailand. If you're in restaurant industry, you'd already know that Nahm was No. 1 best Asian restaurant and in the world 50 best restaurants. Right here in Manhattan, as a result, we have the place to go for upscale Thai. 

Service was super friendly. However, our server might need more food knowledge (first day - understandable!).

Charming, warm, detail oriented and elegant design. Looked at them cooking in open kitchen even made the meal more spectacular.

Overall experience was amazing. Heard they would have awesome bar program created by the beverage guy from 'Employee's Only'. Will definitely go back to try more food with Asian influence cocktails!

Hit and miss!

The restaurant was buzzing with beautiful people but I am guessing it is mainly due to the hype on new opening as opposed to the food. 

Thanks to the previous yelper, we got the crispy branzino to share. It was the best dish we had that night.   Given the name of the restaurant, we stayed focus on seafood.  For appetizer, we had mussels to share...it was quite delicious but a very small portion (there were precisely 8 mussels in the pot)!  In addition to the fried branzino, we also got the Seafood pad cha and Goong Aob Woon Senn...pa cha was super spicy!! Watch out.  Goong aob soon senn came with glass noodle which I love...but part of the noodles were burnt and there were 2 shrimps and 1 piece of fatty pork (didn't taste the usual  pork belly flavor) in there.  For that, they charged $18!!

The service was very good and the hostess was very accommodating (I called to postpone our reservation by 15 mins given the inclement weather).  

It was nice to be one of the first to check out this place but needless to say, I won't be returning.  Will stick with Ngam for my Thai fix!
Very good indeed-- Crab curry is amazing .. If you can handle 5 stars spicy -- go for it!

Definitely get the fish here.

Take this review with a grain of salt, as I have a shellfish allergy, but was still able to try enough stuff to make a meal out of it. From the small plates, I was able to try the Hat Yai Fried Chicken ($12) and the Namtok Pork ($14). Both were decent, nothing particularly special, and probably just what suckers like me have to put up if they can't try the real (i.e. shellfish) stuff.

For the mains, we tried some shellfish stuff as well as the excellent Crispy Garlic Branzino with Fish Sauce ($32). These are definitely NoHo prices, and it's not that much fish for that price, but the fish you do get is excellent, with some super crispy skin and juicy meat. The Crab Curry, which had shellfish, was described as being notably spicy by my dining companions, who were both able to tolerate very spicy food, so be wary of that one.

The vibe is very hip and trendy modern Thai, with colorful seating and stuff that it's actually a little hard to notice and night since it's a super dark restaurant, but you can imagine how nice it will be when they launch lunch and brunch, especially if you get that spot in the front by the open windows.

They have a sign that proudly proclaims there is no pad thai here, so if you are looking for that type of Thai food, you will be disappointed. Otherwise, they have some delicious seafood in a fun setting that could be great for sharing in a group of people that can all eat shellfish.

Fun and adventurous new Thai seafood restaurant. The food is much more authentic than any other Thai restaurant I've eaten at in NYC, also most plates are shared so this is great for dates or groups. Lots of great dishes with shrimp and crab, great balance of flavor and spiciness. Also a veggie curry for those who don't eat seafood. The fried chicken and calamari make for excellent and tasty appetizers. The ambiance is clean with lots of cute Thai inspired details.

questions.question: How long should I plan for dinner?
questions.answer: 1.5 hours max... not really a lingering type of place. It will take that long to get a drink & your food

questions.question: Is it realistic to eat outside in their dinning shed in January?
questions.answer: Greetings! Our outdoor seating is heated and covered, and we are able to provide blankets as needed.  However, it all depends on the weather and temperature outdoors.  Most days are quite comfortable in the outdoor booths.
